Iti imasmiñca loke imasmiñca vajje tibbā bhayasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā hoti, seyyathāpi ukkhittāsike vadhake . Imehi paññāsāya ākārehi imāni pañcindriyāni jānāti passati aññāti paṭivijjhati, idaṃ tathāgatassa indriyaparopariyatte ñāṇa’’nti (paṭi. ma. 1.112).

Loko Vajja

Uppaliniyanti uppalavane. Itaresupi eseva nayo. Antonimuggaposīnīti yāni aññānipi padumāni antonimuggāneva posayanti. Udakaṃ accuggamma ṭhitānīti udakaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitāni. Tattha yāni accuggamma ṭhitāni, tāni sūriyarasmisamphassaṃ āgamayamānāni ṭhitāni ajja pupphanakāni. Yāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, tāni sve pupphanakāni. Yāni udakānuggatāni antoudakaposīni, tāni tatiyadivase pupphanakāni. Udakā pana anuggatāni aññānipi sarojauppalādīni nāma atthi, yāni neva pupphissanti, macchakacchapabhakkhāneva bhavissanti, tāni pāḷiṃ nārūḷhāni. Āharitvā pana dīpetabbānīti dīpitāni. Yatheva hi tāni catubbidhāni pupphāni, evameva ugghaṭitaññū, vipañcitaññū, neyyo, padaparamoti cattāro puggalā. Tattha yassa puggalassa saha udāhaṭavelāya dhammābhisamayo hoti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo ugghaṭitaññū. Yassa puggalassa saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthe vibhajiyamāne dhammābhisamayo hoti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo vipañcitaññū. Yassa puggalassa uddesato paripucchato yonisomanasikaroto kalyāṇamitte sevato bhajato payirupāsato anupubbena dhammābhisamayo hoti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo neyyo. Yassa puggalassa bahumpi suṇato bahumpi bhaṇato bahumpi gaṇhato bahumpi dhārayato bahumpi vācayato na tāya jātiyā dhammābhisamayo hoti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo padaparamo (pu. pa. 148, 149, 150, 151).

Uppaliniya Antonimuggaposīnī Udakaṃ accuggamma ṭhitānī ugghaṭitaññū. vipañcitaññū. neyyo. padaparamo

Tattha bhagavā uppalavanādisadisaṃ dasasahassilokadhātuṃ olokento – ‘‘ajja pupphanakāni viya ugghaṭitaññū, sve pupphanakāni viya vipañcitaññū, tatiyadivase pupphanakāni viya neyyo, macchakacchapabhakkhāni viya padaparamo’’ti addasa. Passanto ca – ‘‘ettakā apparajakkhā, ettakā mahārajakkhā. Tatrāpi ettakā ugghaṭitaññū’’ti evaṃ sabbākārato addasa. Tattha tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ imasmiṃyeva attabhāve bhagavato dhammadesanā atthaṃ sādheti, padaparamānaṃ anāgate vāsanatthāya hoti.

Atha bhagavā imesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthāvahaṃ dhammadesanaṃ viditvā desetukamyataṃ uppādetvā puna te sabbesupi tīsu bhavesu sabbe satte bhabbābhabbavasena dve koṭṭhāse akāsi. Ye sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ye te sattā kammāvaraṇena samannāgatā, vipākāvaraṇena samannāgatā, kilesāvaraṇena samannāgatā, assaddhā acchandikā duppaññā abhabbā niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṃ, ime te sattā abhabbā. Katame sattā bhabbā? Ye te sattā na kammāvaraṇena…pe…ime te sattā bhabbā’’ti (vibha. 827; paṭi. ma. 1.114).

Tattha sabbepi abhabbapuggale pahāya bhabbapuggaleyeva ñāṇena pariggahetvā – ‘‘ettakā rāgacaritā, ettakā dosamohavitakkasaddhābuddhicaritā’’ti cha koṭṭhāse akāsi. Evaṃ katvā – ‘‘dhammaṃ desessāmī’’ti cintesi . Brahmā taṃ ñatvā somanassajāto bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi. Idaṃ sandhāya – ‘‘atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
69. *Ajjhesana* means thus, threefold requesting.

*Buddhacakkhunā* means with the knowledge of the capacity of the faculties and with the knowledge of underlying tendencies.

Indeed, the name of these two knowledges is "*buddhacakkhū*," the name of the knowledge of omniscience is "*samantacakkhū*," the name of the three knowledges of the paths is "*dhammacakkhū*."

Among *apparajakkhe*, those whose passion, etc., is slight in the eye of wisdom, those are *apparajakkhā*.

Those whose is great, those are *mahārajakkhā*.

Those whose faculties, beginning with faith, are sharp, those are *tikkhindriyā*.

Those whose are mild, those are *mudindriyā*.

Those whose qualities such as faith are beautiful, those are *svākārā*.

Those who discern the stated reason, who are easily able to be instructed, those are *suviññāpayā*.

Those who see the next world and fault as fearful, they are named *paralokavajjabhayadassāvino*.

This is the Pāli here: "The faithful individual is with slight passion, the unfaithful individual is with great passion.

...the one who has aroused energy...the lazy one...the one with established mindfulness...the one with disturbed mindfulness...the concentrated one...the unconcentrated one...the wise one...the unwise individual is with great passion."

Thus, the faithful individual is with sharp faculties...the wise individual is one who sees the next world and faults as fearful, the unwise individual does not see the next world and faults as fearful.

*Loko* means aggregate-world ( *khandhaloko*), element-world ( *dhātuloko*), sense-base-world ( *āyatanaloko*), attainment-becoming-world ( *sampattibhavaloko*), adversity-becoming-world ( *vipattibhavaloko*), attainment-arising-world ( *sampattisambhavaloko*), adversity-arising-world ( *vipattisambhavaloko*).

One world: all beings subsist on nutriment ( *āhāraṭṭhitikā*).

Two worlds: name and form ( *nāmañca rūpañca*).

Three worlds: three feelings ( *tisso vedanā*).

Four worlds: four nutriments ( *cattāro āhārā*).

Five worlds: five aggregates of clinging ( *pañcupādānakkhandhā*).

Six worlds: six internal sense bases ( *cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni*).

Seven worlds: seven stations of consciousness ( *satta viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo*).

Eight worlds: eight worldly conditions ( *aṭṭha lokadhammā*).

Nine worlds: nine abodes of beings ( *nava sattāvāsā*).

Ten worlds: ten bases ( *dasāyatanāni*).

Twelve worlds: twelve bases ( *dvādasāyatanāni*).

Eighteen worlds: eighteen elements ( *aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo*).

*Vajja* means all defilements are fault ( *vajjaṃ*), all misconduct is fault ( *vajjaṃ*), all activities are fault ( *vajjaṃ*), all karma leading to becoming is fault ( *vajjaṃ*).

Thus, in this world and in this fault, intense fear is present, just as if a swordsman has raised his sword.

With these qualities of wisdom, he knows, sees, understands, and penetrates these five faculties; this is the knowledge of the capacity of the faculties of the Tathāgata.

*Uppaliniya* means in the lotus grove ( *uppalavane*).
And so with the others.

*Antonimuggaposīnī* means those other lotuses also that nourish only the inner bud.

*Udakaṃ accuggamma ṭhitānī* means those that stand having risen above the water.

There, those that stand having risen above, those standing awaiting the touch of the sun's rays, today are about to blossom.

Those that stand together with the water, tomorrow are about to blossom.

Those that are submerged in the water, nourished within the water, on the third day are about to blossom.

However, there are also other water-lilies and lotuses that are not submerged in the water, and which are not going to blossom, but will become food for fish and turtles; these are not included in the Pāli.

However, having been brought and shown, they are shown.

Just as those flowers are of four kinds, so too the individuals are of four kinds: *ugghaṭitaññū*, *vipañcitaññū*, *neyyo*, and *padaparamo*.

There, for whichever individual, at the very moment of mentioning, there is an understanding of the Dharma, this individual is called *ugghaṭitaññū*.

For whichever individual, when the meaning of what is spoken in brief is analyzed in detail, there is an understanding of the Dharma, this individual is called *vipañcitaññū*.

For whichever individual, through repeated questioning, through proper attention, through associating with, attending to, and waiting upon good friends, gradually there is an understanding of the Dharma, this individual is called *neyyo*.

For whichever individual, even though hearing much, speaking much, learning much, retaining much, reciting much, there is no understanding of the Dharma in that birth, this individual is called *padaparamo*.

There, the Blessed One, looking over the ten thousand world-systems, similar to a lotus grove, saw: "Like those about to blossom today, [are] the *ugghaṭitaññū*; like those about to blossom tomorrow, [are] the *vipañcitaññū*; like those about to blossom on the third day, [are] the *neyyo*; like those that are food for fish and turtles, [are] the *padaparamo*."

And seeing, "So many have little dust, so many have much dust, and even among them, so many are *ugghaṭitaññū*," thus he saw in every way.

There, for the three individuals, the Blessed One's teaching of the Dharma achieves its purpose in this very existence; for the *padaparamo*, it is for the sake of a trace in the future.

Then, the Blessed One, knowing the Dharma-teaching that brings benefit to these four individuals, and generating a desire to teach, again made all those beings in all three existences into two groups, according to whether they are capable or incapable.

Referring to which it was said: "Those beings who are endowed with a hindrance of deeds ( *kammāvaraṇa*), endowed with a hindrance of results ( *vipākāvaraṇa*), endowed with a hindrance of defilements ( *kilesāvaraṇa*), without faith, without desire, unwise, incapable of entering the fixed course, rightly, in wholesome things, these beings are incapable.

Which beings are capable? Those beings who are not with a hindrance of deeds...pe...these beings are capable" (Vibha. 827; Paṭi. Ma. 1. 114).

There, having abandoned all the incapable individuals, and having grasped only the capable individuals with knowledge, he made six groups: "So many are of lustful character, so many are of hateful, deluded, speculative, faithful, and intelligent character."

Having done this, he thought, "I will teach the Dharma."

Brahmā, knowing this, became delighted and addressed the Blessed One with verses.
Concerning this, it was said: "Then, monks, the Great Brahma..." etc.

mula_pali:
70. ‘‘Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito, yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ dhammamayaṃ sumedha, pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu.

‘Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ sokāvakiṇṇaṃ (syā.) janatamapetasoko,

sokāvakiṇṇaṃ (syā.)

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ;

Uṭṭhehi vīra vijitasaṅgāma,

Satthavāha aṇaṇa vicara loke.

Desassu desetu (syā. pī.) bhagavā dhammaṃ,

desetu (syā. pī.)

Aññātāro bhavissantī’ti.
mula_english:
"70. Then, monks, Mahā Brahmā, knowing with his mind the thought in the Blessed Vipassī’s, the Arahant, the perfectly enlightened one’s mind, addressed the Blessed Vipassī, the Arahant, the perfectly enlightened one in verses:

‘Just as one standing on the summit of a mountain of rock might see the people all around,

even so, O wise one, all-seeing, ascend the palace of Dharma, made of Dhamma.

‘Look upon the people plunged in sorrow, rid of sorrow yourself,

beholding those overcome by birth and old age;

Arise, O hero, victorious in battle,

Caravan-Leader, Debtless One, travel through the world.

Teach, O Blessed One, the Dharma,

there will be those who will understand.’"
commentary_pali:
70. Tattha ajjhabhāsīti adhiabhāsi, adhikicca ārabbha abhāsīti attho.

Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhitoti selamaye ekagghane pabbatamuddhani yathāṭhitova, na hi tattha ṭhitassa dassanatthaṃ gīvukkhipanapasāraṇādikiccaṃ atthi. Tathūpamanti tappaṭibhāgaṃ selapabbatūpamaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepattho, yathā selapabbatamuddhani yathāṭhitova cakkhumā puriso samantato janataṃ passeyya, tathā tvampi sumedha, sundarapaññasabbaññutaññāṇena samantacakkhu bhagavā dhammamayaṃ paññāmayaṃ pāsādamāruyha sayaṃ apetasoko sokāvatiṇṇaṃ jātijarābhibhūtaṃ janataṃ apekkhassu, upadhāraya upaparikkha.

Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito Tathūpama

Ayamettha adhippāyo – yathā hi pabbatapāde samantā mahantaṃ khettaṃ katvā tattha kedārapāḷīsu kuṭikāyo katvā rattiṃ aggiṃ jāleyyuṃ. Caturaṅgasamannāgatañca andhakāraṃ assa. Athassa pabbatassa matthake ṭhatvā cakkhumato purisassa bhūmiṃ olokayato neva khettaṃ, na kedārapāḷiyo, na kuṭiyo, na tattha sayitamanussā paññāyeyyuṃ, kuṭikāsu pana aggijālamattameva paññāyeyya. Evaṃ dhammapāsādamāruyha sattanikāyaṃ olokayato tathāgatassa ye te akatakalyāṇā sattā, te ekavihāre dakkhiṇajāṇupasse nisinnāpi buddhacakkhussa āpāthaṃ nāgacchanti, rattiṃ khittasarā viya honti. Ye pana katakalyāṇā veneyyapuggalā, te tassa dūre ṭhitāpi āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, so aggi viya himavantapabbato viya ca. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Dūre santo pakāsenti, himavantova pabbato;

Asantettha na dissanti, rattiṃ khittā yathā sarā’’ti. (dha. pa. 304);

Uṭṭhehīti bhagavato dhammadesanatthaṃ cārikacaraṇaṃ yācanto bhaṇati. Vīrātiādīsu bhagavā vīriyavantatāya vīro, devaputtamaccukilesamārānaṃ vijitattā vijitasaṅgāmo, jātikantarādinittharaṇatthāya veneyyasatthavāhanasamatthatāya satthavāho, kāmacchandaiṇassa abhāvato aṇaṇoti veditabbo.

Uṭṭhehī Vīrā vīro, vijitasaṅgāmo, satthavāho, aṇaṇo
commentary_english:
70. There, *ajjhabhāsī* means adhiabhāsi, meaning he spoke concerning and beginning with.

*sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito* means just as one stands on the peak of a mountain made of rock, one solid mass; there is no need for him to crane his neck or stretch to see. *tathūpama*nti means comparable to that, similar to a mountain of rock. Herein is the meaning in brief: Just as a man with sight, standing on the peak of a mountain of rock, might see the people all around, so too, O Sumedha, the Blessed One, all-seeing with the knowledge of beautiful wisdom, the all-knowing, having ascended the palace made of the Dhamma, made of wisdom, himself without sorrow, should look upon, consider, and examine the people afflicted by sorrow and overcome by birth and aging,

*sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito tathūpama* The idea here is this: Suppose someone were to make a large field all around the foot of a mountain, and having built huts in rows in the field, were to light a fire at night. It would be complete darkness with the four constituents. Then, to a man with sight standing on the summit of that mountain and looking down at the ground, neither the field, nor the rows of fields, nor the huts, nor the people lying there would appear; only the blaze of the fire in the huts would appear. In the same way, to the Tathāgata looking down at the assembly of beings after ascending the palace of the Dhamma, those beings who have not done good deeds do not come into the range of the Buddha's eye even when sitting near the right knee in a single monastery; they are like arrows shot at night. But those individuals who have done good deeds, those who are to be trained, come into range even when standing far away; he is like fire, like a mountain in the Himalayas. It was also said:

"The good make themselves known from afar, like a mountain in the Himalayas; The bad are not seen here, like arrows shot at night." (Dhp. 304);

*uṭṭhehī* means he speaks requesting the Blessed One to wander for the purpose of teaching the Dhamma. In *vīrā* etc., the Blessed One is called *vīro* because he is energetic, *vijitasaṅgāmo* because he has conquered the gods, death, defilements, and Māra, *satthavāho* because he is capable of conveying beings to be trained across the ocean of existence, *aṇaṇo* because of the absence of the debt of sensual desire.

*uṭṭhehī vīrā vīro, vijitasaṅgāmo, satthavāho, aṇaṇo*

mula_pali:
71. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho taṃ mahābrahmānaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

‘Apārutā tesaṃ amatassa dvārā,

Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu saddhaṃ;

Vihiṃsasaññī paguṇaṃ na bhāsiṃ,

Dhammaṃ paṇītaṃ manujesu brahme’ti.

‘‘Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ‘katāvakāso khomhi vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammadesanāyā’ti vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tattheva antaradhāyi.

Aggasāvakayugaṃ
mula_english:
"71. Then, monks, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, addressed that Great Brahma with a verse:

‘Open are the doors to the deathless for those who have ears to hear; let them show their faith. Thinking of causing no harm, I did not speak of what is excellent, the refined dharma, among humans, Brahma.’

Then, monks, that Great Brahma, [thinking:] ‘I have been given the opportunity by Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, for the teaching of the Dharma,’ having bowed down to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, and keeping his right side towards him, vanished there and then.

The foremost pair of disciples"
commentary_pali:
71.Apārutāti vivaṭā. Amatassa dvārāti ariyamaggo. So hi amatasaṅkhātassa nibbānassa dvāraṃ. So mayā vivaritvā ṭhapitoti dasseti. Pamuñcantu saddhanti sabbe attano saddhaṃ pamuñcantu vissajjentu. Pacchimapadadvaye ayamattho, ahañhi attano paguṇaṃ suppavattitampi imaṃ paṇītaṃ uttamaṃ dhammaṃ kāyavācākilamathasaññī hutvā na bhāsiṃ, idāni pana sabbe janā saddhābhājanaṃ upanentu, pūressāmi tesaṃ saṅkappanti.

Aggasāvakayugavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"apārutā" means open, uncovered.
"amatassa dvārā" means the path of the deathless (ariyamaggo).
For it is the gateway to *nirvāṇa*, which is known as the deathless.
He shows that it was opened and established by me.
"pamuñcantu saddhaṃ": Let everyone release and send forth their faith (saddhā).
This is the meaning of the latter two lines: Indeed, I, being weary in body and speech, did not speak this excellent and supreme dharma, [although it was] my own, skillful, and well-practiced. But now, let all people bring forth a vessel of faith; I will fulfill their intention.

Explanation of the foremost disciples.

mula_pali: 72. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa etadahosi – ‘kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, ko imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasanti paṇḍitā viyattā medhāvino dīgharattaṃ apparajakkhajātikā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ khaṇḍassa ca rājaputtassa, tissassa ca purohitaputtassa paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ , te imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissantī’ti.
mula_english:
"72.
Then, monks, it occurred to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘To whom should I first teach the *dharma* (dhammaṃ), who will quickly understand this *dharma* (dhammaṃ)?’ Then, monks, it occurred to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Khaṇḍa the prince and Tissa the son of the *purohita* (purohitaputto) dwell in Bandhumatī, the capital city; they are wise, learned, intelligent, and for a long time have been of little passionate nature.
If now I teach the *dharma* (dhammaṃ) first to Khaṇḍa the prince and to Tissa the son of the *purohita* (purohitaputto), they will quickly understand this *dharma* (dhammaṃ).’"

mula_pali: 73. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva bodhirukkhamūle antarahito bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā kheme migadāye pāturahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dāyapālaṃ migadāyapālaṃ (syā.) āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma dāyapāla, bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ pavisitvā khaṇḍañca rājaputtaṃ tissañca purohitaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – vipassī, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati, so tumhākaṃ dassanakāmo’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, dāyapālo vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ pavisitvā khaṇḍañca rājaputtaṃ tissañca purohitaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘vipassī, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati; so tumhākaṃ dassanakāmo’ti.
mula_english:
"73. Then, monks, the Blessed Vipassī, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, just as a strong man might stretch out his flexed arm or flex it again, vanished from the foot of the Bodhi tree and reappeared in the royal capital of Bandhumatī, in the Deer Park of Khema.

Then, monks, the Blessed Vipassī, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, addressed the park-keeper: ‘Come, good park-keeper, go to Bandhumatī, the royal capital, and say this to Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the chaplain’s son: “The Blessed Vipassī, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has arrived at Bandhumatī, the royal capital, and is staying in the Deer Park of Khema; he wishes to see you.”’

‘Even so, venerable sir,’ said the park-keeper to the Blessed Vipassī, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha. Having agreed, he entered Bandhumatī, the royal capital, and said this to Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the chaplain’s son: ‘The Blessed Vipassī, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has arrived at Bandhumatī, the royal capital, and is staying in the Deer Park of Khema; he wishes to see you.’"
commentary_pali: 73.Bodhirukkhamūleti bodhirukkhassa avidūre ajapālanigrodhe antarahitoti attho. Kheme migadāyeti isipatanaṃ tena samayena khemaṃ nāma uyyānaṃ hoti, migānaṃ pana abhayavāsatthāya dinnattā migadāyoti vuccati. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘kheme migadāye’’ti. Yathā ca vipassī bhagavā, evaṃ aññepi buddhā paṭhamaṃ dhammadesanatthāya gacchantā ākāsena gantvā tattheva otaranti. Amhākaṃ pana bhagavā upakassa ājīvakassa upanissayaṃ disvā – ‘‘upako imaṃ addhānaṃ paṭipanno, so maṃ disvā sallapitvā gamissati. Atha puna nibbindanto āgamma arahattaṃ sacchikarissatī’’ti ñatvā aṭṭhārasayojanamaggaṃ padasāva agamāsi. Dāyapālaṃ āmantesīti disvāva punappunaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘ayyo no, bhante, āgato’’ti vatvā upagataṃ āmantesi.
commentary_english:
73. *bodhirukkhamūle* means "at the foot of the *bodhi* tree," not far from the *bodhi* tree, at the *ajapālanigrodha*, without an interval.

*kheme migadāye* means that at that time, the deer park (*isipatana*) was a garden named Khema; it is called "deer park" (*migadāya*) because it was given for the sake of the deer to live without fear (*abhayavāsa*).

With reference to this, it was said, "*kheme migadāye*."

Just as Vipassī, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), so also other Buddhas, when going for the first time to teach the Dharma, go through the sky and descend right there.

But our Blessed One (*bhagavā*), seeing the potential of Upaka, the ājīvaka, [thought,] "Upaka has set out on this path; having seen me, he will converse with me and go on.

Then, again, becoming disenchanted, he will come back and realize arhatship." Knowing this, he went on foot for eighteen *yojana*.

*dāyapālaṃ āmantesī* means that having seen him, looking again and again, he called out to the approaching one, saying, "Are you our master, venerable sir (*bhante*)?"

mula_pali: 74. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā niyyiṃsu. Yena khemo migadāyo tena pāyiṃsu. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva padikāva (syā.) yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english: “Then, monks, Khaṇḍa the prince, and Tissa the son of the chaplain, having harnessed fine carriages, mounted fine carriages, and drove out of Bandhumatī in fine carriages. They headed for the deer park of Khema. As far as the ground was suitable for carriages, they went by carriage, then alighted from the carriages and proceeded on foot to where Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully awakened Buddha, was. Having approached Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully awakened Buddha, they bowed down and sat down to one side.

mula_pali: 75. ‘‘Tesaṃ vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ ānupubbikathaṃ (sī. pī.) kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva khaṇḍassa ca rājaputtassa tissassa ca purohitaputtassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.
mula_english:
75. The Blessed Vipassī, the *arhat*, the perfectly awakened Buddha, gave them a graduated talk, that is to say, a talk on giving (*dānakathā*), a talk on virtue (*śīlakathā*), a talk on heaven (*svargakathā*), showing the danger, degradation, and corruption of sense-desires, and the profit of renunciation (*naiskramya*).

When the Lord knew that they had ready minds, pliable minds, open minds, uplifted minds, confident minds, he explained to them that teaching on the *dharma* which the awakened ones have themselves discovered: suffering (*duḥkha*), its origin (*samudaya*), its cessation (*nirodha*), and the path (*mārga*).

Just as a clean piece of cloth, free from grime, would properly take dye, in the same way the dustless, stainless eye of *dharma* arose for Khaṇḍa the prince and Tissa the chaplain’s son as they were sitting right there—"Whatever is subject to origination (*samudayadharma*) is all subject to cessation (*nirodhadharma*)."

mula_pali: 76. ‘‘Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’’ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca. Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada’nti.
mula_english:
‘And they, having seen the *dhamma*, having attained the *dhamma*, having known the *dhamma*, having fathomed the *dhamma*, having crossed over and beyond uncertainty (*vicikicchā*), having no more perplexity, having gained fearlessness (*vesārajja*), independence of others with regard to the Teacher’s doctrine, said to Vipassi, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*), “Magnificent, Lord, magnificent!

Just as, Lord, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or carry a lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes could see forms. Even so, Lord, the *dhamma* has been revealed in many ways by the Blessed One.

We go to the Blessed One for refuge (*saraṇaṃ gacchāma*), and to the *dhamma*. May we receive the going-forth (*pabbajja*) in the Lord’s presence, may we receive ordination (*upasampada*)!”

mula_pali:
77. ‘‘Alatthuṃ kho , bhikkhave, khaṇḍo ca rājaputto, tisso ca purohitaputto vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne nekkhamme (syā.) ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ samādapiyamānānaṃ samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

Mahājanakāyapabbajjā
mula_english:
“And so, monks, Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the chaplain’s son, received the going-forth and ordination in the presence of the Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, fully awakened one. Then the Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, fully awakened one, instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a Dhamma talk, revealing the danger, inferiority, and defilement in conditioned things, and the benefit in *nirvāṇa*. As they were being instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, fully awakened one, with a Dhamma talk, before long their minds were freed from the corruptions without clinging."

The going forth of a large group.
commentary_pali:
77.Alatthunti kathaṃ alatthuṃ? Ehibhikkhubhāvena. Bhagavā kira tesaṃ iddhimayapattacīvarassūpanissayaṃ olokento anekāsu jātīsu cīvaradānādīni disvā etha bhikkhavotiādimāha . Te tāvadeva bhaṇḍū kāsāyavasanā aṭṭhahi bhikkhuparikkhārehi sarīrapaṭimukkeheva vassasatikattherā viya bhagavantaṃ namassamānāva nisīdiṃsu.

Sandassesītiādīsu idhalokatthaṃ sandassesi, paralokatthaṃ sandassesi. Idhalokatthaṃ dassento aniccanti dassesi, dukkhanti dassesi, anattāti dassesi, khandhe dassesi, dhātuyo dassesi, āyatanāni dassesi, paṭiccasamuppādaṃ dassesi, rūpakkhandhassa udayaṃ dassento pañca lakkhaṇāni dassesi, tathā vedanākkhandhādīnaṃ, tathā vayaṃ dassentopi udayabbayavasena paññāsalakkhaṇāni dassesi, paralokatthaṃ dassento nirayaṃ dassesi, tiracchānayoniṃ, pettivisayaṃ, asurakāyaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ kusalānaṃ vipākaṃ, channaṃ devalokānaṃ, navannaṃ brahmalokānaṃ sampattiṃ dassesi.

Sandassesī

Samādapesīti catupārisuddhisīlaterasadhutaṅgadasakathāvatthuādike kalyāṇadhamme gaṇhāpesi.

Samādapesī

Samuttejesīti suṭṭhu uttejesi, abbhussāhesi. Idhalokatthañceva paralokatthañca tāsetvā tāsetvā adhigataṃ viya katvā kathesi. Dvattiṃsakammakāraṇapañcavīsatimahābhayappabhedañhi idhalokatthaṃ buddhe bhagavati tāsetvā tāsetvā kathayante pacchābāhaṃ, gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā cātumahāpathe pahārasatena tāḷetvā dakkhiṇadvārena niyyamāno viya āghātanabhaṇḍikāya ṭhapitasīso viya sūle uttāsito viya mattahatthinā maddiyamāno viya ca saṃviggo hoti. Paralokatthañca kathayante nirayādīsu nibbatto viya devalokasampattiṃ anubhavamāno viya ca hoti.

Samuttejesī

Sampahaṃsesīti paṭiladdhaguṇena codesi, mahānisaṃsaṃ katvā kathesīti attho.

Sampahaṃsesī

Saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavanti heṭṭhā paṭhamamaggādhigamatthaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ kathesi, idha pana uparimaggādhigamatthaṃ – ‘‘aniccā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā addhuvā anassāsikā, yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ alaṃ virajjituṃ alaṃ vimuccitu’’ntiādinā (a. ni. 7.66; saṃ. ni. 2.134) nayena saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavañca lāmakabhāvañca tappaccayañca kilamathaṃ pakāsesi. Yathā ca tattha nekkhamme, evamidha – ‘‘santamidaṃ, bhikkhave, nibbānaṃ nāma paṇītaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇa’’ntiādinā nayena nibbāne ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi.

Saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnava

Mahājanakāyapabbajjāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
77. "Alatthuṃ": How did they obtain? By becoming "Come, mendicants."

It is said that the Blessed One, looking at the underlying conditions for their bowl and robe made by psychic power, seeing the giving of robes, etc., in many births, said, "Etha bhikkhavo" [Come, mendicants] etc.

As soon as they were shaved, wearing brown robes, with the eight requisites of a monk, with bodies fully equipped, they sat down, venerating the Blessed One, like elders of a hundred years.

In "sandassesī" etc., he revealed the benefit for this world, he revealed the benefit for the next world.

Showing the benefit for this world, he showed impermanence, he showed suffering, he showed no-self, he showed the aggregates, he showed the elements, he showed the sense bases, he showed dependent origination, showing the arising of the form aggregate, he showed the five characteristics, likewise of the feeling aggregate, etc., likewise showing the passing away, he showed the fifty characteristics by way of arising and passing away; showing the benefit for the next world, he showed hell, the animal realm, the realm of ghosts, the demon body, the result of the three wholesome [deeds], the attainment of the six heavens, of the nine Brahma worlds.

Sandassesī

"Samādapesī": he made them grasp the wholesome qualities such as the fourfold purity of virtue, the thirteen ascetic practices, the ten topics of conversation.

Samādapesī

"Samuttejesī": he greatly encouraged, he heartened. Having frightened them repeatedly with the benefit for this world and the benefit for the next world, he spoke as if he had attained it.

Indeed, while describing the thirty-two acts of karma and the twenty-five divisions of great fear for the benefit of this world, having frightened them repeatedly in the Buddha, the Blessed One, one becomes agitated as if being led away backwards, having bound a tight bond, having struck with a hundred blows in the four great crossroads, being led out through the southern gate, as if his head were placed on the executioner's block, as if impaled on a stake, as if being crushed by a drunken elephant.

And while describing the benefit for the next world, one is as if reborn in hells, and as if experiencing the attainment of heavenly worlds.

Samuttejesī

"Sampahaṃsesī": he blamed them with the acquired qualities, meaning he spoke having made it of great benefit.

Sampahaṃsesī

"Saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ": Below, he spoke of the danger of sensual pleasures for the attainment of the first path, but here, for the attainment of the higher paths - "Impermanent, monks, are conditioned things, unstable, unreliable; for as long as this, monks, it is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned things, enough to be dispassionate, enough to be liberated" etc. (A. Ni. 7.66; Saṃ. Ni. 2.134), in this way he revealed the danger of conditioned things, their wretchedness, their conditionality, and the toil.

And just as there [it was] renunciation, so here - "Peaceful, monks, is this Nibbāna by name, excellent, a refuge, a shelter" etc., in this way he revealed the benefit in Nibbāna.

Saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ

Description of Mahājanaka’s Going Forth

mula_pali: 78. ‘‘Assosi kho, bhikkhave, bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā mahājanakāyo caturāsītipāṇasahassāni – ‘vipassī kira bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati. Khaṇḍo ca kira rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā’ti. Sutvāna nesaṃ etadahosi – ‘na hi nūna so orako dhammavinayo, na sā orakā pabbajjā, yattha khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. Khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissanti, kimaṅgaṃ pana maya’nti. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahājanakāyo caturāsītipāṇasahassāni bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā nikkhamitvā yena khemo migadāyo yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english:
"Monks, the great crowd of eighty-four thousand beings in the capital city of Bandhumatī heard that the Blessed One Vipaśyī, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, had arrived in Bandhumatī and was staying in the Khemā Deer Park.

They heard that Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissā, the son of the chaplain, had shaved off their hair and beards in the presence of the Blessed One Vipaśyī, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, donned yellow robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness.

Having heard this, they thought: “This is certainly no common teaching and discipline, nor a common going forth, for which Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissā, the son of the chaplain, have shaved off their hair and beards, donned yellow robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness.

If Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissā, the son of the chaplain, can shave off their hair and beards, don yellow robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness, why not us?”

Then, monks, that great crowd of eighty-four thousand beings left the capital city of Bandhumatī and went to the Khemā Deer Park where the Blessed One Vipaśyī, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, was. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One Vipaśyī, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, and sat down to one side."
commentary_pali: 78.Mahājanakāyoti tesaṃyeva dvinnaṃ kumārānaṃ upaṭṭhākajanakāyoti.
commentary_english: 78. *Mahājanakāyo* means the attending multitude of those two boys.

mula_pali: 79. ‘‘Tesaṃ vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi. Seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte , atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ caturāsītipāṇasahassānaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.
mula_english:
‘And the Lord Buddha Vipassī, worthy one, completely awakened, delivered to them a graduated discourse. Specifically, he gave a talk on generosity (*dānakathā*), a talk on morality (*śīlakathā*), a talk on heaven (*svargakathā*), and he revealed the danger (*ādīnava*), degradation (*okāra*), and corruption (*saṃkilesa*) of sense-desires (*kāmānaṃ*), and the profit (*ānisaṃsa*) of renunciation (*naiskramya*).

When the Blessed One understood that they had ready minds, pliable minds, minds free from hindrances, uplifted minds, and confident minds, then he revealed the teaching unique to the Buddhas: suffering (*duḥkha*), its origin (*samudaya*), its cessation (*nirodha*), and the path (*mārga*).

Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, would properly absorb dye, in the same way, in those eighty-four thousand beings, as they sat there, the spotless, immaculate eye of the Dharma (*dharmacakṣu*) arose: “Whatever is subject to origination (*samudayadharma*) is all subject to cessation (*nirodhadharma*).”

mula_pali: 80. ‘‘Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’’ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca ( ) natthi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, pāḷiyaṃ pana sabbatthapi dissati. Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ labheyyāma upasampada’’nti.
mula_english:
‘And they, having seen the Dhamma ( *dṛṣṭadharma*), attained the Dhamma (*prāptadharma*), known the Dhamma (*viditadharma*), fathomed the Dhamma (*pariyogāḍhadharma*), having crossed over doubt (*tīrṇavicikitsa*), having no more uncertainty (*vigatakathaṃkathā*), having gained fearlessness (*vaiśārajyaprāpta*), independence of others with regard to the Teacher’s message, said to Vipassin, the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the perfectly awakened Buddha: “Excellent, Lord, excellent!

Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms.

Just so has the Blessed One made clear the Dhamma in various ways (*anekapariyāyena*).

We go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the monastic community (*bhikṣusaṃgha*).

May we receive the going forth (*pravrajyā*) in the presence of the Blessed One, may we receive full ordination (*upasampadā*)!”
commentary_pali: 80.Bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma, dhammañcāti saṅghassa aparipuṇṇattā dvevācikameva saraṇamagamaṃsu.
commentary_english: We go for refuge to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma), and to the Dharma (dhammañcā). Because the Saṅgha was incomplete (saṅghassa aparipuṇṇattā), they took refuge with only a twofold declaration (dvevācikameva saraṇamagamaṃsu).

mula_pali:
81. ‘‘Alatthuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipāṇasahassāni vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ, alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ samādapiyamānānaṃ samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

Purimapabbajitānaṃ dhammābhisamayo
mula_english:
“And those eighty-four thousand, monks, received the going-forth at the hands of the Blessed Lord Vipassi (Vipassī), the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and they received ordination.

Then the Lord Buddha Vipassi (Vipassī), the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed them with a discourse on the Dhamma, inspired them, fired them and delighted them, revealing the danger, degradation, and corruption of conditioned things (saṅkhārānaṃ), and the benefit of *nirvāṇa* (nibbāne).

And through their being instructed, inspired, fired and delighted with this discourse by the Lord Vipassi (Vipassī), the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, it was not long before their minds were freed from the corruptions without remainder.

The Realization of the Dhamma by the Former Ascetics
commentary_pali:
81.Alatthunti pubbe vuttanayeneva ehibhikkhubhāveneva alatthuṃ. Ito anantare pabbajitavārepi eseva nayo.

Cārikāanujānanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
alatthu, as before, was obtained through the state of "come, monk."
So too with the following ordination.
Explanation of allowing wanderings.

mula_pali: 82. ‘‘Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni purimāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni – ‘vipassī kira bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati, dhammañca kira desetī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni yena bandhumatī rājadhānī yena khemo migadāyo yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english: Monks, those former eighty-four thousand ascetics heard, "The Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, fully awakened one, has arrived at Bandhumatī, the capital city, and is staying in the deer park of Khema, and it is said he is teaching the Dharma." Then, monks, those eighty-four thousand ascetics went to Bandhumatī, the capital city, to the deer park of Khema, to the Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, fully awakened one; having approached Vipassī, the Blessed One, the worthy, fully awakened one, they paid homage and sat down to one side.

mula_pali: 83. ‘‘Tesaṃ vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi. Seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ caturāsītipabbajitasahassānaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.
mula_english:
‘And the Lord Vipassī, the Blessed One, the *arhat*, the perfectly awakened Buddha, delivered to them a graduated discourse. Namely, he proclaimed a talk on generosity (*dānakathā*), a talk on morality (*śīlakathā*), a talk on heaven (*svargakathā*), [and] the danger (*ādīnava*), degradation (*okāra*), and corruption (*saṃkilesa*) of sensual pleasures (*kāma*), and the benefit (*ānisaṃsa*) of renunciation (*naiskramya*).

When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready (*kallacitte*), supple (*muducitte*), free from hindrances (*vinīvaraṇacitte*), uplifted (*udaggacitte*), and confident (*pasannacitte*), then he revealed the teaching (*dharmadeśanā*) unique to the Buddhas (*buddhānām*): suffering (*duḥkha*), its origin (*samudaya*), its cessation (*nirodha*), and the path (*mārga*).

Just as a clean cloth, free of stains, would properly absorb dye, in the same way, as those eighty-four thousand renunciates were sitting right there, the stainless, immaculate eye of the Dharma (*dharmacakṣus*) arose within them: “Whatever is subject to origination (*samudayadharma*) is all subject to cessation (*nirodhadharma*).”

mula_pali: 84. ‘‘Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ , bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’’ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ labheyyāma upasampada’’nti.
mula_english: ‘And they, having seen, attained, experienced and penetrated the Dhamma (dharma), having passed beyond doubt, having gained perfect confidence in the Teacher’s (śāstṛ) doctrine (śāsana) without relying on others, said to Vipassī, the Blessed One (bhagavān), the Worthy One (arhan), the Perfectly Awakened One (samyaksaṃbuddha): “Excellent, O Lord (bhante), excellent, O Lord. Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what had been hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring a lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see what is there—in the same way has the Blessed One (bhagavatā) made the Dhamma (dharma) clear in various ways (anekapariyāyena). We go for refuge to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ), to the Dhamma (dhamma), and to the Sangha (saṅgha) of monks (bhikkhusaṅghañca). May we receive the going-forth (pravrajyā) at the Lord’s (bhagavato) hands, may we receive ordination (upasampadā)!”’

mula_pali:
85. ‘‘Alatthuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ samādapiyamānānaṃ samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

Cārikāanujānanaṃ
mula_english:
‘And those eighty-four thousand who had gone forth, monks, received the going forth at the hands of the Blessed Lord Vipassī, the Worthy One, the Fully Awakened One; they received ordination.

Then the Blessed Vipassī, the Worthy One, the Fully Awakened One, instructed, roused, inspired, and delighted them with a discourse on the Dharma, revealing the danger, degradation, and corruption of conditioned things and the benefit of nirvāṇa (nibbāna).

And through their being instructed, roused, inspired, and delighted with this discourse by the Blessed Vipassī, the Worthy One, the Fully Awakened One, before long their minds were freed from the corruptions without grasping.

Permission to Wander
commentary_pali:
85.Parivitakko udapādīti kadā udapādi? Sambodhito satta saṃvaccharāni satta māse satta divase atikkamitvā udapādi. Bhagavā kira pitusaṅgahaṃ karonto vihāsi. Rājāpi cintesi – ‘‘mayhaṃ jeṭṭhaputto nikkhamitvā buddho jāto, dutiyaputto me nikkhamitvā aggasāvako jāto, purohitaputto dutiyaaggasāvako, ime ca avasesā bhikkhū gihikālepi mayhaṃ puttameva parivāretvā vicariṃsu. Ime sabbe idānipi mayhaṃyeva bhāro, ahameva ca ne catūhi paccayehi upaṭṭhahissāmi, aññesaṃ okāsaṃ na dassāmī’’ti vihāradvārakoṭṭhakato paṭṭhāya yāva rājagehadvārā ubhayato khadirapākāraṃ kārāpetvā kilañjehi chādāpetvā vatthehi paṭicchādāpetvā upari ca chādāpetvā suvaṇṇatārakavicittaṃ samolambitatālakkhandhamattaṃ vividhapupphadāmavitānaṃ kārāpetvā heṭṭhā bhūmiyaṃ cittattharaṇehi santharāpetvā anto ubhosu passesu mālāvacchake puṇṇaghaṭe, sakalamaggavāsatthāya ca gandhantare pupphāni pupphantare gandhe ca ṭhapāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi.

Bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto antosāṇiyāva rājagehaṃgantvā bhattakiccaṃ katvā vihāraṃ paccāgacchati. Añño koci daṭṭhumpi na labhati, kuto pana bhikkhaṃ vā dātuṃ, pūjaṃ vā kātuṃ, dhammaṃ vā sotuṃ. Nāgarā cintesuṃ – ‘‘ajja satthu loke uppannassa sattamāsādhikāni sattasaṃvaccharāni, mayañca daṭṭhumpi na labhāma, pageva bhikkhaṃ vā dātuṃ, pūjaṃ vā kātuṃ, dhammaṃ vā sotuṃ. Rājā – ‘mayhameva buddho, mayhameva dhammo, mayhameva saṅgho’ti mamāyitvā sayameva upaṭṭhahi. Satthā ca uppajjamāno sadevakassa lokassa atthāya hitāya uppanno. Na hi raññoyeva nirayo uṇho assa, aññesaṃ nīluppalavanasadiso. Tasmā rājānaṃ vadāma. Sace no satthāraṃ deti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce deti, raññā saddhiṃ yujjhitvāpi saṅghaṃ gahetvā dānādīni puññāni karoma. Na sakkā kho pana suddhanāgareheva evaṃ kātuṃ, ekaṃ jeṭṭhapurisampi gaṇhāmā’’ti.

Te senāpatiṃ upasaṅkamitvā tassetamatthaṃ ārocetvā – ‘‘sāmi, kiṃ amhākaṃ pakkho hosi, udāhu rañño’’ti āhaṃsu. So – ‘‘ahaṃ tumhākaṃ pakkho homi, api ca kho pana paṭhamadivaso mayhaṃ dātabbo’’ti. Te sampaṭicchiṃsu. So rājānaṃ upasaṅkamitvā – ‘‘nāgarā, deva, tumhākaṃ kupitā’’ti āha. Kimatthaṃ tātāti? Satthāraṃ kira tumheyeva upaṭṭhahatha, amhe na labhāmāti. Sace idānipi labhanti, na kuppanti, alabhantā tumhehi saddhiṃ yujjhitukāmā devāti. Yujjhāmi, tāta, nāhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ demīti. Deva tumhākaṃ dāsā tumhehi saddhiṃ yujjhāmāti vadanti, tumhe kaṃ gaṇhitvā yujjhissathāti? Nanu tvaṃ senāpatīti? Nāgarehi vinā na samattho ahaṃ devāti. Tato rājā – ‘‘balavanto nāgarā, senāpatipi tesaññeva pakkho’’ti ñatvā ‘‘aññānipi sattamāsādhikāni sattasaṃvaccharāni mayhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ dadantū’’ti āha. Nāgarā na sampaṭicchiṃsu. Rājā – ‘‘cha vassāni, pañca, cattāri, tīṇi, dve, ekavassa’’nti hāpesi. Evaṃ hāpentepi na sampaṭicchiṃsu. Aññe satta divase yāci. Nāgarā – ‘‘atikakkhaḷaṃ dāni raññā saddhiṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī’’ti anujāniṃsu.

Rājā sattamāsādhikānaṃ sattannaṃ saṃvaccharānaṃ sajjitaṃ dānamukhaṃ sattannameva divasānaṃ vissajjetvā cha divase kesañci apassantānaṃyeva dānaṃ datvā sattame divase nāgare pakkosāpetvā – ‘‘sakkhissatha, tāta, evarūpaṃ dānaṃ dātu’’nti āha. Tepi – ‘‘nanu amheyeva nissāya taṃ devassa uppanna’’nti vatvā – ‘‘sakkhissāmā’’ti āhaṃsu. Rājā piṭṭhihatthena assūni puñchamāno bhagavantaṃ vanditvā – ‘‘bhante, ahaṃ aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ aññassa vāraṃ akatvā yāvajīvaṃ catūhi paccayehi upaṭṭhahissāmīti cintesiṃ. Nāgarā na dāni me anuññātā, nāgarā hi ‘mayaṃ dānaṃ dātuṃ na labhāmā’ti kuppanti. Bhagavā sve paṭṭhāya tesaṃ anuggahaṃ karothā’’ti āha.

Atha dutiyadivase senāpati mahādānaṃ sajjetvā – ‘‘ajja yathā añño koci ekabhikkhampi na deti, evaṃ rakkhathā’’ti samantā purise ṭhapesi. Taṃ divasaṃ seṭṭhibhariyā rodamānā dhītaraṃ āha – ‘‘sace, amma, tava pitā jīveyya, ajjāhaṃ paṭhamaṃ dasabalaṃ bhojeyya’’nti . Sā taṃ āha – ‘‘amma, mā cintayi, ahaṃ tathā karissāmi yathā buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho paṭhamaṃ amhākaṃ bhikkhaṃ paribhuñjissatī’’ti. Tato satasahassagghanikāya suvaṇṇapātiyā nirudakapāyāsassa pūretvā sappimadhusakkarādīhi abhisaṅkharitvā aññāya pātiyā paṭikujjitvā taṃ sumanamālāguḷehi parikkhipitvā mālāguḷasadisaṃ katvā bhagavato gāmaṃ pavisanavelāya sayameva ukkhipitvā dāsigaṇaparivutā nagarā nikkhami. Antarāmagge senāpatiupaṭṭhākā – ‘‘amma, mā ito agamā’’ti vadanti. Mahāpuññā nāma manāpakathā honti, na ca tesaṃ punappunaṃ bhaṇantānaṃ kathā paṭikkhipituṃ sakkā hoti. Sā – ‘‘cūḷapitā mahāpitā mātulā kissa tumhe gantuṃ na dethā’’ti āha. Senāpatinā – ‘‘aññassa kassaci khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ dātuṃ mā dethā’’ti ṭhapitamha ammāti. Kiṃ pana me hatthe khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ passathāti? Mālāguḷaṃ passāmāti . Kiṃ tumhākaṃ senāpati mālāguḷapūjampi kātuṃ na detīti? Deti, ammāti. Tena hi, apetha, apethāti bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā mālāguḷaṃ gaṇhāpetha bhagavāti āha. Bhagavā ekaṃ senāpatissupaṭṭhākaṃ oloketvā mālāguḷaṃ gaṇhāpesi. Sā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā – ‘‘bhagavā, bhavābhave nibbattiyaṃ me sati paritassanajīvitaṃ nāma mā hotu, ayaṃ sumanamālā viya nibbattanibbattaṭṭhāne piyāva homi, nāmena ca sumanā yevā’’ti patthanaṃ katvā satthārā – ‘‘sukhinī hohī’’ti vuttā vanditvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Bhagavā senāpatissa gehaṃ gantvā paññattāsane nisīdi. Senāpati yāguṃ gahetvā upagañchi, satthā pattaṃ pidahi. Nisinno, bhante, bhikkhusaṅghoti. Atthi no eko antarā piṇḍapāto laddhoti. So mālaṃ apanetvā piṇḍapātaṃ addasa. Cūḷupaṭṭhāko āha – ‘‘sāmi, mālāti maṃ vatvā mātugāmo vañcesī’’ti. Pāyāso bhagavantaṃ ādiṃ katvā sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pahoti. Senāpatipi attano deyyadhammaṃ adāsi. Satthā bhattakiccaṃ katvā maṅgalaṃ vatvā pakkāmi. Senāpati – ‘‘kā nāma sā piṇḍapātamadāsī’’ti pucchi. Seṭṭhidhītā, sāmīti. Sappaññā sā itthī, evarūpāya ghare vasantiyā purisassa saggasampatti nāma na dullabhāti taṃ ānetvā jeṭṭhikaṭṭhāne ṭhapesi.

Punadivase nāgarā dānamadaṃsu, punadivase rājāti ekantarikāya dānaṃ dātuṃ ārabhiṃsu. Rājāpi carapurise ṭhapetvā nāgarehi dinnadānato atirekataraṃ deti, nāgarāpi tatheva katvā raññā dinnadānato atirekataraṃ. Rājagehe nāṭakitthiyo daharasāmaṇere vadanti – ‘‘gaṇhatha, tātā, na gahapatikānaṃ gattavatthādīsu puñchitvā bāḷadārakānaṃ kheḷasiṅghāṇikādidhovanahatthehi kataṃ , suciṃ paṇītaṃ kata’’nti. Punadivase nāgarāpi dadamānā vadanti – ‘‘gaṇhatha, tātā, na nagaragāmanigamādīsu saṅkaḍḍhitataṇḍulakhīradadhisappiādīhi, na aññesaṃ jaṅghasīsapiṭṭhiādīni bhañjitvā āharāpitehi kataṃ, jātisappikhīrādīhiyeva kata’’nti. Evaṃ sattasu saṃvaccharesu sattasu māsesu sattasu divasesu ca atikkantesu atha bhagavato ayaṃ vitakko udapādi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘sambodhito satta saṃvaccharāni satta māsāni satta divasāni atikkamitvā udapādī’’ti.
commentary_english:
85. The thought, *parivitakko udapādī*, arose. When did it arise? It arose seven years, seven months, and seven days after his enlightenment. The Blessed One stayed there, showing kindness to his father. The king also thought: “My eldest son, having gone forth, has become a buddha. My second son, having gone forth, has become the foremost disciple. The son of the chaplain is the second foremost disciple. And these remaining monks, even in their householder days, having surrounded my son, wandered about. Now even these all are my burden. I myself will attend to them with the four requisites. I will not give the opportunity to others.” From the gatehouse of the monastery to the gate of the royal palace, on both sides, having had a *khadira* wall built, having had it covered with mats, having had it covered over with cloths, and having had it covered over above, having had various *puṣpa-dāma-vitāna* decorated with golden stars and as tall as a palm tree hung, and having had the ground below strewn with painted carpets, having had full jars placed at the entrance on both sides, in the *mālāvacaka*, and having had flowers placed among perfumes and perfumes among flowers for the sake of the entire road being fragrant, he announced the time to the Blessed One. The Blessed One, surrounded by the Saṃgha of monks, went to the royal palace as far as the inner courtyard, and having performed the meal duties, returned to the monastery. No one else is able to see him, how much less to give alms, to do reverence, or to hear the Dharma! The townspeople thought: “Today it is seven years and seven months since the Teacher arose in the world, and we do not even get to see him, how much less to give alms, to do reverence, or to hear the Dharma! The king, thinking, ‘The Buddha is mine, the Dharma is mine, the Saṃgha is mine,’ attends to him himself, being possessive. The Teacher, arising, has arisen for the benefit and welfare of the world with its devas. Indeed, hell would not be hot for the king alone, but like a grove of blue lotuses for others. Therefore, let us speak to the king. If he gives us the Teacher, that would be good. If he does not give us [the Teacher], having fought with the king, we will take the Saṃgha and perform meritorious deeds such as giving alms. It is not possible to do this just with pure townspeople. Let us take one elder too.” Having approached the commander-in-chief, having announced this matter to him, they said: “Lord, which side are you on, ours or the king’s?” He said: “I am on your side, but the first day must be given to me.” They agreed. He approached the king and said: “The townspeople, Your Majesty, are angry.” “Why, friends?” [he asked.] “You alone attend to the Teacher. We do not get to.” "If they are able to obtain [the Teacher] even now, they will not be angry. If they do not obtain [the Teacher], they wish to fight with you, Your Majesty!" “I will fight, friends, but I will not give the Saṃgha of monks." "Your Majesty, your servants say, 'We will fight with you.' Whom will you take and fight with? Are you not the commander-in-chief? Without the townspeople, I am not capable, Your Majesty.” Then the king, having learned that “the townspeople are powerful, and the commander-in-chief is on their side,” said: "Let even others give the Saṃgha of monks to me for seven years with seven months added!" The townspeople did not agree. The king reduced it: “Six years, five, four, three, two, one year.” Even while he was reducing it like this, they did not agree. He asked for seven other days. The townspeople consented: “It is not fitting to act too harshly with the king now.” The king, having given away in only seven days the provisions for giving that had been prepared for seven years with seven months added, having given alms to some without looking [at them] for six days, on the seventh day, having had the townspeople summoned, said: "Will you be able, friends, to give alms of this kind?" They too, saying, “Is it not because of us that that arose for Your Majesty?”, said, “We will be able.” The king, wiping away his tears with the back of his hand, having bowed to the Blessed One, [said:] “Venerable sir, I was thinking, ‘Without giving a turn to anyone else, I will attend to the Saṃgha of eighty-eight hundred thousand monks for as long as I live with the four requisites.’” The townspeople are not now permitted by me [to give alms]. Indeed, the townspeople are angry, [thinking,] "We are unable to make a gift." The Blessed One said, "Then, starting from today, show them favor."

Then, on the second day, the general prepared a great gift, [stationing] men all around, [saying,] "Today, ensure that not even a single alms-seeker is given [anything] by anyone else." On that day, the treasurer's wife, weeping, said to her daughter, "If, dear, your father were alive, today I would feed the Ten-Powered One first."

. She said to him, "Dear, do not worry. I will act in such a way that the Saṃgha of monks, with the Buddha at its head, will partake of our alms-food first." Then, having filled a golden bowl worth one hundred thousand [coins] with rice porridge without water, having mixed it with ghee, honey, sugar, and so forth, having inverted it with another bowl, having surrounded it with *sumana* flower garlands, having made it similar to a garland of flowers, she herself, lifting it up at the time of entering the Blessed One's village, went out from the city, surrounded by a troop of servant girls. On the road in between, the general's attendants said, "Dear, do not go this way." The stories of those of great merit are pleasing, and it is not possible to reject the words of those who speak again and again. She said, "Why do you not allow [me] to go to [my] paternal uncles, maternal uncles, [and] paternal grandfathers?" The general had it established [that] -- "Do not give anything edible or enjoyable to anyone else" -- [so he] said, "Dear." "But what edible or enjoyable thing do you see in my hand?" "We see a flower garland," they said.

. "Does your general not even allow [you] to make an offering of a flower garland?" "He allows it, dear." "Then, move aside, move aside," she said, and approaching the Blessed One, she had the flower garland accepted by the Blessed One. The Blessed One, gazing at one of the general's attendants, had the flower garland accepted. She, venerating the Blessed One, [made] a wish -- "Blessed One, may I never have a life of suffering when there is rebirth in existence or non-existence. Like this *sumana* flower garland, may I always be dear in the place of repeated rebirths, and may I be named *sumanā*." -- and having made [this] wish, having been told by the Teacher, "May you be happy," having venerated [him], having circumambulated [him] to the right, she departed.

The Blessed One, going to the general's house, sat down on the prepared seat. The general, taking rice gruel, approached. The Teacher covered [his] bowl. "[The] Saṃgha of monks [is] seated, venerable sir," [he said]. "Is there not even one alms-portion obtained in between?" He removed the garland and saw an alms-portion. The lesser attendant said, "Master, the woman deceived [me] by saying 'garland.'" The rice porridge is sufficient for all the monks, having made the Blessed One the first [to partake]. The general also gave his gift-worthy-thing. The Teacher, having done the meal-duty, having spoken a blessing, departed. The general asked, "What [is] the name [of] that [woman] who gave the alms-portion?" "[She is] the treasurer's daughter, master." "She is a wise woman. For a man with such a [woman] living in [his] house, heavenly wealth is not difficult to obtain," he said, and having brought her, he established [her] in the place of the chief [wife].

On another day, the townspeople gave gifts. On another day, the king also began to give gifts on alternate days. The king, also, having stationed roaming men, gave more than the gift given by the townspeople. The townspeople, also, having done likewise, [gave] more than the gift given by the king. In the royal palace, dancing girls said to the young novices, "Take [this]. [It has] not been wiped on the clothes and so forth of householders, [but] has been made with hands washed of the phlegm, snot, and so forth of foolish children.

, It is clean and excellent," they said. On another day, the townspeople also, while giving, said, "Take [this]. [It has] not been drawn together with rice, milk, curds, ghee, and so forth in towns, villages, [and] market towns, [and it has] not been made with the legs, heads, backs, and so forth of others having been broken [to acquire it, but] it has been made purely with ghee, milk, and so forth." Thus, when seven years, seven months, [and] seven days had passed, then this thought arose in the Blessed One's mind.Thus it was said – “Having awakened, after passing seven years, seven months, and seven days, [he] arose."

mula_pali: 86. ‘‘Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā mahābhikkhusaṅgho paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘mahā kho etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ, yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhū anujāneyyaṃ – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave , dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Api ca channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyā’’’ti.
mula_english:
86. Now at that time, in the royal capital of Bandhumatī, there was dwelling a great assembly of monks, numbering six million eight hundred thousand.

Then, monks, it occurred as a thought in the mind of the Blessed Vipassī, the worthy, the fully enlightened one, while he was in seclusion and withdrawn: "Indeed, there is now a great assembly of monks dwelling in the royal capital of Bandhumatī, numbering six million eight hundred thousand. What if I were to give permission to the monks: ‘Wander forth, monks, on tour (cārikaṃ), for the good of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare and happiness of gods (deva) and humans (manussa). Let not two go in the same direction. Teach, monks, the Dharma (dhammaṃ) that is good in the beginning (ādikalyāṇaṃ), good in the middle (majjhekalyāṇaṃ), and good in the end (pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ), with its meaning (sātthaṃ) and with its expression (sabyañjanaṃ), utterly complete (kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ) and perfectly pure (parisuddhaṃ), the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) make known (pakāsetha).

There are beings (sattā) with little dust in their eyes (apparajakkhajātikā), who are falling away through not hearing the Dharma (dhammassa). They will be those who will understand (aññātāro) the Dharma (dhammassa).

Moreover, at the end of six years precisely, the royal capital of Bandhumatī should be approached for the recitation of the Pāṭimokkha (pātimokkhuddesāyā).'"

mula_pali: 87. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro mahābrahmā vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya. Evameva brahmaloke antarahito vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa purato pāturahosi. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Mahā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ, anujānātu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhū – ‘‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’’ti aññātāro (ssabbattha). Api ca, bhante, mayaṃ tathā karissāma yathā bhikkhū channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ upasaṅkamissanti pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Idamavoca, bhikkhave, so mahābrahmā, idaṃ vatvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tattheva antaradhāyi.
mula_english:
87. Then, O monks, a certain Great Brahma, having divined the Lord Buddha Vipassi’s thought, as swiftly as a strong man might stretch his flexed arm, or flex it again.

Just so, having vanished from the Brahma world, he appeared before the Lord Buddha Vipassi, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.

Then that Great Brahma, O monks, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and saluting the Lord Vipassi, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, with joined palms, said this: "Just so, O Lord, just so, O Well-Farer!"

"Great indeed, O venerable one, is the community of monks now dwelling in the capital city of Bandhumati, numbering one hundred and sixty-eight thousand monks. May the Blessed One grant permission to the monks: 'Wander forth, O monks, on a journey for the good of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Let not two go in the same direction. Teach, O monks, the *dharma* that is good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇaṃ*), good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇaṃ*), and good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ*), with the meaning and with the letter, perfectly complete, perfectly pure, proclaim the spiritual life (*brahmacariyaṃ*).

There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are falling away because they do not hear the *dharma*. There will be those who will understand the *dharma*.'"

"And we too, O venerable one, will act in such a way that the monks, at the end of six years, will come together to the royal capital of Bandhumati for the recitation of the *pātimokkha*."

Having spoken thus, O monks, that Great Brahma, having said this, and having paid homage to the Lord Vipassi, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, and keeping him on his right, vanished there and then.
commentary_pali: 87.Aññataromahābrahmāti dhammadesanaṃ āyācitabrahmāva.
commentary_english: 87. A certain Mahābrahmā means Brahmā who requested the teaching of the Dharma.

mula_pali:
88. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘idha mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – mahā kho etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ . Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhū anujāneyyaṃ – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Api ca, channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyāti.

‘‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro mahābrahmā mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva brahmaloke antarahito mama purato pāturahosi. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yenāhaṃ tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Mahā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ. Anujānātu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhū – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ…pe… santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā , assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’ti. Api ca, bhante, mayaṃ tathā karissāma, yathā bhikkhū channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ upasaṅkamissanti pātimokkhuddesāyā’’ti. Idamavoca, bhikkhave, so mahābrahmā, idaṃ vatvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tattheva antaradhāyi’.

‘‘‘Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, caratha cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Api ca, bhikkhave, channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yebhuyyena ekāheneva janapadacārikaṃ pakkamiṃsu.
mula_english:
88. Then, monks, the Lord Vipassī, the *arhat*, the perfectly awakened one, arose from seclusion in the evening and addressed the monks: ‘Here, monks, when I was alone and secluded, such a thought arose in my mind: “This great *bhikkhu-saṃgha* dwells in the capital city of Bandhumatī, [numbering] sixty-eight hundred thousand *bhikkhus*.

Suppose I were to permit the *bhikkhus*: ‘Wander, monks, on tour for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans; let not two go in the same direction; teach, monks, the Dharma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and with expression, wholly complete, perfectly pure *brahmacariya* (holy life).

There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are falling away because they do not hear the Dharma. There will be those who will understand.

And again, monks, at the end of six years, the capital city of Bandhumatī should be approached for the recitation of the *pātimokkha*.

Then, monks, a certain great Brahmā, knowing with his mind the reflection in my mind, just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, even so, vanished in the Brahmā-world and appeared before me.

Then that great Brahmā, monks, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and extending his joined palms towards me, said this to me: "Even so it is, Blessed One, even so it is, Well-Farer.

Great indeed, venerable sir, is the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* now dwelling in the capital city of Bandhumatī, [numbering] sixty-eight hundred thousand *bhikkhus*.

May the Blessed One permit the *bhikkhus*: ‘Wander, monks, on tour for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit and happiness of gods and humans; let not two go in the same direction; teach, monks, the Dharma…pe… There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are falling away because they do not hear the Dharma. There will be those who will understand."

And again, venerable sirs, we will do likewise, just as the *bhikkhus* at the end of six years will approach the capital city of Bandhumatī for the recitation of the *pātimokkha*.’

This is what the great Brahmā said, monks. Having said this, he paid homage to me, circumambulated me to the right, and vanished right there.

‘I allow you, monks, to wander abroad for the good of the many, for the welfare and happiness of devas and humans. Do not go two together, monks, but teach the Dhamma that is lovely in its beginning, lovely in its middle, and lovely in its ending, both in the letter and in the spirit, and display the holy life fully complete and perfect.

There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are falling away because they do not hear the Dhamma. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.”

But at the end of six years precisely you are to come together to the royal capital of Bandhumati to recite the disciplinary code.’

And the majority of those monks left that very day to wander about the country.

mula_pali: 89. ‘‘Tena kho pana samayena jambudīpe caturāsīti āvāsasahassāni honti. Ekamhi hi vasse nikkhante devatā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘nikkhantaṃ kho, mārisā, ekaṃ vassaṃ; pañca dāni vassāni sesāni ; pañcannaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Dvīsu vassesu nikkhantesu… tīsu vassesu nikkhantesu… catūsu vassesu nikkhantesu… pañcasu vassesu nikkhantesu devatā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘nikkhantāni kho , mārisā, pañcavassāni; ekaṃ dāni vassaṃ sesaṃ; ekassa vassassa accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Chasu vassesu nikkhantesu devatā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘nikkhantāni kho, mārisā, chabbassāni, samayo dāni bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ upasaṅkamituṃ pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Atha kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū appekacce sakena iddhānubhāvena appekacce devatānaṃ iddhānubhāvena ekāheneva bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ upasaṅkamiṃsu pātimokkhuddesāyāti pātimokkhuddesāya (?).
mula_english:
‘And at that time there were eighty-four thousand religious residences in Jambudīpa.

After one year had passed, the deities announced: “Friends, one year has passed; now five years remain; at the end of five years you must go to the royal capital of Bandhumatī to recite the Pātimokkha.”

After two years had passed… after three years had passed… after four years had passed… after five years had passed, the deities announced: “Friends, five years have passed; now one year remains; at the end of one year you must go to the royal capital of Bandhumatī to recite the Pātimokkha.”

After six years had passed, the deities announced: “Friends, six years have passed, now is the time to go to the royal capital of Bandhumatī to recite the Pātimokkha!”

Then, monks, some of those monks, by their own psychic power, and some by the psychic power of the deities, came to the royal capital of Bandhumatī in just one day to recite the Pātimokkha.
commentary_pali: 89.Caturāsīti āvāsasahassānīti caturāsīti vihārasahassāni. Te sabbepi dvādasasahassabhikkhugaṇhanakā mahāvihārā abhayagiricetiyapabbatacittalapabbatamahāvihārasadisāva ahesuṃ.
commentary_english:
89. "Eighty-four thousand residences," that is, eighty-four thousand *vihāras*.

All those great *vihāras*, each filled with twelve thousand monks, were similar to the *Abhayagiri-cetiya-pabbata* and the *Cittalapabbata-mahāvihāra*.

mula_pali:
90. ‘‘Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhikkhusaṅghe evaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisati –

‘Khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā,

Nibbānaṃ paramaṃ vadanti buddhā;

Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī,

Na samaṇo samaṇo (sī. syā. pī.) hoti paraṃ viheṭhayanto.

samaṇo (sī. syā. pī.)

‘Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā;

Sacittapariyodapanaṃ, etaṃ buddhānasāsanaṃ.

‘Anūpavādo anūpaghāto anupavādo anupaghāto (pī. ka.), pātimokkhe ca saṃvaro;

anupavādo anupaghāto (pī. ka.)

Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṃ, pantañca sayanāsanaṃ;

Adhicitte ca āyogo, etaṃ buddhānasāsana’nti.

Devatārocanaṃ
mula_english:
90. It is said, "There, good monks, the Blessed One, the worthy *arhan*, the perfectly awakened Buddha, recites the *Pātimokkha* to the *bhikṣu-saṅgha* as follows:

'Forbearance is the highest austerity, *titikkhā*.

The Buddhas say *nirvāṇa* is supreme;

He is not an ascetic who harms another,

Nor is he a *śramaṇa* who injures another.

Abstaining from all evil, undertaking what is wholesome,

Purifying one's own mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

Not speaking ill, not doing harm, restraint according to the *Prātimokṣa*,

Knowing moderation in food, secluded lodging,

Devotion to higher thought: this is the teaching of the Buddhas."

Invocation of the Deities
commentary_pali:
90.Khantī paramaṃ tapoti adhivāsanakhanti nāma paramaṃ tapo. Titikkhāti khantiyā eva vevacanaṃ. Titikkhā saṅkhātā adhivāsanakhanti uttamaṃ tapoti attho. Nibbānaṃ paramanti sabbākārena pana nibbānaṃ paramanti vadanti buddhā. Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātīti yo adhivāsanakhantivirahitattā paraṃ upaghāteti bādheti hiṃsati, so pabbajito nāma na hoti. Catutthapādo pana tasseva vevacanaṃ. ‘‘Na hi pabbajito’’ti etassa hi na samaṇo hotīti vevacanaṃ. Parūpaghātīti etassa paraṃ viheṭhayantoti vevacanaṃ. Atha vā parūpaghātīti sīlūpaghātī. Sīlañhi uttamaṭṭhena paranti vuccati. Yo ca samaṇo paraṃ yaṃ kañci sattaṃ viheṭhayanto parūpaghātī hoti, attano sīlaṃ vināsako, so pabbajito nāma na hotīti attho. Athavā yo adhivāsanakhantiyā abhāvato parūpaghātī hoti, paraṃ antamaso ḍaṃsamakasampi sañcicca jīvitā voropeti, so na hi pabbajito. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Malassa apabbājitattā. ‘‘Pabbājayamattano malaṃ, tasmā pabbajitoti vuccatī’’ti (dha. pa. 388) idañhi pabbajitalakkhaṇaṃ. Yopi na heva kho upaghāteti, na māreti, api ca daṇḍādīhi viheṭheti, so paraṃ viheṭhayanto samaṇo na hoti. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Vihesāya asamitattā. ‘‘Samitattā hi pāpānaṃ , samaṇoti pavuccatī’’ti (dha. pa. 265) idañhi samaṇalakkhaṇaṃ.

Dutiyagāthāya sabbapāpassāti sabbākusalassa. Akaraṇanti anuppādanaṃ. Kusalassāti catubhūmikakusalassa. Upasampadāti paṭilābho. Sacittapariyodapananti attano cittajotanaṃ, taṃ pana arahattena hoti. Iti sīlasaṃvarena sabbapāpaṃ pahāya samathavipassanāhi kusalaṃ sampādetvā arahattaphalena cittaṃ pariyodāpetabbanti etaṃ buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ ovādo anusiṭṭhī ti.

sabbapāpassā Akaraṇa Kusalassā Upasampadā Sacittapariyodapana

Tatiyagāthāya anūpavādoti vācāya kassaci anupavadanaṃ. Anūpaghātoti kāyena upaghātassa akaraṇaṃ. Pātimokkheti yaṃ taṃ paatimokkhaṃ, atipamokkhaṃ, uttamasīlaṃ, pāti vā agativisesehi mokkheti duggatibhayehi, yo vā naṃ pāti, taṃ mokkhetīti ‘‘pātimokkha’’nti vuccati. Tasmiṃ pātimokkhe ca saṃvaro. Mattaññutāti paṭiggahaṇaparibhogavasena pamāṇaññutā. Pantañca sayanāsananti sayanāsanañca saṅghaṭṭanavirahitanti attho. Tattha dvīhiyeva paccayehi catupaccayasantoso dīpito hotīti veditabbo. Etaṃ buddhāna sāsananti etaṃ parassa anupavadanaṃ anupaghātanaṃ pātimokkhasaṃvaro paṭiggahaṇaparibhogesu mattaññutā aṭṭhasamāpattivasibhāvāya vivittasenāsanasevanañca buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ ovādo anusiṭṭhīti. Imā pana sabbabuddhānaṃ pātimokkhuddesagāthā hontīti veditabbā.

anūpavādo Anūpaghāto Pātimokkhe Mattaññutā Pantañca sayanāsana Etaṃ buddhāna sāsana

Devatārocanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
