The mind, imbued with wisdom, becomes completely freed from the corruptions, that is, from the corruption of sensuality (kāmāsava), of becoming (bhavāsava), and of ignorance (avijjāsava).”

mula_pali:
160. Atha kho bhagavā nātike yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena vesālī tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati ambapālivane. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –

‘‘Sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya sampajāno, ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti.

‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti. Sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya sampajāno, ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī’’ti.

Ambapālīgaṇikā
mula_english:
160. Then the Blessed One, having stayed near Nādikā as long as he pleased, said to Venerable Ānanda, “Come, Ānanda, we will head for Vesālī.”

“So be it, Lord,” replied Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *saṅgha* of monks, went to Vesālī.

There he stayed near Vesālī in Ambapālī’s grove.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks:

“Monks, a monk should dwell mindful and clearly aware; this is our instruction to you.

And how, monks, is a monk mindful? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world.

He remains focused on feelings… mind… mental qualities in & of themselves—ardent, alert, & mindful—subduing greed & distress with reference to the world.

This is how a monk is mindful.

“And how, monks, is a monk clearly aware? Here, monks, when going forward & returning, he makes himself alert; when looking toward & looking away… when bending & extending his limbs… when carrying his outer cloak, his upper robe, & his bowl… when eating, drinking, chewing, & savoring… when urinating & defecating… when walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, talking, & remaining silent, he makes himself alert.

This is how a monk is alert.

A monk should be mindful and clearly aware, this is our charge to you!’

Ambapālī the courtesan

mula_pali:
161. Assosi kho ambapālī gaṇikā – ‘‘bhagavā kira vesāliṃ anuppatto vesāliyaṃ viharati mayhaṃ ambavane’’ti. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyāsi. Yena sako ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Assosuṃ kho vesālikā licchavī – ‘‘bhagavā kira vesāliṃ anuppatto vesāliyaṃ viharati ambapālivane’’ti. Atha kho te licchavī bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyiṃsu. Tatra ekacce licchavī nīlā honti nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī pītā honti pītavaṇṇā pītavatthā pītālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī lohitā honti lohitavaṇṇā lohitavatthā lohitālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī odātā honti odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā daharānaṃ daharānaṃ licchavīnaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ yugena yugaṃ paṭivaṭṭesi parivattesi (vi. mahāvagga). Atha kho te licchavī ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘kiṃ, je ambapāli , daharānaṃ daharānaṃ licchavīnaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ yugena yugaṃ paṭivaṭṭesī’’ti? ‘‘Tathā hi pana me, ayyaputtā, bhagavā nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. ‘‘Dehi, je ambapāli, etaṃ ekaṃ (ka.) bhattaṃ satasahassenā’’ti. ‘‘Sacepi me, ayyaputtā, vesāliṃ sāhāraṃ dassatha dajjeyyātha (vi. mahāvagga), evamahaṃ taṃ evampi mahantaṃ (syā.), evaṃ mahantaṃ (sī. pī.) bhattaṃ na dassāmī’’ti neva dajjāhaṃ taṃ bhattanti (vi. mahāvagga). Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – ‘‘jitamha jitamhā (bahūsu) vata bho ambakāya, jitamha vata bho ambakāyā’’ti ‘‘jitamhā vata bho ambapālikāya vañcitamhā vata bho ambapālikāyā’’ti (syā.).

parivattesi (vi. mahāvagga) ekaṃ (ka.) dajjeyyātha (vi. mahāvagga) evampi mahantaṃ (syā.), evaṃ mahantaṃ (sī. pī.) neva dajjāhaṃ taṃ bhattanti (vi. mahāvagga) jitamhā (bahūsu) ‘‘jitamhā vata bho ambapālikāya vañcitamhā vata bho ambapālikāyā’’ti (syā.)

Atha kho te licchavī yena ambapālivanaṃ tena pāyiṃsu. Addasā kho bhagavā te licchavī dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘yesaṃ yehi (vi. mahāvagga), bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ devā tāvatiṃsā adiṭṭhapubbā, oloketha, bhikkhave, licchaviparisaṃ; apaloketha, bhikkhave , licchaviparisaṃ; upasaṃharatha, bhikkhave, licchaviparisaṃ – tāvatiṃsasadisa’’nti. Atha kho te licchavī yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te licchavī bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho te licchavī bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā te licchavī etadavoca – ‘‘adhivutthaṃ adhivāsitaṃ (syā.) kho me, licchavī, svātanāya ambapāliyā gaṇikāya bhatta’’nti. Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – ‘‘jitamha vata bho ambakāya, jitamha vata bho ambakāyā’’ti. Atha kho te licchavī bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

yehi (vi. mahāvagga) adhivāsitaṃ (syā.)
mula_english:
Now Ambapālī the courtesan heard that the Blessed One had arrived at Vesālī and was staying in her mango grove.

Then Ambapālī the courtesan had excellent carriages prepared, mounted a fine carriage, and set out from Vesālī in those excellent carriages. She proceeded towards her own park. Going by carriage as far as the ground was suitable for carriages, she alighted from the carriage and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

The Blessed One instructed, inspired, roused, and delighted Ambapālī the courtesan, who was sitting to one side, with a discourse on the Dhamma. Then Ambapālī the courtesan, instructed, inspired, roused, and delighted by the Blessed One with a discourse on the Dhamma, said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept my invitation for tomorrow's meal, together with the Saṅgha of monks."

The Blessed One accepted in silence. Then Ambapālī the courtesan, knowing of the Blessed One's acceptance, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.

The Licchavis of Vesālī heard, "The Blessed One has arrived at Vesālī and is staying in Ambapālī's grove." Then those Licchavis had excellent carriages prepared, mounted a fine carriage, and set out from Vesālī in those excellent carriages.

Some of those Licchavis were blue, with blue complexions, blue clothes, and blue ornaments; some were yellow, with yellow complexions, yellow clothes, and yellow ornaments; some were red, with red complexions, red clothes, and red ornaments; some were white, with white complexions, white clothes, and white ornaments.

Then Ambapālī the courtesan drove axle to axle, wheel to wheel, and yoke to yoke against the young Licchavis. Then those Licchavis said to Ambapālī the courtesan: "Why, Ambapālī, do you drive axle to axle, wheel to wheel, and yoke to yoke against the young Licchavis?" "Because, noble sirs, the Blessed One has been invited by me for tomorrow's meal, together with the Saṅgha of monks."

"Give us, Ambapālī, that meal for a hundred thousand!"

"Even if you were to give me Vesālī with its surrounding territory, I would not give up that meal."

Then those Licchavis snapped their fingers: "We have been defeated by the mango-woman! We have been defeated by the mango-woman!"
Then the Licchavīs proceeded to Ambapālī's grove.

The Blessed One saw the Licchavīs coming from afar.

Seeing them, he addressed the monks: "Monks, if the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven have never been seen by the monks, behold this assembly of Licchavīs! Observe this Licchavī assembly! Consider this Licchavī assembly - they are like the Tāvatiṃsa gods."

Then the Licchavīs, as far as the ground was suitable for vehicles, traveled by carriage; then, alighting from their carriages, they approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, they respectfully greeted the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

As the Licchavīs were sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, uplifted, and gladdened them with a discourse on the Dhamma (dharma).

Then the Licchavīs, having been instructed, encouraged, uplifted, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a discourse on the Dhamma (dharma), said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One, O venerable sir, accept our meal for tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha (community) of monks."

Then the Blessed One said this to the Licchavīs: "I have already accepted a meal for tomorrow from Ambapālī, the courtesan."

Then the Licchavīs snapped their fingers, saying: "We have been outdone by Ambakā! We have been outdone by Ambakā!"

Then the Licchavīs, delighting in and approving of the Blessed One's words, rose from their seats, respectfully greeted the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.
commentary_pali:
161.Vesāliyaṃviharatīti ettha tena kho pana samayena vesālī iddhā ceva hoti phītācātiādinā khandhake vuttanayena vesāliyā sampannabhāvo veditabbo. Ambapālivaneti ambapāliyā gaṇikāya uyyānabhūte ambavane. Sato bhikkhaveti bhagavā ambapālidassane satipaccupaṭṭhānatthaṃ visesato idha satipaṭṭhānadesanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha saratīti sato. Sampajānātīti sampajāno. Satiyā ca sampajaññena ca samannāgato hutvā vihareyyāti attho. Kāye kāyānupassītiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāsatipaṭṭhāne vakkhāma.

Nīlāti idaṃ sabbasaṅgāhakaṃ. Nīlavaṇṇātiādi tasseva vibhāgadassanaṃ. Tattha na tesaṃ pakativaṇṇo nīlo, nīlavilepanavilittattā panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Nīlavatthāti paṭadukūlakoseyyādīnipi tesaṃ nīlāneva honti. Nīlālaṅkārāti nīlamaṇīhi nīlapupphehi alaṅkatā, rathāpi tesaṃ nīlamaṇikhacitā nīlavatthaparikkhittā nīladdhajā nīlavammikehi nīlābharaṇehi nīlaassehi yuttā, patodalaṭṭhiyopi nīlā yevāti. Iminā nayena sabbapadesu attho veditabbo. Parivaṭṭesīti pahari. Kiṃ je ambapālīti jeti ālapanavacanaṃ, bhoti ambapāli, kiṃ kāraṇāti vuttaṃ hoti. ‘‘Kiñcā’’tipi pāṭho, ayamevettha attho. Sāhāranti sajanapadaṃ. Aṅguliṃ phoṭesunti aṅguliṃ cālesuṃ. Ambakāyāti itthikāya.

Nīlā Nīlavaṇṇā Nīlavatthā Nīlālaṅkārā Parivaṭṭesī Kiṃ je ambapālī Sāhāra Aṅguliṃ phoṭesu Ambakāyā

Yesanti karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, yehi adiṭṭhāti vuttaṃ hoti. Olokethāti passatha. Avalokethāti punappunaṃ passatha. Upasaṃharathāti upanetha. Imaṃ licchaviparisaṃ tumhākaṃ cittena tāvatiṃsasadisaṃ upasaṃharatha upanetha allīyāpetha. Yatheva tāvatiṃsā abhirūpā pāsādikā nīlādinānāvaṇṇā, evamime licchavirājānopīti tāvatiṃsehi samake katvā passathāti attho.

Yesa Olokethā Avalokethā Upasaṃharathā

Kasmā pana bhagavā anekasatehi suttehi cakkhādīnaṃ rūpādīsu nimittaggāhaṃ paṭisedhetvā idha mahantena ussāhena nimittaggāhe uyyojetīti? Hitakāmatāya. Tatra kira ekacce bhikkhū osannavīriyā, tesaṃ sampattiyā palobhento – ‘‘appamādena samaṇadhammaṃ karontānaṃ evarūpā issariyasampatti sulabhā’’ti samaṇadhamme ussāhajananatthaṃ āha. Aniccalakkhaṇavibhāvanatthañcāpi evamāha. Nacirasseva hi sabbepime ajātasattussa vasena vināsaṃ pāpuṇissanti. Atha nesaṃ rajjasirisampattiṃ disvā ṭhitabhikkhū – ‘‘tathārūpāyapi nāma sirisampattiyā vināso paññāyissatī’’ti aniccalakkhaṇaṃ bhāvetvā saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇissantīti aniccalakkhaṇavibhāvanatthaṃ āha.

Adhivāsetūti ambapāliyā nimantitabhāvaṃ ñatvāpi kasmā nimantentīti? Asaddahanatāya ceva vattasīsena ca. Sā hi dhuttā itthī animantetvāpi nimantemīti vadeyyāti tesaṃ cittaṃ ahosi, dhammaṃ sutvā gamanakāle ca nimantetvā gamanaṃ nāma manussānaṃ vattameva.

Adhivāsetū

Veḷuvagāmavassūpagamanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
161. At Vesālī.

“Viharatīti”: Here, in that time, Vesālī was prosperous, as it was said in the Khandhaka, “Vesālī was rich, prosperous, and well-populated." One should know the complete state of Vesālī.

"Ambapālivane": In the mango grove that was the pleasure garden of the courtesan Āmbapālī.

"Sato bhikkhave": The Blessed One, regarding the visit to Āmbapālī, began the discourse on mindfulness, specifically for the purpose of establishing mindfulness.

"Tattha saratīti sato": Because one remembers there, [one is] mindful ( *smṛti* ).

"Sampajānātīti sampajāno": Because one understands completely, [one is] fully aware ( *saṃprajāna* ).

The meaning is that one should live being endowed with mindfulness and full awareness.

"Kāye kāyānupassītiādīsu": Whatever is to be said regarding contemplating the body in the body etc., I will say in the Great Discourse on the Foundations of Mindfulness (Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sūtra).

"Nīlā": This is all-inclusive.

"Nīlavaṇṇā": This etc. is a showing of its distinction.

There, their natural color is not blue, but this is said because of being anointed with blue unguents and ointments.

"Nīlavatthā": Their cloths of *paṭa*, *dukūla*, and *koseyya* etc. are only blue.

"Nīlālaṅkārā": [They are] adorned with blue gems and blue flowers; their chariots are inlaid with blue gems, covered with blue cloths, have blue flags, [and] are equipped with blue armor, blue ornaments, [and] blue horses; even their goad sticks are blue.

In this way, the meaning should be understood in all words.

"Parivaṭṭesīti": Struck.

"Kiṃ je ambapālī": The word "je" is a word of address, "Oh, Āmbapālī, what is the reason?" is what was said.

“Kiñcā’tipi” is another reading; this is its meaning here.

"Sāhāra": With territory.

"Aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ": Snapped their fingers.

"Ambakāyā": To a woman.

“Yesa”: [This] is a word expressing ownership in the sense of instrumentality: “by whom it is unseen” is what is said.

“Olokethā”: Look!

“Avolokethā”: Look again and again!

“Upasaṃharathā”: Bring near!

Bring near and introduce this Licchavi assembly to your mind, like the Tāvatiṃsa gods.

Just as the Tāvatiṃsa are beautiful, pleasing, [and of] various colors beginning with blue, so too are these Licchavi kings: the meaning is "having made [them] equal to the Tāvatiṃsa gods, look!"

Why then does the Blessed One, having forbidden the grasping of signs in forms etc. by the eye etc. in hundreds of discourses, here encourage the grasping of signs with great effort? Because of wishing their benefit.

There, it is said that some monks are of weakened energy, [so] alluring [them] with the attainment of prosperity – "Such dominion and prosperity are easily obtained by those who practice the ascetic life with diligence" – thus he spoke for the purpose of generating enthusiasm for the ascetic life.

And also for the purpose of making manifest the characteristic of impermanence, he spoke thus:

"In a short time, all of these will attain destruction under the control of Ajātasattu."

Then, having seen their prosperity of kingdom and glory, the monks standing [there thought] – "Even for such glory and prosperity there will be destruction!" – having cultivated the characteristic of impermanence together with the discriminations, they will attain arhatship: thus, he spoke for the purpose of making manifest the characteristic of impermanence.
"adhivāsetū" - Knowing that Ambapālī had been invited, why did she invite [him] again? Because of distrust and also because of her seductive nature.

She is a deceitful woman, and they thought, "Even without inviting, she might say 'I invite'," so when it was time to leave after hearing the Dharma, inviting and going is simply the custom of people.

"adhivāsetū" - Description of entering the rainy season retreat in Veḷuvagāma.

mula_pali:
162. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā tassā rattiyā accayena sake ārāme paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘‘kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena ambapāliyā gaṇikāya nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘imāhaṃ, bhante, ārāmaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dammī’’ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā ārāmaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharanto ambapālivane etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.

Veḷuvagāmavassūpagamanaṃ
mula_english:
162. Then, after the night had passed, Ambapālī the courtesan, having had exquisite staple and non-staple food prepared in her own park, announced the time to the Blessed One: “It’s time, reverend Sir, the meal is ready.”

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the forenoon, and taking his bowl and robe, went together with the *saṅgha* of monks to Ambapālī the courtesan’s dwelling; on arrival, he sat down on the seat laid out.

Then Ambapālī the courtesan, with her own hands, served and satisfied the *saṅgha* of monks, with the Buddha at its head, with exquisite staple and non-staple food.

Then, when the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Ambapālī the courtesan, taking a low seat, sat to one side.

As she was sitting to one side, Ambapālī the courtesan spoke to the Blessed One, saying: “This park, O Lord, I offer to the *saṅgha* of monks headed by the Buddha.”

The Blessed One accepted the park (*ārāmaṃ*).

Then the Blessed One, having instructed, inspired, uplifted, and delighted Ambapālī the courtesan with a discourse on the *dharma*, rose from his seat and departed.

Furthermore, while the Blessed One was staying at Vesālī in Ambapālī’s grove, he often gave this *dharma* talk to the monks: “Such is virtue (*śīlaṃ*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*prajñā*).

Concentration (*samādhi*) nurtured with virtue (*śīla*) is of great fruit, great reward.

Discernment (*prajñā*) nurtured with concentration (*samādhi*) is of great fruit, great reward.

The mind nurtured with discernment (*prajñā*) is rightly released from the taints (*āsavā*), that is, the taint of sensuality (*kāmāsavā*), the taint of becoming (*bhavāsavā*), the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsavā*).”

Veḷuvagāmavassūpagamanaṃ (The rains-residence at Veḷuvagāma).

mula_pali: 163. Atha kho bhagavā ambapālivane yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena veḷuvagāmako beḷuvagāmako (sī. pī.) tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena veḷuvagāmako tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā veḷuvagāmake viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, samantā vesāliṃ yathāmittaṃ yathāsandiṭṭhaṃ yathāsambhattaṃ vassaṃ upetha upagacchatha (syā.). Ahaṃ pana idheva veḷuvagāmake vassaṃ upagacchāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā samantā vesāliṃ yathāmittaṃ yathāsandiṭṭhaṃ yathāsambhattaṃ vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Bhagavā pana tattheva veḷuvagāmake vassaṃ upagacchi.
mula_english:
163. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Ambapāli’s grove as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying, "Come, Ānanda, we will go to Veḷuva Village."

"So be it, O Lord," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks ( *bhikkhusaṅgha*), went to Veḷuva Village.

There the Blessed One stayed near Veḷuva Village.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Go now, monks (*bhikkhave*), enter the Rainy season retreat around Vesālī with your friends, acquaintances, & eating companions.

As for me, I shall enter the Rainy season retreat right here near Veḷuva Village."

"So be it, O Lord," those monks replied to the Blessed One, and they entered the Rainy season retreat around Vesālī with their friends, acquaintances, & eating companions.

But the Blessed One spent the Rainy season retreat right there near Veḷuva Village.
commentary_pali: 163.Veḷuvagāmakoti vesāliyā samīpe veḷuvagāmo. Yathāmittantiādīsu mittā mittāva. Sandiṭṭhāti tattha tattha saṅgamma diṭṭhamattā nātidaḷhamittā. Sambhattāti suṭṭhu bhattā sinehavanto daḷhamittā. Yesaṃ yesaṃ yattha yattha evarūpā bhikkhū atthi, te te tattha tattha vassaṃ upethāti attho. Kasmā evamāha? Tesaṃ phāsuvihāratthāya. Tesañhi veḷuvagāmake senāsanaṃ nappahoti, bhikkhāpi mandā. Samantā vesāliyā pana bahūni senāsanāni, bhikkhāpi sulabhā, tasmā evamāha. Atha kasmā – ‘‘yathāsukhaṃ gacchathā’’ti na vissajjesi? Tesaṃ anukampāya. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ahaṃ dasamāsamattaṃ ṭhatvā parinibbāyissāmi, sace ime dūraṃ gacchissanti, mama parinibbānakāle daṭṭhuṃ na sakkhissanti. Atha nesaṃ – ‘‘satthā parinibbāyanto amhākaṃ satimattampi na adāsi, sace jāneyyāma, evaṃ na dūre vaseyyāmā’’ti vippaṭisāro bhaveyya. Vesāliyā samantā pana vasantā māsassa aṭṭha vāre āgantvā dhammaṃ suṇissanti, sugatovādaṃ labhissantī’’ti na vissajjesi.
commentary_english:
163. “*Veḷuvagāmako*” means Veḷuvagāma near Vesālī.

"*Yathāmitta*," etc., [means] friends are just friends.

"*Sandiṭṭhā*" means having met here and there, [they are] merely seen [and] not very firm friends.

"*Sambhattā*" means well-nourished, affectionate, [and] firm friends.

Wherever and to whomever such *bhikkhus* exist, the meaning is that they should spend the rainy season there.

Why did he say that? For their comfortable dwelling.

Because in Veḷuvagāma, lodging is not sufficient, and alms are meager.

But all around Vesālī, there are many lodgings, and alms are easily obtained; therefore, he said that.

Then why did he not dismiss [them] saying, "Go as you please ( *yathāsukhaṃ gacchatha*)?" Out of compassion for them.

Thus, it occurred to him: "I will remain for about ten months and attain *parinirvāṇa*. If these [monks] go far away, they will not be able to see [me] at the time of my *parinirvāṇa*.

Then, they might [think]: “The teacher, while passing into *parinirvāṇa*, did not even give us a word of mindfulness. If we had known, we would not have stayed so far away," and remorse might arise.

Those dwelling all around Vesālī, having come eight times a month, will hear the *dharma*, [and] will obtain the Sugata’s teaching;” therefore, he did not dismiss [them].

mula_pali: 164. Atha kho bhagavato vassūpagatassa kharo ābādho uppajji, bāḷhā vedanā vattanti māraṇantikā. Tā sudaṃ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāsesi avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ, yvāhaṃ anāmantetvā upaṭṭhāke anapaloketvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parinibbāyeyyaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ ābādhaṃ vīriyena paṭipaṇāmetvā jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ adhiṭṭhāya vihareyya’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ ābādhaṃ vīriyena paṭipaṇāmetvā jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ adhiṭṭhāya vihāsi. Atha kho bhagavato so ābādho paṭipassambhi. Atha kho bhagavā gilānā vuṭṭhito gilānavuṭṭhito (saddanīti) aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā vihārā nikkhamma vihārapacchāyāyaṃ paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘diṭṭho me, bhante, bhagavato phāsu; diṭṭhaṃ me, bhante, bhagavato khamanīyaṃ, api ca me, bhante, madhurakajāto viya kāyo. Disāpi me na pakkhāyanti; dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhanti bhagavato gelaññena, api ca me, bhante, ahosi kācideva assāsamattā – ‘na tāva bhagavā parinibbāyissati, na yāva bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāharatī’’’ti.
mula_english:
164. Then, when the Blessed One had entered the rainy season (vassūpagatassa), a severe illness (kharo ābādho) arose in him, with intense (bāḷhā) and deadly (māraṇantikā) pains (vedanā).

The Blessed One (bhagavā), mindful (sato) and fully aware (sampajāno), endured (adhivāsesi) them without being troubled (avihaññamāno).

Then it occurred (etadahosi) to the Blessed One (bhagavato): "It would not be fitting (na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ) if I were to attain final nirvāṇa (parinibbāyeyyaṃ) without addressing (anāmantetvā) my attendants (upaṭṭhāke) and without taking leave (anapaloketvā) of the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ)."

"Why don't I (yaṃnūnāhaṃ), by force of will (vīriyena), overcome (paṭipaṇāmetvā) this illness (imaṃ ābādhaṃ), resolve (adhiṭṭhāya) to maintain the life-force (jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ), and live on (vihareyyaṃ)?"

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), by force of will (vīriyena), overcame (paṭipaṇāmetvā) that illness (taṃ ābādhaṃ), resolved (adhiṭṭhāya) to maintain the life-force (jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ), and lived on (vihāsi).

Then the Blessed One's (bhagavato) illness (so ābādho) subsided (paṭipassambhi).

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), having recovered (vuṭṭhito) from his illness (gilānā), not long (aciravuṭṭhito) after recovering from that sickness (gelaññā), left (nikkhamma) his dwelling (vihārā) and sat down (nisīdi) on a prepared (paññatte) seat (āsane) in the shade (pacchāyāyaṃ) of the building (vihāra).

Then the venerable Ānanda (āyasmā Ānando) approached (upasaṅkami) the Blessed One (bhagavā); having approached (upasaṅkamitvā), he bowed respectfully (abhivādetvā) to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) and sat down (nisīdi) to one side (ekamantaṃ).

Having sat down (nisinno) to one side (ekamantaṃ), the venerable Ānanda (āyasmā Ānando) said (etadavoca) to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): "It is a happy sight for me, venerable sir (diṭṭho me, bhante), to see the Blessed One's (bhagavato) comfort (phāsu); it is a happy sight for me, venerable sir (diṭṭhaṃ me, bhante), to see the Blessed One's (bhagavato) ease (khamanīyaṃ); indeed (api ca me, bhante), my body (kāyo) feels like it is drugged (madhurakajāto viya)."

"I lost my bearings (disāpi me na pakkhāyanti); things (dhammāpi) were unclear to me (na paṭibhanti) because of the Blessed One's (bhagavato) sickness (gelaññena); indeed (api ca me, bhante), there was only a little (kācideva) comfort (assāsamattā) in the thought (iti): 'The Blessed One (bhagavā) will not attain final nirvāṇa (parinibbāyissati) until (na yāva) the Blessed One (bhagavā) has made some pronouncement (udāharati) concerning the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ).'"
commentary_pali:
164.Kharoti pharuso. Ābādhoti visabhāgarogo. Bāḷhāti balavatiyo. Māraṇantikāti maraṇantaṃ maraṇasantikaṃ pāpanasamatthā. Sato sampajāno adhivāsesīti satiṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ katvā ñāṇena paricchinditvā adhivāsesi. Avihaññamānoti vedanānuvattanavasena aparāparaṃ parivattanaṃ akaronto apīḷiyamāno adukkhiyamānova adhivāsesi . Anāmantetvāti ajānāpetvā. Anapaloketvāti na apaloketvā ovādānusāsaniṃ adatvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Vīriyenāti pubbabhāgavīriyena ceva phalasamāpattivīriyena ca. Paṭipaṇāmetvāti vikkhambhetvā. Jīvitasaṅkhāranti ettha jīvitampi jīvitasaṅkhāro. Yena jīvitaṃ saṅkhariyati chijjamānaṃ ghaṭetvā ṭhapiyati, so phalasamāpattidhammopi jīvitasaṅkhāro. So idha adhippeto. Adhiṭṭhāyāti adhiṭṭhahitvā pavattetvā, jīvitaṭṭhapanasamatthaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjeyyanti ayamettha saṅkhepattho.

Kiṃ pana bhagavā ito pubbe phalasamāpattiṃ na samāpajjatīti? Samāpajjati. Sā pana khaṇikasamāpatti. Khaṇikasamāpatti ca antosamāpattiyaṃyeva vedanaṃ vikkhambheti, samāpattito vuṭṭhitamattassa kaṭṭhapātena vā kaṭhalapātena vā chinnasevālo viya udakaṃ puna sarīraṃ vedanā ajjhottharati. Yā pana rūpasattakaṃ arūpasattakañca niggumbaṃ nijjaṭaṃ katvā mahāvipassanāvasena samāpannā samāpatti, sā suṭṭhu vikkhambheti. Yathā nāma purisena pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhetvā hatthehi ca pādehi ca suṭṭhu apabyūḷho sevālo cirena udakaṃ ottharati; evameva tato vuṭṭhitassa cirena vedanā uppajjati. Iti bhagavā taṃ divasaṃ mahābodhipallaṅke abhinavavipassanaṃ paṭṭhapento viya rūpasattakaṃ arūpasattakaṃ niggumbaṃ nijjaṭaṃ katvā cuddasahākārehi sannetvā mahāvipassanāya vedanaṃ vikkhambhetvā – ‘‘dasamāse mā uppajjitthā’’ti samāpattiṃ samāpajji. Samāpattivikkhambhitā vedanā dasamāse na uppajji yeva.

Gilānā vuṭṭhitoti gilāno hutvā puna vuṭṭhito. Madhurakajāto viyāti sañjātagarubhāvo sañjātathaddhabhāvo sūle uttāsitapuriso viya. Na pakkhāyantīti nappakāsanti, nānākārato na upaṭṭhahanti. Dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhantīti satipaṭṭhānādidhammā mayhaṃ pākaṭā na hontīti dīpeti. Tantidhammā pana therassa supaguṇā. Na udāharatīti pacchimaṃ ovādaṃ na deti. Taṃ sandhāya vadati.

Gilānā vuṭṭhito Madhurakajāto viyā Na pakkhāyantī Dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhantī Na udāharatī
commentary_english:
164. *Kharo* means harsh.
*Ābādho* means a disease of a different kind.
*Bāḷhā* means powerful.
*Māraṇantikā* means capable of destroying life, close to death.
*Sato sampajāno adhivāsesī* means having established mindfulness well, having determined with knowledge, he endures.
*Avihaññamāno* means without making repeated changes according to the arising of feelings, without being afflicted, without being made to suffer, he endures.
*Anāmantetvā* means without causing to know.
*Anapaloketvā* means not looking back, it is said that it means not giving instructions or guidance.
*Vīriyenā* means with energy, with the energy of the preliminary stage, and with the energy of the attainment of fruition.
*Paṭipaṇāmetvā* means having checked.
*Jīvitasaṅkhāra* means here, vitality itself is the life-force.
That by which life is fabricated, having joined together what is being destroyed, is established; that *phalasamāpattidhammopi* is the life-force.
That is what is intended here.
*Adhiṭṭhāyā* means having determined, having set forth, may one attain the *phalasamāpatti* capable of establishing life; this is the condensed meaning here.

What, then, does the Blessed One not attain the *phalasamāpatti* before this? He attains it.
But that is a momentary attainment.
And a momentary attainment only checks the feeling within the attainment; like water covering the body again like algae cut off by a piece of wood or a potsherd of one who has just arisen from the attainment.
But that attainment that is attained by means of great insight, having made the aggregate of form and the aggregate of the formless without thickets, without tangles, that checks well.
Just as when a person enters a pond and the algae that has been well cleared away with his hands and feet covers the water after a long time; just so, feeling arises in one who has arisen from that after a long time.
Thus, the Blessed One, as if establishing new insight on that day on the great *bodhipallaṅka*, having made the aggregate of form and the aggregate of the formless without thickets, without tangles, having combined with fourteen aspects, having checked feeling with great insight – "May it not arise in ten months!" – he attained the *samāpatti*.
The feeling checked by *samāpatti* did not arise in ten months.

*Gilānā vuṭṭhito* means having been sick, having arisen again.
*Madhurakajāto viyā* means having a gentle disposition, having a firm disposition, like a man impaled on a stake.
*Na pakkhāyantī* means they do not appear, they do not stand near from various causes.
*Dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhantī* means the *satipaṭṭhānādi-dhammā* are not evident to me, he indicates.
But the *tantidhammā* are well-established for the Elder.
*Na udāharatī* means he does not give the final advice.
Referring to that, he speaks.

*Gilānā vuṭṭhito madhurakajāto viyā na pakkhāyantī dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhantī na udāharatī*

mula_pali:
165. ‘‘Kiṃ panānanda, bhikkhusaṅgho mayi paccāsīsati paccāsiṃsati (sī. syā.)? Desito, ānanda, mayā dhammo anantaraṃ abāhiraṃ karitvā. Natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhi. Yassa nūna, ānanda, evamassa – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā, so nūna, ānanda, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāhareyya. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā. Sakiṃ kiṃ (sī. pī.), ānanda, tathāgato bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāharissati. Ahaṃ kho panānanda, etarahi jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto. Āsītiko me vayo vattati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, jajjarasakaṭaṃ veṭhamissakena veḷumissakena (syā.), veghamissakena (pī.), vedhamissakena, vekhamissakena (ka.) yāpeti, evameva kho, ānanda, veṭhamissakena maññe tathāgatassa kāyo yāpeti. Yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgato sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā ekaccānaṃ vedanānaṃ nirodhā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati, phāsutaro, ānanda, tasmiṃ samaye tathāgatassa kāyo hoti. Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati atāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo . Ye hi keci, ānanda, etarahi vā mama vā accayena attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, tamatagge me te, ānanda, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā’’ti.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro.

Nimittobhāsakathā
mula_english:
165. “Now, Ānanda, does the *bhikkhusaṃgha* expect something from me? I have taught the Dharma, Ānanda, without making (a distinction between) esoteric and exoteric. The Tathāgata has no “teacher’s fist” in respect of doctrines. If there is anyone who thinks: “I shall take charge of the order,” or “The order should refer to me,” let him make some statement about the order. But the thought doesn’t occur to the *Tathāgata* that ‘I will govern the *Saṅgha* of monks,’ or ‘The *Saṅgha* of monks looks to me.’ So why should the *Tathāgata* make a statement about the order? Now I am frail, Ānanda, old, aged, far gone in years. and my life is spent. This is my eightieth year. Just as an old cart is made to go by being held together with straps, so the *Tathāgata’s* body is kept going by being strapped up. It is only when the *Tathāgata* withdraws his attention from outward signs, and by the cessation of certain feelings, enters into the signless concentration of mind, that his body knows comfort. Therefore, Ānanda, you should live as islands unto yourselves, being your own refuge, with no one else as your refuge, with the Dharma as an island, with the Dharma as your refuge, with no other refuge. And how, Ānanda, does a *bhikkhu* live as an island unto himself, being his own refuge, with no one else as his refuge, with the Dharma as an island, with the Dharma as his refuge, with no other refuge? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* remains focused on the body in and of itself—ardent, alert, & mindful—subduing greed & distress with reference to the world. [Likewise,] feelings…mind…mental qualities. Thus, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* lives as an island unto himself, being his own refuge, with no one else as his refuge, with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge. For those who, now or when I am gone, live with themselves as their island, themselves as their refuge, with no other as their refuge; with the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma as their refuge, not with another as their refuge, will be my foremost monks: those who are desirous of training.”

The Second Portion for Recitation.

Account of the Appearance of Signs
commentary_pali:
165.Anantaraṃabāhiranti dhammavasena vā puggalavasena vā ubhayaṃ akatvā. ‘‘Ettakaṃ dhammaṃ parassa na desessāmī’’ti hi cintento dhammaṃ abbhantaraṃ karoti nāma. ‘‘Ettakaṃ parassa desessāmī’’ti cintento dhammaṃ bāhiraṃ karoti nāma. ‘‘Imassa puggalassa desessāmī’’ti cintento pana puggalaṃ abbhantaraṃ karoti nāma. ‘‘Imassa na desessāmī’’ti cintento puggalaṃ bāhiraṃ karoti nāma. Evaṃ akatvā desitoti attho. Ācariyamuṭṭhīti yathā bāhirakānaṃ ācariyamuṭṭhi nāma hoti. Daharakāle kassaci akathetvā pacchimakāle maraṇamañce nipannā piyamanāpassa antevāsikassa kathenti, evaṃ tathāgatassa – ‘‘idaṃ mahallakakāle pacchimaṭṭhāne kathessāmī’’ti muṭṭhiṃ katvā ‘‘pariharissāmī’’ti ṭhapitaṃ kiñci natthīti dasseti.

Ahaṃbhikkhusaṅghanti ahameva bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmīti vā mamuddesikoti ahaṃ uddisitabbaṭṭhena uddeso assāti mamuddesiko. Maṃyeva uddisitvā mama paccāsīsamāno bhikkhusaṅgho hotu, mama accayena vā mā ahesuṃ, yaṃ vā taṃ vā hotūti iti vā yassa assāti attho. Na evaṃ hotīti bodhipallaṅkeyeva issāmacchariyānaṃ vihatattā evaṃ na hoti. Sa kinti so kiṃ. Āsītikoti asītisaṃvacchariko. Idaṃ pacchimavayaanuppattabhāvadīpanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Veṭhamissakenāti bāhabandhacakkabandhādinā paṭisaṅkharaṇena veṭhamissakena. Maññeti jiṇṇasakaṭaṃ viya veṭhamissakena maññe yāpeti. Arahattaphalaveṭhanena catuiriyāpathakappanaṃ tathāgatassa hotīti dasseti.

Ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅgha mamuddesiko Na evaṃ hotī Sa ki Āsītiko Veṭhamissakenā Maññe

Idāni tamatthaṃ pakāsento yasmiṃ, ānanda, samayetiādimāha. Tattha sabbanimittānanti rūpanimittādīnaṃ. Ekaccānaṃ vedanānanti lokiyānaṃ vedanānaṃ. Tasmātihānandāti yasmā iminā phalasamāpattivihārena phāsu hoti, tasmā tumhepi tadatthāya evaṃ viharathāti dasseti. Attadīpāti mahāsamuddagatadīpaṃ viya attānaṃ dīpaṃ patiṭṭhaṃ katvā viharatha. Attasaraṇāti attagatikāva hotha, mā aññagatikā. Dhammadīpadhammasaraṇapadesupi eseva nayo. Tamataggeti tamaagge. Majjhe takāro padasandhivasena vutto. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘ime aggatamāti tamataggā’’ti. Evaṃ sabbaṃ tamayogaṃ chinditvā ativiya agge uttamabhāve ete , ānanda , mama bhikkhū bhavissanti. Tesaṃ atiagge bhavissanti, ye keci sikkhākāmā, sabbepi te catusatipaṭṭhānagocarāva bhikkhū agge bhavissantīti arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye sabbanimittāna Ekaccānaṃ vedanāna Tasmātihānandā Attadīpā Attasaraṇā Dhammadīpadhammasaraṇa Tamatagge

Dutiyabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Nimittobhāsakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
165.
 *Anantaraṃ*, without [regarding] outside.
*Abāhira* means without doing both Dharma [considerations] or individual [considerations].

"I will not teach this much Dharma to another," thinking thus, he makes the Dharma internal, it is said.

"I will teach this much to another," thinking thus, he makes the Dharma external, it is said.

"I will teach this to this individual," thinking thus, he makes the individual internal, it is said.

"I will not teach this to this [individual]," thinking thus, he makes the individual external, it is said.

Thus, *akatvā* [means] without doing; *desitoti* means taught, is the meaning.

*Ācariyamuṭṭhī* [means] as the *ācariyamuṭṭhi* is for outsiders, it is said.

In young age without telling anyone, in the final time, lying on the deathbed, they tell a beloved pupil. Likewise, to the *Tathāgata*: "This, in old age, in the final place I will tell," having made a fist, "I will keep," nothing kept is shown.

*Ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅgha* [means] I myself will care for the monastic community or, *mamuddesiko*, *ahaṃ uddisitabbaṭṭhena uddeso assāti mamuddesiko* [means] I am he who is to be indicated. The indication is his.

Let the monastic community be one that indicates me, expects of me, or may they not be gone at my passing away, or may that or that be, thus it is, is the meaning.

*Na evaṃ hotī*: In the *bodhipallaṅka*, because envy and stinginess are destroyed, thus it is not.

*Sa ki*: What is that?

*Āsītiko*: Eighty years of age.

This is said to illuminate the state of attaining the final age.

*Veṭhamissakenā*: By means of wrapping, with adornment such as armbands, wheel-bands, etc., [it is done] with wrapping.

*Maññe*: Like an old cart, he lives it out, I think, by means of wrapping.

By means of the wrapping of the fruit of Arhatship, he shows that the four postures are for the *Tathāgata*.

I, monastic community, *mamuddesiko*, *na evaṃ hotī*, *sa ki*, *āsītiko*, *veṭhamissakenā*, *maññe*, now, revealing that meaning, he said, "*yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye*," etc.

There, *sabbanimittāna* [means] forms, signs, etc.

*Ekaccānaṃ vedanāna* [means] of worldly feelings.

*Tasmātihānandā* [means] because happiness occurs with this dwelling in the fruit of meditative absorption, therefore, you also should dwell thus for that purpose, he shows.

*Attadīpā* [means] like an island gone to the great ocean, establish yourself as an island, and dwell.

*Attasaraṇā* [means] be those with yourselves as refuge, not others as refuge.

This same principle applies to the phrases *dhammadīpadhammasaraṇa* as well.

*Tamatagge* [means] the highest.

The letter *ta* in the middle is said by way of the combination of words.

This is said: "These are the highest," thus, *tamataggā*.

Thus, having cut off all that connection, exceedingly at the top, in the state of excellence, these, Ānanda, will be my *bhikkhus*.

They will be exceedingly at the top, whoever are desirous of training, all those monks, whose sphere is the four applications of mindfulness, will be at the top, thus, he comprehends the teaching with the secret of Arhatship.

*Yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye, sabbanimittāna, ekaccānaṃ vedanāna, tasmātihānandā, attadīpā, attasaraṇā, dhammadīpadhammasaraṇa, tamatagge*

The explanation of the second Bhanavara is finished.

Explanation of the discourse on the image of light

mula_pali: 166. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaṇhāhi, ānanda, nisīdanaṃ, yena cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ pāvālaṃ (cetiyaṃ (syā.) tenupasaṅkamissāma divā vihārāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā nisīdanaṃ ādāya bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Atha kho bhagavā yena cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho ānando bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.
mula_english: Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, adjusted his lower robe and—taking his bowl & outer robe—went into Vesālī for alms. Having gone for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, returning from his alms round, he addressed Venerable Ānanda, “Get a sitting cloth, Ānanda. We will go to the Cāpāla shrine for the day’s abiding.” “As you say, lord,” Ven. Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and taking the sitting cloth, he followed along behind the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One went to the Cāpāla shrine and, on arrival, sat down on the seat laid out. And Ven. Ānanda, having bowed down to the Blessed One, sat down to one side.
commentary_pali:
166.Vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisīti kadā pāvisi? Ukkacelato nikkhamitvā vesāliṃ gatakāle. Bhagavā kira vuṭṭhavasso veḷuvagāmakā nikkhamitvā sāvatthiṃ gamissāmīti āgatamaggeneva paṭinivattanto anupubbena sāvatthiṃ patvā jetavanaṃ pāvisi. Dhammasenāpati bhagavato vattaṃ dassetvā divāṭṭhānaṃ gato. So tattha antevāsikesu vattaṃ dassetvā paṭikkantesu divāṭṭhānaṃ sammajjitvā cammakkhaṇḍaṃ paññapetvā pāde pakkhāletvā pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā phalasamāpattiṃ pāvisi. Athassa yathāparicchedena tato vuṭṭhitassa ayaṃ parivitakko udapādi – ‘‘buddhā nu kho paṭhamaṃ parinibbāyanti, agasāvakā nu kho’’ti? Tato – ‘‘aggasāvakā paṭhama’’nti ñatvā attano āyusaṅkhāraṃ olokesi. So – ‘‘sattāhameva me āyusaṅkhāro pavattatī’’ti ñatvā – ‘‘kattha parinibbāyissāmī’’ti cintesi. Tato – ‘‘rāhulo tāvatiṃsesu parinibbuto, aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero chaddantadahe, ahaṃ kattha parinibbāyissāmī’’ti puna cintento mātaraṃ ārabbha satiṃ uppādesi – ‘‘mayhaṃ mātā sattannaṃ arahantānaṃ mātā hutvāpi buddhadhammasaṅghesu appasannā, atthi nu kho tassā upanissayo, natthi nu kho’’ti āvajjetvā sotāpattimaggassa upanissayaṃ disvā – ‘‘kassa desanāya abhisamayo bhavissatī’’ti olokento – ‘‘mameva dhammadesanāya bhavissati, na aññassa. Sace kho panāhaṃ appossukko bhaveyyaṃ, bhavissanti me vattāro – ‘sāriputtatthero avasesajanānampi avassayo hoti. Tathā hissa samacittasuttadesanādivase (a. ni. 1.37) koṭisatasahassadevatā arahattaṃ pattā . Tayo magge paṭividdhadevatānaṃ gaṇanā natthi. Aññesu ca ṭhānesu anekā abhisamayā dissanti. Thereva cittaṃ pasādetvā sagge nibbattāneva asītikulasahassāni. So dāni sakamātumicchādassanamattampi harituṃ nāsakkhī’ti. Tasmā mātaraṃ micchādassanā mocetvā jātovarakeyeva parinibbāyissāmī’’ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā – ‘‘ajjeva bhagavantaṃ anujānāpetvā nikkhamissāmī’’ti cundattheraṃ āmantesi. ‘‘Āvuso, cunda, amhākaṃ pañcasatāya bhikkhuparisāya saññaṃ dehi – ‘gaṇhathāvuso pattacīvarāni, dhammasenāpati nāḷakagāmaṃ gantukāmo’ti’’. Thero tathā akāsi. Bhikkhū senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya therassa santikaṃ āgamaṃsu. Thero senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā divāṭṭhānaṃ sammajjitvā divāṭṭhānadvāre ṭhatvā divāṭṭhānaṃ olokento – ‘‘idaṃ dāni pacchimadassanaṃ, puna āgamanaṃ natthī’’ti pañcasatabhikkhuparivuto bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā vanditvā etadavoca –

‘‘Chinno dāni bhavissāmi, lokanātha mahāmuni;

Gamanāgamanaṃ natthi, pacchimā vandanā ayaṃ.

Jīvitaṃ appakaṃ mayhaṃ, ito sattāhamaccaye;

Nikkhipeyyāmahaṃ dehaṃ, bhāravoropanaṃ yathā.

Anujānātu me bhante, bhagavā, anujānātu sugato;

Parinibbānakālo me, ossaṭṭho āyusaṅkhāro’’ti.

Buddhā pana yasmā ‘‘parinibbāhī’’ti vutte maraṇasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ saṃvaṇṇenti nāma, ‘‘mā parinibbāhī’’ti vutte vaṭṭassa guṇaṃ kathentīti micchādiṭṭhikā dosaṃ āropessanti, tasmā tadubhayampi na vadanti. Tena naṃ bhagavā āha – ‘‘kattha parinibbāyissasi sāriputtā’’ti? ‘‘Atthi, bhante, magadhesu nāḷakagāme jātovarako, tatthāhaṃ parinibbāyissāmī’’ti vutte ‘‘yassa dāni tvaṃ, sāriputta, kālaṃ maññasi, idāni pana te jeṭṭhakaniṭṭhabhātikānaṃ tādisassa bhikkhuno dassanaṃ dullabhaṃ bhavissatīti desehi tesaṃ dhamma’’nti āha.

Thero – ‘‘satthā mayhaṃ iddhivikubbanapubbaṅgamaṃ dhammadesanaṃ paccāsīsatī’’ti ñatvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā tālappamāṇaṃ abbhuggantvā puna oruyha bhagavantaṃ vanditvā sattatālappamāṇe antalikkhe ṭhito iddhivikubbanaṃ dassetvā dhammaṃ desesi. Sakalanagaraṃ sannipati. Thero oruyha bhagavantaṃ vanditvā ‘‘gamanakālo me, bhante’’ti āha. Bhagavā ‘‘dhammasenāpatiṃ paṭipādessāmī’’ti dhammāsanā uṭṭhāya gandhakuṭiabhimukho gantvā maṇiphalake aṭṭhāsi. Thero tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā catūsu ṭhānesu vanditvā – ‘‘bhagavā ito kappasatasahassādhikassa asaṅkhyeyyassa upari anomadassisammāsambuddhassa pādamūle nipatitvā tumhākaṃ dassanaṃ patthesiṃ. Sā me patthanā samiddhā, diṭṭhā tumhe, taṃ paṭhamadassanaṃ, idaṃ pacchimadassanaṃ. Puna tumhākaṃ dassanaṃ natthī’’ti – vatvā dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ paggayha yāva dassanavisayo, tāva abhimukhova paṭikkamitvā ‘‘ito paṭṭhāya cutipaṭisandhivasena kismiñci ṭhāne gamanāgamanaṃ nāma natthī’’ti vanditvā pakkāmi. Udakapariyantaṃ katvā mahābhūmicālo ahosi. Bhagavā parivāretvā ṭhite bhikkhū āha – ‘‘anugacchatha, bhikkhave, tumhākaṃ jeṭṭhabhātika’’nti. Bhikkhū yāva dvārakoṭṭhakā agamaṃsu. Thero – ‘‘tiṭṭhatha, tumhe āvuso, appamattā hothā’’ti nivattāpetvā attano parisāyeva saddhiṃ pakkāmi. Manussā – ‘‘pubbe ayyo paccāgamanacārikaṃ carati, idaṃ dāni gamanaṃ na puna paccāgamanāyā’’ti paridevantā anubandhiṃsu. Tepi ‘‘appamattā hotha āvuso, evaṃbhāvino nāma saṅkhārā’’ti nivattāpesi.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto antarāmagge sattāhaṃ manussānaṃ anuggahaṃ karonto sāyaṃ nāḷakagāmaṃ patvā gāmadvāre nigrodharukkhamūle aṭṭhāsi. Atha uparevato nāma therassa bhāgineyyo bahigāmaṃ gacchanto theraṃ disvā upasaṅkamitvā vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. Thero taṃ āha – ‘‘atthi gehe te ayyikā’’ti? Āma, bhanteti. Gaccha amhākaṃ idhāgatabhāvaṃ ārocehi. ‘‘Kasmā āgato’’ti ca vutte ‘‘ajja kira ekadivasaṃ antogāme bhavissati, jātovarakaṃ paṭijaggatha, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ jānāthā’’ti. So gantvā ‘‘ayyike, mayhaṃ mātulo āgato’’ti āha. Idāni kuhinti? Gāmadvāreti. Ekakova, aññopi koci atthīti ? Atthi pañcasatā bhikkhūti. Kiṃ kāraṇā āgatoti? So taṃ pavattiṃ ārocesi. Brāhmaṇī – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho ettakānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ paṭijaggāpeti , daharakāle pabbajitvā mahallakakāle gihī hotukāmo’’ti cintentī jātovarakaṃ paṭijaggāpetvā pañcasatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ kāretvā daṇḍadīpikāyo jāletvā therassa pāhesi.

Thero bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pāsādaṃ abhiruhi. Abhiruhitvā ca jātovarakaṃ pavisitvā nisīdi. Nisajjeva – ‘‘tumhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gacchathā’’ti bhikkhū uyyojesi. Tesu gatamattesuyeva therassa kharo ābādho uppajji, lohitapakkhandikā māraṇantikā vedanā vattanti, ekaṃ bhājanaṃ pavisati, ekaṃ nikkhamati. Brāhmaṇī – ‘‘mama puttassa pavatti mayhaṃ na ruccatī’’ti attano vasanagabbhadvāraṃ nissāya aṭṭhāsi. Cattāro mahārājāno ‘‘dhammasenāpati kuhiṃ viharatī’’ti olokentā ‘‘nāḷakagāme jātovarake parinibbānamañce nipanno, pacchimadassanaṃ gamissāmā’’ti āgamma vanditvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Thero – ke tumheti? Mahārājāno, bhanteti. Kasmā āgatatthāti? Gilānupaṭṭhākā bhavissāmāti. Hotu, atthi gilānupaṭṭhāko, gacchatha tumheti uyyojesi. Tesaṃ gatāvasāne teneva nayena sakko devānamindo, tasmiṃ gate suyāmādayo mahābrahmā ca āgamiṃsu. Tepi tatheva thero uyyojesi.

Brāhmaṇī devatānaṃ āgamanañca gamanañca disvā – ‘‘ke nu kho ete mama puttaṃ vanditvā gacchantī’’ti therassa gabbhadvāraṃ gantvā – ‘‘tāta, cunda, kā pavattī’’ti pucchi. So taṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhitvā – ‘‘mahāupāsikā, bhante āgatā’’ti āha. Thero kasmā avelāya āgatatthāti pucchi. Sā tuyhaṃ tāta dassanatthāyāti vatvā ‘‘tāta ke paṭhamaṃ āgatā’’ti pucchi. Cattāro mahārājāno, upāsiketi. Tāta, tvaṃ catūhi mahārājehi mahantataroti? Ārāmikasadisā ete upāsike, amhākaṃ satthu paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya khaggahatthā hutvā ārakkhaṃ akaṃsūti. Tesaṃ tāta, gatāvasāne ko āgatoti? Sakko devānamindoti. Devarājatopi tvaṃ tāta, mahantataroti? Bhaṇḍagāhakasāmaṇerasadiso esa upāsike, amhākaṃ satthu tāvatiṃsato otaraṇakāle pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā otiṇṇoti. Tassa tāta gatāvasāne jotamāno viya ko āgatoti? Upāsike tuyhaṃ bhagavā ca satthā ca mahābrahmā nāma esoti. Mayhaṃ bhagavato mahābrahmatopi tvaṃ tāta mahantataroti? Āma upāsike, ete nāma kira amhākaṃ satthu jātadivase cattāro mahābrahmāno mahāpurisaṃ suvaṇṇajālena paṭiggaṇhiṃsūti.

Atha brāhmaṇiyā – ‘‘puttassa tāva me ayaṃ ānubhāvo, kīdiso vata mayhaṃ puttassa bhagavato satthu ānubhāvo bhavissatī’’ti cintayantiyā sahasā pañcavaṇṇā pīti uppajjitvā sakalasarīre phari. Thero – ‘‘uppannaṃ me mātu pītisomanassaṃ, ayaṃ dāni kālo dhammadesanāyā’’ti cintetvā – ‘‘kiṃ cintesi mahāupāsike’’ti āha. Sā – ‘‘puttassa tāva me ayaṃ guṇo, satthu panassa kīdiso guṇo bhavissatīti idaṃ, tāta, cintemī’’ti āha. Mahāupāsike, mayhaṃ satthu jātakkhaṇe, mahābhinikkhamane, sambodhiyaṃ, dhammacakkappavattane ca dasasahassilokadhātu kampittha, sīlena samādhinā paññāya vimuttiyā vimuttiñāṇadassanena samo nāma natthi, itipi so bhagavāti vitthāretvā buddhaguṇappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ dhammadesanaṃ kathesi.

Brāhmaṇī piyaputtassa dhammadesanāpariyosāne sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāya puttaṃ āha – ‘‘tāta, upatissa, kasmā evamakāsi, evarūpaṃ nāma amataṃ mayhaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ na adāsī’’ti. Thero – ‘‘dinnaṃ dāni me mātu rūpasāriyā brāhmaṇiyā posāvanikamūlaṃ, ettakena vaṭṭissatī’’ti cintetvā ‘‘gaccha mahāupāsike’’ti brāhmaṇiṃ uyyojetvā ‘‘cunda kā velā’’ti āha. Balavapaccūsakālo, bhanteti. Tena hi bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātehīti. Sannipatito, bhante, saṅghoti. Maṃ ukkhipitvā nisīdāpehi cundāti ukkhipitvā nisīdāpesi. Thero bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘āvuso catucattālīsaṃ vo vassāni mayā saddhiṃ vicarantānaṃ yaṃ me kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā na rocetha, khamatha taṃ āvusoti. Ettakaṃ, bhante, amhākaṃ chāyā viya tumhe amuñcitvā vicarantānaṃ aruccanakaṃ nāma natthi, tumhe pana amhākaṃ khamathāti. Atha thero aruṇasikhāya paññāyamānāya mahāpathaviṃ unnādayanto anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyi. Bahū devamanussā therassa parinibbāne sakkāraṃ kariṃsu.

Āyasmā cundo therassa pattacīvarañca dhātuparissāvanañca gahetvā jetavanaṃ gantvā ānandattheraṃ gahetvā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkami. Bhagavā dhātuparissāvanaṃ gahetvā pañcahi gāthāsatehi therassa guṇaṃ kathetvā dhātucetiyaṃ kārāpetvā rājagahagamanatthāya ānandattherassa saññaṃ adāsi. Thero bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi. Bhagavā mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivuto rājagahaṃ agamāsi. Tattha gatakāle mahāmoggallānatthero parinibbāyi. Bhagavā tassa dhātuyo gahetvā cetiyaṃ kārāpetvā rājagahato nikkhamitvā anupubbena gaṅgābhimukho gantvā ukkacelaṃ agamāsi. Tattha gaṅgātīre bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisīditvā tattha sāriputtamoggallānānaṃ parinibbānappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ suttaṃ desetvā ukkacelato nikkhamitvā vesāliṃ agamāsi. Evaṃ gate atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisīti ayamettha anupubbī kathā.

Nisīdananti ettha cammakkhaṇḍaṃ adhippetaṃ. Udenacetiyanti udenayakkhassa cetiyaṭṭhāne katavihāro vuccati. Gotamakādīsupi eseva nayo. Bhāvitāti vaḍḍhitā. Bahulīkatāti punappunaṃ katā. Yānīkatāti yuttayānaṃ viya katā. Vatthukatāti patiṭṭhānaṭṭhena vatthu viya katā. Anuṭṭhitāti adhiṭṭhitā. Paricitāti samantato citā suvaḍḍhitā. Susamāraddhāti suṭṭhu samāraddhā.

Nisīdana Udenacetiya Gotamakādīsupi Bhāvitā Bahulīkatā Yānīkatā Vatthukatā Anuṭṭhitā Paricitā Susamāraddhā

Iti aniyamena kathetvā puna niyametvā dassento tathāgatassa khotiādimāha. Ettha ca kappanti āyukappaṃ. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ kāle yaṃ manussānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ hoti, taṃ paripuṇṇaṃ karonto tiṭṭheyya. Kappāvasesaṃ vāti – ‘‘appaṃ vā bhiyyo’’ti (dī. ni. 2.7; a. ni. 6.74) vuttavassasatato atirekaṃ vā. Mahāsīvatthero panāha – ‘‘buddhānaṃ aṭṭhāne gajjitaṃ nāma natthi. Yatheva hi veḷuvagāmake uppannaṃ māraṇantikaṃ vedanaṃ dasa māse vikkhambheti, evaṃ punappunaṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā dasa dasa māse vikkhambhento imaṃ bhaddakappameva tiṭṭheyya, kasmā pana na ṭhitoti? Upādinnakasarīraṃ nāma khaṇḍiccādīhi abhibhuyyati, buddhā ca khaṇḍiccādibhāvaṃ apatvā pañcame āyukoṭṭhāse bahujanassa piyamanāpakāleyeva parinibbāyanti. Buddhānubuddhesu ca mahāsāvakesu parinibbutesu ekakeneva khāṇukena viya ṭhātabbaṃ hoti, daharasāmaṇeraparivāritena vā. Tato – ‘aho buddhānaṃ parisā’ti hīḷetabbataṃ āpajjeyya. Tasmā na ṭhito’’ti. Evaṃ vuttepi so na ruccati, ‘‘āyukappo’’ti idameva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ niyamitaṃ.

tathāgatassa kho kappa Kappāvasesaṃ vā
commentary_english:
166. When did [he] enter Vesālī for alms (vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisīti)? When he had left Ukkacela and arrived in Vesālī.

The Blessed One, having spent the rainy season, left Veḷuvagāma and, thinking “I will go to Sāvatthi,” returned by the same route he had come, and gradually reaching Sāvatthi, entered Jetavana.

The General of the Dhamma, having shown the Blessed One his duties, went to his day quarters.

He, having shown his duties to his pupils there, after they had departed, swept the day quarters, spread out a leather seat, washed his feet, folded his legs into the lotus position, and entered the fruition attainment.

Then, when he had arisen from it according to his ability, this thought arose in him: “Do the Buddhas pass away first, or the chief disciples?” Then, realizing “The chief disciples [pass away] first,” he looked over his life-span.

He, knowing that “My life-span lasts only seven days,” thought, “Where shall I pass away?”

Then, thinking again, “Rāhula has passed away in the Tāvatiṃsa heavens, the Elder Aññāsikoṇḍañña in the Chaddanta lake; where shall I pass away?” he directed his mindfulness towards his mother, [thinking,] “Though my mother has been the mother of seven arahants, she is not devoted to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha. Is there a support for her, or is there not?” Considering it, and seeing a support for the path of a stream-enterer, [and] looking to see “Through whose teaching will there be realization?” [he saw:] “It will be through my own teaching of the Dhamma, not through another’s.

If I were to be without zeal, there would be those who would say, ‘The Elder Sāriputta is a refuge even for the remaining people.’

Thus, on the day of teaching the Samacitta Sutta (A.
iii.
37), a hundred thousand myriads of deities attained arahatship.

There is no reckoning of the deities who penetrated the path.

And in other places, many understandings are seen.

Having pleased their minds right there, eighty thousand families were reborn in heaven.

Now, he was not able to bear even the mere sight of his mother's wrong view.

Therefore, resolving “Having freed my mother from wrong view, I will pass away just like Jātovaraka,” he addressed the Elder Cunda, [saying,] “Today itself, having taken leave of the Blessed One, I will depart.”

“Friend Cunda, give a message to the five hundred monks in our community: ‘Friends, take your bowls and robes; the General of the Dhamma wishes to go to Nāḷakagāma.’”

The Elder did so.

The monks, having put their resting places in order, taking their bowls and robes, came to the Elder’s presence.

The Elder, having put his resting place in order, having swept the day quarters, standing at the door of the day quarters, looking at the day quarters, [thought,] “This is now my last sight; there will be no return,” and surrounded by five hundred monks, having approached the Blessed One, having paid homage, said this:

“Now I shall be cut off, O Protector of the World, great sage;

There is no coming or going; this is my last veneration.

My life is short; seven days from now,

I shall lay down my body, like the removal of a burden.

May the Blessed One permit me, O venerable one, may the Well-gone One permit me;

It is time for my passing away; my life-span has been relinquished.”

Since, when Buddhas <pb ed="v" n="2.
0126"/> say “I will pass away,” they are praising death, and when [others] say “Do not pass away,” those with wrong views will accuse them of telling the qualities of Vaṭṭa, therefore they do not say either of those two things.

Therefore, the Blessed One said to him, “Where will you pass away, Sāriputta?” “Venerable one, in Magadha, in the village of Nāḷaka, there is Jātovaraka; there I will pass away.” When this was said, [the Buddha said,] “Now, Sāriputta, you think it is time [to go]; now, however, the sight of such a monk by your elder and younger brothers will be difficult to obtain; teach them the Dhamma.”

The Elder—knowing that “The Teacher anticipates from me a teaching of the Dhamma preceded by a display of psychic power”—having paid homage to the Blessed One, having risen up to the height of a palm tree, and again descending, having paid homage to the Blessed One, <pb ed="p" n="2.
0551"/> standing in the sky at the height of seven palm trees, <pb ed="m" n="2.
0141"/> displayed a display of psychic power and taught the Dhamma.

The whole city gathered together.

The Elder, descending, having paid homage to the Blessed One, said, “It is time for my departure, venerable one.”

The Blessed One, [thinking,] “I will send off the General of the Dhamma,” rising from the Dhamma seat, going towards the Gandhakuti, stood on a jeweled slab.

The Elder, having circumambulated three times, having paid homage in the four places—"Venerable One, from here, above a hundred thousand myriads of aeons, having fallen at the foot of the Fully Enlightened One Anomadassi, I longed for a sight of you.

That longing of mine is fulfilled; you have been seen; that was my first sight, this is my last sight.

There will be no further sight of you”—having said this, raising his joined hands, radiant with the arrangement of his ten fingernails, as far as the range of sight, having retreated facing him, [and saying,] “From here on, through the force of passing away and rebirth, there is no such thing as coming and going in any place,” having paid homage, he departed.
Having made the water boundary, there was a great earthquake.

The Blessed One, having surrounded the monks who were standing, said: "Follow, monks, your elder brother."

The monks went as far as the gate tower.

The Elder, having turned them back, saying, "Stay, friends, be mindful," departed together with his own company.

The people, lamenting, followed, "Formerly, this venerable one traveled on a journey of return, now this going is not for returning again."

He turned them back, [saying,] "Be mindful, friends, such is the nature of conditioned things."

Then, venerable Śāriputra, while bestowing favor on the people along the way for a week, arrived in the evening at the village of Nāḷaka and stood at the foot of a banyan tree at the village gate.

Then Uparevata, the nephew of the Elder, while going outside the village, having seen the Elder, approached, paid homage, and stood.

The Elder said to him: "Is there an aunt in your house?" "Yes, venerable sir."

"Go, announce our arrival here."

"Why have you come?" When [he] was asked, [he replied,] "Today, it seems, [he] will be inside the village for a day; prepare the Jātovaraka, know the dwelling place of the five hundred monks."

He, having gone, said, "Aunt, my maternal uncle has come."

"Where is he now?" "At the village gate."

"Is he alone, or is there anyone else?" "There are five hundred monks."

"For what reason has he come?" He announced that account.

The *brāhmaṇī* [thought], "Why does he have [me] prepare a dwelling place for so many, [thinking,] 'Having gone forth in [his] youth, [he] wants to become a householder in [his] old age?'" Thinking thus, having had the Jātovaraka prepared, having had a dwelling place made for the five hundred monks, having lit lamp stands, she sent [them] to the Elder.

The Elder ascended the palace together with the monks.

Having ascended, he entered the Jātovaraka and sat down.

While sitting, he dismissed the monks, [saying,] "Go to your dwelling places."

As soon as they had gone, a severe sickness arose in the Elder; bloody diarrhea, deadly pains were afflicting [him], one [thing] enters a vessel, [and] one exits.

The *brāhmaṇī* [thought,] "The account of my son does not please me," and stood leaning against the door of her dwelling chamber.

The four Great Kings, looking to see "Where does the general of the Dhamma reside?" [saw that he] "is lying on the *parinirvāṇa* couch in the Jātovaraka in the village of Nāḷaka, we will go for a last viewing," having come, [they] paid homage and stood.

The Elder [asked,] "Who are you?" "Great Kings, venerable sir."

"Why have you come?" "We will be attendants to the sick."

"Enough, there is an attendant to the sick, go," he dismissed them.

At the end of their departure, in that very manner, Śakka, the king of the gods, and, when he had gone, Suyāma and others, and the Great Brahmā, came.

The Elder dismissed them too in the same way.

The *brāhmaṇī*, having seen the coming and going of the deities, [thought,] "Who are these who, having venerated my son, are departing?" Having gone to the chamber door of the Elder, she asked, "Father Cunda, what is the account?"

He, having told her the account, said, "Great laywoman, venerable sir, [they] have come."

The Elder asked, "Why have they come at an improper time?"

She, having said, "Father, for the sake of seeing you," asked, "Father, who came first?"

"The four Great Kings, laywoman."
"Father, are you greater than the four Great Kings?" "These laywomen are like gardeners; since the Teacher's conception, they have been protecting [him] with swords in their hands."

"Father, at the end of their journey, who came?" "Śakra, the lord of the gods."

"Father, are you greater than the king of the gods?" "This laywoman is like a novice who collects goods; at the time of the Teacher's descent from the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, she descended carrying the bowl and robe."

"Father, at the end of his journey, who came shining?" "Laywoman, this is your Blessed One, Teacher, and the Great Brahmā."

"Father, are you greater than my Blessed One, the Great Brahmā?" "Yes, laywoman, on the day of our Teacher's birth, four Great Brahmās received the great man with a golden net."

Then the Brāhmaṇī, thinking, "Such is the power of my son; what will be the power of my son, the Blessed One, the Teacher?" suddenly joy of five colors arose and pervaded her whole body.

The Elder, thinking, "Joy and happiness have arisen in my mother's mind; now is the time for teaching the Dharma," said, "What are you thinking, great laywoman?"

She said, "Father, such is the quality of my son; what will be the quality of the Teacher? This is what I am thinking."

"Great laywoman, at the moment of my Teacher's birth, at the Great Renunciation, at Enlightenment, and at the turning of the Wheel of the Dharma, the ten thousand world-systems trembled. There is no one equal to him in morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the vision of knowledge and liberation." Thus, having expanded, he told a Dharma teaching connected with the Buddha's qualities.

At the end of the Dharma teaching of the Brāhmaṇī's beloved son, having been established in the fruit of stream-entry, she said to her son, "Father, Upatissa, why did you do this? You did not give me such nectar for so long!"

The Elder, thinking, "Now the root of support has been given to my mother, the beautiful Brāhmaṇī; it will suffice with this," having sent away the Brāhmaṇī, he said, "Cunda, what time is it?"

"It is the strong dawn, venerable sir."

"Then assemble the Saṅgha of monks."

"The Saṅgha is assembled, venerable sir."

"Lift me up and seat me, Cunda." Having lifted him up, he seated him.

The Elder addressed the monks: "Friends, for forty-four years that I have been wandering with you, if anything of my bodily or verbal [action] has displeased you, forgive me that, friends."

"Venerable sir, there is nothing unpleasant from you for us who have been wandering without abandoning you like a shadow. But you, forgive us."

Then the Elder, as the tip of the dawn was becoming visible, shaking the great earth, passed into complete nirvāṇa in the element of nirvāṇa without remainder.

Many gods and humans honored the Elder's passing into nirvāṇa.

The venerable Cunda, having taken the bowl and robe and water strainer of the Elder, went to Jetavana, and having taken the venerable Ānanda, approached the Blessed One.

The Blessed One, having taken the water strainer, having spoken of the Elder's virtues in five hundred verses, having had a shrine built for the relics, gave the venerable Ānanda a sign for the purpose of going to Rājagṛha.

The Elder announced to the monks.

The Blessed One, surrounded by a great Saṅgha of monks, went to Rājagṛha.

While there, the venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana passed into nirvāṇa.

The Blessed One, having taken his relics, having had a shrine built, having departed from Rājagṛha, gradually going towards the Ganges, went to Ukkacela.

There, on the bank of the Ganges, having sat down surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks, having taught a sutra connected with the passing into nirvāṇa of Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, having departed from Ukkacela, he went to Vaiśālī.

Thus having gone, then the Blessed One, in the morning time, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vaiśālī for alms. This is the sequential story here.

*Nisīdana* here means a piece of skin.
*Udenacetiya* means the *vihāra* (monastery) built at the place of the shrine of Udena Yakṣa is called.

*Gotamakādīsupi*, this same method [applies].

*Bhāvitā* means cultivated.

*Bahulīkatā* means done again and again.

*Yānīkatā* means made like a yoked vehicle.

*Vatthukatā* means made like a thing (vatthu) by way of being a foundation (patiṭṭhāna).

*Anuṭṭhitā* means established (adhiṭṭhitā).

*Paricitā* means accumulated all around, well developed (suvaḍḍhitā).

*Susamāraddhā* means very well begun (suṭṭhu samāraddhā).

Having spoken thus without restriction and then showing [it] with restriction again, [the text] says, “*Tathāgatassa kho*” etc.

Here, *kappa* means life-span (āyukappaṃ).

At that particular time, one should remain completing the life-span of human beings as it is.

*Kappāvasesaṃ vā* means – “Whether little or much” (Dī.

The elder Mahāsīva, however, said, “There is no such thing as thunder in the wrong place for Buddhas.”

Just as, indeed, in the village of Veḷuva, [he] suppresses the deadly feeling that has arisen for ten months, so too, by repeatedly entering into that attainment for ten months each, one might remain for this fortunate eon (bhadrakappa) itself. Why, then, did [he] not remain? The body that is taken up (upādinnakasarīraṃ), indeed, is overcome by decay etc., and the Buddhas, without attaining the state of non-decay etc., pass into complete nirvāṇa (parinibbāyanti) at the fifth division of life, just at the time when [they] are pleasing and agreeable to many people.

When Buddhas who have attained enlightenment and great disciples have passed into complete nirvāṇa, [the preceptor] ought to remain like a single stump, or surrounded by young novices.

Then – [one] might incur the state of being scorned, [thinking] ‘Alas, the assembly of Buddhas!’

Therefore, [he] did not remain.”

Even when [it is] said thus, it is not pleasing. “Life-span (āyukappaṃ)” is just what is defined in the commentary.

167. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi.

Mārayācanakathā
mula_english:
167. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to venerable Ānanda: "Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine; delightful is the Sattamba Shrine (or Sattambaka); delightful is the Many Sons' Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine; delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them; therefore, the Tathāgata, Ānanda, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon."

Even so, venerable Ānanda, when the Blessed One gave such a blatant sign, such a clear indication, was unable to grasp his meaning; he did not beseech the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One remain, O Lord! May the Well-Gone One remain, O Lord, throughout the world-period, for the welfare and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, well-being, and happiness of gods and humans!", so much was his mind possessed by Māra.

A second time… A third time, the Blessed One addressed venerable Ānanda: "Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine; delightful is the Sattamba Shrine; delightful is the Many Sons' Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine; delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them; therefore, the Tathāgata, Ānanda, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon."

Even so, venerable Ānanda, when the Blessed One gave such a blatant sign, such a clear indication, was unable to grasp his meaning; he did not beseech the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One remain, O Lord! May the Well-Gone One remain, O Lord, throughout the world-period, for the welfare and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, well-being, and happiness of gods and humans!", so much was his mind possessed by Māra.

Then the Blessed One addressed venerable Ānanda: "Go now, Ānanda, and do what seems fitting to you."

"Even so, O Lord," said venerable Ānanda in response to the Blessed One. Rising from his seat, he respectfully saluted the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and sat down under a tree not far away.

The Account of Māra's Request
commentary_pali:
167.Yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittoti ettha tanti nipātamattaṃ. Yathā mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto ajjhotthaṭacitto aññopi koci puthujjano paṭivijjhituṃ na sakkuṇeyya, evameva nāsakkhi paṭivijjhitunti attho. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Māro hi yassa sabbena sabbaṃ dvādasa vipallāsā appahīnā, tassa cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti. Therassa cattāro vipallāsā appahīnā, tenassa māro cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti. So pana cittapariyuṭṭhānaṃ karonto kiṃ karotīti? Bheravaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dasseti, saddārammaṇaṃ vā sāveti, tato sattā taṃ disvā vā sutvā vā satiṃ vissajjetvā vivaṭamukhā honti. Tesaṃ mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetvā hadayaṃ maddati. Tato visaññāva hutvā tiṭṭhanti. Therassa panesa mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetuṃ kiṃ sakkhissati ? Bheravārammaṇaṃ pana dasseti. Taṃ disvā thero nimittobhāsaṃ na paṭivijjhi. Bhagavā jānantoyeva – ‘‘kimatthaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ āmantesī’’ti? Parato ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā’’ti yācite ‘‘tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddha’’nti dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇatthaṃ.

Mārayācanakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
167. "Like one whose mind was possessed by Māra (yathā taṃ māreṇa pariyuṭṭhitacitto)"—here, *taṃ* is merely a particle.

Just as another ordinary person whose mind is possessed by Māra, whose mind is overwhelmed, might not be able to penetrate [the truth], even so, he was not able to penetrate it—this is the meaning.

What is the reason? Māra possesses the mind of one for whom the twelve distortions (*dvādasa vipallāsā*) have not been completely abandoned.

Māra possesses the mind of an elder (*therassa*) for whom the four distortions (*cattāro vipallāsā*) have not been completely abandoned.

So, what does he do while causing this possession of the mind (cittapariyuṭṭhānaṃ karonto)? He displays a terrifying visible object (*bheravaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dasseti*) or causes a terrifying sound to be heard (*saddārammaṇaṃ vā sāveti*). Then, those beings, having abandoned mindfulness (*satiṃ vissajjetvā*) upon seeing or hearing that, become open-mouthed.

Having inserted his hand into their mouths, he crushes their hearts (*hadayaṃ maddati*).

Then, having become unconscious (*visaññāva hutvā*), they remain standing (*tiṭṭhanti*).

Will he be able to insert his hand into the elder's (*therassa*) mouth? Rather, he displays a terrifying object (*bheravārammaṇaṃ pana dasseti*).

Having seen that, the elder (*thero*) did not penetrate the reflected image of the sign (*nimittobhāsaṃ na paṭivijjhi*).

The Blessed One, knowing this, [asked,] "Why did you address [him] up to the third time (kimatthaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ āmantesī)?" Later, when [Māra] was entreated, "Stop, venerable sir, Blessed One (tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā)," [the Buddha said,] "This evil is yours, this transgression is yours (tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddha)," thus, by imputing blame, [he taught] for the purpose of alleviating sorrow (dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇatthaṃ).

The Story of Māra's Entreaty (mārayācanakathāvaṇṇanā)
