Parinibbātudāni , bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni , bhante, bhagavato.

‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, upāsikā bhagavato sāvikā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.

‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi , yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhaṃ ceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ iddhaṃ ceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’’ti .

Evaṃ vutte bhagavā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’’ti.

Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanaṃ
mula_english:
§168. Then, not long after the Venerable Ānanda had departed, Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One said this to the Blessed One: “Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa** (*parinirvāṇa*); may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my monks become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the monks are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my nuns become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the nuns are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my laymen become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the laymen are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my laywomen become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the laywomen are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until this **brahmacarya** (holy life) of mine is successful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.’

But now, Blessed One, this holy life of the Blessed One is successful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Māra the Evil One: “Be without worry, Evil One, before long the complete **nirvāṇa** of the **Tathāgata** will come about. In three months from now, the **Tathāgata** will attain complete **nirvāṇa**."
Relinquishing the life-force (*āyusaṅkhāraossajjanaṃ*)
commentary_pali:
168.Māro pāpimāti ettha māroti satte anatthe niyojento māretīti māro. Pāpimāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. So hi pāpadhammasamannāgatattā ‘‘pāpimā’’ti vuccati. Kaṇho, antako, namuci, pamattabandhūtipi tasseva nāmāni. Bhāsitā kho panesāti ayañhi bhagavato sambodhipattiyā aṭṭhame sattāhe bodhimaṇḍeyeva āgantvā – ‘‘bhagavā yadatthaṃ tumhehi pāramiyo pūritā, so vo attho anuppatto, paṭividdhaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ, kiṃ te lokavicāraṇenā’’ti vatvā, yathā ajja , evameva ‘‘parinibbātu dāni, bhante, bhagavā’’ti yāci. Bhagavā cassa – ‘‘na tāvāha’’ntiādīni vatvā paṭikkhipi. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘bhāsitā kho panesā bhante’’tiādimāha.

Tattha viyattāti maggavasena viyattā. Tatheva vinītā tathā visāradā. Bahussutāti tepiṭakavasena bahu sutametesanti bahussutā. Tameva dhammaṃ dhārentīti dhammadharā. Athavā pariyattibahussutā ceva paṭivedhabahussutā ca. Pariyattipaṭivedhadhammānaṃyeva dhāraṇato dhammadharāti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Dhammānudhammapaṭipannāti ariyadhammassa anudhammabhūtaṃ vipassanādhammaṃ paṭipannā. Sāmīcippaṭipannāti anucchavikapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā. Anudhammacārinoti anudhammacaraṇasīlā. Sakaṃ ācariyakanti attano ācariyavādaṃ. Ācikkhissantītiādīni sabbāni aññamaññassa vevacanāni. Sahadhammenāti sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanena. Sappāṭihāriyanti yāva na niyyānikaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desessanti.

viyattā Bahussutā bahussutā. dhammadharā. Dhammānudhammapaṭipannā Sāmīcippaṭipannā Anudhammacārino Sakaṃ ācariyaka Ācikkhissantī Sahadhammenā Sappāṭihāriya

Brahmacariyanti sikkhattayasaṅgahitaṃ sakalaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. Iddhanti samiddhaṃ jhānassādavasena. Phītanti vuddhippattaṃ sabbaphāliphullaṃ viya abhiññāya sampattivasena. Vitthārikanti vitthataṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ disābhāge patiṭṭhitavasena. Bāhujaññanti bahujanehi ñātaṃ paṭividdhaṃ mahājanābhisamayavasena. Puthubhūtanti sabbākāravasena puthulabhāvappattaṃ. Kathaṃ? Yāva devamanussehisuppakāsitanti yattakā viññujātikā devā ceva manussā ca atthi sabbehi suṭṭhu pakāsitanti attho.

Brahmacariya Iddha Phīta Vitthārika Bāhujañña Puthubhūta Yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita

Appossukkoti nirālayo. Tvañhi pāpima, aṭṭhamasattāhato paṭṭhāya – ‘‘parinibbātu dāni, bhante, bhagavā parinibbātu, sugato’’ti viravanto āhiṇḍittha. Ajja dāni paṭṭhāya vigatussāho hohi; mā mayhaṃ parinibbānatthaṃ vāyāmaṃ karohīti vadati.

Appossukko

Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
168. " *Māro pāpimā* ": Here, *māro* means that which leads beings (*satte*) to misfortune (*anatthe*), therefore it is called *māro*. *Pāpimā* is a synonym for that. Because he is endowed with evil qualities (*pāpadhammasamannāgatattā*), he is called "*pāpimā*." *Kaṇho*, *antako*, *namuci*, *pamattabandhū* are also names for him. " *Bhāsitā kho panesā* ": For, in the eighth week after the Blessed One's attainment of perfect awakening (*sambodhipattiyā*), having come to the *bodhimaṇḍa*, he said, "Blessed One, the purpose for which you have fulfilled the perfections (*pāramiyo*) has been attained; that purpose has been reached; the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ*) has been realized, what is the use of considering the world (*lokavicāraṇena*)?" Just as today, in the same way, he requested, "May the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa* now, venerable sir." The Blessed One refused him, saying, "Not yet," and so on. Referring to that, he said, " *Bhāsitā kho panesā bhante*."

There, *viyattā* means skilled due to the path (*maggavasena*). Likewise, *vinītā* and *visāradā*. *Bahussutā* means that much has been heard by them due to the three baskets (*tepiṭakavasena*), therefore they are *bahussutā*. *Dhammadharā* means those who bear that same Dharma (*dhammaṃ dhārentīti*). Or, both learned in theory (*pariyattibahussutā*) and learned in realization (*paṭivedhabahussutā*). *Dhammadharā* means those who hold to both the Dharma of theory and the Dharma of realization (*pariyattipaṭivedhadhammānaṃyeva dhāraṇato dhammadharāti*). Thus, the meaning here should be understood. *Dhammānudhammapaṭipannā* means those who practice the *vipassanādhamma*, which is in accordance with the Dharma (*ariyadhammassa anudhammabhūtaṃ*). *Sāmīcippaṭipannā* means those who practice the appropriate practice (*anucchavikapaṭipadaṃ*). *Anudhammacārino* means those whose habit is to act in accordance with the Dharma (*anudhammacaraṇasīlā*). *Sakaṃ ācariyaka* means one's own teacher's doctrine (*attano ācariyavādaṃ*). *Ācikkhissantī* and so on, all these are synonyms for each other (*aññamaññassa vevacanāni*). *Sahadhammenā* means with reasoned, causal speech (*sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanena*). *Sappāṭihāriya* means until they teach the Dharma after making it lead to liberation (*niyyānikaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desessanti*).

*Viyattā*, *bahussutā*, *bahussutā*, *dhammadharā*, *dhammānudhammapaṭipannā*, *sāmīcippaṭipannā*, *anudhammacārino*, *sakaṃ ācariyaka*, *ācikkhissantī*, *sahadhammenā*, *sappāṭihāriya*. *Brahmacariya* means the entire holy life (*sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ*) included in the three trainings (*sikkhattayasaṅgahitaṃ*). *Iddha* means successful (*samiddhaṃ*) due to the taste of *jhāna* (*jhānassādavasena*). *Phīta* means having attained growth (*vuddhippattaṃ*), like being full of all fruits and flowers (*sabbaphāliphullaṃ viya*), due to the attainment of higher knowledge (*abhiññāya sampattivasena*). *Vitthārika* means expanded (*vitthataṃ*) due to being established in each and every direction (*tasmiṃ tasmiṃ disābhāge patiṭṭhitavasena*). *Bāhujañña* means known and penetrated by many people (*bahujanehi ñātaṃ paṭividdhaṃ*) due to the agreement of the great multitude (*mahājanābhisamayavasena*). *Puthubhūta* means having attained abundant existence (*puthulabhāvappattaṃ*) due to all aspects (*sabbākāravasena*).

How? *Yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita* means the meaning is that it is well proclaimed by all the *devas* and humans (*devā ceva manussā ca*) who are intelligent (*viññujātikā*) to whatever extent they exist (*yattakā atthi*).

*Brahmacariya*, *iddha*, *phīta*, *vitthārika*, *bāhujañña*, *puthubhūta*, *yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita*. *Appossukko* means without longing (*nirālayo*).

Because you, evil one (*pāpima*), from the eighth week onwards, were wandering about, crying out, "May the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa* now, venerable sir; may the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa*, Sugata." Now, from today onwards, be without enthusiasm (*vigatussāho hohi*); do not make an effort for my *parinirvāṇa* (*mā mayhaṃ parinibbānatthaṃ vāyāmaṃ karohi*)," he says.

*Appossukko*. Description of the abandonment of the life-principle (*āyusaṅkhāraossajjanavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
169. Atha kho bhagavā cāpāle cetiye sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji. Ossaṭṭhe ca bhagavatā āyusaṅkhāre mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso lomahaṃso (syā.), devadundubhiyo devadudrabhiyo (ka.) ca phaliṃsu . Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

‘‘Tulamatulañca sambhavaṃ, bhavasaṅkhāramavassaji muni;

Ajjhattarato samāhito, abhindi kavacamivattasambhava’’nti.

Mahābhūmicālahetu
mula_english:
Then, the Blessed One, at the Cāpāla shrine ( *cāpāle cetiye*), mindfully and clearly comprehending, relinquished the life-principle ( *āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji*).

And as the Blessed One relinquished the life-principle ( *āyusaṅkhāre*), there was a great earthquake ( *mahābhūmicālo ahosi*), frightening and hair-raising ( *bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso*), and heavenly drums ( *devadundubhiyo*) cracked.

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, at that time, uttered this solemn utterance ( *udānaṃ udānesi*):

"The balanced and the unbalanced coming into existence, the sage has relinquished the becoming-principle.

Delighting in the internal, composed, he burst the armor of becoming's origin."

The cause of the great earthquake.
commentary_pali:
169.Sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajīti satiṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ katvā ñāṇena paricchinditvā āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissajji, pajahi. Tattha na bhagavā hatthena leḍḍuṃ viya āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, temāsamattameva pana samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā tato paraṃ na samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ uppādesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ossajī’’ti. ‘‘Ussajjī’’ti pi pāṭho. Mahābhūmicāloti mahanto pathavīkampo. Tadā kira dasasahassī lokadhātu kampittha. Bhiṃsanakoti bhayajanako. Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsūti devabheriyo phaliṃsu, devo sukkhagajjitaṃ gajji, akālavijjulatā nicchariṃsu, khaṇikavassaṃ vassīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Udānaṃ udānesīti kasmā udānesi? Koci nāma vadeyya – ‘‘bhagavā pacchato pacchato anubandhitvā – ‘parinibbāyatha, bhante, parinibbāyatha, bhante’ti upadduto bhayena āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissajjesī’’ti. ‘‘Tassokāso mā hotu, bhītassa udānaṃ nāma natthī’’ti etassa dīpanatthaṃ pītivegavissaṭṭhaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

Udānaṃ udānesī

Tattha sabbesaṃ soṇasiṅgālādīnampi paccakkhabhāvato tulitaṃ paricchinnanti tulaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Kāmāvacarakammaṃ. Na tulaṃ, na vā tulaṃ sadisamassa aññaṃ lokiyaṃ kammaṃ atthīti atulaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Mahaggatakammaṃ. Athavā kāmāvacararūpāvacaraṃ tulaṃ, arūpāvacaraṃ atulaṃ. Appavipākaṃ vā tulaṃ, bahuvipākaṃ atulaṃ. Sambhavanti sambhavassa hetubhūtaṃ, piṇḍakārakaṃ rāsikārakanti attho. Bhavasaṅkhāranti punabbhavasaṅkhāraṇakaṃ. Avassajīti vissajjesi. Munīti buddhamuni. Ajjhattaratoti niyakajjhattarato. Samāhitoti upacārappanāsamādhivasena samāhito. Abhindi kavacamivāti kavacaṃ viya abhindi. Attasambhavanti attani sañjātaṃ kilesaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘savipākaṭṭhena sambhavaṃ, bhavābhisaṅkhāraṇaṭṭhena bhavasaṅkhāranti ca laddhanāmaṃ tulātulasaṅkhātaṃ lokiyakammañca ossaji. Saṅgāmasīse mahāyodho kavacaṃ viya attasambhavaṃ kilesañca ajjhattarato samāhito hutvā abhindī’’ti.

atulaṃ. Sambhava Bhavasaṅkhāra Avassajī Munī Ajjhattarato Samāhito Abhindi kavacamivā Attasambhava

Atha vā tulanti tulento tīrento. Atulañca sambhavanti nibbānañceva sambhavañca. Bhavasaṅkhāranti bhavagāmikammaṃ. Avassaji munīti ‘‘pañcakkhandhā aniccā, pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ nirodho nibbānaṃ nicca’’ntiādinā (paṭi. ma. 3.38) nayena tulayanto buddhamuni bhave ādīnavaṃ, nibbāne ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā taṃ khandhānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ bhavasaṅkhārakammaṃ – ‘‘kammakkhayāya saṃvattatī’’ti (ma. ni. 2.81) evaṃ vuttena kammakkhayakarena ariyamaggena avassaji. Kathaṃ? Ajjhattarato samāhito abhindi kavacamiva attani sambhavaṃ. So hi vipassanāvasena ajjhattarato samathavasena samāhitoti evaṃ pubbabhāgato paṭṭhāya samathavipassanābalena kavacamiva attabhāvaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitaṃ, attani sambhavattā ‘‘attasambhava’’nti laddhanāmaṃ sabbakilesajālaṃ abhindi. Kilesābhāvena ca katakammaṃ appaṭisandhikattā avassaṭṭhaṃ nāma hotīti evaṃ kilesappahānena kammaṃ pajahi, pahīnakilesassa ca bhayaṃ nāma natthi, tasmā abhītova āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, abhītabhāvañāpanatthañca udānaṃ udānesīti veditabbo.

tula Atulañca sambhava Bhavasaṅkhāra Avassaji munī

Mahābhūmicālavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
169. "Mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life-force (*āyusaṅkhāra*)" means, having made mindfulness well-established, having discriminated with knowledge, he abandoned and relinquished the life-force.

There, the Blessed One did not relinquish the life-force as if [throwing] a clod of dirt with his hand. But only, having attained meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) for the duration of three months, he produced the thought, "From now on, I will not attain meditative absorption,"

Referring to that, it was said, "He relinquished."

"He let go" is also a reading.

"A great earthquake (*mahābhūmicālo*)" means a great earth tremor (*pathavīkampo*).

Then, it is said, the ten-thousand world-system trembled.

"Frightful (*bhiṃsanako*)" means causing fear (*bhayajanako*).

"And the drums of the gods sounded (*devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsū*)" means the drums of the gods sounded, the god thundered with dry thunder, untimely lightning flashes shot forth, and a momentary rain fell.

"He uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesī*)" Why did he utter an exclamation of joy? Someone might say, "The Blessed One, following behind, harassed [him] saying, 'Attain complete liberation, *bhante*, attain complete liberation, *bhante*,' out of fear, he relinquished the life-force."

"Lest an opportunity occur for him; for a frightened person, there is no exclamation of joy" for the purpose of illuminating this, he uttered an exclamation of joy permeated with the rush of joy.

"He uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesī*)" There, because the state of being perceived by all, including jackals and foxes etc., is weighed and delimited, [it is] weighed (*tulaṃ*).

What is that? Action belonging to the desire realm (*kāmāvacarakammaṃ*).

Because there is no other worldly action (*lokiyaṃ kammaṃ*) similar or equal to it, [it is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

What is that? Action connected with greatness (*mahaggatakammaṃ*).

Or, action belonging to the desire and form realms (*kāmāvacararūpāvacaraṃ*) [is] weighed (*tulaṃ*), action belonging to the formless realm (*arūpāvacaraṃ*) [is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

Or, action with little result (*appavipākaṃ*) [is] weighed (*tulaṃ*), action with great result (*bahuvipākaṃ*) [is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

"Becoming (*sambhava*)" means having as its cause the arising of becoming, meaning the maker of a lump, the maker of a heap.

"The formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāra*)" means the fashioning of renewed existence (*punabbhavasaṅkhāraṇakaṃ*).

"He relinquished (*avassajī*)" means he released (*vissajjesi*).

"A sage (*munī*)" means a Buddha-sage (*buddhamuni*).

"From inner delight (*ajjhattarato*)" means delighting in one's own inner [being] (*niyakajjhattarato*).

"Concentrated (*samāhito*)" means concentrated through the power of approach-attainment-concentration (*upacārappanāsamādhivasena*).

"He broke through as if [breaking] armor (*abhindi kavacamivā*)" means he broke through as if [breaking] armor (*kavacaṃ viya abhindi*).

"Self-originated (*attasambhava*)" means defilement (*kilesaṃ*) born of self (*attani sañjātaṃ*).

This was said: "Because of having the characteristic of result, [it is] becoming (*sambhavaṃ*), and because of having the characteristic of fashioning existence, [it is called] the formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāranti*), these two designations are obtained. Having weighed the well-known weighed and unweighed [actions], he relinquished worldly action (*lokiyakammañca ossaji*).

In the forefront of battle, the great warrior, like [breaking] armor, having become concentrated from inner delight, broke through defilement (*kilesañca*) born of self (*attasambhavaṃ*)."

81) Thus, with the noble path, spoken of as the cause of the destruction of karma, he released (his life-force).

How? Being inwardly delighted, being concentrated, he broke the armor, as it were, of self-existence in himself.

Because he was inwardly delighted through insight (vipassanā), being concentrated through tranquility (samatha), thus, starting from the preliminary stage, by the power of tranquility and insight, having tied his own existence with strength like an armor, he broke all the nets of defilements, which had the name "self-caused" ( *attasambhava* ) because they arose in himself.

And because of the absence of defilements, and because the karma done (by him) no longer led to rebirth, it was released. Thus, through the abandonment of defilements, he abandoned karma, and for one who has abandoned defilements, there is no fear. Therefore, being without fear, he released the life-sustaining force ( *āyusaṅkhāra* ), and this should be understood as having uttered a solemn utterance for the purpose of making known his state of fearlessness.

Measure, immeasurable, and existence, the formations of becoming, released by the sage.

Description of the Great Earthquake.

mula_pali:
170. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, mahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti?

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, mahā vatāyaṃ, bhante, bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ , bhante, bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho, bhante , hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti?
mula_english:
Then, the Venerable Ānanda considered thus: "How amazing! How wondrous! This earthquake is truly great! This earthquake is exceedingly great, frightening, and hair-raising! And the drums of the gods resounded! What could be the cause (hetu) and what the condition (pratyaya) for such a great earthquake (mahāto bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya)?"

Then, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, and after approaching, paying homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Amazing, O Blessed One! Wondrous, O Blessed One! Truly great, O Blessed One, is this earthquake! Exceedingly great, O Blessed One, is this earthquake, frightening, and hair-raising! And the drums of the gods resounded! What, O Blessed One, could be the cause (hetu) and what the condition (pratyaya) for such a great earthquake (mahāto bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya)?"

mula_pali:
171. ‘‘Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Katame aṭṭha? Ayaṃ, ānanda, mahāpathavī udake patiṭṭhitā, udakaṃ vāte patiṭṭhitaṃ, vāto ākāsaṭṭho. Hoti kho so, ānanda, samayo, yaṃ mahāvātā vāyanti. Mahāvātā vāyantā udakaṃ kampenti. Udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo hetu paṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, samaṇo vā hoti brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto, devo vā mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, tassa parittā pathavīsaññā bhāvitā hoti, appamāṇā āposaññā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti saṅkampeti sampakampeti sampavedheti. Ayaṃ dutiyo hetu dutiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto tusitakāyā cavitvā sato sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ tatiyo hetu tatiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto sato sampajāno mātukucchismā nikkhamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ catuttho hetu catuttho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ pañcamo hetu pañcamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho hetu chaṭṭho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajjati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ sattamo hetu sattamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo hetu aṭṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti.

Aṭṭha parisā
mula_english:
171. “Ānanda, there are these eight reasons, eight causes, for the appearance of a great earthquake.

Which are the eight? This great earth, Ānanda, is established on water, the water is established on wind, and the wind is standing on space.

There comes a time, Ānanda, when great winds blow.

The great winds blowing shake the water.

The water, shaken, shakes the earth.

This is the first reason, the first cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when an ascetic or a Brahmin who has psychic powers and has mastered his mind, or a powerful and mighty deva, develops a limited earth-perception and an immeasurable water-perception,

he makes this earth tremble, quiver, shake, and quake.

This is the second reason, the second cause for the arising of mighty earthquakes.

“Again, Ānanda, when a Bodhisattva departs from the Tusita heaven, mindfully and clearly aware, and descends into his mother’s womb, then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the third reason, the third cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva, mindful and clearly aware, emerges from his mother’s womb, then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the fourth reason, the fourth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the fifth reason, the fifth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata sets in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dharma (anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the sixth reason, the sixth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata, mindful and clearly aware, relinquishes the life-principle (āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajjati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the seventh reason, the seventh cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata attains complete extinction in the *Nirvana*-element without remainder (anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the eighth reason, the eighth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

These, Ānanda, are the eight reasons, the eight causes for the occurrence of a great earthquake.”

Eight Assemblies
commentary_pali:
171.Yaṃ mahāvātāti yena samayena yasmiṃ vā samaye mahāvātā vāyanti, mahāvātā vāyantāpi ukkhepakavātā nāma uṭṭhahanti, te vāyantā saṭṭhisahassādhikanavayojanasatasahassabahalaṃ udakasandhārakaṃ vātaṃ upacchindanti, tato ākāse udakaṃ bhassati, tasmiṃ bhassante pathavī bhassati. Puna vāto attano balena antodhamakaraṇe viya udakaṃ ābandhitvā gaṇhāti, tato udakaṃ uggacchati, tasmiṃ uggacchante pathavī uggacchati. Evaṃ udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti. Etañca kampanaṃ yāva ajjakālāpi hotiyeva, bahalabhāvena pana na ogacchanuggacchanaṃ paññāyati.

Mahiddhiko mahānubhāvoti ijjhanassa mahantatāya mahiddhiko, anubhavitabbassa mahantatāya mahānubhāvo. Parittāti dubbalā. Appamāṇāti balavā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetīti so iddhiṃ nibbattetvā saṃvejento mahāmoggallāno viya, vīmaṃsanto vā mahānāgattherassa bhāgineyyo saṅgharakkhitasāmaṇero viya pathaviṃ kampeti. So kirāyasmā khuraggeyeva arahattaṃ patvā cintesi – ‘‘atthi nu kho koci bhikkhu, yena pabbajitadivaseyeva arahattaṃ patvā vejayanto pāsādo kampitapubbo’’ti? Tato – ‘‘natthi kocī’’ti ñatvā – ‘‘ahaṃ kampessāmī’’ti abhiññābalena vejayantamatthake ṭhatvā pādena paharitvā kampetuṃ nāsakkhi. Atha naṃ sakkassa nāṭakitthiyo āhaṃsu – ‘‘putta saṅgharakkhita, tvaṃ pūtigandheneva sīsena vejayantaṃ kampetuṃ icchasi, suppatiṭṭhito tāta pāsādo, kathaṃ kampetuṃ sakkhissasī’’ti?

Mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo Parittā Appamāṇā So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī

Sāmaṇero – ‘‘imā devatā mayā saddhiṃ keḷiṃ karonti, ahaṃ kho pana ācariyaṃ nālatthaṃ, kahaṃ nu kho me ācariyo sāmuddikamahānāgatthero’’ti āvajjento mahāsamudde udakaleṇaṃ māpetvā divāvihāraṃ nisinnoti ñatvā tattha gantvā theraṃ vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. Tato naṃ thero – ‘‘kiṃ, tāta saṅgharakkhita, asikkhitvāva yuddhaṃ paviṭṭhosī’’ti vatvā ‘‘nāsakkhi, tāta, vejayantaṃ kampetu’’nti pucchi. Ācariyaṃ, bhante, nālatthanti. Atha naṃ thero – ‘‘tāta tumhādise akampente ko añño kampessati. Diṭṭhapubbaṃ te, tāta, udakapiṭṭhe gomayakhaṇḍaṃ pilavantaṃ, tāta, kapallakapūvaṃ pacantā antantena paricchindanti, iminā opammena jānāhī’’ti āha. So – ‘‘vaṭṭissati, bhante, ettakenā’’ti vatvā pāsādena patiṭṭhitokāsaṃ udakaṃ hotūti adhiṭṭhāya vejayantābhimukho agamāsi.

Devadhītaro taṃ disvā – ‘‘ekavāraṃ lajjitvā gato, punapi sāmaṇero eti, punapi etī’’ti vadiṃsu. Sakko devarājā – ‘‘mā mayhaṃ puttena saddhiṃ kathayittha, idāni tena ācariyo laddho, khaṇena pāsādaṃ kampessatī’’ti āha. Sāmaṇeropi pādaṅguṭṭhena pāsādathūpikaṃ pahari. Pāsādo catūhi disāhi oṇamati. Devatā – ‘‘patiṭṭhātuṃ dehi, tāta, pāsādassa patiṭṭhātuṃ dehi, tāta, pāsādassā’’ti viraviṃsu. Sāmaṇero pāsādaṃ yathāṭhāne ṭhapetvā pāsādamatthake ṭhatvā udānaṃ udānesi –

‘‘Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito, ajja pattāsavakkhayaṃ;

Ajja kampemi pāsādaṃ, aho buddhassuḷāratā.

Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito…pe… aho dhammassuḷāratā.

Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito…pe… aho saṅghassuḷāratāti.

Ito paresu chasu pathavīkampesu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāpadāne vuttameva.

Iti imesu aṭṭhasu pathavīkampesu paṭhamo dhātukopena, dutiyo iddhānubhāvena, tatiyacatutthā puññatejena, pañcamo ñāṇatejena, chaṭṭho sādhukāradānavasena, sattamo kāruññabhāvena, aṭṭhamo ārodanena. Mātukucchiṃ okkamante ca tato nikkhamante ca mahāsatte tassa puññatejena pathavī akampittha. Abhisambodhiyaṃ ñāṇatejena abhihatā hutvā akampittha. Dhammacakkappavattane sādhukārabhāvasaṇṭhitā sādhukāraṃ dadamānā akampittha. Āyusaṅkhārossajjane kāruññasabhāvasaṇṭhitā cittasaṅkhobhaṃ asahamānā akampittha. Parinibbāne ārodanavegatunnā hutvā akampittha. Ayaṃ panattho pathavīdevatāya vasena veditabbo, mahābhūtapathaviyā panetaṃ natthi acetanattāti.

Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetūti ettha imeti niddiṭṭhanidassanaṃ. Ettāvatā ca panāyasmā ānando – ‘‘addhā ajja bhagavatā āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho’’ti sallakkhesi. Bhagavā pana sallakkhitabhāvaṃ jānantopi okāsaṃ adatvāva aññānipi aṭṭhakāni sampiṇḍento – ‘‘aṭṭha kho imā’’tiādimāha.

commentary_english:
171. **yaṃ mahāvātā**ti: At whatever time, or at which time, great winds blow, and when those great winds are blowing, winds called "lifting winds" arise, these blowing winds cut through the wind that holds the water, which is sixty-nine million yojanas thick. Then, water pours down in the sky, and as it pours down, the earth pours down. Furthermore, the wind, by its own power, like in the case of inward blowing, binds the water and takes it. Then, the water rises up, and as that water rises up, the earth rises up. Thus, the water, shaken, shakes the earth. (udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti.) And this shaking continues even until today. However, due to its thickness, the sinking and rising are not apparent. **mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo**ti: *Mahiddhiko* because of the greatness of his power, *mahānubhāvo* because of the greatness of what is to be experienced. **parittā**ti: [They are] weak. **appamāṇā**ti: [They are] powerful. **so imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī**ti: He, having created power and causing agitation, like the great Maudgalyāyana, or investigating, like Saṅgharakkhitasāmaṇera, the nephew of Mahānāgatthera, shakes the earth. It is said that venerable Khuragga, having attained arhatship right on the edge of a razor, thought: "Is there any monk by whom, on the very day of his ordination, having attained arhatship, the Vejayanta palace has been shaken before?" Then, knowing that there was none, and thinking, "I will shake it," he stood at the top of the Vejayanta [palace] with the power of his higher knowledge, and struck it with his foot, but was not able to shake it. Then, the celestial courtesans of Śakra said to him: "O son Saṅgharakkhita, you wish to shake the Vejayanta [palace] with a head like a foul smell? The palace is well-established, dear one. How will you be able to shake it?" **mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo parittā appamāṇā so imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī** The novice: "These deities are playing with me. But I have not found a teacher. Where might my teacher, Sāmuddikamahānāgatthera, be?" Reflecting, he realized that [his teacher] had fashioned a water cave in the great ocean and was dwelling there during the day. Knowing this, he went there, paid homage to the elder, and stood [before him]. Then, the elder [said] to him: "Why, dear Saṅgharakkhita, have you entered the battle without training?" And he asked, "Were you able to shake the Vejayanta [palace], dear one?" "Venerable sir, I have not found a teacher." Then, the elder [said] to him: "Dear one, who else will shake [it] if those like you do not shake it? Have you ever seen, dear one, a piece of cow dung floating on the surface of the water, or those who are cooking cakes covering [the water] all around? Understand with this simile." He said: "It will suffice, venerable sir, with this much." Having said this, he resolved, "Let there be water in the place where the palace is established!" and went towards the Vejayanta [palace]. The daughters of the gods, seeing him, said: "Having been ashamed once, he has gone, and again the novice comes, again he comes!" Śakra, the lord of gods, [thought]: "Do not speak with my son! Now, he has found a teacher, and in a moment he will shake the palace!" The novice then struck the pinnacle of the palace with his big toe. The palace bends in the four directions. The deities cried out: "Give a foundation, dear one, to the palace! Give a foundation, dear one, to the palace!" The novice, having placed the palace in its proper place, standing on the top of the palace, uttered a solemn utterance: "Today itself I was ordained; today I attained the destruction of the influxes; Today I shake the palace; Hail to the magnificence of the Buddha!" "Today itself I was ordained…pe… Hail to the magnificence of the Dharma!" "Today itself I was ordained…pe… Hail to the magnificence of the Saṅgha!" Henceforth, what is to be said about the remaining six earth-shakings has already been said in the *Mahāpadāna*. Thus, in these eight earth-shakings, the first is due to disturbance of the elements (dhātukopena), the second due to the power of psychic abilities (iddhānubhāvena), the third and fourth due to the power of merit (puññatejena), the fifth due to the power of knowledge (ñāṇatejena), the sixth due to the giving of approval and offerings (sādhukāradānavasena), the seventh due to compassion (kāruññabhāvena), [and] the eighth due to lamentation (ārodanena). When the great being entered the mother's womb, and when he came out from there, due to the power of his merit, the earth shook. Having been struck by the power of knowledge at complete awakening, it shook. At the turning of the wheel of Dharma, established in the state of giving approval, giving approval, it shook. At the abandoning of the life force, established in a state of compassion, not enduring mental agitation, it shook. Having become agitated and spurred on by the force of lamentation at the *parinirvāṇa*, he did not tremble. However, this meaning should be understood in terms of the *pathavīdevatā* (earth deity), because this does not exist in the great elemental earth, due to its being inanimate.

"These, Ānanda, are the eight causes," here, "these" indicates a specification and example. Furthermore, the venerable Ānanda considered, "Indeed, today the Blessed One has relinquished the life-principle." Although the Blessed One knew the state of having been considered thus, without giving an opportunity, while combining other *aṭṭhakas* (groups of eight), he spoke, beginning with, "These are the eight."

These, Ānanda, are the eight causes. These

Explanation of the Eight Assemblies

mula_pali:
172. ‘‘Aṭṭha kho imā, ānanda, parisā. Katamā aṭṭha? Khattiyaparisā, brāhmaṇaparisā, gahapatiparisā, samaṇaparisā, cātumahārājikaparisā cātummahārājikaparisā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), tāvatiṃsaparisā, māraparisā, brahmaparisā. Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda , anekasataṃ khattiyaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā . Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisaṃ…pe… gahapatiparisaṃ… samaṇaparisaṃ… cātumahārājikaparisaṃ… tāvatiṃsaparisaṃ… māraparisaṃ… brahmaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā. Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Imā kho, ānanda, aṭṭha parisā.

Aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni
mula_english:
172. “Ānanda, there are these eight assemblies. What are the eight? They are the assembly of nobles ( *khattiyaparisā*), the assembly of Brahmins (*brāhmaṇaparisā*), the assembly of householders (*gahapatiparisā*), the assembly of ascetics (*samaṇaparisā*), the assembly of the Four Great Kings (*cātumahārājikaparisā*), the assembly of the Thirty-Three Gods (*tāvatiṃsaparisā*), the assembly of Māras (*māraparisā*), and the assembly of Brahmās (*brahmaparisā*).

I remember well, Ānanda, many hundreds of assemblies of nobles that I have approached. There, before seating myself, before talking, before engaging in conversation, whatever their appearance (*vaṇṇa*) was, my appearance would become. Whatever their voice (*sara*) was, my voice would become. I instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with Dhamma talk.

While I was speaking, they didn’t know me: ‘Who is this who speaks—a *deva* or a *manussa*?’ Having instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with *Dhamma* talk, I disappeared. And still they did not know: “He who has just disappeared — was he a *deva* or a *manussa*?”

I remember well, Ānanda, many hundreds of assemblies of Brahmins… of householders… of ascetics… of the Four Great Kings… of the Thirty-three Gods… of *Māras*… of *Brahmās* that I have approached. There, before seating myself, before talking, before engaging in conversation, whatever their appearance (*vaṇṇa*) was, my appearance would become. Whatever their voice (*sara*) was, my voice would become. I instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with *Dhamma* talk.

While I was speaking, they didn’t know me: ‘Who is this who speaks—a *deva* or a *manussa*?’ Having instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with Dhamma talk, I disappeared. And still they did not know: “He who has just disappeared — was he a *deva* or a *manussa*?” These, Ānanda, are the eight assemblies.

The eight sources of superiority (*aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni*).
commentary_pali:
172. Tattha anekasataṃ khattiyaparisanti bimbisārasamāgamañātisamāgalicchavīsamāgamādisadisaṃ, sā pana aññesu cakkavāḷesupi labbhateyeva. Sallapitapubbanti ālāpasallāpo katapubbo. Sākacchāti dhammasākacchāpi samāpajjitapubbā. Yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇoti te odātāpi honti kāḷāpi maṅguracchavīpi, satthā suvaṇṇavaṇṇova. Idaṃ pana saṇṭhānaṃ paṭicca kathitaṃ. Saṇṭhānampi ca kevalaṃ tesaṃ paññāyatiyeva, na pana bhagavā milakkhusadiso hoti, nāpi āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalo, buddhaveseneva nisīdati. Te pana attano samānasaṇṭhānameva passanti. Yādisako tesaṃ saroti te chinnassarāpi honti gaggarassarāpi kākassarāpi, satthā brahmassarova. Idaṃ pana bhāsantaraṃ sandhāya kathitaṃ. Sacepi hi satthā rājāsane nisinno katheti, ‘‘ajja rājā madhurena sarena kathetī’’ti tesaṃ hoti. Kathetvā pakkante pana bhagavati puna rājānaṃ āgataṃ disvā – ‘‘ko nu kho aya’’nti vīmaṃsā uppajjati. Tattha ko nu kho ayanti imasmiṃ ṭhāne idāneva māgadhabhāsāya sīhaḷabhāsāya madhurenākārena kathento ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito, kiṃ devo, udāhu manussoti evaṃ vīmaṃsantāpi na jānantīti attho. Kimatthaṃ panevaṃ ajānantānaṃ dhammaṃ desetīti? Vāsanatthāya . Evaṃ sutopi hi dhammo anāgate paccayo hoti yevāti anāgataṃ paṭicca deseti. Anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisantiādīnampi soṇadaṇḍakūṭadaṇḍasamāgamādivasena ceva aññacakkavāḷavasena ca sambhavo veditabbo.

Imā pana aṭṭha parisā bhagavā kimatthaṃ āhari? Abhītabhāvadassanatthameva. Imā kira āharitvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, imāpi aṭṭha parisā upasaṅkamitvā dhammaṃ desentassa tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi, māraṃ pana ekakaṃ disvā tathāgato bhāyeyyāti ko evaṃ saññaṃ uppādetumarahati. Abhīto, ānanda, tathāgato acchambhī, sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’ti.

Aṭṭhaabhibhāyatanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
172. There, namely, "[There was] a gathering of many hundreds of *kṣatriyas*," like the gathering of Bimbisāra, a gathering of relatives, a gathering of Licchavis, and so on. But that is obtained in other world systems as well.

"[They] have spoken before" means speech, conversation, has been done before.

"*Sākacchā*" means there have been previous discussions about the *dharma*.

"*Yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo*," as to what was their complexion: they can be white, black, or the color of *maṅgura*, but the Teacher's color is like gold.

This was said with reference to the body.

And indeed, it is only their body that is apparent; the Blessed One is not like a barbarian, nor does he sit wearing jeweled earrings; he sits only in the manner of a Buddha.

But they see only their own similar form.

"*Yādisako tesaṃ saro*," as to what was their voice: they can have broken voices, hoarse voices, or crow-like voices, but the Teacher's voice is like Brahma's.

This was said with reference to a different language.

Even if the Teacher, seated on the royal seat, should speak, they think, "Today the king speaks with a sweet voice."

Having spoken, when the Blessed One had departed, seeing the king come again, the thought arises, "Who now, pray, is this?"

There, "*ko nu kho aya*," in this place, just now, speaking in the Magadhi language, in the Sinhala language, with a sweet manner, who now, pray, is this who has disappeared? Is it a god, or a human?—even while pondering thus, they do not know the meaning.

Why then does he teach the Dharma to those who do not know? For the sake of habituation.

Even the Dharma that has been heard in this way becomes a condition in the future. He teaches having regard to the future.

"*Anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisa*," [there was] a gathering of many hundreds of *brāhmaṇas*, and so on, and also the arising based on the assembly of Soṇadaṇḍa, Kūṭadaṇḍa, and so on, and also based on another world system, should be understood.

Why did the Blessed One bring forward these eight assemblies? Just for the sake of showing the state of being fearless.

It is said that having brought these forward, he spoke thus: "Ānanda, even these eight assemblies, having approached and listened to the Tathāgata teaching the Dharma, there is no fear or hesitation for the Tathāgata. Who is capable of producing the thought that the Tathāgata would be afraid at seeing Māra alone?

Fearless, Ānanda, is the Tathāgata, without trembling, mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life force."

Explanation of the eight abhibhāyatana.

mula_pali:
173. ‘‘Aṭṭha kho imāni, ānanda, abhibhāyatanāni. Katamāni aṭṭha ? Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ odātaṃ odātavaṇṇaṃ odātanidassanaṃ odātanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ . Imāni kho, ānanda, aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni.

Aṭṭha vimokkhā
mula_english:
173. These, Ānanda, are the eight dimensions of mastery. What are the eight?

Perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are limited, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the first dimension of mastery.

Perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are immeasurable, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the second dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are limited, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the third dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are immeasurable, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, of blue colour, of blue lustre. Just as a flax-flower is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, of blue colour, of blue lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are yellow, of yellow colour, of yellow lustre. Just as a *kaṇikāra*-flower is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are yellow, of yellow colour, of yellow lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are red, of red colour, of red lustre. Just as a *bandhujīvaka*-flower is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are red, of red colour, of red lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’
This is the seventh means of mastery.

“Not perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are white, of white colour, of white lustre, white in radiance.

Just as the morning star is white, of white colour, white in appearance, with white luminosity, or like fine Benares muslin which, burnished on both sides, is white, white in color, of a white luster.

So not perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are white, of white colour, of white lustre, white in radiance, and mastering these, one is aware that one knows and sees them.

This is the eighth means of mastery.

These, Ānanda, are the eight means of mastery.

Eight liberations.
commentary_pali:
173.Abhibhāyatanānīti abhibhavanakāraṇāni. Kiṃ abhibhavanti? Paccanīkadhammepi ārammaṇānipi. Tāni hi paṭipakkhabhāvena paccanīkadhamme abhibhavanti, puggalassa ñāṇuttariyatāya ārammaṇāni.

Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññītiādīsu pana ajjhattarūpe parikammavasena ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī nāma hoti. Ajjhattañhi nīlaparikammaṃ karonto kese vā pitte vā akkhitārakāya vā karoti. Pītaparikammaṃ karonto mede vā chaviyā vā hatthapādapiṭṭhesu vā akkhīnaṃ pītakaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Lohitaparikammaṃ karonto maṃse vā lohite vā jivhāya vā akkhīnaṃ rattaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Odātaparikammaṃ karonto aṭṭhimhi vā dante vā nakhe vā akkhīnaṃ setaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Taṃ pana sunīlaṃ supītaṃ sulohitakaṃ suodātakaṃ na hoti, avisuddhameva hoti.

Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatīti yassevaṃ parikammaṃ ajjhattaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, nimittaṃ pana bahiddhā, so evaṃ ajjhattaṃ parikammassa bahiddhā ca appanāya vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. Parittānīti avaḍḍhitāni. Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānīti suvaṇṇāni vā honti, dubbaṇṇāni vā. Parittavaseneva idaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tāni abhibhuyyāti yathā nāma sampannagahaṇiko kaṭacchumattaṃ bhattaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘kiṃ ettha bhuñjitabbaṃ atthī’’ti saṅkaḍḍhitvā ekakabaḷameva karoti, evameva ñāṇuttariko puggalo visadañāṇo – ‘‘kiṃ ettha parittake ārammaṇe samāpajjitabbaṃ atthi, nāyaṃ mama bhāro’’ti tāni rūpāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho. Jānāmipassāmīti iminā panassa ābhogo kathito. So ca kho samāpattito vuṭṭhitassa, na antosamāpattiyaṃ. Evaṃsaññī hotīti ābhogasaññāyapi jhānasaññāyapi evaṃsaññī hoti. Abhibhavanasaññā hissa antosamāpattiyampi atthi, ābhogasaññā pana samāpattito vuṭṭhitasseva.

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī Parittānī Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī Tāni abhibhuyyā Jānāmi passāmī Evaṃsaññī hotī

Appamāṇānīti vaḍḍhitappamāṇāni, mahantānīti attho. Abhibhuyyāti ettha pana yathā mahagghaso puriso ekaṃ bhattavaḍḍhitakaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘aññampi hotu, kiṃ etaṃ mayhaṃ karissatī’’ti taṃ na mahantato passati, evameva ñāṇuttaro puggalo visadañāṇo ‘‘kiṃ ettha samāpajjitabbaṃ, nayidaṃ appamāṇaṃ, na mayhaṃ cittekaggatākaraṇe bhāro atthī’’ti tāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho.

Appamāṇānī Abhibhuyyā

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññīti alābhitāya vā anatthikatāya vā ajjhattarūpe parikammasaññāvirahito.

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatīti yassa parikammampi nimittampi bahiddhāva uppannaṃ, so evaṃ bahiddhā parikammassa ceva appanāya ca vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. Sesamettha catutthābhibhāyatane vuttanayameva. Imesu pana catūsu parittaṃ vitakkacaritavasena āgataṃ, appamāṇaṃ mohacaritavasena, suvaṇṇaṃ dosacaritavasena, dubbaṇṇaṃ rāgacaritavasena. Etesañhi etāni sappāyāni. Sā ca nesaṃ sappāyatā vitthārato visuddhimagge caritaniddese vuttā.

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī

Pañcamaabhibhāyatanādīsu nīlānīti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ. Nīlavaṇṇānīti vaṇṇavasena. Nīlanidassanānīti nidassanavasena, apaññāya mānavivarāni asambhinnavaṇṇāni ekanīlāneva hutvā dissantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Nīlanibhāsānīti idaṃ pana obhāsavasena vuttaṃ, nīlobhāsāni nīlappabhāyuttānīti attho. Etena nesaṃ visuddhataṃ dasseti. Visuddhavaṇṇavaseneva hi imāni cattāri abhibhāyatanāni vuttāni. Umāpupphanti etañhi pupphaṃ siniddhaṃ mudu, dissamānampi nīlameva hoti. Girikaṇṇikapupphādīni pana dissamānāni setadhātukāneva honti. Tasmā idameva gahitaṃ, na tāni. Bārāṇaseyyakanti bārāṇasisambhavaṃ. Tattha kira kappāsopi mudu, suttakantikāyopi tantavāyāpi chekā, udakampi suci siniddhaṃ. Tasmā taṃ vatthaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ hoti; dvīsupi passesu maṭṭhaṃ mudu siniddhaṃ khāyati.

nīlānī Nīlavaṇṇānī Nīlanidassanānī Nīlanibhāsānī Umāpuppha Bārāṇaseyyaka

Pītānītiādīsupi imināva nayena attho veditabbo. ‘‘Nīlakasiṇaṃ uggaṇhanto nīlasmiṃ nimittaṃ gaṇhāti pupphasmiṃ vā vatthasmiṃ vā vaṇṇadhātuyā vā’’tiādikaṃ panettha kasiṇakaraṇañca parikammañca appanāvidhānañca sabbaṃ visuddhimagge vitthārato vuttameva. Imānipi aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni abhītabhāvadassanatthameva ānītāni. Imāni kira vatvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, evarūpāpi samāpattiyo samāpajjantassa ca vuṭṭhahantassa ca tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi, māraṃ pana ekakaṃ disvā tathāgato bhāyeyyāti ko evaṃ saññaṃ uppādetumarahati. Abhīto, ānanda, tathāgato acchambhī, sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’ti.

Pītānī

Aṭṭhavimokkhavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
173. *Abhibhāyatanānī* means the causes of overcoming.

What do they overcome? They overcome opposing qualities and objects.

They overcome opposing qualities by means of being on the opposing side, [and they overcome] objects by means of the excellence of a person's knowledge.

*Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī* etc., [means:] Moreover, *ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī* is what someone is called when internal form is the means of preliminary work.

When doing preliminary work on internal [form], he makes [it] hair, bile, or the pupil of the eye.

When doing preliminary work on yellow [form], he makes [it] fat, skin, the soles of the hands and feet, or the yellow place of the eyes.

When doing preliminary work on red [form], he makes [it] flesh, blood, the tongue, or the red place of the eyes.

When doing preliminary work on white [form], he makes [it] bones, teeth, nails, or the white place of the eyes.

But that is not very blue, very yellow, very red, [or] very white; it is just impure.

*Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī* means, for whomever the preliminary work has arisen internally and the sign is external, in that way, because of the preliminary work being internal and the application being external, it is said, "ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī."

*Parittānī* means undeveloped.

*Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī* means they are either beautiful or ugly.

This *abhibhāyatana* is to be understood as having been spoken of only by way of being limited.

*Tāni abhibhuyyā* means, just as a rich householder, having obtained a ladleful of food, thinks, "What is there to eat here?" and gathers [it] up and makes [it] just one mouthful; even so, a person of superior knowledge, with clear knowledge . . . , thinks, "What is there to attain here in [this] limited object? This is not my burden." Overcoming those forms, he attains [absorption]. The meaning is that he brings the application about together with the arising of the sign.

*Jānāmi passāmī* means that with this, its expanse is spoken of.

And that is for one who has arisen from attainment, not during the attainment.

*Evaṃsaññī hotī* means he is evaṃsaññī even with regard to the perception of expanse and with regard to the perception of *jhāna*.

The perception of overcoming exists for him even during the attainment, but the perception of expanse exists only for one who has arisen from the attainment.

*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī parittānī suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī tāni abhibhuyyā*

*Jānāmi passāmī evaṃsaññī hotī*

*Appamāṇānī* means of increased measure; the meaning is, they are great.

*Abhibhuyyā* means, here, just as a very hungry person, having obtained one portion of food, does not see that it is very large, [thinking,] "Let there be something else; what will this do for me?" Even so, a person of superior knowledge, with clear knowledge, [thinking,] "What is there to attain here? This is not unlimited. There is no burden for me in making concentration of mind," overcoming those, he attains [absorption]. The meaning is that he brings the application about together with the arising of the sign.

*Appamāṇānī abhibhuyyā*

*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī* means he is without the perception of preliminary work on internal form because of not obtaining or because of uselessness.

*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī* means, for whomever the preliminary work and the sign have arisen externally, in that way, because of the preliminary work and the application being external, it is said, "ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī."

The remainder here is just in the manner stated in the fourth *abhibhāyatana*.

Moreover, in these four, the limited comes by way of the disposition of one given to discursive thinking, the unlimited by way of the disposition of one given to delusion, the beautiful by way of the disposition of one given to aversion, [and] the ugly by way of the disposition of one given to passion.

For these, these are suitable.

And their suitability is stated in detail in the chapter on the conduct in the *Visuddhimagga*.

*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī*

In the fifth *abhibhāyatana* etc., *nīlānī* is stated by way of including everything.

*Nīlavaṇṇānī* is by way of color.

*Nīlanidassanānī* is by way of appearance; it is said that the holes in the māna, without wisdom, with unmixed colors, appear as just one blue.

*Nīlanibhāsānī* means that this is stated by way of light; the meaning is, they are blue lights, connected with blue radiance.

By this, he shows their purity.

Indeed, these four *abhibhāyatanas* are stated only by way of pure color.
*umāpuppha* means that this flower is smooth and soft; even when seen, it is only blue.

Girikaṇṇika flowers, etc., however, when seen, are only white in substance.

Therefore, only this is taken, not those.

*bārāṇaseyyaka* means originating in Vārāṇasī.

There, it is said that even the cotton is soft, and the spinners and weavers are skilled, and the water is pure and smooth.

Therefore, that cloth is polished on both sides; on both sides it appears polished, soft, and smooth.

*nīlānī*, *nīlavaṇṇānī*, *nīlanidassanānī*, *nīlanibhāsānī* *umāpuppha* *bārāṇaseyyaka*

*pītānī*, etc., in these also, the meaning should be understood in this way.

"When acquiring the blue *kasiṇa*, he takes the mark in the blue, whether in a flower or in a cloth or in the element of color," etc., here, the making of the *kasiṇa*, the preliminary work, the establishment of the *appanā*, and everything is already extensively stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

These eight sources of superiority (*abhibhāyatana*) have also been brought only for the purpose of showing the state of fearlessness (*abhītabhāva*).

Having said these things, he said thus: "Ānanda, even for the Tathāgata who enters into such attainments (*samāpatti*) and emerges from them, there is no fear or hesitation. Who would think of producing such a notion that the Tathāgata would be afraid upon seeing Māra alone?

Fearless, Ānanda, is the Tathāgata, without trembling, mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life force (*āyusaṅkhāra*)."

*pītānī* Explanation of the Eight Deliverances (*aṭṭhavimokkha*)

mula_pali: 174. ‘‘Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, vimokkhā. Katame aṭṭha? Rūpī rūpāni passati, ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho. Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati, ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho. Subhanteva adhimutto hoti, ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha vimokkhā.
mula_english:
“Now there are eight liberations, Ānanda.

What are the eight? Possessing form, one sees forms. That is the first liberation (*prathamo vimokkho*).

Not percipient of form internally, one sees forms externally. This is the second liberation (*dutiyo vimokkho*).

Experiencing loveliness, one is intent upon it; this is the third liberation (*tatiyo vimokkho*).

Through the complete surmounting of perceptions of material form, the passing away of perceptions of impingement, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity, ‘Space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of space. This is the fourth liberation (*catuttho vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Infinite Space, thinking: “Consciousness is infinite”, one enters and abides in the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness. That is the fifth liberation (*pañcamo vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, thinking: “There is no thing”, one enters and abides in the Sphere of NoThingness. That is the sixth liberation (*chaṭṭho vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of No-Thing- ness, one reaches and abides in the Sphere of Neither-Percep- tion-Nor-Non-Perception. That is the seventh liberation (*sattamo vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception, one enters and abides in the Cessation of Perception and Feeling. That is the eighth liberation (*aṭṭhamo vimokkho*).

These, Ānanda, are the eight liberations (*aṭṭha vimokkhā*).
commentary_pali: 174. Vimokkhakathā uttānatthāyeva. Imepi aṭṭha vimokkhā abhītabhāvadassanatthameva ānītā. Imepi kira vatvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, etāpi samāpattiyo samāpajjantassa ca vuṭṭhahantassa ca tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi…pe… ossajī’’ti.
commentary_english:
174. The discourse on liberation is clear in meaning.

These eight liberations are also brought forth to show the state of fearlessness.

Having said this, he said thus: "Ānanda, for the Tathāgata, even when entering into and emerging from these attainments ( *samāpatti*), there is no fear or timidity... pe... I relinquish."

mula_pali:
175. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ , ānanda, samayaṃ uruvelāyaṃ viharāmi najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā; parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti. Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ –

‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti.
mula_english:
175. “One time, Ānanda, I was staying at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River at the Goat-herd Banyan, newly awakened. Then Māra, the Evil One, approached me and, on arrival, stood to one side. Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One, said this to me: ‘Now is the time for the Blessed Lord’s final Nirvāṇa, O venerable one; may the Well-Gone One be completely liberated! Now is the time for the Blessed Lord’s Parinirvāṇa, O venerable one!’

“When this was said, I, Ānanda, said this to Māra the Evil One: ‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my monks become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my nuns become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my male lay followers become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.’

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my female lay followers become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.’

“‘Evil One, I will not attain *parinirvāṇa* until this holy life of mine is powerful, prosperous, widely spread, disseminated among many people, and well-expounded as far as there are gods and humans.’”
commentary_pali: 175. Idānipi bhagavā ānandassa okāsaṃ adatvāva ekamidāhantiādinā nayena aparampi desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha paṭhamābhisambuddhoti abhisambuddho hutvā paṭhamameva aṭṭhame sattāhe.
commentary_english:
Now, without giving Ānanda an opportunity, the Blessed One began another teaching in the manner of "He spoke one thing" (ekamidāha).

There, *first fully awakened* (paṭhamābhisambuddho) means having become fully awakened, in the first week, in the eighth week.

mula_pali: 176. ‘‘Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato. Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima , parinibbāyissāmi , yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’’nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti.
mula_english:
176. Just now, Ānanda, today at the Cāpāla Shrine, Māra the Evil One approached me, and having approached, stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Ānanda, Māra the Evil One said this to me: ‘Now, venerable sir, let the Blessed One attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāna); let the Well-Gone One attain final **Nirvāṇa**; now is the time for the Blessed One's final **Nirvāṇa**.’

But these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Evil One, I will not attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāyissāmi) until my monks are not yet disciples …pe… until my nuns are not yet disciples …pe… until my male lay followers are not yet disciples …pe… until my female lay followers are not yet disciples …pe… until this holy life (**brahmacariya**) is not powerful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.’

But now, venerable sir, the Blessed One's holy life (**brahmacariyaṃ**) is powerful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.

Now, venerable sir, let the Blessed One attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāna); let the Well-Gone One attain final **Nirvāṇa**; now is the time for the Blessed One's final **Nirvāṇa**.’

mula_pali:
177. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, naciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye tathāgatena satena sampajānena āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho’’ti.

Ānandayācanakathā
mula_english:
“When this was said, I, Ānanda, spoke thus to Māra, the Evil One: ‘Be without worry, Evil One. Before long, the final passing away (parinirvāṇa) of the Tathāgata will occur. In three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain parinirvāṇa.’ And just now, Ānanda, here at the Cāpāla shrine, the Tathāgata, mindful and fully aware, has relinquished the life principle (āyusaṅkhāra).”

The Account of Ānanda's Entreaty
commentary_pali:
177.Ossaṭṭhoti vissajjito paricchinno, evaṃ kira vatvā – ‘‘tenāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu kampitthā’’ti āha.

Ānandayācanakathā
commentary_english:
177. *Ossaṭṭho* means released, distinguished. Thus, it is said, “Then this ten-thousandfold world system trembled.”

The Story of Ānanda's Request

mula_pali:
178. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.

‘‘Alaṃdāni, ānanda. Mā tathāgataṃ yāci, akālodāni, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yācanāyā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando…pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.

‘‘Saddahasi tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa bodhi’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Atha kiñcarahi tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāvatatiyakaṃ abhinippīḷesī’’ti? ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā. So ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’’’ti. ‘‘Saddahasi tvaṃ, ānandā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ tathāgatena evaṃ oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
mula_english:
178. Thus, when this was said, Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One remain for an eon ( *kappa*), O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!”

“Enough, Ānanda. Do not beg the *Tathāgata*. It is not the right time, Ānanda, for begging the *Tathāgata*.”

A second time... A third time, Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One remain for an eon, O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!”

“Ānanda, do you have faith in the *Tathāgata*'s enlightenment (*bodhi*)?” “Yes, venerable one.”

“Then why, Ānanda, did you press the *Tathāgata* so much, even up to the third time?” “Venerable sir, I have heard and learned directly from the Blessed One: ‘Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of power (*iddhipāda*) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.’

The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, has done so. He could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.”

“Do you have faith, Ānanda?” “Yes, venerable one.”

“Therefore, Ānanda, the fault is yours; herein have you failed, inasmuch as you were unable to grasp the plain suggestion, the significant prompting given by the *Tathāgata*, and you did not then entreat the *Tathāgata* to remain: ‘May the Blessed One remain for an eon, O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!’”

“If, Ānanda, you had begged him, the *Tathāgata* would twice have refused you, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the fault, yours is the failure.
commentary_pali: 178.Alanti paṭikkhepavacanametaṃ. Bodhinti catumaggañāṇapaṭiveghaṃ. Saddahasi tvanti evaṃ vuttabhāvaṃ tathāgatassa saddahasīti vadati. Tasmātihānandāti yasmā idaṃ vacanaṃ saddahasi, tasmā tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭanti dasseti.
commentary_english:
"Ala" means this is a word of refusal.

"Bodhi" means the penetration of the knowledge of the four paths (catumārga-jñāna-prativedha).

"Do you believe?" means he says, "Do you believe the state of the Tathāgata's statement thus?"

"Therefore, Ānanda..." Since you believe this statement, therefore, he shows that this is a *dukkata* offense for you.

mula_pali: 179. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ rājagahe viharāmi gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo, ānanda, gijjhakūṭo pabbato.
