Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dve te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
mula_english:
179. “On one occasion, Ānanda, I was staying near Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak Mountain.

And there, Ānanda, I addressed you: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful is the Vulture's Peak Mountain.

Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of spiritual power (*ṛddhipāda*) are developed, practiced frequently, made his vehicle, made his basis, established, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (*kalpa*) or the remainder of an eon.

The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of spiritual power, practiced frequently, made his vehicle, made his basis, established, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken. The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.”

But you, Ānanda—even when the *Tathāgata* had given such a plain sign, such a clear hint—weren't able to understand. You did not entreat the *Tathāgata*: ‘Lord (*bhante*), may the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) remain for an eon (*kalpa*). May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans (*manuṣyā*)’.

If you, Ānanda, had entreated the *Tathāgata*, the *Tathāgata* would have rejected your speech twice, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, the wrong-doing (*duṣkṛta*) is yours; yours is the fault (*aparāddha*).
commentary_pali: 179.Ekamidāhanti idaṃ bhagavā – ‘‘na kevalaṃ ahaṃ idheva taṃ āmantesiṃ, aññadāpi āmantetvā oḷārikaṃ nimittaṃ akāsiṃ, tampi tayā na paṭividdhaṃ, tavevāyaṃ aparādho’’ti evaṃ sokavinodanatthāya nānappakārato therasseva dosāropanatthaṃ ārabhi.
commentary_english: 179. ekamidāhanti Here, the Blessed One [said]: "Not only here I addressed him, but at another time, having addressed him, I made a gross sign, but even that was not understood by her. This is your fault." Thus, for the sake of dispelling sorrow, in various ways, he began to impute fault to the elder himself.

mula_pali: 180. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ tattheva rājagahe viharāmi gotamanigrodhe…pe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi corapapāte… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi tapodārāme… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi jīvakambavane… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi maddakucchismiṃ migadāye tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo gijjhakūṭo pabbato, ramaṇīyo gotamanigrodho, ramaṇīyo corapapāto, ramaṇīyā vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhā, ramaṇīyā isigilipasse kāḷasilā, ramaṇīyo sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāro , ramaṇīyo tapodārāmo, ramaṇīyo veḷuvane kalandakanivāpo, ramaṇīyaṃ jīvakambavanaṃ, ramaṇīyo maddakucchismiṃ migadāyo. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā…pe… ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
mula_english:
“180. Once, Ānanda, I was staying right there near Rājagaha (Rājagṛha) at the Gotama Banyan tree… right there near Rājagaha at Robbers Cliff… right there near Rājagaha in Sattapaṇṇa Cave on the side of Mount Vebhāra… right there near Rājagaha at the Black Rock on Isigili Mountain… right there near Rājagaha in the Cool Forest at the Slope by the Snakes’ Pool… right there near Rājagaha at Tapodārāma (Tapodārāma) Park… right there near Rājagaha at the Bamboo Forest, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground, Venuvana (Veḷuvana)… right there near Rājagaha at Jīvakambavana (Jīvakambavana)… right there near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park.

There also, Ānanda, I addressed you: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful is Gijjhakūṭa (Gṛdhrakūṭa) Mountain; delightful is Gotamanigrodha (Gotamanigrodha); delightful is Corapapāta (Corapapāta); delightful is Sattapaṇṇiguhā (Sattapaṇṇiguhā) on the side of Mount Vebhāra; delightful is the Black Rock on the side of Mount Isigili; delightful is Sappasoṇḍikapabbhāra (Sappasoṇḍikapabbhāra) in the Cool Forest; delightful is Tapodārāma (Tapodārāma) Park; delightful is Kalandakanivāpa (Kalandakanivāpa) in Veḷuvana (Veḷuvana); delightful is Jīvakambavana (Jīvakambavana); delightful is the Maddakucchi Deer Park.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed, practiced frequently, made their vehicle, made their base, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four roads to power (catvāro ṛddhipādāḥ)… could undoubtedly live for a kalpa or the remainder of one.

But you, Ānanda, even when the Tathāgata gave such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint, weren’t able to understand his meaning. You did not beg the Tathāgata: ‘Lord (bhante), may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for a kalpa; may the Well-Gone (sugato) remain for a kalpa, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

If you, Ānanda, had begged the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata would have twice refused you, but after the third time he would have acquiesced.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the wrongdoing; yours is the fault."

mula_pali: 181. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi udene cetiye. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya, tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
mula_english:
“181.”Once, Ānanda, I was staying right here in Vesālī at the Udena shrine.

So also there, Ānanda, I addressed you, saying: ‘Vesālī is delightful, Ānanda; delightful is the Udena shrine.

Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of power (catāro iddhipādā) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or the remainder of an eon (kappāvasesaṃ).

In the Tathāgata, Ānanda, the four bases of power (catāro iddhipādā) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken. He could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or the remainder of an eon (kappāvasesaṃ).’

But you, Ānanda—even when the Tathāgata had given such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint—weren’t able to understand his meaning. You didn’t beg of the Tathāgata, ‘Lord (bhante), may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for an eon (kappaṃ). May the One Well-Gone (sugato) remain for an eon (kappaṃ)—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

For if you had done so, Ananda, twice the Tathāgata might have declined, but the third time he would have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your fault, this is your offense.

mula_pali: 182. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ , ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi gotamake cetiye …pe… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sattambe cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi bahuputte cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sārandade cetiye… idāneva kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
mula_english:
182.
"Once, Ānanda, I was staying at Vesālī at the Gotamaka shrine... at the Sattamba shrine… at the ManySon shrine… at the Sārandada shrine… And just now, Ānanda, today at the Capāla Shrine, I addressed you: ‘Vesālī is refreshing, Ānanda. Refreshing, too, are the Udena shrine, the Gotamaka shrine, the Sattamba shrine, the ManySon shrine, the Sārandada shrine, the Capāla shrine.’

Ānanda, anyone who has developed, cultivated, practiced, and grounded the four bases of power (*catvāro ṛddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā*), and properly undertaken them, could remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or until the end of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed, cultivated, practiced, and grounded the four bases of power (*catvāro ṛddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā*), and properly undertaken them. The Tathāgata could remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or until the end of an eon.”

“But you, Ānanda, even when the Tathāgata had given such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint, weren’t able to understand his meaning. You didn’t beg of the Tathāgata, ‘Lord, may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for an eon (kappaṃ). May the Well-Gone One (sugata) remain for an eon (kappaṃ)—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

If you had begged the Tathāgata, Ānanda, the Tathāgata would twice have refused you, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the fault, yours is the failure.

mula_pali:
183. ‘‘Nanu etaṃ evaṃ (syā. pī.), ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī. pī.) akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena cattaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ ossaṭṭho āyusaṅkhāro, ekaṃsena vācā bhāsitā – ‘na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Tañca taṃ vacanaṃ (sī.) tathāgato jīvitahetu puna paccāvamissatīti paccāgamissatīti (syā. ka.) netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Āyāmānanda, yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sannipatito, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho, yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.
mula_english:
183. “Ānanda, have I not explained this before, that of all things that are dear and beloved there is change, separation, and becoming otherwise? Ānanda, how could this be possible? Whatever is born, become, compounded, is liable to decay—that it should not decay is impossible. And that, Ānanda, which the *Tathāgata* has relinquished, given up, abandoned, and rejected—the life-principle—the *Tathāgata* has spoken with certainty: ‘The *parinirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* will not be long delayed. In three months' time the *Tathāgata* will attain *parinirvāṇa*.’ That the *Tathāgata* would turn back on that statement for the sake of continuing to live is impossible. Come, Ānanda, let us go to the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest.” “So be it, Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with the Venerable Ānanda, went to the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest. Having gone there, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Go, Ānanda, gather in the hall of audience all the monks who dwell in dependence on Vaiśālī.” “So be it, Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Having gathered all the monks who dwelt in dependence on Vaiśālī in the hall of audience, he went to the Blessed One, respectfully greeted him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, “The *bhikkhu-saṃgha* is assembled, Lord. May the Blessed One do what he thinks it is now time to do.”
commentary_pali: 183.Piyehi manāpehīti mātāpitābhātābhaginiādikehi jātiyā nānābhāvo, maraṇena vinābhāvo, bhavena aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha labbhāti tanti tasmā, yasmā sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo, tasmā dasa pāramiyo pūretvāpi, sambodhiṃ patvāpi, dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvāpi, yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ dassetvāpi, devorohaṇaṃ katvāpi, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati, rodantenāpi kandantenāpi na sakkā taṃ kāraṇaṃ laddhunti. Puna paccāvamissatīti yaṃ cattaṃ vantaṃ, taṃ vata puna paṭikhādissatīti attho.
commentary_english:
"piyehi manāpehī" means "variousness" due to kinship with mother, father, brother, sister, and so on, "separation" due to death, "otherness" due to existence.

"taṃ kutettha labbhā" means "ta"nti tasmā, yasmā sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo, tasmā dasa pāramiyo pūretvāpi, sambodhiṃ patvāpi, dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvāpi, yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ dassetvāpi, devorohaṇaṃ katvāpi, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati, rodantenāpi kandantenāpi na sakkā taṃ kāraṇaṃ laddhunti.

"puna paccāvamissatī" means the meaning is that which is given up and vomited, it will be eaten again.

mula_pali: 184. Atha kho bhagavā yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ye te mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, te vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame ca te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Ime kho te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.
mula_english:
184.
Then the Blessed One went to the assembly hall ( *upaṭṭhānasālā* ) and, having arrived, sat down on the prepared seat ( *paññatte āsane nisīdi* ).

Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Therefore, O monks, those things ( *dhammā* ) which I have directly known ( *abhiññā* ) and taught ( *desitā* ), you should thoroughly learn ( *sādhukaṃ uggahetvā* ), practice ( *āsevitabbā* ), develop ( *bhāvetabbā* ), and cultivate ( *bahulīkātabbā* ), so that this holy life ( *brahmacariyaṃ* ) may long endure ( *addhaṇiyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ* ), for the benefit ( *atthāya* ), welfare ( *hitāya* ), and happiness ( *sukhāya* ) of the multitude ( *bahujanahitāya bahujanāya* ), out of compassion ( *anukampāya* ) for the world ( *loka* ), and for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods ( *deva* ) and humans ( *manussānaṃ* ).

"And what, O monks, are those things ( *dhammā* ) which I have directly known ( *abhiññā desitā* ) and taught, that you should thoroughly learn, practice, develop, and cultivate, so that this holy life may long endure, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, and for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans?

They are: the four foundations of mindfulness ( *cattāro satipaṭṭhānā* ), the four right efforts ( *cattāro sammappadhānā* ), the four bases of power ( *cattāro iddhipādā* ), the five faculties ( *pañcindriyāni* ), the five strengths ( *pañca balāni* ), the seven factors of enlightenment ( *satta bojjhaṅgā* ), the Noble Eightfold Path ( *ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo* ).

These, O monks, are the things ( *dhammā* ) which I have directly known and taught, that you should thoroughly learn, practice, develop, and cultivate, so that this holy life may long endure, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, and for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans."
commentary_pali:
184.Yathayidaṃ brahmacariyanti yathā idaṃ sikkhāttayasaṅgahaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. Addhaniyanti addhānakkhamaṃ. Ciraṭṭhitikanti cirappavattivasena ciraṭṭhitikaṃ. Cattāro satipaṭṭhānātiādi sabbaṃ lokiyalokuttaravaseneva kathitaṃ. Etesaṃ pana bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ vinicchayo sabbākārena visuddhimagge paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddese vutto. Sesamettha uttānamevāti.

Tatiyabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Nāgāpalokitavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
184. yathayidaṃ brahmacariyanti, "how this holy life [is lived]" means how this holy life of the teaching is a compendium of the threefold training ( *śikṣā*). addhaniyanti, "lasting" means capable of lasting a long time. ciraṭṭhitikanti, "long-lasting" means long-lasting in terms of continuing for a long time. cattāro satipaṭṭhānātiādi, "the four establishments of mindfulness" etc., all is spoken of only in terms of the mundane and supramundane. However, the analysis of these *bodhipakkhiya* *dharmas* (qualities conducive to enlightenment) has been stated in full in the *Visuddhimagga* in the section on the purification of knowledge and vision of the path. The rest is evident here.

The commentary on the third recitation section is finished.

Commentary on Nāgāpalokita

mula_pali:
185. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘handadāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha. Naciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā ito paraṃ syāmapotthake evaṃpi pāṭho dissati –§daharāpi ca ye vuddhā, ye bālā ye ca paṇḍitā.§aḍḍhāceva daliddā ca, sabbe maccuparāyanā.§yathāpi kumbhakārassa, kataṃ mattikabhājanaṃ.§khuddakañca mahantañca, yañca pakkaṃ yañca āmakaṃ.§sabbaṃ bhedapariyantaṃ, evaṃ maccāna jīvitaṃ.§athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā. –

‘‘Paripakko vayo mayhaṃ, parittaṃ mama jīvitaṃ;

Pahāya vo gamissāmi, kataṃ me saraṇamattano.

‘‘Appamattā satīmanto, susīlā hotha bhikkhavo;

Susamāhitasaṅkappā, sacittamanurakkhatha.

‘‘Yo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati;

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’’ti viharissati (syā.), vihessati (sī.).

viharissati (syā.), vihessati (sī.)

Tatiyo bhāṇavāro.

Nāgāpalokitaṃ
mula_english:
185. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Now, then, monks, I exhort you: All conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive with earnestness.

It will not be long until the Tathāgata’s *parinirvāṇa*.

In three months' time from now, the Tathāgata will attain *parinirvāṇa*."

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Gone One, the Teacher, further said this:

[Note: "Even the young and the old, the foolish and the wise. Rich and poor alike, all are subject to death. Just as a potter makes earthen vessels, whether small or large, baked or unbaked, all are subject to breakage. Further, the Teacher said this:"]

My years are now ripe; little of my life remains.

I will leave you, having made myself my refuge.

Monks, be diligent, mindful, and virtuous.

Be of concentrated resolve, protect your own minds.

Whoever in this *dharma-vinaya* lives diligently,

having abandoned the cycle of birth, will make an end of suffering."

Third recitation section.

Nāgāpalokitaṃ.

mula_pali:
186. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nāgāpalokitaṃ vesāliṃ apaloketvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘idaṃ pacchimakaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa vesāliyā dassanaṃ bhavissati. Āyāmānanda, yena bhaṇḍagāmo bhaṇḍugāmo (ka.) tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhaṇḍagāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Ariyassa, bhikkhave, sīlassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyassa, bhikkhave, samādhissa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, paññāya ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, vimuttiyā ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ sīlaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, ariyo samādhi anubuddho paṭividdho, ariyā paññā anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ariyā vimutti anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Sīlaṃ samādhi paññā ca, vimutti ca anuttarā;

Anubuddhā ime dhammā, gotamena yasassinā.

‘‘Iti buddho abhiññāya, dhammamakkhāsi bhikkhunaṃ;

Dukkhassantakaro satthā, cakkhumā parinibbuto’’ti.

Tatrāpi sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharanto etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.

Catumahāpadesakathā
mula_english:
186. Then, the Blessed One, early in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Vesālī for alms.

Having gone for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, returning from his alms round, gazing on Vesālī with an elephant’s look, he addressed Ven. Ānanda: “Ānanda, this is the Tathāgata’s last look at Vesālī.

Come, Ānanda, let us go to Bhaṇḍagāma.”

“So be it, O Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *Saṅgha* of monks, went to Bhaṇḍagāma.

There the Blessed One stayed near Bhaṇḍagāma.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, it is through not realizing, through not penetrating four principles that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

Which four? It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble virtue (*ariya sīla*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble concentration (*ariya samādhi*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble wisdom (*ariya paññā*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble emancipation (*ariya vimutti*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

But now, monks, the noble virtue has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble concentration has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble wisdom has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble emancipation has been awakened to and penetrated; craving for becoming has been cut off, the guide to becoming is exhausted, and there will be no more rebirth.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having spoken thus, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, then said further:

“Virtue (*sīla*), concentration (*samādhi*), wisdom (*paññā*), and unsurpassed emancipation (*vimutti*);

these *dharmas* have been awakened to by Gotama, the glorious one.”

“Thus the Buddha, having directly known, explained the Dharma to the monks;

the Teacher puts an end to suffering, he who has vision, has attained *parinirvāṇa*.”

There also, the Blessed One, while living in Bhaṇḍagāma, often gave this *Dhamma* talk to the monks: “Such is virtue (*sīla*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*paññā*).

Concentration (*samādhi*) nurtured with virtue (*sīla*) is of great fruit, great reward.

Discernment (*paññā*) nurtured with concentration (*samādhi*) is of great fruit, great reward.

The mind nurtured with discernment (*paññā*) is rightly released from the effluents, i. e. , the effluent of sensuality (*kāmāsava*), the effluent of becoming (*bhavāsava*), the effluent of ignorance (*avijjāsava*).”

Discourse on the Four Great Authorities
commentary_pali:
186.Nāgāpalokitanti yathā hi mahājanassa aṭṭhīni koṭiyā koṭiṃ āhacca ṭhitāni paccekabuddhānaṃ, aṅkusakalaggāni viya, na evaṃ buddhānaṃ. Buddhānaṃ pana saṅkhalikāni viya ekābaddhāni hutvā ṭhitāni, tasmā pacchato apalokanakāle na sakkā hoti gīvaṃ parivattetuṃ. Yathā pana hatthināgo pacchābhāgaṃ apaloketukāmo sakalasarīreneva parivattati, evaṃ parivattitabbaṃ hoti. Bhagavato pana nagaradvāre ṭhatvā – ‘‘vesāliṃ apalokessāmī’’ti citte uppannamatte – ‘‘bhagavā anekāni kappakoṭisahassāni pāramiyo pūrentehi tumhehi na gīvaṃ parivattetvā apalokanakammaṃ kata’’nti ayaṃ pathavī kulālacakkaṃ viya parivattetvā bhagavantaṃ vesālinagarābhimukhaṃ akāsi. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Nanu ca na kevalaṃ vesāliyāva, sāvatthirājagahanāḷandapāṭaligāmakoṭigāmanātikagāmakesupi tato tato nikkhantakāle taṃ taṃ sabbaṃ pacchimadassanameva, tattha tattha kasmā nāgāpalokitaṃ nāpalokesīti? Anacchariyattā. Tattha tattha hi nivattetvā apalokentassetaṃ na acchariyaṃ hoti, tasmā nāpalokesi. Api ca vesālirājāno āsannavināsā, tiṇṇaṃ vassānaṃ upari vinassissanti. Te taṃ nagaradvāre nāgāpalokitaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ katvā gandhamālādīhi pūjessanti, taṃ nesaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissatīti tesaṃ anukampāya apalokesi.

nāgāpalokitaṃ

Dukkhassantakaroti vaṭṭadukkhassa antakaro. Cakkhumāti pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā. Parinibbutoti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto.

Dukkhassantakaro Cakkhumā Parinibbuto

Catumahāpadesavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
186. Nāgāpalokitanti: Just as the bones of the great mass of people are positioned having struck against a billion *koṭis* in the case of the solitary buddhas, like the point of a hook, not so in the case of the Buddhas. But for the Buddhas they are positioned having become joined together like chains. Therefore, at the time of looking back, it is not possible to turn the neck. Just as, however, an elephant, wishing to look back at the rear part, turns around with its entire body, so it should be turned around. However, to the Blessed One, standing at the city gate – the thought having arisen in his mind, “I will look at Vaiśālī" – "O Blessed One, by you, who for countless *kappa-koṭi-sahasras* were fulfilling the perfections (*pāramī*) it was not proper to turn the neck before the act of looking back (*apalokanakamma*) was done,” this earth, having turned around the Blessed One like a potter's wheel turned (him) towards Vaiśālī city. This was said with reference to this.

But indeed, not only to Vaiśālī, but also in Sāvatthi, Rājagaha, Nāḷanda, Pāṭaligāma, Koṭigāma, and Nātikagāmaka, at the time of departing from here and there, all that was only a rear view. Why did he not look back, with the *nāgāpalokita*, there and there? Because it was not wondrous. Indeed, there and there, having turned back and looking, that was not wondrous; therefore, he did not look back. Moreover, the kings of Vaiśālī are near destruction; after three years they will perish. Having made that caitya named nāgāpalokita at that city gate, they will honor (it) with perfumes, garlands, and so on. That will be for their long-lasting benefit and happiness. Out of compassion for them, he looked back.

Nāgāpalokitaṃ

Dukkhassantakaroti: (It is) the end-maker of the round of suffering (*vaṭṭadukkha*). Cakkhumāti: (He) has eyes (*cakkhumā*) with the five eyes (*pañcahi cakkhūhi*). Parinibbutoti: (He) is fully extinguished (*parinibbuto*) by the extinction of defilements (*kilesaparinibbāna*).

Dukkhassantakaro Cakkhumā Parinibbuto

Explanation of the Four Great Authorities (*catumahāpadesavaṇṇanā*)

mula_pali: 187. Atha kho bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena hatthigāmo, yena ambagāmo, yena jambugāmo, yena bhoganagaraṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhoganagaraṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharati ānande sānandare (ka.) cetiye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘cattārome, bhikkhave, mahāpadese desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
187. Then, the Blessed One, having stayed near Bhaṇḍagāma as long as he pleased, addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Hatthigāma, to Ambagāma, to Jambugāma, to Bhoganagara.”

“So be it, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then, the Blessed One, together with a large *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, went to Bhoganagara.

There the Blessed One stayed near Bhoganagara at the Ānanda shrine.

There the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus*, saying: “O *bhikkhus*, I will teach you the four great standards (*mahāpadesa*). Listen, pay close attention, and I will speak.”

“So be it, venerable sir,” those *bhikkhus* replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali: 187.Mahāpadeseti mahāokāse, mahāapadese vā, buddhādayo mahante mahante apadisitvā vuttāni mahākāraṇānīti attho.
commentary_english: "mahāpadese": "mahāokāse", or "mahāapadese"; *buddha*, and so forth, having pointed out the great, great, causes, are declared to be great reasons (mahākāraṇāni), this is the meaning (artha).

mula_pali:
188. ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti otaranti (sī. pī. a. ni. 4.180, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse saṅgho viharati sathero sapāmokkho. Tassa me saṅghassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva osaranti vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā , idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse sambahulā therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā. Tesaṃ me therānaṃ sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ…pe… na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni…pe… vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse eko thero bhikkhu viharati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo. Tassa me therassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāritabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ca sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti , niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā , idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro mahāpadese dhāreyyāthā’’ti.

Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharanto ānande cetiye etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso . Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.

Kammāraputtacundavatthu
mula_english:
188. Monks, a monk might say thus: ‘Face to face with the Blessed One, friend, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma* (law, teaching), this is the *Vinaya* (the monastic discipline), this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* (discourses) and examine them against the *Vinaya*.

If, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they do not conform to the *Sūtras* (see Sī.
Pī.
A.
Ni.
4.
180), and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; this monk has misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they conform to the *Sūtras*, and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; this monk has understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the first Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name lives a *Saṅgha* (community) with elders and a chief.

Face to face with that *Saṅgha* (community), I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* and examine them against the *Vinaya*.

If, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they do not conform to the *Sūtras*, and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; that *Saṅgha* (community) has misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they conform to the *Sūtras*, and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; that *Saṅgha* (community) has understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the second Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name live many elder monks who are learned, who have mastered the traditions, who are upholders of the *Dhamma*, upholders of the *Vinaya*, upholders of the *Mātikā* (the outlines of the *Dhamma*) .

Face to face with those elders, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved… and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; those elders have misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras*…and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; those elders have understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the third Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name lives a single elder monk who is learned, who has mastered the traditions, who is an upholder of the *Dhamma*, an upholder of the *Vinaya*, an upholder of the *Mātikā*.

Face to face with that elder, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* and examine them against the *Vinaya*.
If, when these are compared to the *suttas* (discourses) and verified by the *vinaya* (the monastic discipline), they do not align with the *suttas*, nor are they in accordance with the *vinaya*, then one should conclude: 'Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One (tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ); this *thera* (elder monk) has misunderstood it.'
In that way, *bhikkhus* (monks), you should reject it.
But if, when these are compared to the *suttas* and verified by the *vinaya*, they do align with the *suttas* and are in accordance with the *vinaya*, then one should conclude: 'Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; this *thera* has understood it rightly.'
This, *bhikkhus*, is the fourth great reference (mahāpadesaṃ) you should bear in mind.
"These, *bhikkhus*, are the four great references you should bear in mind."
There also the Blessed One, while dwelling near Bhoganagara at the Ānanda Shrine, frequently gave this Dhamma talk to the monks: "Such is virtue (*sīlaṃ*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*paññā*)."
Concentration (*samādhi*) developed with virtue (*sīla-paribhāvito*) is of great fruit (mahapphalo) and great benefit (mahānisaṃso).
Wisdom (*paññā*) developed with concentration (*samādhi-paribhāvitā*) is of great fruit and great benefit.
The mind (cittaṃ) developed with wisdom is utterly freed from the *āsavas* (influxes or taints), that is, the *kāmāsava* (influx of sensuality), the *bhavāsava* (influx of becoming), and the *avijjāsava* (influx of ignorance)."

188.Neva abhinanditabbanti haṭṭhatuṭṭhehi sādhukāraṃ datvā pubbeva na sotabbaṃ, evaṃ kate hi pacchā ‘‘idaṃ na sametī’’ti vuccamāno – ‘‘kiṃ pubbeva ayaṃ dhammo, idāni na dhammo’’ti vatvā laddhiṃ na vissajjeti. Nappaṭikkositabbanti – ‘‘kiṃ esa bālo vadatī’’ti evaṃ pubbeva na vattabbaṃ, evaṃ vutte hi vattuṃ yuttampi na vakkhati. Tenāha – ‘‘anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā’’ti. Padabyañjanānīti padasaṅkhātāni byañjanāni. Sādhukaṃ uggahetvāti imasmiṃ ṭhāne pāḷi vuttā, imasmiṃ ṭhāne attho vutto, imasmiṃ ṭhāne anusandhi kathito, imasmiṃ ṭhāne pubbāparaṃ kathitanti suṭṭhu gahetvā. Sutte osāretabbānīti sutte otāretabbāni. Vinaye sandassetabbānīti vinaye saṃsandetabbāni.

Ettha ca suttanti vinayo. Yathāha – ‘‘kattha paṭikkhittaṃ? Sāvatthiyaṃ suttavibhaṅge’’ti (cuḷava. 457). Vinayoti khandhako. Yathāha – ‘‘vinayātisāre’’ti. Evaṃ vinayapiṭakampi na pariyādiyati. Ubhatovibhaṅgā pana suttaṃ, khandhakaparivārā vinayoti evaṃ vinayapiṭakaṃ pariyādiyati. Athavā suttantapiṭakaṃ suttaṃ, vinayapiṭakaṃ vinayoti evaṃ dveyeva piṭakāni pariyādiyanti. Suttantābhidhammapiṭakāni vā suttaṃ, vinayapiṭakaṃ vinayoti evampi tīṇi piṭakāni na tāva pariyādiyanti. Asuttanāmakañhi buddhavacanaṃ nāma atthi. Seyyathidaṃ – jātakaṃ, paṭisambhidā, niddeso, suttanipāto, dhammapadaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, vimānavatthu, petavatthu, theragāthā, therīgāthā, apadānanti.

sutta Vinayo

Sudinnatthero pana – ‘‘asuttanāmakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ na atthī’’ti taṃ sabbaṃ paṭipakkhipitvā – ‘‘tīṇi piṭakāni suttaṃ, vinayo pana kāraṇa’’nti āha. Tato taṃ kāraṇaṃ dassento idaṃ suttamāhari –

‘‘Ye kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi, ime dhammā sarāgāya saṃvattanti no virāgāya, saññogāya saṃvattanti no visaññogāya, ācayāya saṃvattanti no apacayāya, mahicchatāya saṃvattanti no appicchatāya, asantuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no santuṭṭhiyā, saṅgaṇikāya saṃvattanti no pavivekāya, kosajjāya saṃvattanti no vīriyārambhāya, dubbharatāya saṃvattanti no subharatāya. Ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – ‘neso dhammo, neso vinayo, netaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Ye ca kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi, ime dhammā virāgāya saṃvattanti no sarāgāya, visaññogāya saṃvattanti no saññogāya, apacayāya saṃvattanti no ācayāya, appicchatāya saṃvattanti no mahicchatāya, santuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no asantuṭṭhiyā, pavivekāya saṃvattanti no saṅgaṇikāya , vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti no kosajjāya, subharatāya saṃvattanti no dubbharatāya. Ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – ‘eso dhammo, eso vinayo, etaṃ satthusāsana’nti’’ (a. ni. 8.53).

Tasmā sutteti tepiṭake buddhavacane otāretabbāni. Vinayeti etasmiṃ rāgādivinayakāraṇe saṃsandetabbānīti ayamettha attho. Na ceva sutte osarantīti suttapaṭipāṭiyā katthaci anāgantvā challiṃ uṭṭhapetvā guḷhavessantara-guḷhaummagga-guḷhavinaya-vedallapiṭakānaṃ aññatarato āgatāni paññāyantīti attho. Evaṃ āgatāni hi rāgādivinaye ca na paññāyamānāni chaḍḍetabbāni honti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘iti hetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyāthā’’ti. Etenupāyena sabbattha attho veditabbo.

sutte Vinaye Na ceva sutte osarantī

Idaṃ, bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyāthāti idaṃ catutthaṃ dhammassa patiṭṭhānokāsaṃ dhāreyyātha.

Idaṃ bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyāthā

Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne imaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ veditabbaṃ. Sutte cattāro mahāpadesā, khandhake cattāro mahāpadesā, cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni, suttaṃ, suttānulomaṃ, ācariyavādo, attanomati, tisso saṅgītiyoti.

Tattha – ‘‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo’’ti dhammavinicchaye patte ime cattāro mahāpadesā pamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ ettha sameti tadeva gahetabbaṃ, itaraṃ viravantassapi na gahetabbaṃ.

‘‘Idaṃ kappati, idaṃ na kappatī’’ti kappiyākappiyavinicchaye patte – ‘‘yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā idaṃ na kappatīti appaṭikkhittaṃ, taṃ ce akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo na kappatī’’tiādinā (mahāva. 305) nayena khandhake vuttā cattāro mahāpadesā pamāṇaṃ. Tesaṃ vinicchayakathā samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttā. Tattha vuttanayena yaṃ kappiyaṃ anulometi, tadeva kappiyaṃ, itaraṃ akappiyanti evaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātabbaṃ.

samantapāsādikāyaṃ

Ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho, vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho, paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho, ṭhapanīyo pañhoti imāni cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni nāma. Tattha ‘‘cakkhuṃ anicca’’nti puṭṭhena – ‘‘āma anicca’’nti ekaṃseneva byākātabbaṃ . Esa nayo sotādīsu. Ayaṃ ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘‘Aniccaṃ nāma cakkhu’’nti puṭṭhena – ‘‘na cakkhumeva, sotampi aniccaṃ ghānampi anicca’’nti evaṃ vibhajitvā byākātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘‘Yathā cakkhu tathā sotaṃ, yathā sotaṃ tathā cakkhu’’nti puṭṭhena ‘‘kenaṭṭhena pucchasī’’ti paṭipucchitvā ‘‘dassanaṭṭhena pucchāmī’’ti vutte ‘‘na hī’’ti byākātabbaṃ, ‘‘aniccaṭṭhena pucchāmī’’ti vutte āmāti byākātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘‘Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’’ntiādīni puṭṭhena pana ‘‘abyākatametaṃ bhagavatā’’ti ṭhapetabbo, esa pañho na byākātabbo. Ayaṃ ṭhapanīyo pañho. Iti tenākārena pañhe sampatte imāni cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni pamāṇaṃ. Imesaṃ vasena so pañho byākātabbo.

cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo ṭhapanīyo

Suttādīsu pana suttaṃ nāma tisso saṅgītiyo ārūḷhāni tīṇi piṭakāni. Suttānulomaṃ nāma anulomakappiyaṃ. Ācariyavādo nāma aṭṭhakathā. Attanomati nāma nayaggāhena anubuddhiyā attano paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha suttaṃ appaṭibāhiyaṃ, taṃ paṭibāhantena buddhova paṭibāhito hoti. Anulomakappiyaṃ pana suttena samentameva gahetabbaṃ, na itaraṃ. Ācariyavādopi suttena samentoyeva gahetabbo, na itaro. Attanomati pana sabbadubbalā, sāpi suttena samentāyeva gahetabbā, na itarā. Pañcasatikā, sattasatikā, sahassikāti imā pana tisso saṅgītiyo. Suttampi tāsu āgatameva pamāṇaṃ, itaraṃ gārayhasuttaṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Tattha otarantānipi hi padabyañjanāni na ceva sutte otaranti, na ca vinaye sandissantīti veditabbāni.

suttaṃ Suttānulomaṃ Ācariyavādo Attanomati tisso saṅgītiyo.

commentary_english:
188.
"'Should not be welcomed' means: One should not give applause with joyful and delighted [hearts], giving approval beforehand, saying, 'Excellent!' For if one does so, and later one is told, 'This does not fit,' if he says, 'Why, was this the Dharma before, and is it not the Dharma now?', he will not give up his view.

"'Should not be rejected' means: One should not say beforehand, 'What is this fool saying?' For if one speaks thus, he will not speak even if it is fitting to speak.

Therefore, it was said: "'Without welcoming, without rejecting.'"

"'Words and consonants' means: the consonants which are reckoned as words.

"'Having thoroughly grasped' means: Having thoroughly grasped, 'In this place the *pāḷi* is spoken, in this place the meaning is spoken, in this place the connection is spoken, in this place what comes before and what comes after is spoken.'

"'Should be tested against the Sūtras' means: They should be tested [by comparing them] with the Sūtras.

"'Should be compared with the Vinaya' means: They should be collated with the Vinaya.

Herein, *sutta* is the Vinaya. As it is said: “Where has it been rejected? In Sāvatthī, in the Sutta-vibhaṅga” (Cuḷava. 457).

*Vinaya* is the Khandhaka. As it is said: “In transgression of the Vinaya.”

Thus, the Vinaya-piṭaka is not completely mastered.

However, the Ubhatovibhaṅga is the Sūtra, the Khandhaka-parivāra is the Vinaya. Thus, the Vinaya-piṭaka is completely mastered.

Alternatively, the Suttanta-piṭaka is the Sūtra, the Vinaya-piṭaka is the Vinaya. Thus, these two Piṭakas are completely mastered.

Or else, the Suttanta-abhidhamma-piṭakas are the Sūtra, the Vinaya-piṭaka is the Vinaya. Even so, the three Piṭakas are not entirely mastered.

For there is no word of the Buddha called "not-Sūtra."

That is to say: the Jātaka, the Paṭisambhidā, the Niddesa, the Sutta-nipāta, the Dhammapada, the Udāna, the Itivuttaka, the Vimānavatthu, the Petavatthu, the Theragāthā, the Therīgāthā, and the Apadāna.

Sūtra and Vinaya

Sudinnatthero, however, having rejected all of that, saying, “There is no word of the Buddha called 'not-Sūtra,'” said: “The three Piṭakas are the Sūtra, but the Vinaya is the cause."

Then, showing that reason, he recited this Sūtra:

“Whatever states you, Gotamī, may know: 'These states lead to passion, not to dispassion; to bondage, not to freedom from bondage; to increase, not to decrease; to great desires, not to fewness of wishes; to discontent, not to contentment; to sociability, not to solitude; to laziness, not to putting forth energy; to difficulty in being supported, not to ease in being supported.'

You should definitely know, Gotamī: 'This is not the Dharma, this is not the Vinaya, this is not the Teacher’s instruction.'

And whatever states you, Gotamī, may know: 'These states lead to dispassion, not to passion; to freedom from bondage, not to bondage; to decrease, not to increase; to fewness of wishes, not to great desires; to contentment, not to discontent; to solitude, not to sociability, to putting forth energy, not to laziness; to ease in being supported, not to difficulty in being supported.'

You should definitely know, Gotamī: 'This is the Dharma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction'” (A. Ni. 8.53).

Therefore, "'Should be tested against the Sūtras' means: They should be tested against the Buddha-word in those three Piṭakas.

"'Vinaya' means: They should be collated with this cause of Vinaya, [which is] aversion to passion, etc." This is the meaning here.

"'And should not be practiced in the Sūtras' means: Without appearing anywhere in the order of the Sūtras, having raised a bark [of doctrine], they appear as having come from one of the Guḷhavessantara, Guḷhaummagga, Guḷhavinaya, or Vedallapiṭaka.

For what has come thus, if it is not apparent in the Vinaya concerning aversion to passion, etc., should be discarded.

Therefore, it was said: “Thus, O *bhikkhus*, you should discard it.”

By this means, the meaning should be understood everywhere.
They do not occur in the sūtras or the Vinaya; indeed, they do not appear in the sūtras.

This, monks, is the fourth Great Referral you should bear in mind: this fourth you should bear in mind as the basis and opportunity for the Dhamma.

This, monks, is the fourth Great Referral you should bear in mind.

But in this case, this miscellaneous matter should be understood. In the sūtras, there are four Great Referrals; in the Khandhaka, four Great Referrals; four ways of answering questions; the sūtra, what accords with the sūtra, the teacher's doctrine, one's own opinion, and the three recitations.

Therein, when a decision about the Dhamma is reached—"This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya"—these four Great Referrals are the standard. Whatever agrees here should be accepted; the other, even if clamoring, should not be accepted.

When a decision about what is allowable and what is not is reached—"This is allowable, this is not allowable"—the four Great Referrals stated in the Khandhaka according to the method beginning with "Whatever, monks, has not been rejected by me, saying, 'This is not allowable,' if it conforms with what is not allowable, if it goes against what is allowable, that is not allowable for you" are the standard.

The discussion of their decision is stated in the *Samantapāsādikā*. According to the method stated there, whatever conforms with what is allowable is allowable, and the other is not allowable; thus, a conclusion should be made.

In the *Samantapāsādikā*:

A question that should be answered directly, a question that should be answered with a distinction, a question that should be answered with a counter-question, a question that should be set aside: these are called the four ways of answering questions (*cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni*).

Therein, when asked, "Is the eye impermanent?", it should be answered directly with "Yes, it is impermanent." This method [applies] to the ear, etc. This is a question that should be answered directly (*ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

When asked, "Is the eye impermanent?", it should be answered by distinguishing, "Not only the eye, but the ear is impermanent, the nose is impermanent." This is a question that should be answered with a distinction (*vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

When asked, "As is the eye, so is the ear; as is the ear, so is the eye," having counter-questioned, "In what sense do you ask?", when [the other] says, "I ask in the sense of seeing," it should be answered, "No." When [the other] says, "I ask in the sense of impermanence," it should be answered, "Yes." This is a question that should be answered with a counter-question (*paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

But when asked about "Is the life-principle the same as the body?", etc., it should be set aside [saying], "This has not been explained by the Blessed One"; this question should not be answered. This is a question that should be set aside (*ṭhapanīyo pañho*).

Thus, when a question arises in that way, these four ways of answering questions are the standard. According to these, that question should be answered.

In the sūtras, etc., the *sūtra* (*suttaṃ*) is the three collections (*piṭaka*) that have ascended to the three recitations (*tisso saṅgītiyo*). *What accords with the sūtra* (*suttānulomaṃ*) is what suitably accords. *The teacher's doctrine* (*ācariyavādo*) is the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*). *One's own opinion* (*attanomati*) is one's own insight through grasping the method by way of subsequent understanding.

Therein, the sūtra is irrefutable; by refuting that, the Buddha himself is refuted. But what suitably accords should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other. The teacher's doctrine, too, should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other. But one's own opinion is the weakest of all; that, too, should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other.

The five-hundred [recitation], the seven-hundred [recitation], the thousand [recitation]: these are the three recitations (*tisso saṅgītiyo*). Even the sūtra that has come down in those [recitations] is the standard; the other, the censured sūtra, should not be accepted.

Therein, even the words and expressions that occur should be understood as not occurring in the sūtra, and not appearing in the Vinaya.
Sūtra, in accordance with the sūtras, the teacher's doctrine, one's own opinion, the three recitations.
