mula_pali:
196. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena kakudhā nadī tenupasaṅkami ; upasaṅkamitvā kakudhaṃ nadiṃ ajjhogāhetvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena ambavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ cundakaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, cundaka, catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, cundaka, nipajjissāmī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā cundako bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasikaritvā. Āyasmā pana cundako tattheva bhagavato purato nisīdi.

Gantvāna buddho nadikaṃ kakudhaṃ,

Acchodakaṃ sātudakaṃ vippasannaṃ;

Ogāhi satthā akilantarūpo sukilantarūpo (sī. pī.),

sukilantarūpo (sī. pī.)

Tathāgato appaṭimo ca appaṭimodha (pī.) loke.

appaṭimodha (pī.)

Nhatvā ca pivitvā cudatāri satthā pivitvā cundakena, pivitvā ca uttari (ka.),

pivitvā cundakena, pivitvā ca uttari (ka.)

Purakkhato bhikkhugaṇassa majjhe;

Vattā satthā (sī. syā. pī.) pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme,

satthā (sī. syā. pī.)

Upāgami ambavanaṃ mahesi.

Āmantayi cundakaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ,

Catugguṇaṃ santhara me nipajjaṃ;

So codito bhāvitattena cundo,

Catugguṇaṃ santhari khippameva.

Nipajji satthā akilantarūpo,

Cundopi tattha pamukhe samukhe (ka.) nisīdīti.

samukhe (ka.)
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks, went to the Kakudha River; having arrived at the Kakudha River, he went down into the river, bathed, drank, and came back out, and then went to a mango grove. Having arrived there, he said to Venerable Cundaka, "Come, Cundaka, please arrange my outer robe folded in four, I am tired, Cundaka, I will lie down."

"As you say, Lord," Venerable Cundaka replied to the Blessed One, and arranged the outer robe folded in four.

Then the Blessed One lay down on his right side in the lion's posture, placing one foot on top of the other, mindful and fully aware, keeping in mind the thought of rising.

And Venerable Cundaka sat down right there in front of the Blessed One.

Having gone to the Kakudha River,
With its clear and pleasant water,
The teacher, tireless in form, entered it,
The Tathāgata, unparalleled in the world.

Having bathed and drunk, the teacher came out,
Surrounded by the community of monks;
The Blessed One, the speaker and initiator of the Dharma here,
Approached the mango grove, the great sage.

He addressed the monk named Cundaka,
"Fold a robe in four for me to lie down on";
Urged on by the well-developed one, Cunda,
Quickly spread out the four-folded robe.

The teacher, tireless in form, lay down,
And Cunda sat there in front of him.
commentary_pali:
196.Nhatvāca pivitvā cāti ettha tadā kira bhagavati nahāyante antonadiyaṃ macchakacchapā ca ubhatotīresu vanasaṇḍo ca sabbaṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇameva hoti. Ambavananti tassāyeva nadiyā tīre ambavanaṃ. Āyasmantaṃ cundakanti tasmiṃ kira khaṇe ānandatthero udakasāṭakaṃ pīḷento ohīyi, cundatthero samīpe ahosi. Taṃ bhagavā āmantesi.

Gantvāna buddho nadikaṃ kakudhanti imāpi gāthā saṅgītikāleyeva ṭhapitā. Tattha pavattā bhagavā idha dhammeti bhagavā idha sāsane dhamme pavattā, caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni pavattānīti attho. Pamukhe nisīdīti satthu puratova nisīdi. Ettāvatā ca thero anuppatto. Evaṃ anuppattaṃ atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi.

Gantvāna buddho nadikaṃ kakudha pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme Pamukhe nisīdī
commentary_english:
196.
Having slain, and having drunk, it was like this: At that time, when the Fortunate One was bathing in the inner river, the fish and turtles, and the forest clumps on both banks, all became of golden color.

"Mango grove": On the bank of that very river was a mango grove.

"Venerable Cundaka": At that moment, Venerable Ānanda, squeezing his water garment, stepped aside, and Venerable Cunda was near.

The Fortunate One addressed him.

Having gone, the Buddha [to] the river Kakudha, these verses were established at the time of the Saṅgīti.

There, "The Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here": The Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here in the dispensation. The meaning is that eighty-four thousand aggregates of the Dharma were promulgated.

"He sat in front": He sat right in front of the Teacher.

By this much, the Elder had arrived.

Having thus arrived, then the Fortunate One addressed Venerable Ānanda.

Having gone, the Buddha [to] the river Kakudha, the Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here, he sat in front.

mula_pali:
197. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho yo kho (ka.), panānanda, cundassa kammāraputtassa koci vippaṭisāraṃ uppādeyya – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, alābhā tassa te dulladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto’ti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, lābhā tassa te suladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto. Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso cunda, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – dve me piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samā samaphalā (ka.) samavipākā samasamavipākā (sī. syā. pī.), ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Katame dve? Yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati. Ime dve piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samavipākā , ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Āyusaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, vaṇṇasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, sukhasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, yasasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, saggasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, ādhipateyyasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacita’nti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

‘‘Dadato puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati,

Saṃyamato veraṃ na cīyati;

Kusalo ca jahāti pāpakaṃ,

Rāgadosamohakkhayā sanibbuto’’ti.

Catuttho bhāṇavāro.

Yamakasālā
mula_english:
197. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "It may come to pass, Ānanda, that someone will cause remorse to Cunda the metalworker, saying: ‘It is no gain to you, friend Cunda, but a loss, that it was from you the *Tathāgata* took his last alms meal, and then came to his end.’

"In this way, Ānanda, the remorse of Cunda the metalworker should be dispelled: ‘It is a gain to you, friend Cunda, a blessing that the *Tathāgata* took his last alms meal from you, and then came to his end.

"For, friend Cunda, I have heard and understood from the Lord’s own lips that these two alms-givings are of very great fruit, of very great result, more fruitful and advantageous than any other.

"Which two? There is that alms offering which when a *Tathāgata* has eaten he attains unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment (*sammāsambodhi*), and that which when he has eaten he attains final *Nibbāna* in the *Nibbāna*-element (*nibbānadhātu*) that has no substrate remaining for further existence.

"These two alms-givings are more fruitful and profitable than all others.

"By his deed the worthy Cunda has accumulated *karma* (*kamma*) which makes for long life, beauty, well being, glory, heavenly rebirth, and sovereignty.”

"In this way, Ānanda, Cunda the metalworker’s remorse should be allayed.”

Then, the Blessed One, having understood the matter, on that occasion, uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):

“Generosity increases merit (*puñña*);
Restraint does not generate enmity (*vera*);
The skillful abandon evil;
With the destruction of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, one is at peace (*sanibbuto*).”

The fourth chapter on recitation.

The Twin Sala Trees.
commentary_pali:
197.Alābhāti ye aññesaṃ dānānisaṃsasaṅkhātā lābhā honti, te alābhā. Dulladdhanti puññavisesena laddhampi manussattaṃ dulladdhaṃ. Yassa teti yassa tava. Uttaṇḍulaṃ vā atikilinnaṃ vā ko jānāti, kīdisampi pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato parinibbuto, addhā te yaṃ vā taṃ vā dinnaṃ bhavissatīti. Lābhāti diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikadānānisaṃsasaṅkhātā lābhā. Suladdhanti tuyhaṃ manussattaṃ suladdhaṃ. Samasamaphalāti sabbākārena samānaphalā.

Nanu ca yaṃ sujātāya dinnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā tathāgato abhisambuddho, so sarāgasadosasamohakāle paribhutto, ayaṃ pana cundena dinno vītarāgavītadosavītamohakāle paribhutto, kasmā ete samaphalāti? Parinibbānasamatāya ca samāpattisamatāya ca anussaraṇasamatāya ca. Bhagavā hi sujātāya dinnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā saupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto, cundena dinnaṃ paribhuñjitvā anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbutoti evaṃ parinibbānasamatāyapi samaphalā. Abhisambujjhanadivase ca catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā samāpattiyo samāpajji, parinibbānadivasepi sabbā tā samāpajjīti evaṃ samāpattisamatāyapi samaphalā. Sujātā ca aparabhāge assosi – ‘‘na kiresā rukkhadevatā, bodhisatto kiresa, taṃ kira piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho , sattasattāhaṃ kirassa tena yāpanaṃ ahosī’’ti. Tassā idaṃ sutvā – ‘‘lābhā vata me’’ti anussarantiyā balavapītisomanassaṃ udapādi. Cundassāpi aparabhāge – ‘‘avasānapiṇḍapāto kira mayā dinno, dhammasīsaṃ kira me gahitaṃ, mayhaṃ kira piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā satthā anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’’ti sutvā ‘‘lābhā vata me’’ti anussarato balavasomanassaṃ udapādīti evaṃ anussaraṇasamatāyapi samaphalāti veditabbā.

parinibbānasamatāya samāpattisamatāyapi anussaraṇasamatāya

Yasasaṃvattanikanti parivārasaṃvattanikaṃ. Ādhipateyyasaṃvattanikanti jeṭṭhakabhāvasaṃvattanikaṃ.

Yasasaṃvattanika Ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika

Saṃyamatoti sīlasaṃyamena saṃyamantassa, saṃvare ṭhitassāti attho. Veraṃ na cīyatīti pañcavidhaṃ veraṃ na vaḍḍhati. Kusalo ca jahāti pāpakanti kusalo pana ñāṇasampanno ariyamaggena anavasesaṃ pāpakaṃ lāmakaṃ akusalaṃ jahāti. Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbutoti so imaṃ pāpakaṃ jahitvā rāgādīnaṃ khayā kilesanibbānena nibbutoti. Iti cundassa ca dakkhiṇaṃ, attano ca dakkhiṇeyyasampattiṃ sampassamāno udānaṃ udānesīti.

Saṃyamato Veraṃ na cīyatī Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto

Catutthabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Yamakasālāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
197. *Alābhā*: "non-gains," meaning those gains that are accounted as benefits of giving (dāna) to others are, in fact, non-gains.
*Dulladdha*: "ill-obtained," meaning that even a human existence obtained through the power of merit (*puṇya*) is ill-obtained.
*Yassa te*: "whose is yours," meaning "whose is thine."
Who knows whether it was hulled or over-soaked, the last alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) that the *Tathāgata* ate before attaining complete extinction (*parinibbāna*)? Assuredly, whatever was given to you will come to pass.
*Lābhā*: "gains," meaning those gains that are accounted as the benefits of giving ( *dāna*) in this life and the next.
*Suladdha*: "well-obtained," meaning this human existence of yours is well-obtained.
*Samasamaphalā*: "equally equal result," meaning results equal in every way.

Now, the alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) that was given to Sujātā, which the *Tathāgata* ate and attained complete enlightenment (*abhisambuddho*), was enjoyed during a time of passion (*sarāga*), hatred (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*). But this alms-food that was given by Cunda was enjoyed during a time devoid of passion (*vītarāga*), devoid of hatred (*vītadosa*), and devoid of delusion (*vītamoha*). Why are these results equal? [They are equal] because of the equality of final extinction (*parinibbānasamatā*), the equality of attainments (*samāpattisamatā*), and the equality of remembrance (*anussaraṇasamatā*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*), having eaten the alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) given by Sujātā and attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) with a remainder of the substrata (*saupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*), and having eaten the alms-food given by Cunda and attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) without a remainder of the substrata (*anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*), thus, the equality of final extinction (*parinibbānasamatā*) is also an equal result.
On the day of complete enlightenment (*abhisambujjhanadivase*) and having attained countless (*catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā*) meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), on the day of final extinction (*parinibbānadivase*) also, all those [attainments] were attained. Thus, the equality of attainments (*samāpattisamatā*) is also an equal result.
Sujātā, at another time, heard – "This is not a tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*); this is a *bodhisattva*. Having eaten this alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*), he has attained unsurpassed complete perfect enlightenment (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ*), and for seven weeks he lived on that."
Having heard this, she remembered – "Gains to me indeed!", and a strong joy and gladness (*balavapītisomanassaṃ*) arose.
To Cunda also, at another time – "The final alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) was given by me; the head of the *Dharma* was taken by me; having eaten the alms-food from me, the Teacher (*satthā*) attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) without a remainder of the substrata (*anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*)," having heard this, he remembered – "Gains to me indeed!", and a strong gladness (*balavasomanassaṃ*) arose. Thus, it should be understood that the equality of remembrance (*anussaraṇasamatā*) is also an equal result.

*Parinibbānasamatāya*. *Samāpattisamatāyapi*. *Anussaraṇasamatāya*.
*Yasasaṃvattanika* means conducive to retinue (*parivārasaṃvattanikaṃ*).
*ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika* means conducive to chieftainship (*jeṭṭhakabhāvasaṃvattanikaṃ*).

*Yasasaṃvattanika*. *ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika*.
*Saṃyamato* means for one who is restrained by the restraint of morality (*sīlasaṃyamena saṃyamantassa*), for one established in restraint (*saṃvare ṭhitassāti attho*).
*Veraṃ na cīyatī* means five kinds of enmity (*pañcavidhaṃ veraṃ*) do not increase (*na vaḍḍhati*).
*Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka* means the skillful one (*kusalo*), the one endowed with wisdom (*ñāṇasampanno*), by means of the noble path (*ariyamaggena*), abandons completely (*anavasesaṃ*) evil (*pāpakaṃ*), base (*lāmakaṃ*), unskillful (*akusalaṃ*).
*Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto* means he, having abandoned this evil (*pāpakaṃ jahitvā*) by means of the destruction of passion (*rāga*), etc., is extinguished (*nibbuto*) by the extinction of defilements (*kilesanibbānena*).

Thus, Cunda's giving (*dakkhiṇaṃ*), and he himself, seeing the accomplishment of worthy recipients (*dakkhiṇeyyasampattiṃ sampassamāno*), uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesīti*).

*Saṃyamato*. *Veraṃ na cīyatī*. *Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka*. *Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto*.
The commentary on the fourth division for recitation is finished.

Explanation of the Yamaka Sala.

mula_pali:
198. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti . ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno.

Tena kho pana samayena yamakasālā sabbaphāliphullā honti akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya.
mula_english:
198. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Come, Ānanda, let us cross to the farther bank of the Hiraññavatī River, and go to the Mallas’ Sāla Grove, in the vicinity of Kusinārā.”

“So be it, Lord.” And the Venerable Ānanda answered the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One with a large *Saṅgha* of monks went to the far shore of the Hiraññavatī River, to Upavattana, the Mallans’ Sal Forest near Kusinārā.

On arrival, he said to Ven. Ānanda, “Please, Ānanda, prepare for me a couch between the twin *yamaka-sāla* trees, with the head to the north. I am weary, Ānanda, and want to lie down.”

“So be it, Lord.” And the Venerable Ānanda, having promised the Blessed One, prepared a bed between the twin *yamaka-sāla* trees, with its head to the north.

Then the Fortunate One lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, after placing one foot on the top of the other, mindfully, with full awareness.

Now at that time the Twin Sal Trees were full of flowering blossoms, outside of flowering time.

They shower, strew, & sprinkle on the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage to him.

Heavenly coral-tree blossoms fell from the sky, showering, strewing, & sprinkling the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage to him.

divine sandal-wood powder fell from the sky, sprinkling and covering the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage.

Heavenly music was playing in the sky, in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

Heavenly songs were sung in the sky, in homage to the *Tathāgata*.
commentary_pali:
198.Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhinti idha bhikkhūnaṃ gaṇanaparicchedo natthi. Veḷuvagāme vedanāvikkhambhanato paṭṭhāya hi – ‘‘na cirena bhagavā parinibbāyissatī’’ti sutvā tato tato āgatesu bhikkhūsu ekabhikkhupi pakkanto nāma natthi. Tasmā gaṇanavītivatto saṅgho ahosi. Upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavananti yatheva hi kalambanadītīrato rājamātuvihāradvārena thūpārāmaṃ gantabbaṃ hoti, evaṃ hiraññavatiyā pārimatīrato sālavanuyyānaṃ, yathā anurādhapurassa thūpārāmo, evaṃ taṃ kusinārāyaṃ hoti. Yathā thūpārāmato dakkhiṇadvārena nagaraṃ pavisanamaggo pācīnamukho gantvā uttarena nivatto, evaṃ uyyānato sālavanaṃ pācīnamukhaṃ gantvā uttarena nivattaṃ. Tasmā taṃ – ‘‘upavattana’’nti vuccati. Antarena yamakasālānaṃuttarasīsakanti tassa kira mañcakassa ekā sālapanti sīsabhāge hoti, ekā pādabhāge. Tatrāpi eko taruṇasālo sīsabhāgassa āsanno hoti, eko pādabhāgassa. Api ca yamakasālā nāma mūlakhandhaviṭapapattehi aññamaññaṃ saṃsibbitvā ṭhitasālāti vuttaṃ. Mañcakaṃ paññapehīti tasmiṃ kira uyyāne rājakulassa sayanamañco atthi, taṃ sandhāya paññapehīti āha. Theropi taṃyeva paññapetvā adāsi.

Kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmīti tathāgatassa hi –

Kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī

‘‘Gocari kaḷāpo gaṅgeyyo, piṅgalo pabbateyyako;

Hemavato ca tambo ca, mandākini uposatho;

Chaddantoyeva dasamo, ete nāgānamuttamā’’ti. –

Ettha yaṃ dasannaṃ gocarisaṅkhātānaṃ pakatihatthīnaṃ balaṃ, taṃ ekassa kaḷāpassāti. Evaṃ dasaguṇavaḍḍhitāya gaṇanāya pakatihatthīnaṃ koṭisahassabalappamāṇaṃ balaṃ, taṃ sabbampi cundassa piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuttakālato paṭṭhāya caṅgavāre pakkhittaudakaṃ viya parikkhayaṃ gataṃ. Pāvānagarato tīṇi gāvutāni kusinārānagaraṃ, etasmiṃ antare pañcavīsatiyā ṭhānesu nisīditvā mahatā ussāhena āgacchantopi sūriyassa atthaṅgamitavelāyaṃ sañjhāsamaye bhagavā sālavanaṃ paviṭṭho. Evaṃ rogo sabbaṃ ārogyaṃ maddanto āgacchati. Etamatthaṃ dassento viya sabbalokassa saṃvegakaraṃ vācaṃ bhāsanto – ‘‘kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī’’ti āha.

Kasmā pana bhagavā evaṃ mahantena ussāhena idhāgato, kiṃ aññattha na sakkā parinibbāyitunti? Parinibbāyituṃ nāma na katthaci na sakkā, tīhi pana kāraṇehi idhāgato, idañhi bhagavā evaṃ passati – ‘‘mayi aññattha parinibbāyante mahāsudassanasuttassa atthuppatti na bhavissati, kusinārāyaṃ pana parinibbāyante yamahaṃ devaloke anubhavitabbaṃ sampattiṃ manussalokeyeva anubhaviṃ, taṃ dvīhi bhāṇavārehi maṇḍetvā desessāmi, taṃ me sutvā bahū janā kusalaṃ kātabbaṃ maññissantī’’ti.

Aparampi passati – ‘‘maṃ aññattha parinibbāyantaṃ subhaddo na passissati, so ca buddhaveneyyo , na sāvakaveneyyo; na taṃ sāvakā vinetuṃ sakkonti. Kusinārāyaṃ parinibbāyantaṃ pana maṃ so upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchissati, pañhāvissajjanapariyosāne ca saraṇesu patiṭṭhāya mama santike pabbajjañca upasampadañca labhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā mayi dharamāneyeva arahattaṃ patvā pacchimasāvako bhavissatī’’ti.

Aparampi passati – ‘‘mayi aññattha parinibbāyante dhātubhājanīye mahākalaho bhavissati, lohitaṃ nadī viya sandissati. Kusinārāyaṃ parinibbute doṇabrāhmaṇo taṃ vivādaṃ vūpasametvā dhātuyo vibhajissatī’’ti. Imehi tīhi kāraṇehi bhagavā evaṃ mahantena ussāhena idhāgatoti veditabbo.

Sīhaseyyanti ettha kāmabhogīseyyā, petaseyyā, sīhaseyyā, tathāgataseyyāti catasso seyyā.

Sīhaseyya

Tattha – ‘‘yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, kāmabhogī sattā vāmena passena sentī’’ti ayaṃ kāmabhogīseyyā. Tesu hi yebhuyyena dakkhiṇena passena sayantā nāma natthi.

kāmabhogīseyyā.

‘‘Yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, petā uttānā sentī’’ti ayaṃ petaseyyā. Appamaṃsalohitattā hi petā aṭṭhisaṅghāṭajaṭitā ekena passena sayituṃ na sakkonti, uttānāva senti.

petaseyyā.

‘‘Sīho, bhikkhave, migarājā dakkhiṇena passena seyyaṃ kappeti…pe… attamano hotī’’ti (a. ni. 4.246) ayaṃ sīhaseyyā. Tejussadattā hi sīho migarājā dve purimapāde ekasmiṃ ṭhāne, pacchimapāde ekasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhapetvā naṅguṭṭhaṃ antarasatthimhi pakkhipitvā purimapādapacchimapādanaṅguṭṭhānaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkhetvā dvinnaṃ purimapādānaṃ matthake sīsaṃ ṭhapetvā sayati. Divasaṃ sayitvāpi pabujjhamāno na utrasanto pabujjhati, sīsaṃ pana ukkhipitvā purimapādādīnaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkheti. Sace kiñci ṭhānaṃ vijahitvā ṭhitaṃ hoti – ‘‘na yidaṃ tuyhaṃ jātiyā sūrabhāvassa ca anurūpa’’nti anattamano hutvā tattheva sayati, na gocarāya pakkamati. Avijahitvā ṭhite pana – ‘‘tuyhaṃ jātiyā ca sūrabhāvassa ca anurūpamida’’nti haṭṭhatuṭṭho uṭṭhāya sīhavijambhitaṃ vijambhitvā kesarabhāraṃ vidhunitvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkamati.

sīhaseyyā.

‘‘Catutthajjhānaseyyā pana tathāgatassa seyyāti vuccati’’ (a. ni. 4.246). Tāsu idha sīhaseyyā āgatā. Ayañhi tejussadairiyāpathattā uttamaseyyā nāma.

tathāgatassa seyyā

Pāde pādanti dakkhiṇapāde vāmapādaṃ. Accādhāyāti atiādhāya, īsakaṃ atikkamma ṭhapetvā. Gopphakena hi gopphake, jāṇunā vā jāṇumhi saṅghaṭṭiyamāne abhiṇhaṃ vedanā uppajjati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ na hoti, seyyā aphāsukā hoti. Yathā pana na saṅghaṭṭeti, evaṃ atikkamma ṭhapite vedanā nuppajjati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, seyyā phāsu hoti. Tasmā evaṃ nipajji. Anuṭṭhānaseyyaṃ upagatattā panettha – ‘‘uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā’’ti na vuttaṃ. Kāyavasena cettha anuṭṭhānaṃ veditabbaṃ, niddāvasena pana taṃ rattiṃ bhagavato bhavaṅgassa okāsoyeva nāhosi. Paṭhamayāmasmiñhi mallānaṃ dhammadesanā ahosi, majjhimayāme subhaddassa pacchimayāme bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ovadi, balavapaccūse parinibbāyi.

Pāde pāda Accādhāyā

Sabbaphāliphullāti sabbe samantato pupphitā mūlato paṭṭhāya yāva aggā ekacchannā ahesuṃ, na kevalañca yamakasālāyeva, sabbepi rukkhā sabbapāliphullāva ahesuṃ. Na kevalañhi tasmiṃyeva uyyāne, sakalañhipi dasasahassacakkavāḷe pupphūpagā pupphaṃ gaṇhiṃsu, phalūpagā phalaṃ gaṇhiṃsu, sabbarukkhānaṃ khandhesu khandhapadumāni, sākhāsu sākhāpadumāni, vallīsu vallipadumāni, ākāsesu ākāsapadumāni pathavītalaṃ bhinditvā daṇḍapadumāni pupphiṃsu. Sabbo mahāsamuddo pañcavaṇṇapadumasañchanno ahosi. Tiyojanasahassavitthato himavā ghanabaddhamorapiñchakalāpo viya, nirantaraṃ mālādāmagavacchiko viya, suṭṭhu pīḷetvā ābaddhapupphavaṭaṃsako viya, supūritaṃ pupphacaṅkoṭakaṃ viya ca atiramaṇīyo ahosi.

Sabbaphāliphullā

Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantīti te yamakasālā bhummadevatāhi sañcalitakhandhasākhaviṭapā tathāgatassa sarīraṃ avakiranti, sarīrassa upari pupphāni vikirantīti attho. Ajjhokirantīti ajjhottharantā viya kiranti. Abhippakirantīti abhiṇhaṃ punappunaṃ pakirantiyeva. Dibbānīti devaloke nandapokkharaṇīsambhavāni, tāni honti suvaṇṇavaṇṇāni paṇṇacchattappamāṇapattāni, mahātumbamattaṃ reṇuṃ gaṇhanti. Na kevalañca mandāravapupphāneva, aññānipi pana dibbāni pāricchattakakoviḷārapupphādīni suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭakāni pūretvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyampi tidasapurepi brahmalokepi ṭhitāhi devatāhi paviṭṭhāni, antalikkhā patanti. Tathāgatassa sarīranti antarā avikiṇṇāneva āgantvā pattakiñjakkhareṇucuṇṇehi tathāgatassa sarīrameva okiranti.

Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantī Ajjhokirantī Abhippakirantī Dibbānī Tathāgatassa sarīra

Dibbānipicandanacuṇṇānīti devatānaṃ upakappanacandanacuṇṇāni. Na kevalañca devatānaṃyeva, nāgasupaṇṇamanussānampi upakappanacandanacuṇṇāni. Na kevalañca candanacuṇṇāneva, kāḷānusārikalohitacandanādisabbadibbagandhajālacuṇṇāni, haritālaañjanasuvaṇṇarajatacuṇṇāni sabbadibbagandhavāsavikatiyo suvaṇṇarajatādisamugge pūretvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiādīsu ṭhitāhi devatāhi paviṭṭhāni antarā avippakiritvā tathāgatasseva sarīraṃ okiranti.

Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇānī

Dibbānipi tūriyānīti devatānaṃ upakappanatūriyāni. Na kevalañca tāniyeva, sabbānipi tantibaddhacammapariyonaddhaghanasusirabhedāni dasasahassacakkavāḷesu devanāgasupaṇṇamanussānaṃ tūriyāni ekacakkavāḷe sannipatitvā antalikkhe vajjantīti veditabbāni.

Dibbānipi tūriyānī

Dibbānipi saṅgītānīti varuṇavāraṇadevatā kira nāmetā dīghāyukā devatā – ‘‘mahāpuriso manussapathe nibbattitvā buddho bhavissatī’’ti sutvā ‘‘paṭisandhiggahaṇadivase naṃ gahetvā gamissāmā’’ti mālaṃ ganthetumārabhiṃsu. Tā ganthamānāva – ‘‘mahāpuriso mātukucchiyaṃ nibbatto’’ti sutvā ‘‘tumhe kassa ganthathā’’ti vuttā ‘‘na tāva niṭṭhāti, kucchito nikkhamanadivase gaṇhitvā gamissāmā’’ti āhaṃsu. Punapi ‘‘nikkhanto’’ti sutvā ‘‘mahābhinikkhamanadivase gamissāmā’’ti. Ekūnatiṃsavassāni ghare vasitvā ‘‘ajja mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhanto’’tipi sutvā ‘‘abhisambodhidivase gamissāmā’’ti. Chabbassāni padhānaṃ katvā ‘‘ajja abhisambuddho’’tipi sutvā ‘‘dhammacakkappavattanadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Sattasattāhāni bodhimaṇḍe vītināmetvā isipatanaṃ gantvā dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’’ntipi sutvā ‘‘yamakapāṭihāriyadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ karī’’tipi sutvā ‘‘devorohaṇadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja devorohaṇaṃ karī’’tipi sutvā ‘‘āyusaṅkhārossajjane gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’tipi sutvā ‘‘na tāva niṭṭhāti, parinibbānadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja bhagavā yamakasālānamantare dakkhiṇena passena sato sampajāno sīhaseyyaṃ upagato balavapaccūsasamaye parinibbāyissati. Tumhe kassa ganthathā’’ti sutvā pana – ‘‘kinnāmetaṃ, ‘ajjeva mātukucchiyaṃ paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi, ajjeva mātukucchito nikkhami, ajjeva mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhami, ajjeva buddho ahosi, ajjeva dhammacakkaṃ pavattayi, ajjeva yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ akāsi, ajjeva devalokā otiṇṇo, ajjeva āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, ajjeva kira parinibbāyissatī’ti. Nanu nāma dutiyadivase yāgupānakālamattampi ṭhātabbaṃ assa. Dasa pāramiyo pūretvā buddhattaṃ pattassa nāma ananucchavikameta’’nti apariniṭṭhitāva mālāyo gahetvā āgamma anto cakkavāḷe okāsaṃ alabhamānā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ lambitvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyāva ādhāvantiyo hatthena hatthaṃ gīvāya gīvaṃ gahetvā tīṇi ratanāni ārabbha dvattiṃsa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni chabbaṇṇarasmiyo dasa pāramiyo aḍḍhachaṭṭhāni jātakasatāni cuddasa buddhañāṇāni ārabbha gāyitvā tassa tassa avasāne ‘‘mahāyaso, mahāyaso’’ti vadanti. Idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ – ‘‘dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāyā’’ti.

Dibbānipi saṅgītānī
commentary_english:
198. "With a great *bhikkhu-saṃgha*": Here, there is no calculation or limitation of the *bhikkhu*s.

From the time of the suppression of the feeling in the *veḷuvagāma*, indeed, having heard that "The Blessed One will not attain *parinirvāṇa* soon," among the *bhikkhu*s who came from here and there, there was not even one *bhikkhu* who departed.

Therefore, the *saṃgha* was beyond calculation.

"*Upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ*": Just as, indeed, from the bank of the *kalamba* river, by the gate of the *rājamātuvihāra*, the *thūpārāma* is to be reached, it is, and so it is with Kusinārā.

Just as from the *thūpārāma* by the southern gate, the road for entering the city faces east, having gone to the north, it turns back, so from the garden, the *sālavana* faces east, having gone to the north, it turns back.

Therefore, it is called "*upavattana*."

"*Antarena yamakasālānaṃ*, *uttarasīsaka*": Of that couch, it seems, one row of *sāla* trees is at the head end, one at the foot end.

Even there, one young *sāla* tree is near the head end, one at the foot end.

Moreover, "*yamakasālā*" means *sāla* trees standing intertwined with each other by roots, trunks, branches, and leaves.

"*Mañcakaṃ paññapehī*": In that garden, it seems, there is a royal couch. With reference to that, he said, "Prepare [it]."

The Elder, having prepared that very thing, gave it.

"I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down": Indeed, of the *tathāgata*:

"I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down."

"Gocari Kaḷāpo Gaṅgeyyo, Piṅgalo Pabbateyyako;

Hemavato ca Tambo ca, Mandākinī Uposatho;

Chaddantoyeva Dasamo, Ete Nāgānamuttamā."

Here, the strength of ten ordinary elephants, reckoned as *gocarisaṅkhātānaṃ*, is that of one *kaḷāpa*.

Thus, by calculation increased tenfold, the strength of the ordinary elephants, a mass of strength of a hundred thousand *koṭi*, all of that, from the time of consuming Cunda's alms-food, was exhausted like water thrown into a cesspool.

From Pāvā-nagara three *gāvuta*s to Kusinārā-nagara, in this interval, having sat down in twenty-five places, though coming with great effort, at the time when the sun had set, at the time of twilight, the Blessed One entered the *sālavana*.

Thus, disease comes crushing all health.

As if showing this meaning, speaking a speech that causes agitation to the whole world – "I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down," he said.

Why, indeed, did the Blessed One come here with such great effort? Is it not possible to attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere? To attain *parinirvāṇa* is not impossible anywhere, but he came here for three reasons. For the Blessed One sees thus: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, the arising of the meaning of the *mahāsudassanasutta* will not occur.

But if I attain *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, I will beautify with two recitations, and teach, that accomplishment that I experienced in the *devaloka* right here in the world of humans. Having heard that from me, many people will think that good should be done."

Moreover, he sees: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, Subhadda will not see me, and he is to be trained by the Buddha, not to be trained by a disciple; the disciples cannot train him.

But if I attain *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, having approached me, he will ask a question, and at the end of the answer to the question, having been established in the refuges, and having received the going forth and the full ordination in my presence, having taken up a meditation subject, while I am still existing, having attained *arahatta*, he will become the last disciple."

Moreover, he sees: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, there will be a great quarrel in the sharing of the relics. Blood will appear like a river.

Having attained *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, the *doṇabrāhmaṇa* will calm that dispute, and will divide the relics."

By these three reasons, it should be understood that the Blessed One came here with such great effort.

"*Sīhaseyya*": Here, *kāmabhogīseyyā*, *petaseyyā*, *sīhaseyyā*, *tathāgataseyyā*—these are the four ways of lying down.

"*Sīhaseyya*": There – "For the most part, *bhikkhu*s, beings who enjoy sensual pleasures lie down on their left side"—this is the *kāmabhogīseyyā*.

Among those, indeed, there is no one who lies down on their right side for the most part.

"*Kāmabhogīseyyā*."

"For the most part, *bhikkhu*s, ghosts lie down supine"—this is the *petaseyyā*.

Because of having little flesh and blood, indeed, ghosts, tangled with a skeleton, are not able to lie down on one side, they lie down only supine.

"*Petaseyyā*."
"The lion, monks, the king of beasts, arranges his lying down on his right side... content in mind" (A.N. 4.246): this is the lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*).

For the lion, the king of beasts, has vigor and strength; he places his two forepaws in one place, his hind paws in another place, tucks his tail between his thighs, observes the space where the forepaws, hind paws, and tail are situated, and lies down placing his head on top of the two forepaws.

Even after sleeping during the day, he awakens without trembling; but raising his head, he observes the place where the forepaws, etc., are situated. If any place has been abandoned, having moved from its position, he becomes discontent, thinking, "This is not befitting your birth and bravery," and he lies down right there, not setting out for pasture. But if they remain without having moved from their position, delighted and pleased, he gets up, stretches in the lion's stretch (*sīhavijambhitaṃ vijambhitvā*), shakes out his mane (*kesarabhāraṃ vidhunitvā*), roars the lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ naditvā*) three times, and sets out for pasture.

lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*)

"The fourth jhāna posture (*catutthajjhānaseyyā*), however, is called the *Tathāgata's posture* (*tathāgatassa seyyā*)" (A.N. 4.246). Among those, the lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*) is mentioned here. For this, due to the vigor and strength of its deportment, is called the supreme posture (*uttamaseyyā*).

*Tathāgata's posture* (*tathāgatassa seyyā*)

"*Foot on foot* (*pāde pāda*)": the left foot on the right foot. "*Having over-placed* (*accādhāyā*)": having placed it slightly crossing over. For if ankle is pressed against ankle, or knee against knee, pain frequently arises, the mind is not one-pointed, and the lying down is uncomfortable. However, when it is placed crossing over in such a way that they do not press against each other, pain does not arise, the mind is one-pointed, and the lying down is comfortable. Therefore, he lies down thus.

Since he has approached the posture of non-rising (*anuṭṭhānaseyyaṃ*), therefore it is not said here, "Having made the perception of rising in his mind." Here, non-rising should be understood in terms of the body; but in terms of sleep, there was no opportunity at all for the Blessed One's life-continuum (*bhavaṅgassa*) during that night. For in the first watch, there was a teaching of the Dhamma to the Mallas; in the middle watch, to Subhadda; in the last watch, he exhorted the community of monks; and in the strong dawn, he attained final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāyi*).

*Foot on foot* (*pāde pāda*) *Having over-placed* (*accādhāyā*)

"*All in full bloom* (*sabbaphāliphullā*)": all were in bloom on all sides, from the root up to the tip, uniformly covered. And not only the twin *sāla* trees, but all the trees were all in full bloom.

For not only in that park alone, but also in the entire ten-thousand world-system (*dasasahassacakkavāḷe*), those fit for flowers took flowers, those fit for fruit took fruit; on the trunks of all the trees were trunk-lotuses, on the branches were branch-lotuses, on the vines were vine-lotuses, in the skies were sky-lotuses, and breaking through the surface of the earth were stalk-lotuses. The entire great ocean was covered with five-colored lotuses. The Himalayas, three thousand yojanas in extent, was like a densely bound peacock's tail feather, like an uninterrupted garland creeper, like a well-pressed, tied flower diadem, and like a fully filled flower basket (*pupphacaṅkoṭakaṃ*), and was exceedingly lovely.

*All in full bloom* (*sabbaphāliphullā*)

"*They were strewing the body of the Tathāgata* (*te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantī*)": those twin *sāla* trees, with their trunks, branches, and boughs moved by the earth-bound deities, were scattering flowers on the body of the Tathāgata, meaning they were strewing flowers on top of the body. "*Scattering over* (*ajjhokirantī*)": they scatter as if spreading over. "*Strewn upon* (*abhippakirantī*)": scattering again and again, repeatedly. "*Divine* (*dibbānī*)": born in the Nanda lotus pond in the world of the gods; those are golden in color, with petals the size of a sunshade, holding pollen the size of a large gourd. And not only *mandārava* flowers alone, but also other divine *pāricchattaka*, *kovidāra*, and other flowers, having filled golden baskets (*suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭakāni*), were thrown by the deities standing at the edge of the world-wheel, in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, and even in the Brahmā world, falling from the sky.
The body of the *tathāgata*, without being scattered in between, having come, with powders of lotus filaments, they sprinkled the body of the *tathāgata*.

Those, sprinkling, scattering, and thoroughly scattering the body of the *tathāgata*, [with] divine...

The body of the *tathāgata*. Divine *candanacuṇṇāni*, divine sandalwood powder prepared for the gods.

Not only for the gods, but also for the *nāgas*, *supaṇṇas*, and humans, [there were] prepared sandalwood powders.

Not only sandalwood powder, but also *kāḷānusārika*, *lohitacandana*, and all sorts of divine fragrant *jāla* powders, *haritāla*, *añjana*, gold, silver powders, all sorts of divine fragrant substances, filling the gold, silver, and other containers, those gods situated in the *cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭi* and others, having entered, without scattering in between, sprinkled the body of the *tathāgata*.

Divine...

Divine *candanacuṇṇāni*, divine musical instruments, musical instruments prepared for the gods.

Not only those, but all sorts of stringed, leather-bound, fully covered, hollow instruments, the musical instruments of gods, *nāgas*, *supaṇṇas*, and humans in ten thousand world systems, having assembled in one world system, are known to play in the sky.

Divine musical instruments, divine songs—the deities *varuṇa* and *vāraṇa*, it is said, these long-lived deities, having heard that “A great man, having been born in the human path, will become a Buddha,” began to string garlands, [thinking,] “On the day of conception, we will take him and go.”

Those stringing garlands, having heard that “A great man has been born in his mother’s womb,” when asked, “For whom are you stringing these?”, said, “It is not yet finished; on the day of his departure from the womb, we will take him and go.”

Again, having heard that “He has departed,” [they said,] “On the day of the Great Departure, we will go.”

Having lived in the house for twenty-nine years, having heard that “Today, he has gone forth on the Great Departure,” [they said,] “On the day of enlightenment, we will go.”

Having practiced asceticism for six years, having heard that “Today, he has become enlightened,” [they said,] “On the day of the turning of the wheel of Dharma, we will go.”

“Having spent seven weeks at the *bodhimaṇḍa*, having gone to *isipatana*, the wheel of Dharma was turned,” having heard this too, [they said,] “On the day of the Twin Miracle, we will go.”

“Today, he performed the Twin Miracle,” having heard this, [they said,] “On the day of the descent from the heavens, we will go.”

“Today, there is the descent from the heavens,” having heard this, [they said,] “At the abandonment of the life force, we will go.”

“Today, he has abandoned the life force,” having heard this, [they said,] “It is not yet finished; on the day of *parinirvāṇa*, we will go.”

“Today, the Blessed One, between the twin *sāla* trees, lying down on his right side, mindful and fully aware, having attained the lion’s posture, at the strong dawn, will pass into *parinirvāṇa*.”

Having heard this, [they asked,] “For whom are you stringing these garlands?”  They responded, “What is this? ‘Today itself, he took rebirth in his mother’s womb, today itself he departed from his mother’s womb, today itself he went forth on the Great Departure, today itself he became a Buddha, today itself he turned the wheel of Dharma, today itself he performed the Twin Miracle, today itself he descended from the heavens, today itself he abandoned the life force, today itself he will pass into *parinirvāṇa*.’

Indeed, by the second day, he should remain only for the time of drinking gruel. It is not fitting for one who has fulfilled the ten perfections and attained Buddhahood.” Having not yet finished [stringing] the garlands, taking the garlands, having come inside the universe, not finding an opportunity, hanging down on the rim of the universe, running towards the rim of the universe, with hand in hand, neck to neck, having taken hold, and beginning with the three jewels, the thirty-two marks of a great man, the six-colored rays, the ten perfections, two and a half *jātaka* hundreds, fourteen Buddha knowledges, singing, at the end of each, they say, “Great fame, great fame.”

Having relied on this, it was said: “Divine songs proceed in the sky in worship of the *tathāgata*.”

Divine songs...

mula_pali:
199. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘sabbaphāliphullā kho, ānanda, yamakasālā akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Na kho, ānanda, ettāvatā tathāgato sakkato vā hoti garukato vā mānito vā pūjito vā apacito vā. Yo kho, ānanda, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tathāgataṃ sakkaroti garuṃ karoti māneti pūjeti apaciyati idaṃ padaṃ sīsyāipotthakesu na dissati, paramāya pūjāya. Tasmātihānanda, dhammānudhammappaṭipannā viharissāma sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārinoti. Evañhi vo, ānanda, sikkhitabba’’nti.

Upavāṇatthero
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, the twin *sāla* trees are in full bloom with untimely blossoms.

They shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine *mandārava* flowers fall from the sky; they shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine sandalwood powder falls from the sky; they shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine musical instruments play in the sky in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

Divine songs resound in the sky in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

But it is not in this way, Ānanda, that the *Tathāgata* is honored, respected, esteemed, worshipped, or venerated.

Rather, Ānanda, whichever *bhikṣu* or *bhikṣuṇī*, *upāsaka* or *upāsikā* lives practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), lives practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), and behaves in accordance with the Dhamma (*anudhammacārī*), that person honors, respects, esteems, worships, and venerates the *Tathāgata* with the highest worship (*paramāya pūjāya*).

Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will live practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammappaṭipannā*), live practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipannā*), and behave in accordance with the Dhamma (*anudhammacārino*)’.

Thus, Ānanda, should you train yourselves."

Upavāṇa the Elder
commentary_pali:
199. Bhagavā pana yamakasālānaṃ antarā dakkhiṇena passena nipannoyeva pathavītalato yāva cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyā, cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭito ca yāva brahmalokā sannipatitāya parisāya mahantaṃ ussāhaṃ disvā āyasmato ānandassa ārocesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ…pe… tathāgatassa pūjāyā’’ti. Evaṃ mahāsakkāraṃ dassetvā tenāpi attano asakkatabhāvameva dassanto na kho, ānanda, ettāvatātiādimāha.

Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘ānanda, mayā dīpaṅkarapādamūle nipannena aṭṭha dhamme samodhānetvā abhinīhāraṃ karontena na mālāgandhatūriyasaṅgītānaṃ atthāya abhinīhāro kato, na etadatthāya pāramiyo pūritā. Tasmā na kho ahaṃ etāya pūjāya pūjito nāma homī’’ti.

Kasmā pana bhagavā aññattha ekaṃ umāpupphamattampi gahetvā buddhaguṇe āvajjetvā katāya pūjāya buddhañāṇenāpi aparicchinnaṃ vipākaṃ vaṇṇetvā idha evaṃ mahantaṃ pūjaṃ paṭikkhipatīti? Parisānuggahena ceva sāsanassa ca ciraṭṭhitikāmatāya. Sace hi bhagavā evaṃ na paṭikkhipeyya, anāgate sīlassa āgataṭṭhāne sīlaṃ na paripūressanti, samādhissa āgataṭṭhāne samādhiṃ na paripūressanti, vipassanāya āgataṭṭhāne vipassanāgabbhaṃ na gāhāpessanti. Upaṭṭhāke samādapetvā pūjaṃyeva kārentā viharissanti. Āmisapūjā ca nāmesā sāsanaṃ ekadivasampi ekayāgupānakālamattampi sandhāretuṃ na sakkoti. Mahāvihārasadisañhi vihārasahassaṃ mahācetiyasadisañca cetiyasahassampi sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkonti. Yena kammaṃ kataṃ, tasseva hoti. Sammāpaṭipatti pana tathāgatassa anucchavikā pūjā. Sā hi tena patthitā ceva, sakkoti sāsanañca sandhāretuṃ, tasmā taṃ dassento yo kho ānandātiādimāha.

yo kho ānandā

Tattha dhammānudhammappaṭipannoti navavidhassa lokuttaradhammassa anudhammaṃ pubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno . Sāyeva pana paṭipadā anucchavikattā ‘‘sāmīcī’’ti vuccati. Taṃ sāmīciṃ paṭipannoti sāmīcippaṭipanno. Tameva pubbabhāgapaṭipadāsaṅkhātaṃ anudhammaṃ carati pūretīti anudhammacārī.

dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno. anudhammacārī.

Pubbabhāgapaṭipadāti ca sīlaṃ ācārapaññatti dhutaṅgasamādānaṃ yāva gotrabhuto sammāpaṭipadā veditabbā. Tasmā yo bhikkhu chasu agāravesu patiṭṭhāya paññattiṃ atikkamati, anesanāya jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno. Yo pana sabbaṃ attano paññattaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ jinavelaṃ jinamariyādaṃ jinakāḷasuttaṃ aṇumattampi na vītikkamati, ayaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipanno nāma. Bhikkhuniyāpi eseva nayo. Yo upāsako pañca verāni dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattati appeti, ayaṃ na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno. Yo pana tīsu saraṇesu, pañcasupi sīlesu, dasasu sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, māsassa aṭṭha uposathe karoti, dānaṃ deti, gandhapūjaṃ mālāpūjaṃ karoti, mātaraṃ pitaraṃ upaṭṭhāti, dhammike samaṇabrāhmaṇe upaṭṭhāti, ayaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipanno nāma. Upāsikāyapi eseva nayo.

Pubbabhāgapaṭipadā

Paramāyapūjāyāti uttamāya pūjāya. Ayañhi nirāmisapūjā nāma sakkoti mama sāsanaṃ sandhāretuṃ. Yāva hi imā catasso parisā maṃ imāya pūjessanti, tāva mama sāsanaṃ majjhe nabhassa puṇṇacando viya virocissatīti dasseti.

Paramāya pūjāyā

Upavāṇattheravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
199. Furthermore, the Blessed One, having lain down between the twin *sāla* trees with his right side, from the surface of the earth up to the circular mouth of the *cakkavāḷa*, and from the circular mouth of the *cakkavāḷa* up to the great effort of the assembly gathered in the Brahmā realm, announced to venerable Ānanda, having seen [it].

That was said by him: "Then, the Blessed One [said] to venerable Ānanda...pe... for the worship of the Tathāgata."

Having shown such great honor, and even showing the state of being incapable of honoring himself by that, he said, beginning with, "No, Ānanda, not with this."

This was said: "Ānanda, by me, having lain down at the base of Dīpaṃkara’s feet, by [me] making an aspiration, having harmonized the eight qualities, [page 2.0578] the aspiration was not made for the sake of garlands, scents, musical instruments, and singing; the perfections were not fulfilled for this purpose. Therefore, I am not called worshiped by this worship."

[Page 2.0578] Why then [page 2.0169] does the Blessed One, having taken even one *umā* flower elsewhere, and having reflected on the qualities of the Buddha, having described the unlimited result even by the knowledge of the Buddha, reject such a great worship here? Due to the favor of the assembly and due to the desire for the long standing of the Dispensation.

If, indeed, the Blessed One would not reject thus, in the future, they will not completely fulfill morality in the place where morality has come; they will not completely fulfill *samādhi* in the place where *samādhi* has come; they will not cause the essence of insight (*vipassanā*) to be grasped in the place where *vipassanā* has come. Having pleased the attendants, they will live only causing worship. And this material worship is not able to maintain the Dispensation even for a single day, even for the time of a single rice-gruel drink. Indeed, thousands of monasteries similar to the Great Monastery and thousands of *cetiya*s similar to the Great *cetiya* are not able to maintain the Dispensation. The *karma* that is done belongs to him alone. Furthermore, right practice is worship befitting the Tathāgata. Indeed, that is desired by him, and it is able to maintain the Dispensation; therefore, showing that, he said, beginning with, "The one, Ānanda."

[Page 2.0169] "The one, Ānanda" [page 2.0152] "Dhammānudhammappaṭipanno": practicing the *anudhamma*, the preliminary practice, of the ninefold supramundane *dharma*,

That practice itself, due to being befitting, is called "proper (*sāmīcī*)". Because he has undertaken that proper [practice], [he is called] "practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*)". Because he lives fulfilling that *anudhamma* known as the preliminary practice, [he is called] "living according to the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*)".

Dhammānudhammappaṭipanno, [page 2.0152] Sāmīcippaṭipanno, Anudhammacārī.

"Preliminary practice (*pubbabhāgapaṭipadā*)" and also morality, rules of conduct, undertaking the *dhuta* practices, up to the mundane right practice, should be understood.

Therefore, that *bhikkhu* who, having stood in the six kinds of disrespect, transgresses the precepts, makes a living by improper means, this one is not practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). But that one who does not transgress even a little all the precepts that he himself has laid down, the proper time of the Jinas, the limit of the Jinas, the black thread of the Jinas, this one is called practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). This is the same method for a *bhikkhunī*.

That lay follower who, having undertaken the five abstinences, [and] the ten unwholesome paths of action, behaves improperly, this one is not practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*).

But that one who is a complete doer in the three refuges, even in the five moralities, [and] in the ten moralities, makes eight *uposatha*s in a month, gives alms, does scent worship, does flower worship, attends to [his] mother [and] father, [page 2.0579] attends to righteous *samaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, this one is called practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). This is the same method for a lay woman.

Preliminary practice (*pubbabhāgapaṭipadā*), [page 2.0579] "for the supreme [page 2.0170] worship (*pūjā*)": for the highest worship. Indeed, this unmaterial worship is able to maintain my Dispensation. Indeed, as long as these four assemblies will worship me with this, so long will my Dispensation shine in the midst of the sky like the full moon, he shows.

mula_pali: 200. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato purato ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāresi – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti. Ko nu kho hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti. Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti? ‘‘Yebhuyyena, ānanda, dasasu lokadhātūsu devatā sannipatitā tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yāvatā, ānanda, kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ samantato dvādasa yojanāni, natthi so padeso vālaggakoṭinitudanamattopi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi apphuṭo. Devatā, ānanda, ujjhāyanti – ‘dūrā ca vatamha āgatā tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ayañca mahesakkho bhikkhu bhagavato purato ṭhito ovārento, na mayaṃ labhāma pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti.
mula_english:
200. Now at that time venerable Upavāṇa was standing in front of the Fortunate One, fanning the Fortunate One.

Then the Fortunate One dismissed venerable Upavāṇa, saying, "Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me."

Then the venerable Ānanda thought: “This venerable Upavāṇa has for long been the Fortunate One’s attendant, keeping close at hand, at his beck and call.

And now in his final hour the Fortunate One tells him to stand aside and not stand in front of him."

What could be the cause, what the reason, that the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, saying, 'Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me?'" Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One: "This, venerable sir, venerable Upavāṇa has for long been the Fortunate One’s attendant, keeping close at hand, at his beck and call.

And now in his final hour the Fortunate One tells him to stand aside and not stand in front of him."

"What now, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, that the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, saying, 'Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me?'" "Ānanda, for the most part, deities have gathered in the ten world-realms to see the *Tathāgata*.

For a distance of twelve *yojanas* around Kusinārā, the Upavattana, the *sāla* grove of the Mallas, there is not a spot that could be pricked with the tip of a hair that is not filled with powerful deities.

The deities, Ānanda, are complaining, ‘From afar have we come to see the *Tathāgata*.

Only occasionally, infrequently, do *Tathāgatas*, worthy ones, perfectly awakened ones arise in the world.

And this day, in the last watch of the night, the *Tathāgata*'s *parinirvāṇa* will come about.

And this eminent *bhikṣu* is standing in front of the Fortunate One, blocking the way. We aren’t getting to see the *Tathāgata* in his final hour.’”
commentary_pali:
200.Apasāresīti apanesi. Apehīti apagaccha. Thero ekavacaneneva tālavaṇṭaṃ nikkhipitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Upaṭṭhākotiādi paṭhamabodhiyaṃ anibaddhupaṭṭhākabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha. Ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā upavāṇoti evaṃ therena vutte ānando upavāṇassa sadosabhāvaṃ sallakkheti, ‘handassa niddosabhāvaṃ kathessāmī’ti bhagavā yebhuyyena ānandātiādimāha. Tattha yebhuyyenāti idaṃ asaññasattānañceva arūpadevatānañca ohīnabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Apphuṭoti asamphuṭṭho abharito vā. Bhagavato kira āsannapadese vālaggamatte okāse sukhumattabhāvaṃ māpetvā dasa dasa mahesakkhā devatā aṭṭhaṃsu. Tāsaṃ parato vīsati vīsati. Tāsaṃ parato tiṃsati tiṃsati. Tāsaṃ parato cattālīsaṃ cattālīsaṃ. Tāsaṃ parato paññāsaṃ paññāsaṃ. Tāsaṃ parato saṭṭhi saṭṭhi devatā aṭṭhaṃsu. Tā aññamaññaṃ hatthena vā pādena vā vatthena vā na byābādhenti. ‘‘Apehi maṃ, mā ghaṭṭehī’’ti vattabbākāraṃ nāma natthi. ‘‘Tā kho pana devatāyo dasapi hutvā vīsatipi hutvā tiṃsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti, na ca aññamaññaṃ byābādhentī’’ti (a. ni. 1.37) vuttasadisāva ahesuṃ. Ovārentoti āvārento. Thero kira pakatiyāpi mahāsarīro hatthipotakasadiso. So paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ pārupitvā atimahā viya ahosi.

Tathāgataṃ dassanāyāti bhagavato mukhaṃ daṭṭhuṃ alabhamānā evaṃ ujjhāyiṃsu. Kiṃ pana tā theraṃ vinivijjha passituṃ na sakkontīti? Āma, na sakkonti. Devatā hi puthujjane vinivijjha passituṃ sakkonti, na khīṇāsave. Therassa ca mahesakkhatāya tejussadatāya upagantumpi na sakkonti. Kasmā pana therova tejussado, na aññe arahantoti? Yasmā kassapabuddhassa cetiye ārakkhadevatā ahosi.

Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā

Vipassimhi kira sammāsambuddhe parinibbute ekagghanasuvaṇṇakkhandhasadisassa dhātusarīrassa ekameva cetiyaṃ akaṃsu, dīghāyukabuddhānañhi ekameva cetiyaṃ hoti. Taṃ manussā ratanāyāmāhi vidatthivitthatāhi dvaṅgulabahalāhi suvaṇṇiṭṭhakāhi haritālena ca manosilāya ca mattikākiccaṃ tilateleneva udakakiccaṃ sādhetvā yojanappamāṇaṃ uṭṭhapesuṃ. Tato bhummā devatā yojanappamāṇaṃ, tato ākāsaṭṭhakadevatā, tato uṇhavalāhakadevatā, tato abbhavalāhakadevatā, tato cātumahārājikā devatā, tato tāvatiṃsā devatā yojanappamāṇaṃ uṭṭhapesunti evaṃ sattayojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ ahosi. Manussesu mālāgandhavatthādīni gahetvā āgatesu ārakkhadevatā gahetvā tesaṃ passantānaṃyeva cetiyaṃ pūjesi.

Tadā ayaṃ thero brāhmaṇamahāsālo hutvā ekaṃ pītakaṃ vatthaṃ ādāya gato. Devatā tassa hatthato vatthaṃ gahetvā cetiyaṃ pūjesi. Brāhmaṇo taṃ disvā pasannacitto ‘‘ahampi anāgate evarūpassa buddhassa cetiye ārakkhadevatā homī’’ti patthanaṃ katvā tato cuto devaloke nibbatti. Tassa devaloke ca manussaloke ca saṃsarantasseva kassapo bhagavā loke uppajjitvā parinibbāyi. Tassāpi ekameva dhātusarīraṃ ahosi. Taṃ gahetvā yojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ kāresuṃ. So tattha ārakkhadevatā hutvā sāsane antarahite sagge nibbattitvā amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle tato cuto mahākule paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā nikkhamma pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Iti cetiye ārakkhadevatā hutvā āgatattā thero tejussadoti veditabbo.

Devatā, ānanda, ujjhāyantīti iti ānanda, devatā ujjhāyanti, na mayhaṃ puttassa añño koci doso atthīti dasseti.

Devatā ānanda, ujjhāyantī
commentary_english:
200. “*Apasāresī*” means *apanesi*.
“*Apehī*” means *apagaccha*.
The elder, with just a single word, having put down the fan, stood to one side.
"*Upaṭṭhāko* tiādi" he said, referring to the state of not being bound to a regular attendant during his initial awakening.
"*Ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā Upavāṇo*" Thus, when the elder had spoken, Ānanda considered Upavāṇa's state of being faulty, and the Blessed One said, "*Yebhuyyena ānandā*," and so forth, to explain that he was actually faultless.
There, "*yebhuyyenā*" this was said referring to the diminished state of both the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*) and the formless deities (*arūpadevatā*).
"*Apphuṭo*" means *asamphuṭṭho* or *abharito*.
It is said that near the Blessed One, in a space the size of a hair tip, having fashioned a subtle form, ten powerful deities (*mahesakkhā devatā*) stood.
Beyond them were twenty [deities], twenty [deities].
Beyond them were thirty [deities], thirty [deities].
Beyond them were forty [deities], forty [deities].
Beyond them were fifty [deities], fifty [deities].
Beyond them were sixty [deities], sixty [deities].
Those deities did not bother each other with their hands, feet, or clothing.
There was no talk such as, "Go away from me, do not touch me."
"Those deities, even having been ten, or having been twenty, or having been thirty, or having been forty, or having been fifty, stand even in a space the size of the tip of a needle, and they do not bother each other," they were just like what was said in A.
ni.

"*Ovārento*" means *āvārento*.
It is said that the elder was, by nature, a very large man, like a young elephant.
Having put on a robe made of rags from a dust heap (*paṃsukūlacīvara*), he was very large.

"*Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā*" means that, not obtaining the chance to see the face of the Blessed One, they murmured thus.
"Why are those deities not able to see through the elder?" Yes, they are not able.
Deities are indeed able to see through ordinary people (*puthujjane*), but not those who have destroyed the āsavas.
And because of the elder's great power (*mahesakkhatāya*) and radiance (*tejussadatāya*), they were not able to approach him.
Why is it that the elder alone is radiant (*tejussado*), and not other *arhats*? Because he was the guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) of the *cetiya* of the Buddha Kassapa.

"*Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā*" In the time of the Buddha Vipassī, when the perfectly awakened one (*sammāsambuddha*) had attained final *nirvāṇa* (*parinibbute*), they made a single *cetiya* for the relics of his body (*dhātusarīra*), which was like a single mass of solid gold. For long-lived Buddhas, there is indeed only one *cetiya*.
Men raised it, using gold bricks (*suvaṇṇiṭṭhakāhi*) inlaid with jewels (*ratanāyāmāhi*) that were a span wide (*vidatthivitthatāhi*) and two finger-breadths thick (*dvaṅgulabahalāhi*), and having accomplished the mud work with *haritāla* and *manosilā*, and the water work with sesame oil (*tilateleneva*), to the measure of a *yojana*.
Then the earth deities [*bhummā devatā*] [raised it] to the measure of a *yojana*, then the sky-dwelling deities [*ākāsaṭṭhakadevatā*], then the hot-cloud deities [*uṇhavalāhakadevatā*], then the rain-cloud deities [*abbhavalāhakadevatā*], then the deities of the Four Great Kings [*cātumahārājikā devatā*], then the deities of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven raised it to the measure of a *yojana*. Thus, that *cetiya* was seven *yojanas* high.
When men came, having taken flowers, scents, cloths, and so forth, the guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*), having taken [those items], worshiped the *cetiya* right in front of those onlookers.

Then this elder, having been a wealthy *brāhmin* [*brāhmaṇamahāsāla*], having taken a single yellow cloth, went [there].
The deity, having taken the cloth from his hand, worshiped the *cetiya*.
The *brāhmin*, having seen that, with a pleased mind, made the aspiration, "May I also, in the future, be a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) of a *cetiya* of a Buddha such as this!" Having made that aspiration, he passed away from there and was reborn in the world of the gods (*devaloke*).
While he was wandering in the world of gods (*devaloka*) and the world of humans (*manussaloka*), Kassapa, the Blessed One, arose in the world and attained complete extinction (*parinibbāyi*). Even he had only one relics-body (*dhātusarīra*). Taking that, they had a league-wide shrine (*yojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ*) built. He, having become a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) there, after the Dispensation had disappeared, was reborn in heaven (*sagge nibbattitvā*), and in the time of our Blessed One, having fallen from there, taking rebirth in a great family (*mahākule paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā*), having gone forth and renounced, attained Arhatship. Thus, because the Elder came having been a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) at the shrine (*cetiye*), he should be known as Tejussada.

"The deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, Ānanda," thus, Ānanda, the deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, showing that there is no other fault in my son.

The deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, Ānanda.

mula_pali:
201. ‘‘Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, bhagavā devatā manasikarotī’’ti manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)? ‘‘Santānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti chinnaṃpādaṃviya papatanti (syā.), āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ cakkhumā (syā. ka.) loke antaradhaṃāyissatī’ti.

‘‘Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antaradhāyissatī’’’ti.

‘‘Yā pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti.

Catusaṃvejanīyaṭṭhānāni
mula_english:
“But, lord, what is the state of the *devatās* the Blessed One is paying attention to?”

“Ānanda, there are *devatās* in space who perceive earth to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon, the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Well-Gone One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Eye will disappear from the world!’

“Ānanda, there are *devatās* on earth who perceive earth to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon, the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Well-Gone One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Eye will disappear from the world!’

“But those *devatās* who are free from craving acquiesce, mindful and clearly comprehending: ‘Impermanent are conditioned things (*saṃskāras*). What else is there to expect?’”

The Four Places That Cause Emotion
commentary_pali:
201.Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhanteti kasmā āha? Bhagavā tumhe – ‘‘devatā ujjhāyantī’’ti vadatha, kathaṃ bhūtā pana tā tumhe manasi karotha , kiṃ tumhākaṃ parinibbānaṃ adhivāsentīti pucchati. Atha bhagavā – ‘‘nāhaṃ adhivāsanakāraṇaṃ vadāmī’’ti tāsaṃ anadhivāsanabhāvaṃ dassento santānandātiādimāha.

Tattha ākāse pathavīsaññiniyoti ākāse pathaviṃ māpetvā tattha pathavīsaññiniyo. Kandantīti rodanti. Chinnapātaṃ papatantīti majjhe chinnā viya hutvā yato vā tato vā papatanti. Āvaṭṭantīti āvaṭṭantiyo patitaṭṭhānameva āgacchanti. Vivaṭṭantīti patitaṭṭhānato parabhāgaṃ vaṭṭamānā gacchanti. Apica dve pāde pasāretvā sakiṃ purato sakiṃ pacchato sakiṃ vāmato sakiṃ dakkhiṇato saṃparivattamānāpi – ‘‘āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭantī’’ti vuccanti. Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyoti pakatipathavī kira devatā dhāretuṃ na sakkoti. Tattha hatthako brahmā viya devatā osīdanti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘oḷārikaṃ hatthaka, attabhāvaṃ abhinimmināhī’’ti (a. ni. 3.128). Tasmā yā devatā pathaviyaṃ pathaviṃ māpesuṃ, tā sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo’’ti.

ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo Kandantī Chinnapātaṃ papatantī Āvaṭṭantī Vivaṭṭantī Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo

Vītarāgāti pahīnadomanassā silāthambhasadisā anāgāmikhīṇāsavadevatā.

Vītarāgā

Catusaṃvejanīyaṭhānavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
201. “What kind [of gods] are they, venerable sir?” Why does he say this? The Blessed One said to you, “You say ‘the gods are murmuring.’" But what kind of gods do you keep in mind?" He asks, "Are you dwelling in nirvāṇa (parinibbāna)?". Then the Blessed One, showing that they do not tolerate, said, "I am not speaking about the cause of tolerating (adhivāsanakāraṇaṃ)," and he began with Santānanda.

There, "those who perceive earth in the sky" (ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo) means those who, having fashioned earth in the sky (ākāse pathaviṃ māpetvā), perceive earth (pathavīsaññiniyo) there. "Weeping (kandantī)" means they are crying (rodanti). "Falling with severed limbs (chinnapātaṃ papatantī)" means having been as if severed in the middle (majjhe chinnā viya hutvā), they fall from here or there (yato vā tato vā papatanti). "Revolving (āvaṭṭantī)" means the revolving ones (āvaṭṭantiyo) come to the very place where they fell (patitaṭṭhānameva āgacchanti). "Spinning around (vivaṭṭantī)" means moving around (vaṭṭamānā gacchanti) to a different place (parabhāgaṃ) from the place where they fell (patitaṭṭhānato). Moreover, even while stretching out two feet, one to the front (purato), one to the back (pacchato), one to the left (vāmatas), one to the right (dakkhiṇato), and revolving (saṃparivattamānāpi), they are called "revolving (āvaṭṭanti) and spinning around (vivaṭṭantī)." "Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo" means the natural earth is not able to hold the gods (devatā dhāretuṃ na sakkoti). There, the gods sink down like Hatthaka Brahmā. Therefore, the Blessed One said (bhagavā) – “Hatthaka, create a gross (oḷārikaṃ) self-image (attabhāvaṃ abhinimmināhī)” (a. ni. 3. 128). Therefore, the statement (vuttaṃ) – "those who perceive earth in the earth (pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo)" – refers to those gods (devatā) who fashioned earth in the earth (pathaviyaṃ pathaviṃ māpesuṃ).

"Free from desire (vītarāgā)" means the anāgāmins (anāgāmi), āsravas-exhausted gods (khīṇāsavadevatā), who have abandoned sadness (pahīnadomanassā), are like stone pillars (silāthambhasadisā).

mula_pali:
202. ‘‘Pubbe , bhante, disāsu vassaṃ vuṭṭhā vassaṃvutthā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhikkhū āgacchanti tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Te mayaṃ labhāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, labhāma payirupāsanāya. Bhagavato pana mayaṃ, bhante, accayena na labhissāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, na labhissāma payirupāsanāyā’’ti.

‘‘Cattārimāni, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni. Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idha tathāgato jāto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’nti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Imāni kho , ānanda, cattāri saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni.

‘‘Āgamissanti kho, ānanda, saddhā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo – ‘idha tathāgato jāto’tipi, ‘idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’tipi, ‘idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’ntipi, ‘idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’tipi. Ye hi keci, ānanda, cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā pasannacittā kālaṅkarissanti, sabbe te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissantī’’ti.

Ānandapucchākathā
mula_english:
202. “Formerly, lord, monks who had spent the Rains in various places used to come to see the Tathāgata. And we used to welcome them so that such inspiring monks might see you and pay their respects. But now, after the Blessed One is gone, we won’t get to see or attend to the monks who inspire the heart.”

“There are four places, Ānanda, that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. Which four? ‘Here the *Tathāgata* was born!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* became fully enlightened in unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* set rolling the unexcelled Wheel of the *Dharma*!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* passed away into the state of *Nirvāṇa* in which no element of clinging remains!’ This, Ānanda, are the four places that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence."

“And truly there will come to these places, Ānanda, pious monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, reflecting: ‘Here the *Tathāgata* was born! Here the *Tathāgata* became fully enlightened in unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment! Here the *Tathāgata* set rolling the unexcelled Wheel of the *Dharma*! Here the *Tathāgata* passed away into the state of *Nirvāṇa* in which no element of clinging remains!’ And any who die while making the pilgrimage to these shrines with a devout heart will, at the breaking-up of the body after death, be reborn in a heavenly world.”

The Story of Ānanda's Questions
commentary_pali:
202.Vassaṃvuṭṭhāti buddhakāle kira dvīsu kālesu bhikkhū sannipatanti upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya kammaṭṭhānaggahaṇatthaṃ, vuṭṭhavassā ca gahitakammaṭṭhānānuyogena nibbattitavisesārocanatthaṃ. Yathā ca buddhakāle, evaṃ tambapaṇṇidīpepi apāragaṅgāya bhikkhū lohapāsāde sannipatiṃsu, pāragaṅgāya bhikkhū tissamahāvihāre. Tesu apāragaṅgāya bhikkhū saṅkārachaḍḍakasammajjaniyo gahetvā āgantvā mahāvihāre sannipatitvā cetiye sudhākammaṃ katvā – ‘‘vuṭṭhavassā āgantvā lohapāsāde sannipatathā’’ti vattaṃ katvā phāsukaṭṭhānesu vasitvā vuṭṭhavassā āgantvā lohapāsāde pañcanikāyamaṇḍale, yesaṃ pāḷi paguṇā, te pāḷiṃ sajjhāyanti. Yesaṃ aṭṭhakathā paguṇā, te aṭṭhakathaṃ sajjhāyanti. Yo pāḷiṃ vā aṭṭhakathaṃ vā virādheti , taṃ – ‘‘kassa santike tayā gahita’’nti vicāretvā ujuṃ katvā gāhāpenti. Pāragaṅgāvāsinopi tissamahāvihāre evameva karonti. Evaṃ dvīsu kālesu sannipatitesu bhikkhūsu ye pure vassūpanāyikāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā gatā visesārocanatthaṃ āgacchanti, evarūpe sandhāya ‘‘pubbe bhante vassaṃvuṭṭhā’’tiādimāha.

Manobhāvanīyeti manasā bhāvite sambhāvite. Ye vā mano manaṃ bhāventi vaḍḍhenti rāgarajādīni pavāhenti, evarūpeti attho. Thero kira vattasampanno mahallakaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā thaddho hutvā na nisīdati, paccuggamanaṃ katvā hatthato chattañca pattacīvarañca gahetvā pīṭhaṃ papphoṭetvā deti, tattha nisinnassa vattaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ paṭijaggitvā deti. Navakaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā tuṇhībhūto na nisīdati, samīpe ṭhatvā vattaṃ karoti. So tāya vattapaṭipattiyā aparihāniṃ patthayamāno evamāha.

Manobhāvanīye

Atha bhagavā – ‘‘ānando manobhāvanīyānaṃ dassanaṃ na labhissāmī’’ti cinteti, handassa, manobhāvanīyānaṃ dassanaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhissāmi, yattha vasanto ito cito ca anāhiṇḍitvāva lacchati manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāyāti cintetvā cattārimānītiādimāha.

cattārimānī

Tattha saddhassāti buddhādīsu pasannacittassa vattasampannassa, yassa pāto paṭṭhāya cetiyaṅgaṇavattādīni sabbavattāni katāneva paññāyanti. Dassanīyānīti dassanārahāni dassanatthāya gantabbāni. Saṃvejanīyānīti saṃvegajanakāni. Ṭhānānīti kāraṇāni, padesaṭhānāneva vā.

saddhassā Dassanīyānī Saṃvejanīyānī Ṭhānānī

Ye hi kecīti idaṃ cetiyacārikāya satthakabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantāti ye ca tāva tattha tattha cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjantā, āsanāni dhovantā bodhimhi udakaṃ siñcantā āhiṇḍanti, tesu vattabbameva natthi asukavihāre ‘‘cetiyaṃ vandissāmā’’ti nikkhamitvā pasannacittā antarā kālaṅkarontāpi anantarāyena sagge patiṭṭhahissanti yevāti dasseti.

Ye hi kecī cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā

Ānandapucchākathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
202. *Vassaṃvuṭṭhā* means that at the time of the Buddha, monks would assemble at two times: near the approach of the rainy season retreat (*vassūpanāyikā*) to receive meditation instruction (*kammaṭṭhāna*), and after the rainy season retreat to announce the attainment of special qualities through the practice of the meditation instruction they had received.

Just as in the time of the Buddha, so too on Tambapaṇṇidīpa (Sri Lanka), monks from Aparagaṅga assembled at the Lohapāsāda (Brazen Palace), and monks from Pāragaṅga assembled at the Tissamahāvihāra.

Of those, the monks from Aparagaṅga, having taken brooms for sweeping away debris and having come to the Mahāvihāra, having assembled and performed the lime-plastering of the *cetiya*, having made the rule, "Having completed the rainy season retreat, come and assemble at the Lohapāsāda," having lived in comfortable places, having completed the rainy season retreat, having come to the Lohapāsāda in the Pañcanikāyamaṇḍala (the area of the five fraternities), those for whom the Pali was well-versed recited the Pali.

Those for whom the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*) was well-versed recited the commentary.

If someone violates the Pali or the commentary, having investigated, "From whom did you receive [this teaching]?" they set it right and cause [him] to take it up [correctly].

The residents of Pāragaṅga also do just this at the Tissamahāvihāra.

Thus, in the case of monks assembled at these two times, those who had previously gone to receive *kammaṭṭhāna* for the *vassūpanāyikā* come to announce their special attainments. Referring to those of such a nature, [the text] begins by saying, "Previously, venerable sirs, *vassaṃvuṭṭhā.*"

*Manobhāvanīye* means cultivated and esteemed in the mind.

Or, those who cultivate and increase in the mind sensual desire (*rāga*), passion (*raja*), etc., and who send [them] forth, this is the meaning.

The elder, endowed with good conduct (*vattasampanno*), having seen an elder monk, being respectful, does not sit down, having gone to meet [him], having taken the umbrella and bowl and robe from his hand, having tapped the seat, he gives [it to him], having performed the duties for the one sitting there, having prepared the lodging, he gives [it to him].

Having seen a novice monk, being silent, he does not sit down, having stood nearby, he performs the duties.

He, desiring non-decline in that practice of duties, spoke thus.

*Manobhāvanīye*

Then, the Blessed One thought, "Ānanda will not obtain the sight of those who are delightful to the mind." Then, because of that, [the Buddha thought]: "I will point out the place of seeing those who are delightful to the mind, where, dwelling there, without wandering here and there, he will easily obtain monks who are delightful to the mind for the purpose of seeing." Having thought this, he began by saying "*cattārimānī*."

*Cattārimānī*: There, *saddhassā* means one whose mind is serene towards the Buddha and so forth, one endowed with good conduct, for whom all the duties, beginning with the duties of the *cetiya*-courtyard, appear to be done from the very start of the day.

*Dassanīyānī* means worthy of being seen, to be gone to for the purpose of seeing.

*Saṃvejanīyānī* means causing agitation.

*Ṭhānānī* means causes, or simply places.

*Saddhassā dassanīyānī saṃvejanīyānī ṭhānānī*: *Ye hi kecī* This was said for the purpose of showing the profitable nature of wandering to a *cetiya*.

There, *cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā* means those who, in various places, sweep the *cetiya* courtyard, wash the seats, sprinkle water on the *bodhi* tree, and wander about. Of those, there is nothing more to be said. [Even] those of serene mind who, having set out thinking, "We will worship the *cetiya*" in a certain monastery, die in between, even they will be established in heaven without obstruction. This he shows.

*Ye hi kecī cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā*: Explanation of Ānanda's question.

mula_pali: 203. ‘‘Kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, mātugāme paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Adassanaṃ, ānandā’’ti. ‘‘Dassane, bhagavā, sati kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Anālāpo, ānandā’’ti . ‘‘Ālapantena pana, bhante, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhāpetabbā’’ti.
mula_english: 203. “How should we conduct ourselves with regard to women, O venerable one?” “By not seeing them, Ānanda.” “If there is seeing, venerable one, how should we conduct ourselves?” “By not speaking, Ānanda.” “If there is speaking, venerable one, how should we conduct ourselves?” “With mindfulness, Ānanda, should one establish oneself.”
commentary_pali:
203.Adassanaṃ, ānandāti yadetaṃ mātugāmassa adassanaṃ, ayamettha uttamā paṭipattīti dasseti. Dvāraṃ pidahitvā senāsane nisinno hi bhikkhu āgantvā dvāre ṭhitampi mātugāmaṃ yāva na passati, tāvassa ekaṃseneva na lobho uppajjati, na cittaṃ calati. Dassane pana satiyeva tadubhayampi assa. Tenāha – ‘‘adassanaṃ ānandā’’ti. Dassane bhagavā sati kathanti bhikkhaṃ gahetvā upagataṭṭhānādīsu dassane sati kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti pucchati. Atha bhagavā yasmā khaggaṃ gahetvā – ‘‘sace mayā saddhiṃ ālapasi, ettheva te sīsaṃ pātessāmī’’ti ṭhitapurisena vā, ‘‘sace mayā saddhiṃ ālapasi, ettheva te maṃsaṃ murumurāpetvā khādissāmī’’ti ṭhitayakkhiniyā vā ālapituṃ varaṃ. Ekasseva hi attabhāvassa tappaccayā vināso hoti, na apāyesu aparicchinnadukkhānubhavanaṃ. Mātugāmena pana ālāpasallāpe sati vissāso hoti, vissāse sati otāro hoti, otiṇṇacitto sīlabyasanaṃ patvā apāyapūrako hoti; tasmā anālāpoti āha. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Sallape asihatthena, pisācenāpi sallape;

Āsīvisampi āsīde, yena daṭṭho na jīvati;

Na tveva eko ekāya, mātugāmena sallape’’ti. (a. ni. 5.55);

Ālapantena panāti sace mātugāmo divasaṃ vā pucchati, sīlaṃ vā yācati, dhammaṃ vā sotukāmo hoti, pañhaṃ vā pucchati, tathārūpaṃ vā panassa pabbajitehi kattabbakammaṃ hoti, evarūpe kāle anālapantaṃ ‘‘mūgo ayaṃ, badhiro ayaṃ, bhutvāva baddhamukho nisīdatī’’ti vadati, tasmā avassaṃ ālapitabbaṃ hoti. Evaṃ ālapantena pana kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti pucchati. Atha bhagavā – ‘‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, mātumattīsu mātucittaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, bhaginimattīsu bhaginicittaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, dhītumattīsu dhītucittaṃ upaṭṭhapethā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 4.127) imaṃ ovādaṃ sandhāya sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhapetabbāti āha.

Ālapantena panā sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhapetabbā
commentary_english:
203. The Blessed One shows that non-seeing (*adassana*) is the highest practice in this matter for women.
