For, a monk who has closed the door and is sitting in his dwelling, as long as he does not see a woman who has come and is standing at the door, to that extent greed does not arise in him, and his mind does not waver. However, if there is seeing, then that entire pair would be his. Therefore, he said, “Non-seeing, Ānanda.”

“When there is seeing, how should the Blessed One be mindful?” Thus, he asks, having taken alms and at the places he has approached, etc., when there is seeing, how should he practice?

Then, the Blessed One [replies]: Since it is better to speak to a standing *yakṣiṇī* who has taken a sword, [saying] – "If you speak with me, I will cut off your head right here!" – or, "If you speak with me, I will chew up your flesh and eat it right here!"

For, by that condition, there is destruction of just one existence, not the experience of unending suffering in the lower realms. However, when there is conversation and chatter with a woman, there is trust, when there is trust, there is intimacy, his mind being inclined, having attained the ruin of virtue, he is a filler of the lower realms; therefore, he said, "Non-speaking (*anālāpa*)."

This was also said:

"One should converse with one holding a sword, one should even converse with a demon,
One should approach a venomous snake, by which one bitten does not live;
But one should never, alone, converse with a woman."

(A.N. 5.55);

“When speaking (*ālapantena*), however”: If a woman asks for the day, or asks for virtue, or wishes to hear the Dharma, or asks a question, or indeed there is some task to be done by the renunciates, at such a time, if one does not speak, [people] would say, “This one is mute, this one is deaf, having eaten, he sits with his mouth shut.” Therefore, one must necessarily speak. Thus, he asks, “When speaking (*ālapantena*), how should one practice?”

Then, the Blessed One [replies]: “Come you, monks, establish a mother-mind in those who are like mothers, establish a sister-mind in those who are like sisters, establish a daughter-mind in those who are like daughters” (S.N. 4.127) – in reference to this advice, he said, “Mindfulness (*sati*), Ānanda, should be established.”

When speaking, mindfulness (*sati*), Ānanda, should be established.

mula_pali: 204. ‘‘Kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Abyāvaṭā tumhe, ānanda, hotha tathāgatassa sarīrapūjāya. Iṅgha tumhe, ānanda, sāratthe ghaṭatha anuyuñjatha sadatthe anuyuñjatha (sī. syā.), sadatthaṃ anuyuñjatha (pī.), sāratthe anuyuñjatha (ka.), sāratthe appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharatha. Santānanda, khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi tathāgate abhippasannā, te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī’’ti.
mula_english: 204. "How, venerable sir (bhante), should we treat the body (śarīra) of the *tathāgata*?" "Ānanda, you should not be occupied with the worship (pūjā) of the body (śarīra) of the *tathāgata*. Rather, Ānanda, strive (ghaṭatha) and be zealous (anuyuñjatha) on your own behalf, for your own good (sāratthe). being heedful (appamattā), ardent (*ātāpino*), & resolute (*pahitattā*) you should apply yourselves to your own good (sāratthe). Ānanda, wise nobles (*khattiyapaṇḍitā*), wise brahmans (*brāhmaṇapaṇḍitā*), & wise householders (*gahapatipaṇḍitā*) are highly confident (*abhippasannā*) in the *tathāgata*. They will conduct the *tathāgata*'s funeral (śarīrapūjaṃ karissantī)."
commentary_pali: 204.Abyāvaṭāti atantibaddhā nirussukkā hotha. Sāratthe ghaṭathāti uttamatthe arahatte ghaṭetha. Anuyuñjathāti tadadhigamāya anuyogaṃ karotha. Appamattāti tattha avippamuṭṭhasatī. Vīriyātāpayogena ātāpino. Kāye ca jīvite ca nirapekkhatāya pahitattā pesitacittā viharatha.
commentary_english:
204. *Abyāvaṭā* means not bound by craving, without attachment.
*Sāratthe ghaṭathā* means strive for the highest purpose, strive for arhathood.
*Anuyuñjathā* means engage in repeated practice for the attainment of that.
*Appamattā* means with unforgotten mindfulness there.
Through the application of energetic heat, *ātāpino*.
In body and in life, being resolutely *pahitattā* through detachment, abide with directed minds.

mula_pali:
205. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī’’ti? ‘‘Rañño, ānanda, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena veṭhenti. Etenupāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ sarīre (syā. ka.) veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe cātummahāpathe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti . Evaṃ kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ vaṇṇakaṃ (sī. pī.) vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.

Thūpārahapuggalo
mula_english:
205. "But how, venerable sir, should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*?"

"Just as they proceed, Ānanda, with the body of a wheel-turning monarch (*rajño cakkavattissa sarīre patipajjanti*), so should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*."

"But how, venerable sir, do they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch?"

"Ānanda, they wrap the body of a wheel-turning monarch in new linen (*ahatena vatthena veṭhenti*). Having wrapped it in new linen, they wrap it in teased cotton. Having wrapped it in teased cotton, they wrap it again in new linen.

In this way, having wrapped the body of the wheel-turning monarch in five hundred layers of linen and cotton, they place it in an iron oil-vat (*āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā*) and cover it with another iron vat. Then, having made a pyre of all kinds of perfumes (*sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā*), they cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. At a crossroads (*cātumahāpathe*) they build a *stūpa* for the wheel-turning monarch.

That is how, Ānanda, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch. Just as they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*. At a crossroads (*cātumahāpathe*) a *stūpa* should be built for the *Tathāgata*. Whoever offers garlands (*mālaṃ vā*), incense (*gandhaṃ vā*), or perfume powder (*cuṇṇakaṃ vā*) there, or reveres, or gladdens their minds, that will be for their long-term benefit and happiness.

A person worthy of a *stūpa*.
commentary_pali:
205.Kathaṃpana, bhanteti tehi khattiyapaṇḍitādīhi kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Addhā maṃ te paṭipucchissanti – ‘‘kathaṃ, bhante, ānanda tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti; ‘‘tesāhaṃ kathaṃ paṭivacanaṃ demī’’ti pucchati. Ahatena vatthenāti navena kāsikavatthena. Vihatena kappāsenāti supothitena kappāsena. Kāsikavatthañhi sukhumattā telaṃ na gaṇhāti, kappāso pana gaṇhāti. Tasmā ‘‘vihatena kappāsenā’’ti āha. Āyasāyāti sovaṇṇāya. Sovaṇṇañhi idha ‘‘ayasa’’nti adhippetaṃ.

Thūpārahapuggalavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
205. "How so? *bhante*?" How should those *kṣatriya* scholars and others act?

Indeed, they will ask me: "How, *bhante*, should the body of the *Tathāgata* be treated?" "How should I give them an answer?" he asks.

"*Ahatena vatthena*" means with new Kāśika cloth.

"*Vihatena kappāsena*" means with well-beaten cotton.

Because Kāśika cloth, due to its fineness, does not absorb oil, but cotton does absorb it.

Therefore, he said, "with well-beaten cotton."

"*Āyasāyā*" means with gold.

Indeed, here, gold is what is meant by "*ayasa*."

Description of the person worthy of a *stūpa*.

mula_pali:
206. ‘‘Cattārome, ānanda, thūpārahā. Katame cattāro? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho, paccekasambuddho thūpāraho, tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho, rājā cakkavattī cakkavatti (syā. ka.) thūpārahoti.

‘‘Kiñcānanda , atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho.

‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato paccekasambuddhassa thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho.

‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa sāvakassa thūpo’ti ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho.

‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho. Ime kho, ānanda cattāro thūpārahā’’ti.

Ānandaacchariyadhammo
mula_english:
“These four, Ānanda, are worthy of a stupa (thūpāraha).

Which four? A *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha (sammāsambuddho), is worthy of a stupa; an individual Buddha (paccekasambuddho) is worthy of a stupa; a disciple (*śrāvaka*) of a *Tathāgata* is worthy of a stupa; a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*) is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, worthy and completely awakened Buddha.’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti). It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is an individual Buddha worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, an individual Buddha’. Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that an individual Buddha is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a disciple of a *Tathāgata* worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of a disciple of that Blessed One, worthy and completely awakened Buddha.’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a disciple of a *Tathāgata* is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a wheel-turning monarch worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that righteous monarch, a king of dharma (dhammarañño).’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a wheel-turning monarch is worthy of a stupa. These, Ānanda, are the four who are worthy of a stupa.”
commentary_pali:
206.Rājā cakkavattīti ettha kasmā bhagavā agāramajjhe vasitvā kālaṅkatassa rañño thūpārahataṃ anujānāti, na sīlavato puthujjanassa bhikkhussāti? Anacchariyattā. Puthujjanabhikkhūnañhi thūpe anuññāyamāne tambapaṇṇidīpe tāva thūpānaṃ okāso na bhaveyya, tathā aññesu ṭhānesu. Tasmā ‘‘anacchariyā te bhavissantī’’ti nānujānāti. Rājā cakkavattī ekova nibbattati, tenassa thūpo acchariyo hoti. Puthujjanasīlavato pana parinibbutabhikkhuno viya mahantampi sakkāraṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

Ānandaacchariyadhammavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
206. rājā cakkavattī: Here, why does the Blessed One, having lived in the midst of houses, approve of a *stūpa* being worthy of a deceased king, but not of a virtuous ordinary *bhikkhu*? Because it is not extraordinary. For if *stūpas* were to be approved for ordinary *bhikkhus*, then even on the island of Tambapaṇṇi there would be no space for *stūpas*, and likewise in other places. Therefore, he does not approve, [saying,] "They will not be extraordinary." A *rājā cakkavattī* arises alone; therefore, his *stūpa* is extraordinary. However, it is indeed fitting to perform even a great honor for an ordinary, virtuous *parinibbuta-bhikkhu*, like one who has attained *parinibbāna*.

Description of Ānanda's Extraordinary Qualities

mula_pali: 207. Atha kho āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno aṭṭhāsi – ‘‘ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘kahaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, ānando’’ti? ‘‘Eso, bhante, āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno ṭhito – ‘ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako’’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena ānandaṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā ānando tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, ānanda, mā soci mā paridevi, nanu etaṃ, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’; taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā. Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Dīgharattaṃ kho te, ānanda, tathāgato paccupaṭṭhito mettena kāyakammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena vacīkammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena manokammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena. Katapuññosi tvaṃ, ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja, khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo’’ti.
mula_english:
207. Then the Venerable Ānanda went into the monastery, leaned against the doorpost, and stood weeping: “Alas, I am still a learner, with much to do! And the Teacher is about to attain parinirvāṇa, he who was so compassionate to me!”

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Where is Ānanda?”

“Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda has gone into the monastery, leaned against the doorpost, and is standing there weeping, saying: ‘Alas, I am still a learner, with much to do! And the Teacher is about to attain *parinirvāṇa*, he who was so compassionate to me!’”

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: “Go, monk, and summon Ānanda in my name, saying, ‘The Teacher calls you, friend Ānanda.’”

“Yes, Venerable Sir,” said that monk in response to the Blessed One. He went to the Venerable Ānanda, and on arrival, he said to the Venerable Ānanda: “The Teacher calls you, friend Ānanda.”

“Very well, friend,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to that monk. Then he went to the Blessed One, and after bowing down to him, sat down to one side.

As the Venerable Ānanda was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to him: “Enough, Ānanda! Do not grieve, do not lament! Have I not already declared that separation, division, and otherness are inevitable with all things that are dear and beloved? Where, Ānanda, could this *not* be found?

That which is born, come into being, compounded, is subject to decay; it is impossible that the body even of the *Tathāgata* should *not* decay.

For a long time, Ānanda, the *Tathāgata* has been attended upon by you with loving-kindness in thought, word, and deed, helpfully, happily, wholeheartedly, and without measure.

You have performed meritorious deeds, Ānanda. Strive on, and you will quickly be free from defilements.” ( *katapuññosi tvaṃ, Ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja, khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo’ti.*)
commentary_pali:
207.Vihāranti idha maṇḍalamālo vihāroti adhippeto, taṃ pavisitvā. Kapisīsanti dvārabāhakoṭiyaṃ ṭhitaṃ aggaḷarukkhaṃ. Rodamāno aṭṭhāsīti so kirāyasmā cintesi – ‘‘satthārā mama saṃvegajanakaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ kathitaṃ, cetiyacārikāya sātthakabhāvo kathito, mātugāme paṭipajjitabbapañho vissajjito, attano sarīre paṭipatti akkhātā, cattāro thūpārahā kathitā, dhuvaṃ ajja bhagavā parinibbāyissatī’’ti, tassevaṃ cintayato balavadomanassaṃ uppajji. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘bhagavato santike rodanaṃ nāma aphāsukaṃ, ekamantaṃ gantvā sokaṃ tanukaṃ karissāmī’’ti, so tathā akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘rodamāno aṭṭhāsī’’ti.

Ahañca vatamhīti ahañca vata amhi, ahaṃ vatamhītipi pāṭho. Yo mama anukampakoti yo maṃ anukampati anusāsati, sve dāni paṭṭhāya kassa mukhadhovanaṃ dassāmi, kassa pāde dhovissāmi, kassa senāsanaṃ paṭijaggissāmi, kassa pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā vicarissāmīti bahuṃ vilapi. Āmantesīti bhikkhusaṅghassa antare theraṃ adisvā āmantesi.

Ahañca vatamhī Yo mama anukampako Āmantesī

Mettenakāyakammenāti mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanadānādikāyakammena. Hitenāti hitavuddhiyā katena. Sukhenāti sukhasomanasseneva katena, na dukkhinā dummanena hutvāti attho. Advayenāti dve koṭṭhāse katvā akatena. Yathā hi eko sammukhāva karoti na parammukhā, eko parammukhāva karoti na sammukhā evaṃ vibhāgaṃ akatvā katenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Appamāṇenāti pamāṇavirahitena. Cakkavāḷampi hi atisambādhaṃ, bhavaggampi atinīcaṃ, tayā kataṃ kāyakammameva bahunti dasseti.

Mettena kāyakammenā Hitenā Sukhenā Advayenā Appamāṇenā

Mettena vacīkammenāti mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanakālārocanādinā vacīkammena. Api ca ovādaṃ sutvā – ‘‘sādhu, bhante’’ti vacanampi mettaṃ vacīkammameva. Mettena manokammenāti kālasseva sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā vivittāsane nisīditvā – ‘‘satthā arogo hotu, abyāpajjo sukhī’’ti evaṃ pavattitena manokammena. Katapuññosīti kappasatasahassaṃ abhinīhārasampannosīti dasseti. Katapuññosīti ca ettāvatā vissattho mā pamādamāpajji, atha kho padhānamanuyuñja. Evañhi anuyutto khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo, dhammasaṅgītikāle arahattaṃ pāpuṇissasi. Na hi mādisassa katapāricariyā nipphalā nāma hotīti dasseti.

Mettena vacīkammenā Mettena manokammenā Katapuññosī
commentary_english:
207. *Vihāra* means here a *vihāra* with a circular arrangement of garlands. Having entered into that.

*Kapisīsa* means the cross-bar (*aggaḷarukkhaṃ*) fixed at the door pillar corner (*dvārabāhakoṭiyaṃ ṭhitaṃ*).

*Rodamāno aṭṭhāsī* means that venerable one thought, “The Teacher has spoken of a dwelling place productive of religious emotion (*saṃvegajanakaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ*), the advantage of pilgrimage to a shrine (*cetiyacārikāya sātthakabhāvo*) has been spoken of, the question to be practiced regarding a woman (*mātugāme paṭipajjitabbapañho*) has been explained, practice regarding one's own body (*attano śarīre paṭipatti*) has been declared, four worthy of a stupa (*cattāro thūpārahā*) have been spoken of, surely today the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*," thinking thus, a strong grief (*balavadomanassaṃ*) arose.

Then this occurred to him: "Weeping (*rodanaṃ*) in the presence of the Blessed One is unseemly (*aphāsukaṃ*), having gone to a secluded place, I will lessen (*tanukaṃ karissāmī’ti*) [my] sorrow (*śokaṃ*)," thus he did.

Therefore it was said – “He stood weeping (*rodamāno aṭṭhāsī*)."

*Ahañca vatamhī* means *ahañca vata amhi*, there is also the reading *ahaṃ vatamhītipi*.

*Yo mama anukampako* means he who has compassion on me (*yo maṃ anukampati*) and instructs me (*anusāsati*), from tomorrow onwards to whom will I give face-washing water (*mukhadhovanaṃ dassāmi*)? Whose feet will I wash (*pāde dhovissāmi*)? Whose lodging will I prepare (*senāsanaṃ paṭijaggissāmi*)? Whose bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ*) having taken, will I wander about (*vicarissāmīti*)? He lamented much (*bahuṃ vilapi*).

*Āmantesī* means having not seen the elder (*theraṃ adisvā*) in the midst of the *bhikkhusaṅgha*, he addressed him (*āmantesi*).

*Ahañca vatamhī yo mama anukampako āmantesī mettena kāyakammenā* means with loving-kindness by way of bodily action (*mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanadānādikāyakammena*).

*Hitenā* means done with the increase of benefit (*hitavuddhiyā katena*).

*Sukhena* means done with pleasure and joy (*sukhasomanasseneva katena*), not having become sorrowful and sad (*na dukkhinā dummanena hutvāti*), is the meaning (*attho*).

*Advayenā* means having made two portions (*dve koṭṭhāse katvā*) by the non-dual (*akatena*).

Just as one makes directly (*sammukhāva karoti*) and not behind the back (*na parammukhā*), one makes behind the back (*parammukhāva karoti*) and not directly (*na sammukhā*), thus without making a division, it is said to be done by the non-dual (*evaṃ vibhāgaṃ akatvā katenāti vuttaṃ hoti*).

*Appamāṇenā* means without measure (*pamāṇavirahitena*).

For even the *cakkavāḷa* is very crowded (*atisambādhaṃ*), even the peak of existence (*bhavaggaṃ*) is very low (*atinīcaṃ*), the bodily action (*kāyakammameva*) done by you (*tayā kataṃ*) shows much (*bahunti dasseti*).

*Mettena kāyakammenā hitenā sukhena advayenā appamāṇenā mettena vacīkammenā* means with loving-kindness by way of verbal action (*mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanakālārocanādinā vacīkammena*).

Moreover, having heard the advice (*ovādaṃ sutvā*) – “Good, venerable sir (*sādhu, bhante*)” – even that word (*vacanampi*) is loving-kindness by way of verbal action (*mettaṃ vacīkammameva*).

*Mettena manokammenā* means having prepared the body (*śarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā*) at the right time itself, having sat down on a secluded seat (*vivittāsane nisīditvā*) – “May the Teacher be without disease (*arogo hotu*), without oppression (*abyāpajjo*), happy (*sukhī*)” – thus with loving-kindness by way of mental action (*evaṃ pavattitena manokammena*).

*Katapuññosī* means it shows that you are accomplished in aspiration for a hundred thousand aeons (*kappasatasahassaṃ abhinīhārasampannosīti dasseti*).

*Katapuññosīti ca ettāvatā vissattho mā pamādamāpajji*, and because you are meritorious in this way, do not become complacent (*vissattho mā pamādamāpajji*), but apply yourself to exertion (*atha kho padhānamanuyuñja*).

For thus applying yourself (*evañhi anuyutto*) you will quickly be without *āsavas* (*khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo*), at the time of the *dharmasaṅgīti* you will attain *arhattva* (*dhammasaṅgītikāle arahattaṃ pāpuṇissasi*).

For it shows that the service done by one like me is not fruitless (*na hi mādisassa katapāricariyā nipphalā nāma hotīti dasseti*).

*Mettena vacīkammenā mettena manokammenā katapuññosī*

mula_pali: 208. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā ahesuṃ, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā bhavissanti, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando; medhāvī, bhikkhave, ānando. Jānāti ‘ayaṃ kālo tathāgataṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo bhikkhunīnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo upāsakānaṃ , ayaṃ kālo upāsikānaṃ, ayaṃ kālo rañño rājamahāmattānaṃ titthiyānaṃ titthiyasāvakāna’nti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Monks, all those who were *arhats*, perfectly awakened Buddhas in the past had just such a chief attendant as Ānanda.

And so too, monks, will those Blessed Lords who come in the future.

Ānanda is wise, monks; Ānanda is intelligent, monks.

He knows, 'This is the right time for monks to come to see the *Tathāgata*, this is the right time for nuns, this is the right time for male lay-followers, this is the right time for female lay-followers, this is the right time for kings, for royal ministers, for leaders of other schools, and for their pupils.'
commentary_pali: 208. Evañca pana vatvā mahāpathaviṃ pattharanto viya ākāsaṃ vitthārento viya cakkavāḷagiriṃ osārento viya sineruṃ ukkhipento viya mahājambuṃ khandhe gahetvā cālento viya āyasmato ānandassa guṇakathaṃ ārabhanto atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi. Tattha ‘‘yepi te, bhikkhave, etarahī’’ti kasmā na vuttaṃ? Aññassa buddhassa natthitāya. Eteneva cetaṃ veditabbaṃ – ‘‘yathā cakkavāḷantarepi añño buddho natthī’’ti. Paṇḍitoti byatto. Medhāvīti khandhadhātuāyatanādīsu kusalo.
commentary_english:
208. And then, after saying this, as if spreading out the great earth, as if expanding the sky, as if lowering the *cakravāḷa* mountain, as if lifting up Mount Meru, as if taking the great *jambu* tree by its trunk and shaking it, beginning a talk about the good qualities of the venerable Ānanda, then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus*.

There, why was it not said, "Those who are here now, *bhikkhus*?" Because there is no other Buddha.

By this very [reason] it should be understood: "Just as there is no other Buddha even within the *cakravāḷa*."

*Paṇḍito* means articulate.

*Medhāvī* means skilled in the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), sense-fields (*āyatana*) and so on.

mula_pali:
209. ‘‘Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā abbhutadhammā (syā. ka.) ānande. Katame cattāro? Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce, ānando, dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande.

‘‘Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā raññe cakkavattimhi. Katame cattāro ? Sace, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā hoti. Atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Sace bhikkhave, brāhmaṇaparisā…pe… gahapatiparisā…pe… samaṇaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, samaṇaparisā hoti, atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cattārome acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave bhikkhunīparisā…pe… upāsakaparisā…pe… upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande’’ti.

Mahāsudassanasuttadesanā
mula_english:
"Monks, Ānanda has these four amazing and astounding qualities. What are the four? If, monks, a company of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they become joyful on seeing him; and if he then speaks to them of the Dharma, they are made joyful by his discourse; before they are sated, monks, the company of monks is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a company of nuns approaches Ānanda to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of nuns is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of male lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of male lay followers is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of female lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech. Before they are sated, monks, the company of female lay followers is, and then Ānanda is silent. These are the four amazing & astounding qualities in Ānanda.

"Monks, a Universal Monarch has these four amazing and astounding qualities. What are the four? If, monks, a group of nobles approaches a Universal Monarch to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he then speaks, they are made joyful by his talk; Before they are sated, monks, the company of nobles is. And then the Universal Monarch remains silent. If a group of Brahmins… of householders… of ascetics approaches a Universal Monarch to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of ascetics is, and then the Universal Monarch remains silent. In the same way, monks, there are these four amazing & astounding qualities in Ānanda. If, monks, a company of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they become joyful on seeing him; and if he then speaks to them of the Dharma, they are made joyful by his discourse; Before they are sated, monks, the company of monks is. And then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of nuns… a group of male lay followers… a group of female lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of female lay followers is. And then Ānanda is silent. There are the four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about Ānanda."
Mahāsudassana Sutta discourse
commentary_pali:
209.Bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāyāti ye bhagavantaṃ passitukāmā theraṃ upasaṅkamanti, ye ca ‘‘āyasmā kirānando samantapāsādiko abhirūpo dassanīyo bahussuto saṅghasobhano’’ti therassa guṇe sutvā āgacchanti, te sandhāya ‘‘bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamantī’’ti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Attamanāti savanena no dassanaṃ sametīti sakamanā tuṭṭhacittā. Dhammanti ‘‘kacci, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci yoniso manasikārena kammaṃ karotha, ācariyupajjhāye vattaṃ pūrethā’’ti evarūpaṃ paṭisanthāradhammaṃ. Tattha bhikkhunīsu – ‘‘kacci, bhaginiyo, aṭṭha garudhamme samādāya vattathā’’ti idampi nānākaraṇaṃ hoti. Upāsakesu āgatesu ‘‘upāsaka, na te kacci sīsaṃ vā aṅgaṃ vā rujjati, arogā te puttabhātaro’’ti na evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Evaṃ pana karoti – ‘‘kathaṃ upāsakā tīṇi saraṇāni pañca sīlāni rakkhatha, māsassa aṭṭha uposathe karotha, mātāpitūnaṃ upaṭṭhānavattaṃ pūretha, dhammikasamaṇabrāhmaṇe paṭijaggathā’’ti. Upāsikāsupi eseva nayo.

Idāni ānandattherassa cakkavattinā saddhiṃ upamaṃ karonto cattārome bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha khattiyāti abhisittā ca anabhisittā ca khattiyajātikā. Te kira – ‘‘rājā cakkavattī nāma abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko ākāsena vicaranto rajjaṃ anusāsati dhammiko dhammarājā’’ti tassa guṇakathaṃ sutvā ‘‘savanena dassanampi sama’’nti attamanā honti. Bhāsatīti kathento – ‘‘kathaṃ, tātā, rājadhammaṃ pūretha, paveṇiṃ rakkhathā’’ti paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Brāhmaṇesu pana – ‘‘kathaṃ ācariyā mante vācetha, kathaṃ antevāsikā mante gaṇhanti, dakkhiṇaṃ vā vatthāni vā kapilaṃ vā alatthā’’ti paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Gahapatīsu – ‘‘kathaṃ tātā, na vo rājakulato daṇḍena vā balinā vā pīḷā atthi, sammā devo dhāraṃ anupavecchati, sassāni sampajjantī’’ti evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Samaṇesu – ‘‘kathaṃ, bhante, pabbajitaparikkhārā sulabhā, samaṇadhamme na pamajjathā’’ti evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti.

cattārome bhikkhave khattiyā Bhāsatī

Mahāsudassanasuttadesanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
209. "The assembly of monks approached Ānanda for a viewing" means those who desired to see the Blessed One approached the elder; and those who, having heard the elder's qualities, that venerable Ānanda was universally pleasing, handsome, delightful, very learned, an ornament to the Saṅgha, came thinking, "Hearing is the same as seeing." That is what is meant by, "The assembly of monks approached Ānanda for a viewing."

This method applies everywhere.

*Attamanā* means with joyful minds, their minds were delighted because the sound came but the sight did not come.

*Dhamma* means the conversational Dhamma, "Are you well, friend? Are you able to live? Do you act with careful consideration? Do you fulfill your duties to your teachers and preceptors?" Such is the nature of conversational Dhamma.

There, with the nuns: "Are you maintaining the eight weighty rules?" This too is a variation.

When lay followers have arrived: "Lay follower, is your head or limb injured? Are your children and siblings free from disease?" One does not engage in such conversation.

But rather, one does this: "How do you lay followers keep the three refuges and five precepts? Do you observe the eight *uposatha* days of the month? Do you fulfill your duties to your mother and father? Do you honor righteous *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*?"

The same method applies to lay women as well.

Now, making a comparison of the venerable Ānanda with a wheel-turning monarch, he says, "These four monks," and so forth.

There, *khattiyā* means those of the *kṣatriya* class, both consecrated and unconsecrated.

It is said that they, having heard the praise of him, "The king, a wheel-turning monarch, is handsome, delightful, pleasing, travels through the sky, governs the kingdom, is righteous, a king of Dharma," are joyful, thinking, "Hearing is the same as seeing."

*Bhāsatī* means while speaking, he engages in conversational exchange: "How, fathers, do you fulfill the royal Dharma? Do you protect the tradition?"

But with *brāhmaṇas*: "How, teachers, do you recite the *mantras*? How do the novices learn the *mantras*? Have you obtained a donation, clothing, or a cow?" He engages in such conversation.

With householders: "How, fathers, is there no oppression from the royal family through punishment or force? Does the *deva* properly provide rain? Do the crops thrive?" He engages in such conversation.

With *śramaṇas*: "How, venerable sirs, are the requisites for renunciants easily obtained? Do you not neglect the Dharma of a *śramaṇa*?" He engages in such conversation.

These four monks, *kṣatriyas*, *bhāsatī*.

Explanation of the teaching of the Mahāsudassana Sūtra.

mula_pali:
210. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mā, bhante, bhagavā imasmiṃ khuddakanagarake ujjaṅgalanagarake sākhānagarake parinibbāyi. Santi, bhante, aññāni mahānagarāni, seyyathidaṃ – campā rājagahaṃ sāvatthī sāketaṃ kosambī bārāṇasī; ettha bhagavā parinibbāyatu. Ettha bahū khattiyamahāsālā, brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatimahāsālā tathāgate abhippasannā. Te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī’’ti ‘‘māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca; māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca – ‘khuddakanagarakaṃ ujjaṅgalanagarakaṃ sākhānagaraka’nti.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano nāma ahosi cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janappadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa ayaṃ kusinārā kusāvatī nāma rājadhānī ahosi, puratthimena ca pacchimena ca dvādasayojanāni āyāmena; uttarena ca dakkhiṇena ca sattayojanāni vitthārena. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devānaṃ āḷakamandā nāma rājadhānī iddhā ceva hoti phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇayakkhā ca subhikkhā ca; evameva kho, ānanda, kusāvatī rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī dasahi saddehi avivittā ahosi divā ceva rattiñca, seyyathidaṃ – hatthisaddena assasaddena rathasaddena bherisaddena mudiṅgasaddena vīṇāsaddena gītasaddena saṅkhasaddena sammasaddena pāṇitāḷasaddena ‘asnātha pivatha khādathā’ti dasamena saddena.

‘‘Gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocehi – ‘ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā, abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi.

Mallānaṃ vandanā
mula_english:
210. When this had been said, the Venerable Ānanda spoke to the Blessed One, saying: “Let not the Blessed One pass away in this insignificant little town, this uncivilized township, this branch township.

There are other great cities, lord, such as Campā, Rājagaha, Sāvatthī, Sāketa, Kosambī, or Bārāṇasī; let the Blessed One attain final nirvāṇa there. In those places there are wealthy nobles, wealthy Brahmins, and wealthy householders who are devoted to the *Tathāgata*. They will provide for the *Tathāgata*'s bodily ( *śarīra*) offering ( *pūjā*)."

“Do not say that, Ānanda! Do not say, ‘This insignificant little town, this uncivilized township, this branch township.’"

“In the past, Ānanda, there was a king named Mahāsudassana, a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous king, a king of righteousness, a conqueror of the four quarters, a stabilizer of his country, endowed with the seven treasures.

This Kusinārā, Ānanda, was the royal capital of King Mahāsudassana, named Kusāvatī. It was twelve *yojanas* long from east to west, and seven *yojanas* wide from north to south.

Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, was powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with humans, and well-supplied with food.

Just as the deva-city of Āḷakamandā is powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with *yakṣas*, and well-supplied with food, so too was Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with humans, and well-supplied with food.

Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, was never without ten sounds, day or night, namely the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of kettle drums, the sound of side drums, the sound of lutes, the sound of singing, the sound of cymbals, the sound of gongs, and as the tenth sound, the sound of clapping and cries of "Eat, drink, and be merry!"

“Go, Ānanda, enter Kusinārā and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the final *nirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* will occur. Approach him, Vāseṭṭhas, approach him. Do not be remorseful later, thinking, “In our own village area the *Tathāgata*’s final *nirvāṇa* took place, but we did not get to see the *Tathāgata* for the last time.”’”

“So be it, lord,” said the Venerable Ānanda, and after agreeing with the Blessed One, he dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went with a companion into Kusinārā.

Veneration of the Mallas
commentary_pali:
210.Khuddakanagaraketi nagarapatirūpake sambādhe khuddakanagarake. Ujjaṅgalanagaraketi visamanagarake. Sākhānagaraketi yathā rukkhānaṃ sākhā nāma khuddakā honti, evameva aññesaṃ mahānagarānaṃ sākhāsadise khuddakanagarake. Khattiyamahāsālāti khattiyamahāsārappattā mahākhattiyā. Esa nayo sabbattha.

Tesu khattiyamahāsālā nāma yesaṃ koṭisatampi koṭisahassampi dhanaṃ nikhaṇitvā ṭhapitaṃ, divasaparibbayo ekaṃ kahāpaṇasakaṭaṃ nigacchati, sāyaṃ dve pavisanti. Brāhmaṇamahāsālā nāma yesaṃ asītikoṭidhanaṃ nihitaṃ hoti, divasaparibbayo eko kahāpaṇakumbho nigacchati, sāyaṃ ekasakaṭaṃ pavisati. Gahapatimahāsālā nāma yesaṃ cattālīsakoṭidhanaṃ nihitaṃ hoti, divasaparibbayo pañca kahāpaṇambaṇāni nigacchanti, sāyaṃ kumbho pavisati.

khattiyamahāsālā Brāhmaṇamahāsālā Gahapatimahāsālā

Māhevaṃ, ānanda, avacāti ānanda, mā evaṃ avaca, na imaṃ ‘‘khuddakanagara’’nti vattabbaṃ. Ahañhi imasseva nagarassa sampattiṃ kathetuṃ – ‘‘anekavāraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ nisīdaṃ mahantena ussāhena, mahantena parakkamena idhāgato’’ti vatvā bhūtapubbantiādimāha. Subhikkhāti khajjabhojjasampannā. Hatthisaddenāti ekasmiṃ hatthimhi saddaṃ karonte caturāsītihatthisahassāni saddaṃ karonti, iti hatthisaddena avivittā, hoti, tathā assasaddena. Puññavanto panettha sattā catusindhavayuttehi rathehi aññamaññaṃ anubandhamānā antaravīthīsu vicaranti, iti rathasaddena avivittā hoti. Niccaṃ payojitāneva panettha bheriādīni tūriyāni, iti bherisaddādīhipi avivittā hoti. Tattha sammasaddoti kaṃsatāḷasaddo. Pāṇitāḷasaddoti pāṇinā caturassaambaṇatāḷasaddo. Kuṭabherisaddotipi vadanti.

Mā hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā bhūtapubba Subhikkhā Hatthisaddenā sammasaddo Pāṇitāḷasaddo

Asnāthapivatha khādathāti asnātha pivatha khādatha. Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, bhuñjatha bhoti iminā dasamena saddena avivittā hoti anupacchinnasaddā. Yathā pana aññesu nagaresu ‘‘kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetha, kudālaṃ gaṇhatha, pacchiṃ gaṇhatha, pavāsaṃ gamissāma, taṇḍulapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, bhattapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, phalakāvudhādīni sajjāni karothā’’ti evarūpā saddā honti, na yidha evaṃ ahosīti dasseti.

Asnātha pivatha khādathā

‘‘Dasamena saddenā’’ti ca vatvā ‘‘kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī sattahi pākārehi parikkhittā ahosī’’ti sabbaṃ mahāsudassanasuttaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā gaccha tvaṃ ānandātiādimāha. Tattha abhikkamathāti abhimukhā kamatha, āgacchathāti attho. Kiṃ pana te bhagavato āgatabhāvaṃ na jānantīti? Jānanti. Buddhānaṃ gatagataṭṭhānaṃ nāma mahantaṃ kolāhalaṃ hoti, kenacideva karaṇīyena nisinnattā na āgatā. ‘‘Te āgantvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhānanisajjokāsaṃ saṃvidahitvā dassantī’’ti tesaṃ santike avelāyampi bhagavā pesesi.

mahāsudassanasuttaṃ gaccha tvaṃ ānandā abhikkamathā

Mallānaṃ vandanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
210. *Khuddakanagarake* means a small town (*nagarapatirūpake sambādhe khuddakanagarake*).

*Ujjaṅgalanagarake* means an uneven town (*visamanagarake*).

*Sākhānagarake* means just as the branches of trees are small, likewise, a small town similar to the branch of a large town (*yathā rukkhānaṃ sākhā nāma khuddakā honti, evameva aññesaṃ mahānagarānaṃ sākhāsadise khuddakanagarake*).

*Khattiyamahāsālā* means great nobles who have attained to the essence of warriors (*khattiyamahāsārappattā mahākhattiyā*).

This method [of explanation] applies to all cases (*esa nayo sabbattha*).

Amongst them, *khattiyamahāsālā* are those who have a hundred *koṭis*, or a thousand *koṭis*, of wealth buried; their daily expenditure amounts to a cartload of *kahāpaṇas*, and two [cartloads] enter in the evening.

*Brāhmaṇamahāsālā* are those who have eighty *koṭis* of wealth deposited; their daily expenditure amounts to a pot of *kahāpaṇas*, and one cart enters in the evening.

*Gahapatimahāsālā* are those who have forty *koṭis* of wealth deposited; their daily expenditure amounts to five *kahāpaṇambaṇas*, and a pot enters in the evening.

*Khattiyamahāsālā*, *brāhmaṇamahāsālā*, *gahapatimahāsālā*:

"Do not speak thus, Ānanda (*mā hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā*)!

It should not be said, "This is a small town" (*na imaṃ khuddakanagara'nti vattabbaṃ*).

For I, to describe the prosperity of this very town, said, "Standing up and sitting down many times, with great effort and great exertion, I came here (*anekavāraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ nisīdaṃ mahantena ussāhena, mahantena parakkamena idhāgato*)", and so on, speaking of former times (*bhūtapubba*).

*Subhikkhā* means abundant with food and drink (*khajjabhojjasampannā*).

*Hatthisaddena* means when one elephant makes a sound, eighty-four thousand elephants make a sound; thus it is not free from the sound of elephants (*iti hatthisaddena avivittā, hoti, tathā assasaddena*), and likewise with the sound of horses.

Here, virtuous beings, yoked to four Sindhava horses, chasing each other, wander in the inner streets; thus it is not free from the sound of chariots (*iti rathasaddena avivittā hoti*).

Here, drums and other musical instruments are always played; thus it is not free from the sound of drums and other things (*iti bherisaddādīhipi avivittā hoti*).

There, *sammasaddo* means the sound of brass cymbals (*kaṃsatāḷasaddo*).

*Pāṇitāḷasaddo* means the sound of clapping with the hands, the sound of four-sided drums (*pāṇinā caturassaambaṇatāḷasaddo*).

Some also say [it is] the sound of kettle drums (*kuṭabherisaddotipi vadanti*).

Do not [speak thus]!

"Do not speak thus, Ānanda (*hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā*)!"

Former times (*bhūtapubba*)

Abundant with food (*subhikkhā*)

With the sound of elephants (*hatthisaddena*)

Sound of cymbals (*sammasaddo*)

Sound of clapping (*pāṇitāḷasaddo*)

Bathed (*asnātha*)

Drink and eat (*pivatha khādathā*) means bathed, drink and eat (*asnātha pivatha khādatha*).

Here is a summary; you are fed, it is not free from this tenth sound (*iminā dasamena saddena avivittā hoti*) and has continuous sound (*anupacchinnasaddā*).

Just as in other towns there are sounds, "Throw away the rubbish, take the hoe, take the basket, we will go to exile, take the rice bag, take the food bag, make the weapons ready (*yathā pana aññesu nagaresu kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetha, kudālaṃ gaṇhatha, pacchiṃ gaṇhatha, pavāsaṃ gamissāma, taṇḍulapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, bhattapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, phalakāvudhādīni sajjāni karothā*)," such sounds there are, but not here, he shows (*na yidha evaṃ ahosīti dasseti*).

Bathed (*asnātha*)

Drink and eat (*pivatha khādathā*)

And having said, "with the tenth sound," and "Kusāvatī, Ānanda, was a capital surrounded by seven walls (*kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī sattahi pākārehi parikkhittā ahosī*)," having finished the entire Great Vision Sūtra (*sabbaṃ mahāsudassanasuttaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā*), he said, "Go you, Ānanda (*gaccha tvaṃ ānandā*)," and so on.

There, *abhikkamathā* means face [it], go forward; the meaning is come (*abhimukhā kamatha, āgacchathāti attho*).

What, do they not know the Blessed One has come (*kiṃ pana te bhagavato āgatabhāvaṃ na jānantīti*)? They know (*jānanti*).

The Buddhas going and standing has a great commotion, because of some duty they did not come due to being seated (*buddhānaṃ gatagataṭṭhānaṃ nāma mahantaṃ kolāhalaṃ hoti, kenacideva karaṇīyena nisinnattā na āgatā*).

"Having come, they will arrange a place for the *bhikkhu* assembly to sit down and will show [it] (*te āgantvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhānanisajjokāsaṃ saṃvidahitvā dassantī*)," even at the wrong time, the Blessed One sent to them (*tesaṃ santike avelāyampi bhagavā pesesi*).

Great Vision Sūtra (*mahāsudassanasuttaṃ*)

Go you, Ānanda (*gaccha tvaṃ ānandā*)

Go forward (*abhikkamathā*)

Explanation of the Mallas' veneration (*mallānaṃ vandanāvaṇṇanā*)

mula_pali:
211. Tena kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre santhāgāre (sī. syā. pī.) sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – ‘‘ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antaradhāyissatī’ti. Atha kho mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘sace kho ahaṃ kosinārake malle ekamekaṃ bhagavantaṃ vandāpessāmi, avandito bhagavā kosinārakehi mallehi bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpeyyaṃ – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando etena upāyena paṭhameneva yāmena kosinārake malle bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi.

Subhaddaparibbājakavatthu
mula_english:
At that time, the Mallas of Kuśinagara were assembled in their council hall on some business or other. Then the venerable Ānanda approached the council hall of the Mallas of Kuśinagara; having approached, he announced to the Mallas of Kuśinagara: “Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the *Tathāgata's* (Tathāgatassa) *parinirvāṇa* (parinibbānaṃ) will take place. Approach, Vāseṭṭhas, approach, Vāseṭṭhas. Do not be remorseful later, thinking, 'The *Tathāgata's parinirvāṇa* (Tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ) occurred in our own village area, and we did not get to see the *Tathāgata* (Tathāgataṃ) for the last time!’”

Having heard the words of the venerable Ānanda, the Mallas, with their sons, daughters-in-law, wives, being afflicted, saddened, their minds overwhelmed with grief, some wept, tearing their hair; they wept, raising their arms; they fell to the ground as if cut off, rolled around, crying, “Too soon will the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavā) attain *parinirvāṇa* (parinibbāyissati), too soon will the *Sugata* (Sugato) attain *parinirvāṇa* (parinibbāyissati), too soon will the eye disappear from the world!”

Then the Mallas, with their sons, daughters-in-law, wives, being afflicted, saddened, their minds overwhelmed with grief, went to Upavattana, the Mallas' Sāla Grove, to where the venerable Ānanda was.

Then the venerable Ānanda thought: “If I were to have each of the Mallas of Kuśinagara pay homage to the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavantaṃ) individually, the night would dawn before they were all presented. Therefore, I should have the Mallas of Kuśinagara arranged by families, each family in turn, and have them pay homage to the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavantaṃ), saying, ‘The Malla named so-and-so, venerable sir, with his sons, wife, retinue, and ministers, pays homage with his head at the feet of the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati).’”

Then the venerable Ānanda had the Mallas of Kuśinagara arranged by families, each family in turn, and had them pay homage to the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavantaṃ), saying, “The Malla named so-and-so, venerable sir, with his sons, wife, retinue, and ministers, pays homage with his head at the feet of the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati).”

Then the venerable Ānanda, by this method, in the first watch of the night itself, had the Mallas of Kuśinagara pay homage to the *Bhagavat* (Bhagavantaṃ).

The Subhadda the Wanderer Incident
commentary_pali:
211.Amhākañca noti ettha no kāro nipātamattaṃ. Aghāvinoti uppannadukkhā. Dummanāti anattamanā. Cetodukkhasamappitāti domanassasamappitā. Kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvāti ekekaṃ kulaparivattaṃ kulasaṅkhepaṃ vīthisabhāgena ceva racchāsabhāgena ca visuṃ visuṃ ṭhapetvā.

Subhaddaparibbājakavatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
211. amhākañca noti ettha no kāro nipātamattaṃ. aghāvinoti uppannadukkhā. dummanāti anattamanā. cetodukkhasamappitāti domanassasamappitā. kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvāti ekekaṃ kulaparivattaṃ kulasaṅkhepaṃ vīthisabhāgena ceva racchāsabhāgena ca visuṃ visuṃ ṭhapetvā.

Here, "amhākañca no" means that the word "no" is merely a particle. "aghāvino" means those who have arisen in suffering ( *utpannaduḥkhā*). "dummanā" means unhappy (*anattamanā*). "cetodukkhasamappitā" means afflicted with mental suffering (*daumanasyasamarpitā*). "kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā" means placing each lineage revolution and lineage summary separately, by way of the street division and also by way of the road division.

subhaddaparibbājakavatthuvaṇṇanā

mula_pali: 212. Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma paribbājako kusinārāyaṃ paṭivasati. Assosi kho subhaddo paribbājako – ‘‘ajja kira rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissatī’’ti. Atha kho subhaddassa paribbājakassa etadahosi – ‘‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’’’nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako…pe… tatiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā’’ti.
mula_english:
212. Now at that time, a wandering ascetic named Subhadda was staying near Kusinārā.

Subhadda the wandering ascetic heard it said, "Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *parinirvāṇa* of the *śramaṇa* Gotama will take place."

Then the thought occurred to Subhadda the wandering ascetic: "I have heard it said by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones, arise in the world."

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now, a doubt has arisen in me, and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

Then Subhadda the wandering ascetic went to the Upavattana, the *sāla* grove of the Mallas, and approached the venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he said to the venerable Ānanda: "I have heard it said, venerable Ānanda, by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones, arise in the world.

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now a doubt has arisen in me—and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

"It would be good, venerable Ānanda, if I could be allowed to see the *śramaṇa* Gotama."

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to Subhadda the wandering ascetic, "Enough, friend Subhadda! Do not disturb the *Tathāgata*. The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) is weary."

A second time... and a third time, Subhadda the wandering ascetic said to the venerable Ānanda, "I have heard it said, venerable Ānanda, by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas arise in the world, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones.

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now a doubt has arisen in me—and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

"It would be good, venerable Ānanda, if I could be allowed to see the *śramaṇa* Gotama."

For a third time, the venerable Ānanda said to Subhadda the wandering ascetic, "Enough, friend Subhadda! Do not disturb the *Tathāgata*. The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) is weary."
commentary_pali:
212.Subhaddonāma paribbājakoti udiccabrāhmaṇamahāsālakulā pabbajito channaparibbājako. Kaṅkhādhammoti vimatidhammo. Kasmā panassa ajja evaṃ ahosīti? Tathāvidhaupanissayattā. Pubbe kira puññakaraṇakāle dve bhātaro ahesuṃ. Te ekatova sassaṃ akaṃsu. Tattha jeṭṭhakassa – ‘‘ekasmiṃ sasse navavāre aggasassadānaṃ mayā dātabba’’nti ahosi. So vappakāle bījaggaṃ nāma datvā gabbhakāle kaniṭṭhena saddhiṃ mantesi – ‘‘gabbhakāle gabbhaṃ phāletvā dassāmā’’ti kaniṭṭho – ‘‘taruṇasassaṃ nāsetukāmosī’’ti āha. Jeṭṭho kaniṭṭhassa ananuvattanabhāvaṃ ñatvā khettaṃ vibhajitvā attano koṭṭhāsato gabbhaṃ phāletvā khīraṃ nīharitvā sappinavanītena saṃyojetvā adāsi, puthukakāle puthukaṃ kāretvā adāsi, lāyanakāle lāyanaggaṃ, veṇikaraṇe veṇaggaṃ, kalāpādīsu kalāpaggaṃ, khalaggaṃ, khalabhaṇḍaggaṃ, koṭṭhagganti evaṃ ekasasse navavāre aggadānaṃ adāsi. Kaniṭṭho pana uddharitvā adāsi.

Tesu jeṭṭhako aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero jāto. Bhagavā – ‘‘kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyya’’nti olokento ‘‘aññāsikoṇḍañño ekasmiṃ sasse nava aggadānāni adāsi, imaṃ aggadhammaṃ tassa desessāmī’’ti sabbapaṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ desesi. So aṭṭhārasahi brahmakoṭīhi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāsi. Kaniṭṭho pana ohīyitvā pacchā dānassa dinnattā satthu parinibbānakāle evaṃ cintetvā satthāraṃ daṭṭhukāmo ahosi.

aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero

Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesīti thero kira – ‘‘ete aññatitthiyā nāma attano gahaṇameva gaṇhanti, tassa vissajjāpanatthāya bhagavato bahuṃ bhāsamānassa kāyavācāvihesā bhavissati, pakatiyāpi ca kilantoyeva bhagavā’’ti maññamāno evamāha. Paribbājako – ‘‘na me ayaṃ bhikkhu okāsaṃ karoti, atthikena pana anuvattitvā kāretabbo’’ti theraṃ anuvattanto dutiyampi tatiyampi āha.

Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī
commentary_english:
212. *Subhaddo nāma paribbājako* means the wanderer Subhadda, who renounced the world from a wealthy, Brahmin family in Northern India and was surrounded by sixty wanderers.

*Kaṅkhādhammo* means the doctrine of doubt, or the doctrine of uncertainty.

Why did that occur for him today? Because of a specific underlying condition.

It is said that in the past, while performing a meritorious act, there were two brothers. They farmed a field together. For the elder brother, there was [this thought]: "In one harvest, I must give the best grain offering nine times."

So, at the time of sowing, he gave the best seed. During the embryonic stage [of the crop], he consulted with his younger brother, "During the embryonic stage, we will split the embryo and give [it as an offering]." The younger brother said, "You wish to destroy the young crop!"

The elder brother, knowing that his younger brother did not agree, divided the field. From his portion, he split the embryo, extracted the milky sap, combined it with ghee and fresh butter, and gave it as an offering. At the time of *puthuka* (a type of grain), he had *puthuka* prepared and gave it as an offering. At the time of reaping, the best of the harvest, at the time of winnowing, the best of the winnowed grain, from bundles, the best bundle, the best of the threshing floor, the best of the threshing-floor produce, the best of the granary—in this way, in one harvest, he gave the best offering nine times.

The younger brother, however, harvested and gave [his offering].

Among them, the elder brother was born as the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña. The Blessed One, looking around, [thought]: "To whom shall I first teach the Dhamma?" [He saw]: "Aññāsikoṇḍañña gave nine best offerings in one harvest. I will teach him this supreme Dhamma." So, he taught the Dhamma first of all. He was established in the fruit of stream-entry together with eighteen *brahma* crores.

The younger brother, however, having been inferior, because he gave the offering later, thinking thus at the time of the Teacher's *parinibbāna*, he wished to see the Teacher.

*Aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero*

*Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī*: It is said that the Elder [Aññāsikoṇḍañña], thinking, "These other sectarians take only their own views. For the Blessed One, speaking much to dismiss them, there will be physical and verbal weariness, and naturally the Blessed One is already tired," spoke thus.

The wanderer [Subhadda]: "This monk does not give me an opportunity. But having persisted with my request I must make him do it." Following the Elder, he spoke a second and third time.

*Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī*

mula_pali: 213. Assosi kho bhagavā āyasmato ānandassa subhaddena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, ānanda, mā subhaddaṃ vāresi, labhataṃ, ānanda, subhaddo tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yaṃ kiñci maṃ subhaddo pucchissati, sabbaṃ taṃ aññāpekkhova pucchissati, no vihesāpekkho. Yaṃ cassāhaṃ puṭṭho byākarissāmi, taṃ khippameva ājānissatī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘gacchāvuso subhadda, karoti te bhagavā okāsa’’nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yeme, bho gotama, samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa, seyyathidaṃ – pūraṇo kassapo, makkhali gosālo, ajito kesakambalo, pakudho kaccāyano, sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto, sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu , udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū’’ti? ‘‘Alaṃ, subhadda, tiṭṭhatetaṃ – ‘sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu, udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū’ti. Dhammaṃ te, subhadda, desessāmi; taṃ suṇāhi sādhukaṃ manasikarohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
213. And the Blessed One heard the talk between Ven. Ānanda & Subhadda the wanderer.

Then the Blessed One called to the Venerable Ānanda and said: “Enough, Ānanda! Do not refuse Subhadda. Subhadda, Ānanda, may be allowed into the presence of the *Tathāgata*.

For whatever Subhadda asks me he will ask in quest of enlightenment and not to annoy me,

And the answer I give him, that he will readily understand.”

Then Ven. Ānanda said to Subhadda the wanderer, “Go ahead, friend Subhadda. The Blessed One gives you his leave. ”

Then Subhadda approached the Lord, exchanged courtesies with him, and sat down to one side.

As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One, “Master Gotama, these *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*, each with his group, each with his community, each the teacher of his group, an honored leader, well-regarded by people at large—i. e. , Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambalin, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Velaṭṭhaputta, & the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: Do they all have direct knowledge as they themselves claim, or do they all not have direct knowledge, or do some of them have direct knowledge and some of them not?

“Enough, Subhadda. Put this question aside: ‘Do they all have direct knowledge as they themselves claim, or do they all not have direct knowledge, or do some of them have direct knowledge and some of them not?

I will teach you the *dharma*, Subhadda. Listen, and pay close attention. I will speak. ”

“As you say, lord,” Subhadda responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said,
commentary_pali: 213.Assosikhoti sāṇidvāre ṭhitassa bhāsato pakatisoteneva assosi, sutvā ca pana subhaddasseva atthāya mahatā ussāhena āgatattā alaṃ ānandātiādimāha. Tattha alanti paṭikkhepatthe nipāto. Aññāpekkhovāti aññātukāmova hutvā. Abbhaññiṃsūti yathā tesaṃ paṭiññā, tatheva jāniṃsu. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – sace nesaṃ sā paṭiññā niyyānikā, sabbe abbhaññaṃsu, no ce, na abbhaññaṃsu. Tasmā kiṃ tesaṃ paṭiññā niyyānikā, aniyyānikāti ayameva tassa pañhassa attho. Atha bhagavā tesaṃ aniyyānikabhāvakathanena atthābhāvato ceva okāsābhāvato ca ‘‘ala’’nti paṭikkhipitvā dhammameva desesi. Paṭhamayāmasmiñhi mallānaṃ dhammaṃ desetvā majjhimayāme subhaddassa, pacchimayāme bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ovaditvā balavapaccūsasamaye parinibbāyissāmicceva bhagavā āgato.
commentary_english:
213.
He heard.

It seems that, standing at the door, he heard the natural sound. And having heard, because he had come with great enthusiasm for the sake of Subhadda, he said, "Enough, Ānanda!" and so on.

Here, *alam* is a particle in the sense of prohibition.

*aññāpekkhovā* means having the desire to know.

*abbhaññiṃsū* means they knew it just as was their promise.

This means: if that promise of theirs is a means of deliverance, all have known it; if not, they have not known it.

Therefore, what is their promise? Is it a means of deliverance, or not a means of deliverance?

This itself is the meaning of that question.

Then the Blessed One, by speaking of the state of not being a means of deliverance, because of the absence of meaning and also because of the absence of opportunity, having rejected it with "Enough!", taught the Dharma itself.

For the Blessed One came, having taught the Dharma to the Mallas in the first watch of the night, to Subhadda in the middle watch, and having exhorted the community of monks in the last watch, [saying,] "I will attain *parinirvāṇa* in the powerful dawn."

mula_pali:
214. ‘‘Yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo na upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhati. Dutiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Tatiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Catutthopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Yasmiñca kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, tatiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, catutthopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati. Imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, idheva, subhadda, samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo, suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehi aññe (pī.). Ime ca idheva (ka.), subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assāti.

‘‘Ekūnatiṃso vayasā subhadda,

Yaṃ pabbajiṃ kiṃkusalānuesī;

Vassāni paññāsa samādhikāni,

Yato ahaṃ pabbajito subhadda.

Ñāyassa dhammassa padesavattī,

Ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthi.

‘‘Dutiyopi samaṇo natthi. Tatiyopi samaṇo natthi. Catutthopi samaṇo natthi. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehi. Ime ca, subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assā’’ti.
mula_english:
“In whatsoever *Dhamma* and Discipline, Subhadda, the noble eightfold path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*) is not found, neither is there found a true ascetic (*samaṇo*) .
There is no contemplative of the second order;
the third,
nor the fourth degree of saintliness.
But in whatsoever *Dhamma* and Discipline the noble eightfold path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*) is found, there is found a true ascetic (*samaṇo*), the second is found, the third is found, and the fourth is found.
Now in this *Dhamma* and Discipline, Subhadda, is found the noble eightfold path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*); and in it alone are also found true ascetics (*samaṇo*). Devoid of true ascetics are the systems of other teachers.
But if here monks live perfectly, the world won’t lack for *arahants*.’

‘I was twenty-nine, Subhadda,
when I went forth seeking what is good;
now fifty years and more have passed
since I went forth, Subhadda.

Living within the domain of the teaching of truth,
outside of this there is no contemplative.

”And there is none of the second degree,
third
nor of the fourth degree of saintliness.
Other schools of such are bare,
But if, Subhadda, the *bhikkhus* live righteously, the world will not be destitute of *arahats*.“
commentary_pali:
214.Samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhatīti paṭhamo sotāpannasamaṇopi tattha natthi, dutiyo sakadāgāmisamaṇopi, tatiyo anāgāmisamaṇopi, catuttho arahattasamaṇopi tattha natthīti attho. ‘‘Imasmiṃ kho’’ti purimadesanāya aniyamato vatvā idāni attano sāsanaṃ niyamento āha. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhīti catunnaṃ maggānaṃ atthāya āraddhavipassakehi catūhi, maggaṭṭhehi catūhi, phalaṭṭhehi catūhīti dvādasahi samaṇehi suññā parappavādā tucchā rittakā. Ime ca subhaddāti ime dvādasa bhikkhū. Sammā vihareyyunti ettha sotāpanno attano adhigataṭṭhānaṃ aññassa kathetvā taṃ sotāpannaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sakadāgāmiādīsu. Sotāpattimaggaṭṭho aññampi sotāpattimaggaṭṭhaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sesamaggaṭṭhesu. Sotāpattimaggatthāya āraddhavipassako attano paguṇaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetvā aññampi sotāpattimaggatthāya āraddhavipassakaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sesamaggatthāya āraddhavipassakesu. Idaṃ sandhāyāha – ‘‘sammā vihareyyu’’nti. Asuñño loko arahantehi assāti naḷavanaṃ saravanaṃ viya nirantaro assa.

Ekūnatiṃso vayasāti vayena ekūnatiṃsavasso hutvā. Yaṃ pabbajinti ettha yanti nipātamattaṃ. Kiṃ kusalānuesīti ‘‘kiṃ kusala’’nti anuesanto pariyesanto. Tattha – ‘‘kiṃ kusala’’nti sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ, taṃ gavesantoti attho. Yato ahanti yato paṭṭhāya ahaṃ pabbajito, etthantare samadhikāni paññāsa vassāni hontīti dasseti. Ñāyassa dhammassāti ariyamaggadhammassa. Padesavattīti padese vipassanāmagge pavattanto. Ito bahiddhāti mama sāsanato bahiddhā. Samaṇopinatthīti padesavattivipassakopi natthi, paṭhamasamaṇo sotāpannopi natthīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Ekūnatiṃso vayasā Yaṃ pabbaji ya Kiṃ kusalānuesī Yato aha Ñāyassa dhammassā Padesavattī Ito bahiddhā Samaṇopi natthī

Ye etthāti ye tumhe ettha sāsane satthārā sammukhā antevāsikābhisekena abhisittā, tesaṃ vo lābhā tesaṃ vo suladdhanti. Bāhirasamaye kira yaṃ antevāsikaṃ ācariyo – ‘‘imaṃ pabbājehi , imaṃ ovada, imaṃ anusāsā’’ti vadati, so tena attano ṭhāne ṭhapito hoti, tasmā tassa – ‘‘imaṃ pabbajehi, imaṃ ovada, imaṃ anusāsā’’ti ime lābhā honti. Therampi subhaddo tameva bāhirasamayaṃ gahetvā evamāha.

Ye etthā

Alattha khoti kathaṃ alattha? Thero kira naṃ ekamantaṃ netvā udakatumbato pānīyena sīsaṃ temetvā tacapañcakakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādāpetvā saraṇāni datvā bhagavato santikaṃ ānesi. Bhagavā upasampādetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhi. So taṃ gahetvā uyyānassa ekamante caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhāya ghaṭento vāyamanto vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhento saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ patvā āgamma bhagavantaṃ vanditvā nisīdi. Taṃ sandhāya – ‘‘acirūpasampanno kho panā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Alattha kho

So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosīti saṅgītikārakānaṃ vacanaṃ. Tattha yo bhagavati dharamāne pabbajitvā aparabhāge upasampadaṃ labhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, upasampadampi vā dharamāneyeva labhitvā aparabhāge kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, kammaṭṭhānampi vā dharamāneyeva gahetvā aparabhāge arahattameva pāpuṇāti, sabbopi so pacchimo sakkhisāvako. Ayaṃ pana dharamāneyeva bhagavati pabbajito ca upasampanno ca kammaṭṭhānañca gahetvā arahattaṃ pattoti.

So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī

Pañcamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Tathāgatapacchimavācāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
214. “*Samaṇo pi tattha na upalabbhatī*ti” means that even the first *sotāpanna-samaṇa* [stream-enterer ascetic] is not there, nor the second *sakadāgāmi-samaṇa* [once-returner ascetic], nor the third *anāgāmi-samaṇa* [non-returner ascetic], nor the fourth *arahatta-samaṇa* [arahat ascetic].

“*Imasmiṃ kho*”ti: Having spoken previously in an unfixed way, he now speaks fixing his own teaching.

“*Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhī*ti”: Empty are the doctrines of others by the twelve *samaṇa*s [ascetics]: by the four who have started to practice insight for the sake of the four paths, by the four who are established in the paths, and by the four who are established in the fruits – empty, hollow, void are the doctrines of others.

“*Ime ca subhaddā*ti”: These twelve monks.

“*Sammā vihareyyu*nti”: Here, the *sotāpanna* [stream-enterer] lives rightly, relating his attainment to another and making him a *sotāpanna* [stream-enterer].

This is the way with the *sakadāgāmi*s [once-returners] and so on.

The one established in the stream-entry path lives rightly, making another also established in the stream-entry path.

This is the way with the remaining path-followers.

The one who has started to practice insight for the sake of the stream-entry path lives rightly, relating his own skillful meditation subject and making another also one who has started to practice insight for the sake of the stream-entry path.

This is the way with the remaining ones who have started to practice insight for the sake of the path.

Intending this, he said: “*Sammā vihareyyu*nti” [they would live rightly].

“*Asuñño loko arahantehi assā*ti”: The world would not be empty of *arahat*s [worthy ones], like a reed-thicket or a grove of Sara reeds, uninterrupted.

“*Ekūnatiṃso vayasā*ti”: Having become twenty-nine years old in age.

“*Yaṃ pabbaji*nti”: Here, “*yaṃ*” is merely a particle.

“*Kiṃ kusalānuesī*ti”: Seeking, searching for “*kiṃ kusalaṃ*?” [what is skillful?].

There – “*kiṃ kusalaṃ*?” refers to the knowledge of omniscience, seeking that, is the meaning.

“*Yato aha*nti”: From when I went forth, in this interval, there are more than fifty years, he indicates.

“*Ñāyassa dhammassā*ti”: Of the Dharma of the Noble Path.

“*Padesavattī*ti”: Proceeding in the place, in the path of insight.

“*Ito bahiddhā*ti”: Outside of my teaching.

“*Samaṇopi natthī*ti”: Even a *padesavatti-vipassaka* [one who practices insight in a certain place] is not there, it is said that even the first *samaṇa*, the *sotāpanna* [stream-enterer], is not there.

*Ekūnatiṃso vayasā yaṃ pabbaji yaṃ kiṃ kusalānuesī yato ahaṃ ñāyassa dhammassā padesavattī ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthī*

“*Ye etthā*ti”: Those of you here in the teaching who are disciples consecrated by the Teacher face-to-face with the sprinkling of discipleship – it is a gain for you, it is well-gained for you.

It seems that in other sects, whatever disciple the teacher says – "Ordain this one, instruct this one, admonish this one" – that one is placed in his own position by him, therefore for him – "Ordain this one, instruct this one, admonish this one" – these are gains.

The Elder Subhadda, also taking up that same other sect, said this.

*Ye etthā*

“*Alattha kho*ti”: How did he obtain? It seems the Elder, having led him to one side, having wet his head with water from a water pot, having related the meditation subject of the five aggregates of skin, having removed his hair and beard, having made him put on ochre robes, having given the refuges, brought him to the presence of the Blessed One.

The Blessed One, having given him the full ordination, indicated the meditation subject.

He, having taken that up, establishing a walking path on one side of the park, striving, endeavoring, developing insight, having attained *arahatta* [worthiness] together with the discriminations, having come back, bowed to the Blessed One and sat down.

Referring to that, it was said: “*Acirūpasampanno kho panā*tiādi” [“Indeed, he was recently fully ordained,” and so on].

*Alattha kho*

“*So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī*ti”: This is the saying of the compilers of the Saṅgīti.

There, whoever goes forth while the Blessed One is living, and in the subsequent part obtains full ordination, having taken up a meditation subject, attains *arahatta* [worthiness], or even having obtained full ordination while he is living, in the subsequent part having taken up a meditation subject, attains *arahatta* [worthiness], or even having taken up a meditation subject while he is living, in the subsequent part attains just *arahatta* [worthiness], all of them are the last disciple by direct acquaintance.

But this one, while the Blessed One was living, both went forth and was fully ordained, and having taken up a meditation subject, attained *arahatta* [worthiness].

*So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī*

The fifth section for recitation is finished.
Explanation of the Last Words of the Tathāgata

mula_pali:
215. Evaṃ vutte subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti, evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada’’nti. ‘‘Yo kho, subhadda, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā’’ti. ‘‘Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ cattāro māse parivasanti, catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi, catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tenahānanda, subhaddaṃ pabbājehī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘lābhā vo, āvuso ānanda; suladdhaṃ vo, āvuso ānanda, ye ettha satthu satthārā (syā.) sammukhā antevāsikābhisekena abhisittā’’ti. Alattha kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā subhaddo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – ‘yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti’ tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā subhaddo arahataṃ ahosi. So bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosīti.

satthārā (syā.)

Pañcamo bhāṇavāro.

Tathāgatapacchimavācā
mula_english:
215. Then Subhadda the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, lord! Magnificent!
Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or reveal what is hidden, or point out the path to one who is lost, or hold up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One.
I go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
May I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence? May I receive the full admission?”

“Subhadda, whoever, having formerly belonged to another sect, wishes to receive the going forth in this Dhamma and Discipline, wishes to receive the full admission, remains on probation for a period of four months. After four months, if the monks are satisfied with him, they give him the going forth and the full admission to the state of a *bhikkhu*.
However, there can be a distinction of persons in this.”

“Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to another sect and desire the going forth and the full admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months, and if at the end of the four months the *bhikkhus* being satisfied with them give them the going forth and the full admission to the *bhikkhus*' state, then I will live on probation for four years.
