At the end of the four years if the *bhikkhus* are satisfied with me, let them give me the going forth and the full admission to the *bhikkhus*' state."

Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda: “Then, Ānanda, let Subhadda receive the going forth.”
“So be it, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.
Then Subhadda the wanderer said to the venerable Ānanda: “It is a gain for you, friend Ānanda; a blessing for you, friend Ānanda, that in the presence of the Teacher himself you have received the sprinkling of ordination as a disciple.”

Then Subhadda the wanderer received the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he received the full admission.
And soon, not long after his full admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the venerable Subhadda, by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the holy life (*brahmacariyapariyosāna*) for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
He understood: ‘Destroyed is birth; the holy life has been lived; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further here.’
And the venerable Subhadda became another one of the *arhats*.
He was the last personal disciple of the Blessed One.

The fifth section for recitation.
The Last Words of the *Tathāgata*.

mula_pali: 216. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho panānanda, tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘atītasatthukaṃ pāvacanaṃ, natthi no satthā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo vo, ānanda, mayā dhammo ca vinayo ca desito paññatto, so vo mamaccayena satthā. Yathā kho panānanda, etarahi bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ āvusovādena samudācaranti, na kho mamaccayena evaṃ samudācaritabbaṃ. Theratarena, ānanda, bhikkhunā navakataro bhikkhu nāmena vā gottena vā āvusovādena vā samudācaritabbo. Navakatarena bhikkhunā therataro bhikkhu ‘bhante’ti vā ‘āyasmā’ti vā samudācaritabbo. Ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatu. Channassa, ānanda, bhikkhuno mamaccayena brahmadaṇḍo dātabbo’’ti. ‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, brahmadaṇḍo’’ti? ‘‘Channo, ānanda, bhikkhu yaṃ iccheyya, taṃ vadeyya. So bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, na anusāsitabbo’’ti.
mula_english:
216. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “It may be, Ānanda, that this thought will occur to you: ‘The teaching has lost its arbitrator; we are without a Teacher.’

But it should not be seen like that, Ānanda.

Ānanda, whatever Dharma (dhammo) and Discipline (vinayo) I have taught and established, that will be your Teacher after my passing (mamaccayena satthā).

Just as now, Ānanda, the monks address one another as ‘friend’ (āvusovādena), it should not be done so after my passing.

The senior monk (theratarena bhikkhunā), Ānanda, may address the newer monk (navakataro bhikkhu) by name (nāmena), clan (gottena), or as ‘friend’ (āvusovādena).

The newer monk (navakatarena bhikkhunā) should address the senior monk (therataro bhikkhu) as ‘venerable sir’ (bhante’ti) or ‘venerable’ (āyasmā’ti).

If the Saṅgha wishes, Ānanda, after my passing, it may abolish the lesser and minor precepts (khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatu).

After my passing, Ānanda, the monk Channa should be given the Brahma-penalty (brahmadaṇḍo dātabbo).’

‘‘But venerable sir (bhante), what is the Brahma-penalty (brahmadaṇḍo)?’’ ‘‘Channa, Ānanda, may say whatever the monk wishes.

He should not be spoken to, admonished, or instructed by the monks (bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, na anusāsitabbo).’’
commentary_pali:
216. Idāni bhikkhusaṅghassa ovādaṃ ārabhi, taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho bhagavātiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha desito paññattoti dhammopi desito ceva paññatto ca, vinayopi desito ceva paññatto ca. Paññatto ca nāma ṭhapito paṭṭhapitoti attho. So vo mamaccayenāti so dhammavinayo tumhākaṃ mamaccayena satthā. Mayā hi vo ṭhiteneva – ‘‘idaṃ lahukaṃ, idaṃ garukaṃ, idaṃ satekicchaṃ, idaṃ atekicchaṃ, idaṃ lokavajjaṃ, idaṃ paṇṇattivajjaṃ, ayaṃ āpatti puggalassa santike vuṭṭhāti, ayaṃ āpatti gaṇassa santike vuṭṭhāti, ayaṃ saṅghassa santike vuṭṭhātī’’ti sattāpattikkhandhavasena otiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ sakhandhakaparivāro ubhatovibhaṅgo vinayo nāma desito, taṃ sakalampi vinayapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati.

Ṭhiteneva ca mayā – ‘‘ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañca indriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’’ti tena tenākārena ime dhamme vibhajitvā vibhajitvā suttantapiṭakaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ sakalampi suttantapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati. Ṭhiteneva ca mayā – ‘‘ime pañcakkhandhā, dvādasāyatanāni, aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo, cattāri saccāni, bāvīsatindriyāni, nava hetū, cattāro āhārā, satta phassā, satta vedanā, satta saññā, satta sañcetanā, satta cittāni. Tatrāpi ‘ettakā dhammā kāmāvacarā, ettakā rūpāvacarā, ettakā arūpāvacarā, ettakā pariyāpannā, ettakā apariyāpannā, ettakā lokiyā, ettakā lokuttarā’ti’’ ime dhamme vibhajitvā vibhajitvā catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānaanantanayamahāpaṭṭhānapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ sakalampi abhidhammapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati.

Iti sabbampetaṃ abhisambodhito yāva parinibbānā pañcacattālīsavassāni bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ – ‘‘tīṇi piṭakāni, pañca nikāyā, navaṅgāni, caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassānī’’ti evaṃ mahāpabhedaṃ hoti. Iti imāni caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni tiṭṭhanti, ahaṃ ekova parinibbāyāmi. Ahañca kho pana dāni ekakova ovadāmi anusāsāmi, mayi parinibbute imāni caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni tumhe ovadissanti anusāsissantīti evaṃ bhagavā bahūni kāraṇāni dassento – ‘‘so vo mamaccayena satthā’’ti ovaditvā puna anāgate cārittaṃ dassento yathā kho panātiādimāha.

yathā kho panā

Tattha samudācarantīti kathenti voharanti. Nāmena vā gottena vāti navakāti avatvā ‘‘tissa, nāgā’’ti evaṃ nāmena vā, ‘‘kassapa, gotamā’’ti evaṃ gottena vā, ‘‘āvuso tissa, āvuso kassapā’’ti evaṃ āvusovādena vā samudācaritabbo. Bhanteti vā āyasmāti vāti bhante tissa, āyasmā tissāti evaṃ samudācaritabbo. Samūhanatūti ākaṅkhamāno samūhanatu, yadi icchati samūhaneyyāti attho. Kasmā pana samūhanathāti ekaṃseneva avatvā vikappavacaneneva ṭhapesīti? Mahākassapassa balaṃ diṭṭhattā. Passati hi bhagavā – ‘‘samūhanathāti vuttepi saṅgītikāle kassapo na samūhanissatī’’ti. Tasmā vikappeneva ṭhapesi.

samudācarantī Nāmena vā gottena vā Bhanteti vā āyasmāti vā Samūhanatū

Tattha – ‘‘ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakānī’’tiādinā nayena pañcasatikasaṅgītiyaṃ khuddānukhuddakakathā āgatāva vinicchayo pettha samantapāsādikāyaṃ vutto. Keci panāhu – ‘‘bhante, nāgasena, katamaṃ khuddakaṃ, katamaṃ anukhuddaka’’nti milindena raññā pucchito. ‘‘Dukkaṭaṃ, mahārāja, khuddakaṃ, dubbhāsitaṃ anukhuddaka’’nti vuttattā nāgasenatthero khuddānukhuddakaṃ jānāti. Mahākassapo pana taṃ ajānanto –

khuddānukhuddakakathā samantapāsādikāyaṃ

‘‘Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho santamhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni, gihinopi jānanti – ‘‘idaṃ vo samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’’ti. Sace mayaṃ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro – ‘‘dhūmakālikaṃ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, yāva nesaṃ satthā aṭṭhāsi, tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṃsu, yato imesaṃ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’’ti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho apaññattaṃ na paññapeyya, paññattaṃ na samucchindeyya, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vatteyya. Esā ñattīti –

Kammavācaṃ sāvesīti. Na taṃ evaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Nāgasenatthero hi – ‘‘paravādino okāso mā ahosī’’ti evamāha. Mahākassapatthero ‘‘khuddānukhuddakāpattiṃ na samūhanissāmī’’ti kammavācaṃ sāvesi.

Brahmadaṇḍakathāpi saṅgītiyaṃ āgatattāsamantapāsādikāyaṃ vinicchitā.

Brahmadaṇḍakathāpi

Kaṅkhāti dveḷhakaṃ. Vimatīti vinicchituṃ asamatthatā, buddho nu kho, na buddho nu kho, dhammo nu kho, na dhammo nu kho, saṅgho nu kho, na saṅgho nu kho, maggo nu kho, na maggo nu kho, paṭipadā nu kho, na paṭipadā nu khoti yassa saṃsayo uppajjeyya, taṃ vo vadāmi ‘‘pucchatha bhikkhave’’ti ayamettha saṅkhepattho. Satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthāti mayaṃ satthusantike pabbajimha, cattāro paccayāpi no satthu santakāva, te mayaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ kaṅkhaṃ akatvā na arahāma ajja pacchimakāle kaṅkhaṃ kātunti sace evaṃ satthari gāravena na pucchatha. Sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetūti tumhākaṃ yo yassa bhikkhuno sandiṭṭho sambhatto, so tassa ārocetu, ahaṃ etassa bhikkhussa kathessāmi, tassa kathaṃ sutvā sabbe nikkaṅkhā bhavissathāti dasseti.

Kaṅkhā Vimatī Satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthā Sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetū

Evaṃ pasannoti evaṃ saddahāmi ahanti attho. Ñāṇamevāti nikkaṅkhabhāvapaccakkhakaraṇañāṇaṃyeva, ettha tathāgatassa na saddhāmattanti attho. Imesañhi, ānandāti imesaṃ antosāṇiyaṃ nisinnānaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ. Yo pacchimakoti yo guṇavasena pacchimako. Ānandattheraṃyeva sandhāyāha.

Evaṃ pasanno Ñāṇamevā Imesañhi, ānandā Yo pacchimako
commentary_english:
216. Now, he begins the instruction to the monastic community, and to show that, it is said, "Then, indeed, the Blessed One," etc. There, "taught and designated" means the Dharma is both taught and designated, and the Vinaya is both taught and designated. "Designated" means named, established, and set forth; this is the meaning. "So vo mamaccayenā" means that the Dharma and Vinaya will be your teacher after my passing. Indeed, by me standing firm – "This is light, this is heavy, this requires treatment, this does not require treatment, this is objectionable to the world, this is objectionable by designation, this offense is resolved in the presence of an individual, this offense is resolved in the presence of a group, this offense is resolved in the presence of the Sangha" – thus, due to the force of the aggregates of offenses, in a matter that has been decided, with its related aggregates, the Ubhatovibhaṅga called the "Vinaya" was taught; all of that Vinaya Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher. And, by me standing firm – "These are the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni), the four right exertions (catvāri samyakprahāṇāni), the four bases of spiritual power (catvāri ṛddhipādāḥ), the five faculties (pañca indriyāṇi), the five powers (pañca balāni), the seven factors of awakening (sapta bojjhaṅgāḥ), the noble eightfold path (āryāṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ)" – in that way, dividing and distinguishing these dharmas, the Sūtra Piṭaka was taught; all of that Sūtra Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher. And, by me standing firm – "These are the five aggregates (pañcakkhandhā), the twelve sense bases (dvādasāyatanāni), the eighteen elements (aṣṭārasa dhātuyo), the four truths (cattāri satyāni), the twenty-two faculties (bāvīsatindriyāni), the nine causes (nava hetū), the four kinds of nutriment (cattāro āhārā), the seven contacts (sapta phassā), the seven feelings (sapta vedanā), the seven perceptions (sapta saññā), the seven volitions (sapta sañcetanā), the seven consciousnesses (sapta cittāni)." There also, 'So many *dharmas* belong to the realm of desire (*kāmāvacarā*), so many belong to the realm of form (*rūpāvacarā*), so many belong to the formless realm (*arūpāvacarā*), so many are included (*pariyāpannā*), so many are not included (*apariyāpannā*), so many are mundane (*lokiyā*), so many are supramundane (*lokuttarā*)' – dividing and distinguishing these *dharmas*, the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, adorned with the twenty-four conditions of the Samantapaṭṭhāna and the Anantanayamahāpaṭṭhāna, was taught; all of that Abhidhamma Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher. Thus, all of this, from complete enlightenment until passing into *nirvāṇa*, for forty-five years, was spoken and uttered – "The three Piṭakas, the five Nikāyas, the nine divisions, the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma (dhammakkhandhasahassānī)" – thus, there is a great distinction. Thus, these eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma remain, but I alone will pass into *nirvāṇa*. And now, indeed, I alone instruct and admonish, but when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, these eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma will instruct and admonish you; thus, the Blessed One, showing many reasons – "The Dharma is your teacher after my passing" – having instructed thus, and again showing the conduct in the future, said "Just as, indeed," etc. Just as, indeed, there, "samudācarantī" means they speak and refer to. "nāmena vā gottena vā" means, not saying "novice," but "Tissa, Nāga," thus by name, or "Kassapa, Gotama," thus by lineage, or "Āvuso Tissa, Āvuso Kassapa," thus with the greeting "Āvuso," one should address him. "bhanteti vā āyasmāti vā" means, "Bhante Tissa, Āyasmā Tissa," thus one should address him. "samūhanatū" means, if he desires, let him remove it; the meaning is, if he wishes, he should remove it. Why, indeed, did he establish it with a differentiating statement instead of saying it with a one-sided statement? Because he saw the strength of Mahākassapa. For the Blessed One sees – "Even if I say, 'Let him remove it,' Kassapa will not remove it at the Saṅgīti time." Therefore, he established it with a differentiating statement. There – "Some elders said thus – having set aside the four pārājikas, the remaining lesser and minor [rules]," – in this way, in the Pañcasatikasaṅgīti, the topic of the lesser and minor [rules] came up, and the decision is said to be in the Samantapāsādikā. Some, however, said – "Bhante Nāgasena, which is lesser, which is minor?" – thus Milinda the king was asked. "Dukkaṭaṃ, Mahārāja, is lesser, dubbhāsitaṃ is minor," because it was said, Nāgasena Thera knows the lesser and minor. But Mahākassapa, not knowing that – "khuddānukhuddakakathā samantapāsādikāyaṃ" "Let the Sangha listen to me, friends, our training rules have gone to the householders, even the householders know – 'This is suitable for you ascetics, sons of the Sakyas, this is not suitable for you.'" If we were to remove the lesser and minor training rules, there would be speakers – "The training rule was designated for those with smoky minds by the ascetic Gotama for the disciples; as long as their teacher remained, so long did these train in the training rules; since their teacher has passed away, now these do not train in the training rules." If it seems appropriate to the Sangha, the Sangha should not lay down what has not been laid down, nor should it abolish what has been laid down. It should proceed in conformity with and according to the training rules that have been laid down. This is the declaration – He recited the Kammavāca. That should not be taken thus. Nāgasena Thera, indeed, said thus – "Lest the opponents have an opportunity." Mahākassapa Thera recited the Kammavāca, "I will not remove the offense regarding the lesser and minor." kaṅkhāti dveḷhakaṃ. vimatīti vinicchituṃ asamatthatā, buddho nu kho, na buddho nu kho, dhammo nu kho, na dhammo nu kho, saṅgho nu kho, na saṅgho nu kho, maggo nu kho, na maggo nu kho, *paṭipadā* nu kho, na *paṭipadā* nu khoti yassa *saṃsayo* *uppajjeyya*, taṃ vo vadāmi ‘‘*pucchatha bhikṣave*’’ti ayamettha *saṅkhepattho*. satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthāti mayaṃ satthusantike *pabbajimha*, *cattāro paccayāpi* no *satthu santakāva*, te mayaṃ ettakaṃ *kālaṃ kaṅkhaṃ akatvā* na *arahāma ajja pacchimakāle kaṅkhaṃ kātunti sace evaṃ satthari gāravena na *pucchatha*. sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetūti tumhākaṃ yo yassa *bhikkhuno sandiṭṭho sambhatto*, so tassa *ārocetu*, ahaṃ etassa *bhikkhussa kathessāmi*, tassa *kathaṃ sutvā sabbe nikkaṅkhā bhavissathāti dasseti*.

kaṅkhā vimatī satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthā sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetū

evaṃ pasannoti evaṃ *saddahāmi ahanti attho*. ñāṇamevāti *nikkaṅkhabhāvapaccakkhakaraṇañāṇaṃyeva*, ettha *tathāgatassa na saddhāmattanti attho*. imesañhi, ānandāti imesaṃ antosāṇiyaṃ nisinnānaṃ *pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ*. yo pacchimakoti yo *guṇavasena pacchimako*. *ānandattheraṃyeva sandhāyāha*.

evaṃ pasanno ñāṇamevā imesañhi, ānandā yo pacchimako

mula_pali: 217. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi , na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’’’ nti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi , na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’’’ nti. Tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, satthugāravenapi na puccheyyātha. Sahāyakopi, bhikkhave, sahāyakassa ārocetū’’ti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe, ‘natthi ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā’’’ti. ‘‘Pasādā kho tvaṃ, ānanda, vadesi, ñāṇameva hettha, ānanda, tathāgatassa. Natthi imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā. Imesañhi, ānanda, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ yo pacchimako bhikkhu, so sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’’ti.
mula_english:
217. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or perplexity about the Buddha, the *Dharma* (dhamma), or the *Sangha* (saṅgha), the path (*mārga*, magge) or the practice (*pratipadā*, paṭipadāya), ask! Do not afterwards feel remorse, thinking: ‘The Teacher (*śāstṛ*, satthā) was there before us, and we failed to ask the Lord face to face!’”

When this was said, the monks were silent.

A second time, … A third time, the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or perplexity about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, the path or the practice, ask! Do not afterwards feel remorse, thinking: ‘The Teacher was there before us, and we failed to ask the Lord face to face!’”

A third time, the monks were silent.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, out of respect for the Teacher (śāstṛ-gāraveṇa) that you do not ask.

Then, monks, let one friend tell it to another.”

When this was said, the monks were silent.

Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Lord (*bhante*), it is marvellous! I clearly perceive that in this *bhikṣu-saṃgha* (bhikkhusaṅghe) there is not one monk who has doubts or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, or about the path or the practice.”

“Out of confidence, Ānanda, you speak thus. But here, Ānanda, the *Tathāgata* (tathāgatassa) knows for certain that in this *bhikṣu-saṃgha* there is not one monk who has doubts or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, or about the path or the practice.

For, Ānanda, among these five hundred monks even the lowest is a *stream-enterer* (sotāpanna), secure from downfall, assured, and bound for enlightenment (*sambodhi-parāyaṇa*).”

mula_pali:
218. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘handa dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā appamādena sampādethā’’ti. Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā.

Parinibbutakathā
mula_english: Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, "Come now, monks, I exhort you: All conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive with earnestness!" This was the last word of the *Tathāgata*.
commentary_pali:
218.Appamādena sampādethāti satiavippavāsena sabbakiccāni sampādeyyātha. Iti bhagavā parinibbānamañce nipanno pañcacattālīsa vassāni dinnaṃ ovādaṃ sabbaṃ ekasmiṃ appamādapadeyeva pakkhipitvā adāsi. Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācāti idaṃ pana saṅgītikārakānaṃ vacanaṃ.

Parinibbutakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"Accomplish [your goals] with diligence (appamādena sampādethā)," meaning you should accomplish all your tasks with mindfulness (satiavippavāsena).

Thus, the Blessed One, lying on the deathbed (parinibbānamañce), having given advice for forty-five years, placed it all into a single word: diligence (appamāda).

"This is the last teaching of the Tathāgata (ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā)," this statement, however, is the word of the compilers (saṅgītikārakānaṃ vacanaṃ).

Explanation of the Discourse on the Final Passing (parinibbutakathāvaṇṇanā).

mula_pali:
219. Atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajji.

Atha kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘parinibbuto, bhante anuruddha , bhagavā’’ti. ‘‘Nāvuso ānanda, bhagavā parinibbuto, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyi.
mula_english:
219. Then the Blessed One entered the first *jhāna*. Rising from the first *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the fourth *jhāna*.

Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of space, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, he entered the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of nothingness, he entered the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he entered the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*).

Then venerable Ānanda said this to venerable Anuruddha: "The Blessed One has attained final *nirvana*, venerable Anuruddha."

"No, friend Ānanda, the Blessed One has not attained final *nirvana*. He has entered the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno*)."

Then the Blessed One, rising from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*), entered the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he entered the dimension of nothingness. Rising from the attainment of the dimension of nothingness, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness. Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of space, he entered the fourth *jhāna*. Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the first *jhāna*. Rising from the first *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the fourth *jhāna*. Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately thereafter, the Blessed One attained final *nirvana* (*parinibbāyi*).
commentary_pali:
219. Ito paraṃ yaṃ parinibbānaparikammaṃ katvā bhagavā parinibbuto, taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhānantiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha parinibbuto bhanteti nirodhaṃ samāpannassa bhagavato assāsapassāsānaṃ abhāvaṃ disvā pucchati. Na āvusoti thero kathaṃ jānāti? Thero kira satthārā saddhiṃyeva taṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajjanto yāva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā vuṭṭhānaṃ, tāva gantvā idāni bhagavā nirodhaṃ samāpanno, antonirodhe ca kālaṅkiriyā nāma natthīti jānāti.

Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji…pe… tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjīti ettha bhagavā catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpajji, terasasu ṭhānesu dutiyajjhānaṃ, tathā tatiyajjhānaṃ, pannarasasu ṭhānesu catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Kathaṃ? Dasasu asubhesu, dvattiṃsākāre aṭṭhasu kasiṇesu, mettākaruṇāmuditāsu, ānāpāne, paricchedākāseti imesu tāva catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Ṭhapetvā pana dvattiṃsākārañca dasa asubhāni ca sesesu terasasu dutiyajjhānaṃ , tesuyeva ca tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Aṭṭhasu pana kasiṇesu, upekkhābrahmavihāre, ānāpāne, paricchedākāse, catūsu arūpesūti imesu pannarasasu ṭhānesu catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Ayampi ca saṅkhepakathāva. Nibbānapuraṃ pavisanto pana bhagavā dhammassāmī sabbāpi catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā samāpattiyo pavisitvā videsaṃ gacchanto ñātijanaṃ āliṅgetvā viya sabbasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavitvā paviṭṭho.

Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji…pe… tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjī

Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyīti ettha jhānasamanantaraṃ, paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaranti dve samanantarāni. Tattha jhānā vuṭṭhāya bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa tattheva parinibbānaṃ jhānasamanantaraṃ nāma. Jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā puna jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa tattheva parinibbānaṃ paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ nāma. Imānipi dve samanantarāneva. Bhagavā pana jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā jhānā vuṭṭhāya jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā bhavaṅgacittena abyākatena dukkhasaccena parinibbāyi. Ye hi keci buddhā vā paccekabuddhā vā ariyasāvakā vā antamaso kunthakipillikaṃ upādāya sabbe bhavaṅgacitteneva abyākatena dukkhasaccena kālaṅkarontīti. Mahābhūmicālādīni vuttanayānevāti.

Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyī jhānasamanantaraṃ paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ Mahābhūmicālādīni
commentary_english:
219. Next, in order to show how the Bhagavān, having performed the preliminary act of *parinirvāṇa*, attained *parinirvāṇa*, it is said, "Then, indeed, the Bhagavān [entered] the first *jhāna*, etc."

There, [the words] "*parinibbuto bhante* [has attained *parinirvāṇa*, venerable sir]" is a question asked after seeing the cessation of inhalation and exhalation of the Bhagavān who has entered cessation (*nirodhaṃ samāpannassa*).

"No, friend" — how does the elder know? The elder, it is said, went along with the Teacher, entering into that and that meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) up to arising from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), and now the Bhagavān has entered cessation (*nirodhaṃ samāpanno*), and knows that there is no death in cessation.

Then, indeed, the Bhagavān, arising from the meditative attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*) entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*)…pe… arising from the third *jhāna*, entered the fourth *jhāna*—here, the Bhagavān entered the first *jhāna* in twenty-four places, the second *jhāna* in thirteen places, likewise the third *jhāna*, and the fourth *jhāna* in fifteen places.

How? In the ten impurities (*asubhesu*), in the thirty-two aspects (*dvattiṃsākāre*), in the eight *kasiṇas*, in loving-kindness (*mettā*), compassion (*karuṇā*), joy (*muditā*), in mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpāne*), in the delimited space (*paricchedākāseti*)—in these twenty-four places, the first *jhāna* was entered.

However, setting aside the thirty-two aspects (*dvattiṃsākārañca*) and the ten impurities (*dasa asubhāni ca*), in the remaining thirteen, the second *jhāna*,… in those same, the third *jhāna* was entered.

However, in the eight *kasiṇas*, equanimity (*upekkhā*), the divine abidings (*brahmavihāre*), mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpāne*), delimited space (*paricchedākāse*), in the four formless realms (*arūpesūti*)—in these fifteen places, the fourth *jhāna* was entered.

This is just a summary talk.

However, the Bhagavān, the lord of the Dharma, entering the city of nirvāṇa (*nibbānapuraṃ pavisanto*), having entered into all the meditative attainments (*samāpatti*) numbering twenty-four *koṭis*, hundreds of thousands, and going to a foreign land, like embracing relatives, having experienced all the bliss of meditative attainment (*sabbasamāpatti-sukhaṃ*), entered.

Then, indeed, the Bhagavān, arising from the meditative attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*) entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*)…pe… arising from the third *jhāna*, entered the fourth *jhāna*.

Having arisen from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately, the Bhagavān attained *parinirvāṇa*—here, immediately after the *jhāna*, immediately after reviewing—these are the two immediate successions.

There, having arisen from *jhāna*, for one who has fallen into the life-continuum (*bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa*), *parinirvāṇa* in that very place is called immediately after *jhāna* (*jhānasamanantaraṃ*).

Having arisen from *jhāna*, again, having reviewed the factors of *jhāna* (*jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā*), for one who has fallen into the life-continuum (*bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa*), *parinirvāṇa* in that very place is called immediately after reviewing (*paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ*).

These two are just immediate successions.

However, the Bhagavān, having entered *jhāna* (*jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā*), having arisen from *jhāna*, having reviewed the factors of *jhāna* (*jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā*), attained *parinirvāṇa* with the life-continuum mind (*bhavaṅgacittena*), unpronounced, with the truth of suffering (*dukkhasaccena*).

Indeed, any Buddhas, solitary Buddhas, or noble disciples, even taking a small ant as the limit, all die with the life-continuum mind (*bhavaṅgacitteneva*), unpronounced, with the truth of suffering (*dukkhasaccena*).

Great earthquakes, etc., are just in accordance with what has been said.

Having arisen from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately, the Bhagavān attained *parinirvāṇa*. Immediately after *jhāna*. Immediately after reviewing. Great earthquakes, etc.

mula_pali:
220. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso. Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā brahmāsahampati imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Sabbeva nikkhipissanti, bhūtā loke samussayaṃ;

Yattha etādiso satthā, loke appaṭipuggalo;

Tathāgato balappatto, sambuddho parinibbuto’’ti.
commentary_pali: 220.Bhūtāti sattā. Appaṭipuggaloti paṭibhāgapuggalavirahito. Balappattoti dasavidhañāṇabalaṃ patto.
commentary_english:
[p. 220]
*bhūtā*ti sattā: *Bhuta* means beings (*sattvāḥ*).
*appaṭipuggalo*ti paṭibhāgapuggalavirahito: *Appaṭipuggalo* means one who is without a counterpart (*paṭibhāga-puggala-virahitaḥ*).
*balappatto*ti dasavidhañāṇabalaṃ patto: *Balappatto* means one who has attained the power of ten kinds of knowledge (*daśavidha-jñāna-balam* *prāptaḥ*).

mula_pali:
221. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā sakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Aniccā vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho’’ti.
commentary_pali: 221.Uppādavayadhamminoti uppādavayasabhāvā. Tesaṃ vūpasamoti tesaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ vūpasamo, asaṅkhataṃ nibbānameva sukhanti attho.
commentary_english:
*uppādavayadhammino* means *uppāda-vaya-sabhāvā*.

*tesaṃ vūpasamo* means *tesaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ vūpasamo*, the unconditioned *nirvāṇa* itself is happiness, is the meaning.

mula_pali:
222. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

‘‘Nāhu assāsapassāso, ṭhitacittassa tādino;

Anejo santimārabbha, yaṃ kālamakarī muni.

‘‘Asallīnena cittena, vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi;

Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ, vimokkho cetaso ahū’’ti.
commentary_pali:
222.Nāhu assāsapassāsoti na jāto assāsapassāso. Anejoti taṇhāsaṅkhātāya ejāya abhāvena anejo. Santimārabbhāti anupādisesaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha paṭicca sandhāya. Yaṃ kālamakarīti yo kālaṃ akari. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘āvuso, yo mama satthā buddhamuni santiṃ gamissāmīti, santiṃ ārabbha kālamakari, tassa ṭhitacittassa tādino idāni assāsapassāso na jāto, natthi, nappavattatī’’ti.

Asallīnenāti alīnena asaṅkuṭitena suvikasiteneva cittena. Vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayīti vedanaṃ adhivāsesi, na vedanānuvattī hutvā ito cito ca samparivatti. Vimokkhoti kenaci dhammena anāvaraṇavimokkho sabbaso apaññattibhāvūpagamo pajjotanibbānasadiso jāto.

Asallīnenā Vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayī Vimokkho
commentary_english:
222.
"There was no in-breath and out-breath" means there was no arising of in-breath and out-breath.
"Without craving" means without craving, due to the absence of craving as a designation of craving.
"Relying on peace" means relying on peace, having approached extinction, conditioned and connected.
"When he made time" means when he did time.
This was said: "Friend, my teacher, the Buddha, the sage, thinking 'I will go to peace,' relying on peace, made time; for him, whose mind was steadfast, of such a nature, now there is no arising of in-breath and out-breath, it is not, it does not occur."

"Without clinging" means with a mind that is unattached, uncontracted, very fully developed.
"He dwelt in feeling" means he endured feeling; not becoming one who follows feeling, going here and there.
"Release" means by some *dharma*, release without obstruction, the attainment of a state of complete non-conceptualization, is like the extinction of a lamp.

Without clinging, he dwelt in feeling, release.

mula_pali:
223. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Tadāsi yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;

Sabbākāravarūpete, sambuddhe parinibbute’’ti.
commentary_pali: 223.Tadāsīti ‘‘saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo’’ti evaṃ heṭṭhā vuttaṃ bhūmicālameva sandhāyāha. Tañhi lomahaṃsanañca bhiṃsanakañca āsi. Sabbākāravarūpeteti sabbavarakāraṇūpete.
commentary_english:
223. "tadāsī" [iti] (thus).
‘‘saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo’’ti: "Together with complete extinction, a great earthquake," thus, concerning the earthquake mentioned below, [it] is said.
tañhi lomahaṃsanañca bhiṃsanakañca āsi: That was hair-raising and terrifying.
"sabbākāravarūpete" [iti] (thus) sabbavarakāraṇūpete: Endowed with all excellent forms, endowed with all excellent causes.

mula_pali: 224. Parinibbute bhagavati ye te tattha bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti, ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto , atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’’ti.
mula_english:
When the Blessed One had attained *parinirvāṇa*, some monks there who were not yet free from passion wept, raising their arms. Some flung themselves down as if their feet were cut off, rolling back and forth, crying, "All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

But those monks who were free from passion endured, mindful and fully aware, reflecting, "Impermanent are compounded things (*saṅkhārā*); what else is to be expected?"
commentary_pali: 224.Avītarāgāti puthujjanā ceva sotāpannasakadāgāmino ca. Tesañhi domanassaṃ appahīnaṃ. Tasmā tepi bāhā paggayha kandanti. Ubhopi hatthe sīse ṭhapetvā rodantīti sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english: 224. avītarāgāti, ordinary people, stream-enterers (sotāpanna), and once-returners (sakadāgāmino) as well. For their sorrow (domanassaṃ) is not abandoned (appahīnaṃ). Therefore (tasmā), they too (tepi), raising their arms (bāhā paggayha), weep (kandanti). Both (ubhopi), placing their hands (hatthe) on their heads (sīse ṭhapetvā), weep (rodantīti). All (sabbaṃ) this is to be understood (veditabbaṃ) in the same way as before (purimanayeneva).

mula_pali:
225. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati . Devatā, āvuso, ujjhāyantī’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, āyasmā anuruddho devatā manasi karotī’’ti bhante anuruddha devatā manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)?

‘‘Santāvuso ānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Santāvuso ānanda, devatā pathaviyā pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto , atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Yā pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca ānando taṃ rattāvasesaṃ dhammiyā kathāya vītināmesuṃ.
mula_english:
225. Then the Venerable Anuruddha addressed the monks, saying: “Enough, friends! Do not grieve, do not lament!

Has not the Blessed One already taught that with all that is dear and beloved there must be change, separation, and severance? (sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo)

What else is there to expect, friends?

Of that which is born, come into being, compounded and subject to decay, how can one say: ‘May it not come to dissolution!’? There can be no such state of things.

The devatās, friends, are complaining.”

“But, venerable sir, of what kind of devatās is the Venerable Anuruddha aware?”

“Friend Ānanda, there are devatās in space who perceive earth; tearing at their hair, they weep; raising their arms, they weep; as if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back and forth, crying, ‘All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!’

“Friend Ānanda, there are devatās on earth who perceive earth; tearing at their hair, they weep; raising their arms, they weep; as if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back and forth, crying, ‘All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*!, All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!’

But those devatās who are free from craving endure patiently, saying: “Impermanent are all compounded things (*aniccā saṅkhārā*)—what else is there to expect?”

Then the Venerable Anuruddha and the Venerable Ānanda spent the rest of the night in religious conversation ( *dhammiyā kathāya*).
commentary_pali:
225.Ujjhāyantīti ‘‘ayyā attanāpi adhivāsetuṃ na sakkonti, sesajanaṃ kathaṃ samassāsessantī’’ti vadantiyo ujjhāyanti. Kathaṃbhūtā pana bhante āyasmā anuruddho devatā manasikarotīti devatā, bhante, kathaṃbhūtā āyasmā anuruddho sallakkheti, kiṃ tā satthu parinibbānaṃ adhivāsentīti?

Atha tāsaṃ pavattidassanatthaṃ thero santāvusotiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. Rattāvasesanti balavapaccūse parinibbutattā rattiyā avasesaṃ cullakaddhānaṃ. Dhammiyā kathāyāti aññā pāṭiyekkā dhammakathā nāma natthi, ‘‘āvuso sadevake nāma loke appaṭipuggalassa satthuno ayaṃ maccurājā na lajjati, kimaṅgaṃ pana lokiyamahājanassa lajjissatī’’ti evarūpāya pana maraṇapaṭisaṃyuttāya kathāya vītināmesuṃ. Tesañhi taṃ kathaṃ kathentānaṃ muhutteneva aruṇaṃ uggacchi.

santāvuso Rattāvasesa Dhammiyā kathāyā
commentary_english:
225. "They criticize ( *ujjhāyantī* )": "These nuns (*ayyā*) cannot even endure it themselves; how will they console the remaining people ( *sesajanaṃ* )?"—thus, speaking, they criticize.

"But venerable sir (*bhante*), how does the venerable Anuruddha attend to the deities ( *devatā manasikarotī* )?"—"Venerable sir, how does the venerable Anuruddha perceive the deities? What do those deities accept about the Teacher’s ( *satthu* ) complete *nirvāṇa* ( *parinibbānaṃ* )?"

Then, in order to show the continuation of those things, the Elder spoke, beginning with “Calm, friend (*santāvuso*)…."

That has only the meaning already stated (*vuttatthameva*).

"Remaining after the night ( *rattāvasesaṃ* )": Because he was completely extinguished (*parinibbutattā*) in the powerful pre-dawn (*balavapaccūse*), the remainder (*avasesaṃ*) of the night [was] a short time (*cullakaddhānaṃ*).

"Of the Dhamma-related talk ( *dhammiyā kathāyā* )": There is no other separate (*aññā pāṭiyekkā*) Dhamma-talk ( *dhammakathā nāma natthi* ): “Friend (*āvuso*), in this world together with the gods (*sadevake loke*), even King Death (*maccurājā*) is not ashamed of the Teacher (*satthuno*) who is an unparalleled individual (*appaṭipuggalassa*); what then need be said of the ordinary masses (*lokiyamahājanassa*)—will he be ashamed?” Thus they spent their time with talk connected to death (*maraṇapaṭisaṃyuttāya kathāya vītināmesuṃ*).

For while they were talking in that way ( *kathaṃ kathentānaṃ* ), in a moment (*muhutteneva*) the dawn ( *aruṇaṃ* ) arose ( *uggacchi* ).

Calm, friend (*santāvuso*). Remainder of the night ( *rattāvasesa* ). Of the Dhamma-related talk ( *dhammiyā kathāyā* ).

mula_pali:
226. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gacchāvuso ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocehi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando āyasmato anuruddhassa paṭissutvā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi. Tena kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre sannipatitā honti teneva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti.

Buddhasarīrapūjā
mula_english:
Then the Venerable Anuruddha spoke to the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Go now, friend Ānanda, to Kusinārā, and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘The Blessed One, Vāsiṣṭhas, has attained *parinirvāṇa*. Now is the time for you to do as you think fit.’”

“So be it, venerable sir.” And the Venerable Ānanda, having assented to the Venerable Anuruddha, prepared himself in the forenoon, and taking bowl and robe, went with a companion into Kusinārā.

Now at that time the Mallas of Kusinārā had gathered in the council hall for some public business.

Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the council hall of the Mallas of Kusinārā; on arrival he announced to the Mallas of Kusinārā: “The Blessed One, Vāsiṣṭhas, has attained *parinirvāṇa*. Now is the time for you to do as you think fit.”

And when they heard the Venerable Ānanda’s words, the Mallas, their sons, their daughters-in-law and their wives were struck with anguish and sorrow, their minds were overcome with grief so that some were tearing their hair and weeping, some were raising their arms and weeping, some were falling to the ground as if cut off at the feet, and rolling around, crying, "All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

The Buddha's bodily veneration.
commentary_pali:
226.Atha khoti aruṇuggaṃ disvāva thero theraṃ etadavoca. Teneva karaṇīyenāti kīdisena nu kho parinibbānaṭṭhāne mālāgandhādisakkārena bhavitabbaṃ, kīdisena bhikkhusaṅghassa nisajjaṭṭhānena bhavitabbaṃ, kīdisena khādanīyabhojanīyena bhavitabbanti, evaṃ yaṃ bhagavato parinibbutabhāvaṃ sutvā kattabbaṃ teneva karaṇīyena.

Buddhasarīrapūjāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
226. Then, having seen the sunrise, the elder spoke thus to the elder.

"In that very way, what kind of offering of garlands, scents, and so forth should be made at the place of complete nirvāṇa? What kind of seating arrangement should be made for the community of monks? What kind of food and edibles should be offered?" Thus, whatever should be done upon hearing of the Blessed One's having attained complete nirvāṇa, should be done in that very way.

Buddha's body-worship description.

mula_pali:
227. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – ‘‘tena hi, bhaṇe, kusinārāyaṃ gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ sannipātethā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ pañca ca dussayugasatāni ādāya yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yena bhagavato sarīraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā ekadivasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.

Atha kho kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ativikālo kho ajja bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpetuṃ, sve dāni mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā dutiyampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, tatiyampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, catutthampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, pañcamampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, chaṭṭhampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.

Atha kho sattamaṃ divasaṃ kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
227. Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara ordered their men: “Go now, gather perfumes (gandha), garlands (mālā), and all musical instruments (tāḷāvacara) in Kuśinagara!”

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara, taking perfumes, garlands, all musical instruments, and five hundred pairs of cloths, went to Upavattana, the Sala Grove of the Mallas, where the Blessed One's body was. Approaching the Blessed One’s body, they honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated it with dances (nacca), songs (gīta), instrumental music (vādita), garlands (mālā), and perfumes (gandha), setting up cloth canopies (celavitāna) and arranging circular wreaths (maṇḍalamāḷa), and spent the day.

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara had this thought: “It is too late today to cremate the Blessed One’s body; we will cremate the Blessed One’s body tomorrow.”

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara, honoring, respecting, and venerating the Blessed One's body with dances, songs, instrumental music, garlands, and perfumes, setting up cloth canopies and arranging circular wreaths, spent the second day, the third day, the fourth day, the fifth day, and the sixth day.

Then, on the seventh day, the Mallas of Kuśinagara had this thought: "We will carry the Blessed One's body with dances, songs, instrumental music, garlands, and perfumes, honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating it, to the south, around the outside of the city (nagara), and cremate the Blessed One's body south of the city."
commentary_pali:
227.Sabbañca tāḷāvacaranti sabbaṃ tūriyabhaṇḍaṃ. Sannipātethāti bheriṃ carāpetvā samāharatha. Te tatheva akaṃsu. Maṇḍalamāḷeti dussamaṇḍalamāḷe. Paṭiyādentāti sajjentā.

Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇanti nagarassa dakkhiṇadisābhāgeneva dakkhiṇadisābhāgaṃ. Bāhirena bāhiranti antonagaraṃ appavesetvā bāhireneva nagarassa bāhirapassaṃ haritvā. Dakkhiṇato nagarassāti anurādhapurassa dakkhiṇadvārasadise ṭhāne ṭhapetvā sakkārasammānaṃ katvā jetavanasadise ṭhāne jhāpessāmāti attho.

Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa Bāhirena bāhira Dakkhiṇato nagarassā
commentary_english:
227.
" *Sabbañca tāḷāvacara* " means all musical instruments.
" *Sannipātethā* " means having caused a drum to be paraded, gather together.
They did just that.
" *Maṇḍalamāḷe* " means cloth maṇḍala-s.
" *Paṭiyādentā* " means equipping.

" *Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa* " means the southern part of the city just like the southern direction part.
" *Bāhirena bāhira* " not leading into the inner city, but having removed the outer part outside the city.
" *Dakkhiṇato nagarassā* " means having placed [it] in a place similar to the southern gate of Anurādhapura, and having performed honor and respect, [we] will cremate [him] in a place similar to Jetavana, is the meaning.

*Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa bāhirena bāhira dakkhiṇato nagarassā*

mula_pali: 228. Tena kho pana samayena aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā’’ti na sakkonti uccāretuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā’ti na sakkonti uccāretu’’nti? ‘‘Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, tumhākaṃ adhippāyo, aññathā devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti? ‘‘Tumhākaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti; devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi naccehi gītehi vāditehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti. ‘‘Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, at that time, eight Malla chiefs, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, tried to lift up the Blessed One's body, thinking, "We will lift up the Blessed One’s body," but they were not able to lift it.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to the venerable Anuruddha: “What is the reason, venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause, why these eight leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, thinking, ‘We will lift up the Blessed One’s body,’ are unable to lift it?” “Vāseṭṭhas, your intention is one thing, and the deities’ intention is another.”

“Then what, venerable sir, is the deities’ intention?” “Vāseṭṭhas, your intention is: ‘We will honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Blessed One’s body with dance, song, music, garlands, and scents, carry it southward to the southern part of the city, outside the city to the south, and cremate the Blessed One’s body there.’ But the deities’ intention, Vāseṭṭhas, is: ‘We will honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Blessed One’s body with heavenly dance, song, music, and scents, carry it northward to the northern part of the city, bring it into the city through the northern gate, carry it through the middle of the city, exit through the eastern gate, and cremate the Blessed One’s body at the Mallas’ shrine called Makuṭabandhana to the east of the city.’”

“As the deities wish, venerable sir, so let it be.”
commentary_pali: 228.Aṭṭha mallapāmokkhāti majjhimavayā thāmasampannā aṭṭhamallarājāno. Sīsaṃ nhātāti sīsaṃ dhovitvā nahātā. Āyasmantaṃ anuruddhanti therova dibbacakkhukoti pākaṭo, tasmā te santesupi aññesu mahātheresu – ‘‘ayaṃ no pākaṭaṃ katvā kathessatī’’ti theraṃ pucchiṃsu. Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyoti bhante, amhākaṃ tāva adhippāyaṃ jānāma. Devatānaṃ kathaṃ adhippāyoti pucchanti. Thero paṭhamaṃ tesaṃ adhippāyaṃ dassento tumhākaṃ khotiādimāha. Makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyanti mallarājūnaṃ pasādhanamaṅgalasālāya etaṃ nāmaṃ. Cittīkataṭṭhena panesā ‘‘cetiya’’nti vuccati.
commentary_english:
228.
"aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā" means eight wrestling champions, [who were] of middle age, endowed with strength, [and were] eight malla kings.
"sīsaṃ nhātā" means having washed the head, [and] having bathed.
"āyasmantaṃ anuruddha" means the venerable Anuruddha, who was known as a *thera* with divine eyes, therefore, even with other great *theras* present, they asked the *thera*, "This one will make it known to us and will speak."
"kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo" means "But how, venerable sir, [is] the intention of the gods?" The monks said, "Venerable sir, we know our own intention."
They ask, "How is the intention of the gods?"
The *thera*, first showing their intention, said, "Your..." and so on.
"makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ" means this name [is] the auspicious hall for the adornment of the malla kings' *cetiya*.
Because of the constructed meaning, it is called "cetiya".

mula_pali: 229. Tena kho pana samayena kusinārā yāva sandhisamalasaṃkaṭīrā jaṇṇumattena odhinā mandāravapupphehi santhatā saṇṭhitā (syā.) hoti. Atha kho devatā ca kosinārakā ca mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha ca bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu.
mula_english:
229. At that time, Kusinārā, even to its rubbish heaps and cesspools ( *sandhisamalasaṃkaṭīrā* ), was covered knee-deep in coral-tree flowers ( *mandāravapupphehi santhatā* ).

Then, the deities ( *devatā* ) and the Mallas of Kusinārā, honoring, respecting, and venerating the Blessed One's ( *bhagavato* ) body ( *sarīraṃ* ) with divine and human dances ( *naccehi* ), songs ( *gītehi* ), music ( *vāditehi* ), garlands ( *mālehi* ), and scents ( *gandhehi* ), carried it to the north of the town ( *uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā* ), entered the town through the north gate ( *uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā* ), carried it through the middle of the town ( *majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā* ), and exited through the east gate ( *puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā* ) to the Mallas’ shrine called Makuṭabandhana to the east of the town ( *puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ* ), and there they laid down the Blessed One's body ( *ettha ca bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu* ).
commentary_pali:
229.Yāvasandhisamalasaṅkaṭīrāti ettha sandhi nāma gharasandhi. Samalaṃ nāma gūtharāsiniddhamanapanāḷi. Saṅkaṭīraṃ nāma saṅkāraṭṭhānaṃ. Dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehīti upari devatānaṃ naccāni honti, heṭṭhā manussānaṃ. Esa nayo gītādīsu. Apica devatānaṃ antare manussā, manussānaṃ antare devatāti evampi sakkarontā pūjentā agamaṃsu. Majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvāti evaṃ hariyamāne bhagavato sarīre bandhulamallasenāpatibhariyā mallikā nāma – ‘‘bhagavato sarīraṃ āharantī’’ti sutvā attano sāmikassa kālaṃ kiriyato paṭṭhāya aparibhuñjitvā ṭhapitaṃ visākhāya pasādhanasadisaṃ mahālatāpasādhanaṃ nīharāpetvā – ‘‘iminā satthāraṃ pūjessāmī’’ti taṃ majjāpetvā gandhodakena dhovitvā dvāre ṭhitā.

Taṃ kira pasādhanaṃ tāsañca dvinnaṃ itthīnaṃ, devadāniyacorassa geheti tīsuyeva ṭhānesu ahosi. Sā ca satthu sarīre dvāraṃ sampatte – ‘‘otāretha, tātā, satthusarīra’’nti vatvā taṃ pasādhanaṃ satthusarīre paṭimuñci. Taṃ sīsato paṭṭhāya paṭimukkaṃ yāvapādatalāgataṃ. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ sattaratanamayena mahāpasādhanena pasādhitaṃ ativiya virocittha. Taṃ sā disvā pasannacittā patthanaṃ akāsi – ‘‘bhagavā yāva vaṭṭe saṃsarissāmi, tāva me pāṭiyekkaṃ pasādhanakiccaṃ mā hotu, niccaṃ paṭimukkapasādhanasadisameva sarīraṃ hotū’’ti.

Atha bhagavantaṃ sattaratanamayena mahāpasādhanena ukkhipitvā puratthimena dvārena nīharitvā puratthimena nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ, ettha bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu.

Mahākassapattheravatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
229.
Yāva…
Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīrā: Here, *sandhi* means house-sandhi.
*Samalaṃ* means gūtharāsiniddhamanapanāḷi.
*Saṅkaṭīraṃ* means saṅkāraṭṭhānaṃ.
*Dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehī*: Above, the dances of the gods occur; below, those of humans.
This is the method in songs, and so forth (gītādīsu).
Moreover, among the gods are humans; among humans are gods; thus they honored and venerated and went.
*Majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā*: Thus, as the Blessed One's body was being carried, Bandhulamallasenāpatibhariyā, named Mallikā, having heard, "They are bringing the Blessed One's body," from the time of her husband’s death, having not enjoyed it, having had the great *latāpasādhana*, similar to Visakha’s finery, which had been kept, brought out—"With this I will honor the Teacher"—having sprinkled it, having washed it with scented water, she stood at the door.

That finery, it is said, was in three places only: in the houses of those two women and the devadāniya thief.
And when she arrived at the door of the Teacher’s body, saying, "Lower it, fathers, the Teacher’s body," she fastened that finery on the Teacher’s body.
That, from the head onward, was covered, extending to the soles of the feet.
The golden-colored body of the Blessed One, adorned with the great finery made of seven jewels, shone exceedingly.
Having seen that, with a pleased mind, she made a request: "As long as I wander in the round (vaṭṭe saṃsarissāmi), may there not be occasional finery-work for me; may my body always be just like covered-with-finery finery."

Then, having lifted up the Blessed One with the great finery made of seven jewels, having carried him out by the eastern gate, they deposited the Blessed One’s body at the Makuṭabandhana Cetiya of the Mallas in the east of the city.

Narration of the Story of Mahākassapatthera

mula_pali:
230. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante ānanda, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī’’ti? ‘‘Rañño, vāseṭṭhā, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena veṭhenti. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti . Evaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – ‘‘tena hi, bhaṇe, mallānaṃ vihataṃ kappāsaṃ sannipātethā’’ti.

Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhesuṃ, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena veṭhesuṃ. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi bhagavato sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ citakaṃ āropesuṃ.

Mahākassapattheravatthu
mula_english:
230. Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to Venerable Ānanda: “How should we treat the body of the Tathāgata, Venerable Ānanda?”

“Vāseṭṭhas, the body of the Tathāgata should be treated in the same way as the body of a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin).”

“But how, Venerable Ānanda, is the body of a wheel-turning monarch treated?”

“Vāseṭṭhas, the body of a wheel-turning monarch is wrapped in new linen. Having wrapped it in new linen, they wrap it in teased cotton wool. Having wrapped it in teased cotton wool, they wrap it in new linen. In this way, they wrap the body of the wheel-turning monarch in five hundred layers of linen and cotton. Then they place it in an iron oil-vat, which is enclosed in another iron vat. They build a pyre of all kinds of perfumes and cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. They build a stupa (thūpaṃ karonti) for the wheel-turning monarch at a crossroads (cātumahāpathe). This is how, Vāseṭṭhas, the body of a wheel-turning monarch is treated. Vāseṭṭhas, the body of the Tathāgata should be treated in the same way. A stupa should be erected at the crossroads for the Tathāgata. And those who offer garlands, scents, or perfume powders there, or bow down there, or gladden their minds there: that will be for their long-term welfare and happiness.”

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā ordered their men: “In that case, gather the Mallas’ teased cotton wool!”

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā wrapped the Blessed One’s body in new linen and then in teased cotton wool. Having wrapped it in teased cotton wool, they wrapped it in new linen. In this way, having wrapped the Blessed One’s body in five hundred layers, they placed it in an iron oil-vat, covered it with another iron vat, made a pyre of all kinds of perfumes, and placed the Blessed One’s body on the pyre.

The Story of the Elder Mahākassapa

mula_pali: 231. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro ājīvako kusinārāya mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti. Addasā kho āyasmā mahākassapo taṃ ājīvakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvā taṃ ājīvakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘apāvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī’’ti? ‘‘Āmāvuso, jānāmi, ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo. Tato me idaṃ mandāravapupphaṃ gahita’’nti. Tattha ye te bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’’ti.
mula_english:
At that time the Venerable Mahākassapa was journeying from Pāvā to Kusinārā along the road, together with a large community of monks, about five hundred monks.

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, leaving the road, sat down at the foot of a certain tree.

At that time a certain Ājīvaka ascetic, carrying a coral-tree flower (mandārava-puṣpa) from Kusinārā, was traveling on the road to Pāvā.

The Venerable Mahākassapa saw that Ājīvaka coming from afar, and having seen him, said to him: “Friend, do you know our teacher (śāstāraṃ)?”

“Yes, friend, I know. The renunciate (śramaṇa) Gotama has been completely passed away (parinirvṛta) for seven days now. That is why I picked this coral-tree flower.”

Thereupon, those monks there who were not free from craving (avītarāgā), some raised their arms and wept, they fell down as if their feet were cut off, rolled around, and writhed, crying: "Too soon has the Blessed One (bhagavān) attained complete extinction (parinirvṛta), too soon has the Well-Gone One (sugato) attained complete extinction, too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

But those monks who were free from craving (vītarāgā), mindful and fully aware, endured, reflecting: "Impermanent (anitya) are conditioned things (saṃskārā); how could it be otherwise?"
commentary_pali:
231.Pāvāyakusināranti pāvānagare piṇḍāya caritvā ‘‘kusināraṃ gamissāmī’’ti addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti. Rukkhamūle nisīdīti ettha kasmā divāvihāranti na vuttaṃ? Divāvihāratthāya anisinnattā. Therassa hi parivārā bhikkhū sabbe sukhasaṃvaddhitā mahāpuññā. Te majjhanhikasamaye tattapāsāṇasadisāya bhūmiyā padasā gacchantā kilamiṃsu. Thero te disvā – ‘‘bhikkhū kilamanti, gantabbaṭṭhānañca na dūraṃ, thokaṃ vissamitvā darathaṃ paṭippassambhetvā sāyanhasamaye kusināraṃ gantvā dasabalaṃ passissāmī’’ti maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā udakatumbato udakena hatthapāde sītale katvā nisīdi. Parivārabhikkhūpissa rukkhamūle nisīditvā yoniso manasikāre kammaṃ kurumānā tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānā nisīdiṃsu. Iti darathavinodanatthāya nisinnattā ‘‘divāvihāra’’nti na vuttaṃ.

Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvāti mahāpātippamāṇaṃ pupphaṃ āgantukadaṇḍake ṭhapetvā chattaṃ viya gahetvā. Addasa khoti āgacchantaṃ dūrato addasa. Disvā ca pana cintesi –

Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā Addasa kho

‘‘Etaṃ ājīvakassa hatthe mandāravapupphaṃ paññāyati, etañca na sabbadā manussapathe paññāyati, yadā pana koci iddhimā iddhiṃ vikubbati, tadā sabbaññubodhisattassa ca mātukucchiokkamanādīsu hoti. Na kho pana ajja kenaci iddhivikubbanaṃ kataṃ, na me satthā mātukucchiṃ okkanto, na kucchito nikkhamanto, nāpissa ajja abhisambodhi, na dhammacakkappavattanaṃ, na yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ, na devorohaṇaṃ, na āyusaṅkhārossajjanaṃ. Mahallako pana me satthā dhuvaṃ parinibbuto bhavissatī’’ti.

Tato – ‘‘pucchāmi na’’nti cittaṃ uppādetvā – ‘‘sace kho pana nisinnakova pucchāmi, satthari agāravo kato bhavissatī’’ti uṭṭhahitvā ṭhitaṭṭhānato apakkamma chaddanto nāgarājā maṇicammaṃ viya dasabaladattiyaṃ meghavaṇṇaṃ paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ pārupitvā dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā satthari katena gāravena ājīvakassa abhimukho hutvā – ‘‘āvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī’’ti āha. Kiṃ pana satthu parinibbānaṃ jānanto pucchi ajānantoti? Āvajjanapaṭibaddhaṃ khīṇāsavānaṃ jānanaṃ, anāvajjitattā panesa ajānanto pucchīti eke. Thero samāpattibahulo, rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānaleṇamaṇḍapādīsu niccaṃ samāpattibaleneva yāpeti, kulasantakampi gāmaṃ pavisitvā dvāre samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā samāpattito vuṭṭhitova bhikkhaṃ gaṇhāti. Thero kira iminā pacchimena attabhāvena mahājanānuggahaṃ karissāmi – ‘‘ye mayhaṃ bhikkhaṃ vā denti gandhamālādīhi vā sakkāraṃ karonti, tesaṃ taṃ mahapphalaṃ hotū’’ti evaṃ karoti. Tasmā samāpattibahulatāya na jānāti. Iti ajānantova pucchatīti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ.

Na hettha ajānanakāraṇaṃ atthi. Abhilakkhitaṃ satthu parinibbānaṃ ahosi, dasasahassilokadhātukampanādīhi nimittehi. Therassa pana parisāya kehici bhikkhūhi bhagavā diṭṭhapubbo, kehici na diṭṭhapubbo, tattha yehipi diṭṭhapubbo, tepi passitukāmāva, yehipi adiṭṭhapubbo, tepi passitukāmāva. Tattha yehi na diṭṭhapubbo, te atidassanakāmatāya gantvā ‘‘kuhiṃ bhagavā’’ti pucchantā ‘‘parinibbuto’’ti sutvā sandhāretuṃ nāsakkhissanti. Cīvarañca pattañca chaḍḍetvā ekavatthā vā dunnivatthā vā duppārutā vā urāni paṭipisantā parodissanti. Tattha manussā – ‘‘mahākassapattherena saddhiṃ āgatā paṃsukūlikā sayampi itthiyo viya parodanti, te kiṃ amhe samassāsessantī’’ti mayhaṃ dosaṃ dassanti. Idaṃ pana suññaṃ mahāaraññaṃ, idha yathā tathā rodantesu doso natthi. Purimataraṃ sutvā nāma sokopi tanuko hotīti bhikkhūnaṃ satuppādanatthāya jānantova pucchi.

Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamoti ajja samaṇo gotamo sattāhaparinibbuto. Tato me idanti tato samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbutaṭṭhānato.

Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo Tato me ida
commentary_english:
231. *Pāvāya* *Kusināra*: Having wandered for alms in Pāvā city, he was one who had set out on the road to Kusināra, thinking, "I will go to Kusināra."

*Rukkhamūle nisīdī*: Here, why was it not said "rest by day"? Because he did not sit down for the purpose of resting by day.

The monks who were the retinue of that elder were all nurtured in comfort and were of great merit.

They, going on foot at midday on ground similar to a heated stone, grew weary.

The elder, seeing them, [thought:] "The monks are weary, and the place to go is not far away; having rested a little, having calmed their distress, having gone to Kusināra in the evening, I will see the Ten-Powered One," he left the road at a certain tree root, spread out his Saṃghāṭī robe, and sat down, having made his hands and feet cool with water from a water pot.

The monks of his retinue also, having sat down at the root of the tree, sat down speaking the virtues of the Triple Gem, making the work [that consists in] appropriate attention.

Thus, because he sat down for the sake of allaying distress, it was not said "rest by day."

*Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā*: Taking a Mandārava flower, placing a flower of the size of a large bowl on a staff for new arrivals, taking it like an umbrella.

*Addasa kho*: He saw him coming from afar.

And having seen [him], he thought:

*Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā* *addasa kho*

"This Mandārava flower appears in the hand of an Ājīvaka; and this does not appear at all times on the path of men; when some powerful one works a miracle, then it is in the events beginning with the entry into the mother's womb of the All-Knowing Bodhisattva.

But today a miracle has not been worked by anyone, my teacher has not entered a mother's womb, nor is he emerging from [it], nor is today his complete awakening, nor the turning of the wheel of the Dharma, nor the twin miracle, nor the descent from the gods, nor the casting off of the life force.

My teacher is old; surely he will be completely extinguished."

Then – producing the thought "Shall I ask or not?" – [he thought:] "If, indeed, I ask while sitting, disrespect to the Teacher will have been done," having risen up, having gone away from the place where he was standing, Chaddanta the Nāga-king, covering himself with a patched-together robe the color of a cloud, like a jeweled skin, having placed his Anjali gesture, radiant with the joining of his ten fingernails, upon his head, having become face to face with the Ājīvaka with reverence done to the Teacher, he said, "Friend, do you know our Teacher?"

What? Knowing the complete extinction of the Teacher, did he ask, or not knowing? The knowing of those whose outflows are ended is bound to reflection; but because he did not reflect, he asked not knowing, some say.

The Elder is one who frequents meditative attainments; constantly he spends [his time] in places for night, places for day, cave shelters, pavilions, etc., only by the force of meditative attainment; having entered even a village that belongs to a family, having achieved meditative attainment at the door, having risen from meditative attainment, he takes alms.

The Elder, it seems, by this final existence of his, [thinks] "I will do a favor to the great multitude of people: 'May that be of great fruit to those who give me alms or do honor with incense, garlands, etc.,'" thus he acts.

Therefore, he does not know due to his abundance of meditative attainments.

Thus, they say, "He asks not knowing"; that is not to be accepted.

There is no cause for not knowing here.

The Teacher's complete extinction was marked, by signs such as the shaking of the ten-thousand world-spheres, etc.

In that Elder's assembly, the Blessed One had been seen previously by some monks, but not seen previously by others; among them, even those by whom he had been seen previously were desirous of seeing [him], and even those by whom he had not been seen previously were desirous of seeing [him].

Among them, those by whom he had not been seen previously, going in their extreme desire to see, asking "Where is the Blessed One?", hearing "He is completely extinguished," will not be able to bear it.

Having cast aside their robes and their bowls, wearing a single garment or badly clothed or poorly covered, striking their breasts, they will wail.

There, people [will say:] "These rag-robe wearers who have come together with the Elder Mahākassapa, even they themselves wail like women; how will they console us?" They will show fault in me.

But this is an empty great forest; here, even if they weep in any way, there is no fault.

Having heard beforehand, grief also becomes thin, he asked knowing, indeed, for the sake of the monks' production of mindfulness.

*Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo*: Today, the ascetic Gotama is one who has been completely extinguished for a week.

*Tato me idaṃ*: From that, from the place of complete extinction of the ascetic Gotama.

*Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo* *tato me idaṃ*

mula_pali: 232. Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma vuddhapabbajito tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho subhaddo vuddhapabbajito te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha, sumuttā mayaṃ tena mahāsamaṇena. Upaddutā ca homa – ‘idaṃ vo kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Idāni pana mayaṃ yaṃ icchissāma, taṃ karissāma, yaṃ na icchissāma, na taṃ karissāmā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ , āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.
mula_english:
232. Now at that time, one Subhadda, who had renounced only in his old age, was seated in the assembly.

Then Subhadda, who had gone forth when old, said to those monks: “Enough, friends! Do not grieve, do not lament! We are well rid of that great ascetic (mahāsamaṇa). We were always bothered by his saying: “It is fitting for you to do this, it is not fitting for you to do that!” But now we will be able to do as we like and we won’t do what we don’t like."

Then the Venerable Mahākāśyapa addressed the monks, saying: “Enough friends! Do not grieve, do not lament! For has not the Blessed One declared that with all that is dear and beloved there must be change (nānābhāva), separation (vinābhāva), and severance (aññathābhāva)? So why all this, friends? Whatever is born (jātaṃ), become (bhūtaṃ), compounded (saṅkhataṃ) is subject to decay (palokadhammaṃ), it cannot be that even the body (śarīraṃ) of the *Tathāgata* does not decay.’; There can be no such state of things."
commentary_pali:
232.Subhaddo nāma vuḍḍhapabbajitoti ‘‘subhaddo’’ti tassa nāmaṃ. Vuḍḍhakāle pana pabbajitattā ‘‘vuḍḍhapabbajito’’ti vuccati. Kasmā pana so evamāha? Bhagavati āghātena. Ayaṃ kireso khandhake āgate ātumāvatthusmiṃ nahāpitapubbako vuḍḍhapabbajito bhagavati kusinārato nikkhamitvā aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ ātumaṃ āgacchante bhagavā āgacchatīti sutvā – ‘‘āgatakāle yāgupānaṃ karissāmī’’ti sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhite dve putte etadavoca – ‘‘bhagavā kira, tātā, ātumaṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi; gacchatha tumhe, tātā, khurabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya nāḷiyāvāpakena anugharakaṃ anugharakaṃ āhiṇḍatha loṇampi telampi taṇḍulampi khādanīyampi saṃharatha bhagavato āgatassa yāgupānaṃ karissāmā’’ti (mahāva. 303). Te tathā akaṃsu.

Manussā te dārake mañjuke paṭibhāneyyake disvā kāretukāmāpi akāretukāmāpi kārentiyeva. Katakāle – ‘‘kiṃ gaṇhissatha tātā’’ti pucchanti. Te vadanti – ‘‘na amhākaṃ aññena kenaci attho, pitā pana no bhagavato, āgatakāle yāgudānaṃ dātukāmo’’ti. Taṃ sutvā manussā aparigaṇetvāva yaṃ te sakkonti āharituṃ, sabbaṃ denti. Yampi na sakkonti, manussehi pesenti. Atha bhagavati ātumaṃ āgantvā bhusāgāraṃ paviṭṭhe subhaddo sāyanhasamayaṃ gāmadvāraṃ gantvā manusse āmantesi – ‘‘upāsakā, nāhaṃ tumhākaṃ santikā aññaṃ kiñci paccāsīsāmi, mayhaṃ dārakehi ābhatāni taṇḍulādīniyeva saṅghassa pahonti. Yaṃ hatthakammaṃ, taṃ me dethā’’ti. ‘‘Idañcidañca gaṇhathā’’ti sabbūpakaraṇāni gāhetvā vihāre uddhanāni kāretvā ekaṃ kāḷakaṃ kāsāvaṃ nivāsetvā tādisameva pārupitvā – ‘‘idaṃ karotha, idaṃ karothā’’ti sabbarattiṃ vicārento satasahassaṃ vissajjetvā bhojjayāguñca madhugoḷakañca paṭiyādāpesi. Bhojjayāgu nāma bhuñjitvā pātabbayāgu, tattha sappimadhuphāṇitamacchamaṃsapupphaphalarasādi yaṃ kiñci khādanīyaṃ nāma sabbaṃ pakkhipati kīḷitukāmānaṃ sīsamakkhanayoggā hoti sugandhagandhā.

Atha bhagavā kālasseva sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto piṇḍāya carituṃ ātumanagarābhimukho pāyāsi. Manussā tassa ārocesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā piṇḍāya gāmaṃ pavisati, tayā kassa yāgu paṭiyāditā’’ti. So yathānivatthapāruteheva tehi kāḷakakāsāvehi ekena hatthena dabbiñca kaṭacchuñca gahetvā brahmā viya dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhapetvā vanditvā – ‘‘paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā yāgu’’nti āha.

Tato ‘‘jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchantī’’ti khandhake āgatanayena bhagavā pucchitvā ca sutvā ca taṃ vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ vigarahitvā tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ akappiyasamādānasikkhāpadañca, khurabhaṇḍapariharaṇasikkhāpadañcāti dve sikkhāpadāni paññapetvā – ‘‘bhikkhave, anekakappakoṭiyo bhojanaṃ pariyesanteheva vītināmitā, idaṃ pana tumhākaṃ akappiyaṃ adhammena uppannaṃ bhojanaṃ, imaṃ paribhuttānaṃ anekāni attabhāvasahassāni apāyesveva nibbattissanti, apetha mā gaṇhathā’’ti bhikkhācārābhimukho agamāsi. Ekabhikkhunāpi na kiñci gahitaṃ.

Subhaddo anattamano hutvā ayaṃ ‘‘sabbaṃ jānāmī’’ti āhiṇḍati. Sace na gahitukāmo, pesetvā ārocetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ pakkāhāro nāma sabbaciraṃ tiṭṭhanto sattāhamattaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Idañhi mama yāvajīvaṃ pariyattaṃ assa. Sabbaṃ tena nāsitaṃ, ahitakāmo ayaṃ mayhanti bhagavati āghātaṃ bandhitvā dasabale dharante kiñci vattuṃ nāsakkhi. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ uccā kulā pabbajito mahāpuriso, sace kiñci vakkhāmi, maṃyeva santajjessatī’’ti. Svāyaṃ ajja ‘‘parinibbuto bhagavā’’ti sutvā laddhassāso viya haṭṭhatuṭṭho evamāha.

Thero taṃ sutvā hadaye pahāradānaṃ viya matthake patitasukkhāsani viya maññi, dhammasaṃvego cassa uppajji – ‘‘sattāhamattaparinibbuto bhagavā, ajjāpissa suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sarīraṃ dharatiyeva, dukkhena bhagavatā ārādhitasāsane nāma evaṃ lahu mahantaṃ pāpakasaṭaṃ kaṇṭako uppanno, alaṃ kho panesa pāpo vaḍḍhamāno aññepi evarūpe sahāye labhitvā sakkā sāsanaṃ osakkāpetu’’nti. Tato thero cintesi –

‘‘Sace kho panāhaṃ imaṃ mahallakaṃ idheva pilotikaṃ nivāsāpetvā chārikāya okirāpetvā nīharāpessāmi, manussā ‘samaṇassa gotamassa sarīre dharamāneyeva sāvakā vivadantī’ti amhākaṃ dosaṃ dassessanti adhivāsemi tāva.

Bhagavatā hi desito dhammo asaṅgahitapuppharāsisadiso. Tattha yathā vātena pahaṭapupphāni yato vā tato vā gacchanti, evameva evarūpānaṃ pāpapuggalānaṃ vasena gacchante gacchante kāle vinaye ekaṃ dve sikkhāpadāni nassissanti, sutte eko dve pañhāvārā nassissanti, abhidhamme ekaṃ dve bhūmantarāni nassissanti, evaṃ anukkamena mūle naṭṭhe pisācasadisā bhavissāma; tasmā dhammavinayasaṅgahaṃ karissāma. Evañhi sati daḷhaṃ suttena saṅgahitāni pupphāni viya ayaṃ dhammavinayo niccalo bhavissati.

Etadatthañhi bhagavā mayhaṃ tīṇi gāvutāni paccuggamanaṃ akāsi, tīhi ovādehi upasampadaṃ adāsi, kāyato apanetvā kāye cīvaraparivattanaṃ akāsi, ākāse pāṇiṃ cāletvā candūpamaṃ paṭipadaṃ kathento maṃ kāyasakkhiṃ katvā kathesi, tikkhattuṃ sakalasāsanadāyajjaṃ paṭicchāpesi. Mādise bhikkhumhi tiṭṭhamāne ayaṃ pāpo sāsane vuḍḍhiṃ mā alattha. Yāva adhammo na dippati, dhammo na paṭibāhiyati. Avinayo na dippati vinayo na paṭibāhiyati. Adhammavādino na balavanto honti, dhammavādino na dubbalā honti; avinayavādino na balavanto honti, vinayavādino na dubbalā honti. Tāva dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmi. Tato bhikkhū attano attano pahonakaṃ gahetvā kappiyākappiyaṃ kathessanti. Athāyaṃ pāpo sayameva niggahaṃ pāpuṇissati, puna sīsaṃ ukkhipituṃ na sakkhissati, sāsanaṃ iddhañceva phītañca bhavissatī’’ti.
