So evaṃ nāma mayhaṃ cittaṃ uppannanti kassaci anārocetvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ samassāsesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo…pe… netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.
commentary_english:
232 Subhadda by name, an old renunciate, thus: “Subhadda” is his name.

In old age, however, because of having renounced, he is called “old renunciate.”

But why did he say that? Out of contempt for the Blessed One.

It seems that this same Subhadda, when the Khandhaka had come, having gone forth from Kusināra to Ātumā, an old renunciate who formerly was a barber in Ātumā, when the Blessed One was coming to Ātumā together with thirteen hundred monks, having heard, “The Blessed One is coming,” said this to his two sons who were abiding in the state of a novice: “The Blessed One, fathers, is coming to Ātumā together with a great Saṃgha of monks, thirteen hundred monks; go, fathers, taking a razor and a bag with a barber’s implement, wander from house to house collecting salt, oil, rice, and food.” Having gathered it together, “We will prepare rice-gruel and a drink for the Blessed One who has come” (Mahāva.
303).

They did just that.

People, having seen those boys who were charming and clever, being desirous of having [their hair] cut, even when not desiring to have it cut, would have it cut.

At the time of the cutting, they would ask, “What will you take, fathers?”

They would say, “We have no need for anything else, but our father wishes to give rice-gruel as a gift to the Blessed One when he has come.”

Having heard that, people, without reckoning it, whatever they were able to bring, they would give everything.

Whatever they were not able to [bring themselves], they would send by means of people.

Then, when the Blessed One, having come to Ātumā, had entered the storehouse, Subhadda, at the time of the evening, going to the village gate, addressed the people: “Lay followers, I do not expect anything else from your presence, but only the rice and so forth that has been brought by my boys is sufficient for the Saṃgha.

Whatever is manual labor, give that to me.”

“Take this and take that,” having caused all the equipment to be taken, having had the rice removed in the monastery, having dressed in a single blackish-brown robe and having wrapped another just like it, thinking, “Do this, do that,” the whole night, having spent a hundred thousand, he had both edible rice-gruel and honey-cakes prepared.

Edible rice-gruel is called rice-gruel to be drunk after having eaten, in which all edible things such as ghee, honey, molasses, fish, meat, flowers, fruit juice, and so forth are put, and it is suitable for anointing the head of those who desire to play, [and] it is fragrant.

Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, having taken care of his body, surrounded by the Saṃgha of monks, set out towards the city of Ātumā for alms.

People announced to him, “The Blessed One is entering the village for alms; by whom has rice-gruel been prepared?”

He, just as if having dressed in those blackish-brown robes which had already been worn, taking both a ladle and a spoon in one hand, like Brahmā, establishing his right knee on the ground, having bowed down, said, “May the Blessed One accept the rice-gruel from me, O Bhante!”

Then, “Even though knowing, the Tathāgatas ask,” according to the manner come [down] in the Khandhaka, the Blessed One, both having asked and having heard, censuring that old renunciate, in that matter, having made known two precepts: the precept of unallowable acceptance and the precept of not using a razor and bag, “Monks, even though seeking food for countless aeons, it has been rejected, but this food of yours is unallowable, arisen through unrighteousness; for those who have eaten this, many thousands of existences will arise only in the apāyas, go away, do not take [it]!” he went towards the alms round.

Nothing was taken by even one monk.

Subhadda, having become displeased, [thought], “This one wanders about [saying], ‘I know everything.’”

If [one] does not desire to take [it], [one] should send [it back] and announce [it].

This cooked food, indeed, while abiding for a very long time, may abide for only seven days.

This, indeed, would be enough for my whole life.

Everything was destroyed by him; this one is desirous of harm to me,” having bound contempt towards the Blessed One, while the Ten-Powered One was enduring, he was not able to say anything.

Thus it seemed to him: “This one has gone forth from a high family, a great man; if I say anything, he himself will rebuke me.”

Today, having heard, “The Blessed One has attained nirvāṇa,” delighted and pleased, he said thus.

The elder, having heard that, thought, “It is like giving a blow to [my] heart, like a thunderbolt fallen on [my] head,” and agitation about the Dhamma arose in him: “The Blessed One has attained nirvāṇa only seven days [ago], even today his body of golden color endures, in a sāsana brought about with difficulty by the Blessed One, a thorn, a great heap of evil, has arisen so quickly, it is enough, indeed, that this evil one, while growing, having obtained other companions of this sort, is able to cause the sāsana to decline.”

Then the elder thought:

“If, indeed, I, having had this old man settled right here in a dilapidated [dwelling], having had ashes scattered [on him], were to cause [him] to be removed, people will show blame to us, ‘Even while the body of the samaṇa Gotama endures, the disciples are quarreling,’ therefore I will endure for a while.”
[Thus,] the Dharma is taught by the Blessed One, it is like a heap of flowers not held together.

Just as flowers scattered by the wind go here and there, in the same way, because of such evil individuals, as time goes on, one or two precepts (*śikṣāpada*) will be lost from the monastic discipline (*vinaya*), one or two question series (*pañhāvāra*) will be lost from the sūtras, one or two levels of existence (*bhūmantara*) will be lost from the *Abhidhamma*. Thus, gradually, when the root is destroyed, we will become like demons. Therefore, let us make a compilation of the Dharma and the Discipline (*dharma-vinaya-saṅgaha*).

Thus, when that is the case, this *dharma-vinaya*, like flowers held together firmly by a thread (*sūtra*), will be unshakeable.

The Blessed One did these things for me: He came out three *gāvutas* to meet me, he gave me ordination (*upasampada*) with three instructions (*ovāda*), having removed [the robe] from his own body, he made a robe exchange with my body, having moved his hand in the sky, while relating the simile of the moon, having made me a bodily witness (*kāyasakkhi*), he spoke; three times he had me accept the entire inheritance of the teaching (*sakalasāsanadāyajja*).

While a monk like me is standing, may this evil not attain growth in the teaching (*śāsana*).

As long as what is not *dharma* does not shine forth, *dharma* is not rejected.

What is not discipline (*avinaya*) does not shine forth, discipline (*vinaya*) is not rejected.

Those who speak what is not *dharma* are not strong, those who speak *dharma* are not weak; those who speak what is not discipline (*avinaya*) are not strong, those who speak discipline (*vinaya*) are not weak.

So long will I recite the Dharma and the Discipline (*dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmi*).

Then the monks, having taken what was enough for themselves, will speak of what is allowable (*kappiya*) and what is not allowable (*akappiya*).

Then this evil one will himself attain restraint (*niggaha*), he will not be able to lift his head again, and the teaching (*śāsana*) will be prosperous (*iddha*) and thriving (*phīta*)".

So, without announcing to anyone that such a thought had arisen in my mind, he encouraged the monastic community (*bhikkhusaṅgha*).

Therefore it was said, "Then the venerable Mahākassapa…pe… this is not a valid reason (*ṭhānaṃ vijjatī*)".

mula_pali: 233. Tena kho pana samayena cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā’’ti na sakkonti āḷimpetuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā’ti na sakkonti āḷimpetu’’nti? ‘‘Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti? ‘‘Devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘ayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Na tāva bhagavato citako pajjalissati, yāvāyasmā mahākassapo bhagavato pāde sirasā na vandissatī’’’ti. ‘‘Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū’’ti.
mula_english:
At that time, four leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, tried to ignite the Blessed One's pyre, thinking, "We will ignite the Blessed One's pyre," but they were unable to ignite it.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to the Venerable Anuruddha: "What is the reason, Venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause that these four leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, try to ignite the Blessed One's pyre, thinking, 'We will ignite the Blessed One's pyre,' but are unable to ignite it?"

"The intention of the deities (*devatā*), Vāseṭṭhas, is otherwise."

"How is the intention of the deities, venerable sir?"

"The intention of the deities, Vāseṭṭhas, is this: 'The Venerable Mahākāśyapa (*mahākassapo*) is traveling along the road from Pāvā to Kusinārā with a large *saṅgha* of approximately five hundred monks. The Blessed One's pyre will not be lit until the Venerable Mahākāśyapa (*mahākassapo*) has paid homage at the feet of the Blessed One with his head.'"

"As the deities (*devatā*) wish, venerable sir, so be it!"
commentary_pali:
233.Citakanti vīsaratanasatikaṃ candanacitakaṃ. Āḷimpessāmāti aggiṃ gāhāpessāma. Na sakkonti āḷimpetunti aṭṭhapi soḷasapi dvattiṃsapi janā jālanatthāya yamakayamakaukkāyo gahetvā tālavaṇṭehi bījantā bhastāhi dhamantā tāni tāni kāraṇāni karontāpi na sakkontiyeva aggiṃ gāhāpetuṃ. Devatānaṃ adhippāyoti ettha tā kira devatā therassa upaṭṭhākadevatāva. Asītimahāsāvakesu hi cittāni pasādetvā tesaṃ upaṭṭhākāni asītikulasahassāni sagge nibbattāni. Tattha there cittaṃ pasādetvā sagge nibbattā devatā tasmiṃ samāgame theraṃ adisvā – ‘‘kuhiṃ nu kho amhākaṃ kulūpakatthero’’ti antarāmagge paṭipannaṃ disvā ‘‘amhākaṃ kulūpakattherena avandite citako mā pajjalitthā’’ti adhiṭṭhahiṃsu.

Manussā taṃ sutvā – ‘‘mahākassapo kira nāma bho bhikkhu pañcahi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ ‘dasabalassa pāde vandissāmī’ti āgacchati. Tasmiṃ kira anāgate citako na pajjalissati. Kīdiso bho so bhikkhu kāḷo odāto dīgho rasso, evarūpe nāma bho bhikkhumhi ṭhite kiṃ dasabalassa parinibbānaṃ nāmā’’ti keci gandhamālādihatthā paṭipathaṃ gacchiṃsu. Keci vīthiyo vicittā katvā āgamanamaggaṃ olokayamānā aṭṭhaṃsu.
commentary_english:
233. *Citaka* means a sandalwood pyre worth twenty *vīsaratanas*.

*Āḷimpessāmā* means we will set fire to it.

*Na sakkonti āḷimpetu* means even eighty, sixteen, or thirty-two people, taking tongs for kindling the fire, fanning with palm leaves, blowing with bellows, and doing various things, are not able to kindle the fire.

*Devatānaṃ adhippāyo*: Here, those deities were the attending deities of the Elder.

Having pleased their minds towards eighty great disciples, eighty thousand families who were their attendants were reborn in heaven.

There, the deities, having been reborn in heaven after pleasing their minds towards the Elder, not seeing the Elder in that gathering, [thought,] "Where is our family-supporting Elder?" Seeing him entering the road in between, they resolved, "May the pyre not be kindled until our family-supporting Elder has paid homage."

Humans, having heard that, "It is said that a monk named Mahākassapa is coming with five hundred monks, [thinking,] 'I will worship the feet of the One with Ten Powers.'

It is said that the pyre will not be kindled until he arrives.

What kind of monk is he? Is he black, white, tall, short? What is the parinirvāṇa of the One with Ten Powers when such a monk is present?" Some, with garlands and perfumes in their hands, went to meet him on the road.

Some, having decorated the streets, stood looking at the road of arrival.

mula_pali: 234. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena kusinārā makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ, yena bhagavato citako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandi. Tānipi kho pañcabhikkhusatāni ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandiṃsu. Vandite ca panāyasmatā mahākassapena tehi ca pañcahi bhikkhusatehi sayameva bhagavato citako pajjali.
mula_english:
234. Then, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa went to the Blessed One's pyre, at the Mallas' shrine called Makuṭabandhana in Kuśinārā. Approaching it, he arranged his robe over one shoulder, placed his hands palm-to-palm in reverence, circumambulated the pyre three times, and bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet (bhagavato pāde śirasā vandi).

And the five hundred monks, too, arranging their robes over one shoulder, placing their hands palm-to-palm in reverence, circumambulated the pyre three times, and bowed their heads at the Blessed One's feet (bhagavato pāde śirasā vandiṃsu).

And when homage had been paid by the Venerable Mahākāśyapa and the five hundred monks, the Blessed One's pyre burst into flame spontaneously.
commentary_pali:
234.Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena kusinārā…pe… sirasā vandīti thero kira citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā āvajjantova sallakkhesi – ‘‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne sīsaṃ, imasmiṃ ṭhāne pādā’’ti. Tato pādānaṃ samīpe ṭhatvā abhiññāpādakaṃ catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya – ‘‘arāsahassapaṭimaṇḍitacakkalakkhaṇapatiṭṭhitā dasabalassa pādā saddhiṃ kappāsapaṭalehi pañca dussayugasatāni suvaṇṇadoṇiṃ candanacitakañca dvedhā katvā mayhaṃ uttamaṅge sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhahantū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi. Saha adhiṭṭhānacittena tāni pañca dussayugasatāni dvedhā katvā valāhakantarā puṇṇacando viya pādā nikkhamiṃsu. Thero vikasitarattapadumasadise hatthe pasāretvā suvaṇṇavaṇṇe satthupāde yāva gopphakā daḷhaṃ gahetvā attano siravare patiṭṭhapesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘bhagavato pāde sirasā vandī’’ti.

Mahājano taṃ acchariyaṃ disvā ekappahāreneva mahānādaṃ nadi, gandhamālādīhi pūjetvā yathāruci vandi. Evaṃ pana therena ca mahājanena ca tehi ca pañcahi bhikkhusatehi vanditamatte puna adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthi. Pakatiadhiṭṭhānavaseneva therassa hatthato muccitvā alattakavaṇṇāni bhagavato pādatalāni candanadāruādīsu kiñci acāletvāva yathāṭhāne patiṭṭhahiṃsu, yathāṭhāne ṭhitāneva ahesuṃ. Bhagavato hi pādesu nikkhamantesu vā pavisantesu vā kappāsaaṃsu vā dasikatantaṃ vā telabindu vā dārukkhandhaṃ vā ṭhānā calitaṃ nāma nāhosi. Sabbaṃ yathāṭhāne ṭhitameva ahosi. Uṭṭhahitvā pana atthaṅgate cande viya sūriye viya ca tathāgatassa pādesu antarahitesu mahājano mahākanditaṃ kandi. Parinibbānakālato adhikataraṃ kāruññaṃ ahosi.

Sayamevabhagavato citako pajjalīti idaṃ pana kassaci pajjalāpetuṃ vāyamantassa adassanavasena vuttaṃ. Devatānubhāvena panesa samantato ekappahāreneva pajjali.

Sayameva bhagavato citako pajjalī
commentary_english:
Thereupon, the venerable Mahākāśyapa went to Kuśinārā…pe… bowed with his head [at the Buddha's feet]. The elder, after circumambulating the pyre, contemplated, "In this place is the head, in this place are the feet."

Then, standing near the feet, having attained the fourth *jhāna* that is the basis for higher knowledge, and having arisen from it, he made a resolution: "May the feet of the Ten-Powered One, adorned with a thousand-spoked wheel mark, together with cotton cloths and five hundred pairs of garments, split the golden trough and the sandalwood pyre in two and be established on my head!"

With the mind of resolution, those five hundred pairs of garments, split in two, the feet emerged like the full moon from behind the clouds.

The elder, extending his hands similar to a blossomed red lotus, having firmly grasped the Teacher's feet, golden in color, up to the ankles, placed them on his excellent head.

Therefore it was said, "He bowed with his head at the feet of the Blessed One (Bhagavat)."

The great crowd, seeing that wonder, cried out with a great noise in one voice, and worshiped with garlands and perfumes, and bowed as they pleased.

Thus, when the elder and the great crowd and those five hundred monks had bowed, there was no further need for a resolution.

By the power of the natural resolution itself, having been released from the elder's hands, the Blessed One's (Bhagavat) soles, the color of lac, were established in their proper place without moving anything at all on the sandalwood and wooden pyre, and they remained in their proper place.

Indeed, whether the Blessed One's (Bhagavat) feet were going out or entering, neither cotton threads, nor woven threads, nor a drop of oil, nor a piece of wood, moved from their place.

Everything remained just as it was.

Having arisen, when the Tathāgata's feet were hidden, like the moon or the sun at sunset, the great crowd wept with a great lamentation.

The compassion was greater than at the time of complete nirvāṇa.

The pyre of the Blessed One (Bhagavat) ignited spontaneously—this was said because someone trying to ignite it could not be seen.

By the power of the deities, it blazed up on all sides with a single burst.

The pyre of the Blessed One (Bhagavat) ignited spontaneously.

mula_pali:
235. Jhāyamānassa kho pana bhagavato sarīrassa yaṃ ahosi chavīti vā cammanti vā maṃsanti vā nhārūti vā lasikāti vā, tassa neva chārikā paññāyittha, na masi; sarīrāneva avasissiṃsu. Seyyathāpi nāma sappissa vā telassa vā jhāyamānassa neva chārikā paññāyati, na masi; evameva bhagavato sarīrassa jhāyamānassa yaṃ ahosi chavīti vā cammanti vā maṃsanti vā nhārūti vā lasikāti vā, tassa neva chārikā paññāyittha, na masi; sarīrāneva avasissiṃsu. Tesañca pañcannaṃ dussayugasatānaṃ dveva dussāni na ḍayhiṃsu yañca sabbaabbhantarimaṃ yañca bāhiraṃ. Daḍḍhe ca kho pana bhagavato sarīre antalikkhā udakadhārā pātubhavitvā bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesi. Udakasālatopi udakaṃ sālatopi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) abbhunnamitvā bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesi. Kosinārakāpi mallā sabbagandhodakena bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīrāni sattāhaṃ sandhāgāre sattipañjaraṃ karitvā dhanupākāraṃ parikkhipāpetvā parikkhipitvā (syā.) naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkariṃsu garuṃ kariṃsu mānesuṃ pūjesuṃ.

Sarīradhātuvibhājanaṃ
mula_english:
235. And when the Blessed One’s body was burned, what had been skin ( *chavīti*), tissue (*cammanti*), flesh (*maṃsanti*), sinew (*nhārūti*), or joint-fluid (*lasikāti*) all vanished, and not even ashes (*chārikā*) or dust (*masi*) remained; only the bones (*śarīrāneva*) remained.

Just as when ghee (*sappissa*) or oil (*telassa*) is burned, no ashes (*chārikā*) or dust (*masi*) remain, so it was with the Blessed One’s body… only the bones (*śarīrāneva*) were left.

And of the five hundred linen wrappings (*dussayugasatānaṃ*), only two were not consumed, the innermost (*sabbaabbhantarimaṃ*) and the outermost (*bāhiraṃ*).

And when the Lord’s body was burnt up, a shower of water (*udakadhārā*) from the sky (*antalikkhā*) appeared and extinguished (*nibbāpesi*) the Blessed One’s pyre (*citakaṃ*).

Water shooting up from a Sal tree (*udakasālatopi*) as well extinguished the Blessed One’s pyre (*citakaṃ*).

The Kusinārā Mallans, with all kinds of scented water (*sabbagandhodakena*), extinguished the Blessed One’s pyre (*citakaṃ*).

Then the Mallās of Kusinārā honored the relics (*śarīrāni*) for a week (*sattāhaṃ*) in their assembly hall (*sandhāgāre*), having made a lattice-work of spears (*sattipañjaraṃ karitvā*) and an encircling wall of bows (*dhanupākāraṃ parikkhipāpetvā*), with dancing (*naccehi*), singing (*gītehi*), garlands (*mālehi*) and music (*vāditehi*) and scents (*gandhehi*), they worshipped (*sakkariṃsu*), honored (*garuṃ kariṃsu*), respected (*mānesuṃ*) and venerated (*pūjesuṃ*) them.

[Section on] The division of the relics (*śarīradhātuvibhājanaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
235.Sarīrāneva avasissiṃsūti pubbe ekagghanena ṭhitattā sarīraṃ nāma ahosi. Idāni vippakiṇṇattā sarīrānīti vuttaṃ sumanamakuḷasadisā ca dhotamuttasadisā ca suvaṇṇasadisā ca dhātuyo avasissiṃsūti attho. Dīghāyukabuddhānañhi sarīraṃ suvaṇṇakkhandhasadisaṃ ekameva hoti. Bhagavā pana – ‘‘ahaṃ na ciraṃ ṭhatvā parinibbāyāmi, mayhaṃ sāsanaṃ tāva sabbattha na vitthāritaṃ, tasmā parinibbutassāpi me sāsapamattampi dhātuṃ gahetvā attano attano vasanaṭṭhāne cetiyaṃ katvā paricaranto mahājano saggaparāyaṇo hotū’’ti dhātūnaṃ vikiraṇaṃ adhiṭṭhāsi. Kati, panassa dhātuyo vippakiṇṇā, kati na vippakiṇṇāti. Catasso dāṭhā, dve akkhakā, uṇhīsanti imā satta dhātuyo na vippakiriṃsu, sesā vippakiriṃsūti. Tattha sabbakhuddakā dhātu sāsapabījamattā ahosi, mahādhātu majjhe bhinnataṇḍulamattā, atimahatī majjhe bhinnamuggamattāti.

Udakadhārāti aggabāhumattāpi jaṅghamattāpi tālakkhandhamattāpi udakadhārā ākāsato patitvā nibbāpesi. Udakasālatoti parivāretvā ṭhitasālarukkhe sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ, tesampi hi khandhantaraviṭapantarehi udakadhārā nikkhamitvā nibbāpesuṃ. Bhagavato citako mahanto. Samantā pathaviṃ bhinditvāpi naṅgalasīsamattā udakavaṭṭi phalikavaṭaṃsakasadisā uggantvā citakameva gaṇhanti. Gandhodakenāti suvaṇṇaghaṭe rajataghaṭe ca pūretvā ābhatanānāgandhodakena. Nibbāpesunti suvaṇṇamayarajatamayehi aṭṭhadaṇḍakehi vikiritvā candanacitakaṃ nibbāpesuṃ.

Udakadhārā Udakasālato Gandhodakenā Nibbāpesu

Ettha ca citake jhāyamāne parivāretvā ṭhitasālarukkhānaṃ sākhantarehi viṭapantarehi pattantarehi jālā uggacchanti, pattaṃ vā sākhā vā pupphaṃ vā daḍḍhā nāma natthi, kipillikāpi makkaṭakāpi jālānaṃ antareneva vicaranti . Ākāsato patitaudakadhārāsupi sālarukkhehi nikkhantaudakadhārāsupi pathaviṃ bhinditvā nikkhantaudakadhārāsupi dhammakathāva pamāṇaṃ. Evaṃ citakaṃ nibbāpetvā pana mallarājāno santhāgāre catujjātiyagandhaparibhaṇḍaṃ kāretvā lājapañcamāni pupphāni vikiritvā upari celavitānaṃ bandhitvā suvaṇṇatārakādīhi khacitvā tattha gandhadāmamālādāmaratanadāmāni olambetvā santhāgārato yāva makuṭabandhanasaṅkhātā sīsapasādhanamaṅgalasālā, tāva ubhohi passehi sāṇikilañjaparikkhepaṃ kāretvā upari celavitānaṃ bandhāpetvā suvaṇṇatārakādīhi khacitvā tatthapi gandhadāmamālādāmaratanadāmāni olambetvā maṇidaṇḍavaṇṇehi veṇūhi ca pañcavaṇṇaddhaje ussāpetvā samantā vātapaṭākā parikkhipitvā susammaṭṭhāsu vīthīsu kadaliyo ca puṇṇaghaṭe ca ṭhapetvā daṇḍakadīpikā jāletvā alaṅkatahatthikkhandhe saha dhātūhi suvaṇṇadoṇiṃ ṭhapetvā mālāgandhādīhi pūjentā sādhukīḷitaṃ kīḷantā antonagaraṃ pavesetvā santhāgāre sarabhamayapallaṅke ṭhapetvā upari setacchattaṃ dhāresuṃ. Evaṃ katvā – ‘‘atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīrāni sattāhaṃ santhāgāre sattipañjaraṃ karitvā’’ti sabbaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Tattha sattipañjaraṃ karitvāti sattihatthehi purisehi parikkhipāpetvā. Dhanupākāranti paṭhamaṃ tāva hatthikumbhena kumbhaṃ paharante parikkhipāpesuṃ, tato asse gīvāya gīvaṃ paharante, tato rathe āṇikoṭiyā āṇikoṭiṃ paharante, tato yodhe bāhunā bāhuṃ paharante. Tesaṃ pariyante koṭiyā koṭiṃ paharamānāni dhanūni parikkhipāpesuṃ. Iti samantā yojanappamāṇaṃ ṭhānaṃ sattāhaṃ sannāhagavacchikaṃ viya katvā ārakkhaṃ saṃvidahiṃsu. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘dhanupākāraṃ parikkhipāpetvā’’ti.

sattipañjaraṃ karitvā Dhanupākāra

Kasmā panete evamakaṃsūti? Ito purimesu hi dvīsu sattāhesu te bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhānanisajjokāsaṃ karontā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ saṃvidahantā sādhukīḷikāya okāsaṃ na labhiṃsu. Tato nesaṃ ahosi – ‘‘imaṃ sattāhaṃ sādhukīḷitaṃ kīḷissāma, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ amhākaṃ pamattabhāvaṃ ñatvā kocideva āgantvā dhātuyo gaṇheyya, tasmā ārakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā kīḷissāmā’’ti. Te tathā evamakaṃsu.

Sarīradhātuvibhajanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
235. "Only bodily relics remained," because earlier, due to being in a solid mass, it was called a *śarīra*.

Now, due to being scattered, it is said "bodily relics," the meaning being that the *dhātus* that remained were like *sumana* buds, like washed pearls, and like gold.

Indeed, the *śarīra* of Buddhas of long life is like a golden trunk, a single mass.

The Blessed One, however, thought: "I will not attain complete extinction (*parinirvāṇa*) for long; my teaching has not yet been spread everywhere. Therefore, even after my complete extinction, may the great multitude, taking even a mustard seed's worth of relics, constructing a *caitya* in their own dwelling places, and attending to it, be destined for heaven!" He determined the scattering of the relics.

How many of his relics were scattered, and how many were not scattered?

Four teeth, two collarbones, and the *uṇhīsa*; these seven relics were not scattered; the rest were scattered.

There, the smallest relics were the size of mustard seeds; the large relics were the size of broken rice grains; the very large ones were the size of broken mung beans.

"A stream of water" means that even a stream of water the size of the tip of one's hand, the size of one's shin, or the size of a *tāla* trunk fell from the sky and extinguished it.

"From the water hall" means that this was said in reference to the *sāla* trees standing encircling it. Even from them, streams of water, having emerged from within the trunk and branches, extinguished it.

The Blessed One's funeral pyre was large.

Even after splitting the earth all around, water channels the size of a plowshare, like crystal earrings, rose up and took hold of the pyre itself.

"*Gandhodakena* (with scented water)" means having filled golden jars and silver jars with water scented with various fragrances that had been brought.

"*Nibbāpesuṃ* (they extinguished it)" means having scattered the *candanacitaka* with golden and silver *aṭṭhadaṇḍakas*, they extinguished it.

Streams of water, from the water hall, with scented water, they extinguished it.

Here, when the pyre was burning, from within the branches, twigs, and leaves of the *sāla* trees standing encircling it, flames arose; yet neither leaves, nor branches, nor flowers were seen burnt; even ants and monkeys wandered within the flames.

Even in the streams of water falling from the sky, in the streams of water emerging from the *sāla* trees, in the streams of water splitting the earth and emerging, the Dharma talk itself was the measure.

Having thus extinguished the pyre, the Malla kings, in the *santhāgāra*, having prepared a perfume mixture of four kinds, having scattered parched grain and five kinds of flowers, having fastened a cloth canopy above, having studded it with golden stars and the like, having hung garlands of perfumes, garlands of flowers, and garlands of jewels there, from the *santhāgāra* as far as the *sīsapasādhanamaṅgalasālā* known as the crown-binding hall, having caused a screen of fine linen to be made on both sides, having caused a cloth canopy to be fastened above, having studded it with golden stars and the like, having hung garlands of perfumes, garlands of flowers, and garlands of jewels there as well, having raised five-colored flags with staffs adorned with jewels and with bamboo, having surrounded it all around with wind banners, having placed bananas and full jars on the very well-swept paths, having lit lamps on poles, having placed a golden urn with the relics on the adorned elephant's shoulder, and worshiping with garlands, perfumes, and the like, while playing meritorious games, having entered the inner city, having placed it on a couch made of *sarabha* wood in the *santhāgāra*, they held a white umbrella above.

Having done thus – "Then the Mallas of Kuśināgara, having made a cage of spears around the Blessed One's *śarīra* for seven days in the *santhāgāra*" – all this should be understood.

There, "*sattipañjaraṃ karitvā* (having made a cage of spears)" means having caused men with spears in their hands to encircle it.

"*dhanupākāra* (a rampart of bows)" means first, they caused elephants to encircle it, striking trunk against trunk; then horses, striking neck against neck; then chariots, striking axle-ends against axle-ends; then warriors, striking arm against arm.

At the end of these, they caused bows, shooting arrows everywhere, to encircle it.

Thus, having made the place, about a league in extent, for seven days like a coat of mail, they established a guard.

With reference to this, it was said – "having caused a rampart of bows to encircle it."

*sattipañjaraṃ karitvā* (having made a cage of spears), *dhanupākāra* (a rampart of bows).

Why did they do this? Because in the two previous weeks, while preparing a place to sit and lie down for the community of monks, while arranging food and provisions, they did not obtain an opportunity for meritorious games.

Then it occurred to them – "During this week, we will play meritorious games. However, this place is such that someone might come, discover our state of negligence, and take the relics; therefore, having established a guard, we will play games."

They did thus.

Explanation of the Division of the Relics of the Body.

mula_pali:
236. Assosi kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesi – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo ahampi khattiyo, ahampi arahāmi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, ahampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmī’’ti.

Assosuṃ kho vesālikā licchavī – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho vesālikā licchavī kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti.

Assosuṃ kho kapilavatthuvāsī sakyā – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho kapilavatthuvāsī sakyā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā amhākaṃ ñātiseṭṭho , mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti.

Assosuṃ kho allakappakā bulayo thūlayo (syā.) – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho allakappakā bulayo kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti .

thūlayo (syā.)

Assosuṃ kho rāmagāmakā koḷiyā – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho rāmagāmakā koḷiyā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti.

Assosi kho veṭṭhadīpako brāhmaṇo – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho veṭṭhadīpako brāhmaṇo kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesi – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo ahaṃ pismi brāhmaṇo, ahampi arahāmi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, ahampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmī’’ti.

Assosuṃ kho pāveyyakā mallā – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte kosinārakā mallā te saṅghe gaṇe etadavocuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā amhākaṃ gāmakkhette parinibbuto, na mayaṃ dassāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāga’’nti.
mula_english:
236. Then King Ajātaśatru, son of the queen Videhi, of Magadha, heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then King Ajātaśatru, son of the queen Videhi, of Magadha, sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and I am also a *kṣatriya*. I am worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. I will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Licchavis of Vaiśālī heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Licchavis of Vaiśālī sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and we are also *kṣatriyas*. We are worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. We will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Śākyas residing at Kapilavastu heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Śākyas residing at Kapilavastu sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was the best of our relatives. We are worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. We will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Bulis of Allakappa heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Bulis of Allakappa sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and we are also *kṣatriyas*. We are worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. We will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Koliyas of Rāmagāma heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Koliyas of Rāmagāma sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and we are also *kṣatriyas*. We are worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. We will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Brahmin of Veṭṭhadīpa heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Brahmin of Veṭṭhadīpa sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and I am a *brāhmaṇa*. I am worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. I will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

The Mallas of Pāveyyaka heard: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa at Kuśinārā.”

Then the Mallas of Pāveyyaka sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā, saying: “The Blessed One was a *kṣatriya*, and we are also *kṣatriyas*. We are worthy to receive a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One. We will build a *stūpa* and hold a great festival for the relics of the Blessed One."

When this was said, the Mallas of Kuśinārā said to the *saṃgha* and the assembly: “The Blessed One has attained complete nirvāṇa in our village. We will not give a share of the relics (*śarīra*) of the Blessed One."
commentary_pali:
236.Assosikho rājāti kathaṃ assosi? Paṭhamameva kirassa amaccā sutvā cintayiṃsu – ‘‘satthā nāma parinibbuto, na so sakkā puna āharituṃ. Pothujjanikasaddhāya pana amhākaṃ raññā sadiso natthi, sace esa imināva niyāmena suṇissati, hadayamassa phalissati. Rājā kho pana amhehi anurakkhitabbo’’ti te tisso suvaṇṇadoṇiyo āharitvā catumadhurassa pūretvā rañño santikaṃ gantvā etadavocuṃ – ‘‘deva , amhehi supinako diṭṭho, tassa paṭighātatthaṃ tumhehi dukūladupaṭṭaṃ nivāsetvā yathā nāsāpuṭamattaṃ paññāyati, evaṃ catumadhuradoṇiyā nipajjituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti. Rājā atthacarānaṃ amaccānaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā ‘‘evaṃ hotu tātā’’ti sampaṭicchitvā tathā akāsi.

Atheko amacco alaṅkāraṃ omuñcitvā kese pakiriya yāya disāya satthā parinibbuto, tadabhimukho hutvā añjaliṃ paggayha rājānaṃ āha – ‘‘deva, maraṇato muccanakasatto nāma natthi, amhākaṃ āyuvaḍḍhano cetiyaṭṭhānaṃ puññakkhettaṃ abhisekasiñcako so bhagavā satthā kusinārāya parinibbuto’’ti. Rājā sutvāva visaññījāto catumadhuradoṇiyaṃ usumaṃ muñci. Atha naṃ ukkhipitvā dutiyāya doṇiyā nipajjāpesuṃ. So puna saññaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘tātā, kiṃ vadethā’’ti pucchi. ‘‘Satthā, mahārāja, parinibbuto’’ti. Rājā punapi visaññījāto catumadhuradoṇiyā usumaṃ muñci. Atha naṃ tatopi ukkhipitvā tatiyāya doṇiyā nipajjāpesuṃ. So puna saññaṃ labhitvā ‘‘tātā, kiṃ vadethā’’ti pucchi. ‘‘Satthā, mahārāja, parinibbuto’’ti. Rājā punapi visaññījāto, atha naṃ ukkhipitvā nahāpetvā matthake ghaṭehi udakaṃ āsiñciṃsu.

Rājā saññaṃ labhitvā āsanā vuṭṭhāya gandhaparibhāvite maṇivaṇṇe kese vikiritvā suvaṇṇaphalakavaṇṇāya piṭṭhiyaṃ pakiritvā pāṇinā uraṃ paharitvā pavāḷaṅkuravaṇṇāhi suvaṭṭitaṅgulīhi suvaṇṇabimbisakavaṇṇaṃ uraṃ sibbanto viya gahetvā paridevamāno ummattakavesena antaravīthiṃ otiṇṇo, so alaṅkatanāṭakaparivuto nagarato nikkhamma jīvakambavanaṃ gantvā yasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinnena bhagavatā dhammo desito taṃ oloketvā – ‘‘bhagavā sabbaññu, nanu imasmiṃ ṭhāne nisīditvā dhammaṃ desayittha, sokasallaṃ me vinodayittha, tumhe mayhaṃ sokasallaṃ nīharittha, ahaṃ tumhākaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, idāni pana me paṭivacanampi na detha, bhagavā’’ti punappunaṃ paridevitvā ‘‘nanu bhagavā ahaṃ aññadā evarūpe kāle ‘tumhe mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivārā jambudīpatale cārikaṃ carathā’ti suṇomi, idāni panāhaṃ tumhākaṃ ananurūpaṃ ayuttaṃ pavattiṃ suṇomī’’ti evamādīni ca vatvā saṭṭhimattāhi gāthāhi bhagavato guṇaṃ anussaritvā cintesi – ‘‘mama parideviteneva na sijjhati, dasabalassa dhātuyo āharāpessāmī’’ti evaṃ assosi. Sutvā ca imissā visaññibhāvādipavattiyā avasāne dūtaṃ pāhesi. Taṃ sandhāya atha kho rājātiādi vuttaṃ.

atha kho rājā

Tattha dūtaṃ pāhesīti dūtañca paṇṇañca pesesi. Pesetvā ca pana – ‘‘sace dassanti, sundaraṃ. No ce dassanti, āharaṇupāyena āharissāmī’’ti caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannayhitvā sayampi nikkhantoyeva. Yathā ca ajātasattu, evaṃ licchavīādayopi dūtaṃ pesetvā sayampi caturaṅginiyā senāya nikkhamiṃsuyeva. Tattha pāveyyakā sabbehi āsannatarā kusinārato tigāvutantare nagare vasanti, bhagavāpi pāvaṃ pavisitvāva kusināraṃ gato. Atha kasmā paṭhamataraṃ na āgatāti ce? Mahāparivārā panete rājāno mahāparivāraṃ karontāva pacchato jātā.

dūtaṃ pāhesī

Te saṅghe gaṇe etadavocunti sabbepi te sattanagaravāsino āgantvā – ‘‘amhākaṃ dhātuyo vā dentu, yuddhaṃ vā’’ti kusinārānagaraṃ parivāretvā ṭhite – ‘‘etaṃ bhagavā amhākaṃ gāmakkhette’’ti paṭivacanaṃ avocuṃ. Te kira evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘na mayaṃ satthu sāsanaṃ pahiṇimha, nāpi gantvā ānayimha. Satthā pana sayameva āgantvā sāsanaṃ pesetvā amhe pakkosāpesi. Tumhepi kho pana yaṃ tumhākaṃ gāmakkhette ratanaṃ uppajjati, na taṃ amhākaṃ detha. Sadevake ca loke buddharatanasamaṃ ratanaṃ nāma natthi, evarūpaṃ uttamaratanaṃ labhitvā mayaṃ na dassāma. Na kho pana tumhehiyeva mātuthanato khīraṃ pītaṃ, amhehipi mātuthanato khīraṃ pītaṃ. Na tumheyeva purisā, amhepi purisā hotū’’ti aññamaññaṃ ahaṃkāraṃ katvā sāsanapaṭisāsanaṃ pesenti, aññamaññaṃ mānagajjitaṃ gajjanti. Yuddhe pana sati kosinārakānaṃyeva jayo abhavissa. Kasmā? Yasmā dhātupāsanatthaṃ āgatā devatā nesaṃ pakkhā ahesuṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana – ‘‘bhagavā amhākaṃ gāmakkhette parinibbuto, na mayaṃ dassāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāga’’nti ettakameva āgataṃ.

Te saṅghe gaṇe etadavocu
commentary_english:
236. How did [the king] hear, "The teacher has passed away"?

First, his ministers, having heard, thought, "The teacher *nāma* has attained *parinirvāṇa*; it is not possible to bring him back again. There is no one similar to our king in his faith in ordinary people. If he hears this news with this content, his heart will break."

The king must be protected by us." So, they brought three golden *doṇis*, filled them with the four sweets, went to the king, and said, "Oh king, we saw a dream; in order to counteract that, you should wear *dukūladupaṭṭa* and lie down in the *catumadhuradoṇi* so that only the tip of your nose is visible."

The king, having heard the words of the ministers who were seeking his welfare, agreed, saying, "So be it, fathers," and he did so.

Then a certain minister, having taken off his ornaments, disheveled his hair, and with his hands folded in the direction in which the Teacher had attained *parinirvāṇa*, said to the king, "Oh king, there is no power to escape from death. That Blessed One, the Teacher, who increased our life, who was like a *cetiyaṭṭhāna*, a field of merit, and the sprinkler of the *abhiṣeka*, has attained *parinirvāṇa* in Kuśinārā."

The king, having heard this, fainted and emitted heat in the *catumadhuradoṇi*.

Then, having lifted him up, they laid him down in the second *doṇi*.

He, again regaining consciousness, asked, "Fathers, what are you saying?"

"The Teacher, oh great king, has attained *parinirvāṇa*."

The king, again having fainted, emitted heat in the *catumadhuradoṇi*.

Then, having lifted him up from there, they laid him down in the third *doṇi*.

He, again regaining consciousness, asked, "Fathers, what are you saying?"

"The Teacher, oh great king, has attained *parinirvāṇa*."

The king, again having fainted, then, having lifted him up, bathed him and poured water on his head with pots.

The king, having regained consciousness, rose from his seat, scattered his hair, which was fragrant and the color of jewels, sprinkled them on his back which was the color of a golden *phalaka*, struck his chest with his hands, and as if sewing his chest of the color of a golden *bimbisaka* with his well-rounded fingers of the color of coral sprouts, lamenting, descended into the main street in the guise of a madman. He, surrounded by adorned actors, went out of the city to Jīvakambavana and, having looked at that place where the Dharma was taught by the Blessed One who was seated, [said] - "Oh Blessed One, all-knowing one, did you not sit in this place and teach the Dharma, remove my grief? You removed my grief, I have gone to you for refuge, now you do not even give me a reply, oh Blessed One!" Having lamented again and again, "Oh Blessed One, I hear that you, together with a great community of *bhikkhus*, wander on the surface of Jambudvīpa at such a time, but now I hear of your unsuitable and improper behavior!" Having said such things and recited approximately sixty verses, recollecting the qualities of the Blessed One, he thought, "It is not effective by my lamenting alone, I will have the relics of the one with ten powers brought." Thus he heard.

And having heard of this course of events, ending with his fainting, he sent a messenger.

With reference to that, "Then the king" etc. was said.

Then the king sent a messenger, sending both a messenger and a gift.

And having sent [him], he thought, "If they give [the relics], it is beautiful. If they do not give [them], I will bring [them] by means of taking." Having assembled a four-division army, he himself set out.

Just as Ajātaśatru did, so also the Licchavis and others, having sent a messenger, themselves set out with a four-division army.

There, the Pāveyyakas live in a city three *gāvutas* away from Kuśinārā, which is nearer to all [the kings]. The Blessed One also, having entered Pāvā, went to Kuśinārā.

Then why did [they] not come sooner? These kings with great retinues came later while making great retinues.

Having sent a messenger, "They said this to the *saṅgha* and *gaṇa*," means that all those inhabitants of the seven cities, having come and surrounded the city of Kuśinārā [and] being stationed [there], said this answer, "This Blessed One is in our village area."

They said thus, "We did not send the Teacher’s message, nor did we go and bring [him].

The Teacher himself came and sent a message, and made us call out.

Also, you do not give us the jewels that arise in your village area.

And in the world with gods, there is no jewel equal to the jewel of the Buddha. Having obtained such an excellent jewel, we will not give [it]."

It is not only you who have drunk milk from your mother's breast, we too have drunk milk from our mother's breast.

It is not only you who are men, we too are men!" Having made such mutual egotism, they send messages and counter-messages, they thunder mutual prideful thunder.
In war, however, if it occurred, the victory would have belonged to the Kuśinārakas alone.

Why? Because the deities who came to worship the relics were not on their side.

Moreover, in the Pali [text] – "The Blessed One has attained complete extinction in our village area; we will not give a share of the Blessed One's relics" – only this much has come.

They said this in the assembly, in the group.

mula_pali:
237. Evaṃ vutte doṇo brāhmaṇo te saṅghe gaṇe etadavoca –

‘‘Suṇantu bhonto mama ekavācaṃ,

Amhāka chandānurakkhaṇatthaṃ niggahītalopo; Buddho ahu khantivādo;

chandānurakkhaṇatthaṃ niggahītalopo

Na hi sādhu yaṃ uttamapuggalassa,

Sarīrabhāge siyā sampahāro.

Sabbeva bhonto sahitā samaggā,

Sammodamānā karomaṭṭhabhāge;

Vitthārikā hontu disāsu thūpā,

Bahū janā cakkhumato pasannā’’ti.
commentary_pali:
237.Evaṃ vutte doṇo brāhmaṇoti doṇabrāhmaṇo imaṃ tesaṃ vivādaṃ sutvā – ‘‘ete rājāno bhagavato parinibbutaṭṭhāne vivādaṃ karonti, na kho panetaṃ patirūpaṃ, alaṃ iminā kalahena, vūpasamessāmi na’’nti so gantvā te saṅghe gaṇe etadavoca. Kimavoca? Unnatappadese ṭhatvā dvibhāṇavāraparimāṇaṃ doṇagajjitaṃ nāma avoca. Tattha paṭhamabhāṇavāre tāva ekapadampi te na jāniṃsu. Dutiyabhāṇavārapariyosāne – ‘‘ācariyassa viya bho saddo, ācariyassa viya bho saddo’’ti sabbe niravā ahesuṃ. Jambudīpatale kira kulaghare jātā yebhuyyena tassa na antevāsiko nāma natthi. Atha so te attano vacanaṃ sutvā nirave tuṇhībhūte viditvā puna etadavoca – ‘‘suṇantu bhonto’’ti etaṃ gāthādvayaṃ avoca.

Tattha amhākaṃ buddhoti amhākaṃ buddho. Ahu khantivādoti buddhabhūmiṃ appatvāpi pāramiyo pūrento khantivāditāpasakāle dhammapālakumārakāle chaddantahatthikāle bhūridattanāgarājakāle campeyyanāgarājakāle saṅkhapālanāgarājakāle mahākapikāle aññesu ca bahūsu jātakesu paresu kopaṃ akatvā khantimeva akāsi. Khantimeva vaṇṇayi. Kimaṅgaṃ pana etarahi iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu tādilakkhaṇaṃ patto, sabbathāpi amhākaṃ buddho khantivādo ahosi, tassa evaṃvidhassa. Na hi sādhu yaṃ uttamapuggalassa, sarīrabhāge siyā sampahāroti na hi sādhuyanti na hi sādhu ayaṃ. Sarīrabhāgeti sarīravibhāganimittaṃ, dhātukoṭṭhāsahetūti attho. Siyā sampahāroti āvudhasampahāro sādhu na siyāti vuttaṃ hoti.

amhākaṃ buddho Ahu khantivādo Na hi sādhu yaṃ uttamapuggalassa, sarīrabhāge siyā sampahāroti na hi sādhuya Sarīrabhāge Siyā sampahāro

Sabbeva bhonto sahitāti sabbeva bhonto sahitā hotha, mā bhijjatha. Samaggāti kāyena ca vācāya ca ekasannipātā ekavacanā samaggā hotha. Sammodamānāti cittenāpi aññamaññaṃ sammodamānā hotha. Karomaṭṭhabhāgeti bhagavato sarīrāni aṭṭha bhāge karoma . Cakkhumatoti pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumato buddhassa. Na kevalaṃ tumheyeva, bahujanopi pasanno, tesu ekopi laddhuṃ ayutto nāma natthīti bahuṃ kāraṇaṃ vatvā saññāpesi.

Sabbeva bhonto sahitā Samaggā Sammodamānā Karomaṭṭhabhāge Cakkhumato
commentary_english:
237. Thus, when it was said, “Doṇa the *brāhmaṇa*,” Doṇa the *brāhmaṇa*, having heard their dispute, [thought:] “These kings are disputing at the place of the Blessed One’s complete extinction! This is not fitting. Enough of this quarrel! I will settle it,” and so, having gone to that assembly and group, he said this:

What did he say? Having stood in an elevated region, he spoke what is called “Doṇa's Roar,” [a recitation] measuring two *bhāṇavāras*. There, during the first *bhāṇavāra*, they did not understand even a single word. At the conclusion of the second *bhāṇavāra*, they all became silent, [saying,] “The voice is like the teacher’s, the voice is like the teacher’s!” It is said that in the *jambudvīpa*, there are very many born in a family residence for whom there is no one called a pupil. Then, having heard their words, knowing that they were silent and without protection, he again said this: “Listen, good sirs!” He spoke these two verses.

There, “Our Buddha,” [means:] our Buddha.

“He was an advocate of patience,” [means:] even without reaching the *buddha*-ground, while fulfilling the perfections, at the time of the ascetic advocate of patience, at the time of the *dhammapāla* prince, at the time of the six-tusked elephant, at the time of the Nāga-king Bhūridatta, at the time of the Nāga-king Campeyya, at the time of the Nāga-king Saṅkhapāla, at the time of the great monkey, and in many other *jātakas*, without making anger towards others, he only made patience. He only praised patience. What need to say that now, having attained such characteristics in desirable and undesirable things, in every way, our Buddha was an advocate of patience, for him of such a kind?

“Indeed, it is not good that there should be a blow on the body of the supreme person,” [means:] this is indeed not good.

“On the body,” [means:] on account of the division of the body; the meaning is, the elements are the cause of the components.

“There might be a blow,” [means:] it is said that a blow with a weapon would not be good.

“All of you good sirs, being united,” [means:] all of you good sirs, being united, be harmonious!

“Being harmonious,” [means:] be harmonious, with body and speech, being of one assembly and one speech!

“Being delighted,” [means:] be delighted with each other, even in mind!

“Let us make eight parts,” [means:] let us make eight parts of the Blessed One’s relics.

“Possessing vision,” [means:] of the Buddha possessing vision with the five eyes. Not only you, but also many people are pleased; he persuaded [them], saying that there was no one among them unfit to receive [a part], speaking many reasons.

mula_pali:
238. ‘‘Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, tvaññeva bhagavato sarīrāni aṭṭhadhā samaṃ savibhattaṃ vibhajāhī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho doṇo brāhmaṇo tesaṃ saṅghānaṃ gaṇānaṃ paṭissutvā bhagavato sarīrāni aṭṭhadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitvā te saṅghe gaṇe etadavoca – ‘‘imaṃ me bhonto tumbaṃ dadantu ahampi tumbassa thūpañca mahañca karissāmī’’ti. Adaṃsu kho te doṇassa brāhmaṇassa tumbaṃ.

Assosuṃ kho pippalivaniyā pipphalivaniyā (syā.) moriyā – ‘‘bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto’’ti. Atha kho pippalivaniyā moriyā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Natthi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgo, vibhattāni bhagavato sarīrāni. Ito aṅgāraṃ harathā’’ti. Te tato aṅgāraṃ hariṃsu āhariṃsu (syā. ka.).

pipphalivaniyā (syā.) āhariṃsu (syā. ka.)

Dhātuthūpapūjā
mula_english:
238. “In that case, *brāhmaṇa*, you yourself divide the *Bhagavat's* relics into eight equal portions, well divided.”

“So be it, good sirs,” replied Doṇa the *brāhmaṇa* to those assemblies and groups. Having divided the *Bhagavat's* relics into eight equal portions, well divided, he said to those assemblies and groups: “Give me this urn, good sirs, and I too will build a *stūpa* for the urn and a great ceremony.”

They gave the urn to Doṇa the *brāhmaṇa*.

The Moriyas of Pipphalivana heard: “The *Bhagavat*, they say, has attained complete *nirvāṇa* in Kuśinārā.”

Then the Moriyas of Pipphalivana sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kuśinārā: “The *Bhagavat* was a *kṣatriya*, and we too are *kṣatriyas*. We are worthy to receive a portion of the *Bhagavat's* relics. We too will build a *stūpa* and a great ceremony for the *Bhagavat's* relics.”

“There is no portion of the *Bhagavat's* relics; the *Bhagavat's* relics have been divided. Take the embers from here.”

They took the embers from there.

Relic *stūpa* veneration.
commentary_pali:
238.Tesaṃ saṅghānaṃ gaṇānaṃ paṭissutvāti tesaṃ tesaṃ tato tato samāgatasaṅghānaṃ samāgatagaṇānaṃ paṭissuṇitvā. Bhagavatosarīrāni aṭṭhadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitvāti ettha ayamanukkamo – doṇo kira tesaṃ paṭissuṇitvā suvaṇṇadoṇiṃ vivarāpesi. Rājāno āgantvā doṇiyaṃyeva ṭhitā suvaṇṇavaṇṇā dhātuyo disvā – ‘‘bhagavā sabbaññu pubbe mayaṃ tumhākaṃ dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ chabbaṇṇabuddharasmikhacitaṃ asītianubyañjanasamujjalitasobhaṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sarīraṃ addasāma, idāni pana suvaṇṇavaṇṇāva dhātuyo avasiṭṭhā jātā, na yuttamidaṃ bhagavā tumhāka’’nti parideviṃsu.

Brāhmaṇopi tasmiṃ samaye tesaṃ pamattabhāvaṃ ñatvā dakkhiṇadāṭhaṃ gahetvā veṭhantare ṭhapesi, atha pacchā aṭṭhadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhaji, sabbāpi dhātuyo pākatikanāḷiyā soḷasa nāḷiyo ahesuṃ, ekekanagaravāsino dve dve nāḷiyo labhiṃsu. Brāhmaṇassa pana dhātuyo vibhajantasseva sakko devānamindo – ‘‘kena nu kho sadevakassa lokassa kaṅkhacchedanatthāya catusaccakathāya paccayabhūtā bhagavato dakkhiṇadāṭhā gahitā’’ti olokento ‘‘brāhmaṇena gahitā’’ti disvā – ‘‘brāhmaṇopi dāṭhāya anucchavikaṃ sakkāraṃ kātuṃ na sakkhissati, gaṇhāmi na’’nti veṭhantarato gahetvā suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭake ṭhapetvā devalokaṃ netvā cūḷāmaṇicetiye patiṭṭhapesi.

Brāhmaṇopi dhātuyo vibhajitvā dāṭhaṃ apassanto corikāya gahitattā – ‘‘kena me dāṭhā gahitā’’ti pucchitumpi nāsakkhi. ‘‘Nanu tayāva dhātuyo bhājitā, kiṃ tvaṃ paṭhamaṃyeva attano dhātuyā atthibhāvaṃ na aññāsī’’ti attani dosāropanaṃ sampassanto – ‘‘mayhampi koṭṭhāsaṃ dethā’’ti vattumpi nāsakkhi. Tato – ‘‘ayampi suvaṇṇatumbo dhātugatikova, yena tathāgatassa dhātuyo mitā, imassāhaṃ thūpaṃ karissāmī’’ti cintetvā imaṃ me bhonto tumbaṃ dadantūti āha.

imaṃ me bhonto tumbaṃ dadantū

Pippalivaniyāmoriyāpi ajātasattuādayo viya dūtaṃ pesetvā yuddhasajjāva nikkhamiṃsu.

Pippalivaniyā moriyāpi

Dhātuthūpapūjāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
238. *tesaṃ saṅghānaṃ gaṇānaṃ paṭissutvā* means having promised those assembled *saṅghas* and groups from here and there. *bhagavato sarīrāni aṭṭhadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitvā* Here, the sequence is as follows: It seems that Doṇa, having promised them, had the golden *doṇi* opened. The kings, having come and seeing the relics of golden color situated in the *doṇi* itself, lamented, "Blessed One, all-knowing one, formerly we saw your body of golden color adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, inlaid with the six-colored Buddha rays, and radiant with the eighty minor marks, but now only relics of golden color remain. This is not fitting, Blessed One."

A brahmin, also at that time, knowing their state of negligence, took the right tooth and placed it inside a wrapping. Then, afterwards, he divided [the relics] well, equally into eight parts. All the relics were sixteen *nāḷis* by the natural *nāḷi* measure; the inhabitants of each city obtained two *nāḷis* each. While the brahmin was dividing the relics, Sakka, the king of the gods, looking around, [thinking,] "By whom was the Blessed One's right tooth, which was the basis for the talk of the four truths for the sake of cutting off the doubt of the world with its gods, taken?" Seeing that "it was taken by the brahmin," [he thought,] "The brahmin will not be able to show honor to the tooth as is fitting. I will take it." Having taken it from within the wrapping, having placed it in a golden casket, having taken it to the world of the gods, he established it in the Cūḷāmaṇi shrine.

The brahmin, also, having divided the relics, not seeing the tooth, since it was taken by stealth, was not even able to ask, "By whom was my tooth taken?" Realizing that "Surely, the relics were divided by you; why did you not know the existence of your own relic from the beginning?" [and] perceiving the imputation of fault in himself, he was not even able to say, "Give me a share too." Then, thinking, "This golden *tumba* is also connected with the relics, by which the relics of the Tathāgata were measured; I will make a stupa for it," he said, *imaṃ me bhonto tumbaṃ dadantū*.

*imaṃ me bhonto tumbaṃ dadantū* The *moriyas* of Pippalivana, like Ajātasattu and others, having sent a messenger, went out ready for war.

*pippalivaniyā moriyāpi* Description of the worship of the relic stupa.

mula_pali: 239. Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto rājagahe bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akāsi. Vesālikāpi licchavī vesāliyaṃ bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Kapilavatthuvāsīpi sakyā kapilavatthusmiṃ bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Allakappakāpi bulayo allakappe bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Rāmagāmakāpi koḷiyā rāmagāme bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Veṭṭhadīpakopi brāhmaṇo veṭṭhadīpe bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akāsi. Pāveyyakāpi mallā pāvāyaṃ bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Kosinārakāpi mallā kusinārāyaṃ bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Doṇopi brāhmaṇo tumbassa thūpañca mahañca akāsi. Pippalivaniyāpi moriyā pippalivane aṅgārānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu. Iti aṭṭha sarīrathūpā navamo tumbathūpo dasamo aṅgārathūpo. Evametaṃ bhūtapubbanti.
mula_english:
Then King Ajātaśatru, son of the Videhi queen, of Magadha, built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Rājagṛha.

The Licchavis of Vaiśālī also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Vaiśālī.

The Śākyas of Kapilavastu also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Kapilavastu.

The Bulis of Allakappa also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Allakappa.

The Koliyas of Rāmagrāma also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Rāmagrāma.

The *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) of Veṭhadīpa also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Veṭhadīpa.

The Mallas of Pāvā also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Pāvā.

The Mallas of Kuśinārā also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the relics of the Blessed One in Kuśinārā.

The *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) Doṇa also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the urn.

The Moriyas of Pipphalivana also built a great *stūpa* (thūpa) for the embers in Pipphalivana.

Thus, there were eight *stūpas* (thūpa) for the relics, the ninth for the urn, and the tenth for the embers.

Thus it was in the past.
commentary_pali:
239.Rājagahe bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akāsīti kathaṃ akāsi? Kusinārato yāva rājagahaṃ pañcavīsati yojanāni, etthantare aṭṭhausabhavitthataṃ samatalaṃ maggaṃ kāretvā yādisaṃ mallarājāno makuṭabandhanassa ca santhāgārassa ca antare pūjaṃ kāresuṃ. Tādisaṃ pañcavīsatiyojanepi magge pūjaṃ kāretvā lokassa anukkaṇṭhanatthaṃ sabbattha antarāpaṇe pasāretvā suvaṇṇadoṇiyaṃ pakkhittadhātuyo sattipañjarena parikkhipāpetvā attano vijite pañcayojanasataparimaṇḍale manusse sannipātāpesi. Te dhātuyo gahetvā kusinārato sādhukīḷitaṃ kīḷantā nikkhamitvā yattha yattha suvaṇṇavaṇṇāni pupphāni passanti, tattha tattha dhātuyo sattiantare ṭhapetvā pūjaṃ akaṃsu. Tesaṃ pupphānaṃ khīṇakāle gacchanti, rathassa dhuraṭṭhānaṃ pacchimaṭṭhāne sampatte satta divase sādhukīḷitaṃ kīḷanti. Evaṃ dhātuyo gahetvā āgacchantānaṃ satta vassāni satta māsāni satta divasāni vītivattāni.

Micchādiṭṭhikā – ‘‘samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbutakālato paṭṭhāya balakkārena sādhukīḷitāya upaddutamha sabbe no kammantā naṭṭhā’’ti ujjhāyantā manaṃ padosetvā chaḷāsītisahassamattā apāye nibbattā. Khīṇāsavā āvajjitvā ‘‘mahājano manaṃ padosetvā apāye nibbattī’’ti disvā – ‘‘sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ dhātuāharaṇūpāyaṃ kāressāmā’’ti tassa santikaṃ gantvā tamatthaṃ ārocetvā – ‘‘dhātuāharaṇūpāyaṃ karohi mahārājā’’ti āhaṃsu. Sakko āha – ‘‘bhante, puthujjano nāma ajātasattunā samo saddho natthi, na so mama vacanaṃ karissati, apica kho māravibhiṃsakasadisaṃ vibhiṃsakaṃ dassessāmi, mahāsaddaṃ sāvessāmi, yakkhagāhakakhipitakaarocake karissāmi, tumhe ‘amanussā mahārāja kupitā dhātuyo āharāpethā’ti vadeyyātha, evaṃ so āharāpessatī’’ti. Atha kho sakko taṃ sabbaṃ akāsi.

Therāpi rājānaṃ upasaṅkamitvā – ‘‘mahārāja, amanussā kupitā, dhātuyo āharāpehī’’ti bhaṇiṃsu. Rājā – ‘‘na tāva, bhante, mayhaṃ cittaṃ tussati, evaṃ santepi āharantū’’ti āha. Sattamadivase dhātuyo āhariṃsu. Evaṃ āhatā dhātuyo gahetvā rājagahe thūpañca mahañca akāsi. Itarepi attano attano balānurūpena āharitvā sakasakaṭṭhānesu thūpañca mahañca akaṃsu.
commentary_english:
239. How did [he] do that when [it says,] "In Rajagṛha, he made a *stūpa* and a great [offering] for the relics of the Blessed One (*bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca akāsī*)"? From Kuśināra to Rajagṛha is twenty-five *yojana*s. In between, having had a level road constructed that was eight *ausabha*s wide, just as the Malla kings made offerings at the *makuṭabandhana* and assembly hall, in the same way, having made offerings along the twenty-five *yojana* road, in order to cause the world to be without longing, everywhere in the inner market, having spread out the relics that were placed in a golden urn, having had a *sattipañjara* placed around [them], he had people assemble in his own conquered territory, in a circular area of five hundred *yojana*s. Having taken those relics, departing from Kuśināra, playing well, wherever they saw golden-colored flowers, there, having placed the relics in the *satti*, they made offerings. As those flowers withered, they proceeded, and when the yoke of the chariot reached the western place, they played well for seven days. In this way, as they were taking the relics and coming, seven years, seven months, and seven days passed.

Those with wrong views – "Since the time of the *parinirvāṇa* of the *śramaṇa* Gautama, all our work has been ruined by the forced good play" – complaining, having corrupted their minds, eighty-six thousand were reborn in the *apāya*s. The *khīṇāsava*s, reflecting, seeing that "The great mass of people, having corrupted their minds, have been reborn in the *apāya*s," [said:] "We will have Śakra, the king of the gods, make a means for obtaining the relics (*dhātuāharaṇūpāyaṃ kāressāmā*)," and going to his presence, announcing that matter, they said, "Make a means for obtaining the relics, great king (*dhātuāharaṇūpāyaṃ karohi mahārājā*)."

Śakra said – "Reverend ones (*bhante*), an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) named Ajātaśatru does not have faith like that. He will not do my bidding. Moreover, I will show a frightening form similar to Māra's Vibhīṃsaka, I will make a great noise, I will make [it seem like] *yakṣa*s are seizing [people] and throwing them into the *arocaka*. You should say, 'O great king (*mahārāja*), non-humans are angry, bring the relics here!' In this way he will have [them] brought here."

Then Śakra did all of that.

The *thera*s also, approaching the king, said – "O great king (*mahārāja*), non-humans are angry, bring the relics here!"

The king [said] – "My mind is not pleased yet, reverend ones (*bhante*), but even so, let them bring [them] here."

On the seventh day, they brought the relics.

In this way, having taken the relics that were brought, in Rajagṛha, he made a *stūpa* and a great [offering].

The others also, each according to their power, having brought [relics], in their own places, made a *stūpa* and a great [offering].

mula_pali:
240. Aṭṭhadoṇaṃ cakkhumato sarīraṃ, sattadoṇaṃ jambudīpe mahenti.

Ekañca doṇaṃ purisavaruttamassa, rāmagāme nāgarājā maheti.

Ekāhi dāṭhā tidivehi pūjitā, ekā pana gandhārapure mahīyati;

Kāliṅgarañño vijite punekaṃ, ekaṃ pana nāgarājā maheti.

Tasseva tejena ayaṃ vasundharā,

Āyāgaseṭṭhehi mahī alaṅkatā;

Evaṃ imaṃ cakkhumato sarīraṃ,

Susakkataṃ sakkatasakkatehi.

Devindanāgindanarindapūjito ,

Manussindaseṭṭhehi tatheva pūjito;

Taṃ vandatha taṃ taṃ vandatha (syā.) pañjalikā labhitvā,

taṃ taṃ vandatha (syā.)

Buddho have kappasatehi dullabhoti.

Cattālīsa samā dantā, kesā lomā ca sabbaso;

Devā hariṃsu ekekaṃ, cakkavāḷaparamparāti.

Mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
240. Eight portions were the relics of the One with Eyes (cakkhumato sarīraṃ), seven honored in Jambudīpa (Jambudīpe).

One portion of the best of men (purisavaruttamassa) the Nāga king honors in Rāmagāma.

One tooth is worshipped by the gods of the Thirty-three (tidivehi pūjitā), one is honored in Gandhārapura;

Again, one [tooth relic] is in the territory of the Kalinga king (kāliṅgarañño vijite), one the Nāga king honors.

By his (tasseva) very power this earth (vasundharā),

is adorned with splendid Āyāgas (āyāgaseṭṭhehi mahī alaṅkatā);

Thus, this body of the One with Eyes (cakkhumato sarīraṃ),

is well-honored by those worthy of honor.

Worshipped by the lords of gods, Nāgas, and men (devindanāgindanarindapūjito),

similarly worshipped by the best of men;

Having gained reverence, revere him (taṃ vandatha) with joined hands,

For hard indeed it is Through hundreds of ages to meet with an All-Enlightened One! (buddho have kappasatehi dullabhoti).

Forty-four even teeth, hairs and body hairs entirely;

The gods took away each one, in successive world-circles.

The third Mahāparinibbāna Sutta is finished.
commentary_pali:
240.Evametaṃ bhūtapubbanti evaṃ etaṃ dhātubhājanañceva dasathūpakaraṇañca jambudīpe bhūtapubbanti pacchā saṅgītikārakā āhaṃsu. Evaṃ patiṭṭhitesu pana thūpesu mahākassapatthero dhātūnaṃ antarāyaṃ disvā rājānaṃ ajātasattuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ‘‘mahārāja, ekaṃ dhātunidhānaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti āha. Sādhu, bhante, nidhānakammaṃ tāva mama hotu, sesadhātuyo pana kathaṃ āharāmīti? Na, mahārāja, dhātuāharaṇaṃ tuyhaṃ bhāro, amhākaṃ bhāroti. Sādhu, bhante, tumhe dhātuyo āharatha, ahaṃ dhātunidhānaṃ karissāmīti. Thero tesaṃ tesaṃ rājakulānaṃ paricaraṇamattameva ṭhapetvā sesadhātuyo āhari. Rāmagāme pana dhātuyo nāgā pariggaṇhiṃsu, tāsaṃ antarāyo natthi. ‘‘Anāgate laṅkādīpe mahāvihāre mahācetiyamhi nidahissantī’’ti tā na āharitvā sesehi sattahi nagarehi āharitvā rājagahassa pācīnadakkhiṇadisābhāge ṭhatvā – ‘‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne yo pāsāṇo atthi, so antaradhāyatu, paṃsu suvisuddhā hotu, udakaṃ mā uṭṭhahatū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi.

Rājā taṃ ṭhānaṃ khaṇāpetvā tato uddhatapaṃsunā iṭṭhakā kāretvā asītimahāsāvakānaṃ cetiyāni kāreti. ‘‘Idha rājā kiṃ kāretī’’ti pucchantānampi ‘‘mahāsāvakānaṃ cetiyānī’’ti vadanti, na koci dhātunidhānabhāvaṃ jānāti. Asītihatthagambhīre pana tasmiṃ padese jāte heṭṭhā lohasanthāraṃ santharāpetvā tattha thūpārāme cetiyagharappamāṇaṃ tambalohamayaṃ gehaṃ kārāpetvā aṭṭha aṭṭha haricandanādimaye karaṇḍe ca thūpe ca kārāpesi. Atha bhagavato dhātuyo haricandanakaraṇḍe pakkhipitvā taṃ haricandanakaraṇḍakampi aññasmiṃ haricandanakaraṇḍake, tampi aññasminti evaṃ aṭṭha haricandanakaraṇḍe ekato katvā eteneva upāyena te aṭṭha karaṇḍe aṭṭhasu haricandanathūpesu, aṭṭha haricandanathūpe aṭṭhasu lohitacandanakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha lohitacandanakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu lohitacandanathūpesu, aṭṭha lohitacandanathūpe aṭṭhasu dantakaraṇḍesu , aṭṭha dantakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu dantathūpesu, aṭṭha dantathūpe aṭṭhasu sabbaratanakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha sabbaratanakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu sabbaratanathūpesu, aṭṭha sabbaratanathūpe aṭṭhasu suvaṇṇakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha suvaṇṇakaraṇḍe, aṭṭhasu suvaṇṇathūpesu, aṭṭha suvaṇṇathūpe aṭṭhasu rajatakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha rajatakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu rajatathūpesu, aṭṭha rajatathūpe, aṭṭhasu maṇikaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha maṇikaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu maṇithūpesu, aṭṭha maṇithūpe aṭṭhasu lohitaṅkakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha lohitaṅkakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu lohitaṅkathūpesu, aṭṭha lohitaṅkathūpe aṭṭhasu masāragallakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha masāragallakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu masāragallathūpesu, aṭṭha masāragallathūpe aṭṭhasu phalikakaraṇḍesu, aṭṭha phalikakaraṇḍe aṭṭhasu phalikamayathūpesu pakkhipi.

Sabbesaṃ uparimaṃ phalikacetiyaṃ thūpārāmacetiyappamāṇaṃ ahosi, tassa upari sabbaratanamayaṃ gehaṃ kāresi, tassa upari suvaṇṇamayaṃ, tassa upari rajatamayaṃ, tassa upari tambalohamayaṃ gehaṃ. Tattha sabbaratanamayaṃ vālikaṃ okiritvā jalajathalajapupphānaṃ sahassāni vippakiritvā aḍḍhachaṭṭhāni jātakasatāni asītimahāthere suddhodanamahārājānaṃ mahāmāyādeviṃ satta sahajāteti sabbānetāni suvaṇṇamayāneva kāresi. Pañcapañcasate suvaṇṇarajatamaye puṇṇaghaṭe ṭhapāpesi, pañca suvaṇṇaddhajasate ussāpesi. Pañcasate suvaṇṇadīpe, pañcasate rajatadīpe kārāpetvā sugandhatelassa pūretvā tesu dukūlavaṭṭiyo ṭhapesi.

Athāyasmā mahākassapo – ‘‘mālā mā milāyantu, gandhā mā vinassantu, dīpā mā vijjhāyantū’’ti adhiṭṭhahitvā suvaṇṇapaṭṭe akkharāni chindāpesi –

‘‘Anāgate piyadāso nāma kumāro chattaṃ ussāpetvā asoko dhammarājā bhavissati. So imā dhātuyo vitthārikā karissatī’’ti.

Rājā sabbapasādhanehi pūjetvā ādito paṭṭhāya dvāraṃ pidahanto nikkhami, so tambalohadvāraṃ pidahitvā āviñchanarajjuyaṃ kuñcikamuddikaṃ bandhitvā tattheva mahantaṃ maṇikkhandhaṃ ṭhapetvā – ‘‘anāgate daliddarājā imaṃ maṇiṃ gahetvā dhātūnaṃ sakkāraṃ karotū’’ti akkharaṃ chindāpesi.

Sakko devarājā vissakammaṃ āmantetvā – ‘‘tāta, ajātasattunā dhātunidhānaṃ kataṃ, ettha ārakkhaṃ paṭṭhapehī’’ti pahiṇi. So āgantvā vāḷasaṅghāṭayantaṃ yojesi, kaṭṭharūpakāni tasmiṃ dhātugabbhe phalikavaṇṇakhagge gāhetvā vātasadisena vegena anupariyāyantaṃ yantaṃ yojetvā ekāya eva āṇiyā bandhitvā samantato giñjakāvasathākārena silāparikkhepaṃ katvā upari ekāya pidahitvā paṃsuṃ pakkhipitvā bhūmiṃ samaṃ katvā tassa upari pāsāṇathūpaṃ patiṭṭhapesi. Evaṃ niṭṭhite dhātunidhāne yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā theropi parinibbuto, rājāpi yathākammaṃ gato, tepi manussā kālaṅkatā.

Aparabhāge piyadāso nāma kumāro chattaṃ ussāpetvā asoko nāma dhammarājā hutvā tā dhātuyo gahetvā jambudīpe vitthārikā akāsi. Kathaṃ? So nigrodhasāmaṇeraṃ nissāya sāsane laddhappasādo caturāsīti vihārasahassāni kāretvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pucchi – ‘‘bhante, mayā caturāsīti vihārasahassāni kāritāni, dhātuyo kuto labhissāmī’’ti? Mahārāja, – ‘‘dhātunidhānaṃ nāma atthī’’ti suṇoma, na pana paññāyati – ‘‘asukasmiṃ ṭhāne’’ti. Rājā rājagahe cetiyaṃ bhindāpetvā dhātuṃ apassanto paṭipākatikaṃ kāretvā bhikkhubhikkhuniyo upāsakaupāsikāyoti catasso parisā gahetvā vesāliṃ gato. Tatrāpi alabhitvā kapilavatthuṃ. Tatrāpi alabhitvā rāmagāmaṃ gato. Rāmagāme nāgā cetiyaṃ bhindituṃ na adaṃsu, cetiye nipatitakudālo khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ hoti. Evaṃ tatrāpi alabhitvā allakappaṃ veṭhadīpaṃ pāvaṃ kusināranti sabbattha cetiyāni bhinditvā dhātuṃ alabhitvāva paṭipākatikāni katvā puna rājagahaṃ gantvā catasso parisā sannipātāpetvā – ‘‘atthi kenaci sutapubbaṃ ‘asukaṭṭhāne nāma dhātunidhāna’nti’’ pucchi.

Tatreko vīsavassasatiko thero – ‘‘asukaṭṭhāne dhātunidhāna’’nti na jānāmi, mayhaṃ pana pitā mahāthero maṃ sattavassakāle mālācaṅkoṭakaṃ gāhāpetvā – ‘‘ehi sāmaṇera, asukagacchantare pāsāṇathūpo atthi, tattha gacchāmā’’ti gantvā pūjetvā – ‘‘imaṃ ṭhānaṃ upadhāretuṃ vaṭṭati sāmaṇerā’’ti āha. Ahaṃ ettakaṃ jānāmi mahārājāti āha. Rājā ‘‘etadeva ṭhāna’’nti vatvā gacche hāretvā pāsāṇathūpañca paṃsuñca apanetvā heṭṭhā sudhābhūmiṃ addasa. Tato sudhañca iṭṭhakāyo ca hāretvā anupubbena pariveṇaṃ oruyha sattaratanavālukaṃ asihatthāni ca kaṭṭharūpakāni samparivattakāni addasa. So yakkhadāsake pakkosāpetvā balikammaṃ kāretvāpi neva antaṃ na koṭiṃ passanto devatānaṃ namassamāno – ‘‘ahaṃ imā dhātuyo gahetvā caturāsītiyā vihārasahassesu nidahitvā sakkāraṃ karomi, mā me devatā antarāyaṃ karontū’’ti āha.

Sakko devarājā cārikaṃ caranto taṃ disvā vissakammaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tāta, asoko dhammarājā ‘dhātuyo nīharissāmī’ti pariveṇaṃ otiṇṇo, gantvā kaṭṭharūpakāni hārehī’’ti. So pañcacūḷagāmadārakavesena gantvā rañño purato dhanuhattho ṭhatvā – ‘‘harāmi mahārājā’’ti āha. ‘‘Hara, tātā’’ti saraṃ gahetvā sandhimhiyeva vijjhi, sabbaṃ vippakiriyittha. Atha rājā āviñchane bandhaṃ kuñcikamuddikaṃ gaṇhi, maṇikkhandhaṃ passi. ‘‘Anāgate daliddarājā imaṃ maṇiṃ gahetvā dhātūnaṃ sakkāraṃ karotū’’ti puna akkharāni disvā kujjhitvā – ‘‘mādisaṃ nāma rājānaṃ daliddarājāti vattuṃ ayutta’’nti punappunaṃ ghaṭetvā dvāraṃ vivarāpetvā antogehaṃ paviṭṭho.

Aṭṭhārasavassādhikānaṃ dvinnaṃ vassasatānaṃ upari āropitadīpā tatheva pajjalanti. Nīluppalapupphāni taṅkhaṇaṃ āharitvā āropitāni viya, pupphasanthāro taṅkhaṇaṃ santhato viya, gandhā taṃ muhuttaṃ pisitvā ṭhapitā viya rājā suvaṇṇapaṭṭaṃ gahetvā – ‘‘anāgate piyadāso nāma kumāro chattaṃ ussāpetvā asoko nāma dhammarājā bhavissati so imā dhātuyo vitthārikā karissatī’’ti vācetvā – ‘‘diṭṭho bho, ahaṃ ayyena mahākassapattherenā’’ti vatvā vāmahatthaṃ ābhujitvā dakkhiṇena hatthena apphoṭesi. So tasmiṃ ṭhāne paricaraṇadhātumattameva ṭhapetvā sesā dhātuyo gahetvā dhātugehaṃ pubbe pihitanayeneva pidahitvā sabbaṃ yathāpakatiyāva katvā upari pāsāṇacetiyaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā caturāsītiyā vihārasahassesu dhātuyo patiṭṭhāpetvā mahāthere vanditvā pucchi – ‘‘dāyādomhi, bhante, buddhasāsane’’ti. Kissa dāyādo tvaṃ, mahārāja, bāhirako tvaṃ sāsanassāti. Bhante, channavutikoṭidhanaṃ vissajjetvā caturāsīti vihārasahassāni kāretvā ahaṃ na dāyādo, añño ko dāyādoti? Paccayadāyako nāma tvaṃ mahārāja, yo pana attano puttañca dhītarañca pabbājeti, ayaṃ sāsane dāyādo nāmāti. So puttañca dhītarañca pabbājesi. Atha naṃ therā āhaṃsu – ‘‘idāni, mahārāja, sāsane dāyādosī’’ti.

Evametaṃbhūtapubbanti evaṃ etaṃ atīte dhātunidhānampi jambudīpatale bhūtapubbanti. Tatiyasaṅgītikārāpi imaṃ padaṃ ṭhapayiṃsu.

Evametaṃ bhūtapubba

Aṭṭhadoṇaṃ cakkhumato sarīrantiādigāthāyo pana tambapaṇṇidīpe therehi vuttāti.

Aṭṭhadoṇaṃ cakkhumato sarīra

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Mahāparinibbānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
240. “*Evametaṃ bhūtapubba*nti:* thus it was in the past.” Thus, in *Jambudvīpa*, there was a vessel for relics and also the requisites for ten *stūpas*. So said the compilers of the *Sangīti* later on.

In this way, when the *stūpas* had been established, Mahākassapa, seeing danger to the relics, approached King Ajātasattu and said, “Great King, it is fitting to make one deposit for the relics.”

“Good, venerable sir, let the act of depositing the relics be mine for now, but how shall I bring the remaining relics?” “No, Great King, the bringing of the relics is your burden, [it is] our burden.”

“Good, venerable sir, you bring the relics, I shall make a deposit for the relics.”

The elder, having left only the service of those royal families, brought the remaining relics.

But at Rāmagāma, the Nāgas took possession of the relics; there was no danger to them.

“In the future, they will deposit [them] in the great *vihāra* in the island of Laṅkā in the great *cetiya*." Not having brought them there, having brought [them] from the remaining seven cities, having stood in the eastern-southern direction of Rājagaha, he made a resolution: “May this stone in this place disappear, may the dust be very pure, may water not rise up."

The king, having had that place dug, then, having had bricks made with the dust that was lifted up, had *cetiyas* made for eighty great disciples.

“What is the king having made here?” Even to those who asked, they say, “*Cetiyas* for the great disciples.” No one knows the state of the relic deposit.

When that place, eighty cubits deep, had been prepared, having had a metal layer spread out below, having had a house made there in the *stūpa* garden, the size of a *cetiya* house, made of copper metal, he had eight sets of reliquaries and *stūpas* made of fragrant sandalwood, etc.

Then, having placed the relics of the Blessed One in a sandalwood reliquary, he placed that sandalwood reliquary also in another sandalwood reliquary, and that one also in another. In this way, having put together eight sandalwood reliquaries, by this very means, he placed those eight reliquaries in eight sandalwood *stūpas*, [and] eight sandalwood *stūpas* in eight *lohitacandana* reliquaries, [and] eight *lohitacandana* reliquaries in eight *lohitacandana* *stūpas*, [and] eight *lohitacandana* *stūpas* in eight ivory reliquaries, eight ivory reliquaries in eight ivory *stūpas*, eight ivory *stūpas* in eight reliquaries of all jewels, eight reliquaries of all jewels in eight *stūpas* of all jewels, eight *stūpas* of all jewels in eight gold reliquaries, eight gold reliquaries, [and] eight gold *stūpas*, eight gold *stūpas* in eight silver reliquaries, eight silver reliquaries in eight silver *stūpas*, eight silver *stūpas*, [and] eight jewel reliquaries, eight jewel reliquaries in eight jewel *stūpas*, eight jewel *stūpas* in eight *lohitaṅka* reliquaries, eight *lohitaṅka* reliquaries in eight *lohitaṅka* *stūpas*, [and] eight *lohitaṅka* *stūpas* in eight *masāragalla* reliquaries, eight *masāragalla* reliquaries in eight *masāragalla* *stūpas*, [and] eight *masāragalla* *stūpas* in eight crystal reliquaries, [and] eight crystal reliquaries in eight *stūpas* made of crystal.

The uppermost crystal *cetiya* of all was the size of a *stūpa* garden *cetiya*. Above that, he had a house made of all jewels, above that one of gold, above that one of silver, [and] above that a house of copper metal.

There, having scattered sand made of all jewels, having scattered thousands of water-born and land-born flowers, [and] two and a half *jātaka* centuries, [and the images of] eighty great elders, King Śuddhodana, Mahāmāyādevī, [and] the seven co-nascent ones, he had all these made of gold.

He had five sets of five hundred gold and silver, full water-jars placed, [and] five sets of five hundred gold flags raised.

Having had five hundred gold lamps and five hundred silver lamps made, having filled [them] with fragrant oil, he placed wicks of *dukūla* cloth in them.

Then venerable Mahākassapa, having resolved: “May the garlands not fade, may the fragrances not perish, may the lamps not be extinguished,” had letters carved on a gold plate:

“In the future, a youth named Piyadāsa, having raised an umbrella, will become a righteous king named Aśoka.

He will cause these relics to be widely distributed.”

The king, having worshiped [the relics] with all adornments, went out, closing the door from the beginning. Having closed that copper metal door, and having tied a key-ring to the opening rope, having placed a large jewel mass there, he had a letter carved: “In the future, a poor king, having taken this jewel, should make an offering to the relics.”

Sakko, the king of the gods, having addressed Vissakamma: “Dear Vissakamma, a relic deposit has been made by Ajātasattu; establish protection here,” sent [him].

Having come, he joined a valve that makes a clanging sound; having taken wooden figures, in that relic chamber, to a crystal-colored sword, having joined a machine that goes around with a speed like the wind, and having fastened [it] with a single pin, having made a stone enclosure on all sides in the shape of a *giñjakāvasatha*, and having covered [it] with a single [stone] on top, having poured dust, having made the ground even, he established a stone *stūpa* above that.

When the relic deposit had been completed in this way, having lived for their entire life span, the elder also was completely extinguished, the king also went according to his *karma*, [and] those people also died.

In a later time, a youth named Piyadāsa, having raised an umbrella, having become a righteous king named Aśoka, took those relics and caused [them] to be widely distributed in *Jambudvīpa*.

How [did he do that]? Relying on the *sāmaṇera* Nigrodha, having gained faith in the dispensation, having had eighty-four thousand *vihāras* made, he asked the *bhikkhu* *saṃgha*: “Venerable sirs, eighty-four thousand *vihāras* have been made by me; from where shall I obtain relics?” “Great King, we hear that there is such a thing as a relic deposit, but it is not known where it is located."

The king, having had a *cetiya* broken up in Rājagaha, not seeing the relics, having had a *paṭipākatika* made, having taken the four assemblies—*bhikkhus*, *bhikkhunīs*, male lay followers, [and] female lay followers—went to Vesālī.

Not finding [them] there either, [he went] to Kapilavatthu.

Not finding [them] there either, he went to Rāmagāma.

At Rāmagāma, the Nāgas did not allow [him] to break up the *cetiya*; the hammer that fell on the *cetiya* broke into pieces.
Thus, even there, not obtaining Allakappa, Veṭhadīpa, Pāvā, Kusināra, having broken the *cetiya*s everywhere, not obtaining any relics, having made (them) *paṭipākatika*, again going to Rājagaha, having convened the four assemblies, (he) asked – “Has it ever been heard by anyone, ‘At such-and-such a place, there is a deposit of relics’?”

There, one *thera*, one hundred and twenty years old – “At such-and-such a place, there is a deposit of relics,” I do not know. But my father, a great *thera*, when I was seven years old, having had (me) take a garland basket – “Come, *sāmaṇera*, in such-and-such a grove-interval, there is a stone *thūpa*."

"There is, let us go there,” having gone, having worshipped – “This place is fit to be remembered, *sāmaṇera*,” he said.
“I know only this much, great king,” he said.
The king said, “This is the very place,”

having said (this), having gone to the site, having had (them) remove the stone *thūpa* and the dust, he saw a lime-covered ground below.
Then, having had the lime and the bricks removed, gradually descending into the enclosure, he saw sand of seven jewels, sword-handles, and wood-figures that revolved.
