There, *abhirūpā*: because she has more beauty through the completeness of (her) build. *dassanīyā*: because, when being looked at, she pleases the eyes; therefore, (she) should be looked at even after abandoning other distracting business. *pāsādikā*: because, when being looked at, she gladdens the mind through (the quality of) delight. *paramāya*: thus, because she brings about delight, (she is) excellent. *vaṇṇapokkharatāyā*: by beauty of complexion. *samannāgatā*: endowed. *abhirūpā*: because she is neither too tall nor too short. *dassanīyā*: because she is neither too thin nor too fat. *pāsādikā*: because she is neither too dark nor too fair. *paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā*: because she has surpassed human complexion (and) has attained divine complexion. For the aura of humans does not radiate outwards. But the aura of gods radiates even very far.

*abhirūpā. dassanīyā. pāsādikā. paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāyā samannāgatā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā*

However, her bodily aura illuminates an area measuring twelve cubits. And in *nātidīghādīsu*, by the first pair, excellence of height is stated; by the second pair, excellence of girth; by the third pair, excellence of complexion is stated. Or even by these six, the absence of bodily misfortune (is stated); by *atikkantā mānusivaṇṇa* (surpassed human complexion), bodily accomplishment is stated. *tūlapicuno vā kappāsapicuno*: either cotton wool or cotton wool that has been put in ghee and kept, (and) that has been struck a hundred times. *sīte*: in the king’s cold season. *uṇhe*: in the king’s hot season. *candanagandho*: always, the scent of freshly ground *haricandana* sandalwood, combined from four kinds (of sandalwood), wafts from (her) body. *uppalagandho vāyatī*: at the time of laughing and speaking, the very fragrant scent of a blue lotus (*nīluppala*) that has just blossomed wafts from (her) mouth.

*atikkantā mānusivaṇṇa tūlapicuno vā kappāsapicuno sīte uṇhe candanagandho uppalagandho vāyatī*

However, in order to show conduct conforming to her bodily accomplishment, thus endowed with excellence of beauty, touch, and scent, *taṃ kho panā* etc. was said. There, having seen the king, she gets up from her seat first, as if burnt by fire: *pubbuṭṭhāyinī*. When he is seated, having done the business of fanning etc. with a palm-leaf fan, she afterwards lies down (or) sits down: *pacchānipātinī*. "What shall I do, sire?"—she replies to the question "What (shall I do)?" with that speech: *kiṃ kārapaṭissāvinī*. She behaves and acts only in a way pleasing to the king: *manāpacārinī*. She speaks only that which is dear to the king: *piyavādinī*.

*taṃ kho panā pubbuṭṭhāyinī.*
Following closely behind.
What is the cause of the response?
Not causing harm to the mind.
Speaking pleasantly.

Now – to show that "her own conduct is pure in nature, not deceitful," etc., he begins with "taṃ kho panā," etc.
There, "*no aticarī*" means not transgressing, but behaving [properly]; it means that, except for the king, she did not desire any other man even in her thoughts.

"*taṃ kho panā no aticarī*" There, those qualities of her that were mentioned at the beginning, such as "beautiful," etc., and at the end, such as "getting up early," etc., those are natural qualities.
Furthermore, it should be understood that qualities such as "surpassing human complexion," etc., arise in a *cakravartin* based on merit, starting from the appearance of the *cakra-ratna*, through the influence of prior actions.

Moreover, beauty and so forth are fully perfected in all ways from the appearance of the *cakra-ratna*.
Therefore, he says, "Such a jewel of a woman appeared."

Explanation of the Jewel of a Householder.

mula_pali:
250. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa gahapatiratanaṃ pāturahosi. Tassa kammavipākajaṃ dibbacakkhu pāturahosi yena nidhiṃ passati sassāmikampi assāmikampi. So rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘appossukko tvaṃ, deva, hohi, ahaṃ te dhanena dhanakaraṇīyaṃ karissāmī’ti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tameva gahapatiratanaṃ vīmaṃsamāno nāvaṃ abhiruhitvā majjhe gaṅgāya nadiyā sotaṃ ogāhitvā gahapatiratanaṃ etadavoca – ‘attho me, gahapati, hiraññasuvaṇṇenā’ti. ‘Tena hi, mahārāja, ekaṃ tīraṃ nāvā upetū’ti. ‘Idheva me, gahapati, attho hiraññasuvaṇṇenā’ti. Atha kho taṃ, ānanda, gahapatiratanaṃ ubhohi hatthehi udakaṃ omasitvā pūraṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa kumbhiṃ uddharitvā rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ etadavoca – ‘alamettāvatā mahārāja, katamettāvatā mahārāja, pūjitamettāvatā mahārājā’ti? Rājā mahāsudassano evamāha – ‘alamettāvatā gahapati, katamettāvatā gahapati, pūjitamettāvatā gahapatī’ti. Rañño , ānanda, mahāsudassanassa evarūpaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pāturahosi.

Pariṇāyakaratanaṃ
mula_english:
‘Furthermore, Ānanda, the Householder-Treasure (*gṛhapatiratna*) appeared to King Mahāsudassana.

With the divine eye (*divyacakṣu*) born of past action (*karmavipākaja*), he saw where treasure (*nidhi*), owned (*sassāmika*) and ownerless (*assāmika*), was hidden.

He approached the King Mahāsudassana and said: “Have no anxiety, Your Majesty, I will manage your wealth properly.”

Once, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana, testing that very Householder-Treasure, boarded a ship and had it taken to the current in the middle of the Ganges River. Then he said to the Householder-Treasure: “Householder, I need gold coins (*hiraṇyasuvarṇa*)!”

“Well then, great king (*mahārāja*), let the ship be brought to one bank.”

“I need the gold coins (*hiraṇyasuvarṇa*) right here, householder!”

Then, Ānanda, that Householder-Treasure, touching the water with both hands, drew out a vessel filled with gold coins (*hiraṇyasuvarṇa*), and said to King Mahāsudassana: “Is that enough, great king (*mahārāja*)? Is that sufficient, great king (*mahārāja*)? Are you satisfied, great king (*mahārāja*)?” King Mahāsudassana said: “That is enough, householder, that is sufficient, householder, I am satisfied, householder.”

And that is how, Ānanda, such a Householder-Treasure (*gṛhapatiratna*) appeared to King Mahāsudassana.

The Counselor-Treasure (*pariṇāyakaratna*).
commentary_pali:
250. Evaṃ pātubhūtaitthiratanassa pana rañño cakkavattino dhanakaraṇīyānaṃ kiccānaṃ yathāsukhaṃ pavattanatthaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pātubhavati. So pakatiyāva mahābhogo, mahābhogakule jāto. Rañño dhanarāsivaḍḍhako seṭṭhigahapati hoti. Cakkaratanānubhāvasahitaṃ panassa kammavipākajaṃ dibbacakkhu pātubhavati, yena antopathaviyampi yojanabbhantare nidhiṃ passati, so taṃ sampattiṃ disvā tuṭṭhamānaso gantvā rājānaṃ dhanena pavāretvā sabbāni dhanakaraṇīyāni sampādeti . Mahāsudassanassāpi tatheva sampādesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘puna caparaṃ ānanda…pe… evarūpaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pāturahosī’’ti.

Pariṇāyakaratanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Thus, for a king, a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin), when the jewel of a treasurer (gahapati-ratana) appears, it is for the successful accomplishment of tasks relating to the management of wealth.

He is by nature very wealthy, born into a very wealthy family. He is a wealthy householder (seṭṭhi-gahapati) who increases the king's treasury. Along with the power of the wheel jewel (cakra-ratana), a divine eye (dibba-cakkhu) born of his karma appears, by which he sees treasures even under the earth within a league. Seeing that wealth, with a delighted mind, he goes and enriches the king with wealth, and accomplishes all tasks relating to wealth. He accomplished it similarly for Mahāsudassana as well. Therefore, it was said: "Again, Ānanda...pe... such a jewel of a treasurer appeared."

Description of the jewel of a leader (pariṇāyaka-ratana).

mula_pali:
251. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa pariṇāyakaratanaṃ pāturahosi paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī paṭibalo rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upayāpetabbaṃ upayāpetuṃ, apayāpetabbaṃ apayāpetuṃ, ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetuṃ. So rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘appossukko tvaṃ, deva, hohi, ahamanusāsissāmī’ti. Rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa evarūpaṃ pariṇāyakaratanaṃ pāturahosi.

‘‘Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imehi sattahi ratanehi samannāgato ahosi.

Catuiddhisamannāgato
mula_english:
Again, Ānanda, the Counsellor- Jewel (*pariṇāyakaratana*) appeared to King Mahāsudassana, a wise, learned, intelligent, and capable advisor to King Mahāsudassana, who could bring him what should be brought, remove what should be removed, and establish what should be established. He approached King Mahāsudassana and said: ‘Have no fear, Your Majesty (*deva*), I will instruct you.’

Again, Ānanda, such a Counsellor-Jewel (*pariṇāyakaratana*) appeared to King Mahāsudassana.

King Mahāsudassana, Ānanda, possessed these seven jewels (*ratanehi*).

Possessing the four kinds of spiritual power (*catuiddhisamannāgato*).
commentary_pali:
251. Evaṃ pātubhūtagahapatiratanassa pana rañño cakkavattissa sabbakiccasaṃvidhānasamatthaṃ pariṇāyakaratanaṃ pātubhavati. So rañño jeṭṭhaputtova hoti. Pakatiyā eva so paṇḍito byatto medhāvī vibhāvī. Rañño puññānubhāvaṃ nissāya panassa attano kammānubhāvena paracittañāṇaṃ uppajjati. Yena dvādasayojanāya rājaparisāya cittācāraṃ ñatvā rañño hite ca ahite ca vavatthapetuṃ samattho hoti, sopi taṃ attano ānubhāvaṃ disvā tuṭṭhahadayo rājānaṃ sabbakiccānusāsanena pavāreti. Mahāsudassanampi tatheva pavāresi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘puna caparaṃ…pe… pariṇāyakaratanaṃ pāturahosī’’ti.

Tattha ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetunti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhānantare ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetuṃ.

ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetu

Catuiddhisamannāgatavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Thus, for a king, a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*), there arises a householder-gem (*gahapatiratanassa*) who is capable of managing all affairs, a counselor-gem (*pariṇāyakaratanaṃ*) who has manifested. He is the king's eldest son, naturally wise, learned, intelligent, and discerning. Relying on the king's meritorious power (*puññānubhāvaṃ*), he develops the ability to know the minds of others (*paracittañāṇaṃ*) through his own karmic power (*kammānubhāvena*). By this, knowing the conduct of the minds of the royal assembly within twelve *yojanas*, he is capable of determining what is beneficial and harmful to the king. He, too, seeing that power of his own, with a delighted heart, invites the king with advice on all matters. Mahāsudassana also invited him in the same way. Therefore, it was said, "Again, furthermore... the counselor-gem appeared."

There, *ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetu* means to place what should be placed in that particular location.

*ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetu*

Explanation of the possession of the four kinds of success (*catuiddhisamannāgatavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
252. ‘‘Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano catūhi iddhīhi samannāgato ahosi. Katamāhi catūhi iddhīhi? Idhānanda, rājā mahāsudassano abhirūpo ahosi dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato ativiya aññehi manussehi. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imāya paṭhamāya iddhiyā samannāgato ahosi.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano dīghāyuko ahosi ciraṭṭhitiko ativiya aññehi manussehi. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imāya dutiyāya iddhiyā samannāgato ahosi.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano appābādho ahosi appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya ativiya aññehi manussehi. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imāya tatiyāya iddhiyā samannāgato ahosi.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ , ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ piyo ahosi manāpo. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, pitā puttānaṃ piyo hoti manāpo, evameva kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ piyo ahosi manāpo. Raññopi, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa brāhmaṇagahapatikā piyā ahesuṃ manāpā. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, pitu puttā piyā honti manāpā, evameva kho, ānanda, raññopi mahāsudassanassa brāhmaṇagahapatikā piyā ahesuṃ manāpā.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano caturaṅginiyā senāya uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyāsi. Atha kho, ānanda, brāhmaṇagahapatikā rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ataramāno, deva, yāhi, yathā taṃ mayaṃ cirataraṃ passeyyāmā’ti. Rājāpi, ānanda, mahāsudassano sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘ataramāno, sārathi, rathaṃ pesehi, yathā ahaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatike cirataraṃ passeyya’nti. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imāya catutthiyā catutthāya (syā.) iddhiyā samannāgato ahosi. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano imāhi catūhi iddhīhi samannāgato ahosi.

catutthāya (syā.)

Dhammapāsādapokkharaṇī
mula_english:
252. Again, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was endowed with four powers (*ṛddhi*).

What are the four powers? Here, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was handsome, good to look at, pleasing, possessing the fairest complexion, surpassing other men. King Mahāsudassana was endowed with this first power.

Furthermore, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was long-lived, enduring longer than other men. King Mahāsudassana was endowed with this second power.

Furthermore, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was free from illness, free from sickness, possessing a healthy digestion, less subject to cold and heat than other men. King Mahāsudassana was endowed with this third power.

Furthermore, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was loved and liked by *brāhmaṇas* and householders (*gṛhapati*). Just as a father is loved and liked by his children, so too, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was loved and liked by *brāhmaṇas* and householders. Ānanda, the *brāhmaṇas* and householders were loved and liked by King Mahāsudassana. Just as children are loved and liked by their father, so too, Ānanda, the *brāhmaṇas* and householders were loved and liked by King Mahāsudassana.

Once, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana went to the pleasure park with his fourfold army (*caturaṅginī senā*). Then, Ānanda, the *brāhmaṇas* and householders approached King Mahāsudassana and said, ‘O King, go slowly, so that we may see you for a longer time.’

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana said to the charioteer, ‘Charioteer, drive the chariot slowly, so that I may see the *brāhmaṇas* and householders for a longer time.’

King Mahāsudassana was endowed with this fourth power. King Mahāsudassana was endowed with these four powers.

The Dharma-palace-pond. (*dharmapāsādapokkharaṇī*)
commentary_pali:
252.Samavepākiniyāti samavipācaniyā. Gahaṇiyāti kammajatejodhātuyā. Tattha yassa bhuttamattova āhāro jīrati, yassa vā pana puṭabhattaṃ viya tattheva tiṭṭhati, ubhopete na samavepākiniyā samannāgatā. Yassa pana puna bhattakāle bhattachando uppajjateva, ayaṃ samavepākiniyā samannāgatoti.

Dhammapāsādapokkharaṇivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
" *Samavepākinīyā* " means *samavipācanīyā*.

" *Gahaṇīyā* " means *kammajatejodhātuyā*.

There, for whomever food is digested immediately after being eaten, or for whomever it remains there like food in a container, both of these are not endowed with *samavepākinī*.

But for whomever a desire for food arises at mealtime, this one is endowed with *samavepākinī*.

Description of the *dhammapāsādapokkharaṇī*.

mula_pali:
253. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāsu tālantarikāsu dhanusate dhanusate pokkharaṇiyo māpeyya’nti.

‘‘Māpesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tāsu tālantarikāsu dhanusate dhanusate pokkharaṇiyo. Tā kho panānanda, pokkharaṇiyo catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ iṭṭhakāhi citā ahesuṃ – ekā iṭṭhakā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā, ekā veḷuriyamayā, ekā phalikamayā.

‘‘Tāsu kho panānanda, pokkharaṇīsu cattāri cattāri sopānāni ahesuṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ, ekaṃ sopānaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ ekaṃ veḷuriyamayaṃ ekaṃ phalikamayaṃ. Sovaṇṇamayassa sopānassa sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayassa sopānassa rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Veḷuriyamayassa sopānassa veḷuriyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, phalikamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Phalikamayassa sopānassa phalikamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, veḷuriyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Tā kho panānanda, pokkharaṇiyo dvīhi vedikāhi parikkhittā ahesuṃ ekā vedikā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā. Sovaṇṇamayāya vedikāya sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayāya vedikāya rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Atha kho, ānanda , rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāsu pokkharaṇīsu evarūpaṃ mālaṃ ropāpeyyaṃ uppalaṃ padumaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sabbotukaṃ sabbajanassa anāvaṭa’nti. Ropāpesi kho , ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tāsu pokkharaṇīsu evarūpaṃ mālaṃ uppalaṃ padumaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sabbotukaṃ sabbajanassa anāvaṭaṃ.
mula_english:
253. Then, Ānanda, it occurred to King Mahāsudassana: ‘Suppose I were to construct lotus ponds (*pokkharaṇiyo*) between the palm trees, a hundred bow-lengths apart.’

‘King Mahāsudassana then constructed lotus ponds between the palm trees, a hundred bow-lengths apart.

Those lotus ponds, Ānanda, were lined with four-colored bricks: one brick of gold (*sovaṇṇamayā*), one of silver (*rūpiyamayā*), one of beryl (*veḷuriyamayā*), and one of crystal (*phalikamayā*).

Those lotus ponds, Ānanda, each had four staircases of four colors: one staircase of gold (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ*), one of silver (*rūpiyamayaṃ*), one of beryl (*veḷuriyamayaṃ*), and one of crystal (*phalikamayaṃ*).

The gold staircase had gold posts (*thambhā*), with silver railings (*sūciyo*) and banisters (*uṇhīsañca*). The silver staircase had silver posts, with gold railings and banisters. The beryl staircase had beryl posts, with crystal railings and banisters. The crystal staircase had crystal posts, with beryl railings and banisters.

Those lotus ponds, Ānanda, were surrounded by two parapets (*vedikāhi*), one of gold (*sovaṇṇamayā*) and one of silver (*rūpiyamayā*). The gold parapet (*vedikā*) had gold posts (*thambhā*), with silver railings (*sūciyo*) and banisters (*uṇhīsañca*). The silver parapet had silver posts, with gold railings and banisters.

Then, Ānanda, it occurred to King Mahāsudassana: ‘Suppose I were to plant in these lotus ponds such garlands (*mālaṃ*) of blue lotuses (*uppalaṃ*), red lotuses (*padumaṃ*), white lotuses (*kumudaṃ*), and white water lilies (*puṇḍarīkaṃ*) that would last through all seasons (*sabbotukaṃ*) and be accessible (*anāvaṭa’nti*) to everyone (*sabbajanassa*)?’

King Mahāsudassana then planted in those lotus ponds such garlands of blue lotuses, red lotuses, white lotuses and white water lilies that would last through all seasons and be accessible to everyone.
commentary_pali: 253.Māpesi khoti nagare bheriṃ carāpetvā janarāsiṃ kāretvā na māpesi, rañño pana saha cittuppādeneva bhūmiṃ bhinditvā caturāsīti pokkharaṇīsahassāni nibbattiṃsu. Tāni sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Dvīhi vedikāhīti ekāya iṭṭhakānaṃ pariyanteyeva parikkhittā ekāya pariveṇaparicchedapariyante. Etadahosīti kasmā ahosi? Ekadivasaṃ kira nahatvā ca pivitvā ca gacchantaṃ mahājanaṃ mahāpuriso oloketvā ime ummattakaveseneva gacchanti. Sace etesaṃ ettha piḷandhanapupphāni bhaveyyuṃ, bhaddakaṃ siyāti. Athassa etadahosi. Tattha sabbotukanti pupphaṃ nāma ekasmiṃyeva utumhi pupphati. Ahaṃ pana tathā karissāmi – ‘‘yathā sabbesu utūsu pupphissatī’’ti cintesiṃ. Ropāpesīti nānāvaṇṇauppalabījādīni tato tato āharāpetvā na ropāpesi, saha cittuppādeneva panassa sabbaṃ ijjhati. Taṃ loko raññā ropitanti maññi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘ropāpesī’’ti. Tato paṭṭhāya mahājano nānappakāraṃ jalajathalajamālaṃ piḷandhitvā nakkhattaṃ kīḷamāno viya gacchati.
commentary_english:
253. "Because he caused to be measured (māpesi kho)," he did not cause to be measured by having a town crier circulate with a drum and assemble the people. But for the king, with the arising of the mind itself, splitting the earth, eighty-four thousand lotus ponds (caturaśīti pokkharaṇīsahassāni) sprang up.

This was said with reference to that.

"With two vedikās (dvīhi vedikāhī)," [means:] by one, they were enclosed just at the edge of the bricks; by the other, at the limit of the enclosure’s boundary.

"This occurred to him (etadahosī)," why did it occur? One day, the great being (mahāpuriso), having looked upon a great crowd (mahājanaṃ) going along, having bathed and drunk, [thought:] "These go along just like those in the guise of madmen."

If there should be flowers for their adornment here, it would be good.

Then this occurred to him.

There, "all-seasonal (sabbotuka)" means a flower is named [that] blossoms in only one season.

But I will do thus – "Just as it will blossom in all seasons (yathā sabbesu utūsu pupphissatī)," he thought.

"He caused to be planted (ropāpesī)," he did not cause to be planted by fetching seeds etc. of various kinds of lotuses from here and there, but with the arising of the mind itself, everything succeeded for him.

The world thought that it was planted by the king.

Therefore it was said – "He caused to be planted (ropāpesī)."

From then on, the great crowd, having adorned themselves with various kinds of water- and land-born garlands (jalajathalajamālaṃ), playing at the festival (nakkhattaṃ kīḷamāno), goes along as if….

mula_pali:
254. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāsaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ tīre nhāpake purise ṭhapeyyaṃ, ye āgatāgataṃ janaṃ nhāpessantī’ti. Ṭhapesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tāsaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ tīre nhāpake purise, ye āgatāgataṃ janaṃ nhāpesuṃ.

‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāsaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ tīre evarūpaṃ dānaṃ paṭṭhapeyyaṃ – annaṃ annaṭṭhikassa annatthitassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), evaṃ sabbattha pakabhirūpeneva dissati, pānaṃ pānaṭṭhikassa, vatthaṃ vatthaṭṭhikassa, yānaṃ yānaṭṭhikassa, sayanaṃ sayanaṭṭhikassa, itthiṃ itthiṭṭhikassa, hiraññaṃ hiraññaṭṭhikassa, suvaṇṇaṃ suvaṇṇaṭṭhikassā’ti. Paṭṭhapesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tāsaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ tīre evarūpaṃ dānaṃ – annaṃ annaṭṭhikassa, pānaṃ pānaṭṭhikassa, vatthaṃ vatthaṭṭhikassa, yānaṃ yānaṭṭhikassa, sayanaṃ sayanaṭṭhikassa, itthiṃ itthiṭṭhikassa, hiraññaṃ hiraññaṭṭhikassa, suvaṇṇaṃ suvaṇṇaṭṭhikassa.

annatthitassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), evaṃ sabbattha pakabhirūpeneva dissati
mula_english:
Then, Ānanda, it occurred to King Mahāsudassana: “Suppose I were to place bathmen on the banks of these ponds, to bathe those who come there?”

And he did place bathmen on the banks of those ponds, Ānanda, and they bathed those who came there.

Then, Ānanda, it occurred to King Mahāsudassana: “Suppose I were to establish charitable posts on the banks of these ponds, so that those who want food can get food (*annaṃ annaṭṭhikassa*), those who want drink can get drink (*pānaṃ pānaṭṭhikassa*), those who want clothes can get clothes (*vatthaṃ vatthaṭṭhikassa*), those who want transport can get transport (*yānaṃ yānaṭṭhikassa*), those who want a sleeping-place can get a sleeping-place (*sayanaṃ sayanaṭṭhikassa*), those who want a wife can get a wife (*itthiṃ itthiṭṭhikassa*), and those who want gold coin can get gold coin (*hiraññaṃ hiraññaṭṭhikassa, suvaṇṇaṃ suvaṇṇaṭṭhikassa*)?”

And he did establish such charitable posts on the banks of those ponds, Ānanda: food for those who want food (*annaṃ annaṭṭhikassa*), drink for those who want drink (*pānaṃ pānaṭṭhikassa*), clothes for those who want clothes (*vatthaṃ vatthaṭṭhikassa*), transport for those who want transport (*yānaṃ yānaṭṭhikassa*), a sleeping-place for those who want a sleeping-place (*sayanaṃ sayanaṭṭhikassa*), a wife for those who want a wife (*itthiṃ itthiṭṭhikassa*), gold coin for those who want gold coin (*hiraññaṃ hiraññaṭṭhikassa*), and gold for those who want gold (*suvaṇṇaṃ suvaṇṇaṭṭhikassa*).
commentary_pali:
254. Atha rājā tato uttaripi janaṃ sukhasamappitaṃ kātukāmo – ‘‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāsaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ tīre’’tiādinā janassa sukhavidhānaṃ cintetvā sabbaṃ akāsi. Tattha nhāpesunti añño sarīraṃ ubbaṭṭesi, añño cuṇṇāni yojesi, añño tīre nahāyantassa udakaṃ āhari, añño vatthāni paṭiggahesi ceva adāsi ca.

Paṭṭhapesi khoti kathaṃ paṭṭhapesi? Itthīnañca purisānañca anucchavike alaṅkāre kāretvā itthimattameva tattha paricāravasena sesaṃ sabbaṃ pariccāgavasena ṭhapetvā rājā mahāsudassano dānaṃ deti, taṃ paribhuñjathāti bheriṃ carāpesi. Mahājano pokkharaṇītīraṃ āgantvā nahatvā vatthāni parivattetvā nānāgandhehi vilitto piḷandhanavicittamālo dānaggaṃ gantvā anekappakāresu yāgubhattakhajjakesu aṭṭhavidhapānesu ca yo yaṃ icchati, so taṃ khāditvā ca pivitvā ca nānāvaṇṇāni khomasukhumāni vatthāni nivāsetvā sampattiṃ anubhavitvā yesaṃ tādisāni atthi, te ohāya gacchanti. Yesaṃ pana natthi, te gahetvā gacchanti. Hatthiassayānādīsupi nisīditvā thokaṃ vicaritvā anatthikā ohāya, atthikā gahetvā gacchanti. Varasayanesu nipajjitvā sampattiṃ anubhavitvā anatthikā ohāya, atthikā gahetvā gacchanti. Itthīhipi saddhiṃ sampattiṃ anubhavitvā anatthikā ohāya, atthikā gahetvā gacchanti. Sattavidharatanapasādhanāni ca pasādhetvāpi sampattiṃ anubhavitvā anatthikā ohāya, atthikā gahetvā gacchanti. Tampi dānaṃ uṭṭhāya samuṭṭhāya dīyateva. Jambudīpavāsikānaṃ aññaṃ kammaṃ natthi, rañño dānaṃ paribhuñjantāva vicaranti.

Paṭṭhapesi kho
commentary_english:
254. Then the king, desiring to bring happiness to the people even further, thinking about how to provide happiness for the people with things like, "I should [do something] on the bank of these lotus ponds," did everything.

There, the *nhāpesu*, one person scrubbed the body, another mixed the powders, another brought water to the one bathing on the bank, another accepted and gave clothes.

How did he establish it? Having made unsuitable decorations for the women and men, keeping only the women there for service, and setting aside everything else for relinquishment, King Mahāsudassana gave a donation, proclaiming, "Enjoy this!" with a drum.

The great mass of people, having come to the bank of the lotus pond, having bathed, having changed clothes, anointed with various fragrances, adorned with garlands of various ornaments, having gone to the place of giving, whatever one desired among the various kinds of gruel, rice, snacks, and eight kinds of drinks, having eaten and drunk that, having put on clothes of various colors, fine linen, having experienced prosperity, those for whom such things existed, they left, abandoning them.

But those for whom [such things] did not exist, they took [them] and left.

Having sat on elephants, horses, chariots, and so on, having wandered around a bit, those without need left, abandoning [them], those with need took [them] and left.

Having lain down on excellent beds, having experienced prosperity, those without need left, abandoning [them], those with need took [them] and left.

Even with women, having experienced prosperity together, those without need left, abandoning [them], those with need took [them] and left.

Having prepared the seven kinds of jewel ornaments, and even having adorned [themselves], having experienced prosperity, those without need left, abandoning [them], those with need took [them] and left.

That donation was given rising up and rising up again.

There was no other work for the inhabitants of Jambudvīpa; they wandered around only enjoying the king's donation.

mula_pali: 255. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, brāhmaṇagahapatikā pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ ādāya rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘idaṃ, deva, pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ devaññeva uddissa ābhataṃ, taṃ devo paṭiggaṇhatū’ti. ‘Alaṃ bho, mamapidaṃ pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ dhammikena balinā abhisaṅkhataṃ, tañca vo hotu, ito ca bhiyyo harathā’ti. Te raññā paṭikkhittā ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘na kho etaṃ amhākaṃ patirūpaṃ, yaṃ mayaṃ imāni sāpateyyāni punadeva sakāni gharāni paṭihareyyāma. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ rañño mahāsudassanassa nivesanaṃ māpeyyāmā’ti. Te rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘nivesanaṃ te deva, māpessāmā’ti. Adhivāsesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
Then:

‘‘Then, Ānanda, the Brahman householders, taking abundant wealth (*sāpateyya*), approached King Mahāsudassana and said: ‘This, O King, is abundant wealth (*sāpateyya*) brought for the king's sake; may the king accept it.’"

“Enough, friends, I have enough wealth (*sāpateyya*) collected by righteous revenues; let this be yours, and take away even more than this!”

Being refused by the king (*rājan*), they withdrew to one side and considered: “It is not right for us to take these riches (*sāpateyya*) back to our own homes. Suppose we were to build a dwelling (*nivesana*) for King Mahāsudassana.”

They approached King Mahāsudassana and said: “We will build a dwelling (*nivesana*) for you, O King.”

King Mahāsudassana assented in silence, Ānanda.
commentary_pali: 255. Atha brāhmaṇagahapatikā cintesuṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ rājā evarūpaṃ dānaṃ dadantopi ‘mayhaṃ taṇḍulādīni vā khīrādīni vā dethā’ti na kiñci āharāpeti, na kho pana amhākaṃ – ‘rājā āharāpetī’ti tuṇhīmāsituṃ patirūpa’’nti te bahuṃ sāpateyyaṃ saṃharitvā rañño upanāmesuṃ. Tasmā – ‘‘atha kho, ānanda, brāhmaṇagahapatikā’’tiādimāha. Evaṃ samacintesunti kasmā evaṃ cintesuṃ? Kassaci gharato appaṃ ābhataṃ, kassaci bahu. Tasmiṃ paṭisaṃhariyamāne – ‘‘kiṃ taveva gharato sundaraṃ ābhataṃ, na mayhaṃ gharato, kiṃ taveva gharato bahu , na mayha’’nti evaṃ kalahasaddopi uppajjeyya, so mā uppajjitthāti evaṃ samacintesuṃ.
commentary_english:
Then the *brāhmaṇa* householders thought, “This king, even while giving such a gift, does not ask for anything, saying, ‘Give me rice and milk, etc.’ It is not fitting for us to remain silent, [thinking,] ‘The king will ask.’” So, having collected much property, they offered it to the king.

Therefore, he said, “Then, Ānanda, the *brāhmaṇa* householders, etc.”

*evaṃ samacintesuṃ*: Why did they think thus? Someone brought a little from home, someone brought a lot.

While that was being given back – “What, was something beautiful brought from your house, not from my house? What, was a lot brought from your house, not from mine?” – thus, even the sound of quarreling might arise. So, they considered thus: “Let that not arise!”

mula_pali:
256. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, sakko devānamindo rañño mahāsudassanassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya vissakammaṃ visukammaṃ (ka.) devaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma vissakamma, rañño mahāsudassanassa nivesanaṃ māpehi dhammaṃ nāma pāsāda’nti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, ānanda, vissakammo devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva devesu tāvatiṃsesu antarahito rañño mahāsudassanassa purato pāturahosi. Atha kho, ānanda, vissakammo devaputto rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ etadavoca – ‘nivesanaṃ te deva, māpessāmi dhammaṃ nāma pāsāda’nti. Adhivāsesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano tuṇhībhāvena.

‘‘Māpesi kho, ānanda, vissakammo devaputto rañño mahāsudassanassa nivesanaṃ dhammaṃ nāma pāsādaṃ. Dhammo, ānanda, pāsādo puratthimena pacchimena ca yojanaṃ āyāmena ahosi. Uttarena dakkhiṇena ca aḍḍhayojanaṃ vitthārena. Dhammassa, ānanda, pāsādassa tiporisaṃ uccatarena vatthu citaṃ ahosi catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ iṭṭhakāhi – ekā iṭṭhakā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā, ekā veḷuriyamayā, ekā phalikamayā.

‘‘Dhammassa, ānanda, pāsādassa caturāsīti thambhasahassāni ahesuṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ – eko thambho sovaṇṇamayo, eko rūpiyamayo, eko veḷuriyamayo, eko phalikamayo. Dhammo, ānanda, pāsādo catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ phalakehi santhato ahosi – ekaṃ phalakaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ, ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ, ekaṃ veḷuriyamayaṃ, ekaṃ phalikamayaṃ.

‘‘Dhammassa, ānanda, pāsādassa catuvīsati sopānāni ahesuṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ – ekaṃ sopānaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ, ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ, ekaṃ veḷuriyamayaṃ, ekaṃ phalikamayaṃ. Sovaṇṇamayassa sopānassa sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayassa sopānassa rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Veḷuriyamayassa sopānassa veḷuriyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ phalikamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Phalikamayassa sopānassa phalikamayā thambhā ahesuṃ veḷuriyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca.

‘‘Dhamme, ānanda, pāsāde caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni ahesuṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ – ekaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ, ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ, ekaṃ veḷuriyamayaṃ , ekaṃ phalikamayaṃ. Sovaṇṇamaye kūṭāgāre rūpiyamayo pallaṅko paññatto ahosi, rūpiyamaye kūṭāgāre sovaṇṇamayo pallaṅko paññatto ahosi, veḷuriyamaye kūṭāgāre dantamayo pallaṅko paññatto ahosi, phalikamaye kūṭāgāre sāramayo pallaṅko paññatto ahosi. Sovaṇṇamayassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre rūpiyamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa rūpiyamayo khandho sovaṇṇamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Rūpiyamayassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre sovaṇṇamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa sovaṇṇamayo khandho, rūpiyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Veḷuriyamayassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre phalikamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa phalikamayo khandho, veḷuriyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Phalikamayassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre veḷuriyamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa veḷuriyamayo khandho, phalikamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca.
mula_english:
‘Then, Ānanda, Śakra, the ruler of the gods, knowing in his mind King Mahāsudassana’s thought, said to the attendant-deva Viśvakarman: “Come, friend Viśvakarman, and build a dwelling for King Mahāsudassana, a palace called *Dharma* (Dhammaṃ nāma pāsāda)”.

‘Very good, Lord’ (evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti), Viśvakarman replied and, as swiftly as a strong man might stretch his flexed arm or flex it again, he at once vanished from the Heaven of the Thirty-Three and appeared before King Mahāsudassana.

Then, Ānanda, Viśvakarman said to King Mahāsudassana: “I will build a dwelling for you, your majesty, a palace called *Dharma* (Dhammaṃ nāma pāsāda)”.

The King assented by silence,

Viśvakarman built him the Palace of *Dharma* (Dhammaṃ nāma pāsādaṃ).

The Palace of *Dharma* (dhammo), Ānanda, was a *yojana* in length from east to west,

and half a *yojana* wide from north to south.

The whole palace, Ānanda, was faced up to three times a man’s height with tiles of four colours, gold (*sovaṇṇa*), silver (*rūpiya*), beryl (*veḷuriya*) and crystal (*phalika*).

It contained eighty-four thousand columns, Ānanda, of the same four colours: gold (*sovaṇṇamayo*), silver (*rūpiyamayo*), beryl (*veḷuriyamayo*) and crystal (*phalikamayo*).

The palace, Ānanda, was overlaid with flagstones of four colours: gold (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ*), silver (*rūpiyamayaṃ*), beryl (*veḷuriyamayaṃ*) and crystal (*phalikamayaṃ*).

It had twenty-four staircases, Ānanda, of the same four colours: gold (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ*), silver (*rūpiyamayaṃ*), beryl (*veḷuriyamayaṃ*) and crystal (*phalikamayaṃ*).

The gold staircases had gold posts with silver railings and banisters (*sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca*).

The silver had silver posts with gold railings and banisters (*rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca*).

The beryl staircases had beryl posts with crystal railings and banisters (*veḷuriyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ phalikamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca*).

The crystal staircases had crystal posts with beryl railings and banisters (*phalikamayā thambhā ahesuṃ veḷuriyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca*).

In the Dharma Palace, Ānanda, there were eighty-four thousand peaked houses (*caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni ahesuṃ*), of four colours – one peaked house was golden (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ*), one was silver (*rūpiyamayaṃ*), one was beryl (*veḷuriyamayaṃ*), and one was crystal (*phalikamayaṃ*).

In the golden peaked house there was a silver couch made ready, in the silver peaked house there was a golden couch made ready, in the beryl peaked house there was an ivory couch made ready, and in the crystal peaked house there was a sandalwood couch made ready.

On the door of the gold peaked house a silver palm-tree stood, its trunk made of silver, and its leaves and fruits of gold (*rūpiyamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa rūpiyamayo khandho sovaṇṇamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca*).

On the door of the silver peaked house a golden palm-tree stood, its trunk made of gold, and its leaves and fruits of silver (*sovaṇṇamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa sovaṇṇamayo khandho, rūpiyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca*).

On the door of the beryl peaked house a crystal palm-tree stood, its trunk made of crystal, and its leaves and fruits of beryl (*phalikamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa phalikamayo khandho, veḷuriyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca*).

On the door of the crystal peaked house a beryl palm-tree stood, its trunk made of beryl, and its leaves and fruits of crystal (*veḷuriyamayo tālo ṭhito ahosi, tassa veḷuriyamayo khandho, phalikamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca*).
commentary_pali: 256.Ehi tvaṃ sammāti ehi tvaṃ vayassa. Dhammaṃ nāma pāsādanti pāsādassa nāmaṃ āropetvāva āṇāpesi. Vissakammo pana kīva mahanto deva pāsādo hotūti paṭipucchitvā dīghato yojanaṃ vitthārato aḍḍhayojanaṃ sabbaratanamayova hotūti vuttepi ‘evaṃ hotu, bhaddaṃ tava vacana’nti tassa paṭissuṇitvā dhammarājānaṃ sampaṭicchāpetvā māpesi. Tattha evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti kho ānandāti evaṃ bhaddaṃ tava iti kho ānanda. Paṭissutvāti sampaṭicchitvā, vatvāti attho. Tuṇhībhāvenāti samaṇadhammapaṭipattikaraṇokāso me bhavissatīti icchanto tuṇhībhāvena adhivāsesi. Sāramayoti candanasāramayo.
commentary_english:
256.
“Come, you are correct ( *ehi tvaṃ sammā* )" means come, you are of age.
"A Dharma is named a palace ( *dhammaṃ nāma pāsāda*)", he ordered that the name be assigned to the palace.
Then, having questioned Viśvakarman, "How large should the divine palace be?", and even after it was said that it should be a *yojana* in length, half a *yojana* in width, and made entirely of jewels, he agreed to it, saying, “So be it, good is your word ( *evaṃ hotu, bhaddaṃ tava vacana*)”, and after accepting that, he had the king of Dharma construct it.
There, "*evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti kho ānandā*" means thus, good is your word, Ānanda.
"*paṭissutvā*" means having accepted, having spoken, is the meaning ( *attho*).
"*tuṇhībhāvenā*" means the opportunity to practice the ascetic Dharma ( *samaṇadhammapaṭipattikaraṇokāso* ) will be mine ( *me bhavissatīti* ), desiring this, he consented with silence ( *tuṇhībhāvena adhivāsesi*).
"*sāramayo*" means made of sandalwood essence ( *candanasāramayo*).

mula_pali: 257. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ mahāviyūhassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre sabbasovaṇṇamayaṃ tālavanaṃ māpeyyaṃ, yattha divāvihāraṃ nisīdissāmī’ti. Māpesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano mahāviyūhassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre sabbasovaṇṇamayaṃ tālavanaṃ, yattha divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Dhammo, ānanda , pāsādo dvīhi vedikāhi parikkhitto ahosi, ekā vedikā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā. Sovaṇṇamayāya vedikāya sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayāya vedikāya rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ, sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca.
mula_english:
257. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana thought: 'Suppose I were to have a grove of palm trees made entirely of gold by the door of the great gabled chamber where I sit during the day, where I might take my daytime rest?'

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana had a grove of palm trees made entirely of gold by the door of the great gabled chamber, where he took his daytime rest.

The *dharma*, Ānanda, the palace was surrounded by two parapets, one of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), and the other of silver (*rūpiyamaya*).

The gold parapet had gold posts, and silver railings and banisters.

The silver parapet had silver posts, and gold railings and banisters.
commentary_pali: 257.Dvīhi vedikāhīti ettha ekā vedikā panassa uṇhīsamatthake ahosi, ekā heṭṭhā paricchedamatthake.
commentary_english: [p. 257] "By two vedikās": here, one vedikā was on his uṇhīsa-head, and one below, on the pariccheda-head.

mula_pali: 258. ‘‘Dhammo, ānanda, pāsādo dvīhi kiṅkiṇikajālehi kiṅkaṇikajālehi (syā. ka.) parikkhitto ahosi – ekaṃ jālaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Sovaṇṇamayassa jālassa rūpiyamayā kiṅkiṇikā ahesuṃ, rūpiyamayassa jālassa sovaṇṇamayā kiṅkiṇikā ahesuṃ. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddo ahosi vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, pañcaṅgikassa tūriyassa suvinītassa suppaṭitāḷitassa sukusalehi kusalehi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) samannāhatassa saddo hoti, vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca, evameva kho, ānanda, tesaṃ kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddo ahosi vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca. Ye kho panānanda, tena samayena kusāvatiyā rājadhāniyā dhuttā ahesuṃ soṇḍā pipāsā, te tesaṃ kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddena paricāresuṃ. Niṭṭhito kho panānanda, dhammo pāsādo duddikkho ahosi musati cakkhūni. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno abbhuggamamāno (sī. pī. ka.) duddikkho dudikkho (pī.) hoti musati cakkhūni; evameva kho, ānanda, dhammo pāsādo duddikkho ahosi musati cakkhūni.
mula_english: 258. "Ānanda, the Dhamma Palace ( *dhammo pāsādo*) was surrounded by two nets of bells (*dvīhi kiṅkiṇikajālehi*) – one net was gold (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ*) and one was silver (*rūpiyamayaṃ*). The golden net (*sovaṇṇamayassa jālassa*) had silver bells (*rūpiyamayā kiṅkiṇikā ahesuṃ*), and the silver net (*rūpiyamayassa jālassa*) had golden bells (*sovaṇṇamayā kiṅkiṇikā ahesuṃ*). And when those nets of bells (*kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ*) were stirred by the wind (*vāteritānaṃ*), their sound (*saddo*) was lovely (*vaggu*), delightful (*rajanīyo*), sweet (*khamanīyo*), and intoxicating (*madanīyo*). Just as, Ānanda, when a five-piece orchestra (*pañcaṅgikassa tūriyassa*) is well-tuned (*suvinītassa*) and skillfully played (*suppaṭitāḷitassa*) by very skilled musicians (*sukusalehi*), its sound (*saddo hoti*) is lovely (*vaggu*), delightful (*rajanīyo*), sweet (*khamanīyo*), and intoxicating (*madanīyo*), so too, Ānanda, was the sound (*saddo ahosi*) of those nets of bells (*kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ*) when stirred by the wind (*vāteritānaṃ*)—lovely (*vaggu*), delightful (*rajanīyo*), sweet (*khamanīyo*), and intoxicating (*madanīyo*). And those who were libertines (*dhuttā ahesuṃ*) and drunkards (*soṇḍā pipāsā*) in Kusāvati at that time (*tena samayena kusāvatiyā rājadhāniyā*), had their desires assuaged (*paricāresuṃ*) by the sound (*saddena*) of those nets of bells (*kiṅkiṇikajālānaṃ vāteritānaṃ*). When the Dhamma Palace (*dhammo pāsādo*) was finished (*niṭṭhito*), Ānanda, it was hard to look at (*duddikkho ahosi*), dazzling to the eyes (*musati cakkhūni*). Just as in the last month of the Rains (*vassānaṃ pacchime māse*), in autumn (*saradasamaye*), when there is a clear and cloudless sky (*viddhe vigatavalāhake deve*), the sun (*ādicco*) breaking through the mists (*nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno*) is hard to look at (*duddikkho hoti*), dazzling to the eyes (*musati cakkhūni*); so too, Ānanda, was the Dhamma Palace (*dhammo pāsādo*) hard to look at (*duddikkho ahosi*), dazzling to the eyes (*musati cakkhūni*)."
commentary_pali: 258.Duddikkho ahosīti duuddikkho, pabhāsampattiyā duddasoti attho. Musatīti harati phandāpeti niccalabhāvena patiṭṭhātuṃ na deti. Viddheti ubbiddhe, meghavigamena dūrībhūteti attho. Deveti ākāse.
commentary_english:
258. *Duddikkho ahosī* means *duuddikkho*, the meaning is difficult to see because of the attainment of light.

*Musatī* means it removes, agitates, does not allow to be established by means of stillness.

*Viddhe* means *ubbiddhe*, the meaning is removed, far away by the departure of the clouds.

*Deve* means in the sky (ākāśa).

mula_pali:
259. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhammassa pāsādassa purato dhammaṃ nāma pokkharaṇiṃ māpeyya’nti. Māpesi kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano dhammassa pāsādassa purato dhammaṃ nāma pokkharaṇiṃ. Dhammā, ānanda, pokkharaṇī puratthimena pacchimena ca yojanaṃ āyāmena ahosi, uttarena dakkhiṇena ca aḍḍhayojanaṃ vitthārena. Dhammā, ānanda, pokkharaṇī catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ iṭṭhakāhi citā ahosi – ekā iṭṭhakā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā, ekā veḷuriyamayā, ekā phalikamayā.

‘‘Dhammāya, ānanda, pokkharaṇiyā catuvīsati sopānāni ahesuṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ – ekaṃ sopānaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ, ekaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ, ekaṃ veḷuriyamayaṃ, ekaṃ phalikamayaṃ. Sovaṇṇamayassa sopānassa sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayassa sopānassa rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Veḷuriyamayassa sopānassa veḷuriyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ phalikamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Phalikamayassa sopānassa phalikamayā thambhā ahesuṃ veḷuriyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca.

‘‘Dhammā, ānanda, pokkharaṇī dvīhi vedikāhi parikkhittā ahosi – ekā vedikā sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā. Sovaṇṇamayāya vedikāya sovaṇṇamayā thambhā ahesuṃ rūpiyamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca. Rūpiyamayāya vedikāya rūpiyamayā thambhā ahesuṃ sovaṇṇamayā sūciyo ca uṇhīsañca.

‘‘Dhammā, ānanda, pokkharaṇī sattahi tālapantīhi parikkhittā ahosi – ekā tālapanti sovaṇṇamayā, ekā rūpiyamayā, ekā veḷuriyamayā, ekā phalikamayā, ekā lohitaṅkamayā, ekā masāragallamayā, ekā sabbaratanamayā. Sovaṇṇamayassa tālassa sovaṇṇamayo khandho ahosi rūpiyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Rūpiyamayassa tālassa rūpiyamayo khandho ahosi sovaṇṇamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Veḷuriyamayassa tālassa veḷuriyamayo khandho ahosi phalikamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Phalikamayassa tālassa phalikamayo khandho ahosi veḷuriyamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Lohitaṅkamayassa tālassa lohitaṅkamayo khandho ahosi masāragallamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Masāragallamayassa tālassa masāragallamayo khandho ahosi lohitaṅkamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Sabbaratanamayassa tālassa sabbaratanamayo khandho ahosi, sabbaratanamayāni pattāni ca phalāni ca. Tāsaṃ kho panānanda, tālapantīnaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddo ahosi, vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, pañcaṅgikassa tūriyassa suvinītassa suppaṭitāḷitassa sukusalehi samannāhatassa saddo hoti vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca, evameva kho, ānanda, tāsaṃ tālapantīnaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddo ahosi vaggu ca rajanīyo ca khamanīyo ca madanīyo ca. Ye kho panānanda, tena samayena kusāvatiyā rājadhāniyā dhuttā ahesuṃ soṇḍā pipāsā, te tāsaṃ tālapantīnaṃ vāteritānaṃ saddena paricāresuṃ.

‘‘Niṭṭhite kho panānanda, dhamme pāsāde niṭṭhitāya dhammāya ca pokkharaṇiyā rājā mahāsudassano ‘ye ye ko panānanda (syā. ka.) tena samayena samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā’, te sabbakāmehi santappetvā dhammaṃ pāsādaṃ abhiruhi.

ye ko panānanda (syā. ka.)

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro.

Jhānasampatti
mula_english:
259. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana thought: ‘Suppose I were to have a lotus pond called *Dhamma* made in front of the *Dhamma* Palace?’

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana had a lotus pond called *Dhamma* made in front of the *Dhamma* Palace.

This *Dhamma* lotus pond, Ānanda, was one *yojana* in length from east to west, and half a *yojana* in width from north to south.

This *Dhamma* lotus pond, Ānanda, was built of four kinds of bricks: one kind of brick was made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), one was made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), one was made of beryl (*veḷuriya*), and one was made of crystal (*phalikamaya*).

To this *Dhamma* lotus pond, Ānanda, there were twenty-four staircases of four different kinds: one staircase was made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), one was made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), one was made of beryl (*veḷuriya*), and one was made of crystal (*phalikamaya*).

The staircase made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*) had posts made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), and railings and banisters made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*).

The staircase made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*) had posts made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), and railings and banisters made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*).

The staircase made of beryl (*veḷuriya*) had posts made of beryl (*veḷuriya*), and railings and banisters made of crystal (*phalikamaya*).

The staircase made of crystal (*phalikamaya*) had posts made of crystal (*phalikamaya*), and railings and banisters made of beryl (*veḷuriya*).

The *Dhamma* lotus pond, Ānanda, was surrounded by two parapets: one parapet was made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), and one was made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*).

The parapet made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*) had posts made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), and railings and banisters made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*).

The parapet made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*) had posts made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), and railings and banisters made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*).

The *Dhamma* lotus pond, Ānanda, was surrounded by seven rows of palm trees: one row of palm trees was made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), one was made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), one was made of beryl (*veḷuriya*), one was made of crystal (*phalikamaya*), one was made of ruby (*lohitaṅkamaya*), one was made of emerald (*masāragalla*), and one was made of all kinds of gems (*sabbaratnamaya*).

The gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*) palm trees had trunks made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*), and leaves and fruits made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*).

The silver (*rūpiyamaya*) palm trees had trunks made of silver (*rūpiyamaya*), and leaves and fruits made of gold (*sovaṇṇamaya*).

The beryl (*veḷuriya*) palm trees had trunks made of beryl (*veḷuriya*), and leaves and fruits made of crystal (*phalikamaya*).

The crystal (*phalikamaya*) palm trees had trunks made of crystal (*phalikamaya*), and leaves and fruits made of beryl (*veḷuriya*).

The ruby (*lohitaṅkamaya*) palm trees had trunks made of ruby (*lohitaṅkamaya*), and leaves and fruits made of emerald (*masāragalla*).

The emerald (*masāragalla*) palm trees had trunks made of emerald (*masāragalla*), and leaves and fruits made of ruby (*lohitaṅkamaya*).

The palm trees made of all gems (*sabbaratnamaya*) had trunks made of all gems (*sabbaratnamaya*), and leaves and fruits made of all gems (*sabbaratnamaya*).

The sound of those rows of palm trees, Ānanda, stirred by the wind, was lovely, delightful, sweet, and intoxicating.

Just as the sound of a five-piece orchestra, Ānanda, when well-tuned, well-beaten, and skillfully played, is lovely, delightful, sweet, and intoxicating, so too, Ānanda, the sound of those rows of palm trees stirred by the wind was lovely, delightful, sweet, and intoxicating.

Those who at that time were libertines and drunkards in the capital city of Kusāvatī, Ānanda, had their desires assuaged by the sound of those palm trees stirred by the wind.

When the *Dhamma* Palace and the *Dhamma* lotus pond were finished, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana, having satisfied every wish of those who at the time were ascetics or Brahmins, or revered as such, ascended into the *Dhamma* Palace.

The First Recitation Section.
jhānasampatti
commentary_pali:
259.Māpesi khoti ahaṃ imasmiṃ ṭhāne pokkharaṇiṃ māpemi, tumhākaṃ gharāni bhindathāti na evaṃ kāretvā māpesi. Cittuppādavaseneva panassa bhūmiṃ bhinditvā tathārūpā pokkharaṇī ahosi. Te sabbakāmehīti sabbehi icchiticchitavatthūhi, samaṇe samaṇaparikkhārehi, brāhmaṇe brāhmaṇaparikkhārehi santappesīti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

commentary_english:
But if they eat a meal from me, they’ll be able to bring back meals for the sick in good time, and the sick will be able to eat.
And if they eat a meal from me, they'll be able to bring back meals for the sick in good time, and the sick will be able to eat.
"Those with all desires" means all desired objects, ascetics with ascetic requisites, and Brahmins with Brahmin requisites, were satisfied.
