Explanation of the accomplishment of *dhyāna*

mula_pali:
260. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘kissa nu kho me idaṃ kammassa phalaṃ kissa kammassa vipāko, yenāhaṃ etarahi evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo’ti? Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘tiṇṇaṃ kho me idaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ tiṇṇaṃ kammānaṃ vipāko, yenāhaṃ etarahi evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo, seyyathidaṃ dānassa damassa saṃyamassā’ti.

‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano yena mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahāviyūhassa kūṭāgārassa dvāre ṭhito udānaṃ udānesi – ‘tiṭṭha, kāmavitakka, tiṭṭha, byāpādavitakka, tiṭṭha, vihiṃsāvitakka. Ettāvatā kāmavitakka, ettāvatā byāpādavitakka, ettāvatā vihiṃsāvitakkā’ti.
mula_english:
260. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana thought: ‘Of what *karma* is this the fruit, of what *karma* is this the result, that I am now so mighty and powerful?’ Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana thought: ‘It is the fruit, the result of three kinds of *karma*: namely, of *dāna* (giving), *dama* (self-control), and *saṃyama* (abstinence).’

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana went to the great *mahāviyūha kūṭāgāra* (gabled chamber); having gone there, standing at the door of the *mahāviyūha kūṭāgāra*, he exclaimed: ‘Cease, thought of *kāma* (desire)! Cease, thought of *byāpāda* (ill-will)! Cease, thought of *vihiṃsā* (cruelty)!

Thus far the thought of *kāma* (desire), thus far the thought of *byāpāda* (ill-will), thus far the thought of *vihiṃsā* (cruelty)!’
commentary_pali:
260.Mahiddhikoti cittuppādavaseneva caturāsītipokkharaṇīsahassānaṃ nibbattisaṅkhātāya mahatiyā iddhiyā samannāgato. Mahānubhāvoti tesaṃyeva anubhavitabbānaṃ mahantatāya mahānubhāvena samannāgato. Seyyathidanti nipāto, tassa – ‘‘katamesaṃ tiṇṇa’’nti attho. Dānassāti sampattipariccāgassa. Damassāti āḷavakasutte paññā damoti āgato. Idha attānaṃ damentena kataṃ uposathakammaṃ. Saṃyamassāti sīlassa.

Bodhisattapubbayogavaṇṇanā

Idha ṭhatvā panassa pubbayogo veditabbo – rājā kira pubbe gahapatikule nibbatti. Tena ca samayena dharamānakasseva kassapabuddhassa sāsane eko thero araññe vāsaṃ vasati, bodhisatto attano kammena araññaṃ paviṭṭho theraṃ disvā upasaṅkamitvā vanditvā therassa nisajjanaṭṭhānacaṅkamanaṭṭhānāni oloketvā pucchi – ‘‘idheva, bhante, ayyo vasatī’’ti? Āma, upāsakāti sutvā – ‘‘idheva ayyassa paṇṇasālaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti cintetvā attano kammaṃ pahāya dabbasambhāraṃ koṭṭetvā paṇṇasālaṃ katvā chādetvā bhittiyo mattikāya limpitvā dvāraṃ yojetvā kaṭṭhattharaṇaṃ katvā – ‘‘karissati nu kho paribhogaṃ, na karissatī’’ti ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Thero antogāmato āgantvā paṇṇasālaṃ pavisitvā kaṭṭhattharaṇe nisīdi. Upāsakopi āgantvā vanditvā samīpe nisinno ‘‘phāsukā, bhante, paṇṇasālā’’ti pucchi. Phāsukā, bhaddamukha, pabbajitasāruppāti. Vasissatha, bhante, idhāti? Āma, upāsakāti, so adhivāsanākārena vasissatīti ñatvā nibaddhaṃ mayhaṃ gharadvāraṃ āgantabbanti paṭijānāpetvā – ‘‘ekaṃ me, bhante, varaṃ dethā’’ti āha. Atikkantavarā, upāsaka, pabbajitāti. Bhante, yañca kappati, yañca anavajjanti. Vadehi upāsakāti. Bhante, nibaddhavasanaṭṭhāne nāma manussā maṅgale vā amaṅgale vā āgamanaṃ icchanti, anāgacchantassa kujjhanti. Tasmā aññaṃ nimantitaṭṭhānaṃ gantvāpi mayhaṃ gharaṃ pavisitvāva bhattakiccaṃ niṭṭhāpetabbanti. Thero adhivāsesi.

So paṇṇasālāya kaṭasāṭakaṃ pattharitvā mañcapīṭhaṃ paññapesi, apassenaṃ nikkhipi, pādakathalikaṃ ṭhapesi, pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇi, caṅkamaṃ katvā vālikaṃ okiri, mige āgantvā bhittiṃ ghaṃsitvā mattikaṃ pātente disvā kaṇṭakavatiṃ parikkhipi. Pokkharaṇiṃ otaritvā udakaṃ āḷulikaṃ karonte disvā anto pāsāṇehi cinitvā bahi kaṇṭakavatiṃ parikkhipitvā antovatipariyante tālapantiyo ropeti, mahācaṅkame sammaṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ āḷulente disvā caṅkamampi vatiyā parikkhipitvā antovatipariyante tālapantiṃ ropesi. Evaṃ āvāsaṃ niṭṭhapetvā therassa ticīvaraṃ, piṇḍapātaṃ, osadhaṃ, paribhogabhājanaṃ, ārakaṇṭakaṃ, pipphalikaṃ, nakhacchedanaṃ, sūciṃ, kattarayaṭṭhiṃ, upāhanaṃ, udakatumbaṃ, chattaṃ, dīpakapallakaṃ, malaharaṇiṃ. Parissāvanaṃ, dhamakaraṇaṃ, pattaṃ, thālakaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi pabbajitānaṃ paribhogajātaṃ, sabbaṃ adāsi. Therassa bodhisattena adinnaparikkhāro nāma nāhosi. So sīlāni rakkhanto uposathaṃ karonto yāvajīvaṃ theraṃ upaṭṭhahi. Thero tattheva vasanto arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyi.

Bodhisattopi yāvatāyukaṃ puññaṃ katvā devaloke nibbattitvā tato cuto manussalokaṃ āgacchanto kusāvatiyā rājadhāniyā nibbattitvā mahāsudassano rājā ahosi.

‘‘Evaṃ nātimahantampi, puññaṃ āyatane kataṃ;

Mahāvipākaṃ hotīti, kattabbaṃ taṃ vibhāvinā’’.

Mahāviyūhanti rajatamayaṃ mahākūṭāgāraṃ. Tattha vasitukāmo hutvā agamāsi, ettāvatā kāmavitakkāti kāmavitakka tayā ettāvatā nivattitabbaṃ, ito paraṃ tuyhaṃ abhūmi, idaṃ jhānāgāraṃ nāma, nayidaṃ tayā saddhiṃ vasanaṭṭhānanti evaṃ tayo vitakke kūṭāgāradvāreyeva nivattesi.

Mahāviyūha ettāvatā kāmavitakkā jhānāgāraṃ
commentary_english:
260. *Mahiddhiko* means endowed with great *iddhi* power, said to be the production of eighty-four thousand lotus ponds, by the power of the arising of thought alone.

*Mahānubhāvo* means endowed with great power (*mahānubhāvena*), due to the greatness of those very things that are to be experienced (*anubhavitabbānaṃ*).

*Seyyathidaṃ* is a particle (*nipāto*), its meaning is "Which three?"

*Dānassa* is the relinquishing of prosperity.

*Damassa* is what comes in the Āḷavaka Sutta as wisdom (*paññā*) is *dama*. Here, it is the *uposatha* act done by one taming himself.

*Saṃyamassa* is of moral discipline (*sīlassa*).

**Account of a Bodhisattva's Former Endeavor**

Here, moreover, his former endeavor should be understood: It is said that formerly a king was born in a householder's family. And at that time, in the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa, while he was still alive, an Elder lived dwelling in a forest. The Bodhisattva, having entered the forest by his own doing (*kammena*), saw the Elder, approached, paid homage, and having looked over the Elder's places for sitting and walking, asked, "Does the Venerable one live just here?" "Yes, lay follower." Having heard that, thinking, "It is fitting to make a leaf hut for the Venerable One right here," having abandoned his own work, having collected the necessary materials, having made a leaf hut, having roofed it, having plastered the walls with clay, having fitted a door, having made a wooden platform, he sat down to one side, [thinking], "Will he make use of it, or will he not?"

The Elder, having come from inside the village, entered the leaf hut and sat down on the wooden platform. The lay follower too, having come, paid homage, sat down nearby and asked, "Is the leaf hut comfortable, Venerable Sir?" "Comfortable, good sir, appropriate for one gone forth." "Will you dwell here, Venerable Sir?" "Yes, lay follower." Knowing that he will dwell there in the manner of acceptance, having made him promise, "You must come to my house-door regularly," he said, "Grant me one boon, Venerable Sir." "Those gone forth have transcended boons, lay follower." "Venerable Sir, [grant me] what is allowable and what is blameless." "Speak, lay follower." "Venerable Sir, in a regular dwelling place, people want one to come for auspicious or inauspicious [occasions]; they get angry with one who does not come. Therefore, even having gone to another invited place, you must complete the meal duty only after entering my house." The Elder assented.

He spread out a mat of woven leaves in the leaf hut, prepared a couch and a seat, put aside a pillow, placed a footstool, dug a lotus pond, made a walk and scattered sand on it. Having seen deer coming, rubbing against the wall, and causing the clay to fall, he fenced it around with a thorny hedge. Having seen [the Elder] going down into the lotus pond and stirring up the water, having built it inside with stones, having fenced around the outside with a thorny hedge, he planted rows of palm trees around the inner perimeter. Having seen [the Elder] stirring up the place that had been swept on the great walk, having fenced the walk around with a fence, he planted a row of palm trees around the inner perimeter.

Thus, having completed the dwelling, he gave to the Elder the triple robe, alms food, medicine, a bowl for use, a toothpick, a *pipphalika*, a nail cutter, a needle, a needle case, a walking stick, sandals, a water pot, an umbrella, a lamp stand, a dirt remover, a straining cloth, a water dipper, a bowl, a dish, or whatever else there might be that is for the use of those gone forth, everything. There was no requisite un-given to the Elder by the Bodhisattva. Maintaining the moral precepts, doing the *uposatha*, he attended to the Elder as long as he lived. The Elder, dwelling there, attained arahantship and passed away.

The Bodhisattva too, having done merit for as long as he lived, was reborn in the world of the gods, and from there, passing away, coming to the world of humans, having been reborn in the royal capital of Kusāvatī, became King Mahāsudassana.

"Thus, even a not very great merit, done in a worthy place;

is of great result, so it should be done by one who discerns."

*Mahāviyūha* means a great peaked house made of silver.
Having desired to dwell there, he went, "[Up] to here [only are] thoughts of sensual desire (kāmavitakkā)," [meaning] thoughts of sensual desire should be turned back by you up to here; from here on, [this] is not your place; this is called a meditation hall (jhānāgāraṃ), [and] this is not a dwelling place with you." Thus, he turned back the three thoughts right there at the door of the peaked house.
mahāviyūha, up to here [only are] thoughts of sensual desire (kāmavitakkā), meditation hall (jhānāgāraṃ).

mula_pali: 261. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ pavisitvā sovaṇṇamaye pallaṅke nisinno vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsi. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsi. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihāsi, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedesi, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsi. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsi.
mula_english:
261. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana, having entered the great gabled chamber, the *kūṭāgāra*, sat down on the golden couch, detached from sense-desires (*kāmehi vivicca*), detached from unwholesome mental states (*akusalehi dhammehi*), entered and remained in the first *jhāna*, which is with thinking and pondering (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ*), born of detachment (*vivekajaṃ*), filled with delight and joy (*pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ*).

With the subsiding of thinking and pondering (*vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā*), by gaining inner tranquility and oneness of mind (*ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ*), he entered and remained in the second *jhāna*, which is without thinking and pondering (*avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ*), born of concentration (*samādhijaṃ*), filled with delight and joy (*pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ*).

And with the fading away of delight (*pītiyā ca virāgā*), remaining imperturbable (*upekkhako ca vihāsi*), mindful and clearly aware (*sato ca sampajāno*), he experienced in himself that joy of which the Noble Ones (*ariyā*) say: “Happy is he who dwells with equanimity and mindfulness (*upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī*)”, he entered and remained in the third *jhāna* (*tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ*).

And, having given up pleasure (*sukhassa ca pahānā*) and pain (*dukkhassa ca pahānā*), and with the disappearance of former gladness and sadness (*pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā*), he entered and remained in the fourth *jhāna* which is beyond pleasure and pain (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*), and purified by equanimity and mindfulness (*upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 261.Paṭhamajjhānantiādīsu visuṃ kasiṇaparikammakiccaṃ nāma natthi. Nīlakasiṇena atthe sati nīlamaṇiṃ, pītakasiṇena atthe sati suvaṇṇaṃ, lohitakasiṇena atthe sati rattamaṇiṃ, odātakasiṇena atthe sati rajatanti olokitaolokitaṭṭhāne kasiṇameva paññāyati.
commentary_english:
261. In the *paṭhamajjhāna* and so forth, there is no separate thing called *kasiṇaparikammakiccaṃ*.

When there is the blue *kasiṇa*, a sapphire; when there is the yellow *kasiṇa*, gold; when there is the red *kasiṇa*, a ruby; when there is the white *kasiṇa*, silver; in the places looked at, only the *kasiṇa* appears.

mula_pali:
262. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano mahāviyūhā kūṭāgārā nikkhamitvā sovaṇṇamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ pavisitvā rūpiyamaye pallaṅke nisinno mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihāsi. Tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihāsi tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi.

Caturāsīti nagarasahassādi
mula_english:
‘Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana, emerging from the great gabled chamber, went to the golden gabled chamber and, seated cross-legged on the silver couch, stayed pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness ( *mettāsahagatena cetasā*).
Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth.
Thus above, below, and across; everywhere, in its entirety, he dwelt pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness ( *mettāsahagatena cetasā*), abundant, exalted, immeasurable ( *appamāṇena*), without hostility and without ill-will.
With a mind imbued with compassion ( *karuṇāsahagatena cetasā*)…and so on… with a mind imbued with sympathetic joy ( *muditāsahagatena cetasā*)…and so on… with a mind imbued with equanimity ( *upekkhāsahagatena cetasā*) he dwelt pervading one direction, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth.
Thus above, below, and across; everywhere, in its entirety, he dwelt pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity ( *upekkhāsahagatena cetasā*), abundant, exalted, immeasurable ( *appamāṇena*), without hostility and without ill-will.

caturāsīti nagarasahassādi
commentary_pali:
262.Mettāsahagatenātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ sabbampi visuddhimagge vuttameva. Iti pāḷiyaṃ cattāri jhānāni, cattāri appamaññāneva vuttāni. Mahāpuriso pana sabbāpi aṭṭha samāpattiyo, pañca abhiññāyo ca nibbattetvā anulomapaṭilomādivasena cuddasahākārehi samāpattiyo pavisanto madhupaṭalaṃ paviṭṭhabhamaro madhurasena viya samāpattisukheneva yāpeti.

Caturāsītinagarasahassādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
In regards to that which should be said in the *mettāsahagatenā* and so on, all of that has already been said in the *Visuddhimagga*.

Thus, in the Pāli [text], four *jhānas* and four *appamaññas* are mentioned.

Moreover, the great person, having produced all eight *samāpattis* and five *abhiññās*, entering into the *samāpattis* with fourteen aspects in the manner of direct order, reverse order, and so forth, lives enjoying the bliss of *samāpatti*, like a bee that has entered a honeycomb with sweet essence.

Description of eighty-four thousand cities and so on.

mula_pali: 263. ‘‘Rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa caturāsīti nagarasahassāni ahesuṃ kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni; caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni ahesuṃ dhammapāsādappamukhāni; caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni ahesuṃ mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni; caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni ahesuṃ sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni; caturāsīti nāgasahassāni ahesuṃ sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni; caturāsīti assasahassāni ahesuṃ sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni; caturāsīti rathasahassāni ahesuṃ sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni; caturāsīti maṇisahassāni ahesuṃ maṇiratanappamukhāni; caturāsīti itthisahassāni ahesuṃ subhaddādevippamukhāni; caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni ahesuṃ gahapatiratanappamukhāni; caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni ahesuṃ anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni; caturāsīti dhenusahassāni ahesuṃ duhasandanāni dukūlasandanāni(pī.) dukūlasandānāni dukūlasandanāni (pī.) dukūlasandānāni (saṃ. ni. 3.96) kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni; caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni ahesuṃ khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ ; (rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa) ( ) sī. ipotthakesu natthi caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni ahesuṃ sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyittha.
mula_english: “Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana had eighty-four thousand cities, Kusāvatī being the chief among them; eighty-four thousand palaces, Dhamma Palace being the chief; eighty-four thousand gabled halls, the Great Array Hall being the chief; eighty-four thousand couches of gold, silver, ivory, and sandalwood, covered with fleece, wool, and embroidered covers, spread with antelope hides, with awnings, and with red cushions at both ends; eighty-four thousand elephants adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with nets of gold thread, the Uposatha elephant being the chief; eighty-four thousand horses adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with nets of gold thread, the Valāhaka horse being the chief; eighty-four thousand chariots with lion-skin coverings, tiger-skin coverings, leopard-skin coverings, and yellow woolen coverings, adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with nets of gold thread, the Vejayanta chariot being the chief; eighty-four thousand jewels, the jewel-treasure being the chief; eighty-four thousand women, Subhaddā being the chief; eighty-four thousand householders, the householder-treasure being the chief; eighty-four thousand nobles, attendants, the advisor-treasure being the chief; eighty-four thousand milk cows with jute tethers and bronze milk pails; eighty-four thousand kotis of cloths of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk, and fine wool; King Mahāsudassana had eighty-four thousand rice platters brought to him every morning and evening."
commentary_pali: 263.Kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhānīti kusāvatī rājadhānī tesaṃ nagarānaṃ pamukhā sabbaseṭṭhāti attho. Bhattābhihāroti abhiharitabbabhattaṃ.
commentary_english:
263. *kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhānī* means Kusāvatī is the capital city and the foremost and best of those cities.

*bhattābhihāro* means food that should be brought.

mula_pali:
264. ‘‘Tena kho panānanda, samayena rañño mahāsudassanassa caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchanti. Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa etadahosi – ‘imāni kho me caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchanti, yaṃnūna vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena dvecattālīsaṃ dvecattālīsaṃ nāgasahassāni sakiṃ sakiṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyu’nti. Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano pariṇāyakaratanaṃ āmantesi – ‘imāni kho me, samma pariṇāyakaratana, caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchanti, tena hi, samma pariṇāyakaratana, vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena dvecattālīsaṃ dvecattālīsaṃ nāgasahassāni sakiṃ sakiṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchantū’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, ānanda, pariṇāyakaratanaṃ rañño mahāsudassanassa paccassosi. Atha kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa aparena samayena vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena dvecattālīsaṃ dvecattālīsaṃ nāgasahassāni sakiṃ sakiṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgamaṃsu.

Subhaddādeviupasaṅkamanaṃ
mula_english:
“And at that time, Ānanda, eighty-four thousand elephants of King Mahāsudassana came to wait upon him morning and evening. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana thought: ‘These eighty-four thousand elephants come to wait upon me morning and evening. Suppose that, at the end of each century, forty-two thousand elephants were to come to wait upon me, turn and turn about.’ Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana addressed his jewel-counselor: ‘These eighty-four thousand elephants come to wait upon me morning and evening, good jewel-counselor. Therefore, good jewel-counselor, let forty-two thousand elephants come to wait upon me, turn and turn about, at the end of each century.’ ‘Yes, sire,’ Ānanda, the jewel-counselor replied to King Mahāsudassana. Then, Ānanda, at a later time, at the end of each century, forty-two thousand elephants came to wait upon King Mahāsudassana, turn and turn about.

Subhaddā’s Approach
commentary_pali:
264.Vassasatassavassasatassāti kasmā evaṃ cintesi? Tesaṃ saddena ukkaṇṭhitvā, ‘‘samāpannassa saddo kaṇṭako’’ti (a. ni. 10.72) hi vuttaṃ. Tasmā saddena ukkaṇṭhito mahāpuriso. Atha kasmā mā āgacchantūti na vadati? Idāni rājā na passatīti nibaddhavattaṃ na labhissanti, taṃ tesaṃ mā uppajjitthāti na vadati.

Subhaddādeviupasaṅkamanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
264.
Why did he think thus, "a hundred years of rain"? Having been vexed by their noise, "noise is a thorn to one who has attained concentration," for this is said (A.
N.
10.
72).
Therefore, the great man was vexed by the noise.
Then why does he not say, "May they not come"? Now, thinking, "the king does not see," they will not obtain a fixed allowance; he does not say [this] thinking, "may that not arise for them."

Subhaddādeviupasaṅkamanavaṇṇanā

mula_pali: 265. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddāya deviyā bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena etadahosi – ‘ciraṃ diṭṭho kho me rājā mahāsudassano. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyya’nti. Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī itthāgāraṃ āmantesi – ‘etha tumhe sīsāni nhāyatha pītāni vatthāni pārupatha. Ciraṃ diṭṭho no rājā mahāsudassano, rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, ayye’ti kho, ānanda, itthāgāraṃ subhaddāya deviyā paṭissutvā sīsāni nhāyitvā pītāni vatthāni pārupitvā yena subhaddā devī tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī pariṇāyakaratanaṃ āmantesi – ‘kappehi, samma pariṇāyakaratana, caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ, ciraṃ diṭṭho no rājā mahāsudassano, rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devī’ti kho, ānanda, pariṇāyakaratanaṃ subhaddāya deviyā paṭissutvā caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ kappāpetvā subhaddāya deviyā paṭivedesi – ‘kappitā kho, devi, caturaṅginī senā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī caturaṅginiyā senāya saddhiṃ itthāgārena yena dhammo pāsādo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā dhammaṃ pāsādaṃ abhiruhitvā yena mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā mahāviyūhassa kūṭāgārassa dvārabāhaṃ ālambitvā aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano saddaṃ sutvā – ‘kiṃ nu kho mahato viya janakāyassa saddo’ti mahāviyūhā kūṭāgārā nikkhamanto addasa subhaddaṃ deviṃ dvārabāhaṃ ālambitvā ṭhitaṃ, disvāna subhaddaṃ deviṃ etadavoca – ‘ettheva, devi, tiṭṭha mā pāvisī’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, mahāviyūhā kūṭāgārā sovaṇṇamayaṃ pallaṅkaṃ nīharitvā sabbasovaṇṇamaye tālavane paññapehī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, ānanda, so puriso rañño mahāsudassanassa paṭissutvā mahāviyūhā kūṭāgārā sovaṇṇamayaṃ pallaṅkaṃ nīharitvā sabbasovaṇṇamaye tālavane paññapesi. Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno.
mula_english:
265. Then, Ānanda, after many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, Queen Subhaddā thought: “It is a long time since I saw King Mahāsudassana. Suppose I were to go and see King Mahāsudassana?”

Then, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā addressed her women: “Come now, wash your heads, put on yellow clothes. It is long since we saw King Mahāsudassana, we shall go to see King Mahāsudassana.”

“Very good, Your Majesty,” they replied to Queen Subhaddā, and having washed their heads, put on yellow clothes, and then approached Queen Subhaddā.

Then, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā addressed the Counsellor-Jewel ( *pariṇāyakaratanaṃ* ): “Friend Counsellor-Jewel, draw up the fourfold army ( *caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ* ). It is long since we saw King Mahāsudassana, we shall go to see King Mahāsudassana.”

“Very good, Your Majesty,” Ānanda, the Counsellor-Jewel replied to Queen Subhaddā, and having drawn up the fourfold army, he reported to Queen Subhaddā: “The fourfold army has been drawn up, Your Majesty, now is the time to do as you think fit.”

Then, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā, together with the fourfold army and her women, went to the Dhamma Palace ( *dhammo pāsādo* ); and having entered, ascended to the great gabled chamber (*mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ*).

Having approached, she stood leaning against the door-post ( *dvārabāhaṃ* ) of the great gabled chamber.

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana, hearing the noise, thought: “What is this great noise, as of a crowd of people?” and coming out of the great gabled chamber, he saw Queen Subhaddā standing leaning against the door-post, and seeing Queen Subhaddā, he said this: “Stay there, Queen, do not enter!”

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana addressed a certain man: “Come, fellow, go to the great gabled chamber, bring out the golden couch (*sovaṇṇamayaṃ pallaṅkaṃ*) and place it among the golden palm-trees (*tālavane*).”

“Very good, Sire,” Ānanda, the man replied to King Mahāsudassana, and brought the golden couch out of the great gabled chamber and placed it among the golden palm-trees.

Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana lay down on his right side in the lion posture ( *sīhaseyyaṃ* ), placing one foot on the other, mindful and clearly aware.
commentary_pali: 265.Etadahosīti kadā etaṃ ahosi. Rañño kālaṅkiriyadivase. Tadā kira devatā cintesuṃ – ‘‘rājā anāthakālaṅkiriyaṃ mā karotu, orodhehi bahūhi dhītūhi puttehi parivāritova karotū’’ti. Atha deviṃ āvaṭṭetvā tassā evaṃ cittaṃ uppādesuṃ. Pītāni vatthānīti tāni kira pakatiyā rañño manāpāni, tasmā tāni pārupathāti āha. Ettheva devi tiṭṭhāti devi imaṃ jhānāgāraṃ nāma tumhehi saddhiṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ na hoti, jhānarativindanaṭṭhānaṃ mama, mā idha pāvisīti.
commentary_english: 265. Etadahosīti, when did this happen? On the day of the king's death. Then the deities thought: "May the king not die without protection, but die surrounded by many daughters and sons from his harem." Then, having turned the goddess, they produced such a thought in her mind. Pītāni vatthānīti, those yellow cloths were naturally pleasing to the king; therefore, he said they were suitable for wearing. Etheva devi tiṭṭhāti, "O goddess, stay right here!" This meditation chamber (jhānāgāra) is not a place to live with you, it is my place for attaining meditative joy, do not enter here.

mula_pali:
266. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddāya deviyā etadahosi – ‘vippasannāni kho rañño mahāsudassanassa indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, mā heva kho rājā mahāsudassano kālamakāsī’ti rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ etadavoca –

‘Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi, jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva , chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti itthisahassāni itthiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi, jīvite apekkhaṃ karohi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyati. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ janehi jīvite apekkhaṃ karohī’ti.
mula_english:
Then, Ānanda, Subhaddā the goddess had this thought: ‘The senses of King Mahāsudassana are clear, the color of his skin is pure and bright, may King Mahāsudassana not die at this moment!’ Thus, she spoke to King Mahāsudassana:

‘These eighty-four thousand cities, O Majesty, of which Kusāvatī is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand palaces, O Majesty, of which the Dhamma Palace is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand gabled halls, O Majesty, of which the Mahāviyūha Gabled Hall is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand couches, O Majesty, made of gold, made of silver, made of ivory, made of sandalwood, covered with woolen blankets, covered with cotton blankets, covered with silk blankets, spread with kadali-deer hide, with head-covers, with red cushions at both ends, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand elephants, O Majesty, adorned with gold ornaments, with gold banners, covered with golden nets, of which the Uposatha Nāga King is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand horses, O Majesty, adorned with gold ornaments, with gold banners, covered with golden nets, of which the Valāhaka Horse King is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand chariots, O Majesty, surrounded by lion skins, surrounded by tiger skins, surrounded by leopard skins, surrounded by brown woolen blankets, adorned with gold ornaments, with gold banners, covered with golden nets, of which the Vejayanta Chariot is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand jewels, O Majesty, of which the Jewel-Gem is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand women, O Majesty, of which the Woman-Gem is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand householders, O Majesty, of which the Householder-Gem is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand warriors, O Majesty, who follow you, of which the Counselor-Gem is the chief, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand cows, O Majesty, with easily drawn milk, with bronze milk pails, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand crore cloths, O Majesty, of fine linen, of fine cotton, of fine silk, of fine wool, these, O Majesty, are yours.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!
These eighty-four thousand pots of food, O Majesty, with morning and evening offerings of food, are offered to you.
Make a wish, O Majesty, arouse the desire to live there!’

commentary_pali:
266.Etadahosīti loke sattā nāma maraṇāsannakāle ativiya virocanti, tenassa rañño vippasannaindriyabhāvaṃ disvā evaṃ ahosi, tato mā rañño kālaṅkiriyā ahosīti tassa kālaṅkiriyaṃ anicchamānā sampati guṇamassa kathayitvā tiṭṭhamānākāraṃ karissāmīti cintetvā imāni te devātiādimāha. Tattha chandaṃ janehīti pemaṃ uppādehi, ratiṃ karohi. Jīvite apekkhanti jīvite sāpekkhaṃ, ālayaṃ, taṇhaṃ karohīti attho.

Evaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ devīti ‘‘mayaṃ kho, deva, itthiyo nāma pabbajitānaṃ upacārakathaṃ na jānāma, kathaṃ vadāma mahārājā’’ti rājānaṃ ‘‘pabbajito aya’’nti maññamānāya deviyā vutte – ‘‘evaṃ kho maṃ, tvaṃ devi, samudācarāhī’’tiādimāha. Garahitāti buddhehi paccekabuddhehi sāvakehi aññehi ca paṇḍitehi bahussutehi garahitā. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Sāpekkhakālakiriyā hi attanoyeva gehe yakkhakukkuraajagoṇamahiṃsamūsikakukkuṭaūkāmaṅgulādibhāvena nibbattanakāraṇaṃ hoti.

Evaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ devī Garahitā
commentary_english:
Thus it was: in the world, beings are seen to shine exceedingly at the time of approaching death. Seeing the king's clear state of senses, thus it was. Then, fearing the king's death, and not desiring his death, she praised his qualities and, thinking she would make a standing likeness, she said, "These are your gods," and so on.

There, create desire (*chandaṃ janehi*), generate love (*prema*), make delight (*ratim karohi*).

"Life is desired (*jīvite apekkha*)": in life, there is longing, attachment, and craving, this is the meaning.

Thus it was, you goddess (*evaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ devī*): "We, O god, as women, do not know how to speak words of service to the renunciates. How should we speak, O great king?" Thus said the goddess, thinking of the king, "He is a renunciate." "Thus it was, you goddess, behave thus," and so on, she said.

Despicable (*garahitā*): despicable to the Buddhas, the *pratyekabuddhas*, the disciples (*śrāvaka*), and other learned and greatly learned ones.

What is the cause (*kiṃ kāraṇā*)? Conditioned dying (*sāpekkhakālakiriyā*) is the cause of being reborn in one's own house as a *yakṣa*, dog, goat, buffalo, mouse, cock, bedbug, finger-sized being, and so on.

Thus it was, you goddess (*evaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ devī*), despicable (*garahitā*).

mula_pali:
267. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano subhaddaṃ deviṃ etadavoca –

‘Dīgharattaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ, devi, iṭṭhehi kantehi piyehi manāpehi samudācarittha; atha ca pana maṃ tvaṃ pacchime kāle aniṭṭhehi akantehi appiyehi amanāpehi samudācarasī’ti. ‘Kathaṃ carahi taṃ, deva, samudācarāmī’ti? ‘Evaṃ kho maṃ tvaṃ, devi, samudācara – ‘‘sabbeheva, deva, piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo, mā kho tvaṃ, deva, sāpekkho kālamakāsi, dukkhā sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā, garahitā ca sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te , deva, caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti itthisahassāni subhaddādevippamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni. Ettha deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te deva caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyati. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsī’’’ti.
mula_english:
267. Thus spoken, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana said this to Queen Subhaddā:

‘For a long time, my lady, you have treated me with things that are pleasing, lovely, dear, and agreeable; but now, in my final hour, you treat me with things that are displeasing, unlovely, unendearing, and disagreeable.’

‘How then, sire, should I treat you?’ ‘In this way, my lady, you should treat me: “All beloved and agreeable things are subject to separation, to loss, to change. Do not die, sire, with longing. Painful is death with longing; despicable is death with longing.”

These eighty-four thousand cities, sire, of which Kusāvatī, the royal capital, is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand palaces, sire, of which the Dhamma Palace is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand gabled halls, sire, of which the Mahāviyūha Gabled Hall is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand couches, sire, made of gold ( *sovarṇamaya*), made of silver ( *rūpiyamaya*), made of ivory (*dantamaya*), made of sandalwood ( *sāramaya*), covered with woolen blankets ( *gonakatthatā*), covered with embroidered coverlets (*paṭikatthatā*), covered with patchwork coverlets ( *paṭalikatthatā*), spread with choice deer hides ( *kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni*), with awnings ( *souttaracchadāni*), with red cushions at both ends ( *ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni*). Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand elephants, sire, adorned with gold ornaments ( *sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with gold banners ( *sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), of which Uposatha, the Nāga king, is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand horses, sire, adorned with gold ornaments (*sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with gold banners ( *sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), of which Valāhaka, the horse king, is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand chariots, sire, surrounded by lion skins ( *sīhacammaparivārāni*), surrounded by tiger skins (*byagghacammaparivārāni*), surrounded by leopard skins ( *dīpicammaparivārāni*), surrounded by woolen blankets ( *paṇḍukambalaparivārāni*), adorned with gold ornaments ( *sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with gold banners ( *sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), of which Vejayanta, the chariot, is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand jewels, sire, of which the jewel-gem is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand women, sire, of whom Subhaddā the queen is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand householders, sire, of whom the householder-jewel is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand *kṣatriyas*, sire, who are followers, of whom the general-jewel is the chief. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand cows, sire, with easily drawn milk, with bronze milk pails. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four *koṭis* of cloths, sire, of fine linen (*khomasukhumānaṃ*), of fine cotton (*kappāsikasukhumānaṃ*), of fine silk (*koseyyasukhumānaṃ*), of fine wool (*kambalasukhumānaṃ*). Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.

These eighty-four thousand dishes of rice, sire, are brought to you every morning and evening. Abandon desire, sire, abandon longing for life.’"

mula_pali:
268. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ānanda, subhaddā devī parodi assūni pavattesi. Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī assūni puñchitvā pamajjitvā (sī. syā. pī.), puñjitvā (ka.) rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ etadavoca –

‘Sabbeheva , deva, piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo, mā kho tvaṃ, deva, sāpekkho kālamakāsi, dukkhā sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā, garahitā ca sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te , deva, caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni . Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha, jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti itthisahassāni itthiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha, jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te , deva, caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyati. Ettha , deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsī’ti.

Brahmalokūpagamaṃ
mula_english:
‘Thus,’ Ānanda, when it was said, Queen Subhaddā cried out and burst into tears.

Then, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā, wiping away her tears, said this to King Mahāsudassana:

‘Sire, all things that are pleasing and attractive are liable to change, to vanish, to become otherwise. Do not, Sire, die filled with longing. To die filled with longing is painful and blameworthy.
These eighty-four thousand cities are yours, of which Kusāvatī, the royal capital, is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand palaces are yours, of which Dhamma Palace is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand gabled halls are yours, of which the Great Gabled Hall is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand couches are yours, made of gold, silver, ivory and sandalwood, covered with fleeces, wool, spread with Kadali-deer hide, with head-covers and red cushions at both ends.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand elephants are yours, adorned with gold ornaments, with golden banners and covered with nets of gold, of which the Uposatha Nāga king is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand horses are yours, adorned with gold ornaments, with golden banners and covered with nets of gold, of which the Valāhaka steed king is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand chariots are yours, surrounded by lion skins, tiger skins and panther skins, surrounded by woolen blankets, adorned with gold ornaments, with golden banners and covered with nets of gold, of which the Vejayanta chariot is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand jewels are yours, of which the jewel-gem is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand women are yours, of which the woman-jewel is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand householders are yours, of which the householder-jewel is the chief.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand nobles are yours, followed by the guide-jewel, the leading jewel.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand milch cows are yours, easily milked, with bronze milk-pails for milking.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand crore cloths are yours, made of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk and fine wool.
Here, Sire, abandon desire, abandon the longing to live.
These eighty-four thousand dishes of rice are yours, with evening and morning meals regularly served.’
Here
deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsī’ti. brahmalokūpagamaṃ

O deity, abandon desire, abandon longing for life, thus [it is said]. Ascent to the world of Brahman.
commentary_pali:
268.Athakho, ānanda, subhaddā devī assūni puñchitvāti devī ekamantaṃ gantvā roditvā kanditvā assūni puñchitvā etadavoca.

Brahmalokūpagamavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī assūni puñchitvā: Then, Ānanda, Subhaddā the goddess, wiping away her tears,
brahmalokūpagamavaṇṇanā: Description of going to the Brahma world.

mula_pali: 269. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano nacirasseva kālamakāsi. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā manuññaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuttāvissa bhattasammado hoti, evameva kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa māraṇantikā vedanā ahosi. Kālaṅkato ca, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano sugatiṃ brahmalokaṃ upapajji. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano caturāsīti vassasahassāni kumārakīḷaṃ kīḷitaṃ (ka.), kīḷikaṃ (sī. pī.) kīḷi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni oparajjaṃ kāresi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni rajjaṃ kāresi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni gihibhūto gihībhūto (sī. pī.) dhamme pāsāde brahmacariyaṃ cari brahmacariyamacari (ka.). So cattāro brahmavihāre bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā brahmalokūpago ahosi.
mula_english:
269.
‘‘Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana not long after died.

And just as, Ānanda, a householder or his son might feel drowsy after a delicious meal, so, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana had a deadly sensation.

And after King Mahāsudassana had died, Ānanda, he was reborn in a good destination, the Brahma-world (brahmalokaṃ).

King Mahāsudassana, Ānanda, engaged in boyish sports for eighty-four thousand years.

For eighty-four thousand years he exercised the viceroyalty.

For eighty-four thousand years he ruled as King.

For eighty-four thousand years, as a householder, he lived the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ cari) in the Dhamma palace.

Having developed the four divine abodes (brahmavihāre), on the dissolution of his body, after death, he was reborn in the Brahma-world (brahmalokūpago ahosi).
commentary_pali: 269.Gahapatissa vāti kasmā āha? Tesaṃ kira soṇaseṭṭhiputtādīnaṃ viya mahatī sampatti hoti, soṇassa kira seṭṭhiputtassa ekā bhattapāti dve satasahassāni agghati. Iti tesaṃ tādisaṃ bhattaṃ bhuttānaṃ muhuttaṃ bhattasammado bhattamucchā bhattakilamatho hoti.
commentary_english: "Why is *gahapatissa vā* [said]?" It is said that for them, like Soṇaseṭṭhiputta and others, there is great wealth. It is said that one food bowl of Soṇa the merchant's son is worth two hundred thousand. Thus, for them, having eaten such food, there is for a moment food-intoxication (*bhattasammado*), food-fainting (*bhattamucchā*), food-weariness (*bhattakilamatho*).

mula_pali: 270. ‘‘Siyā kho panānanda, evamassa – ‘añño nūna tena samayena rājā mahāsudassano ahosī’ti, na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ahaṃ tena samayena rājā mahāsudassano ahosiṃ. Mama tāni caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni, mama tāni caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti itthisahassāni subhaddādevippamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni, mama tāni caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ, mama tāni caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyittha.
mula_english: 270. Now, Ānanda, you might think, 'At that time King Mahāsudassana was someone else.' But Ānanda, you should not see it that way. At that time, I was King Mahāsudassana. Those eighty-four thousand cities, of which Kuśāvatī was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand palaces, of which the Dharma Palace was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand peaked houses, of which the Great Array Peaked House was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand couches – made of gold ( *sovaṇṇamaya* ), made of silver ( *rūpiyamaya* ), made of ivory ( *dantamaya* ), made of hardwood (*sāramaya*), covered with long-fleeced woolen blankets (*gonakatthatāni*), with patchwork quilts (*paṭikatthatāni*), with embroidered coverlets (*paṭalikatthatāni*), with coverings of choice deer hide (*kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni*) – with awnings (*sauttaracchadāni*), with cushions red on both sides (*ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni*) were mine; those eighty-four thousand elephants adorned with gold (*sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with golden banners (*sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), headed by the Upoṣatha Nāga-king, were mine; those eighty-four thousand horses adorned with gold (*sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with golden banners (*sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), headed by the Vālāhaka horse-king, were mine; those eighty-four thousand chariots with coverings of lion skins (*sīhacammaparivārāni*), coverings of tiger skins (*byagghacammaparivārāni*), coverings of leopard skins (*dīpicammaparivārāni*), coverings of yellow woolen blankets (*paṇḍukambalaparivārāni*), adorned with gold (*sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni*), with golden banners (*sovaṇṇadhajāni*), covered with nets of gold (*hemajālapaṭicchannāni*), headed by the Vejayanta chariot, were mine; those eighty-four thousand jewels, of which the jewel-gem was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand women, of which Subhaddādevī was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand householders, of which the householder-gem was the chief, were mine; those eighty-four thousand nobles, the followers of the counselor-gem, were mine; those eighty-four thousand milk cows, easy to milk, with bronze milk pails, were mine; those eighty-four *koṭi*s of thousands of cloths, of fine linen (*khomasukhumānaṃ*), of fine cotton (*kappāsikasukhumānaṃ*), of fine silk (*koseyyasukhumānaṃ*), of fine wool (*kambalasukhumānaṃ*), were mine; and twice daily, morning and evening, eighty-four thousand rice-soup dishes were brought to me as food.

mula_pali: 271. ‘‘Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītinagarasahassānaṃ ekaññeva taṃ nagaraṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ kusāvatī rājadhānī. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītipāsādasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so pāsādo hoti, yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ dhammo pāsādo. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītikūṭāgārasahassānaṃ ekaññeva taṃ kūṭāgāraṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītipallaṅkasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so pallaṅko hoti, yaṃ tena samayena paribhuñjāmi yadidaṃ sovaṇṇamayo vā rūpiyamayo vā dantamayo vā sāramayo vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītināgasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so nāgo hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ uposatho nāgarājā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītiassasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so asso hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ valāhako assarājā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītirathasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so ratho hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ vejayantaratho. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītiitthisahassānaṃ ekāyeva sā itthī hoti, yā tena samayena paccupaṭṭhāti khattiyānī vā vessinī vessāyinī (syā.), velāmikānī (ka. sī. pī.) velāmikā (saṃ. ni. 3.96) vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītivatthakoṭisahassānaṃ ekaṃyeva taṃ dussayugaṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena paridahāmi khomasukhumaṃ vā kappāsikasukhumaṃ vā koseyyasukhumaṃ vā kambalasukhumaṃ vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītithālipākasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so thālipāko hoti, yato nāḷikodanaparamaṃ bhuñjāmi tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ.
mula_english:
271. ‘And of those eighty-four thousand cities, Ānanda, there was just one city in which I dwelt at that time, namely, Kusāvatī, the capital.
And of those eighty-four thousand palaces, Ānanda, there was just one palace in which I dwelt at that time, namely, the Dhamma Palace.
And of those eighty-four thousand peaked-roof halls, Ānanda, there was just one peaked-roof hall in which I dwelt at that time, namely, the Great Array peaked-roof hall.
And of those eighty-four thousand couches, Ānanda, there was just one couch that I used at that time, namely, one made of gold, silver, ivory, or heartwood.
And of those eighty-four thousand elephants, Ānanda, there was just one elephant that I rode at that time, namely, the royal elephant Uposatha.
And of those eighty-four thousand steeds, Ānanda, there was just one steed that I rode at that time, namely, the royal steed Valāhaka.
And of those eighty-four thousand chariots, Ānanda, there was just one chariot that I rode at that time, namely, the Vejayanta chariot.
And of those eighty-four thousand women, Ānanda, there was just one woman who attended on me at that time, namely, the noble Khattiyānī or the merchant's daughter Vessinī.
And of those eighty-four thousand kotis of garments, Ānanda, there was only one pair of garments that I wore at that time, one made either of fine linen *khoma*, fine cotton *kappāsika*, fine silk *koseyya*, or fine wool *kambala*.
And of those eighty-four thousand rice-offerings, Ānanda, there was just one plate from which I ate at most a measure of rice (*nāḷikodana*) with suitable curry (*sūpeyya*).’
commentary_pali:
271.Yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmīti yattha vasāmi, taṃ ekaṃyeva nagaraṃ hoti, avasesesu puttadhītādayo ceva dāsamanussā ca vasiṃsu. Pāsādakūṭāgāresupi eseva nayo. Pallaṅkādīsupi ekaṃyeva pallaṅkaṃ paribhuñjati, sesā puttādīnaṃ paribhogā honti. Itthīsupi ekāva paccupaṭṭhāti, sesā parivāramattā honti, paridahāmīti ekameva dussayugaṃ nivāsemi, sesāni parivāretvā vicarantānaṃ asītisahassādhikānaṃ soḷasannaṃ purisasatasahassānaṃ honti. Bhuñjāmīti paramappamāṇena nāḷikodanamattaṃ bhuñjāmi, sesaṃ parivāretvā vicarantānaṃ cattālīsasahassādhikānaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ purisasatasahassānaṃ hotīti dasseti. Ekathālipāko hi dasannaṃ janānaṃ pahoti.

Etāni pana caturāsīti nagarasahassāni ceva pāsādasahassāni ca kūṭāgārasahassāni ca ekissāyeva paṇṇasālāya nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni nipajjanatthāya dinnamañcakassa nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti hatthisahassāni assasahassāni rathasahassāni nisīdanatthāya dinnapīṭhassa nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti maṇisahassāni ekadīpassa nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti pokkharaṇīsahassāni ekapokkharaṇiyā nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti itthisahassāni puttasahassāni gahapatisahassāni paribhogabhājanapattathālaka dhamakaraṇa parissāvana ārakaṇṭaka pipphalaka nakhacchedana kuñcikakaṇṇamalaharaṇī pādakathalika upāhana chatta kattarayaṭṭhidānassa nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti dhenusahassāni gorasadānassa nissandena nibbattāni. Caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni nivāsanapārupanadānassa nissandena nibbattāni . Caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni bhojanadānassa nissandena nibbattānīti veditabbāni.
commentary_english:
271. "That which I, at that time, inhabit (ajjhāvasāmī)" means that the city where I dwell is only one; in the remaining [cities], sons, daughters, and slaves lived. The same method applies to palaces and peaked houses. Among couches and so on, he enjoys only one couch; the rest are for the enjoyment of his sons and so on. Among women, only one attends to him; the rest are merely attendants. "I put on (paridahāmī)" means I wear only one pair of garments; the rest are for the sixteen hundred thousand men who wander around, surrounded by a retinue of over eighty thousand. "I eat (bhuñjāmī)" means I eat only a nāḷi measure of rice with the highest restraint; he shows that the rest is for the eight hundred thousand men who wander around, surrounded by a retinue of over forty thousand. One pot of cooked rice is enough for ten people.

However, it should be understood that these eighty-four thousand cities, thousands of palaces, and thousands of peaked houses arose from the overflow (nissandena) of a single leaf hut. The eighty-four thousand couches arose from the overflow of the couch given for lying down. The eighty-four thousand elephants, thousands of horses, and thousands of chariots arose from the overflow of the seat given for sitting. The eighty-four thousand jewels arose from the overflow of a single lamp. The eighty-four thousand ponds arose from the overflow of a single pond. The eighty-four thousand women, thousands of sons, thousands of householders, containers for enjoyment, bowls, dishes, water filters, ārākaṇṭaka, pipphalaka, nail clippers, keys, earwax removers, footstools, shoes, umbrellas, scissors, staffs, [all arose from the overflow of his] giving. The eighty-four thousand cows arose from the overflow of giving dairy products. The eighty-four thousand crores of cloths arose from the overflow of giving clothes for wearing and wrapping. The eighty-four thousand pots of cooked rice arose from the overflow of giving food.

mula_pali:
272. ‘‘Passānanda, sabbete saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā. Evaṃ aniccā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā; evaṃ addhuvā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā; evaṃ anassāsikā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā! Yāvañcidaṃ, ānanda , alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccituṃ.

‘‘Chakkhattuṃ kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, abhijānāmi imasmiṃ padese sarīraṃ nikkhipitaṃ, tañca kho rājāva samāno cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyapatto sattaratanasamannāgato, ayaṃ sattamo sarīranikkhepo. Na kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, taṃ padesaṃ samanupassāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yattha tathāgato aṭṭhamaṃ sarīraṃ nikkhipeyyā’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Aniccā vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho’’ti.

Mahāsudassanasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
272. ‘See, Ānanda, all those conditioned states (*saṅkhārā*) of the past have vanished and changed! Thus, Ānanda, conditioned states (*saṅkhārā*) are impermanent (*aniccā*); thus, Ānanda, conditioned states (*saṅkhārā*) are unstable (*addhuvā*); thus, Ānanda, conditioned states (*saṅkhārā*) can bring us no comfort (*anassāsikā*)! Ānanda, it is enough to experience revulsion (*nibbindituṃ*) towards all formations (*sabbasaṅkhāresu*), enough to become dispassionate (*virajjituṃ*) towards them, enough to be liberated (*vimuccituṃ*) from them.’

‘Six times, Ānanda, I recall discarding the body (*sarīraṃ nikkhipitaṃ*) in this place, and at the seventh time I discarded it as a wheel-turning monarch (*cakkavattī*), a righteous king (*dhammiko dhammarājā*) who had conquered the four quarters (*cāturanto*) and established a firm rule (*vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyapatto*), and who possessed the seven treasures (*sattaratanasamannāgato*). This is the seventh discarding of the body (*sarīranikkhepo*). But, Ānanda, I do not see any place in this world (*sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake*) with its devas and maras and Brahmas, or in this generation with its ascetics and Brahmins (*sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya*), princes and people (*sadevamanussāya*), where the *Tathāgata* will for an eighth time discard the body (*sarīraṃ nikkhipeyya*.’

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*). Having said this, the Well-Gone (*sugato*), the Teacher (*satthā*) then said further:

"Impermanent (*aniccā*) indeed are conditioned states (*saṅkhārā*), by nature they rise and decay;

Having arisen, they are destroyed; their passing away is bliss (*tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho*."’

The Great Splendor Discourse (*mahāsudassanasuttaṃ*) is finished, the fourth.
commentary_pali:
272. Evaṃ bhagavā mahāsudassanassa sampattiṃ ādito paṭṭhāya vitthārena kathetvā sabbaṃ taṃ dārakānaṃ paṃsvāgārakīḷanaṃ viya dassento parinibbānamañcake nipannova passānandātiādimāha. Tattha vipariṇatāti pakativijahanena nibbutapadīpo viya apaññattikabhāvaṃ gatā. Evaṃ aniccā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārāti evaṃ hutvā abhāvaṭṭhena aniccā.

Ettāvatā bhagavā yathā nāma puriso satahatthubbedhe campakarukkhe nisseṇiṃ bandhitvā abhiruhitvā campakapupphaṃ ādāya nisseṇiṃ muñcanto otareyya, evameva nisseṇiṃ bandhanto viya anekavassakoṭisatasahassubbedhaṃ mahāsudassanasampattiṃ āruyha sampattimatthake ṭhitaṃ aniccalakkhaṇaṃ ādāya nisseṇiṃ muñcanto viya otiṇṇo. Teneva pubbe vasabharājā dīghabhāṇakattherānaṃ lohapāsādassa pācīnapasse ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ imaṃ suttaṃ sajjhāyantānaṃ sutvā – ‘‘kiṃ, bho, mayhaṃ ayyakena ettha vuttaṃ, attano khāditapītaṭṭhāne sampattimeva kathetī’’ti cintento – ‘‘evaṃ aniccā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā’’ti vuttakāle ‘‘imaṃ, bho, disvā pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumatā evaṃ vutta’’nti vāmahatthaṃ samiñjitvā dakkhiṇahatthena apphoṭetvā – ‘‘sādhu sādhū’’ti tuṭṭhahadayo sādhukāraṃ adāsi.

Evaṃ addhuvāti evaṃ udakapupphuḷādayo viya dhuvabhāvavirahitā. Evaṃ anassāsikāti evaṃ supinake pītapānīyaṃ viya anulittacandanaṃ viya ca assāsavirahitā.

Evaṃ addhuvā Evaṃ anassāsikā

Sarīraṃ nikkhipeyyāti sarīraṃ chaḍḍeyya. Idāni aññassa sarīrassa nikkhepo vā paṭijagganaṃ vā natthi kilesapahīnattā, ānanda, tathāgatassāti vadati. Idaṃ pana vatvā puna theraṃ āmantesi, cakkavattino ānubhāvo nāma rañño pabbajitassa sattame divase antaradhāyati. Mahāsudassanassa pana kālaṅkiriyato sattameva divase sattaratanapākārā sattaratanatālā caturāsīti pokkharaṇīsahassāni dhammapāsādo dhammapokkharaṇī cakkaratananti sabbametaṃ antaradhāyīti. Hatthiādīsu pana ayaṃ dhammatā khīṇāyukā saheva kālaṅkaronti. Āyusese sati hatthiratanaṃ uposathakulaṃ gacchati, assaratanaṃ valāhakakulaṃ, maṇiratanaṃ vepullapabbatameva gacchati. Itthiratanassa ānubhāvo antaradhāyati. Gahapatiratanassa cakkhu pākatikameva hoti. Pariṇāyakaratanassa veyyattiyaṃ nassati.

Sarīraṃ nikkhipeyyā

Idamavoca bhagavāti idaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āruḷhañca anāruḷhañca sabbaṃ bhagavā avoca. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

Idamavoca bhagavā

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Mahāsudassanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
272. Thus, the Blessed One, having extensively described the prosperity of Mahāsudassana, starting from the beginning, and showing all that as children's play with sand houses, said, ending with "seeing bliss" (passānandā).

There, "having undergone change" (vipariṇatā) means having gone to a state of non-perception, like an extinguished lamp due to the abandonment of nature.

"Thus, impermanent are conditioned things (evaṃ aniccā kho, *ānanda*, saṅkhārā)" means thus, having been, they are impermanent due to the state of non-being.

In this way, the Blessed One, just as a man, having built a ladder on a *campaka* tree a hundred cubits high, and having climbed up, and having taken a *campaka* flower, would descend, releasing the ladder, just so, having ascended to the prosperity of Mahāsudassana, which is a hundred thousand million leagues high, and having stood at the top of the prosperity, having taken the characteristic of impermanence, he descended, releasing the ladder.

Therefore, formerly, King Vasabha, having heard the long reciters of the *sūtra* reciting this *sūtra* in the eastern side of the iron palace, on the ambala support, thinking, "What, sir, has been said here by my ancestor? He only describes the prosperity in the place where he ate and drank," at the time when "Thus, impermanent are conditioned things, *ānanda*," was said, "This, sir, having seen with five eyes, was thus said by the one with vision," having contracted his left hand, and having clapped with his right hand, he gave approval, his heart delighted, saying, "Good, good!"

"Thus, unstable (evaṃ addhuvā)" means thus, like water bubbles and so on, devoid of a stable nature.

"Thus, without breath (evaṃ anassāsikā)" means thus, like water drunk in a dream, and like *candana* sandalwood smeared on, devoid of breath.

Thus, unstable. Thus, without breath.

"The body one should discard (sarīraṃ nikkhipeyya)" means the body one should abandon (sarīraṃ chaḍḍeyya).

Now, there is no discarding or attending to another body for the Tathāgata, *ānanda*, because of the abandonment of defilements, thus he speaks.

Having said this, he again addressed the elder: "The power of a wheel-turning monarch disappears on the seventh day after he renounces the world."

Moreover, on the seventh day after the death of Mahāsudassana, the seven jeweled walls, the seven jeweled palisades, the eighty-four thousand lotus ponds, the Dharma palace, the Dharma lotus pond, the jewel wheel—all this disappeared.

Moreover, among elephants and others, this is the nature: when their life is exhausted, they die together.

When life is remaining, the elephant jewel goes to the Uposatha clan, the horse jewel to the Valāhaka clan, the jewel gem goes to Mount Vipulla itself.

The power of the woman jewel disappears.

The eye of the householder jewel is just natural.

The skill of the advisor jewel is destroyed.

The body one should discard.

"Thus spoke the Blessed One (idamavoca bhagavā)" means the Blessed One spoke all this, both that which is established in the Pāli and that which is not established.

The rest is just of obvious meaning.

Thus spoke the Blessed One.

Thus ends the Mahāsudassana Sutta Commentary in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, Commentary to the Dīgha Nikāya.

mula_pali: 273. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nātike nādike (sī. syā. pī.) viharati giñjakāvasathe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu cetiyavaṃsesu (ka.) kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu macchasurasenesu (syā.), macchasūrasenesu (sī. pī.) – ‘‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno upapannoti (ka.). Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva sakiṃdeva (ka.) imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’’ti.
mula_english:
273. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Nātika in the Brick House (Giñjakāvasatha). Then on that occasion, the Blessed One was describing the rebirths of the devotees who had passed away in various districts all around – in Kāsi, Kosala, the Vajjis, the Mallas, the Cetis, the Vaṃsas, the Kurus, the Pañcālas, and the Middle Sūrasenas – [saying]: “So-and-so has been reborn there, so-and-so has been reborn there.”

More than fifty Nātika devotees, with the destruction of the five lower fetters (orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni), were reborn spontaneously (opapātikā), and would attain *parinirvāṇa* there, not liable to return from that world.

Rather more than ninety Nātika devotees, with the destruction of the three fetters and weakening of greed, hatred, and delusion (rāgadosamohānaṃ), were once-returners (sakadāgāmino), and after coming to this world only once, would make an end of suffering (duḥkha).

More than five hundred Nātika devotees, with the destruction of the three fetters, were stream-enterers (sotāpannā), not liable to the downward course, assured, destined for enlightenment (*sambodhi*).

mula_pali: 274. Assosuṃ kho nātikiyā paricārakā – ‘‘bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ pañhāveyyākaraṇaṃ (syā. ka.) sutvā.
mula_english:
And then the Nātika attendants heard: “The Blessed One is declaring, up and down the country, regarding devotees who have died and passed away, their rebirths in Kāsi, Kosala, the Vajjis, the Mallas, the Cetis, the Vaṃsas, the Kurus, the Pañcālas, and the Middle Sūrasenas: ‘So-and-so has been reborn there, so-and-so has been reborn there.’

More than fifty Nātika attendants, through the destruction of the five lower fetters ( *orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*), have been reborn spontaneously ( *opapātikā*) there, and will attain final emancipation ( *parinibbāyino*) there, without returning from that world ( *anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā*).

Rather more than ninety Nātika attendants, through the destruction of three fetters, and the lessening of lust ( *rāga*), hatred ( *dosa*), and delusion ( *moha*), are once-returners ( *sakadāgāmino*), who, on returning only once more to this world, will put an end to suffering ( *dukkhassantaṃ karissanti*).

More than five hundred Nātika attendants, through the destruction of three fetters, are stream-enterers ( *sotāpannā*), no longer subject to falling away ( *avinipātadhammā*), assured, destined for enlightenment ( *sambodhiparāyaṇā*).’

And with that, the Nātika attendants were delighted, joyful, filled with elation and happiness, having heard the Blessed One's exposition of questions ( *pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ*) .

mula_pali:
275. Assosi kho āyasmā ānando – ‘‘bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā’’ti.

Ānandaparikathā
mula_english:
275. The Venerable Ānanda heard that the Blessed One was explaining the rebirths of various attendants who had died and passed away throughout the country—in Kāśī and Kosala, among the Vajjis and the Mallas, the Cetis and Vaṃsas, the Kurus and Pañcālas, and the Macchas and Śūrasenas—saying, "So-and-so has been reborn there, so-and-so has been reborn there."

More than fifty attendants from Nādika, through the destruction of the five lower fetters ( *orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā* ), were reborn spontaneously ( *opapātikā* ), and would attain *parinirvāṇa* there, never to return to this world ( *anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā* ).

More than ninety attendants from Nādika, through the destruction of the three fetters and the weakening of greed ( *rāga* ), hatred ( *dosa* ), and delusion ( *moha* ), were once-returners ( *sakadāgāmino* ), who, after returning to this world only once more, would put an end to suffering ( *dukkhassantaṃ karissanti* ).

And more than five hundred attendants from Nādika, through the destruction of the three fetters, were stream-enterers ( *sotāpannā* ), no longer subject to falling into states of woe, assured, destined for full enlightenment ( *sambodhi* ).

Then the attendants from Nādika were delighted, pleased, and filled with joy and happiness to hear the Blessed One's answers to their questions.

The Story about Ānanda ( *ānandaparikathā* ).

mula_pali: 276. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘ime kho panāpi ahesuṃ māgadhakā paricārakā bahū ceva rattaññū ca abbhatītā kālaṅkatā. Suññā maññe aṅgamagadhā aṅgamāgadhakehi aṅgamāgadhikehi (syā.) paricārakehi abbhatītehi kālaṅkatehi. Te kho panāpi tena kho panāpi (syā.) ahesuṃ buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārino. Te abbhatītā kālaṅkatā bhagavatā abyākatā; tesampissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Ayaṃ kho panāpi ahosi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro dhammiko dhammarājā hito brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ negamānañceva jānapadānañca. Apissudaṃ manussā kittayamānarūpā viharanti – ‘evaṃ no so dhammiko dhammarājā sukhāpetvā kālaṅkato, evaṃ mayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño vijite phāsu phāsukaṃ (syā.) viharimhā’ti. So kho panāpi ahosi buddhe pasanno dhamme pasanno saṅghe pasanno sīlesu paripūrakārī. Apissudaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘yāva maraṇakālāpi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpo kālaṅkato’ti. So abbhatīto kālaṅkato bhagavatā abyākato. Tassapissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Bhagavato kho pana sambodhi magadhesu. Yattha kho pana bhagavato sambodhi magadhesu, kathaṃ tatra bhagavā māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya. Bhagavā ce kho pana māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya, dīnamanā ninnamanā (syā.), dīnamānā (sī. pī.) tenassu māgadhakā paricārakā; yena kho panassu dīnamanā māgadhakā paricārakā kathaṃ te bhagavā na byākareyyā’’ti?
mula_english:
And he thought: ‘There were also Magadhan attendants of long standing who have died and passed away.

I think Aṅgamagadha is empty of Aṅgamāgadhas.

They were devoted to the Buddha, devoted to the Dharma, devoted to the Saṃgha, and perfectly fulfilled in morality.

They have died and passed away and the Blessed One has not declared [their destiny]; it would be good to have a declaration about this: it would make the multitude have faith and so attain a good rebirth.

Now King Śreṇiya Bimbisāra of Magadha was a righteous and lawful king, a friend of Brahmins, householders, townsfolk and country-dwellers.

People living there rejoiced, saying: ‘Thus, having made [us] happy, that righteous and lawful king has passed away, so we lived comfortably in the realm of that righteous and lawful king.’

And he was devoted to the Buddha, devoted to the Dharma, devoted to the Saṃgha, and perfectly fulfilled in morality.

People said: “King Śreṇiya Bimbisāra of Magadha, who praised the Blessed One until the moment of his death, is dead!”

He has passed away, he has died and the Blessed One has not declared [his destiny].

It would be good to have a declaration about this; it would make the multitude have faith and so attain a good rebirth.

Besides, the Blessed One gained complete awakening in Magadha.

Since the Blessed One gained complete awakening in Magadha, why does the Blessed One not declare the future destiny of the Magadhan attendants who have died and passed away?

If the Blessed One does not declare the future destiny of the Magadhan attendants who have died and passed away, the Magadhan attendants would be unhappy; since the Magadhan attendants would be unhappy, why would the Blessed One not declare it?”

mula_pali: 277. Idamāyasmā ānando māgadhake paricārake ārabbha eko raho anuvicintetvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – ‘‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇāti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā’’ti . Ime kho panāpi, bhante, ahesuṃ māgadhakā paricārakā bahū ceva rattaññū ca abbhatītā kālaṅkatā. Suññā maññe aṅgamagadhā aṅgamāgadhakehi paricārakehi abbhatītehi kālaṅkatehi. Te kho panāpi, bhante, ahesuṃ buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārino, te abbhatītā kālaṅkatā bhagavatā abyākatā. Tesampissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Ayaṃ kho panāpi, bhante, ahosi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro dhammiko dhammarājā hito brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ negamānañceva jānapadānañca. Apissudaṃ manussā kittayamānarūpā viharanti – ‘evaṃ no so dhammiko dhammarājā sukhāpetvā kālaṅkato. Evaṃ mayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño vijite phāsu viharimhā’ti.
