So kho panāpi, bhante, ahosi buddhe pasanno dhamme pasanno saṅghe pasanno sīlesu paripūrakārī. Apissudaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘yāva maraṇakālāpi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpo kālaṅkato’ti. So abbhatīto kālaṅkato bhagavatā abyākato; tassapissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Bhagavato kho pana, bhante, sambodhi magadhesu. Yattha kho pana , bhante, bhagavato sambodhi magadhesu, kathaṃ tatra bhagavā māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya? Bhagavā ce kho pana, bhante, māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya dīnamanā tenassu māgadhakā paricārakā; yena kho panassu dīnamanā māgadhakā paricārakā kathaṃ te bhagavā na byākareyyā’’ti. Idamāyasmā ānando māgadhake paricārake ārabbha bhagavato sammukhā parikathaṃ katvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.
mula_english:
277. Then the venerable Ānanda, reflecting in solitude concerning the Magadhan devotees, rose at dawn, approached the Blessed One, saluted him, and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Lord, I have heard that the Blessed One is declaring the destiny of departed devotees in various regions—in Kāśi, Kosala, the Vajjis, the Mallas, the Cetis, the Vaṃsas, the Kurus, the Pañcālas, and the Middle Śūrasenas—[saying,] ‘So-and-so has been reborn there, so-and-so has been reborn there.’

More than fifty Nādika devotees, having abandoned the five lower fetters, have been reborn spontaneously and will attain *Nirvāṇa* without returning to this world.

More than ninety Nādika devotees, having abandoned the three fetters, and with the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners, who, returning only once more to this world, will make an end of suffering.

More than five hundred Nādika devotees, having abandoned the three fetters, are stream-enterers, no longer subject to downfall, assured, destined for enlightenment.

Through this, the Nādika devotees were delighted, joyful, filled with rapture and gladness, having heard the Blessed One's explanation of the questions.

These too, Lord, were Magadhan devotees, many and long-standing, who have passed away.

I think Aṅga and Magadha are empty of Magadhan devotees who have passed away.

Those too, Lord, were devoted to the Buddha, devoted to the *Dharma*, devoted to the *Saṃgha*, and perfect in their morality. Those have passed away, but have not been declared by the Blessed One.

For them too, there is a good explanation, many people would be pleased, and then they would go to a good destination.

This too, Lord, was King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, a righteous king, a king of *Dharma*, a benefactor to *Brāhmaṇas* and householders, as well as to townsfolk and countryfolk.

People are living recounting: ‘Thus that righteous king of ours, that king of *Dharma*, having made us happy, has passed away.

Thus we lived easily in the domain of that righteous king of *Dharma*.’

He too, Lord, was devoted to the Buddha, devoted to the *Dharma*, devoted to the *Saṃgha*, and perfect in his morality.

People say: ‘Even until the time of his death, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, praising the Blessed One, has passed away.’

He has passed away, but has not been declared by the Blessed One; for him too, there is a good explanation, many people would be pleased, and then they would go to a good destination.

Moreover, Lord, the Blessed One’s enlightenment was in Magadha.

Since, Lord, the Blessed One’s enlightenment was in Magadha, how is it that the Blessed One does not declare the destiny of the Magadhan devotees who have passed away? If the Blessed One did not declare the destiny of the Magadhan devotees who have passed away, the Magadhan devotees would be saddened; since the Magadhan devotees would be saddened, how could the Blessed One not declare it?”

Then the venerable Ānanda, speaking thus to the Blessed One about the Magadhan devotees, rose from his seat, saluted the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.
commentary_pali: 277.Bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpoti aho buddho, aho dhammo, aho saṅgho; aho dhammo svākkhātoti evaṃ kittayantova kālamakāsi. Bahujano pasīdeyyāti amhākaṃ pitā mātā bhātā bhaginī putto dhītā sahāyako, tena amhehi saddhiṃ ekato bhuttā, ekato sayitā, tassa idañcidañca manāpaṃ akarimha, so kira anāgāmī sakadāgāmī sotāpanno; aho sādhu, aho suṭṭhūti evaṃ bahujano pasādaṃ āpajjeyya.
commentary_english: 277. bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpoti, thinking, "O Buddha! O Dharma! O Saṅgha! O the well-spoken Dharma!" in this way, he passed away while praising the Blessed One. bahujano pasīdeyyāti, [thinking,] "He is our father, mother, brother, sister, son, daughter, friend. Because of him, we ate together, slept together, and we did what was pleasing to him." He is said to be a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*), a stream-enterer (*sotāpanno*). "O good! O very good!" In this way, many people would gain faith.

mula_pali: 278. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante āyasmante ānande pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya nātikaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Nātike piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā giñjakāvasathaṃ pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā aṭṭhikatvā (sī. syā. pī.) manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā sabbacetasā (pī.) samannāharitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi – ‘‘gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’’ti. Addasā kho bhagavā māgadhake paricārake ‘‘yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito giñjakāvasathā nikkhamitvā vihārapacchāyāyaṃ paññatte āsane nisīdi.
mula_english:
Then, when the venerable Ānanda had recently departed, the Lord, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered Nātika for alms.

Having wandered for alms in Nātika, after the meal, returning from the alms-round, having washed his feet, having entered the Brick House, concerning the Magadhan devotees, having made a basis for reflection, having pondered, bringing everything to mind, on the prepared seat, he sat down, thinking: “I shall know their destiny and future state, whatever their destiny, whatever their future state.”

The Lord saw the Magadhan devotees, [and considered] “whatever their destiny, whatever their future state.”

Then, in the evening, the Lord, arising from seclusion, leaving the Brick House, sat down on the prepared seat in the shade of the monastery ( *vihāra*).
commentary_pali: 278.Gatinti ñāṇagatiṃ. Abhisamparāyanti ñāṇābhisamparāyameva. Addasā khoti kittake jane addasa? Catuvīsatisatasahassāni.
commentary_english: 278. *Gati* means knowledge (*jñāna*) as *gati*. *Abhisamparāya* means precisely knowledge as *abhisamparāya*. *Addasā kho*, how many people saw? Twenty-four hundred thousand.

mula_pali:
279. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘upasantapadisso upasantapatiso (ka.) bhante bhagavā bhātiriva bhagavato mukhavaṇṇo vippasannattā indriyānaṃ. Santena nūnajja bhante bhagavā vihārena vihāsī’’ti? ‘‘Yadeva kho me tvaṃ, ānanda, māgadhake paricārake ārabbha sammukhā parikathaṃ katvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto, tadevāhaṃ nātike piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā giñjakāvasathaṃ pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā samannāharitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃ – ‘gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’ti. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, ānanda, māgadhake paricārake ‘yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’’’ti.

Janavasabhayakkho
mula_english:
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, having bowed down to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Lord, the Blessed One's countenance looks calmed, the complexion of the Blessed One's face is clear, because the senses are so serene.

Lord, does the Blessed One dwell today in peace?" "Ānanda, after you spoke to me face to face about the devotees of Magadha and then left, I went to Nadika for alms, and after the meal, returning from the alms round, having washed my feet, I entered the Brick House, and reflecting on the devotees of Magadha, focusing my mind, considering everything in my heart, I sat down on the prepared seat, thinking: 'I will know their destiny, their future state—what their destiny is, what their future state is.'

I saw, Ānanda, the devotees of Magadha—'such is their destiny, such their future state.'"

Janavasabha Yakka
commentary_pali:
279.Upasantapadissoti upasantadassano. Bhātirivāti ativiya bhāti, ativiya virocati. Indriyānanti manacchaṭṭhānaṃ indriyānaṃ. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ ānandāti neva dasa, na vīsati, na sataṃ, na sahassaṃ, anūnādhikāni catuvīsatisatasahassāni addasanti āha.

Janavasabhayakkhavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
279.
*Upasantapadisso* means *upasantadassano*.
*Bhātirivā* means *ativiya bhāti, ativiya virocati*.
*Indriyāna* means *manacchaṭṭhānaṃ indriyānaṃ*.
*Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ ānandā* means *neva dasa, na vīsati, na sataṃ, na sahassaṃ, anūnādhikāni catuvīsatisatasahassāni addasanti āha*.

Explanation of the Janavasabha Yaksha.

mula_pali:
280. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, antarahito yakkho saddamanussāvesi – ‘janavasabho ahaṃ bhagavā ; janavasabho ahaṃ sugatā’ti. Abhijānāsi no tvaṃ, ānanda, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ sutaṃ sutvā (pī.) yadidaṃ janavasabho’’ti?

‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, bhante, abhijānāmi ito pubbe evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ sutaṃ yadidaṃ janavasabhoti, api ca me, bhante, lomāni haṭṭhāni ‘janavasabho’ti nāmadheyyaṃ sutvā. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘na hi nūna so orako yakkho bhavissati yadidaṃ evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ supaññattaṃ yadidaṃ janavasabho’’ti. ‘‘Anantarā kho, ānanda, saddapātubhāvā uḷāravaṇṇo me yakkho sammukhe pāturahosi . Dutiyampi saddamanussāvesi – ‘bimbisāro ahaṃ bhagavā; bimbisāro ahaṃ sugatāti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sahabyataṃ upapajjāmi, so tato cuto manussarājā bhavituṃ pahomi so tato cuto manussarājā, amanussarājā divi homi (sī. pī.).

so tato cuto manussarājā, amanussarājā divi homi (sī. pī.)

Ito satta tato satta, saṃsārāni catuddasa;

Nivāsamabhijānāmi, yattha me vusitaṃ pure.
mula_english:
280. Then the voice of a *yakkha* who had passed over cried out: “I am Janavasabha, Lord! I am Janavasabha, Well-Farer!”

Well, Ānanda, do you know anyone who formerly bore the name of Janavasabha?'

‘I must admit, Lord (bhante), that I have never heard such a name; and yet, on hearing the name “Janavasabha” my hairs stood on end. And I thought: “He whose name is Janavasabha will not be such a low-ranking *yakkha*!”’

Immediately after the sound manifested, a *yakkha* of great beauty appeared before me.

And uttered a second cry: “I am Bimbisāra, Lord! I am Bimbisāra, Well-Farer!

I have now for the seventh time been reborn into the entourage of the Lord Vessavana. Thus having passed away as a king of humans, I am now able to become a king of humans.

Seven times from here, seven times from there, fourteen existences; I remember the dwelling where I lived before.
commentary_pali:
280. Disvā pana me ettako jano maṃ nissāya dukkhā pamuttoti balavasomanassaṃ uppajji, cittaṃ pasīdi, cittassa pasannattā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ lohitaṃ pasīdi, lohitassa pasannattā manacchaṭṭhāni indriyāni pasīdiṃsūti sabbamidaṃ vatvā atha kho ānandātiādimāha. Tattha yasmā so bhagavato dhammakathaṃ sutvā dasasahassādhikassa janasatasahassassa jeṭṭhako hutvā sotāpanno jāto, tasmā janavasabhotissa nāmaṃ ahosi.

Ito sattāti ito devalokā cavitvā satta. Tato sattāti tato manussalokā cavitvā satta. Saṃsārāni catuddasāti sabbāpi catuddasakhandhapaṭipāṭiyo. Nivāsamabhijānāmīti jātivasena nivāsaṃ jānāmi. Yattha me vusitaṃ pureti yattha devesu ca vessavaṇassa sahabyataṃ upagatena manussesu ca rājabhūtena ito attabhāvato pureyeva mayā vusitaṃ. Pure evaṃ vusitattā eva ca idāni sotāpanno hutvā tīsu vatthūsu bahuṃ puññaṃ katvā tassānubhāvena upari nibbattituṃ samatthopi dīgharattaṃ vusitaṭṭhāne nikantiyā balavatāya ettheva nibbatto.

Ito sattā Tato sattā Saṃsārāni catuddasā Nivāsamabhijānāmī Yattha me vusitaṃ pure
commentary_english:
280. Seeing that so many people had been freed from suffering through reliance on me, a strong joy arose. My mind was calmed, and with the calming of my mind, the blood that arose from my mind was calmed. With the calming of my blood, the six faculties of mind were calmed. Having said all this, he then spoke, beginning with, "Then, Ānanda..."

There, because he, having heard the Blessed One's *dharma* talk, became the eldest of a hundred thousand people, exceeding ten thousand, and became a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*), therefore he was named Janavasabha Tissa.

"From here, beings" means beings, having passed away from here, from the world of the gods (*devaloka*).

"From there, beings" means beings, having passed away from there, from the world of humans (*manuṣyaloka*).

"*Saṃsārāni catuddasā*" means all the fourteen aggregates in order.

"I remember my dwelling" means I know my dwelling by way of birth (*jāti*).

"Where I have dwelt before" means where, among the gods and among humans, having attained companionship with Vessavaṇa and having been a king, I have dwelt before, even before this existence (*attabhāva*).

Because I had dwelt thus before, and because now, having become a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*), having done much merit (*puṇya*) in the three objects, although capable of being reborn above through the power of that, he was reborn right here due to the strong attachment to the place where he had dwelt for a long time.

From here, beings. From there, beings. The fourteen migrations (*saṃsārāni catuddasā*). I remember my dwelling (*nivāsamabhijānāmī*). Where I have dwelt before.

mula_pali:
281. ‘Dīgharattaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmi, āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāyā’ti. ‘Acchariyamidaṃ āyasmato janavasabhassa yakkhassa, abbhutamidaṃ āyasmato janavasabhassa yakkhassa. ‘‘Dīgharattaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmī’’ti ca vadesi, ‘‘āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāyā’’ti ca vadesi, kutonidānaṃ panāyasmā janavasabho yakkho evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ visesādhigamaṃ sañjānātīti? Na aññatra, bhagavā, tava sāsanā, na aññatra aññattha (sī. pī.), sugata, tava sāsanā; yadagge ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati ekantikato ekantato (syā.), ekantagato (pī.) abhippasanno, tadagge ahaṃ, bhante, dīgharattaṃ avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmi, āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāya. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, vessavaṇena mahārājena pesito virūḷhakassa mahārājassa santike kenacideva karaṇīyena addasaṃ bhagavantaṃ antarāmagge giñjakāvasathaṃ pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā samannāharitvā nisinnaṃ – ‘‘gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’’ti. Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhante, yaṃ vessavaṇassa mahārājassa tassaṃ parisāyaṃ bhāsato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘‘yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – bhagavantañca dakkhāmi, idañca bhagavato ārocessāmīti. Ime kho me, bhante, dvepaccayā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ’.

Devasabhā
mula_english:
‘For a long time, Lord (bhante), I have known myself to be exempt from states of woe, and now the desire arises in me to become a Once-Retumer.’
‘It is amazing, it is astonishing that the reverend yakṣa Janavasabha should say this.

‘‘For a long time, Lord (bhante), I have known myself to be exempt from states of woe,’’ you said, ‘‘and now the desire arises in me to become a Once-Retumer,’’ you said, what is the reason, venerable Janavasabha, that the yakṣa knows such outstanding, excellent attainments? Not otherwise, Blessed One (bhagavā), than through your teaching (sāsanā), not otherwise, Well-Gone One (sugata), than through your teaching (sāsanā); from the time when I became fully committed and gained complete faith in the Blessed One (bhagavati), from then on, Lord (bhante), for a long time I have known myself to be exempt from states of woe, and now the desire arises in me to become a Once-Retumer.

And here, Lord (bhante), having been sent by King Vessavana on some business to King Virūḷhaka, I saw the Lord (bhagavantaṃ) entering the Brick House and, having thought over, considered and given his whole mind to the question of the Magadhan devotees, he sat down, saying: ‘I shall know their destiny and future lot, whatever it is.’

And since I had only just heard King Vessavana announce to his assembly what those folk’s fates were,

it is no wonder that I thought: ‘I will go and see the Lord (bhagavantaṃ) and report this to him.’

And these, Lord (bhante), are the two reasons why I came to see the Lord (bhagavantaṃ).’

Devasabhā
commentary_pali:
281.Āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhatīti imināhaṃ sotāpannoti na suttappamattova hutvā kālaṃ vītināmesiṃ. Sakadāgāmimaggatthāya pana me vipassanā āraddhā. Ajjeva ajjeva paṭivijjhissāmīti evaṃ saussāho viharāmīti dasseti. Yadaggeti laṭṭhivanuyyāne paṭhamadassane sotāpannadivasaṃ sandhāya vadati. Tadagge ahaṃ, bhante, dīgharattaṃ avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmīti taṃdivasaṃ ādiṃ katvā, ahaṃ, bhante, purimaṃ catuddasaattabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ dīgharattaṃ avinipāto laṭṭhivanuyyāne sotāpattimaggavasena adhigataṃ avinipātadhammataṃ sañjānāmīti attho. Anacchariyanti anuacchariyaṃ. Cintayamānaṃ punappunaṃ acchariyamevidaṃ yaṃ kenacideva karaṇīyena gacchanto bhagavantaṃ antarāmagge addasaṃ. Idampi acchariyaṃ yañca vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sayaṃparisāya bhāsato bhagavato diṭṭhasadisameva sammukhā sutaṃ. Dve paccayāti antarāmagge diṭṭhabhāvo ca vessavaṇassa sammukhā sutaṃ ārocetukāmatā ca.

Devasabhāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
281. āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhatīti: “And also hope remains for me.” Thus, I am a stream-enterer, and not having become negligent through learning the *sūtras*, I pass the time. Furthermore, *vipassanā* (insight meditation) has been started by me for the sake of the path of a once-returner ( *sakadāgāmin*). "Today, indeed, today I will penetrate (the truth)," thus he shows that he dwells with enthusiasm. yadaggeti: “From when?” He speaks referring to the day of becoming a stream-enterer at the first sight in the Laṭṭhi-grove (*laṭṭhivanuyyāna*). tadagge ahaṃ, bhante, dīgharattaṃ avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmīti: “From then, venerable sir, for a long time I recognize non-falling, non-lapse." Having made that day the beginning, venerable sir, I recognize for a long time, the fourteen previous existences, the non-falling that was attained in the Laṭṭhi-grove through the path of stream-entry, the nature of non-falling." Such is the meaning. anacchariyanti : “Not wonderful.” *Anuacchariyaṃ*: Not-wonderful. Thinking again and again, “This is a wonder, that while going for some business, I saw the Blessed One on the road in between ( *antarāmagga* ). This too is a wonder yañca vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sayaṃparisāya bhāsato bhagavato diṭṭhasadisameva sammukhā sutaṃ: and that which was heard face to face is just like what the Blessed One said to the assembly of Vessavaṇa, the Great King ( *mahārāja* ). dve paccayāti: “Two causes.” *Antarāmagge diṭṭhabhāvo ca vessavaṇassa sammukhā sutaṃ ārocetukāmatā ca*: The state of having seen [him] on the road in between and the desire to announce what was heard face to face by Vessavaṇa.

devasabhāvaṇṇanā

: Description of the assembly of the gods ( *devasabhā* ).

mula_pali:
282. ‘Purimāni , bhante, divasāni purimatarāni tadahuposathe pannarase vassūpanāyikāya puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā. Mahatī ca dibbaparisā dibbā parisā (sī. pī.) samantato nisinnā honti nisinnā hoti (sī.), sannisinnā honti sannipatitā (ka.), cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti. Puratthimāya disāya dhataraṭṭho mahārājā pacchimābhimukho pacchābhimukho (ka.) nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; dakkhiṇāya disāya virūḷhako mahārājā uttarābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; pacchimāya disāya virūpakkho mahārājā puratthābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; uttarāya disāya vessavaṇo mahārājā dakkhiṇābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā . Yadā, bhante, kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti. Idaṃ nesaṃ hoti āsanasmiṃ; atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hoti. Ye te, bhante, devā bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā adhunūpapannā tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ, te aññe deve atirocanti vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā ‘‘dibbā vata bho kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’’ti. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

‘‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā saindakā (sī.);

saindakā (sī.)

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine yasassino (syā.);

yasassino (syā.)

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’’nti.

‘Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyosomattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā ‘‘dibbā vata, bho, kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’’ti. Atha kho, bhante, yenatthena devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā vuttavacanāpi taṃ vuttavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti. Paccānusiṭṭhavacanāpi taṃ paccānusiṭṭhavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti, sakesu sakesu āsanesu ṭhitā avipakkantā adhipakkantā (ka.).

vuttavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) paccānusiṭṭhavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) adhipakkantā (ka.)

Te vuttavākyā rājāno, paṭiggayhānusāsaniṃ;

Vippasannamanā santā, aṭṭhaṃsu samhi āsaneti.
mula_english:
282. ‘Lord, in earlier days, long ago, on the fast-day of the fifteenth at the beginning of the Rains, on the full-moon night all the gods of the Kevala aeon and the Thirty-Three Gods (trāyastriṃśa) were seated in the Sudharma Hall (sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ), assembled together.

A great congregation of divine beings (divyapariṣad) was seated all around, and the Four Great Kings (catvāro mahārājāno) were seated in the four directions (catuddisā). The Great King Dhṛtarāṣṭra (dhataraṭṭho mahārājā) from the east was at the head of his followers, facing west; the Great King Virūḍhaka (virūḷhako mahārājā) from the south… facing north; the Great King Virūpākṣa (virūpakkho mahārājā) from the west… facing east; and the Great King Vaiśravaṇa (vessavaṇo mahārājā) from the north… facing south.

Whenever, Lord, the gods of the Kevala aeon and the Thirty-Three Gods were seated in the Sudharma Hall, assembled together, and a great congregation of divine beings was seated all around, and the Four Great Kings were seated in the four directions, that was their seating arrangement; then afterwards came our seats.

And those gods who, having lived the holy life under the Blessed One (bhagavati), had recently appeared in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, outshone the other gods in brightness (varṇena) and glory (yasasā).

And for that reason the Thirty-Three Gods were pleased, happy, filled with delight and joy, saying: ‘The hosts of the gods are growing, the hosts of the asuras are declining!’

Then, Lord, Śakra (śakro devānāmindo), ruler of the gods, seeing the satisfaction of the Thirty-Three, rejoiced with these verses:

“The Thirty-Three Gods, together with Indra (sahiṃdakā), rejoice;

honoring the Tathāgata (tathāgataṃ namassantā), and the sacred Dharma (dharmassa) and its excellence (sudhammataṃ).

Seeing new-come gods, fair (varṇavante) and glorious (yasassine);

having lived the holy life in the Sugata (sugatasmiṃ), they have come here.

They outshine the others in color (varṇena), glory (yasasā), and life (āyunā);

they are disciples (śāvakā) of the greatly wise (bhūripaññassa), they have attained distinction here.”

Seeing this, the Thirty-Three Gods, together with Indra, rejoice;

honoring the Tathāgata, and the sacred Dharma and its excellence.’

‘And for that reason, Lord, the Thirty-Three Gods were even more pleased, happy, filled with delight and joy, saying: “The hosts of the gods are growing, the hosts of the asuras are declining!”

Then, Lord, the Thirty-Three Gods, having consulted and deliberated about the matter concerning which they had assembled in the Sudharma Hall, the Four Great Kings were also in attendance at that meeting.

And the Four Great Kings were advised and admonished on this matter as they stood by their seats unmoving.
Note: This is called *paccānusiṭṭhavacanā* (Ka.).

Note: *Adhipakkantā* (Ka.).

Verse: Those kings, having spoken words, receiving instructions;

Being of delighted mind, stood together on the seat.
commentary_pali:
282.Sannipatitāti kasmā sannipatitā? Te kira catūhi kāraṇehi sannipatanti. Vassūpanāyikasaṅgahatthaṃ, pavāraṇāsaṅgahatthaṃ, dhammasavanatthaṃ, pāricchattakakīḷānubhavanatthanti. Tattha sve vassūpanāyikāti āsāḷhīpuṇṇamāya dvīsu devalokesu devā sudhammāya devasabhāya sannipatitvā mantenti asukavihāre eko bhikkhu vassūpagato, asukavihāre dve tayo cattāro pañca dasa vīsati tiṃsaṃ cattālīsaṃ paññāsaṃ sataṃ sahassaṃ bhikkhū vassūpagatā, etthettha ṭhāne ayyānaṃ ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ karothāti evaṃ vassūpanāyikasaṅgaho kato hoti.

Tadāpi eteneva kāraṇena sannipatitā. Idaṃ tesaṃ hoti āsanasminti idaṃ tesaṃ catunnaṃ mahārājānaṃ āsanaṃ hoti. Evaṃ tesu nisinnesu atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hoti.

Idaṃ tesaṃ hoti āsanasmi

Yenatthenāti yena vassūpanāyikatthena. Taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvāti taṃ araññavāsino bhikkhusaṅghassa ārakkhatthaṃ cintayitvā. Etthettha vuṭṭhabhikkhusaṅghassa ārakkhaṃ saṃvidahathāti catūhi mahārājehi saddhiṃ mantetvā. Vuttavacanāpi tanti tettiṃsa devaputtā vadanti, mahārājāno vuttavacanā nāma. Tathā tettiṃsa devaputtā paccānusāsanti, itare paccānusiṭṭhavacanā nāma. Padadvayepi pana tanti nipātamattameva. Avipakkantāti agatā.

Yenatthenā Taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā Vuttavacanāpi ta vuttavacanā paccānusiṭṭhavacanā Avipakkantā
commentary_english:
282. Why did they assemble? They assemble for four reasons:

For the purpose of the *vassūpanāyika-saṅgaha*, for the purpose of the *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha*, for the purpose of hearing the Dharma, and for the purpose of experiencing the *pāricchattaka* game.

There, on the full moon day of Āsāḷhī, the gods in the two heavens, having assembled in the Sudhamma *devasabhā*, consult, "In such and such a *vihāra*, one *bhikkhu* has entered the rainy season retreat; in such and such a *vihāra*, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand *bhikkhus* have entered the rainy season retreat. Here in this place, you should make well-arranged protection for the noble ones." Thus, the *vassūpanāyika-saṅgaha* is done.

Then also, they assembled for this same reason.

"This belongs to them, in the seat." This seat belongs to the four Great Kings ( *catunnaṃ mahārājānaṃ*).

Thus, when they are seated, then afterwards our seat is.

"By which meaning?" By the meaning of the *vassūpanāyika*.

"Having thought about that meaning, having consulted about that meaning." Having thought about the protection of the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* dwelling in the forest.

"Here you should arrange the protection of the *vuṭṭha-bhikkhu-saṅgha*." Having consulted with the four Great Kings.

"*Vuttavacanāpi ta*." The thirty-three *devaputras* speak; the Great Kings are called "*vuttavacanā*."

Likewise, the thirty-three *devaputras* instruct, the others are called "*paccānusiṭṭhavacanā*."

Even in the two words, *pana tanti* is merely a particle.

"*Avipakkantā*." Not gone.

*Yenatthenā taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā vuttavacanāpi ta vuttavacanā paccānusiṭṭhavacanā avipakkantā*

mula_pali:
283. ‘Atha kho, bhante, uttarāya disāya uḷāro āloko sañjāyi, obhāso pāturahosi atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘‘yathā kho, mārisā, nimittāni dissanti, uḷāro āloko sañjāyati, obhāso pātubhavati, brahmā pātubhavissati. Brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimittaṃ pātubhāvāya yadidaṃ āloko sañjāyati obhāso pātubhavatīti.

‘‘Yathā nimittā dissanti, brahmā pātubhavissati;

Brahmuno hetaṃ nimittaṃ, obhāso vipulo mahā’’ti.

Sanaṅkumārakathā
mula_english:
‘“And then, Lord (bhante), a glorious radiance (uḷāro āloko) shone forth from the north (uttarāya disāya), and a splendour (obhāso) was seen greater than the sheen of the gods (devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ).

And then, Lord (bhante), Śakra (sakko), the lord of the gods (devānamindo), addressed the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three (deve tāvatiṃse): ‘Gentlemen (mārisā), when such signs (nimittāni) are seen, such light (uḷāro āloko) is seen and such radiance (obhāso) shines forth, Brahmā (brahmā) will appear. This is the preliminary sign (pubbanimittaṃ) of Brahmā’s (brahmuno) appearance (pātubhāvāya): that a light (āloko) shines forth and a radiance (obhāso) appears.’

‘When such signs (nimittā) are seen, Brahmā (brahmā) will appear; this is Brahmā’s (brahmuno) sign (nimittaṃ), a great (mahā) and vast (vipulo) radiance (obhāso).’”

The Discourse on Sanankumara
commentary_pali:
283.Uḷāroti vipulo mahā. Devānubhāvanti yā sā sabbadevatānaṃ vatthālaṅkāravimānasarīrānaṃ pabhā dvādasa yojanāni pharati. Mahāpuññānaṃ pana sarīrappabhā yojanasataṃ pharati. Taṃ devānubhāvaṃ atikkamitvā.

Brahmunohetaṃ pubbanimittanti yathā sūriyassa udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ yadidaṃ aruṇuggaṃ, evameva brahmunopi etaṃ – ‘‘pubbanimitta’’nti dīpeti.

Brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimitta

Sanaṅkumārakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
283. *Uḷāro* means vast, great.

*Devānubhāva* means that the light ( *pabhā*) of all the gods' garments (*vatthālaṅkāra*), palaces (*vimāna*), and bodies (*sarīra*) pervades twelve *yojana*s.

Moreover, the light (*sarīrappabhā*) of those with great merit (*mahāpuññānaṃ*) pervades a hundred *yojana*s.

Having surpassed that divine power (*devānubhāvaṃ atikkamitvā*).

*Brahmuno* [See footnote] *hetaṃ pubbanimitta* means that just as for the sun (*sūriyassa*) rising (*udayato*), this is the precursor (*pubbaṅgamaṃ*), this is the preliminary sign (*pubbanimittaṃ*), namely the rising of the dawn (*aruṇuggaṃ*), even so, this is what Brahman (*brahmuno*) indicates – "preliminary sign" (*pubbanimitta*).

*Brahmuno* [See footnote] *hetaṃ pubbanimitta*

Description of the *Sanaṅkumārakathā*.

mula_pali:
284. ‘Atha kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’’ti. Cattāropi mahārājāno yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’’ti. Idaṃ sutvā devā tāvatiṃsā ekaggā samāpajjiṃsu – ‘‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’’ti.

‘Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā pātubhavati. Yo kho pana, bhante, brahmuno pakativaṇṇo anabhisambhavanīyo so devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ cakkhupathasmiṃ. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati , so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhante, sovaṇṇo viggaho mānusaṃ viggahaṃ atirocati; evameva kho, bhante, yadā brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, na tassaṃ parisāyaṃ koci devo abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimanteti. Sabbeva tuṇhībhūtā pañjalikā pallaṅkena nisīdanti – ‘‘yassadāni devassa pallaṅkaṃ icchissati brahmā sanaṅkumāro, tassa devassa pallaṅke nisīdissatī’’ti.

‘Yassa kho pana, bhante, devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ; uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto adhunābhisitto rajjena, uḷāraṃ so labhati vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Evameva kho, bhante, yassa devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Atha , bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā kumāravaṇṇī kumāravaṇṇo (syā. ka.) hutvā pañcasikho devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāturahosi. So vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīdi. Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso supaccatthate vā pallaṅke same vā bhūmibhāge pallaṅkena nisīdeyya; evameva kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

kumāravaṇṇo (syā. ka.)

‘‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

‘‘Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

‘‘Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

‘‘Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’’nti.
mula_english:
284. Then, venerable sir, the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three ( *Tāvatiṃsa*) sat down each in their proper seat, thinking, "Let us understand this radiance; whatever its result will be, we will go to it, having realized it!"

The four Great Kings also sat down each in their proper seat, thinking, "Let us understand this radiance; whatever its result will be, we will go to it, having realized it!"

Having heard this, the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, with unified minds, thought, "Let us understand this radiance; whatever its result will be, we will go to it, having realized it!"

Venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanankumāra appears to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, he manifests a coarse ( *oḷārikaṃ*) form and appears.

Venerable sir, the natural color of Brahmā, which cannot be overcome, is in the sight of the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.

When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra appears to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, he outshines the other gods in beauty and glory ( *yasas*).

Just as a golden image outshines a human image, so too, venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanankumāra appears to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, he outshines the other gods in beauty and glory ( *yasas*).

When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra appears to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, no god in that assembly greets him, rises for him, or invites him with a seat.

All sit silently, with their palms joined in reverence ( *pañjalikā*), cross-legged, thinking, "Brahmā Sanankumāra will sit on the couch ( *pallaṅkaṃ*) of whichever god he desires at this time."

Venerable sir, whichever god Brahmā Sanankumāra sits on the couch ( *pallaṅka*) of, that god obtains great ( *uḷāraṃ*) attainment of Vedic knowledge ( *vedapaṭilābhaṃ*); that god obtains great ( *uḷāraṃ*) attainment of joy ( *somanassapaṭilābhaṃ*).

Just as, venerable sir, a Khattiya king, anointed on the head, newly consecrated to the kingdom, obtains great ( *uḷāraṃ*) attainment of Vedic knowledge ( *vedapaṭilābhaṃ*), and obtains great ( *uḷāraṃ*) attainment of joy ( *somanassapaṭilābhaṃ*),

so too, venerable sir, whichever god Brahmā Sanankumāra sits on the couch (*pallaṅka*) of, that god obtains great (*uḷāraṃ*) attainment of Vedic knowledge (*vedapaṭilābhaṃ*); that god obtains great (*uḷāraṃ*) attainment of joy (*somanassapaṭilābhaṃ*).

Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra, having manifested a coarse ( *oḷārikaṃ*) form, having become of youthful color ( *kumāravaṇṇī*), became Pañcasikha and appeared to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.

He rose up into the sky ( *vehāsaṃ*) and sat cross-legged in the atmosphere ( *ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīdi*).

Just as, venerable sir, a strong man might sit down cross-legged on a well-spread couch ( *pallaṅke*) or on a level ground, so too, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra, having risen up into the sky ( *vehāsaṃ*) and sat cross-legged in the atmosphere ( *ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā*), having known the delight ( *sampasādaṃ*) of the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, rejoiced with these verses:

“Indeed, the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three (*Tāvatiṃsā*), along with Indra, are delighted;

honoring the *Tathāgata* and the true Dharma ( *dhamma*).

And seeing the new gods, beautiful and glorious;

having lived the holy life ( *brahmacariyaṃ*) in the Sugata, they have come here.

They outshine the others in beauty and glory ( *yasas*);

disciples of the wise one, they have attained distinction here.

Having seen this, the *Tāvatiṃsa* gods, along with Indra, are delighted;

honoring the *Tathāgata* and the true Dharma ( *dhamma*)."
commentary_pali:
284.Anabhisambhavanīyoti apattabbo, na taṃ devā tāvatiṃsā passantīti attho. Cakkhupathasminti cakkhupasāde āpāthe vā. So devānaṃ cakkhussa āpāthe sambhavanīyo pattabbo na hoti, na abhibhavatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Heṭṭhā heṭṭhā hi devatā uparūpari devānaṃ oḷārikaṃ katvā māpitameva attabhāvaṃ passituṃ sakkonti, vedapaṭilābhanti tuṭṭhipaṭilābhaṃ. Adhunābhisitto rajjenāti sampati abhisitto rajjena. Ayaṃ panattho duṭṭhagāmaṇiabhayavatthunā dīpetabbo –

So kira dvattiṃsa damiḷarājāno vijitvā anurādhapure pattābhiseko tuṭṭhasomanassena māsaṃ niddaṃ na labhi, tato – ‘‘niddaṃ na labhāmi, bhante’’ti bhikkhusaṅghassa ācikkhi. Tena hi, mahārāja, ajja uposathaṃ adhiṭṭhāhīti. So ca uposathaṃ adhiṭṭhāsi. Saṅgho gantvā – ‘‘cittayamakaṃ sajjhāyathā’’ti aṭṭha ābhidhammikabhikkhū pesesi. Te gantvā – ‘‘nipajja tvaṃ, mahārājā,’’ti vatvā sajjhāyaṃ ārabhiṃsu. Rājā sajjhāyaṃ suṇantova niddaṃ okkami. Therā – rājānaṃ mā pabodhayitthāti pakkamiṃsu. Rājā dutiyadivase sūriyuggamane pabujjhitvā there apassanto – ‘‘kuhiṃ ayyā’’ti pucchi. Tumhākaṃ niddokkamanabhāvaṃ ñatvā gatāti. Natthi, bho, mayhaṃ ayyakassa dārakānaṃ ajānanakabhesajjaṃ nāma, yāva niddābhesajjampi jānanti yevāti āha.

Pañcasikhoti pañcasikhagandhabbasadiso hutvā. Pañcasikhagandhabbadevaputtassa kira sabbadevatā attabhāvaṃ mamāyanti. Tasmā brahmāpi tādisaṃyeva attabhāvaṃ nimminitvā pāturahosi. Pallaṅkena nisīdīti pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisīdi.

Pañcasikho Pallaṅkena nisīdī

Vissaṭṭhoti sumutto apalibuddho. Viññeyyoti atthaviññāpano. Mañjūti madhuro mudu. Savanīyoti sotabbayuttako kaṇṇasukho. Bindūti ekagghano. Avisārīti suvisado avippakiṇṇo. Gambhīroti nābhimūlato paṭṭhāya gambhīrasamuṭṭhito, na jivhādantaoṭṭhatālumattappahārasamuṭṭhito. Evaṃ samuṭṭhito hi amadhuro ca hoti, na ca dūraṃ sāveti. Ninnādīti mahāmeghamudiṅgasaddo viya ninnādayutto. Apicettha pacchimaṃ pacchimaṃ padaṃ purimassa purimassa atthoyevāti veditabbo. Yathāparisanti yattakā parisā, tattakameva viññāpeti. Anto parisāyaṃ yevassa saddo samparivattati, na bahiddhā vidhāvati. Ye hi kecīti ādi bahujanahitāya paṭipannabhāvadassanatthaṃ vadati. Saraṇaṃ gatāti na yathā vā tathā vā saraṇaṃ gate sandhāya vadati. Nibbematikagahitasaraṇe pana sandhāya vadati. Gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentīti gandhabbadevagaṇaṃ paripūrenti. Iti amhākaṃ satthu loke uppannakālato paṭṭhāya cha devalokādīsu piṭṭhaṃ koṭṭetvā pūritanāḷi viya saravananaḷavanaṃ viya ca nirantaraṃ jātaparisāti āha.

Vissaṭṭho Viññeyyo Mañjū Savanīyo Bindū Avisārī Gambhīro Ninnādī Yathāparisa Ye hi kecī Saraṇaṃ gatā Gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentī

Bhāvitaiddhipādavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
284. "Not liable to arise" means that the gods of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven do not see him.

"In the range of the eye" means in the eye faculty or in the field of vision.

He is not liable to arise or attainable in the field of vision of the gods; it is said that he does not surpass [them].

For the deities below can see the created self-image of the deities above by making it gross. "Acquisition of the *Veda*" means acquisition of satisfaction.

"Anointed now with kingship" means anointed just now with kingship.

The meaning here should be explained by the story of *Duṭṭhagāmaṇi Abhaya*:

It seems that having conquered thirty-two *Damiḷa* kings and having attained consecration in *Anurādhapura*, he did not obtain sleep for a month due to joyful satisfaction; then he said to the community of monks, "I do not obtain sleep, venerable sirs."

Then [they said], "Well then, great king, undertake the *uposatha* today."

And he undertook the *uposatha*.

The *saṃgha* went and sent eight *Abhidhamma* monks, saying, "Recite the *Cittayamaka*."

They went and said, "Lie down, great king," and began the recitation.

The king fell asleep while listening to the recitation.

The elders left, [thinking,] "The king should not be awakened."

The king, awakening on the second day at sunrise, not seeing the elders, asked, "Where are the venerable sirs?"

"[They] have gone, knowing that you were overcome by sleep."

"There is no medicine for not knowing among the children of my ancestors; they even know sleep medicine," he said.

"Having become like *Pañcasikha*", meaning having become similar to the *Pañcasikha Gandhabba*.

It seems that all the deities cherish the self-image of the son of the *Pañcasikha Gandhabba* god.

Therefore, Brahmā himself, having created just such a self-image, appeared.

"*Nisīdī* on the *pallaṅka*", meaning having bent the *pallaṅka*, he sat down.

*Pañcasikha nisīdī* on the *pallaṅka* means "*vissaṭṭho*", completely freed and unimpeded.

"*Viññeyyo*", meaning making known the meaning.

"*Mañjū*" means sweet and soft.

"*Savanīyo*", meaning connected with what should be heard, pleasing to the ear.

"*Bindū*", meaning unified.

"*Avisārī*", meaning very clear and not scattered.

"*Gambhīro*" means arising deeply from the base of the navel, not arising from a mere striking of the tongue, teeth, lips, and palate.

For thus arisen, it is indeed unpleasant and does not sound far away.

"*Ninnādī*", meaning having the quality of resounding like the sound of a great cloud *mudiṅga*.

Moreover, here it should be understood that each succeeding word is the meaning of each preceding word.

"*Yathāparisa*", meaning he makes known as much as the assembly is.

His sound revolves within the assembly itself; it does not run outside.

"*Ye hi kecī*", meaning he speaks, beginning with "whoever" to show that they have undertaken [this] for the welfare of many people.

"*Saraṇaṃ gatā*", meaning he does not speak referring to those who have gone for refuge in just any way whatsoever.

But he speaks referring to those who have taken refuge with unwavering certainty.
Filling the *gandhabba* body means they fill the *gandhabba* deva group.

Thus, he said that from the time of our teacher's arising in the world, continuously, like a filled tube by pressing the back in the six *devaloka* realms, beginning with those, like a forest of reeds and *nala* reeds, there is a community that is born.

Vissaṭṭho, viññeyyo, mañjū, savanīyo, bindū

Avisārī, gambhīro, ninnādī

Yathāparisa, ye hi kecī

Saraṇaṃ gatā, gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentī. Explanation of the development of the bases of psychic power.

mula_pali:
285. ‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha; imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti vissaṭṭho ca viññeyyo ca mañju ca savanīyo ca bindu ca avisārī ca gambhīro ca ninnādī ca. Yathāparisaṃ kho pana, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sarena viññāpeti; na cassa bahiddhā parisāya ghoso niccharati. Yassa kho pana, bhante, evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti, so vuccati ‘‘brahmassaro’’ti.

‘Atha kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro tettiṃse attabhāve abhinimminitvā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ paccekapallaṅkesu pallaṅkena paccekapallaṅkena (ka.) nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Ye hi keci, bho, buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā sīlesu paripūrakārino te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā appekacce paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce tusitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce yāmānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti. Ye sabbanihīnaṃ kāyaṃ paripūrenti, te gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentī’’’ti.

paccekapallaṅkena (ka.)
mula_english:
285. ‘Regarding this matter, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumara spoke; regarding this matter, venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanankumara spoke, his voice possessed eight qualities: it was distinct (vissaṭṭho), intelligible (viññeyyo), pleasant (mañju), attractive (savanīyo), compact (bindu), concise (avisārī), deep (gambhīro), and resonant (ninnādī).

And when Brahmā Sanankumara made it known to the assembly with that voice, venerable sir, its sound did not carry outside the assembly.

Whoever, venerable sir, has such a voice endowed with eight qualities is said to have the "voice of Brahmā" (brahmassaro).

‘Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumara, multiplying his form thirty-three times, sat down cross-legged on each individual couch of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, and addressed the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, saying: "What do you think, lords, gods of the Trāyastriṃśa? The Blessed One has set forth for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans.

Those, whoever they may be, reverend sirs, who have gone for refuge to the Buddha (buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā), gone for refuge to the Dharma (dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā), gone for refuge to the Saṃgha (saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā), and are completely fulfilling the precepts (sīlesu paripūrakārino), upon the breaking up of the body, after death (kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā), some arise in the company of the gods who control what is created by others (paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti), some arise in the company of the gods who delight in creation (nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti), some arise in the company of the Tusita gods (tusitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti), some arise in the company of the Yama gods (yāmānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti), some arise in the company of the Trāyastriṃśa gods (tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti), and some arise in the company of the Cātumahārājika gods (cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti).

Those who completely fulfill the lowest body, they completely fulfill the Gandhabba body (gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentīti)."’

mula_pali:
286. ‘Imamatthaṃ , bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha; imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato ghosoyeva devā maññanti – ‘‘yvāyaṃ mama pallaṅke svāyaṃ ekova bhāsatī’’ti.

Ekasmiṃ bhāsamānasmiṃ, sabbe bhāsanti nimmitā;

Ekasmiṃ tuṇhimāsīne, sabbe tuṇhī bhavanti te.

Tadāsu devā maññanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Yvāyaṃ mama pallaṅkasmiṃ, svāyaṃ ekova bhāsatīti.

‘Atha kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro ekattena attānaṃ upasaṃharati, ekattena attānaṃ upasaṃharitvā sakkassa devānamindassa pallaṅke pallaṅkena nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

Bhāvitaiddhipādo
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, this was the meaning Brahma Sanankumara spoke; venerable sir, as Brahma Sanankumara spoke this meaning, the gods thought, ‘Indeed, the one speaking is sitting on my couch, he is speaking to me alone.’”

When one speaks, all created beings speak;

When one is seated in silence, all of them are silent.

Then the gods, the Tāvatiṃsa gods, along with Indra, thought:

‘Indeed, the one speaking is sitting on my couch, he is speaking to me alone.’

“Then, venerable sir, Brahma Sanankumara identified himself with oneness, and having identified himself with oneness, he sat down cross-legged on the couch of Sakka, the lord of the gods, and addressed the Tāvatiṃsa gods:

the development of the base for magical power.

mula_pali:
287. ‘‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro iddhipādā paññattā iddhipahutāya iddhibahulīkatāya (syā.) iddhivisavitāya iddhivisevitāya (syā.) iddhivikubbanatāya. Katame cattāro? Idha bho bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Vīriyasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Cittasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Ime kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro iddhipādā paññattā iddhipahutāya iddhivisavitāya iddhivikubbanatāya.

‘‘‘Ye hi keci bho atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhosuṃ, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Yepi hi keci bho anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhossanti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Yepi hi keci bho etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Passanti no bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā mamapimaṃ evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ mahābrahme’’ti. ‘‘Ahampi kho bho imesaṃyeva catunnañca iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā evaṃ mahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo’’ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

Tividho okāsādhigamo
mula_english:
287. “‘What do you think, lords of the Thirty-Three? These four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*) have been well proclaimed by that Lord, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, for abundance of power, for the expansion of power, for the manifestation of power.

What are the four? Here, a monk develops the road to power (*ṛddhipāda*) that is concentration of intention (*chanda-samādhi*) accompanied by effort of will. He develops the road to power (*ṛddhipāda*) that is concentration of energy (*vīriya-samādhi*) accompanied by effort of will. He develops the road to power (*ṛddhipāda*) that is concentration of consciousness (*citta-samādhi*) accompanied by effort of will. He develops the road to power (*ṛddhipāda*) that is concentration of investigation (*vīmaṃsā-samādhi*) accompanied by effort of will. These are the four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*) proclaimed by that Lord, who knows and sees, the Arahant, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, for abundance of power, for the expansion of power, for the manifestation of power.

“‘Whatever ascetics or Brahmins have in the past realized such diverse powers, all have developed and cultivated just these four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*). And whatever ascetics or Brahmins in the future will realize such diverse powers, all will have developed and cultivated just these four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*). And whatever ascetics or Brahmins now realize such diverse powers, all have developed and cultivated just these four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*). Do you, lords of the Thirty-Three, see such a manifestation of power as mine?’ ‘Yes, Great Brahma.’ ‘Well, I too have such great power and majesty because I have developed and cultivated these four roads to power (*ṛddhipāda*).'”

This was the burden of Brahmā Sanankumāra's speech. After speaking this, Brahmā Sanankumāra addressed the gods of the Thirty-Three:

The Threefold Way of Gaining Access
commentary_pali:
287.Yāvasupaññattā cime tena bhagavatāti tena mayhaṃ satthārā bhagavatā yāva supaññattā yāva sukathitā. Iddhipādāti ettha ijjhanaṭṭhena iddhi, patiṭṭhānaṭṭhena pādāti veditabbā. Iddhipahutāyāti iddhipahonakatāya. Iddhivisavitāyāti iddhivipajjanabhāvāya, punappunaṃ āsevanavasena ciṇṇavasitāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Iddhivikubbanatāyāti iddhivikubbanabhāvāya, nānappakārato katvā dassanatthāya. Chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgatantiādīsu chandahetuko chandādhiko vā samādhi chandasamādhi, kattukamyatāchandaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhissetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Padhānabhūtā saṅkhārā padhānasaṅkhārā. Catukiccasādhakassa sammappadhānavīriyassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Samannāgatanti chandasamādhinā ca padhānasaṅkhārena ca upetaṃ. Iddhipādanti nipphattipariyāyena ijjhanaṭṭhena vā, ijjhanti etāya sattā iddhā vuddhā ukkaṃsagatā hontīti iminā vā pariyāyena iddhīti saṅkhyaṃ gatānaṃ abhiññācittasampayuttānaṃ chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena pādabhūto sesacittacetasikarāsīti attho. Vuttañhetaṃ – ‘‘iddhipādoti tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho’’ti (vibha. 434). Iminā nayena sesesupi attho veditabbo. Yatheva hi chandaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhi chandasamādhīti vutto, evaṃ vīriyaṃ, cittaṃ, vīmaṃsaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhi vīmaṃsāsamādhīti vuccati. Apica upacārajjhānaṃ pādo, paṭhamajjhānaṃ iddhi. Saupacāraṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ pādo, dutiyajjhānaṃ iddhīti evaṃ pubbabhāge pādo, aparabhāge iddhīti evamettha attho veditabbo. Vitthārena iddhipādakathā visuddhimagge ca vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāya ca vuttā.

Keci pana ‘‘nipphannā iddhi. Anipphanno iddhipādo’’ti vadanti, tesaṃ vādamaddanatthāya abhidhamme uttaracūḷikavāro nāma ābhato – ‘‘cattāro iddhipādā chandiddhipādo, vīriyiddhipādo, cittiddhipādo, vīmaṃsiddhipādo. Tattha katamo chandiddhipādo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhāpaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ. Yo tasmiṃ samaye chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando, ayaṃ vuccati chandiddhipādo, avasesā dhammā chandiddhipādasampayuttā’’ti (vibha. 458). Ime pana lokuttaravaseneva āgatā. Tattha raṭṭhapālatthero chandaṃ dhuraṃ katvā lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ nibbattesi. Soṇatthero vīriyaṃ dhuraṃ katvā, sambhūtatthero cittaṃ dhuraṃ katvā, āyasmā mogharājā vīmaṃsaṃ dhuraṃ katvāti.

uttaracūḷikavāro

Tattha yathā catūsu amaccaputtesu ṭhānantaraṃ patthetvā rājānaṃ upanissāya viharantesu eko upaṭṭhāne chandajāto rañño ajjhāsayañca ruciñca ñatvā divā ca ratto ca upaṭṭhahanto rājānaṃ ārādhetvā ṭhānantaraṃ pāpuṇi. Yathā so, evaṃ chandadhurena lokuttaradhammanibbattako veditabbo.

Eko pana – ‘‘divase divase upaṭṭhātuṃ ko sakkoti, uppanne kicce parakkamena ārādhessāmī’’ti kupite paccante raññā pahito parakkamena sattumaddanaṃ katvā ṭhānantaraṃ pāpuṇi. Yathā so, evaṃ vīriyadhurena lokuttaradhammanibbattako veditabbo.

Eko – ‘‘divase divase upaṭṭhānampi urena sattisarapaṭicchannampi bhāroyeva, mantabalena ārādhessāmī’’ti khattavijjāya kataparicayattā mantasaṃvidhānena rājānaṃ ārādhetvā ṭhānantaraṃ pāpuṇāti. Yathā so, evaṃ cittadhurena lokuttaradhammanibbattako veditabbo.

Aparo – ‘‘kiṃ imehi upaṭṭhānādīhi, rājāno nāma jātisampannassa ṭhānantaraṃ denti, tādisassa dento mayhaṃ dassatī’’ti jātisampattimeva nissāya ṭhānantaraṃ pāpuṇi, yathā so, evaṃ suparisuddhaṃ vīmaṃsaṃ nissāya vīmaṃsadhurena lokuttaradhammanibbattako veditabbo.

Anekavihitanti anekavidhaṃ. Iddhividhanti iddhikoṭṭhāsaṃ.

Anekavihita Iddhividha

Tividhaokāsādhigamavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
287. "As well proclaimed by that Blessed One": As well proclaimed, as well spoken by that Blessed One, my Teacher.

"Bases of spiritual power ( *iddhipāda*)": Here, it should be understood that *iddhi* is in the sense of succeeding, and *pāda* in the sense of foundation.

"Abounding in spiritual power": Because of abounding in spiritual power.

"Skill in spiritual power": For the state of the arising of spiritual power, it is said to be the state of being skilled through familiarity cultivated by repeated practice.

"The state of transforming by means of spiritual power": For the state of transforming by means of spiritual power, for the sake of showing [things] having made [them] of various kinds.

"Endowed with the will-concentration-effort formation": Among these and others, concentration that has will as its cause or will as its excess is will-concentration (*chandasamādhi*); this is a designation for the concentration that has been attained by making the will to do ( *kattukamyatāchandaṃ*) the ruler.

Formations that are effort (*padhāna*) are effort-formations (*padhānasaṅkhārā*). This is a term for the energy of right endeavour accomplishing its fourfold function.

"Endowed" (*samannāgata*): Endowed with will-concentration (*chandasamādhi*) and with effort-formation (*padhānasaṅkhāra*).

"Base of spiritual power" (*iddhipāda*): The meaning is, the total of consciousness and its remaining concomitants except the concentration and the will, which are, in the sense of resolve, the road to the concentration due to zeal and will to strive associated with the direct-knowledge consciousness, which latter are themselves termed “power” either by treatment as “production” or in the sense of “succeeding” or by treatment in this way, “beings succeed by its means, thus they are successful; they are enriched, promoted" (*iddhipāda*).

And it was said, "The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness of such a one is the base of spiritual power" (Vibha. 434).

The meaning should be understood in the remaining [cases] too in this way.

Just as will, having made will the ruler, the concentration that has been attained is called will-concentration (*chandasamādhi*), so is it said that energy, mind, and investigation, having made [them] the ruler, the concentration that has been attained is investigation-concentration (*vīmaṃsāsamādhi*).

Moreover, access concentration is a base (*pāda*), the first *jhāna* is spiritual power (*iddhi*). Access to the first *jhāna* is a base (*pāda*), the second *jhāna* is spiritual power (*iddhi*); thus, in the former part is the base (*pāda*), in the latter part is spiritual power (*iddhi*); thus the meaning should be understood here.

The extended discussion of the bases of spiritual power (*iddhipādakathā*) has been spoken in the *Visuddhimagga* and in the *Vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathā*.

But some say, "Spiritual power (*iddhi*) is accomplished. The base of spiritual power (*iddhipāda*) is unaccomplished." In order to crush their view, in the Abhidhamma the section called *Uttaracūḷikavāra* was brought: "There are four bases of spiritual power (*iddhipāda*): the base of spiritual power of will (*chandiddhipāda*), the base of spiritual power of energy (*vīriyiddhipāda*), the base of spiritual power of mind (*cittiddhipāda*), the base of spiritual power of investigation (*vīmaṃsiddhipāda*). Therein, what is the base of spiritual power of will (*chandiddhipāda*)? Here, a bhikkhu, on the occasion when he develops the supramundane *jhāna* that is an outlet and leads to dispersal, having abandoned the field of false views with the reaching of the first grade, secluded from sense desires he enters upon and dwells in the first *jhāna*, which is of painful practice and slow in direct knowledge. The will, the wishing to do, the desire to do, the skillful will for the Dhamma that exists at that time is called the base of spiritual power of will (*chandiddhipāda*); the remaining *dharmas* are associated with the base of spiritual power of will" (Vibha. 458). But these have come only in the sense of the supramundane. There, the Elder Raṭṭhapāla, having made will the burden, produced the supramundane Dhamma; the Elder Soṇa, having made energy the burden; the Elder Sambhūta, having made mind the burden; the venerable Mogharāja, having made investigation the burden.

*Uttaracūḷikavāra* There, just as among four sons of ministers who, desiring a higher position, lived depending on the king, one, will being born in service, knowing both the king's inclination and his liking, pleasing the king by attending [to him] by day and by night, attained a higher position; just as that one, so should the producer of supramundane *dhamma* by means of the burden of will be understood.

But another one, "Who can attend [to him] day by day? When an affair has arisen, I will please [him] by means of prowess," having been sent by the king to a frontier region that was in revolt, having crushed the enemy by means of prowess, attained a higher position; just as that one, so should the producer of supramundane *dhamma* by means of the burden of energy be understood.

Another one, "Attending [to him] day by day, even though covered with armor and a hundred arrows, is indeed a burden; I will please [him] by means of the power of a *mantra*," having made familiarity in the science of the ruling class, pleasing the king by means of the arrangement of a *mantra*, attains a higher position; just as that one, so should the producer of supramundane *dhamma* by means of the burden of mind be understood.
Another [example]: "What [is the use] of these services and the like? Kings give a higher position to one endowed with good birth. Giving to such a one, will he give to me?" Relying only on good birth, he attained a higher position. Just as he [did], so should one know that, relying on perfectly pure investigation, the one who bears the burden of investigation brings about supramundane Dharma.

*anekavihita* means *anekavidhaṃ*, of various kinds.
*iddhividha* means *iddhikoṭṭhāsaṃ*, the division of psychic power.

mula_pali:
288. ‘‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāvañcidaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo okāsādhigamā anubuddhā sukhassādhigamāya. Katame tayo? Idha bho ekacco saṃsaṭṭho viharati kāmehi saṃsaṭṭho akusalehi dhammehi. So aparena samayena ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. So ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ asaṃsaṭṭho viharati kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭho akusalehi dhammehi. Tassa asaṃsaṭṭhassa kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭhassa akusalehi dhammehi uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ pāmujjaṃ (pī. ka.) jāyetha, evameva kho, bho, asaṃsaṭṭhassa kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭhassa akusalehi dhammehi uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya.

‘‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bho, idhekaccassa oḷārikā kāyasaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti, oḷārikā vacīsaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti, oḷārikā cittasaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti. So aparena samayena ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. Tassa ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ oḷārikā kāyasaṅkhārā paṭippassambhanti, oḷārikā vacīsaṅkhārā paṭippassambhanti, oḷārikā cittasaṅkhārā paṭippassambhanti. Tassa oḷārikānaṃ kāyasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ vacīsaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ cittasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ jāyetha, evameva kho bho oḷārikānaṃ kāyasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ vacīsaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ cittasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya.

‘‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bho, idhekacco ‘idaṃ kusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. ‘Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. So aparena samayena ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. So ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ, ‘idaṃ kusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Tassa avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ jāyetha , evameva kho, bho, avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tatiyo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya. Ime kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo okāsādhigamā anubuddhā sukhassādhigamāyā’’ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha, imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

Catusatipaṭṭhānaṃ
mula_english:
‘What do my lords of the Thirty-Three think? There are three gateways to the attainment of bliss proclaimed by the Lord (Bhagavat) who knows and sees, the *arhat*, the Fully Awakened One (*sammāsambuddha*).

Which three? In the first place someone dwells in association with sense-desires (*kāmehi saṃsaṭṭho*), with unwholesome conditions (*akusalehi dhammehi*). At some time he hears the *Ariyadhamma* (Aryan Dharma), he pays close attention (*yoniso manasi karoti*) and practises in conformity with it (*dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati*). By so doing he comes to live dissociated from such sense-desires and unwholesome conditions. As a result of this dissociation, pleasant feeling (*sukhaṃ*) arises, and what is more, gladness (*somanassaṃ*). Just as pleasure might give birth to rejoicing, so from pleasant feeling he experiences gladness. This, is the first gateway to the attainment of bliss proclaimed by the Lord who knows and sees, the *arhat*, the Fully Awakened One.

‘In the second place there is someone in whom the gross *kāyasaṃkhāra* (bodily formations), *vāksaṃskāra* (verbal formations) and *cittasaṃkhāra* (mental formations) are not allayed (*appaṭippassaddhā*). At some time he hears the *Ariyadhamma*, he pays close attention and practises in conformity with it. As a result, his gross bodily, verbal and mental formations are allayed (*paṭippassambhanti*). As a result of this allaying, pleasant feeling arises, and what is more, gladness. Just as pleasure might give birth to rejoicing, so from the allaying of the gross bodily, verbal and mental formations pleasant feeling arises, and what is more, gladness. This is the second gateway to the attainment of bliss proclaimed by the Lord who knows and sees, the *arhat*, the Fully Awakened One.

‘In the third place there is someone who does not in truth know what is wholesome (*kusala*) and what is unwholesome (*akusala*). He does not in truth know what is blameworthy (*sāvajjaṃ*) and what is blameless (*anavajjaṃ*), what is to be practised (*sevitabbaṃ*) and what is not to be practised (*na sevitabbaṃ*), what is base (*hīnaṃ*) and what is noble (*paṇītaṃ*), and what is foul (*kaṇha*), fair (*sukka*) or mixed in quality (*kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ*). At some time he hears the *Ariyadhamma*, he pays close attention and practises in conformity with it. As a result, he comes to know in reality what is right and wrong, what is blameworthy and what is blameless, what is to be practised and what is not to be practised, what is base and what is noble, and what is foul, fair and mixed in quality. In him who knows and sees thus, ignorance (*avijjā*) is dispelled and knowledge (*vijjā*) arises. With the waning of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, pleasant feeling arises, and what is more, gladness. Just as pleasure might give birth to rejoicing, so from the waning of ignorance and the arising of knowledge pleasant feeling arises, and what is more, gladness. This is the third gateway to the attainment of bliss proclaimed by the Lord who knows and sees, the *arhat*, the Fully Awakened One. These are the three gateways to the attainment of bliss proclaimed by the Lord who knows and sees.’

‘This was the burden of Brahma Sanankumara’s speech. Brahma Sanankumara gave this discourse and addressed the gods of the Thirty-Three:
The four *smṛtyupasthānas*
commentary_pali:
288.Sukhassādhigamāyāti jhānasukhassa maggasukhassa phalasukhassa ca adhigamāya. Saṃsaṭṭhoti sampayuttacitto. Ariyadhammanti ariyena bhagavatā buddhena desitaṃ dhammaṃ. Suṇātīti satthu sammukhā bhikkhubhikkhunīādīhi vā desiyamānaṃ suṇāti. Yoniso manasikarotīti upāyato pathato kāraṇato ‘anicca’ntiādivasena manasi karoti. ‘‘Yoniso manasikāro nāma upāyamanasikāro pathamanasikāro, anicce aniccanti dukkhe dukkhanti anattani anattāti asubhe asubhanti saccānulomikena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anvāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro, ayaṃ vuccati yonisomanasikāro’’ti. Evaṃ vutte yonisomanasikāre kammaṃ ārabhatīti attho. Asaṃsaṭṭhoti vatthukāmehipi kilesakāmehipi asaṃsaṭṭho viharati. Uppajjati sukhanti uppajjati paṭhamajjhānasukhaṃ. Sukhā bhiyyo somanassanti samāpattito vuṭṭhitassa jhānasukhapaccayā aparāparaṃ somanassaṃ uppajjati. Pamudāti tuṭṭhākārato dubbalapīti. Pāmojjanti balavataraṃ pītisomanassaṃ. Paṭhamo okāsādhigamoti paṭhamajjhānaṃ pañcanīvaraṇāni vikkhambhetvā attano okāsaṃ gahetvā tiṭṭhati, tasmā ‘‘paṭhamo okāsādhigamo’’ti vuttaṃ.

Oḷārikāti ettha kāyavacīsaṅkhārā tāva oḷārikā hontu, cittasaṅkhārā kathaṃ oḷārikāti? Appahīnattā. Kāyasaṅkhārā hi catutthajjhānena pahīyanti, vacīsaṅkhārā dutiyajjhānena, cittasaṅkhārā nirodhasamāpattiyā. Iti kāyavacīsaṅkhāresu pahīnesupi te tiṭṭhantiyevāti pahīne upādāya appahīnattā oḷārikā nāma jātā. Sukhanti nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa uppannaṃ catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpattisukhaṃ. Sukhā bhiyyo somanassati phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhitassa aparāparaṃ somanassaṃ. Dutiyo okāsādhigamoti catutthajjhānaṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ vikkhambhetvā attano okāsaṃ gahetvā tiṭṭhati, tasmā ‘‘dutiyo okāsādhigamo’’ti vuttaṃ. Dutiyatatiyajjhānāni panettha catutthe gahite gahitāneva hontīti visuṃ na vuttānīti.

Oḷārikā Sukha Dutiyo okāsādhigamo

Idaṃ kusalantiādīsu kusalaṃ nāma dasakusalakammapathā. Akusalanti dasaakusalakammapathā. Sāvajjadukādayopi etesaṃ vaseneva veditabbā. Sabbañceva panetaṃ kaṇhañca sukkañca sappaṭibhāgañcāti kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ. Nibbānameva hetaṃ appaṭibhāgaṃ. Avijjā pahīyatīti vaṭṭapaṭicchādikā avijjā pahīyati. Vijjā uppajjatīti arahattamaggavijjā uppajjati. Sukhanti arahattamaggasukhañceva phalasukhañca. Sukhā bhiyyo somanassanti phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhitassa aparāparaṃ somanassaṃ. Tatiyo okāsādhigamoti arahattamaggo sabbakilese vikkhambhetvā attano okāsaṃ gahetvā tiṭṭhati, tasmā ‘‘tatiyo okāsādhigamo’’ti vutto. Sesamaggā pana tasmiṃ gahite antogadhā evāti visuṃ na vuttā.

Idaṃ kusala kusalaṃ Akusala Sāvajjadukādayo kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ. Avijjā pahīyatī Vijjā uppajjatī Sukha Tatiyo okāsādhigamo

Ime pana tayo okāsādhigamā aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇavasena vitthāretvā kathetabbā. Kathaṃ? Sabbāni ārammaṇāni visuddhimagge vuttanayeneva upacāravasena ca appanāvasena ca vavatthapetvā catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhamajjhānaṃ ‘‘paṭhamo okāsādhigamo’’ti kathetabbaṃ. Terasasu ṭhānesu dutiyatatiyajjhānāni, pannarasasu ṭhānesu catutthajjhānañca nirodhasamāpattiṃ pāpetvā ‘‘dutiyo okāsādhigamo’’ti kathetabbaṃ. Dasa upacārajjhānāni pana maggassa padaṭṭhānabhūtāni tatiyaṃ okāsādhigamaṃ bhajanti. Apica tīsu sikkhāsu adhisīlasikkhā paṭhamaṃ okāsādhigamaṃ bhajati, adhicittasikkhā dutiyaṃ, adhipaññāsikkhā tatiyanti evaṃ sikkhāvasenapi kathetabbaṃ. Sāmaññaphalepi cūḷasīlato yāva paṭhamajjhānā paṭhamo okāsādhigamo , dutiyajjhānato yāva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā dutiyo , vipassanāto yāva arahattā tatiyo okāsādhigamoti evaṃ sāmaññaphalasuttantavasenapi kathetabbaṃ. Tīsu pana piṭakesu vinayapiṭakaṃ paṭhamaṃ okāsādhigamaṃ bhajati, suttantapiṭakaṃ dutiyaṃ, abhidhammapiṭakaṃ tatiyanti evaṃ piṭakavasenapi kathetabbaṃ.
