Pubbe kira mahātherā vassūpanāyikāya imameva suttaṃ paṭṭhapenti. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Tīṇi piṭakāni vibhajitvā kathetuṃ labhissāmāti. Tepiṭakena hi samodhānetvā kathentassa dukkathitanti na sakkā vattuṃ. Tepiṭakaṃ bhajāpetvā kathitameva idaṃ suttaṃ sukathitaṃ hotīti.

Catusatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
288. *sukhassādhigamāyā* means for the attainment of the happiness of absorption, the happiness of the path, and the happiness of the fruit. *saṃsaṭṭho* means with associated mind. *ariyadhamma*nti means the Dhamma taught by the noble Lord Buddha. *suṇātī*ti means he hears [the Dhamma] being taught in the presence of the Teacher or by monks, nuns, etc. *yoniso manasikarotī*ti means he applies his mind in a methodical way, with reason, with cause, in the manner of 'impermanent' etc. “‘*yoniso manasikāro* nāma upāyamanasikāro pathamanasikāro, anicce aniccanti dukkhe dukkhanti anattani anattāti asubhe asubhanti saccānulomikena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anvāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro, ayaṃ vuccati yonisomanasikāro’ti.*” means wise consideration is right thinking and attention according to reality. When a thing is impermanent, one considers it as impermanent; this turning of the mind to the actuality of things, the repeated dwelling thereon and the thinking in keeping therewith, - this is called the ‘wise consideration.’ When *yoniso manasikāra* is spoken in this way, it means one undertakes the action. *asaṃsaṭṭho*ti means he dwells not associated with sense pleasures or defilements. *uppajjati sukha*nti means the happiness of the first absorption arises. *sukhā bhiyyo somanassa*nti means when one arises from that attainment, joy arises again and again due to the happiness of absorption. *pamudā*ti means weak joy due to satisfaction. *pāmojja*nti means stronger joy. *paṭhamo okāsādhigamo*ti means the first absorption stands having suppressed the five hindrances and having taken its opportunity, therefore it is said “the first attainment of opportunity”. *oḷārikā*ti Here, the bodily and verbal processes are coarse, how are mental processes coarse? Because they are not abandoned. Bodily processes are abandoned by the fourth absorption, verbal processes by the second absorption, mental processes by the cessation attainment. Thus, even when bodily and verbal processes are abandoned, they still remain, because they are not abandoned based on what has been abandoned, they are called coarse. *sukha*nti means the happiness of the fruit attainment of the fourth absorption that arises for one arising from cessation. *sukhā bhiyyo somanassa*ti means joy again and again for one arising from the fruit attainment. *dutiyo okāsādhigamo*ti means the fourth absorption stands having suppressed happiness and suffering and having taken its opportunity, therefore it is said “the second attainment of opportunity.” But the second and third absorptions are already taken when the fourth is taken, therefore they are not mentioned separately. *idaṃ kusala*ntiādīsu *kusalaṃ* nāma dasakusalakammapathā means In this wholesome, wholesome means the ten paths of wholesome action. *akusala*nti means the ten paths of unwholesome action. *sāvajjadukādayo*pi etesaṃ vaseneva veditabbā means the pairs of blameworthy things should be understood in the same way. sabbañceva panetaṃ kaṇhañca sukkañca sappaṭibhāgañcāti *kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ.* means all of this is black and white and has a counterpart. nibbānameva hetaṃ appaṭibhāgaṃ means only *nirvāṇa* does not have a counterpart. *avijjā pahīyatī*ti means ignorance that covers the round [of rebirth] is abandoned. *vijjā uppajjatī*ti means the knowledge of the path of arahantship arises. *sukha*nti means both the happiness of the path of arahantship and the happiness of the fruit. *sukhā bhiyyo somanassa*nti means joy again and again for one arising from the fruit attainment. *tatiyo okāsādhigamo*ti means the path of arahantship stands having suppressed all the defilements and having taken its opportunity, therefore it is said “the third attainment of opportunity.” But the remaining paths are already included when that is taken, therefore they are not mentioned separately. But these three attainments of opportunity should be spoken of extensively in terms of the thirty-eight objects. How? Having discriminated all objects in the *Visuddhimagga* in the way that has been described, by way of approach and by way of absorption, in twenty-four places, the first *jhāna* should be spoken of as "the first attainment of opportunity" (*okāsādhigama*). In thirteen places, having brought the second and third *jhānas*, and in fifteen places, having brought the fourth *jhāna* and the cessation attainment (*nirodhasamāpatti*) to completion, it should be spoken of as "the second attainment of opportunity." However, the ten approach *jhānas*, being the foundation of the path, partake of the third attainment of opportunity. Moreover, of the three trainings (*śikṣā*), the training in higher ethics (*adhiśīlaśikṣā*) partakes of the first attainment of opportunity, the training in higher mind (*adhicittaśikṣā*) the second, the training in higher wisdom (*adhiprajñāśikṣā*) the third; thus, it should be spoken of in terms of the training. Also, in the fruits of religious life (*sāmaññaphala*), from the Lesser Precepts (*cūḷasīla*) up to the first *jhāna* is the first attainment of opportunity. From the second *jhāna* up to the peak of existence (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) is the second. From insight (*vipaśyanā*) up to *arhatship* is the third attainment of opportunity; thus, it should be spoken of even in terms of the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta*. Moreover, of the three baskets (*piṭaka*), the *Vinaya Piṭaka* partakes of the first attainment of opportunity, the *Sūtra Piṭaka* the second, the *Abhidharma Piṭaka* the third; thus, it should be spoken of even in terms of the *piṭaka*.

Previously, it seems, the great elders established just this *sūtra* for the rains-residence ceremony (*vassūpanāyikā*). Why? [Thinking,] "We will be able to divide and speak of the three *piṭakas*." Indeed, it is not possible to say that the speech of one who, having brought it into accord with the three *piṭakas*, is badly spoken. Having caused [others] to practice the three *piṭakas*, just that *sūtra* is well-spoken.

Commentary on the Four Foundations of Mindfulness (*catusatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā*)

mula_pali:
289. ‘‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paññattā kusalassādhigamāya. Katame cattāro? Idha , bho, bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharanto tattha sammā samādhiyati, sammā vippasīdati. So tattha sammā samāhito sammā vippasanno bahiddhā parakāye ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati…pe… bahiddhā paravedanāsu ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati…pe… bahiddhā paracitte ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharanto tattha sammā samādhiyati, sammā vippasīdati. So tattha sammā samāhito sammā vippasanno bahiddhā paradhammesu ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ime kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paññattā kusalassādhigamāyā’’ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

Satta samādhiparikkhārā
mula_english:
‘What do my lords of the Thirty-Three think? How well has the Lord Buddha who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, pointed out the four foundations of mindfulness ( *cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*) for the attainment of that which is good!

What are the four? Here, a monk abides contemplating the body as body ( *kāye kāyānupassī*) , earnestly, clearly aware, mindful and having put away all hankering and fretting for the world. As he thus dwells contemplating his own body as body, he becomes perfectly concentrated and perfectly serene. Being thus calm and serene, he gains knowledge and vision externally of the bodies of others. He abides contemplating his own feelings as feelings… He gains knowledge and vision externally of the feelings of others. he abides contemplating his own mind as mind… He gains knowledge and vision externally of the minds of others. he abides contemplating his own mind-objects as mind-objects, earnestly, clearly aware, mindful and having put away all hankering and fretting for the world. As he thus dwells contemplating his own mind-objects as mind-objects, he becomes perfectly concentrated and perfectly serene. Being thus calm and serene, he gains knowledge and vision externally of the mind-objects of others. These are the four foundations of mindfulness well pointed out by the Lord Buddha who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, for the attainment of that which is good.’

This was the burden of Brahma Sanankumara’s speech.

He went on:

Seven requisites for concentration
commentary_pali:
289.Kusalassādhigamāyāti maggakusalassa ceva phalakusalassa ca adhigamatthāya. Ubhayampi hetaṃ anavajjaṭṭhena khemaṭṭhena vā kusalameva. Tattha sammāsamādhiyatīti tasmiṃ ajjhattakāye samāhito ekaggacitto hoti. Bahiddhā parakāye ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbattetīti attano kāyato parassa kāyābhimukhaṃ ñāṇaṃ peseti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Sabbattheva ca satimāti padena kāyādipariggāhikā sati, lokoti padena pariggahitakāyādayova loko. Cattāro cete satipaṭṭhānā lokiyalokuttaramissakā kathitāti veditabbā.

Sattasamādhiparikkhāravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
289. *kusalassādhigamāyā* means for the attainment of wholesome things, that is, for the attainment of the wholesome path (*maggakusala*) and the wholesome fruit (*phalakusala*).

Both of these are wholesome (*kusala*) because of being blameless (*anavajjaṭṭhena*) or because of being secure (*khemaṭṭhena*).

*tattha sammāsamādhiyatī* means in that internal body (*ajjhattakāye*), he is collected (*samāhito*) and of one-pointed mind (*ekaggacitto hoti*).

*bahiddhā parakāye ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbattetī* means from his own body (*attano kāyato*), he sends (*peseti*) knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ*) towards the body of another (*parassa kāyābhimukhaṃ*).

This method (*nayaḥ*) applies to all instances (*sabbattha*).

And everywhere (*sabbattha eva ca*) *satimā* by the word means mindfulness (*sati*) that takes hold of the body (*kāyādipariggāhikā*), *loko* by the word means the world (*loko*) is just the body and so on that has been taken hold of (*pariggahitakāyādayova*).

These four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro cete satipaṭṭhānā*) are said to be a mixture (*missakā*) of the mundane (*lokiya*) and the supramundane (*lokuttara*); this should be understood (*veditabbā*).

Explanation of the requisites of the seven samādhis (*sattasamādhiparikkhāravaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
290. ‘‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena satta samādhiparikkhārā sammāsamādhissa paribhāvanāya sammāsamādhissa pāripūriyā. Katame satta? Sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati. Yā kho, bho, imehi sattahaṅgehi cittassa ekaggatā parikkhatā, ayaṃ vuccati, bho, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso itipi saparikkhāro itipi. Sammādiṭṭhissa bho, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti. Sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti , sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti, sammāñāṇassa sammāvimutti pahoti. Yañhi taṃ, bho, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi apārutā amatassa dvārā’ti idameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Svākkhāto hi, bho, bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko, akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi apārutā amatassa dvārā dvārāti (syā. ka.).

‘‘‘Ye hi keci, bho, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā , ye cime opapātikā dhammavinītā sātirekāni catuvīsatisatasahassāni māgadhakā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Atthi cevettha sakadāgāmino.

‘‘Atthāyaṃ athāyaṃ (sī. syā.) itarā pajā, puññābhāgāti me mano;

athāyaṃ (sī. syā.)

Saṅkhātuṃ nopi sakkomi, musāvādassa ottappa’’nti.
mula_english:
290. “What do you think, lords of the Thirty-Three? How well has the Lord Buddha, who knows and sees, pointed out the seven requisites of concentration (*satta samādhiparikkhārā*) for the development of right concentration (*sammāsamādhi*) and the perfection of right concentration (*sammāsamādhissa pāripūriyā*)!

What are the seven? Right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), right intention (*sammāsaṅkappo*), right speech (*sammāvācā*), right action (*sammākammanto*), right livelihood (*sammāājīvo*), right effort (*sammāvāyāmo*), and right mindfulness (*sammāsati*).

That one-pointedness of mind that is produced by these seven factors is called the noble right concentration (*ariyo sammāsamādhi*) with its bases and requisites.

From right view arises right thought (*sammāsaṅkappo*), from right thought arises right speech (*sammāvācā*), from right speech arises right action (*sammākammanto*), from right action arises right livelihood (*sammāājīvo*), from right livelihood arises right effort (*sammāvāyāmo*), from right effort arises right mindfulness (*sammāsati*), from right mindfulness arises right concentration (*sammāsamādhi*), from right concentration arises right knowledge (*sammāñāṇaṃ*), and from right knowledge arises right liberation (*sammāvimutti*).

If anyone truthfully declaring: ‘Well-proclaimed by the Lord is the Dharma (*dhammo*), visible here and now (*sandiṭṭhiko*), timeless (*akāliko*), inviting inspection (*ehipassiko*), leading onward (*opaneyyiko*), to be comprehended by the wise each one for himself (*paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi*) , open are the doors of the Deathless (*amatassa dvārā*)!’ he would be speaking in accordance with the highest truth.

For indeed, my lords, the Dharma (*dhammo*) is well-proclaimed by the Lord, visible here and now (*sandiṭṭhiko*), timeless (*akāliko*), inviting inspection (*ehipassiko*), leading onward (*opaneyyiko*), to be comprehended by the wise, each one for him or herself, and, too, the doors to the Deathless (*amatassa dvārā*) are open!”

“Those who have unshakeable faith (*aveccappasādena samannāgatā*) in the Buddha, the Dharma (*dhamme*) and the Sangha (*saṅghe*), and are endowed with the virtues pleasing to the Noble Ones (*ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā*), those beings who have arisen here on account of their Dhamma-training (*opapātikā dhammavinītā*), amounting to more than twenty-four hundred Magadhan followers who have passed over, have by the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) become Stream-Winners (*sotāpannā*), incapable of falling into states of woe (*avinipātadhammā*) and certain of enlightenment (*niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā*).

and indeed there are Once-Returners (*sakadāgāmino*) here too.

“This other generation is for profit, my mind is for a share of merit;

I am not able to count (them), dread of lying.”
commentary_pali:
290.Samādhiparikkhārāti ettha tayo parikkhārā. ‘‘Ratho sīlaparikkhāro jhānakkho cakkavīriyo’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.4) hi ettha alaṅkāro parikkhāro nāma. ‘‘Sattahi nagaraparikkhārehi suparikkhataṃ hotī’’ti (a. ni. 7.67) ettha parivāro parikkhāro nāma. ‘‘Gilānapaccayajīvitaparikkhāro’’ti (dī. ni. 3.182) ettha sambhāro parikkhāro nāma. Idha pana parivāraparikkhāravasena ‘‘satta samādhiparikkhārā’’ti vuttaṃ. Parikkhatāti parivāritā. Ayaṃ vuccati so ariyo sammāsamādhīti ayaṃ sattahi ratanehi parivuto cakkavattī viya sattahi aṅgehi parivuto ‘‘ariyo sammāsamādhī’’ti vuccati. Saupaniso itipīti saupanissayo itipi vuccati, saparivāro yevāti vuttaṃ hoti. Sammādiṭṭhissāti sammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa. Sammāsaṅkappo pahotīti sammāsaṅkappo pavattati. Esa nayo sabbapadesu. Ayaṃ panattho maggavasenāpi phalavasenāpi veditabbo. Kathaṃ? Maggasammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa maggasammāsaṅkappo pahoti…pe… maggañāṇe ṭhitassa maggavimutti pahoti. Tathā phalasammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa phalasammāsaṅkappo pahoti…pe… phalasammāñāṇe ṭhitassa phalavimutti pahotīti.

Svākkhātotiādīni visuddhimagge vaṇṇitāni. Apārutāti vivaṭā. Amatassāti nibbānassa. Dvārāti pavesanamaggā. Aveccappasādenāti acalappasādena. Dhammavinītāti sammāniyyānena niyyātā.

Svākkhāto visuddhimagge Apārutā Amatassā Dvārā Aveccappasādenā Dhammavinītā

Atthāyaṃ itarā pajāti anāgāmino sandhāyāha, anāgāmino ca atthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Puññabhāgāti puññakoṭṭhāsena nibbattā. Ottappanti ottappamāno. Tena kadāci nāma musā assāti musāvādabhayena saṅkhātuṃ na sakkomi, na pana mama saṅkhātuṃ balaṃ natthīti dīpeti.

Atthāyaṃ itarā pajā Puññabhāgā Ottappa
commentary_english:
290. *Samādhiparikkhārā* means here three requisites.

“The chariot has the requisite of virtue (*śīla*), the axle of *jhāna*, the wheel of energy (*vīrya*)” (Saṃ. Ni. 5.4) here, the requisite (*parikkhāra*) means an ornament (*alaṅkāra*).

“It is well fortified with seven city requisites” (A. Ni. 7.67) here, requisite (*parikkhāra*) means an entourage (*parivāra*).

“Requisite for the sick, means of sustenance, requisite for life” (Dī. Ni. 3.182) here, requisite (*parikkhāra*) means equipment (*sambhāra*).

Here, however, "seven requisites of *samādhi*" is stated in terms of the requisite of entourage (*parivāraparikkhāra*).

*Parikkhatā* means surrounded (*parivāritā*).

*Ayaṃ vuccati so ariyo sammāsamādhī* means this: just as a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*) is surrounded by seven jewels, so "noble right *samādhi*" is said to be surrounded by seven factors.

*Saupaniso itipī* means *saupanissayo itipi* is also said, it is said to be just with an entourage (*saparivāro*).

*Sammādiṭṭhissā* means for one established in right view (*sammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa*).

*Sammāsaṅkappo pahotī* means right thought (*sammāsaṅkappo*) proceeds (*pavattati*).

The same method applies to all the remaining cases.

But this meaning should be understood in terms of the path (*magga*) and also in terms of the fruit (*phala*).

How? For one established in right view of the path (*magga-sammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa*) right thought of the path (*magga-sammāsaṅkappo*) proceeds…pe… for one established in knowledge of the path (*maggañāṇe ṭhitassa*) liberation of the path (*maggavimutti*) proceeds.

Likewise, for one established in right view of the fruit (*phala-sammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa*) right thought of the fruit (*phala-sammāsaṅkappo*) proceeds…pe… for one established in knowledge of the fruit (*phala-sammāñāṇe ṭhitassa*) liberation of the fruit (*phalavimutti*) proceeds.

*Svākkhāto* etc. are described in the *Visuddhimagga*.

*Apārutā* means open (*vivaṭā*).

*Amatassā* means of *Nibbāna* (*nirvāṇa*).

*Dvārā* means paths of entry (*pavesanamaggā*).

*Aveccappasādenā* means with unwavering faith (*acalappasādena*).

*Dhammavinītā* means led out by the right guidance (*sammāniyyānena niyyātā*).

*Svākkhāto*, *Visuddhimagge*, *apārutā*, *amatassā*, *dvārā*, *aveccappasādenā*, *dhammavinītā*

*Atthāyaṃ itarā pajā* he says with reference to the non-returner (*anāgāmino sandhāyāha*), it is said that non-returners exist (*anāgāmino ca atthīti vuttaṃ hoti*).

*Puññabhāgā* means produced by a meritorious portion (*puññakoṭṭhāsena nibbattā*).

*Ottappa* means a measure of reverence (*ottappamāno*).

Therefore, "never may I be false" means he reveals that I am not able to be reckoned because of fear of false speech (*musāvādabhayena saṅkhātuṃ na sakkomi*), but not that I do not have the power to be reckoned (*na pana mama saṅkhātuṃ balaṃ natthīti dīpeti*).

*Atthāyaṃ itarā pajā*, *puññabhāgā*, *ottappa*

mula_pali: 291. ‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha, imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato vessavaṇassa mahārājassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, evarūpopi nāma uḷāro satthā bhavissati, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyissantī’’ti. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vessavaṇassa mahārājassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya vessavaṇaṃ mahārājānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññati bhavaṃ vessavaṇo mahārājā atītampi addhānaṃ evarūpo uḷāro satthā ahosi, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyiṃsu. Anāgatampi addhānaṃ evarūpo uḷāro satthā bhavissati, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyissantī’’’ti.
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, this was the meaning spoken by Brahmā Sanankumāra. As Brahmā Sanankumāra was speaking this meaning, such a thought arose in the mind of the Great King Vessavaṇa: ‘It is amazing, it is wonderful, that such a glorious ( *uḷāra*) Teacher (*satthā*) should arise, that there should be such a glorious ( *uḷāra*) proclamation of the Dharma (*dhammakkhānaṃ*), and that such glorious ( *uḷārā*) paths to the sublime (*visesādhigamā*) should be made known (*paññāyissantī*)!’"

Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra, knowing with his mind the thought in the mind of the Great King Vessavaṇa, said this to the Great King Vessavaṇa: "What do you think, Great King Vessavaṇa? In the past ( *atītampi addhānaṃ*) there has been such a glorious (*uḷāro*) Teacher (*satthā*), such a glorious (*uḷāraṃ*) proclamation of the Dharma (*dhammakkhānaṃ*), and such glorious (*uḷārā*) paths to the sublime (*visesādhigamā*) were made known (*paññāyiṃsu*).

And there will be again in the future (*anāgatampi addhānaṃ*) such a glorious (*uḷāro*) Teacher (*satthā*), such a glorious (*uḷāraṃ*) proclamation of the Dharma (*dhammakkhānaṃ*), and such glorious (*uḷārā*) paths to the sublime (*visesādhigamā*) will be made known (*paññāyissantī*).'"
commentary_pali: 291.Taṃ kiṃ maññati bhavanti iminā kevalaṃ vessavaṇaṃ pucchati, na panassa evarūpo satthā nāhosīti vā na bhavissatīti vā laddhi atthi. Sabbabuddhānañhi abhisamaye viseso natthi.
commentary_english: What does he think that is, O Bhava? With this, he only asks Vessavaṇa. But the view that a teacher of such a form did not exist or will not exist does not exist for him. Indeed, there is no difference in the clear understanding of all Buddhas.

mula_pali:
292. ‘‘‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ abhāsi, imamatthaṃ vessavaṇo mahārājā brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhāsato sammukhā sutaṃ sutvā (sī. pī.) sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ sayaṃ parisāyaṃ ārocesi’’.

Imamatthaṃ janavasabho yakkho vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sayaṃ parisāyaṃ bhāsato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ paṭiggahetvā (sī. pī.) bhagavato ārocesi. Imamatthaṃ bhagavā janavasabhassa yakkhassa sammukhā sutvā sammukhā paṭiggahetvā sāmañca abhiññāya āyasmato ānandassa ārocesi, imamatthamāyasmā ānando bhagavato sammukhā sutvā sammukhā paṭiggahetvā ārocesi bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Tayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitanti.

paṭiggahetvā (sī. pī.)

Janavasabhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra spoke about this matter to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven. The great king Vessavaṇa heard this matter directly from Brahmā Sanankumāra as he spoke to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, accepted it directly, and announced it himself in the assembly.”

Janavasabha the Yaksha heard this matter directly from the great king Vessavaṇa as he spoke in his own assembly, accepted it directly, and reported it to the Blessed One.

Having heard this matter directly from Janavasabha the Yaksha and having accepted it directly, the Blessed One, through his own understanding, related it to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda, having heard this matter directly from the Blessed One and having accepted it directly, related it to the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

And so this holy life has become successful, prosperous, extended, popular, widespread, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.

The Janavasabha Sutta, the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
292.Sayaṃparisāyanti attano parisāyaṃ. Tayidaṃ brahmacariyanti taṃ idaṃ sakalaṃ sikkhattayabrahmacariyaṃ. Sesaṃ uttānameva. Imāni pana padāni dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi ṭhapitānīti.

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Janavasabhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
292. *Sayaṃparisāya* means in his own assembly.

*Tayidaṃ brahmacariya* means that entire three-fold training and holy life.

The rest is evident.

These words, however, were established by the elders who compiled the Dhamma.

Thus ends the commentary on the Janavasabha Sutta in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, commentary to the Dīgha Nikāya.

mula_pali:
293. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho pañcasikho gandhabbaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbataṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yaṃ kho me, bhante, devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ārocemi taṃ bhagavato’’ti. ‘‘Ārocehi me tvaṃ, pañcasikhā’’ti bhagavā avoca.

Devasabhā
mula_english:
Thus have I heard: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on the Vulture Peak (Gijjhakūṭa) mountain.

Then, late in the night, Pañcasikha (Pañcasikho), son of a Gandharva, illuminating the entire Vulture Peak (Gijjhakūṭa) mountain with surpassing radiance, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Pañcasikha, the Gandharva's son, said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir (bhante), I will announce to the Blessed One what I have heard and directly received in the presence of the gods of the Thirty-three (tāvatiṃsānaṃ)."

"Tell me then, Pañcasikha," said the Blessed One.

Devasabhā (devasabhā, assembly of the gods).
commentary_pali:
293.Evaṃme sutanti mahāgovindasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – pañcasikhoti pañcacūḷo pañcakuṇḍaliko. So kira manussapathe puññakammakaraṇakāle daharo pañcacūḷakadārakakāle vacchapālakajeṭṭhako hutvā aññepi dārake gahetvā bahigāme catumaggaṭṭhānesu sālaṃ karonto pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇanto setuṃ bandhanto visamaṃ maggaṃ samaṃ karonto yānānaṃ akkhapaṭighātanarukkhe harantoti evarūpāni puññāni karonto vicaritvā daharova kālamakāsi. Tassa so attabhāvo iṭṭho kanto manāpo ahosi. So kālaṃ katvā cātumahārājikadevaloke navutivassasatasahassappamāṇaṃ āyuṃ gahetvā nibbatti. Tassa tigāvutappamāṇo suvaṇṇakkhandhasadiso attabhāvo ahosi. So sakaṭasahassamattaṃ ābharaṇaṃ pasādhetvā navakumbhamatte gandhe vilimpitvā dibbarattavatthadharo rattasuvaṇṇakaṇṇikaṃ piḷandhitvā pañcahi kuṇḍalakehi piṭṭhiyaṃ vattamānehi pañcacūḷakadārakaparihāreneva vicarati. Tenetaṃ ‘‘pañcasikho’’ tveva sañjānanti.

Abhikkantāya rattiyāti abhikkantāya khīṇāya rattiyā, ekakoṭṭhāsaṃ atītāyāti attho. Abhikkantavaṇṇoti atiiṭṭhakantamanāpavaṇṇo. Pakatiyāpi hesa kantavaṇṇo, alaṅkaritvā āgatattā pana abhikkantavaṇṇo ahosi. Kevalakappanti anavasesaṃ samantato. Anavasesattho ettha kevalasaddo. Kevalaparipuṇṇanti ettha viya. Samantato attho kappasaddo, kevalakappaṃ jetavanantiādīsu viya. Obhāsetvāti ābhāya pharitvā, candimā viya sūriyo viya ca ekobhāsaṃ ekapajjotaṃ karitvāti attho.

Abhikkantāya rattiyā Abhikkantavaṇṇo Kevalakappa Obhāsetvā

Devasabhāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
293. Thus have I heard: the Mahāgovindasutta.

Here, there is a word-by-word explanation of terms that are not obvious: *pañcasikho* means one with five crests (*pañcacūḷo*), one with five earrings (*pañcakuṇḍaliko*). It is said that in the path of humans, while doing meritorious deeds, when he was young, as a boy with five crests, he was the eldest of the cowherds. Taking other boys, outside the village, at the crossroads, constructing halls, digging ponds, building bridges, leveling uneven roads, and removing trees that obstructed the axles of vehicles, he wandered about doing such meritorious deeds and passed away while still young. That existence of his was desired, lovely, and pleasing. After passing away, he was reborn in the heaven of the Four Great Kings, having taken a lifespan of ninety hundred thousand years. His form was three *gāvuta*s in size, like a golden mountain peak. Adorning himself with ornaments worth a thousand cartloads, anointing himself with nine pots of perfume, wearing divine red clothes, wearing red golden earrings, he wanders about with an entourage like that of a five-crested boy, with five earrings circling around his back. Therefore, they recognize him as "Pañcasikha."

*abhikkantāya rattiyā*: *abhikkantāya khīṇāya rattiyā*, meaning, after one portion of the night has passed. *abhikkantavaṇṇo*: of exceedingly desired, lovely, pleasing color. By nature, he was of lovely color, but because he came adorned, he was of exceedingly lovely color. *kevalakappaṃ*: without remainder, completely. Here, the word *kevala* has the meaning of "without remainder." Like in *kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ*. The word *kappa* has the meaning of "completely," as in *kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃtiādīsu*. *obhāsetvā*: having pervaded with radiance (*ābhāya pharitvā*), like the moon or the sun, having made it all one glow, all one illumination.

*abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ obhāsetvā*

Description of the divine assembly.

mula_pali:
294. ‘‘Purimāni, bhante, divasāni purimatarāni tadahuposathe pannarase pavāraṇāya puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā; mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti; puratthimāya disāya dhataraṭṭho mahārājā pacchimābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; dakkhiṇāya disāya virūḷhako mahārājā uttarābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; pacchimāya disāya virūpakkho mahārājā puratthābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; uttarāya disāya vessavaṇo mahārājā dakkhiṇābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā. Yadā bhante, kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti, idaṃ nesaṃ hoti āsanasmiṃ; atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hoti.

‘‘Ye te, bhante, devā bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā adhunūpapannā tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ, te aññe deve atirocanti vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā; ‘dibbā vata, bho, kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’ti.
mula_english:
294. "In earlier days, venerable sir, long ago, on the fifteenth, the *uposatha* day, on the full moon night of the *pavāraṇa*, the Kevalakappa gods and the Thirty-three gods were assembled and gathered in the Sudhamma assembly hall; and a great divine assembly was seated all around, and the Four Great Kings were seated in the four directions. In the eastern direction, the Great King Dhṛtarāṣṭra was seated facing west, having the gods in front of him. In the southern direction, the Great King Virūḍhaka was seated facing north, having the gods in front of him. In the western direction, the Great King Virūpākṣa was seated facing east, having the gods in front of him. In the northern direction, the Great King Vaiśravaṇa was seated facing south, having the gods in front of him.

"When, venerable sir, the Kevalakappa gods and the Thirty-three gods were assembled and gathered in the Sudhamma assembly hall, and a great divine assembly was seated all around, and the Four Great Kings were seated in the four directions, this was their seating arrangement; then afterward, our seating arrangement was made.

"Those gods, venerable sir, who, having lived the holy life under the Blessed One, have recently appeared in the heaven of the Thirty-three, outshone the other gods in beauty and glory.

"Therefore, venerable sir, the Thirty-three gods were delighted, joyful, filled with joy and gladness, saying: 'The hosts of the gods are increasing, the hosts of the *asuras* are decreasing!'"
commentary_pali:
294.Sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyanti sudhammāya nāma itthiyā ratanamattakaṇṇikarukkhanissandena nibbattasabhāyaṃ . Tassā kira phalikamayā bhūmi, maṇimayā āṇiyo , suvaṇṇamayā thambhā, rajatamayā thambhaghaṭikā ca saṅghātā ca, pavāḷamayāni vāḷarūpāni, sattaratanamayā gopānasiyo ca pakkhapāsakā ca mukhavaṭṭi ca, indanīlaiṭṭhakāhi chadanaṃ, sovaṇṇamayaṃ chadanapīṭhaṃ, rajatamayā thūpikā, āyāmato ca vitthārato ca tīṇi yojanasatāni, parikkhepato navayojanasatāni, ubbedhato pañcayojanasatāni, evarūpāyaṃ sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ.

Dhataraṭṭhotiādīsu dhataraṭṭho gandhabbarājā gandhabbadevatānaṃ koṭisatasahassena parivuto koṭisatasahassasuvaṇṇamayāni phalakāni ca suvaṇṇasattiyo ca gāhāpetvā puratthimāya disāya pacchimābhimukho dvīsu devalokesu devatā purato katvā nisinno.

Dhataraṭṭho dhataraṭṭho

Virūḷhako kumbhaṇḍarājā kumbhaṇḍadevatānaṃ koṭisatasahassena parivuto koṭisatasahassarajatamayāni phalakāni ca suvaṇṇasattiyo ca gāhāpetvā dakkhiṇāya disāya uttarābhimukho dvīsu devalokesu devatā purato katvā nisinno.

Virūḷhako

Virūpakkho nāgarājā nāgānaṃ koṭisatasahassena parivuto koṭisatasahassamaṇimayāni mahāphalakāni ca suvaṇṇasattiyo ca gāhāpetvā pacchimāya disāya puratthimābhimukho dvīsu devalokesu devatā purato katvā nisinno.

Virūpakkho

Vessavaṇo yakkharājā yakkhānaṃ koṭisatasahassena parivuto koṭisatasahassapavāḷamayāni mahāphalakāni ca suvaṇṇasattiyo ca gāhāpetvā uttarāya disāya dakkhiṇābhimukho dvīsu devalokesu devatā purato katvā nisinnoti veditabbo.

Vessavaṇo

Atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hotīti tesaṃ pacchato amhākaṃ nisīdituṃ okāso pāpuṇāti. Tato paraṃ pavisituṃ vā passituṃ vā na labhāma. Sannipātakāraṇaṃ panettha pubbe vuttaṃ catubbidhameva. Tesu vassūpanāyikasaṅgaho vitthārito. Yathā pana vassūpanāyikāya, evaṃ mahāpavāraṇāyapi puṇṇamadivase sannipatitvā ‘‘ajja kattha gantvā kassa santike pavāressāmā’’ti mantenti. Tattha sakko devānamindo yebhuyyena piyaṅgudīpamahāvihārasmiṃyeva pavāreti. Sesā devatā pāricchattakādīni dibbapupphāni ceva dibbacandanacuṇṇāni ca gahetvā attano attano manāpaṭṭhānameva gantvā pavārenti. Evaṃ pavāraṇasaṅgahatthāya sannipatanti .

Atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hotī

Devaloke pana āsāvatī nāma latā atthi. Sā pupphissatīti devā vassasahassaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gacchanti. Pāricchattake pupphamāne ekavassaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gacchanti. Te tassa paṇḍupalāsādibhāvato paṭṭhāya attamanā honti. Yathāha –

āsāvatī

‘‘Yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāricchattako koviḷāro paṇḍupalāso hoti, attamanā, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā tasmiṃ samaye honti – ‘paṇḍupalāso kho dāni pāricchattako koviḷāro, na cirasseva pannapalāso bhavissatī’ti. Yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāricchattako koviḷāro pannapalāso hoti, khārakajāto hoti, jālakajāto hoti, kuṭumalakajāto hoti, korakajāto hoti. Attamanā, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā tasmiṃ samaye honti – ‘korakajāto dāni pāricchattako koviḷāro na cirasseva sabbapāliphullo bhavissatī’ti (a. ni. 7.69).

Sabbapāliphullassa kho pana, bhikkhave, pāricchattakassa koviḷārassa samantā paññāsa yojanāni ābhāya phuṭaṃ hoti, anuvātaṃ yojanasataṃ gandho gacchati. Ayamānubhāvo pāricchattakassa koviḷārassā’’ti.

Pupphite pāricchattake ārohaṇakiccaṃ vā aṅkusakaṃ gahetvā namanakiccaṃ vā pupphāharaṇatthaṃ caṅkoṭakakiccaṃ vā natthi, kantanakavāto uṭṭhahitvā pupphāni vaṇṭato kantati, sampaṭicchanakavāto sampaṭicchati, pavesanakavāto sudhammaṃ devasabhaṃ paveseti, sammajjanakavāto purāṇapupphāni nīharati, santharaṇakavāto pattakaṇṇikakesarāni naccanto santharati, majjhaṭṭhāne dhammāsanaṃ hoti. Yojanappamāṇo ratanapallaṅko upari tiyojanena setacchattena dhārayamānena, tadanantaraṃ sakkassa devarañño āsanaṃ atthariyati. Tato tettiṃsāya devaputtānaṃ, tato aññāsaṃ mahesakkhadevatānaṃ. Aññataradevatānaṃ pana pupphakaṇṇikāva āsanaṃ hoti.

Devā devasabhaṃ pavisitvā nisīdanti. Tato pupphehi reṇuvaṭṭi uggantvā upari kaṇṇikaṃ āhacca nipatamānā devatānaṃ tigāvutappamāṇaṃ attabhāvaṃ lākhārasaparikammasajjitaṃ viya karoti. Tesaṃ sā kīḷā catūhi māsehi pariyosānaṃ gacchati. Evaṃ pāricchattakakīḷānubhavanatthāya sannipatanti.

Māsassa pana aṭṭhadivase devaloke mahādhammasavanaṃ ghusati. Tattha sudhammāyaṃ devasabhāyaṃ sanaṅkumāro vā mahābrahmā, sakko vā devānamindo, dhammakathikabhikkhu vā, aññataro vā dhammakathiko devaputto dhammakathaṃ katheti. Aṭṭhamiyaṃ pakkhassa catunnaṃ mahārājānaṃ amaccā, cātuddasiyaṃ puttā, pannarase sayaṃ cattāro mahārājāno nikkhamitvā suvaṇṇapaṭṭañca jātihiṅgulakañca gaṇhitvā gāmanigamarājadhāniyo anuvicaranti. Te – ‘‘asukā nāma itthī vā puriso vā buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato. Saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato. Pañcasīlāni rakkhati. Māsassa aṭṭha uposathe karoti. Mātuupaṭṭhānaṃ pūreti. Pituupaṭṭhānaṃ pūreti. Asukaṭṭhāne uppalahatthakasatena pupphakumbhena pūjā katā. Dīpasahassaṃ āropitaṃ. Akāladhammasavanaṃ kāritaṃ. Chattavedikā puṭavedikā kucchivedikā sīhāsanaṃ sīhasopānaṃ kāritaṃ. Tīṇi sucaritāni pūreti. Dasakusalakammapathe samādāya vattatī’’ti suvaṇṇapaṭṭe jātihiṅgulakena likhitvā āharitvā pañcasikhassa hatthe denti. Pañcasikho mātalissa hatthe deti. Mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devarañño deti.

Yadā puññakammakārakā bahū na honti, potthako khuddako hoti, taṃ disvāva devā – ‘‘pamatto, vata bho mahājano viharati, cattāro apāyā paripūrissanti, cha devalokā tucchā bhavissantī’’ti anattamanā honti. Sace pana potthako mahā hoti, taṃ disvāva devā – ‘‘appamatto, vata bho, mahājano viharati, cattāro apāyā suññā bhavissanti , cha devalokā paripūrissanti, buddhasāsane puññāni karitvā āgate mahāpuññe purakkhatvā nakkhattaṃ kīḷituṃ labhissāmā’’ti attamanā honti. Taṃ potthakaṃ gahetvā sakko devarājā vāceti. Tassa pakatiniyāmena kathentassa saddo dvādasa yojanāni gaṇhāti. Uccena sarena kathentassa ca sakalaṃ dasayojanasahassaṃ devanagaraṃ chādetvā tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ dhammasavanatthāya sannipatanti. Idha pana pavāraṇasaṅgahatthāya sannipatitāti veditabbā.

Tathāgataṃ namassantāti navahi kāraṇehi tathāgataṃ namassamānā . Dhammassa ca sudhammatanti svākkhātatādibhedaṃ dhammassa sudhammataṃ ujuppaṭipannatādibhedaṃ saṅghassa ca suppaṭipattinti attho.

Tathāgataṃ namassantā Dhammassa ca sudhammata

Aṭṭhayathābhuccavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
294. *Sudhammāyaṃ sabhāya* means in the Sudhammā assembly hall, which was created by the essence of the *ratanamattakaṇṇika* tree for a woman named Sudhammā.

Its ground is made of crystal, the nails are made of jewels, the pillars are made of gold, the pillar bases and roofs are made of silver, the balustrades are made of coral, the railings and side walls and doorways are made of seven precious substances, the roof is covered with *indanīla* bricks, the roof platform is made of gold, the spire is made of silver, and its length and breadth are three hundred *yojanas*, its circumference is nine hundred *yojanas*, and its height is five hundred *yojanas*. Such is the Sudhammā assembly hall.

*Dhataraṭṭho* etc., *Dhṛtarāṣṭra* is the Gandharva king, surrounded by a hundred thousand *koṭis* of Gandharva deities, having taken a hundred thousand *koṭis* of gold-made leaves and gold weapons, facing west in the eastern direction, with deities placed in front in the two divine worlds, sits down.

*Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Dhṛtarāṣṭra*, *Virūḷhako* is the Kumbhāṇḍa king, surrounded by a hundred thousand *koṭis* of Kumbhāṇḍa deities, having taken a hundred thousand *koṭis* of silver-made leaves and gold weapons, facing north in the southern direction, with deities placed in front in the two divine worlds, sits down.

*Virūḷhako*, *Virūpākṣa* is the Nāga king, surrounded by a hundred thousand *koṭis* of Nāgas, having taken a hundred thousand *koṭis* of jewel-made great leaves and gold weapons, facing east in the western direction, with deities placed in front in the two divine worlds, sits down.

*Virūpākṣa*, *Vaiśravaṇa* is the Yakṣa king, surrounded by a hundred thousand *koṭis* of Yakṣas, having taken a hundred thousand *koṭis* of coral-made great leaves and gold weapons, facing south in the northern direction, with deities placed in front in the two divine worlds, should be understood.

*Vaiśravaṇa*, "*atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hotī*" means after them, we get the opportunity to sit down. After that, we are unable to enter or see. The cause of assembly here has been previously stated as only fourfold. Among them, the rain-retreat collection has been expanded. Just as for the rain-retreat collection, so too for the great *Pravāraṇā*, having assembled on the full-moon day, they contemplate, "Where shall we go today, near whom shall we end the retreat?". There, Śakra, the lord of the gods, mostly ends the retreat in the Piyaṅgudīpa great monastery itself. The remaining deities, taking divine flowers and divine sandalwood powders etc. from the Pāricchattaka tree, go to their own agreeable places and end the retreat. Thus, they assemble for the sake of the *Pravāraṇā* collection.

"*atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hotī*"

In the divine world, there is a creeper named *Āsāvatī*. Thinking, "It will blossom," the gods attend for a thousand years. When the Pāricchattaka tree is blossoming, they attend for one year. From the time it is yellowing, they are delighted. As it was said:

*Āsāvatī* "In whatever time, monks, the Pāricchattaka koviḷāra of the gods of the Thirty-three becomes yellow-leaved, the gods of the Thirty-three are delighted at that time - 'Now the Pāricchattaka koviḷāra is yellow-leaved, it will soon be full of leaves'. In whatever time, monks, the Pāricchattaka koviḷāra of the gods of the Thirty-three is full of leaves, it is *khārakajāta*, it is *jālakajāta*, it is *kuṭumalakajāta*, it is *korakajāta*. The gods of the Thirty-three are delighted at that time - 'Now the Pāricchattaka koviḷāra is *korakajāta*, it will soon be completely full of flowers' (A.
Ni.
7.
69).

Moreover, monks, from all around the completely flowered Pāricchattaka koviḷāra, fifty *yojanas* are illuminated by light, and the scent travels a hundred *yojanas* downwind. This is the power of the Pāricchattaka koviḷāra."

When the Pāricchattaka is flowering, there is no need for climbing or taking a hook for bending, or for a *caṅkoṭaka* device for the purpose of gathering flowers, the wind that cuts rises up and cuts the flowers from the stems, the receiving wind receives them, the entering wind causes them to enter the Sudhammā divine assembly hall, the sweeping wind carries away the old flowers, the scattering wind scatters the petal-stamens dancing, and in the middle is the Dharma seat. A jewel-couch of the measure of a *yojana*, with a white umbrella held above by three *yojanas*, then a seat is spread out for Śakra, the divine king. Then for the thirty-three sons of the gods, then for the other powerful deities.
On one occasion, a seat was prepared like a flower garland for some of the deities.

Gods, having entered the gods’ assembly hall, sit down.

Then, a stream of pollen, having risen up from the flowers, striking the top of the garland and falling, makes the bodies of the deities, which are about three *gāvutas* in size, appear as if adorned with lacquered ornamentation.

That play of theirs comes to an end in four months.

Thus, they gather together for the sake of experiencing the *Pāricchattaka* tree game.

Moreover, on the eighth day of the month, a great Dhamma-hearing is announced in the world of the gods.

There in the Sudhamma assembly hall of the gods, either Sanankumāra or Mahābrahmā, or Sakka, the lord of the gods, or a *dhamma*-preaching *bhikkhu*, or another *dhamma*-preaching divine son, tells a *dhamma* talk.

On the eighth day of the fortnight, the ministers of the four great kings; on the fourteenth, the sons; on the fifteenth, the four great kings themselves, having gone forth, taking a golden plate and native cinnabar, wander through villages, towns, and capital cities.

They [announce]: “So-and-so, whether woman or man, has gone for refuge to the Buddha, has gone for refuge to the *Dhamma*, has gone for refuge to the *Saṃgha*.

He observes the five precepts.

He performs the observance day on the eighth day of the month.

He fills the needs of his mother.

He fills the needs of his father.

In such and such a place, an offering was made with a hundred *uppala* water lily hand-baskets and flower vases.

A thousand lamps were lit.

An untimely *dhamma*-hearing was arranged.

A tiered platform with parasols, a *puṭa* platform, a *kucchi* platform, a lion throne, and a lion staircase were arranged.

He fulfills the three kinds of good conduct.

Taking up the ten paths of wholesome action, he behaves accordingly,” having written this on a golden plate with native cinnabar, they bring it and give it into the hand of *Pañcasikha*.

*Pañcasikha* gives it into the hand of *Mātali*.

*Mātali*, the charioteer, gives it to Sakka, the king of the gods.

When there are not many doers of meritorious deeds, the book becomes small; having seen that, the gods [think]: “Alas, the great multitude is heedless! The four woeful states will be filled, and the six heavens will become empty,” and they become unhappy.

If, however, the book is large, having seen that, the gods [think]: “Alas, the great multitude is heedful! The four woeful states will become empty, the six heavens will be filled, and having performed meritorious deeds in the Buddha’s dispensation, having come, and placing great merit in front, we will obtain the chance to play at the festival,” and they become happy.

Having taken that book, Sakka, the king of the gods, reads it.

As he speaks with his natural intonation, the sound reaches twelve *yojanas*.

And as he speaks with a loud voice, it covers the entire city of the gods, ten thousand *yojanas* in extent, and stands [there].

Thus, they gather together for the sake of hearing the *Dhamma*.

Here, however, it should be understood that they have gathered together for the sake of the blessing of the *Pravāraṇā*.

“Honoring the *Tathāgata*”: by nine reasons, honoring the *Tathāgata*.

“And the good *Dhamma* of the *Dhamma*”: the excellence of the *Dhamma* as being well-proclaimed, etc.; the excellence of the *Dhamma* as being upright in practice, etc.; and of the *Saṃgha* as being of good practice: this is the meaning.

“Honoring the *Tathāgata*."
of the Dharma and its excellent nature; the explanation of the eight things as they really are.

mula_pali:
295. ‘‘Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’nti.

‘‘Tena sudaṃ , bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyoso mattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā; ‘dibbā vata, bho, kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’’’ti.

Aṭṭha yathābhuccavaṇṇā
mula_english:
“Then, venerable sir, Śakra, the lord of the gods, knowing the satisfaction of the gods of the Thirty-three, rejoiced with these verses:

‘The gods of the Thirty-three, together with Indra, are truly rejoicing,
paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the good nature of the Dharma.

Seeing the new gods, endowed with beauty and fame,
who, having lived the holy life under the Sugata, have come here.

They outshine the others in beauty and in the union with fame;
disciples of great wisdom, they have attained distinction here.

Having seen this, the Thirty-three rejoice, together with Indra,
paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the good nature of the Dharma.’

“Then, venerable sir, the gods of the Thirty-three became even more delighted, joyous, filled with joy and gladness, thinking: ‘The divine bodies are truly filled, while the bodies of the asuras are declining.’”

Eight qualities as they really are.

mula_pali:
296. ‘‘Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘iccheyyātha no tumhe, mārisā, tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sotu’nti? ‘Icchāma mayaṃ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sotu’nti. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā? Yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evaṃ bahujanahitāya paṭipannaṃ bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Svākkhāto kho pana tena bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi. Evaṃ opaneyyikassa dhammassa desetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Idaṃ kusalanti kho pana tena bhagavatā supaññattaṃ, idaṃ akusalanti supaññattaṃ. Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāganti supaññattaṃ. Evaṃ kusalākusalasāvajjānavajjasevitabbāsevitabbahīna-paṇītakaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgānaṃ dhammānaṃ paññapetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Supaññattā kho pana tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā, saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Seyyathāpi nāma gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakena saṃsandati sameti, evameva supaññattā tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā, saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Evaṃ nibbānagāminiyā paṭipadāya paññapetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Abhinipphanno abhinippanno (pī. ka.) kho pana tassa bhagavato lābho abhinipphanno siloko, yāva maññe khattiyā sampiyāyamānarūpā viharanti, vigatamado kho pana so bhagavā āhāraṃ āhāreti. Evaṃ vigatamadaṃ āhāraṃ āharayamānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

abhinippanno (pī. ka.)

‘‘Laddhasahāyo kho pana so bhagavā sekhānañceva paṭipannānaṃ khīṇāsavānañca vusitavataṃ. Te bhagavā apanujja ekārāmataṃ anuyutto viharati. Evaṃ ekārāmataṃ anuyuttaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Yathāvādī kho pana so bhagavā tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī, iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī. Evaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipannaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Tiṇṇavicikiccho kho pana so bhagavā vigatakathaṃkatho pariyositasaṅkappo ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Evaṃ tiṇṇavicikicchaṃ vigatakathaṃkathaṃ pariyositasaṅkappaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā’ti.
mula_english:
‘Then, venerable sir, Śakra, the lord of the gods, knowing the satisfaction of the gods of the Thirty-Three, addressed the gods of the Thirty-Three, saying: “Would you like to hear eight truthful praises of that Blessed One?” “Yes, venerable sir, we would like to hear eight truthful praises of that Blessed One.”

Then, venerable sir, Śakra, the lord of the gods of the Thirty-Three, spoke these eight truthful praises of the Blessed One: “What do my lords, the gods of the Thirty-Three, think? The Blessed One acts for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans.

Thus, we can find no teacher who acts for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans, and who is endowed with these qualities, whether we consider the past or the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Well-proclaimed, truly, is the Dharma by that Blessed One, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be realised by the wise each one for himself.

And we can find no proclaimer of such an onward-leading Dharma, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“This is skillful,” is well-proclaimed by that Blessed One, “this is unskillful,” is well-proclaimed.

“This is blameworthy, this is blameless, this is to be cultivated, this is not to be cultivated, this is inferior, this is superior, this is dark, white, and mixed,” is well-proclaimed.

And we can find none who is a proclaimer of these skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, to be cultivated and not to be cultivated, inferior and superior, dark, white and mixed dharmas, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Well-proclaimed, truly, is the path leading to nirvāṇa for the disciples by that Blessed One; nirvāṇa and the path coincide."

Just as the water of the Ganges meets and joins with the water of the Yamunā, so too the path leading to *nirvāṇa* has been properly declared to the disciples by the Blessed One, and *nirvāṇa* and the path meet.

And we can find no proclaimer of the path leading to *nirvāṇa*, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“The gain of that Blessed One is well-obtained, his fame is well-established; so much so that I think the nobles live with pleasing forms; the Blessed One partakes of food without arrogance.

And we can find no teacher who partakes of food without arrogance, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“And the Lord has gained companions, both learners and those who, having lived the life, have abolished the corruptions.

The Blessed One abandons [evil] and lives devoted to singleness.

And we can find no such teacher devoted to singleness, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“The Blessed One is a speaker in accordance with reality and a doer in accordance with reality; a doer in accordance with reality and a speaker in accordance with reality.” Thus, as the speaker is in accordance with reality, so is the doing, as the doing is in accordance with reality, so is the speaking.

And we can find no teacher who acts in accordance with the Dharma, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“The Blessed One has crossed over doubt, has overcome perplexity, has reached the end of speculation, has attained the essence of the holy life.”

And we can find no teacher who has crossed over doubt, has overcome perplexity, has reached the end of speculation, and has attained the essence of the holy life, endowed with these qualities, either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

commentary_pali:
296.Yathābhucceti yathābhūte yathāsabhāve. Vaṇṇeti guṇe. Payirudāhāsīti kathesi. Bahujanahitāyapaṭipannoti kathaṃ paṭipanno? Dīpaṅkarapādamūle aṭṭha dhamme samodhānetvā buddhatthāya abhinīharamānopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno nāma hoti.

Dānapāramī, sīlapāramī, nekkhammapāramī, paññāpāramī, vīriyapāramī, khantipāramī, saccapāramī, adhiṭṭhānapāramī, mettāpāramī, upekkhāpāramīti kappasatasahassādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni imā dasa pāramiyo pūrentopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno.

Khantivāditāpasakāle, cūḷadhammapālakumārakāle, chaddantanāgarājakāle, bhūridattacampeyyasaṅkhapālanāgarājakāle, mahākapikāle ca tādisāni dukkarāni karontopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno. Vessantarattabhāve ṭhatvā sattasatakamahādānaṃ datvā sattasu ṭhānesu pathaviṃ kampetvā pāramīkūṭaṃ gaṇhantopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno. Tato anantare attabhāve tusitapure yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhantopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno.

Tattha pañca pubbanimittāni disvā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatāhi yācito pañca mahāvilokanāni viloketvā devānaṃ saṅgahatthāya paṭiññaṃ datvā tusitapurā cavitvā mātukucchiyaṃ paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhantopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno.

Dasa māse mātukucchiyaṃ vasitvā lumbinīvane mātukucchito nikkhamantopi, ekūnatiṃsavassāni agāraṃ ajjhāvasitvā mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhamitvā anomanadītīre pabbajantopi, chabbassāni padhānena attānaṃ kilametvā bodhipallaṅkaṃ āruyha sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ paṭivijjhantopi, sattasattāhaṃ bodhimaṇḍe yāpentopi, isipatanaṃ āgamma anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattentopi, yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ karontopi, devorohaṇaṃ orohantopi, buddho hutvā pañcacattālīsa vassāni tiṭṭhantopi, āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajantopi, yamakasālānamantare anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyantopi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno. Yāvassa sāsapamattāpi dhātuyo dharanti, tāva bahujanahitāya paṭipannoti veditabbo. Sesapadāni etasseva vevacanāni. Tattha pacchimaṃ pacchimaṃ purimassa purimassa attho.

Neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahīti atītepi buddhato aññaṃ na samanupassāma, anāgatepi na samanupassāma, etarahi pana aññassa satthuno abhāvatoyeva aññatra tena bhagavatā na samanupassāmāti ayamettha attho. Aṭṭhakathāyampi hi – ‘‘atītānāgatā buddhā amhākaṃ satthārā sadisāyeva, kiṃ sakko kathetī’’ti vicāretvā – ‘‘etarahi bahujanahitāya paṭipanno satthā amhākaṃ satthāraṃ muñcitvā añño koci natthi, tasmā na passāmāti kathetī’’ti vuttaṃ. Yathā ca ettha, evaṃ ito paresupi padesu ayamattho veditabbo. Svākkhātādīni ca kusalādīni ca vuttatthāneva.

Neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahī

Gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakenāti gaṅgāyamunānaṃ samāgamaṭṭhāne udakaṃ vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi saṃsandati sameti, majjhe bhinnasuvaṇṇaṃ viya ekasadisameva hoti, na mahāsamuddaudakena saṃsaṭṭhakāle viya visadisaṃ. Parisuddhassa nibbānassa paṭipadāpi parisuddhāva. Na hi daharakāle vejjakammādīni katvā agocare caritvā mahallakakāle nibbānaṃ daṭṭhuṃ sakkā, nibbānagāminī pana paṭipadā parisuddhāva vaṭṭati ākāsūpamā. Yathā hi ākāsampi alaggaṃ parisuddhaṃ candimasūriyānaṃ ākāse icchiticchitaṭṭhānaṃ gacchantānaṃ viya nibbānaṃ gacchantassa bhikkhuno paṭipadāpi kule vā gaṇe vā alaggā abaddhā ākāsūpamā vaṭṭati. Sā panesā tādisāva bhagavatā paññattā kathitā desitā. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā cā’’ti.

Gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakenā

Paṭipannānanti paṭipadāya ṭhitānaṃ. Vusitavatanti vutthavāsānaṃ etesaṃ. Laddhasahāyoti etesaṃ tattha tattha saha ayanato sahāyo. ‘‘Adutiyo asahāyo appaṭisamo’’ti idaṃ pana asadisaṭṭhena vuttaṃ. Apanujjāti tesaṃ majjhepi phalasamāpattiyā viharanto cittena apanujja, apanujjeva ekārāmataṃ anuyutto viharatīti attho.

Paṭipannāna Vusitavata Laddhasahāyo Apanujjā

Abhinipphannokho pana tassa bhagavato lābhoti tassa bhagavato mahālābho uppanno. Kadā paṭṭhāya uppanno? Abhisambodhiṃ patvā sattasattāhaṃ atikkamitvā isipatane dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvā anukkamena devamanussānaṃ damanaṃ karontassa tayo jaṭile pabbājetvā rājagahaṃ gatassa bimbisāradamanato paṭṭhāya uppanno. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’’nti (saṃ. ni. 2.70). Satasahassakappādhikesu catūsu asaṅkhyeyyesu ussannapuññanissandasamuppanno lābhasakkāro mahogho viya ajjhottharamāno āgacchati.

Abhinipphanno kho pana tassa bhagavato lābho

Ekasmiṃ kira samaye rājagahe sāvatthiyaṃ sākete kosambiyaṃ bārāṇasiyaṃ bhagavato paṭipāṭibhattaṃ nāma uppannaṃ, tattheko – ‘‘ahaṃ sataṃ vissajjetvā dānaṃ dassāmī’’ti paṇṇaṃ likhitvā vihāradvāre bandhi. Añño – ahaṃ dve satāni. Añño – ahaṃ pañca satāni. Añño – ahaṃ sahassaṃ. Añño – ahaṃ dve sahassāni. Añño – ahaṃ pañca. Dasa. Vīsati. Paññāsaṃ; añño – ahaṃ satasahassaṃ. Añño – ahaṃ dve satasahassāni vissajjetvā dānaṃ dassāmī’’ti paṇṇaṃ likhitvā vihāradvāre bandhi. Janapadacārikaṃ carantampi okāsaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘dānaṃ dassāmī’’ti sakaṭāni pūretvā mahājano anubandhiyeva. Yathāha – ‘‘tena kho pana samayena jānapadā manussā bahuṃ loṇampi telampi taṇḍulampi khādanīyampi sakaṭesu āropetvā bhagavato piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti – ‘yattha paṭipāṭiṃ labhissāma, tattha bhattaṃ karissāmā’ti’’ (mahāva. 282). Evaṃ aññānipi khandhake ca vinaye ca bahūni vatthūni veditabbāni.

Asadisadāne panesa lābho matthakaṃ patto. Ekasmiṃ kira samaye bhagavati janapadacārikaṃ caritvā jetavanaṃ sampatte rājā nimantetvā dānaṃ adāsi. Dutiyadivase nāgarā adaṃsu. Puna tesaṃ dānato atirekaṃ rājā, tassa dānato atirekaṃ nāgarāti evaṃ bahūsu divasesu gatesu rājā cintesi – ‘‘ime nāgarā divase divase atirekataraṃ karonti, pathavissaro pana rājā nāgarehi dāne parājitoti garahā bhavissatī’’ti. Athassa mallikā upāyaṃ ācikkhi. So rājaṅgaṇe sālakalyāṇipadarehi maṇḍapaṃ kāretvā taṃ nīluppalehi chādetvā pañca āsanasatāni paññāpetvā pañca hatthisatāni āsanānaṃ pacchābhāge ṭhapetvā ekekena hatthinā ekekassa bhikkhuno setacchattaṃ dhārāpesi. Dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ āsanānaṃ antare sabbālaṅkārapaṭimaṇḍitā ekekā khattiyadhītā catujjātiyagandhaṃ pisati. Niṭṭhitaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ majjhaṭṭhāne gandhambaṇe pakkhipati, taṃ aparā khattiyadhītā nīluppalahatthakena samparivatteti. Evaṃ ekekassa bhikkhuno tisso tisso khattiyadhītaro parivārā, aparā sabbālaṅkārapaṭimaṇḍitā itthī tālavaṇṭaṃ gahetvā bījati, aññā dhamakaraṇaṃ gahetvā udakaṃ parissāveti, aññā pattato udakaṃ harati. Bhagavato cattāri anagghāni ahesuṃ. Pādakathalikā ādhārako apassenaphalakaṃ chattapādamaṇīti imāni cattāri anagghāni ahesuṃ. Saṅghanavakassa deyyadhammo satasahassaṃ agghati. Tasmiñca dāne aṅgulimālatthero saṅghanavako ahosi. Tassa āsanasamīpe ānīto hatthī taṃ upagantuṃ nāsakkhi. Tato rañño ārocesuṃ. Rājā – ‘‘añño hatthī natthī’’ti? Duṭṭhahatthī pana atthi, ānetuṃ na sakkāti. Sammāsambuddho – saṅghanavako kataro mahārājāti? Aṅgulimālatthero bhagavāti. Tena hi taṃ duṭṭhahatthiṃ ānetvā ṭhapetu, mahārājāti. Hatthiṃ maṇḍayitvā ānayiṃsu. So therassa tejena nāsāvātasañcaraṇamattampi kātuṃ nāsakkhi. Evaṃ nirantaraṃ satta divasāni dānaṃ dīyittha. Sattame divase rājā dasabalaṃ vanditvā – ‘‘bhagavā mayhaṃ dhammaṃ desethā’’ti āha.

Tassañca parisati kāḷo ca juṇho cāti dve amaccā honti. Kāḷo cintesi – ‘‘nassati rājakulassa santakaṃ, kiṃ nāmete ettakā janā karissanti, bhuñjitvā vihāraṃ gantvā niddāyissanteva, idaṃ pana eko rājapuriso labhitvā kiṃ nāma na kareyya, aho nassati rañño santaka’’nti. Juṇho cintesi – ‘‘mahantaṃ idaṃ rājattanaṃ nāma, ko añño idaṃ kātuṃ sakkhissati? Kiṃ rājā nāma so, yo rājattane ṭhitopi evarūpaṃ dānaṃ dātuṃ na sakkotī’’ti. Bhagavā parisāya ajjhāsayaṃ olokento tesaṃ dvinnaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā – ‘‘sace ajja juṇhassa ajjhāsayena dhammakathaṃ kathemi, kāḷassa sattadhā muddhā phalissati . Mayā kho pana sattānuddayatāya pāramiyo pūritā. Juṇho aññasmimpi divase mayi dhammaṃ kathayante maggaphalaṃ paṭivijjhissati, idāni pana kāḷaṃ olokessāmī’’ti rañño catuppadikameva gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Na ve kadariyā devalokaṃ vajanti,

Bālā have nappasaṃsanti dānaṃ;

Dhīro ca dānaṃ anumodamāno,

Teneva so hoti sukhī paratthā’’ti. (dha. pa. 177);

Rājā anattamano hutvā – ‘‘mayā mahādānaṃ dinnaṃ, satthā ca me mandameva dhammaṃ kathesi, nāsakkhiṃ maññe dasabalassa cittaṃ gahetu’’nti. So bhuttapātarāso vihāraṃ gantvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā pucchi – ‘‘mayā, bhante, mahantaṃ dānaṃ dinnaṃ, anumodanā ca me na mahatī katā, ko nu kho me, bhante, doso’’ti? Natthi, mahārāja, tava doso, parisā pana aparisuddhā, tasmā dhammaṃ na desesinti. Kasmā pana bhagavā parisā na suddhāti? Satthā dvinnaṃ amaccānaṃ parivitakkaṃ ārocesi. Rājā kāḷaṃ pucchi – ‘‘evaṃ, tāta, kāḷā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mahārājā’’ti. ‘‘Mayi mama santakaṃ dadamāne tava kataraṃ ṭhānaṃ rujjati, na taṃ sakkomi passituṃ, pabbājetha naṃ mama raṭṭhato’’ti āha. Tato juṇhaṃ pakkosāpetvā pucchi – ‘‘evaṃ kira, tāta, cintesī’’ti? ‘‘Āma, mahārājā’’ti. ‘‘Tava cittānurūpameva hotū’’ti tasmiṃyeva maṇḍape evaṃ paññattesuyeva āsanesu pañca bhikkhusatāni nisīdāpetvā tāyeva khattiyadhītaro parivārāpetvā rājagehato dhanaṃ gahetvā mayā dinnasadisameva satta divasāni dānaṃ dehīti. So tathā adāsi. Datvā sattame divase – ‘‘dhammaṃ bhagavā desethā’’ti āha.

Satthā dvinnampi dānānaṃ anumodanaṃ ekato katvā dve mahānadiyo ekoghapuṇṇā kurumāno viya mahādhammadesanaṃ desesi. Desanāpariyosāne juṇho sotāpanno ahosi. Rājā pasīditvā dasabalassa bāhiravatthuṃ nāma adāsi. Evaṃ abhinipphanno kho pana tassa bhagavato lābhoti veditabbo.

Abhinipphannosilokoti vaṇṇaguṇakittanaṃ. Sopi bhagavato dhammacakkappavattanato paṭṭhāya abhinipphanno. Tato paṭṭhāya hi bhagavato khattiyāpi vaṇṇaṃ kathenti. Brāhmaṇāpi gahapatayopi nāgā supaṇṇā gandhabbā devatā brahmānopi kittiṃ vatvā – ‘‘itipi so bhagavā’’tiādinā. Aññatitthiyāpi vararojassa sahassaṃ datvā samaṇassa gotamassa avaṇṇaṃ kathehīti uyyojesuṃ. So sahassaṃ gahetvā dasabalaṃ pādatalato paṭṭhāya yāva kesantā apalokayamāno likkhāmattampi vajjaṃ adisvā – ‘‘vippakiṇṇadvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇe asītianubyañjanavibhūsite byāmappabhāparikkhitte suphullitapāricchattakatārāgaṇasamujjalitaantalikkhavicittakusumasassirikanandanavanasadise anavajjaattabhāve avaṇṇaṃ vadantassa mukhampi viparivatteyya, muddhāpi sattadhā phaleyya, avaṇṇaṃ vattuṃ upāyo natthi, vaṇṇameva vadissāmī’’ti pādatalato paṭṭhāya yāva kesantā atirekapadasahassena vaṇṇameva kathesi. Yamakapāṭihāriye panesa vaṇṇo nāma matthakaṃ patto. Evaṃ abhinipphanno silokoti.

Abhinipphanno siloko vaṇṇo

Yāva maññe khattiyāti khattiyā brāhmaṇā vessā suddā nāgā supaṇṇā yakkhā asurā devā brahmānoti sabbeva te sampiyāyamānarūpā haṭṭhatuṭṭhā viharanti. Vigatamado kho panāti ettakā maṃ janā sampiyāyamānarūpā viharantīti na madapamatto hutvā davādivasena āhāraṃ āhāreti, aññadatthu vigatamado kho pana so bhagavā āhāraṃ āhāreti.

Yāva maññe khattiyā Vigatamado kho panā

Yathāvādīti yaṃ vācāya vadati, tadanvayamevassa kāyakammaṃ hoti. Yañca kāyena karoti, tadanvayamevassa vacīkammaṃ hoti. Kāyo vā vācaṃ, vācā vā kāyaṃ nātikkamati, vācā kāyena, kāyo ca vācāya sameti. Yathā ca –

Yathāvādī

‘‘Vāmena sūkaro hoti, dakkhiṇena ajāmigo;

Sarena nelako hoti, visāṇena jaraggavo’’ti. –

Ayaṃ sūkarayakkho sūkare disvā sūkarasadisaṃ vāmapassaṃ dassetvā te gahetvā khādati, ajāmige disvā taṃsadisaṃ dakkhiṇapassaṃ dassetvā te gahetvā khādati, nelakavacchake disvā vacchakaravaṃ ravanto te gahetvā khādati, goṇe disvā tesaṃ visāṇasadisāni visāṇāni māpetvā te dūratova – ‘‘goṇo viya dissatī’’ti evaṃ upagate gahetvā khādati. Yathā ca dhammikavāyasajātake sakuṇehi puṭṭho vāyaso – ‘‘ahaṃ vātabhakkho, vātabhakkhatāya mukhaṃ vivaritvā pāṇakānañca maraṇabhayena ekeneva pādena ṭhito, tasmā tumhepi –

‘‘Dhammaṃ caratha bhaddaṃ vo, dhammaṃ caratha ñātayo;

Dhammacārī sukhaṃ seti, asmiṃ loke paramhi cā’’ti.

Sakuṇesu vissāsaṃ uppādesi, tato –

‘‘Bhaddako vatāyaṃ pakkhī, dijo paramadhammiko;

Ekapādena tiṭṭhanto, dhammo dhammoti bhāsatī’’ti.

Evaṃ vissāsamāgate sakuṇe khādittha. Tena tesaṃ vācā kāyena, kāyo ca vācāya na sameti, na evaṃ bhagavato. Bhagavato pana vācā kāyena, kāyo ca vācāya sametiyevāti dasseti.

Tiṇṇā taritā vicikicchā assāti tiṇṇavicikiccho. ‘‘Kathamidaṃ kathamida’’nti evarūpā vigatā kathaṃkathā assāti vigatakathaṃkatho. Yathā hi mahājano – ‘‘ayaṃ rukkho, kiṃ rukkho nāma, ayaṃ gāmo, ayaṃ janapado, idaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, kiṃ raṭṭhaṃ nāma, kasmā nu kho ayaṃ rukkho ujukkhandho, ayaṃ vaṅkakkhandho, kasmā kaṇṭako koci ujuko hoti, koci vaṅko, pupphaṃ kiñci sugandhaṃ, kiñci duggandhaṃ, phalaṃ kiñci madhuraṃ, kiñci amadhura’’nti sakaṅkhova hoti, na evaṃ satthā. Satthā hi – ‘‘imesaṃ nāma dhātūnaṃ ussannussannattā idaṃ evaṃ hotī’’ti vigatakathaṃkathova . Yathā ca paṭhamajjhānādilābhīnaṃ dutiyajjhānādīsu kaṅkhā hoti. Paccekabuddhānampi hi sabbaññutaññāṇe yāthāvasanniṭṭhānābhāvato vohāravasena kaṅkhā nāma hotiyeva, na evaṃ buddhassa. So hi bhagavā sabbattha vigatakathaṃkathoti dasseti.

tiṇṇavicikiccho. vigatakathaṃkatho.

Pariyositasaṅkappoti yathā keci sīlamattena, keci vipassanāmattena, keci paṭhamajjhānena…pe… keci nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā, keci sotāpannabhāvamattena…pe… keci arahattena, keci sāvakapāramīñāṇena, keci paccekabodhiñāṇena pariyositasaṅkappā paripuṇṇamanorathā honti, na evaṃ mama satthā. Mama pana satthā sabbaññutaññāṇena pariyositasaṅkappoti dasseti.

Pariyositasaṅkappo

Ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyanti karaṇatthe paccattavacanaṃ, adhikāsayena uttamanissayabhūtena ādibrahmacariyena porāṇabrahmacariyabhūtena ca ariyamaggena tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho pariyositasaṅkappoti attho. ‘‘Pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu sāmaṃ saccāni abhisambujjhi, tattha ca sabbaññutaṃ patto, balesu ca vasībhāva’’nti hi vacanato pariyositasaṅkappatāpi bhagavato ariyamaggeneva nipphannāti.

Ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya
commentary_english:
296. *Yathābhucce* means according to what is true, according to its own nature. *Vaṇṇe* means qualities (guṇa). *Payirudāhāsī* means he spoke. *Bahujanahitāya paṭipanno* means how does he practice? He is called one who practices for the benefit of many, having harmonized the eight dharmas at the foot of Dīpaṅkara and aspiring to Buddhahood. Giving (dānapāramī), ethical discipline (śīlapāramī), renunciation (nekkhammapāramī), wisdom (prajñāpāramī), diligent perseverance (vīryapāramī), forbearance (kṣāntipāramī), truthfulness (saccapāramī), resolute determination (adhiṭṭhānapāramī), loving-kindness (mettāpāramī), and equanimity (upekkhāpāramī) are the four immeasurable qualities, exceeding hundreds of thousands of aeons; he is one who practices for the benefit of many, even while fulfilling these ten perfections (pāramitās). In the time of Khantivāditāpasa, in the time of Cūḷadhammapālakumāra, in the time of Chaddantanāgarāja, in the time of Bhūridattacampeyyasaṅkhapālanāgarāja, and in the time of Mahākapi, he is one who practices for the benefit of many, even while performing such difficult deeds. Having remained in the state of Vessantara and having given the great gift of seven hundred, having caused the earth to tremble in seven places, he is one who practices for the benefit of many, even while taking the pinnacle of perfections (pāramīkūṭa). Then, in the immediately following existence, in the Tusita heaven, he is one who practices for the benefit of many, even while remaining there for the duration of his life. There, having seen the five preliminary signs, having been requested by the gods of ten thousand world-systems, having considered the five great contemplations, having given the pledge to the gods for the sake of their welfare, he is one who practices for the benefit of many, having passed away from the Tusita heaven and taken rebirth in his mother's womb. Having dwelt in his mother's womb for ten months, having emerged from his mother's womb in the Lumbinī Grove, having lived in a house for twenty-nine years, having gone forth in the great renunciation, having become a renunciate on the bank of the Anoma River, having tormented himself with exertion for six years, having ascended the *bodhipallaṅka*, having penetrated the knowledge of omniscience, having spent seven weeks at the *bodhimaṇḍa*, having arrived at Isipatana, having set in motion the unexcelled Wheel of the Dharma, having performed the Twin Miracle, having descended from the heaven of the gods, having become a Buddha and having remained for forty-five years, having relinquished the life force, having attained *parinirvāṇa* in the element of *nirvāṇa* without remainder between the twin *sāla* trees, he is one who practices for the benefit of many. As long as even a mustard seed's worth of his relics remain, so long should he be known as one who practices for the benefit of many. The remaining words are synonyms of this. There, the latter is the meaning of the former. "We do not regard [him] in the past, nor do we now," means that even in the past, we do not regard another besides the Buddha; even in the future, we do not regard [another]; but now, because of the absence of another teacher, we do not regard [another] other than by that Blessed One—this is the meaning here. Moreover, in the commentary, it is said: "The Buddhas of the past and future are similar to our teacher, who is able to speak?" Having considered, "Now, the teacher who practices for the benefit of many, having released our teacher, there is no other whatsoever; therefore, we do not see [another]," it is said. Just as here, so also in the remaining places, this meaning should be understood. *Svākkhāta* and so forth, and *kusala* and so forth, [have] the same meaning as stated. "We do not regard [him] in the past, nor do we now." "*Gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakenā*" means that in the place of confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna, the water mingles and unites in color, smell, and taste, and in the middle, it is just the same, like refined gold; it is not dissimilar, as when mixed with ocean water. The practice of the pure *nirvāṇa* is also pure. For it is not possible to see *nirvāṇa* in old age, having done medical work and so forth in youth and having wandered in unsuitable places; but the practice leading to *nirvāṇa* is pure and like the sky. Just as the sky is unattached and pure, so too, like the moon and sun going to desired places in the sky, the practice of a *bhikkhu* who goes to *nirvāṇa* is unattached to families or groups, is unfettered and like the sky. That, indeed, is how it was declared, spoken, and taught by the Blessed One. Therefore, it was said, " *Nirvāṇa* and the practice meet." "*Gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakenā*" "*Paṭipannāna*" means standing in practice. "*Vusitavata*" means for those who have lived [the holy life]. "*Laddhasahāyo*" means for them, a companion from going together there. "Without a second, without a companion, without an equal," this, however, was said with the meaning of incomparable. "*Apanujjā*" means even in their midst, while dwelling in the attainment of fruition, having forsaken [distractions] with his mind, just he, devoted to solitude, dwells—this is the meaning. *Paṭipannāna vusitavata laddhasahāyo apanujjā* *Abhinipphanno* "What gain, indeed, [was] to that Blessed One?" means that a great gain arose to that Blessed One.From when did this arise? Having attained complete enlightenment, having passed seven weeks, having set the wheel of the Dhamma in motion at Ṛṣipatana, as he was gradually taming gods and humans, after ordaining three ascetics with matted hair, and after going to Rājagṛha, from the taming of Bimbisāra this arose. With reference to what was said: "Now at that time, the Blessed One was honored, respected, esteemed, venerated, revered, and a recipient of robes, alms food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites" (Saṃ. Ni. 2. 70). The gain and honor that arose from the outpouring of merit accumulated over four incalculable eons beyond one hundred thousand eons comes like a great flood that overwhelms [everything]. The gain of that Blessed One was perfected. It is said that once upon a time in Rājagṛha, Śrāvastī, Sāketa, Kauśāmbī, and Vārāṇasī, a turn-based meal for the Blessed One arose. There, one person wrote a pledge on a leaf saying, "I will spend one hundred [coins] and give a donation," and tied it to the monastery door. Another: "I [will give] two hundred." Another: "I [will give] five hundred." Another: "I [will give] one thousand." Another: "I [will give] two thousand." Another: "I [will give] five." Ten. Twenty. Fifty; another: "I [will give] one hundred thousand." Another: "I will spend two hundred thousand [coins] and give a donation," and wrote a pledge on a leaf and tied it to the monastery door. Even while wandering on a tour through the country, having obtained an opportunity, filling carts [with goods] saying "I will give a donation," a great crowd followed behind. As he said: "Now at that time, the people of the country, loading much salt, oil, rice, and edibles onto carts, followed behind the Blessed One, thinking: 'Where we will obtain a turn [to give], there we will prepare a meal'" (Mahāva. 282). Thus, other things too should be known from the Khandhaka and the Vinaya. This gain reached its peak in unequaled giving. It is said that once upon a time, when the Blessed One, having wandered on a tour through the country, arrived at Jetavana, the king invited [him] and gave a donation. On the second day, the townspeople gave. Again, the king [gave] more than their donation, and the townspeople [gave] more than his donation. Thus, after many days had passed, the king thought: "These townspeople are doing more and more each day. It will be a disgrace if King Prasenajit is defeated in giving by the townspeople." Then Mallikā told him a plan. He had a pavilion made in the royal courtyard with auspicious Śāla saplings and decorated it with blue lotuses. Having prepared five hundred seats, having placed five hundred elephants behind the seats, he had each elephant hold a white parasol for each monk. Between every two seats, a Kṣatriya maiden, adorned with all ornaments, ground four kinds of fragrant substances. Having finished grinding, they would put it in a fragrant bowl in the middle, and another Kṣatriya maiden would stir it with a blue lotus hand. Thus, for each monk, there were three Kṣatriya maidens as attendants. Another woman, adorned with all ornaments, took a palm fan and fanned [him], another took a water filter and filtered water, another brought water from the bowl. The Blessed One had four priceless things. A footrest, a support, a leaning board, and a parasol foot jewel—these were the four priceless things. The gift worthy of the Sangha-novice is worth one hundred thousand. And in that donation, Aṅgulimāla Thera was a Sangha-novice. The elephant that was brought near his seat was unable to approach him. Then they reported to the king. The king: “Is there no other elephant?” But there was a rogue elephant, (but) it is not possible to bring (him). The Perfectly Awakened One: “Which Saṃgha-novice (is) the best, Great King?” Aṅgulimāla, venerable sir. “Then bring that rogue elephant and keep (him) there, Great King.” They decorated the elephant and brought (him). He, by the elder's power, was not able to make even the slightest movement of his nostril wind. Thus, continuously for seven days, alms were given. On the seventh day, the king, having venerated the Daśabala, said, “Venerable One, teach me the Dharma!”

And in his assembly were two advisors, Kāḷa and Juṇha. Kāḷa thought, “The property of the royal family is being destroyed. What will these many people do? Having eaten, they will go to the monastery and fall asleep. But if one royal official obtains this, what might he not do? Alas, the king's property is being destroyed!” Juṇha thought, “This royal estate is great indeed. Who else will be able to do this? What kind of king is he, who, even while situated in his royal estate, is not able to give such alms?” The Blessed One, looking upon the inclinations of the assembly, knowing the inclinations of those two, (thought:) “If today I speak a Dharma-talk according to Juṇha's inclination, Kāḷa's head will split into seven pieces. I have fulfilled the perfections through compassion for beings. Juṇha, even on another day, while I am speaking the Dharma, will penetrate the path and the fruit. Now, however, I will look to Kāḷa," and spoke this verse of four lines to the king:

“Misers do not go to the world of the gods,

fools surely do not praise giving;

but the wise one, rejoicing in giving,

by that very (deed) is happy in the next world.” (Dha. Pa. 177);

The king, being displeased, (thought:) “I have given a great gift, but the Teacher spoke to me of only a small matter of Dharma. I was not able, I think, to grasp the mind of the Daśabala.” He, having eaten his morning meal, went to the monastery, venerated the Blessed One, and asked: “I, venerable sir, have given a great gift, but the approval was not great for me.
