What, venerable sir, is my fault?” (The Buddha said:) “There is no fault of yours, Great King, but the assembly is impure, therefore I did not teach the Dharma." “Why, venerable sir, is the assembly not pure?” The Teacher told (him) the deliberation of the two advisors. The king asked Kāḷa: “Is it so, dear Kāḷa?” “Yes, Great King.” “While I am giving my own property, what place of yours is being ruined? I am not able to see that. Banish him from my kingdom!” he said. Then, having summoned Juṇha, he asked: “Is it true that you thought thus, dear?” “Yes, Great King.” “May it be just as your mind approves!” Thus, in that very pavilion, on seats arranged in just that way, having seated five hundred monks, and having those very daughters of nobles attend (to them), having taken wealth from the royal palace, (he said:) “Give alms for seven days, just like I gave!” He gave thus. Having given, on the seventh day he said, “May the Blessed One teach the Dharma!”

The Teacher, having made the approval of both almsgivings one, as if making two great rivers full with one flood, taught a great Dharma-teaching. At the end of the teaching, Juṇha became a stream-enterer (sotāpanna). The king, being pleased, gave a "Bāhiravatthu"-named (gift) to the Daśabala. Thus, it should be understood, that gain of that Blessed One was completely accomplished. Here is the translation: [He is] fully accomplished; *śiloka* means the praising of [the Buddha's] virtues and qualities. That [praise] also became fully accomplished, starting from the time the Blessed One set in motion the Wheel of the Dharma. From then on, even *kṣatriyas* told of [his] virtues. Even *brāhmaṇas*, householders, *nāgas*, *suparṇas*, *gandharvas*, gods, [and] *Brahmās*, having spoken [his] praise, [said]—"So indeed is the Blessed One," etc. Even other sectarians, having given a thousand [coins] to Vararoja, incited [him], "Go and speak disparagingly of the *śramaṇa* Gautama!" Having taken the thousand [coins], and looking for a fault from the soles of the feet up to the ends of the hairs of the head of the one with the ten powers, not seeing even the slightest fault, [he said]—"If I, in the presence of the faultless being who is adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man that are scattered [all over his body], who is resplendent with the eighty minor marks, who is surrounded by a fathom's extent of light, [and] who is like a Nandanavana forest abounding with diverse flowers and with the beauty of the multitude of stars of the *pāricchattaka* tree in full bloom in the sky, should speak disparagingly, even my mouth would be turned inside out, and my head would split into seven pieces! There is no way to speak disparagingly. I will speak only of [his] virtues!"—From the soles of his feet up to the ends of the hairs of his head, he spoke only of [his] virtues with an abundance of a thousand more words. In the Twin Miracle, this virtue, namely, attained the highest point. Thus, the *śiloka* is fully accomplished. [He is] fully accomplished; *śiloka*, virtue. As far as "I think *kṣatriyas*," the *kṣatriyas*, *brāhmaṇas*, *vaiśyas*, *śūdras*, *nāgas*, *suparṇas*, *yakṣas*, *asuras*, gods, [and] *Brahmās*—all of them live happily, with delighted and joyful minds, in a state of loving-kindness. "He is without intoxication, indeed" means: Thinking, "So many people live happily in a state of loving-kindness towards me," he does not partake of food through being intoxicated by pride, through [being influenced by] fire, etc. Rather, that Blessed One partakes of food without intoxication, indeed. As far as "I think *kṣatriyas*," [and] "He is without intoxication, indeed." "He speaks according to what he does" means: Whatever he speaks with his voice, his bodily action is in accordance with that. Whatever he does with his body, his verbal action is in accordance with that. The body does not transgress the voice, nor does the voice transgress the body; the voice accords with the body, and the body accords with the voice. And as [it is said]: "On the left [side] there is a pig, on the right a goat; With sound there is a *nelaka*, with horn a decrepit ox." This pig-*yakṣa*, having seen pigs, shows a pig-like left side, and taking them, eats [them]. Having seen goats, [he] shows a similar right side, and taking them, eats [them]. Having seen *nelaka* calves, roaring the roar of a calf, he takes them and eats [them]. Having seen bulls, creating horns similar to their horns, and even from afar [saying]—"He looks like a bull!"—when they have approached in this way, he takes and eats [them]. And as in the *Dhammika-vāyasa-jātaka*, the crow, being asked by the birds—"I am a wind-eater; for the sake of [my] being a wind-eater, having opened my mouth, and through fear of death for the beings, I stand on one foot only; therefore, may you also—" "Practice the Dharma, may good fortune be yours; practice the Dharma, relatives! The practitioner of the Dharma sleeps happily in this world and in the next." He instilled confidence in the birds. Then— "This bird is auspicious, twice-born, and extremely righteous; Standing on one foot, he speaks, 'Dharma, Dharma!'" In this way, he ate the birds that had come to trust [him]. Therefore, their voice does not accord with [their] body, nor does their body accord with [their] voice. The Blessed One is not like that. But the Blessed One's voice accords with [his] body, and [his] body accords with [his] voice. [Thus] he shows. One who has crossed over, who has traversed doubt, is "one who has crossed over doubt." "How is this? How is that?" When doubt of this sort is gone, he is "one from whom questioning is gone." Just as, indeed, the masses [ask]—"This is a tree; what is the name of this tree? This is a village; this is a district; this is a kingdom; what is the name of this kingdom? Why, now, is this tree straight-trunked, [and] this one crooked-trunked? Why is one thorn straight, [and] one crooked? One flower is fragrant, [and] one foul-smelling; one fruit is sweet, [and] one unsweet?"—he is with doubt. The Teacher is not like that. For the Teacher—"Because of the prominence and non-prominence of these elements, this is so"—is without questioning. And as for those who have gained the first *dhyāna*, etc., there is doubt about the second *dhyāna*, etc. Even for the *pratyekabuddhas* there is, through the lack of a thorough ascertainment in the knowledge of omniscience, doubt in terms of convention, indeed. The Buddha is not like that. For that Blessed One shows that he is everywhere free from questioning. One who has crossed over doubt. One from whom questioning is gone. That is "pariyositasaṅkappo": Just as some [consider their aims] fulfilled merely by morality (sīla), some merely by insight (vipassanā), some by the first jhāna…pe… some by the attainment of the state of neither perception nor non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatana-samāpatti), some merely by the state of a stream-enterer (sotāpanna)…pe… some by arahantship, some by the knowledge of a disciple's perfection, some by the knowledge of a Paccekabuddha; [these] have their aims fulfilled and their wishes complete, but my teacher is not like that. But my teacher shows [that his] aim is fulfilled by the knowledge of omniscience (sabbaññutaññāṇa). "pariyositasaṅkappo, ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya": "[The phrase] 'inclined to the original holy life' (ādibrahmacariya)" is a word denoting the instrument, [meaning] that one whose doubts are crossed over, whose questioning is dispelled, by the noble path (ariyamagga), which is the foremost basis, the original holy life, the ancient holy life, is "pariyositasaṅkappo"; this is the meaning. For it is said, "Formerly, regarding things unheard of before, he himself awakened to the truths (saccāni), and there he attained omniscience (sabbaññutaṃ), and mastery in the powers (balesu)," therefore, the Blessed One's state of having fulfilled his aim (pariyositasaṅkappatā) is accomplished by the noble path (ariyamagga) alone. "ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya"

mula_pali: 297. ‘‘Ime kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyoso mattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sutvā. Tatra, bhante, ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘aho vata, mārisā, cattāro sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘tiṭṭhantu, mārisā, cattāro sammāsambuddhā, aho vata, mārisā, tayo sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘tiṭṭhantu, mārisā, tayo sammāsambuddhā, aho vata, mārisā, dve sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti.
mula_english:
297. Then, venerable sir, Śakka, the lord of the gods, proclaimed these eight truthful statements in praise of the Blessed One to the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.

Having heard the Blessed One’s eight truthful statements in praise, the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three were even more pleased, overjoyed, and filled with delight and happiness.

Then, venerable sir, some gods exclaimed, “Oh, if only four fully enlightened Buddhas were to arise in the world and teach the Dharma just like the Blessed One! That would be for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans!”

Some gods exclaimed: “Never mind four fully enlightened Buddhas — three would suffice! That would be for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans!”

Some gods exclaimed: “Never mind three fully enlightened Buddhas, gentlemen — two would suffice! That would be for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans!”
commentary_pali: 297.Yathariva bhagavāti yathā bhagavā, evaṃ ekasmiṃ jambudīpatale catūsu disāsu cārikaṃ caramānā aho vata cattāro jinā dhammaṃ deseyyunti paccāsisamānā vadanti. Athāpare tīsu maṇḍalesu ekato vicaraṇabhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā tayo sammāsambuddhāti āhaṃsu. Apare – ‘‘dasa pāramiyo nāma pūretvā catunnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā uppatti dullabhā, sace pana eko nibaddhavāsaṃ vasanto dhammaṃ deseyya, eko cārikaṃ caranto, evampi jambudīpo sobheyya ceva, bahuñca hitasukhamadhigaccheyyā’’ti cintetvā aho vata, mārisāti āhaṃsu.
commentary_english: "As if the Blessed One (yathariva bhagavā)": Just as the Blessed One (yathā bhagavā), thus, on one surface of Jambudvīpa (jambudīpatale), wandering in the four directions (catūsu disāsu), they, hoping, say, "Oh, may there be four Jinas who teach the Dharma (dhammaṃ deseyyunti)!" Then others, desiring the state of wandering together in the three realms (tīsu maṇḍalesu ekato vicaraṇabhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā), said, "There are three perfectly awakened Buddhas (tayo sammāsambuddhā)." Others [said]: "Having fulfilled the ten perfections (dasa pāramiyo nāma pūretvā), the arising of four or three [Buddhas] is difficult (catunnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā uppatti dullabhā). If one, dwelling in constant residence (eko nibaddhavāsaṃ vasanto), should teach the Dharma (dhammaṃ deseyya), [and] one, wandering on pilgrimage (eko cārikaṃ caranto), even so, Jambudvīpa (jambudīpo) would shine and gain much benefit and happiness (bahuñca hitasukhamadhigaccheyyā." Thinking thus, they said, "Oh, indeed, friends (aho vata, mārisā)!"

mula_pali:
298. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte , bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse etadavoca – ‘aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, mārisā, anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Aho vata, mārisā, so bhagavā appābādho appātaṅko ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Atha kho, bhante, yenatthena devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā vuttavacanāpi taṃ cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti. Paccānusiṭṭhavacanāpi taṃ cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti, sakesu sakesu āsanesu ṭhitā avipakkantā.

Te vuttavākyā rājāno, paṭiggayhānusāsaniṃ;

Vippasannamanā santā, aṭṭhaṃsu samhi āsaneti.
mula_english:
“When this was said, venerable sir, Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven: ‘This is impossible, gentlemen, it cannot happen that two *arhats*, perfectly awakened Buddhas, should arise simultaneously in a single world-system. This cannot be. May this Blessed Lord continue to live long, for many years to come, free from sickness and disease! That would be for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit and happiness of gods and humans!’

“And then, venerable sir, the Four Great Kings were advised and admonished on this matter, after the Thirty-Three Gods had consulted and deliberated together about the matter concerning which they had assembled in the Sudharmā Hall, and they gave considered opinions. The Four Great Kings remained standing by their seats, unmoving.

Having received the instruction, those kings, whose words were spoken, accepted the teaching; being of joyful mind and serene, they stood in their assembly seats.
commentary_pali:
298.Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yanti ettha ṭhānaṃ avakāsoti ubhayametaṃ kāraṇādhivacanameva. Kāraṇañhi tiṭṭhati ettha tadāyattavuttitāya phalanti ṭhānaṃ. Okāso viya cassa taṃ tena vinā aññattha abhāvatoti avakāso. Yanti karaṇatthe paccattaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘yena kāraṇena ekissā lokadhātuyā dve buddhā ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, taṃ kāraṇaṃ natthī’’ti.

Ettha ca –

‘‘Yāvatā candimasūriyā, pariharanti disā bhanti virocanā;

Tāva sahassadhā loko, ettha te vattate vaso’’ti. (ma. ni. 1.503) –

Gāthāya ekacakkavāḷameva ekā lokadhātu. ‘‘Sahassī lokadhātu akampitthā’’ti (a. ni. 3.126) āgataṭṭhāne cakkavāḷasahassaṃ ekā lokadhātu. ‘‘Ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato tisahassimahāsahassilokadhātuṃ sarena viññāpeyya, obhāsena ca phareyyā’’ti (a. ni. 3.81) āgataṭṭhāne tisahassimahāsahassī ekā lokadhātu. ‘‘Ayañca dasasahassī lokadhātū’’ti (ma. ni. 3.201) āgataṭṭhāne dasacakkavāḷasahassāni ekā lokadhātu. Taṃ sandhāya ekissā lokadhātuyāti āha. Ettakañhi jātikhettaṃ nāma. Tatrāpi ṭhapetvā imasmiṃ cakkavāḷe jambudīpassa majjhimadesaṃ na aññatra buddhā uppajjanti jātikhettato pana paraṃ buddhānaṃ uppattiṭṭhānameva na paññāyati. Yenatthenāti yena pavāraṇasaṅgahatthena.

ekissā lokadhātuyā jātikhettaṃ nāma. Yenatthenā

Sanaṅkumārakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
298. In " *aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso ya* ," both *ṭhānaṃ* and *avakāso* are expressions for cause. Indeed, *kāraṇaṃ* abides (*tiṭṭhati*) here, since the result depends on it, it is a *ṭhānaṃ* (place). Since that (*kāraṇaṃ*) is like an opportunity (*okāso*), because without it, it is not found elsewhere, it is an *avakāso* (opportunity). The *ya* means the affix in the sense of instrument. This is what is meant: "There is no cause (*kāraṇaṃ*) by which two Buddhas could arise together in one world-element (*ekissā lokadhātuyā*)."

And here:

"As far as the moon and sun revolve, illuminating the directions with their light, so far a thousandfold world; there your power prevails." (Ma. Ni. 1.503) –

In the verse, a single *cakkavāḷa* is a single *lokadhātu*. In the passage where it says, "The thousandfold world-element trembled" (A. Ni. 3.126), a thousand *cakkavāḷas* are a single *lokadhātu*. In the passage where it says, "If he wished, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could make the three-thousand great-thousandfold world-element known with his voice, and pervade it with his light" (A. Ni. 3.81), a three-thousand great-thousandfold [world] is a single *lokadhātu*. In the passage where it says, "And this is a ten-thousandfold world-element" (Ma. Ni. 3.201), ten thousand *cakkavāḷas* are a single *lokadhātu*. Referring to that, he said, "in one world-element (*ekissā lokadhātuyā*)."

This much is called a "birth-field" (*jātikhettaṃ nāma*). Even there, setting aside the central region of Jambudīpa in this *cakkavāḷa*, Buddhas do not arise elsewhere. Beyond the birth-field, the very place of the Buddhas' arising is not known. " *yenatthenā* " means by which means of invitation and acceptance.

*ekissā lokadhātuyā jātikhettaṃ nāma.* *yenatthenā*

The Account of Sanankumāra

mula_pali:
299. ‘‘Atha kho, bhante, uttarāya disāya uḷāro āloko sañjāyi, obhāso pāturahosi atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘yathā kho, mārisā, nimittāni dissanti, uḷāro āloko sañjāyati, obhāso pātubhavati , brahmā pātubhavissati; brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimittaṃ pātubhāvāya, yadidaṃ āloko sañjāyati obhāso pātubhavatīti.

‘Yathā nimittā dissanti, brahmā pātubhavissati;

Brahmuno hetaṃ nimittaṃ, obhāso vipulo mahā’ti.

Sanaṅkumārakathā
mula_english:
‘And then, Lord, a glorious radiance ( *uḷāro āloko*) shone forth from the north (*uttarāya disāya*), and a splendour (*obhāso*) was seen greater than the sheen of the devas (*devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ*).

And Sakka ( *sakko*), the lord of the gods ( *devānamindo*), said to the Thirty-Three Gods (*deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi*) : ‘Gentlemen (*mārisā*), when such signs (*nimittāni*) are seen, such light (*āloko*) is seen and such radiance (*obhāso*) shines forth, Brahmā ( *brahmā*) will appear (*pātubhavissati*). Such signs are an indication that he will appear (*brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimittaṃ pātubhāvāya*).'

‘As signs appear (*yathā nimittā dissanti*), Brahmā will appear (*brahmā pātubhavissati*);

This sign of Brahmā ( *brahmuno hetaṃ nimittaṃ*) is a great and radiant light (*obhāso vipulo mahā’ti*).'

The Story of Sanankumara.

mula_pali:
300. ‘‘Atha kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti. Cattāropi mahārājāno yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti. Idaṃ sutvā devā tāvatiṃsā ekaggā samāpajjiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti.

‘‘Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā pātubhavati. Yo kho pana, bhante, brahmuno pakativaṇṇo, anabhisambhavanīyo so devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ cakkhupathasmiṃ. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhante, sovaṇṇo viggaho mānusaṃ viggahaṃ atirocati, evameva kho, bhante, yadā brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, na tassaṃ parisāyaṃ koci devo abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimanteti. Sabbeva tuṇhībhūtā pañjalikā pallaṅkena nisīdanti – ‘yassadāni devassa pallaṅkaṃ icchissati brahmā sanaṅkumāro, tassa devassa pallaṅke nisīdissatī’ti. Yassa kho pana, bhante, devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ . Seyyathāpi, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto adhunābhisitto rajjena, uḷāraṃ so labhati vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati somanassapaṭilābhaṃ, evameva kho, bhante, yassa devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā antarahito imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

uḷāraṃ so labhati vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati somanassapaṭilābhaṃ,

‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

‘Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

‘Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

‘Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’nti.
mula_english:
300. Then, venerable sir, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven sat down each in their proper seat, thinking, "Let us discern this radiance, and whatever its result will be, having realized it, we shall go." The Four Great Kings also sat down each in their proper seat, thinking, "Let us discern this radiance, and whatever its result will be, having realized it, we shall go." Having heard this, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, with one-pointed minds, attained concentration, thinking, "Let us discern this radiance, and whatever its result will be, having realized it, we shall go."

Venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanatkumāra appears to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, he appears having created an coarse form. But, venerable sir, the natural complexion of Brahmā is unapprehendable to the path of sight of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanatkumāra appears to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, he outshines the other gods in radiance and glory. Just as, venerable sir, a golden statue outshines a human statue, even so, venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanatkumāra appears to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, he outshines the other gods in radiance and glory. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanatkumāra appears to the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, none of that assembly salutes him, rises, or invites him with a seat. All remain silent, with hands clasped, sitting cross-legged, thinking, "Whichever god's couch Brahmā Sanatkumāra desires, on that god's couch he will sit."

Venerable sir, whichever god's couch Brahmā Sanatkumāra sits on, that god obtains great attainment of knowledge, that god obtains great attainment of joy. Just as, venerable sir, a Kṣatriya king, anointed as the head, now consecrated with kingship, *obtains great attainment of knowledge, obtains great attainment of joy,* even so, venerable sir, whichever god's couch Brahmā Sanatkumāra sits on, that god obtains great attainment of knowledge, that god obtains great attainment of joy.

Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanatkumāra, having known the satisfaction of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, vanished and approved with these verses:

"The gods, indeed, rejoice, the Trāyastriṃśa with Indra; honoring the Tathāgata, and the good law of the Dharma."

"Seeing the new gods also, beautiful and glorious; having lived the holy life in the Sugata, they have come here."

"They outshine the others, in radiance, glory, and life; disciples of the one with great wisdom, having attained distinction here."

"Having seen this, they rejoice, the Trāyastriṃśa with Indra; honoring the Tathāgata, and the good law of the Dharma."
commentary_pali: 300.Vaṇṇena ceva yasasā cāti alaṅkāraparivārena ca puññasiriyā cāti attho.
commentary_english: "vaṇṇena ceva yasasā cā" means with embellishment and retinue, and with the glory of merit (puṇya-śrī).

mula_pali:
301. ‘‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro abhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante , brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti vissaṭṭho ca viññeyyo ca mañju ca savanīyo ca bindu ca avisārī ca gambhīro ca ninnādī ca. Yathāparisaṃ kho pana, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sarena viññāpeti, na cassa bahiddhā parisāya ghoso niccharati. Yassa kho pana, bhante, evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti, so vuccati ‘brahmassaro’ti. Atha kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘sādhu, mahābrahme, etadeva mayaṃ saṅkhāya modāma; atthi ca sakkena devānamindena tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhuccā vaṇṇā bhāsitā; te ca mayaṃ saṅkhāya modāmā’ti.

Aṭṭha yathābhuccavaṇṇā
mula_english:
“This was the burden of Brahmā Sanankumāra’s speech.

This was the burden of Brahmā Sanankumāra's speech, and as Brahmā Sanankumāra spoke, his voice possessed eight qualities: it was distinct (*vissaṭṭho*), intelligible (*viññeyyo*), pleasant (*mañju*), attractive (*savanīyo*), compact (*bindu*), concise (*avisārī*), deep (*gambhīro*), and resonant (*ninnādī*).

And when Brahmā Sanankumāra spoke to the assembly with that voice, its sound did not carry outside the assembly.

Venerable sir, whoever has such a voice with eight qualities is said to have the voice of Brahmā (*brahmassaro*).

Then, venerable sir, the Thirty-three Gods said this to Brahmā Sanankumāra: ‘It is well, Great Brahmā (*mahābrahme*)! We rejoice, having considered this. Also, eight truthful qualities (*aṭṭha yathābhuccā vaṇṇā*) of that Blessed One (*bhagavato*) have been spoken by Śakra (*sakkena*), lord of the gods (*devānamindena*); we also rejoice, having considered them.’

Eight Truthful Qualities (*aṭṭha yathābhuccavaṇṇā*)
commentary_pali:
301.Sādhu mahābrahmeti ettha sampasādane sādhusaddo. Saṅkhāya modāmāti jānitvā modāma.

Govindabrāhmaṇavatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Good, O great Brahma, here in serene joy is the term *sādhu*.

Having reckoned, let us rejoice; having known, let us rejoice.

Narration of the story of Govinda the Brahmin.

mula_pali:
302. ‘‘Atha , bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘sādhu, devānaminda, mayampi tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe suṇeyyāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ mahābrahme’ti kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññati, bhavaṃ mahābrahmā? Yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evaṃ bahujanahitāya paṭipannaṃ bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Svākkhāto kho pana tena bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi. Evaṃ opaneyyikassa dhammassa desetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Idaṃ kusala’nti kho pana tena bhagavatā supaññattaṃ, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti supaññattaṃ, ‘idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti supaññattaṃ. Evaṃ kusalākusalasāvajjānavajjasevitabbāsevitabbahīnapaṇītakaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgānaṃ dhammānaṃ paññāpetāraṃ. Imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Supaññattā kho pana tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Seyyathāpi nāma gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakena saṃsandati sameti, evameva supaññattā tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Evaṃ nibbānagāminiyā paṭipadāya paññāpetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Abhinipphanno kho pana tassa bhagavato lābho abhinipphanno siloko, yāva maññe khattiyā sampiyāyamānarūpā viharanti. Vigatamado kho pana so bhagavā āhāraṃ āhāreti. Evaṃ vigatamadaṃ āhāraṃ āharayamānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Laddhasahāyo kho pana so bhagavā sekhānañceva paṭipannānaṃ khīṇāsavānañca vusitavataṃ, te bhagavā apanujja ekārāmataṃ anuyutto viharati. Evaṃ ekārāmataṃ anuyuttaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Yathāvādī kho pana so bhagavā tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī; iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī. Evaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭippannaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘‘Tiṇṇavicikiccho kho pana so bhagavā vigatakathaṃkatho pariyositasaṅkappo ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ . Evaṃ tiṇṇavicikicchaṃ vigatakathaṃkathaṃ pariyositasaṅkappaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā’ti.
mula_english:
302. Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanankumāra said this to Śakka, the lord of the gods: “It is well, lord of the gods, that we also might hear those eight truthful praises of the Blessed One.”

“Very well, Great Brahma,” said Śakka, the lord of the gods, and he repeated those eight truthful praises of Brahmā Sanankumāra, the Blessed One.

“What do you think, Lord Mahābrahmā? As regards the way in which the Lord has striven for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare and happiness of gods and humans—

And we can find no teacher endowed with such qualities, whether we consider the past or the present, other than that Lord.

“The *dharma* has been well proclaimed by that Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, onward leading, to be experienced individually by the wise.”

And we can find no proclaimer of such an onward-leading *dharma*, either in the past or in the present, other than the Lord.

“This is skillful” has been well proclaimed by that Blessed One, “this is unskillful” has been well proclaimed, “this is blameworthy, this is blameless, this is to be cultivated, this is not to be cultivated, this is inferior, this is superior, this is with counterpart, this is without counterpart” has been well proclaimed.

And we can find none who is a proclaimer of such things…other than the Lord.

“The path leading to *nirvāṇa* has been well taught by that Blessed One to his disciples, and *nirvāṇa* and the path converge.

Just as the water of the Ganges meets and joins with the water of the Yamunā, so too the way leading to *nirvāṇa* has been properly declared to the disciples by the Blessed One, and *nirvāṇa* and the path meet.”

And we can find no proclaimer of the path leading to *nirvāṇa* . . . other than the Lord.

"That Blessed One's gain has been fully accomplished; his fame has been fully accomplished, so much so that the *kṣatriyas* live delighting in his form."

The Blessed One is without intoxication, he partakes of food.

And we can find no teacher who does this… other than the Lord.

“That Blessed One has obtained help from the learners and those practicing, the *arhats* and those who have lived the holy life; the Blessed One, rejecting these, is intent on solitude."

And we can find no such teacher . . . other than the Lord.

“The Lord speaks as he acts, and acts as he speaks; thus the Lord speaks as he acts, and acts as he speaks."

And we can find no teacher who does likewise, in every detail of *dharma*…other than the Lord.

“That Blessed One has overcome doubt, is without uncertainty, has brought his aims to completion, he has attained the essence of the holy life.”

Thus, having overcome doubt, being without uncertainty, having brought his aims to completion, he has attained the essence of the holy life.

And we can find no teacher who has done the like, whether we consider the past or the present, other than the Lord.

mula_pali:
303. ‘‘Ime kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro attamano hoti pamudito pītisomanassajāto bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sutvā. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā kumāravaṇṇī hutvā pañcasikho devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāturahosi . So vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīdi. Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso supaccatthate vā pallaṅke same vā bhūmibhāge pallaṅkena nisīdeyya, evameva kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

Govindabrāhmaṇavatthu
mula_english:
"‘And when Sakka, lord of gods, had thus proclaimed these eight truthful statements in praise of Brahmā Sanankumāra,
And Brahma Sanankumara was pleased, overjoyed, and filled with delight and happiness at what he had heard in the Lord’s praise.
Then, Lord, Brahma Sanankumara, having assumed a grosser form (oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ), appeared in the shape of the youth Pañcasikha to the Thirty-Three Gods.
Rising up in the air, he appeared floating cross-legged (pallaṅkena),
Just as, Lord, a strong man might sit cross-legged (pallaṅkena) on a well-covered seat or on level ground, just so, Lord, Brahma Sanankumara, rising up in the air, appeared floating cross-legged (pallaṅkena) and addressed the gods of the Thirty-Three –

The Story of Govinda the Brahmin

mula_pali:
304. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva dīgharattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavā ahosi. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bho, rājā disampati nāma ahosi. Disampatissa rañño govindo nāma brāhmaṇo purohito ahosi. Disampatissa rañño reṇu nāma kumāro putto ahosi. Govindassa brāhmaṇassa jotipālo nāma māṇavo putto ahosi. Iti reṇu ca rājaputto jotipālo ca māṇavo aññe ca cha khattiyā iccete aṭṭha sahāyā ahesuṃ. Atha kho, bho, ahorattānaṃ accayena govindo brāhmaṇo kālamakāsi. Govinde brāhmaṇe kālaṅkate rājā disampati paridevesi – ‘‘yasmiṃ vata, bho, mayaṃ samaye govinde brāhmaṇe sabbakiccāni sammā vossajjitvā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārema, tasmiṃ no samaye govindo brāhmaṇo kālaṅkato’’ti. Evaṃ vutte bho reṇu rājaputto rājānaṃ disampatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mā kho tvaṃ, deva, govinde brāhmaṇe kālaṅkate atibāḷhaṃ paridevesi. Atthi, deva, govindassa brāhmaṇassa jotipālo nāma māṇavo putto paṇḍitataro ceva pitarā, alamatthadasataro ceva pitarā; yepissa pitā atthe anusāsi, tepi jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ kumārā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ devā’’ti.

Mahāgovindavatthu
mula_english:
304. “How long do the gods of the *tāvatiṃsa* heaven think that Blessed Lord was one of great wisdom?

Once upon a time, sir, there was a king named Disampati.

Disampati the king had a chaplain named Govinda, a *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin).

King Disampati had a son named Reṇu, a prince.

Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) had a son named Jotipāla, a youth.

Thus, Prince Reṇu and Jotipāla the youth, along with six other *khattiya*s (warriors), were a band of eight friends.

Then, sir, after the passing of days and nights, Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) passed away.

Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) having passed away, King Disampati lamented: ‘Alas, at the very moment when we had entrusted all our responsibilities to Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin), and were abandoning ourselves to the pleasures of the five senses, Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) has passed away!’

Having been spoken thus, Prince Reṇu said to King Disampati: ‘Sire, do not mourn the death of Govinda the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) overmuch!

There is, sire, Govinda the *brāhmaṇa*'s (Brahmin's) son Jotipāla, a youth, who is more clever and discerning than his father; whatever his father advised concerning advantage, that is now Jotipāla the youth's advice.’

‘Is that so, young prince?’ ‘Yes, your majesty.’

The Great Govinda Narrative
commentary_pali:
304.Yāva dīgharattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavāti ettakanti paricchinditvā na sakkā vattuṃ, atha kho yāva dīgharattaṃ aticirarattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavā. Noti kathaṃ tumhe maññathāti. Atha sayamevetaṃ pañhaṃ byākātukāmo – ‘‘anacchariyametaṃ, mārisā, yaṃ idāni pāramiyo pūretvā bodhipallaṅke tiṇṇaṃ mārānaṃ matthakaṃ bhinditvā paṭividdhaasādhāraṇañāṇo so bhagavā mahāpañño bhaveyya, kimettha acchariyaṃ, aparipakkāya pana bodhiyā padesañāṇe ṭhitassa sarāgādikālepi mahāpaññabhāvameva vo, mārisā, kathessāmī’’ti bhavapaṭicchannakāraṇaṃ āharitvā dassento bhūtapubbaṃ bhotiādimāha.

Purohitoti sabbakiccāni anusāsanapurohito. Govindoti govindiyābhisekena abhisitto , pakatiyā panassa aññadeva nāmaṃ, abhisittakālato paṭṭhāya ‘‘govindo’’ti saṅkhyaṃ gato. Jotipāloti jotanato ca pālanato ca jotipālo. Tassa kira jātadivase sabbāvudhāni ujjotiṃsu. Rājāpi paccūsasamaye attano maṅgalāvudhaṃ pajjalitaṃ disvā bhīto aṭṭhāsi. Govindo pātova rājūpaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā sukhaseyyaṃ pucchi rājā – ‘‘kuto me ācariya, sukhaseyyā’’ti vatvā taṃ kāraṇaṃ ārocesi. Mā bhāyi, mahārāja, mayhaṃ putto jāto, tassānubhāvena sakalanagare āvudhāni pajjaliṃsūti. Rājā – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho me kumāro paccatthiko bhaveyyā’’ti cintetvā suṭṭhutaraṃ bhāyi. ‘‘Kiṃ vitakkesi mahārājā’’ti ca puṭṭho tamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha naṃ govindo ‘‘mā bhāyi mahārāja, neso kumāro tumhākaṃ dubbhissati, sakalajambudīpe pana tena samo paññāya na bhavissati, mama puttassa vacanena mahājanassa kaṅkhā chijjissati, tumhākañca sabbakiccāni anusāsissatī’’ti samassāseti. Rājā tuṭṭho – ‘‘kumārassa khīramūlaṃ hotū’’ti sahassaṃ datvā ‘‘kumāraṃ mahallakakāle mama dassethā’’ti āha. Kumāro anupubbena vuḍḍhimanuppatto. Jotitattā panassa pālanasamatthatāya ca jotipālotveva nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘jotanato ca pālanato ca jotipālo’’ti.

Purohito Govindo Jotipālo

Sammā vossajjitvāti sammā vossajjitvā. Ayameva vā pāṭho. Alamatthadasataroti samattho paṭibalo atthadaso alamatthadaso, taṃ alamatthadasaṃ tiretīti alamatthadasataro. Jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyāti sopi jotipālaṃyeva pucchitvā anusāsatīti dasseti.

Sammā vossajjitvā Alamatthadasataro Jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyā
commentary_english:
304. *yāva dīgharattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavā* means it is not possible to express by cutting off at *ettakanti*, but rather *yāva dīgharattaṃ aticirarattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavā*.

*no* means how do you think?

Then, desiring to explain this question himself – ‘‘This is not astonishing, friends, that now having fulfilled the perfections on the enlightenment-seat, having split the head of the three Māras, that Blessed One would be one with knowledge that is unshared; what is astonishing in this? But for the undeveloped enlightenment, in the region of knowledge," after bringing a hidden cause, showing *bhūtapubbaṃ bho* etc., he says:

*purohito* means all tasks are guided by the advisor.

*govindo* means anointed with the Govinda-anointing, but by nature his name was something else; from the time of the anointing onwards, he went to the designation “Govinda”.

*jotipālo* means Jotipāla is from illuminating and from protecting.

It is said that on his birthday all weapons shone.

The king, too, at dawn, seeing his own auspicious weapon blazing, was frightened and stood there.

Govinda, going early to the king's presence, asked about his pleasant sleep. The king said – “Where, teacher, is there pleasant sleep for me?” Saying this, he told the reason.

“Do not fear, Great King, a son has been born to me; by his power, the weapons in the entire city blazed up.”

The king, thinking, “Could this boy become an adversary for me?”, was greatly frightened.

“What are you thinking, Great King?” he was asked, and he told that matter.

Then Govinda reassured him, “Do not fear, Great King, this boy will not betray you; but in all of Jambudvīpa there will be no one equal to him in wisdom; by the words of my son, the doubt of the great mass of people will be cut off, and he will guide all your tasks.”

The king, pleased, giving a thousand, said, “Let there be milk-money for the boy; show me the boy when he is old.”

The boy, in due course, attained growth.

However, because of his being illuminated and because of his capacity for protecting, they made his name Jotipāla.

Therefore it was said – “Jotipāla is from illuminating and from protecting.”

*purohito* *govindo* *jotipālo* *sammā vossajjitvā* means having properly relinquished.

Or this is the reading.

*alamatthadasataro* means capable, counter-force, aim-seeing, all-aim-seeing, that which crosses over that all-aim-seeing is *alamatthadasataro*.

*jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyā* means even he, having asked Jotipāla, shows that he guides.

*sammā vossajjitvā* *alamatthadasataro* *jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyā*

mula_pali:
305. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, rājā disampati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena jotipālo nāma māṇavo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘bhavamatthu bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ, rājā disampati bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantayati, rājā disampati bhoto jotipālassa māṇavassa dassanakāmo’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho, bho, so puriso disampatissa rañño paṭissutvā yena jotipālo māṇavo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘bhavamatthu bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ, rājā disampati bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantayati , rājā disampati bhoto jotipālassa māṇavassa dassanakāmo’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho bho jotipālo māṇavo tassa purisassa paṭissutvā yena rājā disampati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā disampatinā raññā saddhiṃ sammodi; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho, bho, jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ rājā disampati etadavoca – ‘‘anusāsatu no bhavaṃ jotipālo, mā no bhavaṃ jotipālo anusāsaniyā paccabyāhāsi. Pettike taṃ ṭhāne ṭhapessāmi, govindiye abhisiñcissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho, bho, so jotipālo māṇavo disampatissa rañño paccassosi. Atha kho, bho, rājā disampati jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ govindiye abhisiñci, taṃ pettike ṭhāne ṭhapesi. Abhisitto jotipālo māṇavo govindiye pettike ṭhāne ṭhapito yepissa pitā atthe anusāsi tepi atthe anusāsati, yepissa pitā atthe nānusāsi, tepi atthe anusāsati; yepissa pitā kammante abhisambhosi, tepi kammante abhisambhoti, yepissa pitā kammante nābhisambhosi, tepi kammante abhisambhoti. Tamenaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘govindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo, mahāgovindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo’’ti. Iminā kho evaṃ, bho, pariyāyena jotipālassa māṇavassa govindo mahāgovindotveva samaññā udapādi.

Rajjasaṃvibhajanaṃ
mula_english:
“Then, King Disampati addressed a certain man, ‘Come here, my good man, go to the youth Jotipāla and say to him: “May the Reverend Jotipāla be well! King Disampati summons the Reverend Jotipāla; King Disampati wishes to see the young Jotipāla.”’

‘Very good, Your Majesty,’ said the man to King Disampati, and he went to the youth Jotipāla. Having arrived, he said to Jotipāla, ‘May the Reverend Jotipāla be well! King Disampati summons the Reverend Jotipāla; King Disampati wishes to see the young Jotipāla.’

‘Very good, sir,’ said the youth Jotipāla to the man, and he went to King Disampati. Having arrived, he exchanged courteous greetings with King Disampati, and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the King Disampati said to the youth Jotipāla, ‘May the Reverend Jotipāla manage our affairs; may the Reverend Jotipāla not refuse management. I will install you in your father's place, and I will consecrate you in the office of *govindiye*.’

‘Very good, sir,’ said the youth Jotipāla to King Disampati in response.

Then, King Disampati consecrated the youth Jotipāla in the office of *govindiye*, and installed him in his father's place.

Once installed, Jotipāla managed the affairs that his father had managed and also those that his father had not managed. He accomplished the tasks his father had accomplished and also those his father had not accomplished.

The people said of him, ‘Truly, Govinda is a *brāhmaṇa*, truly, the *brāhmaṇa* is a *mahāgovinda* (great steward) !’

Thus it was, sir, by this means that the designation *govinda* (steward), *mahāgovinda* (great steward) arose for the youth Jotipāla.

Division of royal power.
commentary_pali:
305.Bhavamatthubhavantaṃ jotipālanti bhoto jotipālassa bhavo vuddhi visesādhigamo sabbakalyāṇañceva maṅgalañca hotūti attho. Sammodanīyaṃ kathanti? ‘‘Alaṃ, mahārāja, mā cintayi, dhuvadhammo esa sabbasattāna’’ntiādinā nayena maraṇappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ sokavinodanapaṭisanthārakathaṃ pariyosāpetvā. Mā no bhavaṃ jotipālo anusāsaniyāpaccabyāhāsīti mā paṭibyākāsi, ‘‘anusāsā’’ti vutto – ‘‘nāhaṃ anusāsāmī’’ti no mā anusāsaniyā paccakkhāsīti attho. Abhisambhosīti saṃvidahitvā paṭṭhapesi. Manussā evamāhaṃsūti taṃ pitarā mahāpaññataraṃ sabbakiccāni anusāsantaṃ sabbakamme abhisambhavantaṃ disvā tuṭṭhacittā govindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo, mahāgovindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇoti evamāhaṃsu. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, ‘‘govindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo ahosi etassa pitā; ayaṃ pana mahāgovindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo’’ti.

Rajjasaṃvibhajanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
305. bhavamatthubhavantaṃ jotipālanti: May there be prosperity for venerable Jyotipāla! The meaning is: may there be increase, special attainment, and all good fortune and blessing for venerable Jyotipāla. sammodanīyaṃ kathanti? What is a pleasing conversation? Having concluded the consoling and comforting talk connected with death by the method beginning with "Enough, great king, do not think, this is the fixed nature of all beings," etc. mā no bhavaṃ jotipālo anusāsaniyāpaccabyāhāsīti: Do not refuse to advise us! The meaning is: do not reject instruction by saying, when asked "Advise us," "I am not advising." abhisambhosīti: Having arranged, he established [it]. manussā evamāhaṃsūti: Having seen him, who was more wise than his father, instructing in all affairs, and managing all business, the people, with delighted minds, spoke thus: govindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo, mahāgovindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo. idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti: This was said: "Govinda was indeed a Brahman, sir, the father of this one; but this one is Mahāgovinda, indeed a Brahman, sir."

Description of the Division of the Kingdom

mula_pali: 306. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – ‘‘disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Āyantu, bhonto, yena reṇu rājaputto tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ evaṃ vadetha – ‘‘mayaṃ kho bhoto reṇussa sahāyā piyā manāpā appaṭikūlā, yaṃsukho bhavaṃ taṃsukhā mayaṃ, yaṃdukkho bhavaṃ taṃdukkhā mayaṃ. Disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro bhavantaṃ reṇuṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Sace bhavaṃ reṇu rajjaṃ labhetha, saṃvibhajetha no rajjenā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ bho’’ti kho, bho, te cha khattiyā mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘mayaṃ kho bhoto reṇussa sahāyā piyā manāpā appaṭikūlā ; yaṃsukho bhavaṃ taṃsukhā mayaṃ, yaṃdukkho bhavaṃ taṃdukkhā mayaṃ. Disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana bho jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro bhavantaṃ reṇuṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Sace bhavaṃ reṇu rajjaṃ labhetha, saṃvibhajetha no rajjenā’’ti. ‘‘Ko nu kho, bho, añño mama vijite sukho bhavetha sukhā bhaveyyātha (ka.), sukhaṃ bhaveyyātha, sukhamedheyyātha (sī. pī.),sukha medhetha (?), aññatra bhavantebhi? Sacāhaṃ, bho, rajjaṃ labhissāmi, saṃvibhajissāmi vo rajjenā’’’ti.
mula_english:
306. Then, the brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda went to those six nobles; having gone, he said this to those six nobles: “King Disampati is aged, old, decrepit, advanced in years, and has reached old age. Who knows how long he will live? It is possible that when King Disampati dies, the royal electors would consecrate Prince Reṇu as king.

Go, gentlemen, to Prince Reṇu and say this to him: “We are the friends of Lord Reṇu, beloved, dear, agreeable, and not opposed; whatever happiness *bhavaṃ* experiences, that is our happiness; whatever suffering *bhavaṃ* experiences, that is our suffering."

King Disampati is aged, old, decrepit, advanced in years, and has reached old age. Who knows how long he will live? It is possible that when King Disampati dies, the royal electors would consecrate Prince Reṇu as king.

If *bhavaṃ* Reṇu should gain the kingship, he should share the kingdom with us."

"Very well, sir," the six nobles replied to the brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda, and they went to Prince Reṇu; having gone, they said this to Prince Reṇu: "We are the friends of Lord Reṇu, beloved, dear, agreeable, and not opposed; whatever happiness *bhavaṃ* experiences, that is our happiness; whatever suffering *bhavaṃ* experiences, that is our suffering."

King Disampati is aged, old, decrepit, advanced in years, and has reached old age. Who knows how long he will live? It is possible that when King Disampati dies, the royal electors would consecrate Prince Reṇu as king.

If *bhavaṃ* Reṇu should gain the kingship, he should share the kingdom with us."

"Who else in my realm should be happy other than you? If I gain the kingship, I will share the kingdom with you."
commentary_pali: 306.Yenate cha khattiyāti ye te ‘‘sahāyā’’ti vuttā cha khattiyā, te kira reṇussa ekapitikā kaniṭṭhabhātaro, tasmā mahāgovindo ‘‘ayaṃ abhisitto etesaṃ rajjasaṃvibhāgaṃ kareyya vā na vā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ te paṭikacceva reṇussa santikaṃ pesetvā paṭiññaṃ gaṇhāpeyya’’nti cintento yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami. Rājakattāroti rājakārakā amaccā.
commentary_english:
306.
*yena*, *te ca khattiyā* means, those *kṣatriyas* who are called "companions," they were younger brothers of Reṇu, born of the same father. Therefore, Mahāgovinda, thinking, "This one has been consecrated; he may or may not divide the kingdom among them. Why shouldn't I send someone ahead to Reṇu and have him take a promise?" approached those six *kṣatriyas*.
*rājakattāro* means royal officials, ministers (*amātya*).

mula_pali: 307. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, ahorattānaṃ accayena rājā disampati kālamakāsi. Disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ rajje abhisiñciṃsu. Abhisitto reṇu rajjena pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – ‘‘disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato. Abhisitto reṇu rajjena pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti, madanīyā kāmā? Āyantu, bhonto, yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ evaṃ vadetha – disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato, abhisitto bhavaṃ reṇu rajjena, sarati bhavaṃ taṃ vacana’’’nti?
mula_english:
“Then, in due course, King Disampati passed away. When King Disampati had died, the king-makers anointed Prince Reṇu as king. And having been anointed king, Reṇu indulged in the five objects of desire (*pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti*).

Then the great Govinda Brāhmaṇa went to the six nobles and said to them: ‘Gentlemen, now King Disampati is dead.’ Having been anointed king, Reṇu indulged in the five objects of desire (*pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti*). Who knows the pleasures that make one intoxicated? Come, sirs, go to King Reṇu and say to King Reṇu: ‘King Disampati is dead, and Lord Reṇu has been anointed king. Do you remember that promise?’”
commentary_pali: 307.Madanīyā kāmāti madakarā pamādakarā kāmā. Gacchante gacchante kāle esa anussaritumpi na sakkuṇeyya, tasmā āyantu bhonto āgacchantūti attho.
commentary_english: 307. *Madanīyā kāmā* means desires that cause intoxication, desires that cause negligence. As time goes on, one might not remember this, therefore, the meaning is "may the venerable ones come, may they arrive."

mula_pali: 308. ‘‘‘Evaṃ , bho’’ti kho, bho, te cha khattiyā mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato, abhisitto bhavaṃ reṇu rajjena, sarati bhavaṃ taṃ vacana’’nti? ‘‘Sarāmahaṃ, bho, taṃ vacanaṃ vacananti (syā. ka.). Ko nu kho, bho, pahoti imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitu’’nti? ‘‘Ko nu kho, bho, añño pahoti, aññatra mahāgovindena brāhmaṇenā’’ti? Atha kho, bho, reṇu rājā aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘rājā taṃ, bhante, reṇu āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ devā’’ti kho, bho, so puriso reṇussa rañño paṭissutvā yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘rājā taṃ, bhante, reṇu āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tassa purisassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇunā raññā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho, bho, mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ reṇu rājā etadavoca – ‘‘etu, bhavaṃ govindo, imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajatū’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo reṇussa rañño paṭissutvā imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhaji. Sabbāni sakaṭamukhāni paṭṭhapesi aṭṭhapesi (sī. pī.). Tatra sudaṃ majjhe reṇussa rañño janapado hoti.
mula_english:
308. ‘“Yes, sir,” the six nobles replied to the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa*, and they went to King Reṇu. Having approached King Reṇu, they said this: “King Disampati is dead, sir, and the esteemed Reṇu has been anointed king. Do you remember your word, sir?”’ “I remember that word, sir.”

“Who now, sir, is capable of dividing this great earth, which is broad in the north and narrow like the front of a cart in the south, into seven equal, well-divided parts?” “Who else, sir, is capable, other than the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa*?” Then King Reṇu addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, go to the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa*. Having gone, tell the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa* this: ‘King Reṇu summons you, venerable sir.’”

‘“Yes, sir,”’ that man replied to King Reṇu, and he went to the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa*. Having gone, he said this to the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa*: “King Reṇu summons you, venerable sir.”

‘“Yes, sir,”’ the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa* replied to that man, and he went to King Reṇu. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with King Reṇu. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down to one side. Then, Reṇu the king, said to the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa* who was sitting to one side: “Come, esteemed Govinda, divide this great earth, which is broad in the north and narrow like the front of a cart in the south, into seven equal, well-divided parts.”

‘“Yes, sir,”’ the Great Steward *brāhmaṇa* replied to Reṇu the king, and he divided this great earth, which is broad in the north and narrow like the front of a cart in the south, into seven equal, well-divided parts. He established all the cart-fronts. And King Reṇu’s country was in the center.
commentary_pali:
308.Sarāmahaṃ bhoti tadā kira manussānaṃ saccavādikālo hoti, tasmā ‘‘kadā mayā vuttaṃ, kena diṭṭhaṃ, kena suta’’nti abhūtaṃ avatvā ‘‘sarāmahaṃ bho’’ti āha. Sammodanīyaṃ kathanti kiṃ mahārāja devattaṃ gate raññe mā cintayittha, dhuvadhammo esa sabbasattānaṃ, evaṃbhāvino saṅkhārāti evarūpaṃ paṭisanthārakathaṃ. Sabbāni sakaṭamukhāni paṭṭhapesīti sabbāni cha rajjāni sakaṭamukhāni paṭṭhapesi. Ekekassa rañño rajjaṃ tiyojanasataṃ hoti, reṇussa rañño rajjosaraṇapadeso dasagāvutaṃ, majjhe pana reṇussa rajjaṃ vitānasadisaṃ ahosi. Kasmā evaṃ paṭṭhapesīti? Kālena kālaṃ rājānaṃ passituṃ āgacchantā aññassa rajjaṃ apīḷetvā attano attano rajjapadeseneva āgamissanti ceva gamissanti ca. Pararajjaṃ otiṇṇassa hi – ‘‘bhattaṃ detha, goṇaṃ dethā’’ti vadato manussā ujjhāyanti – ‘‘ime rājāno attano attano vijitena na gacchanti, amhākaṃ pīḷaṃ karontī’’ti. Attano vijitena gacchantassa ‘‘amhākaṃ santikā iminā idañcidañca laddhabbamevā’’ti manussā pīḷaṃ na maññanti. Imamatthaṃ cintayitvā mahāgovindo ‘‘sammodamānā rājāno ciraṃ rajjamanusāsantū’’ti evaṃ paṭṭhapesi.

‘‘Dantapuraṃ kaliṅgānaṃ, assakānañca potanaṃ;

Māhissati avantīnaṃ, sovīrānañca rodukaṃ.

Mithilā ca videhānaṃ, campā aṅgesu māpitā;

Bārāṇasī ca kāsīnaṃ, ete govindamāpitā’’ti. –

Etāni satta nagarāni mahāgovindeneva tesaṃ rājūnaṃ atthāya māpitāni.

‘‘Sattabhū brahmadatto ca, vessabhū bharato saha;

Reṇu dve ca dhataraṭṭhā, tadāsuṃ satta bhāradhā’’ti. –

Imāni tesaṃ sattannampi nāmāni. Tesu hi eko sattabhū nāma ahosi, eko brahmadatto nāma, eko vessabhū nāma, eko teneva saha bharato nāma, eko reṇu nāma, dve pana dhataraṭṭhāti ime satta jambudīpatale bhāradhā mahārājāno ahesunti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Kittisaddaabbhuggamanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
308. "I remember, sir," at that time, it seems, was the time when humans spoke the truth. Therefore, without saying what was untrue, "When was it said by me, by whom was it seen, by whom was it heard?", he said, "I remember, sir."

"Congenial talk": What, O great king, even though the king has passed away, do not be concerned; this is the steadfast law for all beings, such is the nature of conditioned things—such was the consoling talk.

"He had all the chariot-mouths set up": He had all six kingdoms' chariot-mouths set up.

The kingdom of each king was three hundred yojanas. The border region of King Reṇu's kingdom was ten gāvutas, but in the middle, King Reṇu's kingdom was like a canopy.

Why did he have [them] set up in this way? [So that] those coming to see the king from time to time would come and go only within their own kingdom's borders, without oppressing another's kingdom.

For when someone has entered another's kingdom and says, "Give food, give an ox!", people complain, "These kings do not travel within their own territory, they cause oppression for us."

But when someone travels within their own territory, people do not think it is oppressive, [thinking], "From our own stores, this and that should indeed be given to him."

Reflecting on this matter, Mahāgovinda had it set up in this way, [thinking], "May the kings, being in harmony, long rule the kingdom."

"Dantapura of the Kaliṅgas, Potana of the Assakas;

Māhissati of the Avantīs, Roduka of the Sovīras.

Mithilā was measured out for the Videhas, Campā in the Aṅgas;

Bārāṇasī for the Kāsīs—these were measured out by Govinda."

These seven cities were measured out by Mahāgovinda himself for the benefit of those kings.

"Sattabhū and Brahmadatta, Vessabhū together with Bharata;

Reṇu and two Dhataraṭṭhas—at that time, there were seven Bhāradhās."

These are the names of those seven.

Among them, one was named Sattabhū, one was named Brahmadatta, one was named Vessabhū, one was named Bharata together with him, one was named Reṇu, but two were named Dhataraṭṭha—these seven Bhāradhā great kings were on the surface of Jambudīpa.

The explanation of the First Bhāṇavāra is finished.

The explanation of the Rising of the Sound of Fame

mula_pali:
309. Dantapuraṃ kaliṅgānaṃ kāliṅgānaṃ (syā. pī. ka.), assakānañca potanaṃ.

Mahesayaṃ māhissati (sī. syā. pī.) avantīnaṃ, sovīrānañca rorukaṃ.

māhissati (sī. syā. pī.)

Mithilā ca videhānaṃ, campā aṅgesu māpitā;

Bārāṇasī ca kāsīnaṃ, ete govindamāpitāti.
mula_english:
309. Dantapura belonged to the Kaliṅgas, and Potana to the Assakas.

Mahissati belonged to the Avantis, and Roruka to the Soviras.

Mithilā belonged to the Videhas, and Campā was measured out in the Aṅgas;

Vārāṇasī belonged to the Kāsīs; these were measured out by Govinda.

mula_pali:
310. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā yathāsakena lābhena attamanā ahesuṃ paripuṇṇasaṅkappā – ‘‘yaṃ vata no ahosi icchitaṃ, yaṃ ākaṅkhitaṃ, yaṃ adhippetaṃ, yaṃ abhipatthitaṃ, taṃ no laddha’’nti.

‘‘Sattabhū brahmadatto ca, vessabhū bharato saha;

Reṇu dve dhataraṭṭhā ca, tadāsuṃ satta bhāradhā’ti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

Kittisaddaabbhuggamanaṃ
mula_english:
310. Then, the six nobles, delighted and completely satisfied with their respective gains, [exclaimed]: "What we wanted, desired, aimed for, and longed for, we have obtained!"

"Brahmadatta with Sattabhū, Vessabhū with Bharata together;

Reṇu and the two Dhataraṭṭhas, they were the seven Bhāradhā."

The first section of recitation is finished.

The rise of the sound of fame.

mula_pali: 311. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘yathā kho bhavaṃ govindo reṇussa rañño sahāyo piyo manāpo appaṭikūlo. Evameva kho bhavaṃ govindo amhākampi sahāyo piyo manāpo appaṭikūlo, anusāsatu no bhavaṃ govindo; mā no bhavaṃ govindo anusāsaniyā paccabyāhāsī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tesaṃ channaṃ khattiyānaṃ paccassosi. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo satta ca rājāno khattiye muddhāvasitte rajje muddhābhisitte rajjena (syā.) anusāsi, satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni mante vācesi.
mula_english:
Then, the six nobles approached the great Govinda, the *brāhmaṇa*, and having approached, they said this to the great Govinda, the *brāhmaṇa*: "Just as you, venerable Govinda, were a friend, dear, agreeable, and not hostile to King Reṇu, so also are you to us. Venerable Govinda, please instruct us! May venerable Govinda not reject our instruction."

"So be it, sir," replied the great Govinda, the *brāhmaṇa*, to those six nobles.

Then, the great Govinda, the *brāhmaṇa*, instructed seven kings, *kṣatriyas*, who had been consecrated with the crown, in their kingdoms, and he taught the *mantras* to seven eminent *brāhmaṇas* and seven hundred bathing ascetics.
commentary_pali:
311.Upasaṅkamiṃsūti ‘‘amhākaṃ ayaṃ issariyasampatti na aññassānubhāvena, mahāgovindassānubhāvena nipphannā. Mahāgovindo amhe satta rājāno samagge katvā jambudīpatale patiṭṭhāpesi, pubbūpakārissa pana na sukarā paṭikiriyā kātuṃ. Amhe sattapi jane esoyeva anusāsatu, etaṃyeva senāpatiñca purohitañca karoma, evaṃ no vuddhi bhavissatī’’ti cintetvā upasaṅkamiṃsu. Mahāgovindopi – ‘‘mayā ete samaggā katā, sace etesaṃ añño senāpati purohito ca bhavissati, tato attano attano senāpatipurohitānaṃ vacanaṃ gahetvā aññamaññaṃ bhindissanti, adhivāsemi nesaṃ senāpatiṭṭhānañca purohitaṭṭhānañcā’’ti cintetvā ‘‘evaṃ bho’’ti paccassosi.

Satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāleti ‘‘ahaṃ sabbaṭṭhānesu sammukho bhaveyyaṃ vā na vā, yatthāhaṃ sammukho na bhavissāmi, tattheva te kattabbaṃ karissantī’’ti satta anupurohite ṭhapesi. Te sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle’’ti. Divasassa dvikkhattuṃ vā sāyaṃ pāto vā nahāyantīti nahātakā. Vatacariyapariyosāne vā nahātā, tato paṭṭhāya brāhmaṇehi saddhiṃ na khādanti na pivantīti nahātakā.

Satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle nahātakā.
commentary_english:
"They approached," [regarding] "Our lordly fortune has been produced not by the power of another, but by the power of Mahāgovinda. Mahāgovinda, having made us seven kings harmonious, established [us] on the surface of Jambudvīpa; but repayment is not easy for one who has done a prior service. Let this very one instruct us seven also; let us make this very one both general and chaplain; thus there will be growth for us," thinking thus, they approached.

Mahāgovinda also [thought]: "By me these were made harmonious; if another general and chaplain will be theirs, then having taken the word of their own general and chaplain, they will divide from one another; I will accept their office of general and the office of chaplain," thinking thus, he replied, "Yes, sirs."

"Seven great Brāhmaṇa households," [means] "In all places, whether I should be present or not, wherever I shall not be present, there they will do what should be done," [saying this] he established seven assistant chaplains.

With reference to that, this was said: "Seven great Brāhmaṇa households."

Because they bathe twice a day, either evening or morning, [they are called] "bathers (nahātaka)."

Or, having bathed at the end of their observance of vows, from then on, because they do not eat nor drink together with Brahmins, [they are called] "bathers (nahātaka)."

"Seven great Brāhmaṇa households." "Bathers (nahātaka)."

mula_pali: 312. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa aparena samayena evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchi abbhuggañchi (sī. pī.) – ‘‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’’ti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘mayhaṃ kho evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi , na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyeyyaṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyeyya’’nti.
mula_english:
"Furthermore, in course of time, a good report was spread about the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda: 'The *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda can see Brahmā with his own eyes, he talks with Brahmā face to face, and consults with Brahmā!'

Then the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda thought: 'Now, this good report about me has spread: "The *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda can see Brahmā with his own eyes, he talks with Brahmā face to face, and consults with Brahmā!" But it is not true that I see Brahmā, nor talk with Brahmā face to face, nor discuss with Brahmā, nor consult with Brahmā. But I have heard these words of old and venerable *brāhmaṇas*, teachers and their teachers: "He who dwells in seclusion during the four months of the rainy season, practicing the meditation of compassion (*karuṇā-dhyāna*), sees Brahmā, talks with Brahmā face to face, discusses with Brahmā, and consults with Brahmā." Suppose I were to dwell in seclusion during the four months of the rainy season, practicing the meditation of compassion (*karuṇa-dhyāna*)!'
commentary_pali: 312.Abbhuggacchīti abhiuggacchi. Tadā kira manussānaṃ ‘‘na brahmunā saddhiṃ amantetvā sakkā evaṃ sakalajambudīpaṃ anusāsitu’’nti nisinnanisinnaṭṭhāne ayameva kathā pavattittha. Na kho panāhanti mahāpuriso kira – ‘‘ayaṃ mayhaṃ abhūto vaṇṇo uppanno, vaṇṇuppatti kho pana na bhāriyā, uppannassa vaṇṇassa rakkhanameva bhāriyaṃ, ayañca me acintetvā amantetvā karontasseva vaṇṇo uppannova, cintetvā mantetvā karontassa pana vitthārikataro bhavissatī’’ti brahmadassane upāyaṃ pariyesanto taṃ disvā sutaṃ kho pana metantiādiatthaṃ parivitakkesi.
commentary_english:
Abhuggacchī means abhiuggacchi.

At that time, the talk arose among people sitting in their seats, "Without consulting with Brahmā, it is not possible to govern the entire Jambudvīpa in this way."

Na kho panāha means the great man (mahāpurisa) thought, "This unprecedented praise has arisen for me, but the arising of praise is not a burden; protecting the praise that has arisen is the burden. And this praise has arisen for me without thinking or consulting; but if I think and consult, it will be even more extensive." Seeking a means in the sight of Brahmā, having seen that, he pondered the meaning beginning with sutaṃ kho pana meta.

mula_pali: 313. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.
mula_english:
“So then, venerable sir, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda approached King Reṇu. Having approached, he said this to King Reṇu: 'Venerable sir, such a good report has arisen about me: "The *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā with his own eyes; the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda converses, discusses, and consults with Brahmā."'

"But I, venerable sir, do not see Brahmā with my own eyes, nor do I converse with Brahmā, nor do I discuss with Brahmā, nor do I consult with Brahmā."

"However, I have heard it said by aged and respectable *brāhmaṇas*, the teachers of teachers, that anyone who withdraws into meditation for the four months of the rainy season (vassike cattāro māse), developing the absorption on compassion (karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati), can see Brahmā with his own eyes, talk with him face to face and consult with him."

"I wish, venerable sir, to go into retreat for the four months of the rainy season (vassike cattāro māse), to develop the absorption on compassion (karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ). Nobody is to come near me except to bring me food (bhattābhihārenā)."

"Reverend Govinda, do as you think fit."
commentary_pali: 313.Yenareṇu rājā tenupasaṅkamīti evaṃ me antarā daṭṭhukāmo vā sallapitukāmo vā na bhavissati, yato chinnapalibodho sukhaṃ viharissāmīti palibodhupacchedanatthaṃ upasaṅkami, esa nayo sabbattha.
commentary_english: Thus: "By whom King Reṇu was approached," thinking, "He will not be one who desires to see me, or one who desires to converse with me," because he is one who has cut off encumbrances. He approached for the purpose of cutting off encumbrances, thinking, "I will dwell at ease." This is the principle everywhere.

mula_pali: 314. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – ‘‘mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ, ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’’’ti.
mula_english:
“Then, the venerable *mahāgovinda* brahmin went to the six *khattiyas* and, having approached them, said this to the six *khattiyas*: ‘Indeed, a good report has risen about me, ‘*Mahāgovinda* the brahmin sees Brahmā, *Mahāgovinda* the brahmin discusses, converses, and consults with Brahmā.’

But I do not see Brahmā, nor do I discuss, converse, or consult with Brahmā.

I have heard it said by old and elderly brahmins, the teachers of teachers, ‘Whoever secludes himself for the four months of the rainy season, cultivating the *karuṇā* *jhāna*, sees Brahmā, discusses with Brahmā, converses with Brahmā, consults with Brahmā.’

I wish, venerable sirs, to seclude myself for the four months of the rainy season and cultivate the *karuṇā* *jhāna*. No one should approach me except the one bringing food.’

‘Reverend Govinda, do as you think fit.’”

mula_pali: 315. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā satta ca nhātakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni etadavoca – ‘‘mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti, brahmunā sallapati, brahmunā mantetī’ti. Tena hi, bho, yathāsute yathāpariyatte mante vitthārena sajjhāyaṃ karotha, aññamaññañca mante vācetha; icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā’’ti. ‘‘Yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.
mula_english:
315. Then, the brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda went to those seven wealthy brāhmaṇas and the seven hundred bathing ascetics, and having gone, said this to those seven wealthy brāhmaṇas and the seven hundred bathing ascetics: "This auspicious sound of praise has arisen about me: 'The brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda directly sees Brahmā; the brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda converses, discusses, and consults with Brahmā.'

But it is not true that I see Brahmā; I do not converse with Brahmā, I do not discuss with Brahmā, I do not consult with Brahmā.

But I have heard this said by old and elderly brāhmaṇas, teachers of teachers: 'That person who secludes himself during the four months of the rainy season and cultivates the compassionate meditation, that person sees Brahmā, converses with Brahmā, discusses with Brahmā, consults with Brahmā.'

Therefore, gentlemen, extensively recite the *mantras* as they have been heard and learned, and teach the *mantras* to each other. I desire, gentlemen, to seclude myself during the four months of the rainy season and to cultivate the compassionate meditation; no one should approach me except the one who brings the food."

"Reverend Govinda, do as you think fit."

mula_pali: 316. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo etadavoca – ‘‘mayhaṃ kho, bhotī, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhotī, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti, brahmunā sallapati, brahmunā mantetīti, icchāmahaṃ, bhotī, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā’’ti. ‘‘Yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’’’ti.
mula_english: Then, the brahmin Mahāgovinda went to his forty equal-ranking wives; having approached, he said this to his forty equal-ranking wives: "Indeed, ladies, such a good report about me has arisen: 'The brahmin Mahāgovinda directly sees Brahmā, the brahmin Mahāgovinda talks, discusses, and consults with Brahmā.' But I do not see Brahmā, ladies, nor do I talk with Brahmā, nor do I discuss with Brahmā, nor do I consult with Brahmā. But this has been heard by me from old, aged brahmins, teachers and teachers' teachers, when they were speaking: 'He who secludes himself for four months in the rainy season, and cultivates the *karuṇā-jhāna*, will see Brahmā, will talk with Brahmā, will discuss with Brahmā, will consult with Brahmā.’ I want, ladies, to seclude myself for four months in the rainy season, to cultivate the *karuṇā-jhāna*; no one should approach me except with one meal offering." "Now is the time for you to do what you think fit, Master Govinda."
commentary_pali: 316.Sādisiyoti samavaṇṇā samajātikā.
commentary_english: 316. sādisiyoti samavaṇṇā samajātikā.

mula_pali:
317. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo puratthimena nagarassa navaṃ sandhāgāraṃ kārāpetvā vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyi, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyi; nāssudha koci upasaṅkamati upasaṅkami (pī.) aññatra ekena bhattābhihārena. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena ahudeva ukkaṇṭhanā ahu paritassanā – ‘‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi na brahmunā sallapāmi na brahmunā mantemī’’’ti.

Brahmunā sākacchā
mula_english:
“Then, revered sir, the great Govinda, the *brāhmaṇa*, had a new meeting hall built to the east of the city. For the four months of the rainy season, he secluded himself, practicing the *jhāna* of compassion (*karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyi*). No one approached him except to bring him food. Then, revered sir, at the end of the four months, the *brāhmaṇa* great Govinda felt dissatisfaction and weariness. He thought: ‘I have heard it said by old and aged *brāhmaṇas*, teachers, and teachers of teachers: “Whoever secludes himself for the four months of the rainy season, practicing the *jhāna* of compassion, sees Brahmā, converses with Brahmā (*brahmunā sākaccheti*), discusses with Brahmā, and consults with Brahmā.” But I do not see Brahmā, nor do I converse with Brahmā, discuss with Brahmā, or consult with Brahmā!’"
Conversation with Brahmā.
commentary_pali:
317.Navaṃ sandhāgāraṃ kāretvāti rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānacaṅkamanasampannaṃ vassike cattāro māse vasanakkhamaṃ bahi naḷaparikkhittaṃ vicittaṃ āvasathaṃ kāretvā. Karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyīti karuṇāya tikacatukkajjhānaṃ jhāyi, karuṇāmukhena panettha avasesāpi tayo brahmavihārā gahitāva. Ukkaṇṭhanā paritassanāti jhānabhūmiyaṃ ṭhitassa anabhiratiukkaṇṭhanā vā bhayaparitassanā vā natthi, brahmuno pana āgamanapatthanā āgamanataṇhā ahūti attho.

Brahmunāsākacchāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"Having caused a new *sandhāgāra* to be made": having caused a delightful dwelling to be made, equipped with a night-quarters, a day-quarters and a promenade, suitable for dwelling in for four months in the rainy season, enclosed outside by reeds.

"Meditating on the *karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ*": meditating on the *jhāna* that is a triad or a tetrad of compassion (*karuṇā*); here, through the aspect of compassion, the remaining three divine abodes (*brahmavihārā*) are also included.

"*Ukkaṇṭhanā paritassanā*": For one established in the ground of *jhāna*, there is no discontent or longing, nor fear or anxiety. But for Brahmā, there was longing for arrival, thirst for arrival, is the meaning.

Description of conversation with Brahmā

mula_pali:
318. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, brahmā sanaṅkumāro mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva, brahmaloke antarahito mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa sammukhe pāturahosi. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa ahudeva bhayaṃ ahu chambhitattaṃ ahu lomahaṃso yathā taṃ adiṭṭhapubbaṃ rūpaṃ disvā. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘‘Vaṇṇavā yasavā sirimā, ko nu tvamasi mārisa;

Ajānantā taṃ pucchāma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya’’nti.

‘‘Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānanti, brahmaloke sanantanaṃ sanantica (ka.);

sanantica (ka.)

Sabbe jānanti maṃ devā, evaṃ govinda jānahi’’.

‘‘‘Āsanaṃ udakaṃ pajjaṃ, madhusākañca madhupākañca (sī. syā. pī.) brahmuno;

madhupākañca (sī. syā. pī.)

Agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma, agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ’’.

‘‘Paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasi;

Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya, samparāya sukhāya ca;

Katāvakāso pucchassu, yaṃ kiñci abhipatthita’’nti.
mula_english:
318. Then, Brahmā Sanankumara, knowing with his mind the thoughts in the mind of the brahmin Mahāgovinda, as quickly as a strong man might stretch out his flexed arm or flex it again, vanished from the Brahma world and appeared before the brahmin Mahāgovinda.

Then, the brahmin Mahāgovinda felt fear, trembling, and his hair stood on end, seeing such a sight as he had never seen before.

Then, the brahmin Mahāgovinda, frightened, agitated, with hair standing on end, addressed Brahmā Sanankumara in verse:

"Varnava, Yasava, Sirima, who are you, Mārisa?"

"Not knowing you, we ask you, how should we know you?"

"The Kumaras know me, the eternal one, in the Brahma world;"

"All the gods know me, thus, Govinda, know me."

"A seat, water, a lamp, and honey-sweetness belong to Brahmā;"

"We ask you for worth, may you grant us worth."

"We accept your worth, which you, Govinda, declare;

for the sake of visible benefit, for future happiness;

having made an opportunity, ask whatever you desire."
commentary_pali:
318.Bhayanti cittutrāsabhayameva. Ajānantāti ajānamānā. Kathaṃ jānemu taṃ mayanti (dī. ni. 2.179) mayaṃ kinti taṃ jānāma, ayaṃ katthavāsiko, kinnāmo, kiṃ gottotiādīnaṃ ākārānaṃ kena ākārena taṃ dhārayāmāti attho.
