Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānantīti maṃ ‘‘kumāro’’ti ‘‘daharo’’ti jānanti. Brahmaloketi seṭṭhaloke. Sanantananti ciratanaṃ porāṇakaṃ . Ahaṃ so porāṇakumāro sanaṅkumāro nāma brahmāti dasseti. Evaṃ govinda jānāhīti govinda paṇḍita, tvaṃ evaṃ jānāhi, evaṃ maṃ dhārehi.

Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānantī Brahmaloke Sanantana Evaṃ govinda jānāhī

‘‘Āsanaṃ udakaṃ pajjaṃ, madhusākañca brahmuno;

Agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma, agghaṃ kurutu no bhava’’nti. –

Ettha agghanti atithino upanāmetabbaṃ vuccati. Teneva idamāsanaṃ paññattaṃ, ettha nisīdatha, idaṃ udakaṃ parisuddhaṃ, ito pānīyaṃ pivatha, pāde dhovatha, idaṃ pajjaṃ pādānaṃ hitatthāya abhisaṅkhataṃ telaṃ, ito pāde makkhetha, idaṃ madhusākanti. Bodhisattassa brahmacariyaṃ na aññesaṃ brahmacariyasadisaṃ hoti, na so ‘‘idaṃ sve, idaṃ tatiyadivase bhavissatī’’ti sannidhiṃ nāma karoti. Madhusākaṃ pana aloṇaṃ adhūpanaṃ atakkaṃ udakena seditasākaṃ, taṃ sandhāyesa – ‘‘idaṃ paribhuñjathā’’ti vadanto ‘‘agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāmā’’tiādimāha. Ime sabbepi agghā brahmuno atthi. Te agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma. Evaṃ pucchantānañca agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ, paṭiggaṇhātu no bhavaṃ idamagghanti vuttaṃ hoti. Kiṃ panesa – ‘‘ito ekampi brahmā na bhuñjatī’’ti idaṃ na jānātīti. No na jānāti, jānantopi attano santike āgato atithi pucchitabboti vattasīsena pucchati.

aggha agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma. agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ,

Atha kho brahmā – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho paṇḍito mama paribhogakaraṇābhāvaṃ ñatvā pucchati, udāhu kohaññe ṭhatvā pucchatī’’ti samannāharanto ‘‘vattasīse ṭhito pucchatī’’ti ñatvā paṭiggaṇhituṃ dāni me vaṭṭatīti paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasīti āha. Yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasi – ‘‘idamāsanaṃ paññattaṃ, ettha nisīdathā’’tiādi, tatra te mayaṃ āsane nisinnā nāma homa, pānīyaṃ pītā nāma homa, pādāpi me dhotā nāma hontu, telenapi makkhitā nāma hontu, udakasākampi paribhuttaṃ nāma hotu, tayā dinnaṃ adhivāsitakālato paṭṭhāya yaṃ yaṃ tvaṃ bhāsasi, taṃ taṃ mayā paṭiggahitameva hoti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasī’’ti. Evaṃ pana agghaṃ paṭiggaṇhitvā pañhassa okāsaṃ karonto diṭṭhadhammahitatthāyātiādimāha.

paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasī diṭṭhadhammahitatthāyā

Kaṅkhīakaṅkhiṃ paravediyesūti ahaṃ savicikiccho bhavantaṃ parena sayaṃ abhisaṅkhatattā parassa pākaṭesu paravediyesu pañhesu nibbicikicchaṃ.

Kaṅkhī akaṅkhiṃ paravediyesū

Hitvā mamattanti idaṃ mama, idaṃ mamāti upakaraṇataṇhaṃ cajitvā. Manujesūti sattesu, manujesu yo koci manujo mamattaṃ hitvāti attho. Ekodibhūtoti ekībhūto, eko tiṭṭhanto eko nisīdantoti. Vacanattho panettha eko udeti pavattatīti ekodi, tādiso bhūtoti ekodibhūto . Karuṇedhimuttoti karuṇājhāne adhimutto, taṃ jhānaṃ nibbattetvāti attho. Nirāmagandhoti vissagandhavirahito. Ettha ṭhitoti etesu dhammesu ṭhito. Ettha ca sikkhamānoti etesu dhammesu sikkhamāno. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana upari mahāgovindena ca brahmunā ca vuttoyeva.

Hitvā mamatta Manujesū Ekodibhūto Karuṇedhimutto Nirāmagandho Ettha ṭhito Ettha ca sikkhamāno
commentary_english:
318. *Bhaya*nti: [means] fear is only the fear of mental fright.
*Ajānantā*ti: [means] not knowing.
*Kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya*nti: (Dīgha Nikāya 2.179) [means] How do we know him? What is his native place? What is his name? What is his lineage? What is the meaning of the various forms?
*Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānantī*ti: [means] They know me as “*Kumāra*,” as “young."
*Brahmaloke*ti: [means] in the best of worlds.
*Sanantana*nti: [means] ancient and old.
I, that ancient youth, am showing [the way to] *Sanaṃkumāra*, called Brahmā.
*Evaṃ govinda jānāhī*ti: [means] Thus, O Govinda, the wise, you should understand, thus hold me in mind.

*Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānantī Brahmaloke Sanantana*
*Evaṃ govinda jānāhī*
‘‘A seat, water, the commoner, and honey-cakes of Brahmā.’’
“We ask you for a gift, please give us a gift!”
–
Here, *aggha*nti means that which should be offered to a guest.
With this in mind, this seat was designated: “Sit here. This water is pure. Drink this water. Wash your feet. This commoner is oil mixed for the benefit of the feet, anoint your feet with this. This is honey-cake.”
A bodhisattva’s *brahmacarya* is not like the *brahmacarya* of others; he does not give rise to the thought, “This will be tomorrow, this will be the day after tomorrow.”
But honey-cakes are saltless, unfumigated, without buttermilk, and are vegetables cooked with water. Thinking about this, he said, “Eat this,” and “we ask you for a gift,” and so forth.
All these gifts belong to Brahmā.
They "ask you for a gift."
And when asked thus, "[Please] give us a gift," it is said that one should accept this gift.
What then? He does not know that even one Brahmā does not eat this.
No, he does not know. Even knowing, he asks with proper courtesy because a guest who has come into his presence should be asked.

*Aggha*
*Agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma.*
*Agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ,*
Then Brahmā thinks, “Why is this wise one asking after knowing that I lack the means to enjoy these things? Or does he ask standing far off in a corner?” Understanding that he is asking with proper courtesy, he now deems it proper to accept and says, "we accept the gift that you, Govinda, declare."
What you, Govinda, declare is, "This seat is designated; sit here," and so forth; in that case, we are named as sitting on the seat, we are named as having drunk the water, may our feet be named as having been washed, may they be named as having been anointed with oil, may even the vegetables cooked in water be named as having been consumed; whatever you declare, from the time it is given by you, all that is accepted by me.
Therefore it was said – “We accept the gift that you, Govinda, declare.”
Having thus accepted the gift, and making an opportunity for questioning, he said, "for the sake of what is beneficial in this life," and so forth.

*Paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasī Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāyā*
*Kaṅkhī Akaṅkhiṃ paravediyesū*ti: I am without doubt about the questions of you, who are skilled in the knowledge of others, because of what has been self-produced through another.

*Kaṅkhī Akaṅkhiṃ paravediyesū Hitvā mamatta*nti: [means] giving up the craving for possessions, [thinking,] “This is mine, this is mine.”
*Manujesū*ti: [means] Among beings, whoever gives up the thought of "mine" among humans.
*Ekodibhūto*ti: [means] become one; one standing, one sitting.
Here, the meaning of the word "one" is "it arises and proceeds." Therefore, *ekodibhūto* is one who has become that.

319. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘katāvakāso khomhi brahmunā sanaṅkumārena. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ puccheyyaṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ vā atthaṃ samparāyikaṃ vā’ti? Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘kusalo kho ahaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ atthānaṃ, aññepi maṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ atthaṃ pucchanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ samparāyikaññeva atthaṃ puccheyya’nti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Pucchāmi brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ,

Kaṅkhī akaṅkhiṃ paravediyesu;

Katthaṭṭhito kimhi ca sikkhamāno,

Pappoti macco amataṃ brahmaloka’’nti.

‘‘Hitvā mamattaṃ manujesu brahme,

Ekodibhūto karuṇedhimutto karuṇādhimutto (sī. syā. pī.);

karuṇādhimutto (sī. syā. pī.)

Nirāmagandho virato methunasmā,

Etthaṭṭhito ettha ca sikkhamāno;

Pappoti macco amataṃ brahmaloka’’nti.
mula_english:
319. “Then the great steward, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda, thought: ‘I have been given an opportunity by Brahmā Sanankumāra. Should I ask Brahmā Sanankumāra about advantage in this life (*dṛṣṭadharma*) or benefit in the life to come (*samparāyika*)?’ Then the great steward, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda, thought: ‘I am skilled in matters of advantage in this life, and others ask me about advantage in this life. Suppose I were to ask Brahmā Sanankumāra for something of benefit in the life to come (*samparāyika*)?’ Then the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda addressed Brahmā Sanankumāra in these verses:

“I ask Brahmā Sanankumāra,
Doubting among those free from doubt who follow other paths;
Where does a mortal stand, in what does he train,
To attain the deathless world of Brahmā (*brahmaloka*)?”

“Having given up affection in human beings, Brahmā,
Being of one origin, released by compassion (*karuṇā*);
Free from the stench of desire, abstaining from sexual intercourse,
Standing here, training here,
A mortal attains the deathless world of Brahmā (*brahmaloka*).”

320. ‘‘Hitvā mamatta’nti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, ‘iti hitvā mamatta’nti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. ‘Ekodibhūto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ, iti ekodibhūto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. ‘Karuṇedhimutto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadhotiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Iti ‘karuṇedhimutto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Āmagandhe ca kho ahaṃ bhoto bhāsamānassa na ājānāmi.

‘‘Ke āmagandhā manujesu brahme,

Ete avidvā idha brūhi dhīra;

Kenāvaṭā kenāvuṭā (syā.) vāti pajā kurutu kururū (syā.), kuruṭṭharū (pī.), kurūru (?),

kenāvuṭā (syā.) kururū (syā.), kuruṭṭharū (pī.), kurūru (?)

Āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā’’ti.

‘‘Kodho mosavajjaṃ nikati ca dubbho,

Kadariyatā atimāno usūyā;

Icchā vivicchā paraheṭhanā ca,

Lobho ca doso ca mado ca moho;

Etesu yuttā anirāmagandhā,

Āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā’’ti.

‘‘Yathā kho ahaṃ bhoto āmagandhe bhāsamānassa ājānāmi. Te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.

mula_english:
320. “I understand “Spuming possessive thoughts” as follows.

This means that one renounces one’s possessions, small or great, leaves one’s relatives, few or many, and, shaving off hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness. This is how I understand “Spuming possessive thoughts”.

I understand “Alone, intent” as follows.

That means that one goes off on one’s own and chooses a lodging in the forest (*araññaṃ*), at the foot of a tree (*rukkhamūlaṃ*), in a mountain glen (*pabbataṃ kandaraṃ*), in a rocky cave (*giriguhaṃ*), a charnel-ground (*susānaṃ*), in the jungle (*vanapatthaṃ*) or on a heap of grass in the open (*abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ*). This is how I understand “Alone, intent”.

I understand “Compassion-filled” as follows.

That means that one dwells suffusing one quarter with a mind filled with compassion (*karuṇāsahagatena cetasā*), then a second, then a third and a fourth quarter.

Thus above, below, across, everywhere, all around, one dwells suffusing the whole world with a mind filled with compassion (*karuṇāsahagatena cetasā*)—abundant, exalted, measureless, without hatred (*averena*), without ill-will (*abyāpajjena*).

That is how I understand “Compassion-filled”.

But the Lord’s words about “Aloof from stench” I do not understand:

‘What is stench among men, Brahman?

Tell us, wise one, who do not know these things.

What is it that veils, what does the populace do,

that they are liable to misery, shut out from the Brahmā world?’

‘Anger, lying speech, trickery, and deceit,

Stinginess, arrogance, envy,

Selfishness, capriciousness, harming others,

Greed, hate, pride, and delusion:

Those attached to these are not aloof from stench,

and are liable to misery, shut out from the Brahmā world.’

‘As I understand the Lord’s words about the stench,

these things are not easy to overcome if one lives the household life.

I will therefore go forth from the household life into the homeless state.’

‘Reverend Govinda, do as you think fit.’

Kenāvaṭā vāti pajā kurutūti katamena kilesāvaraṇena āvaritā pajā pūtikā vāyati. Āpāyikāti apāyūpagā. Nivutabrahmalokāti nivuto pihito brahmaloko assāti nivutabrahmaloko. Katamena kilesena pajāya brahmalokūpago maggo nivuto pihito paṭicchannoti pucchati.

Kodho mosavajjaṃ nikati ca dubbhoti kujjhanalakkhaṇo kodho ca, paravisaṃvādanalakkhaṇo musāvādo ca, sadisaṃ dassetvā vañcanalakkhaṇā nikati ca, mittadubbhanalakkhaṇo dubbho ca. Kadariyatā atimāno usūyāti thaddhamacchariyalakkhaṇā kadariyatā ca, atikkamitvā maññanalakkhaṇo atimāno ca, parasampattikhīyanalakkhaṇā usūyā ca. Icchā vivicchā paraheṭhanā cāti taṇhālakkhaṇā icchā ca, macchariyalakkhaṇā vivicchā ca, vihiṃsālakkhaṇā paraheṭhanā ca. Etesu yuttā anirāmagandhāti etesu cuddasasu kilesesu yuttā pajā nirāmagandhā na hoti, āmagandhā sakuṇapagandhā pūtigandhāyevāti vadati. Āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokāti esā pana āpāyikā ceva hoti, paṭicchannabrahmalokamaggā cāti. Idaṃ pana suttaṃ kathentena āmagandhasuttena dīpetvā kathetabbaṃ, āmagandhasuttampi iminā dīpetvā kathetabbaṃ.

commentary_english:
320. There, “*ete avidvā*” means, I am ignorant of these raw smells, I do not know, is the meaning.

“*idha brūhi dhīrā*” means, you are wise and learned, tell me here, speak, say.

“*kenāvaṭā vāti pajā kurutū*” means, by which defilement-covering is the population covered and stinking?

"*āpāyikā*" means leading to the *apāya*s (states of misery).

"*nivutabrahmalokā*" means, the *brahmaloka* (world of Brahmā) is covered and hidden, therefore, it is a covered *brahmaloka*.

With which defilement is the path to the *brahmaloka* covered, hidden, concealed for the population, he asks.

*kodho mosavajjaṃ nikati ca dubbho* means, anger is characterized by irritation, false speech is characterized by deceiving others, *nikati* is characterized by deceiving after showing something similar, and *dubbho* is characterized by betraying friends.

*kadariyatā atimāno usūyā* means, *kadariyatā* is characterized by stubborn miserliness, *atimāna* is characterized by exaggerating conceit, and *usūyā* is characterized by envying the prosperity of others.

*icchā vivicchā paraheṭhanā cā* means, *icchā* is characterized by craving, *vivicchā* is characterized by miserliness, and *paraheṭhanā* is characterized by harming others.

*lobho ca doso ca mado ca moho* means, greed is characterized by clinging everywhere, aversion (*dosa*) is characterized by ill-will, pride (*mada*) is characterized by intoxication, and delusion (*moha*) is characterized by bewilderment.

*etesu yuttā anirāmagandhā* means, the population that is connected with these fourteen defilements is not without the raw smell; they are raw-smelling and corpse-smelling. He speaks as if they have a foul smell.

*āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā* means, indeed, it leads to the *apāya*s and it is the path to the covered *brahmaloka*.

This *sutta* should be explained by someone reciting the *Āmagandhasutta*, and the *Āmagandhasutta* should be explained by this.

*kodho mosavajjaṃ nikati ca dubbho* *kadariyatā atimāno usūyā* *usūyā ca.*
*icchā vivicchā paraheṭhanā cā* *lobho ca doso ca mado ca moho* *etesu yuttā anirāmagandhā*
*āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā* *āmagandhasuttena*

*te na sunimmadayā* means, these raw smells are not easily subdued; they are difficult to abandon and difficult to conquer, is the meaning.

*yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī* means, "Whomever, Govinda, you consider it the right time to ordain, let that be the one. Thus, my coming to your presence will be a good coming, the talk of the recited Dharma will be well-spoken, and you, dear one, are the foremost person in all of Jambudvīpa, young, standing in your first age. Thus, abandoning such great prosperity, splendor, and delights, your renunciation is like an elephant tearing its iron bonds and going away, it is very noble. This is called the Buddha-lineage.” After solidifying the great man's resolve, Brahmā Sanankumāra went to the Brahmaloka.

*te na sunimmadayā* *yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī*

321. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘aññaṃ dāni bhavaṃ purohitaṃ pariyesatu, yo bhoto rajjaṃ anusāsissati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho , agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti.

‘‘Āmantayāmi rājānaṃ, reṇuṃ bhūmipatiṃ ahaṃ;

Tvaṃ pajānassu rajjena, nāhaṃ porohicce rame’’.

‘‘Sace te ūnaṃ kāmehi, ahaṃ paripūrayāmi te;

Yo taṃ hiṃsati vāremi, bhūmisenāpati ahaṃ;

Tuvaṃ pitā ahaṃ putto, mā no govinda pājahi’’ pājehi (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇitapāṭhantaraṃ).

pājehi (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇitapāṭhantaraṃ)

‘‘Namatthi ūnaṃ kāmehi, hiṃsitā me na vijjati;

Amanussavaco sutvā, tasmāhaṃ na gahe rame’’.

‘‘Amanusso kathaṃvaṇṇo, kiṃ te atthaṃ abhāsatha;

Yañca sutvā jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī’’.

‘‘Upavutthassa me pubbe, yiṭṭhukāmassa me sato;

Aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthato’’.

‘‘Tato me brahmā pāturahu, brahmalokā sanantano;

So me pañhaṃ viyākāsi, taṃ sutvā na gahe rame’’.

‘‘Saddahāmi ahaṃ bhoto, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasi;

Amanussavaco sutvā, kathaṃ vattetha aññathā.

‘‘Te taṃ anuvattissāma, satthā govinda no bhavaṃ;

Maṇi yathā veḷuriyo, akāco vimalo subho;

Evaṃ suddhā carissāma, govindassānusāsane’’ti.

‘‘‘Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma. Atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

mula_english:
321. Then, the brāhmin Mahāgovinda approached King Reṇu and, having approached, said this to King Reṇu: “Now, may you seek another *purohita* (family priest) who will instruct your kingdom. I wish to go forth from the householder’s life to homelessness. As I have heard from Brahmā speaking of the stench of sensual pleasures, it is not easily overcome by one living in a household. I will go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness.”

“I summon King Reṇu, the lord of the earth; may you understand the kingdom, for I do not delight in the office of family priest.”

“If you lack sensual pleasures, I will fulfill them for you; I restrain him who injures you, for I am the commander of the army of the earth; you are my father, I am your son, do not abandon us, Govinda!”

“There is no lack with sensual pleasures, no injurer of me is found; having heard the voice of a non-human, therefore I do not delight in a house.”

“A non-human—what sort of description, what benefit did he speak to you? And having heard what, do you abandon us, alone in our home?”

“Formerly, when I had observed the upavasatha vow, when I was one who desired to sacrifice, the fire was blazing, surrounded by *kuśa* grass.”

“Then Brahmā appeared to me, the eternal one from the Brahmā-world; he explained a question to me, having heard which, I do not delight in a house.”

“I trust you, sir, in what you say, Govinda; having heard the voice of a non-human, how could you speak otherwise?

“We will follow you, Govinda, you are our teacher; like a beryl gem, clear, stainless, beautiful, thus we will live purely in Govinda’s instruction.”

“‘If the honorable Govinda goes forth from the householder’s life to homelessness, we too will go forth from the householder’s life to homelessness. Then, whatever your destiny, that will be our destiny.’”

Āha . Tassattho – yo taṃ hiṃsati, taṃ vāremi, kevalaṃ tumhe ‘‘asuko’’ti ācikkhatha, ahamettha kattabbaṃ jānissāmīti. Tassattho – tvaṃ pitiṭṭhāne tiṭṭha, ahaṃ puttaṭṭhāne ṭhassāmi. Mā no tvaṃ bho govinda, pajahi, mā pariccajīti. Atha mahāpuriso yaṃ rājā cintesi, tassa attani abhāvaṃ dassento –

‘‘Na matthi ūnaṃ kāmehi, hiṃsitā me na vijjati;

Amanussavaco sutvā, tasmāhaṃ na gahe rame’’ti. –

Āha. Tattha na matthīti na me atthi. Gaheti gehe. Atha naṃ rājā pucchi –

na matthī Gahe

‘‘Amanusso kathaṃ vaṇṇo, kiṃ te atthaṃ abhāsatha;

Yañca sutvā jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī’’ti.

Tattha jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalīti brāhmaṇassa sampattibharite gehe saṅgahavasena attano gehe karonto yaṃ sutvā amhākaṃ gehe ca amhe ca kevalī sabbe aparisese jambudīpavāsino jahāsīti vadati.

jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī

Athassa ācikkhanto mahāpuriso upavutthassa me pubbetiādimāha. Tattha upavutthassāti cattāro māse ekībhāvaṃ upagantvā vutthassa. Yiṭṭhakāmassa me satoti yajitukāmassa me samānassa. Aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthatoti kusapattehi paritthato sappidadhimadhuādīni pakkhipitvā aggi jalayitumāraddho āsi, evaṃ aggiṃ jāletvā ‘‘mahājanassa dānaṃ dassāmī’’ti evaṃ cintetvā ṭhitassa mamāti ayamettha attho.

upavutthassa me pubbe upavutthassā Yiṭṭhakāmassa me sato Aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthato

Sanantanoti sanaṅkumāro brahmā. Tato rājā sayampi pabbajitukāmo hutvā saddahāmītiādimāha. Tattha kathaṃ vattetha aññathāti kathaṃ tumhe aññathā vattissatha. Te taṃ anuvattissāmāti te mayampi tumheyeva anuvattissāma, anupabbajissāmāti attho. ‘‘Anuvajissāmā’’tipi pāṭho, tassa anugacchissāmāti attho. Akācoti nikkāco akakkaso. Govindassānusāsaneti tava govindassa sāsane. Bhavantaṃ govindameva satthāraṃ karitvā carissāmāti vadati.

Sanantano saddahāmī kathaṃ vattetha aññathā Te taṃ anuvattissāmā Akāco Govindassānusāsane

Cha khattiyaāmantanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
321. The great man thought: "It is not right for me to leave here and become a renunciate. I should advise the royal family on matters of benefit. Therefore, I will inform the king. If he also becomes a renunciate, that would be excellent. If he does not become a renunciate, I will hand over the office of the family priest and then I will become a renunciate." Thinking this, he approached the king, and thus it was said: "Then, O venerable Mahāgovinda,...pe... I do not delight in the priesthood."

There, *tvaṃ pajānassu rajjenā* means: You yourself should know by your kingdom. *nāhaṃ porohicce rame* means: I do not delight in the state of being a family priest. I am weary [of it]. Know another advisor, I do not delight in the priesthood.

*tvaṃ pajānassu rajjenā nāhaṃ porohicce rame* Then the king thought: "Surely, the pleasures of the Brāhman, who has been in seclusion for four months, have become meager." Thinking this and inviting him with wealth, he said: "If you are lacking in pleasures, I will fulfill them for you." Then, saying this again, he thought: "Could it be that someone has harmed this one who is living alone?"

"Whoever harms you, I will stop [him], I am the commander of the earth's army;
You are the father, I am the son, do not abandon us, O Govinda."

Thus he spoke.
The meaning of that is: Whoever harms you, I will stop [him]. Simply tell [me] "This is the one," and I will know what should be done here. *bhūmisenāpati aha* means: Or rather, I am the lord of the earth, and I myself will make you accept this kingdom. *tuvaṃ pitā ahaṃ putto* means: You will stand in the place of the father, and I in the place of the son.

So you, having taken my mind, O Govinda, direct [your] mind to yourself; behave as you wish. But I, following your mind, while eating the alms given by you, either with a sword and shield in hand, will attend to you, or I will drive your chariot. "mā no govinda, pajahī" is another reading.

The meaning of that is: You stand in the place of the father, I will stand in the place of the son. O Govinda, do not abandon us, do not forsake [us]! Then the great man, showing the king the absence of self in what the king was thinking,

*bhūmisenāpati aha tuvaṃ pitā ahaṃ putto* "I lack nothing in sensual pleasures; there is no one who harms me;

Having heard the words of a non-human, therefore I do not delight in the house."

Thus he spoke. There, *na matthī* means: There is nothing for me. *gahe* means: in the house. Then the king asked him:

*na matthī gahe* "O non-human, what is the description, what beneficial thing did they say to you;

And having heard what, you have abandoned us, both me and you alone in the house?"

There, *jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī* means: He says that, making [his] own house, which was filled with the wealth of the Brāhman's house, like the Brāhman's with the means of generosity, and having heard what, he has abandoned us in our house, both me and you alone, all the remaining inhabitants of Jambudvīpa.

*jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī* Then, explaining it to him, the great man spoke, beginning with *upavutthassa me pubbe*. There, *upavutthassā* means: To one who has lived, having approached oneness for four months. *yiṭṭhakāmassa me sato* means: To me, who had the desire to sacrifice,

*aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthato* means: The fire was blazing, surrounded by kusa grass. Having thrown into it butter, curd, honey, etc., the fire was started, and having thus lit the fire, thinking thus, "I will give a gift to the great multitude of people," this is the meaning of that which was stood by me.

*upavutthassa me pubbe upavutthassā yiṭṭhakāmassa me sato aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthato* *sanantano* means Sanankumāra is Brahmā. Then the king himself, wanting to become a renunciate, spoke, beginning with *saddahāmī*. There, *kathaṃ vattetha aññathā* means: How would you speak otherwise? *te taṃ anuvattissāmā* means: We also will follow you, we will become renunciates.
Also, a reading is "anuvajissāmā," which means "we will go after."

*Akāco* means without glass, not rough.

*Govindassānusāsane* means in your, Govinda's, instruction.

He says, "Having made you, Govinda, the teacher, I will conduct myself."

Eternal. I believe. How could you speak otherwise? We will follow that. Without glass. In Govinda's instruction. Description of the six Kṣatriya invitations.

mula_pali: 322. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – ‘‘aññaṃ dāni bhavanto purohitaṃ pariyesantu, yo bhavantānaṃ rajje anusāsissati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘‘ime kho brāhmaṇā nāma dhanaluddhā; yaṃnūna mayaṃ mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dhanena sikkheyyāmā’’ti. Te mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘saṃvijjati kho, bho, imesu sattasu rajjesu pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ, tato bhoto yāvatakena attho, tāvatakaṃ āharīyata’’nti. ‘‘Alaṃ, bho, mamapidaṃ pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ bhavantānaṃyeva vāhasā. Tamahaṃ sabbaṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘‘ime kho brāhmaṇā nāma itthiluddhā; yaṃnūna mayaṃ mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ itthīhi sikkheyyāmā’’ti. Te mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘saṃvijjanti kho, bho, imesu sattasu rajjesu pahūtā itthiyo, tato bhoto yāvatikāhi attho, tāvatikā ānīyata’’nti. ‘‘Alaṃ, bho, mamapimā mamapitā (ka.), mamapi (sī.) cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo. Tāpāhaṃ sabbā pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyanti’’.
mula_english:
322. Then the great Govinda brahmin approached those six nobles; having approached, he said this to those six nobles: “Now, your honors, look for another family priest ( *purohita*), who will instruct your kingdoms.

I wish, sir, to go forth from the household life into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ*).

As I have heard the Brahmā speaking of the raw smell (*āmagandhe*) , those who dwell in a house do not easily get rid of it.

I will go forth, sir, from household to homelessness."

Then the six nobles went aside and considered thus: "These brahmins are greedy for wealth (*dhanaluddhā*); why don't we win over the great Govinda brahmin with wealth (*dhanena*)?"

They approached the great Govinda brahmin and said thus: "There exists, sir, in these seven kingdoms, abundant property (*sāpateyyaṃ*), let as much as you need be brought from there."

"Enough, sir, I have enough abundant property (*sāpateyyaṃ*) from you, gentlemen, as offering (*vāhasā*).

I will renounce all that and go forth from household to homelessness.

As I have heard the Brahmā speaking of the raw smell (*āmagandhe*) , those who dwell in a house do not easily get rid of it. I will go forth, sir, from household to homelessness."

Then the six nobles went aside and considered thus: "These *brāhmaṇas* are greedy for women (*itthiluddhā*); why don't we win over the great Govinda brahmin with women (*itthīhi*)?"

They approached the great Govinda brahmin and said thus: "There exist, sir, in these seven kingdoms, abundant women (*itthiyo*), let as many as you need be brought from there."

"Enough, sir, I have these forty wives (*bhariyā*) of equal rank. I will renounce all those and go forth from household to homelessness.

As I have heard the Brahmā speaking of the raw smell (*āmagandhe*), those who dwell in a house do not easily get rid of it, I will go forth, sir, from household to homelessness."
commentary_pali: 322.Yenate cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkamīti reṇuṃ rājānaṃ ‘‘sādhu mahārāja rajjaṃ nāma mātaraṃ pitaraṃ bhātibhaginīādayopi māretvā gaṇhantesu sattesu evaṃ mahantaṃ rajjasiriṃ pahāya pabbajitukāmena uḷāraṃ mahārājena kata’’nti upatthambhetvā daḷhataramassa ussāhaṃ katvā upasaṅkami . Evaṃ samacintesunti rañño cintitanayeneva kadāci brāhmaṇassa bhogā parihīnā bhaveyyunti maññamānā samacintesuṃ. Dhanena sikkheyyāmāti upalāpeyyāma saṅgaṇheyyāma. Tāvatakaṃ āharīyatanti tāvatakaṃ āharāpiyatu gaṇhiyatu, yattakaṃ icchatha, tattakaṃ gaṇhathāti vuttaṃ hoti. Bhavantānaṃyeva vāhasāti bhavante paccayaṃ katvā, tumhehi dinnattāyeva pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ jātaṃ.
commentary_english:
322. Because of that, those *kṣatriyas* approached King Reṇu, saying, "Well done, Great King! It is indeed difficult to renounce such great royal splendor, even to one who desires to renounce, considering that beings kill even their mother, father, brothers, sisters, and so forth, for the sake of kingship. It is a noble act that has been done by the Great King!" Thus, they encouraged him, strengthened his resolve, and approached [him].

Thus they considered: "The possessions of the *brāhmaṇa* might be diminished sometime or other, just as the king thought." Thus they considered.

"[Let us] train with wealth!" Thus, we would cajole [him] and gather [supporters].

"*tāvatakaṃ āharīyata*," means: "Let it be brought, let it be taken, however much you desire, take that much." This is what is said.

"*bhavantānaṃyeva vāhasā*" means: Having made you the cause, a great abundance of property has arisen, solely because of what was given by you.

mula_pali:
323. ‘‘Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatīti.

‘‘Sace jahatha kāmāni, yattha satto puthujjano;

Ārambhavho daḷhā hotha, khantibalasamāhitā.

‘‘Esa maggo ujumaggo, esa maggo anuttaro;

Saddhammo sabbhi rakkhito, brahmalokūpapattiyāti.

‘‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo satta vassāni āgametu. Sattannaṃ vassānaṃ accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, satta vassāni, nāhaṃ sakkomi, bhavante, satta vassāni āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ mantāya (bahūsu) boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’’nti. ‘‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo chabbassāni āgametu…pe… pañca vassāni āgametu… cattāri vassāni āgametu… tīṇi vassāni āgametu… dve vassāni āgametu… ekaṃ vassaṃ āgametu, ekassa vassassa accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

mantāya (bahūsu)

‘‘‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, ekaṃ vassaṃ, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante ekaṃ vassaṃ āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ , caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo satta māsāni āgametu, sattannaṃ māsānaṃ accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, satta māsāni, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante satta māsāni āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ. Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ , kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti.

‘‘‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo cha māsāni āgametu…pe… pañca māsāni āgametu… cattāri māsāni āgametu… tīṇi māsāni āgametu… dve māsāni āgametu… ekaṃ māsaṃ āgametu… addhamāsaṃ āgametu, addhamāsassa accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, addhamāso, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante addhamāsaṃ āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo sattāhaṃ āgametu, yāva mayaṃ sake puttabhātaro rajjena rajje (syā.) anusāsissāma, sattāhassa accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti. ‘‘Na ciraṃ kho, bho, sattāhaṃ, āgamessāmahaṃ bhavante sattāha’’nti.

rajje (syā.)

Brāhmaṇamahāsālādīnaṃ āmantanā
mula_english:
323. If the Reverend Govinda goes forth from the household life into homelessness, we will do likewise. Wherever you go, we will follow. If you abandon desires, where the ordinary person is attached, be firm, strong in effort, possessing patience, strength, and collectedness. This is the straight path, this is the unsurpassed path; the true *dharma* is protected by the virtuous, for attaining birth in Brahma's world. Therefore, Reverend Govinda, wait seven years. After the passing of seven years, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Wherever you go, we will follow. "Too long, sir, are seven years. I am unable to wait for you for seven years. Who, sir, knows the duration of life? The next world is to be reached; this teaching is to be understood; virtue is to be done; the holy life is to be lived; there is no immortality for that which is born. As I have heard from Brahma speaking of the stench of the world, which cannot easily be overcome by one living the household life, I will go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness." Therefore, Reverend Govinda, wait six years...five years...four years...three years...two years...one year. After the passing of one year, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Wherever you go, we will follow. "Too long, sir, is one year. I am unable to wait for you for one year. Who, sir, knows the duration of life? The next world is to be reached; this teaching is to be understood; virtue is to be done, the holy life is to be lived; there is no immortality for that which is born. As I have heard from Brahma speaking of the stench of the world, which cannot easily be overcome by one living the household life, I will go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness." Therefore, Reverend Govinda, wait seven months. After the passing of seven months, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Wherever you go, we will follow. "Too long, sir, are seven months. I am unable to wait for you for seven months. Who, sir, knows the duration of life? The next world is to be reached; this teaching is to be understood; virtue is to be done; the holy life is to be lived; there is no immortality for that which is born. As I have heard from Brahma speaking of the stench of the world, which cannot easily be overcome by one living the household life, I will go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness." Therefore, Reverend Govinda, wait six months...five months...four months...three months...two months...one month...half a month. After the passing of half a month, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Wherever you go, we will follow. "Too long, sir, is half a month. I am unable to wait for you for half a month. Who, sir, knows the duration of life? The next world is to be reached; this teaching is to be understood; virtue is to be done; the holy life is to be lived; there is no immortality for that which is born. As I have heard from Brahma speaking of the stench of the world, which cannot easily be overcome by one living the household life, I will go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness." Therefore, Reverend Govinda, wait seven days, while we instruct our own sons and brothers in the kingdom. After the passing of seven days, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Wherever you go, we will follow. "Seven days is not long, sir. I will wait for you seven days." ) Note

Calling to the *brāhmaṇa* great-householders and others
commentary_pali:
323.Sace jahatha kāmānīti sace vatthukāme ca kilesakāme ca pariccajatha. Yattha satto puthujjanoti yesu kāmesu puthujjano satto laggo laggito. Ārambhavho daḷhā hothāti evaṃ sante vīriyaṃ ārabhatha, asithilaparakkamataṃ adhiṭṭhāya daḷhā bhavatha. Khantībalasamāhitāti khantibalena samannāgatā bhavathāti rājūnaṃ ussāhaṃ janeti.

Esa maggo ujumaggoti esa karuṇājhānamaggo ujumaggo nāma. Esa maggo anuttaroti eseva brahmalokūpapattiyā asadisamaggo uttamamaggo nāma. Saddhammo sabbhi rakkhitoti eso eva ca buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakehi sabbhirakkhitadhammo nāma. Iti karuṇājhānassa vaṇṇabhaṇanenāpi tesaṃ anivattanatthāya daḷhīkammameva karoti.

Esa maggo ujumaggo Esa maggo anuttaro Saddhammo sabbhi rakkhito

Ko nu kho pana bho jānāti jīvitānanti bho jīvitaṃ nāma udakapupphuḷūpamaṃ tiṇagge ussāvabindūpamaṃ taṅkhaṇaviddhaṃsanadhammaṃ, tassa ko gatiṃ jānāti, kismiṃ khaṇe bhijjissati? Gamanīyo samparāyoti paraloko pana avassaṃ gantabbova, tattha paṇḍitena kulaputtena mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ. Mantā vuccati paññā, tāya mantetabbaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ, upaparikkhitabbañca jānitabbañcāti attho. Karaṇatthe vā bhummaṃ. Mantāyaṃ boddhabbanti mantāya bujjhitabbaṃ, ñāṇena jānitabbanti attho. Kiṃ bujjhitabbaṃ? Jīvitassa dujjānatā, samparāyassa ca avassaṃ gamanīyatā, bujjhitvā ca pana sabbapalibodhe chinditvā kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ. Kasmā? Yasmā natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ.

Ko nu kho pana bho jānāti jīvitāna Gamanīyo samparāyo mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ. Mantāyaṃ boddhabba kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ.

Brāhmaṇamahāsālādīnaṃ āmantanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
323. If you abandon desires (kāmānī), that means you relinquish both material desires (vatthukāme) and defiled desires (kilesakāme).
Where the ordinary person (puthujjano) is attached (satto), that means the ordinary person is attached, clinging, and intensely clinging to those desires (kāmesu).
"Be firm, initiating effort (vīriyaṃ)" means in such a situation, initiate effort, and being resolute, be firm, upholding unwavering exertion (asithilaparakkamataṃ adhiṭṭhāya daḷhā bhavatha).
"Endowed with forbearance, strength, and concentration (khantībalasamāhitā)" means be endowed with the strength of forbearance; it generates enthusiasm for kings (rājūnaṃ ussāhaṃ janeti).

This is the straight path (ujumaggo): this is called the straight path, the path of compassion-jhāna (karuṇājhānamaggo ujumaggo nāma).
This is the unsurpassed path (anuttaro): this is the unsurpassed path, the path that is unlike any other, the excellent path leading to rebirth in the Brahma-world (brahmalokūpapattiyā asadisamaggo uttamamaggo nāma).
The true Dharma (saddhammo) is protected by the virtuous (sabbhi): this is the Dharma protected by the virtuous, namely, by the Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples (buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakehi sabbhirakkhitadhammo nāma).
Thus, even through recounting the virtues of compassion-jhāna (karuṇājhānassa vaṇṇabhaṇanenāpi), one only makes the commitment firmer, so that they do not turn back (anivattanatthāya daḷhīkammameva karoti).

This is the straight path; this is the unsurpassed path.
The true Dharma is protected by the virtuous. Who, indeed, knows about the life of beings (jīvitāna)? Life is like a water bubble, like a dewdrop on a blade of grass, with a nature that is destroyed in an instant; who knows its destiny (gatiṃ jānāti), at what moment it will break? The next world (samparāyo) is to be traveled (gamanīyo): the next world is certainly to be traveled; there, a wise person (paṇḍitena), a scion of a good family (kulaputtena), should be instructed in wisdom (mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ).
Wisdom (mantā) is called understanding (paññā); through that, one should be instructed, understand, examine, and know; this is the meaning (attho).
Or, in the sense of instrumentality (karaṇatthe), it is abundance (bhummaṃ).
"Should be instructed in wisdom (mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ)" means one should be instructed in wisdom; it means one should know through knowledge (ñāṇena jānitabbanti attho).
What should be understood (bujjhitabbaṃ)? The difficulty of knowing about life (jīvitassa dujjānatā), and the necessity of traveling to the next world (samparāyassa gamanīyatā); and having understood, and having cut off all attachments (sabbapalibodhe chinditvā), one should do what is skillful (kusalaṃ kattabbaṃ), one should live the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ caritabbaṃ).
Why (kasmā)? Because for that which is born, there is no non-death (natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ).

Who, indeed, knows about the life of beings? The next world is to be traveled. Should be instructed in wisdom.
Should be instructed in wisdom, one should do what is skillful, one should live the holy life.
Praise of the invitation of the Brahmins, great householders, and others (brāhmaṇamahāsālādīnaṃ āmantanāvaṇṇanā)

mula_pali:
324. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā satta ca nhātakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni etadavoca – ‘‘aññaṃ dāni bhavanto ācariyaṃ pariyesantu, yo bhavantānaṃ mante vācessati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa. Te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Mā bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Pabbajjā, bho, appesakkhā ca appalābhā ca; brahmaññaṃ mahesakkhañca mahālābhañcā’’ti. ‘‘Mā bhavanto evaṃ avacuttha – ‘‘pabbajjā appesakkhā ca appalābhā ca, brahmaññaṃ mahesakkhañca mahālābhañcā’’ti. Ko nu kho, bho, aññatra mayā mahesakkhataro vā mahālābhataro vā! Ahañhi, bho, etarahi rājāva raññaṃ brahmāva brāhmaṇānaṃ brahmānaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) devatāva gahapatikānaṃ. Tamahaṃ sabbaṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

Bhariyānaṃ āmantanā
mula_english:
“Then, Reverend, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda approached those seven wealthy *brāhmaṇas* and the seven hundred bathing *brāhmaṇas*; having approached, he said this to those seven wealthy *brāhmaṇas* and seven hundred bathing *brāhmaṇas*: “Now, gentlemen, seek another teacher who will recite the *mantras* for you. I wish to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness. As I have heard from Brahmā speaking about the stench of the world, those who live the household life cannot easily overcome it; I will go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness.”

“[Reverend] Govinda, do not go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness! The homeless life has little power and little profit; the *brāhmaṇa* life has great power and great profit!”

“Gentlemen, do not speak thus: ‘The homeless life has little power and little profit; the *brāhmaṇa* life has great power and great profit!’ Who other than me has greater power or greater profit? For now, I am like a king to kings, like Brahmā to *brāhmaṇas*, like a deity to householders. I am giving all this up to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness. As I have heard from Brahmā speaking about the stench of the world, those who live the household life cannot easily overcome it; I will go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness.”

“If the Reverend Govinda goes forth from the householder’s life into homelessness, we too will go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness; whatever your destiny, that will be our destiny.”

Calling the Wives
commentary_pali:
324.Appesakkhā ca appalābhā cāti bho pabbajjā nāma appayasā ceva, pabbajitakālato paṭṭhāya hi rajjaṃ pahāya pabbajitaṃ viheṭhetvā viheṭhetvā lāmakaṃ anāthaṃ katvāva kathenti. Appalābhā ca, sakalagāmaṃ caritvāpi ajjhoharaṇīyaṃ dullabhameva. Idaṃ pana brahmaññaṃmahesakkhañca mahāyasattā, mahālābhañca lābhasakkārasampannattā. Bhavañhi etarahi sakalajambudīpe aggapurohito sabbattha aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggabhattaṃ aggagandhaṃ aggamālaṃ labhatīti.

Rājāva raññanti ahañhi bho etarahi pakatiraññaṃ majjhe cakkavattirājā viya. Brahmāva brahmānanti pakatibrahmānaṃ majjhe mahābrahmasadiso. Devatāva gahapatikānanti avasesagahapatikānaṃ panamhi sakkadevarājasadiso.

Rājāva rañña Brahmāva brahmāna Devatāva gahapatikāna

Bhariyānaṃ āmantanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Appesakkhā ca appalābhā cā: "Monastics are those of little expectation and little gain," for indeed, from the time of ordination, they despise possessions and, by repeatedly afflicting the ordained one, they declare them base and helpless.

Appalābhā ca: And little gain, even wandering in every village, what is suitable to be eaten is difficult to obtain.

Idaṃ pana brahmaññaṃ: But this is Brahman-hood.

Mahesakkhañca mahāyasattā, mahālābhañca lābhasakkārasampannattā: And those great beings of great power and great gain are accomplished in gain, honor, and reverence.

Bhavañhi etarahi sakalajambudīpe aggapurohito sabbattha aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggabhattaṃ aggagandhaṃ aggamālaṃ labhatīti: "For you now, in all of Jambudvīpa, are the foremost priest, everywhere obtaining the foremost seat, the foremost water, the foremost food, the foremost perfume, and the foremost garland."

Rājāva rañña: "Like a king among kings," for I am now among ordinary kings like a *cakravartin* king.

Brahmāva brahmāna: "Like Brahmā among Brahmans," for among ordinary Brahmans, I am like Mahābrahmā.

Devatāva gahapatikāna: "Like a god among householders," for among the remaining householders, I am like Śakra, the king of the gods.

Rājāva rañña brahmāva brahmāna devatāva gahapatikāna: Like a king among kings, like Brahmā among Brahmans, like a god among householders.

Bhariyānaṃ āmantanāvaṇṇanā: Description of the invitation to the wives.

mula_pali:
325. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo etadavoca – ‘‘yā bhotīnaṃ icchati, sakāni vā ñātikulāni gacchatu aññaṃ vā bhattāraṃ pariyesatu. Icchāmahaṃ, bhotī, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bhotī, agārasmā anagāriya’’nti. ‘‘Tvaññeva no ñāti ñātikāmānaṃ, tvaṃ pana bhattā bhattukāmānaṃ. Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī’’ti.

Mahāgovindapabbajjā
mula_english:
“Then, the *brāhmaṇa* Great Steward went to his forty equal wives and said: ‘Whichever of you ladies wishes to may go back to her own family (*ñātikulāni*) and seek another husband.
I mean to go forth from the household life (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ*) into homelessness.
After what Brahmā has told me about the stench of the world (*āmagandhe*), which cannot easily be overcome by one living the household life (*agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā*),
I will go forth from home (*agārasmā*) into homelessness.’
‘You alone are the kinsman we could wish for (*ñāti ñātikāmānaṃ*), the only husband we want (*bhattā bhattukāmānaṃ*).
If the Reverend Govinda goes forth from the household life (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ*) into homelessness (*pabbajissati*), we will do likewise (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma*). Wherever you go (*yā te gati*), we will follow (*sā no gati bhavissatī*).’”

Mahāgovindapabbajjā
commentary_pali:
325.Cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyoti sādisiyova cattārīsā bhariyā, aññā panassa tīsu vayesu nāṭakitthiyo bahukāyeva.

Mahāgovindapabbajjāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo" means forty wives similar to her. That is, forty wives similar to Sādisī, but he had many actresses in his three periods of life.

Explanation of the Great Govinda Renunciation

mula_pali: 326. ‘‘Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tassa sattāhassa accayena kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Pabbajitaṃ pana mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ satta ca rājāno khattiyā muddhāvasittā satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā satta ca nhātakasatāni cattārīsā ca bhariyā sādisiyo anekāni ca khattiyasahassāni anekāni ca brāhmaṇasahassāni anekāni ca gahapatisahassāni anekehi ca itthāgārehi itthiyo kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitaṃ anupabbajiṃsu. Tāya sudaṃ, bho, parisāya parivuto mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo gāmanigamarājadhānīsu cārikaṃ carati. Yaṃ kho pana, bho, tena samayena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upasaṅkamati, tattha rājāva hoti raññaṃ, brahmāva brāhmaṇānaṃ, devatāva gahapatikānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena manussā khipanti vā upakkhalanti vā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘namatthu mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa, namatthu satta purohitassā’’’ti.
mula_english:
326. Then, the great steward, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda, at the end of those seven days, having shaved off his hair and beard, donned yellow robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness.

And with the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda who had gone forth, went forth the seven anointed *Kṣatriya* kings, the seven wealthy and distinguished *brāhmaṇas*, the seven hundred advanced pupils, his forty equal wives, several thousand *Kṣatriyas*, several thousand *brāhmaṇas*, several thousand householders, even some harem-women, having shaved off their hair and beards and donned yellow robes, following the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda from the household life into homelessness.

Surrounded by that assembly, the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda traveled on tour through villages, towns, and capital cities.

And whenever at that time the *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda would approach a village or town, he was like a king to kings, like Brahmā to the *brāhmaṇas*, like a deity to householders.

And in those days, whenever people sneezed or stumbled, they would say: ‘Praise be to the great *brāhmaṇa* Mahāgovinda! Praise be to the Minister of Seven!’
commentary_pali: 326.Cārikaṃ caratīti gāmanigamapaṭipāṭiyā cārikaṃ carati, gatagataṭṭhāne buddhakolāhalaṃ viya hoti. Manussā ‘‘mahāgovindapaṇḍito kira āgacchatī’’ti sutvā puretarameva maṇḍapaṃ kāretvā maggaṃ alaṅkaritvā paccuggantvā gaṇhitvā enti, mahālābhasakkāro mahogho viya ajjhottharanto uppajji. Sattapurohitassāti sattannaṃ rājūnaṃ purohitassa. Iti yathā etarahi evarūpesu vā ṭhānesu kismiñcideva dukkhe uppanne ‘‘namo buddhassā’’ti vadanti, evaṃ tadā ‘‘namatthu mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa, namatthu sattapurohitassā’’ti vadanti.
commentary_english:
326. *cārikaṃ caratī* means he wanders as a mendicant monk in due order from village to village and town to town; at each place he goes, it is like a *buddhakolāhalaṃ*.

People, having heard that "the great learned Govinda is coming," build a pavilion well in advance, decorate the road, go out to meet him, and take him in. A great wave of gain and honor arose, overwhelming [them].

*sattapurohitassā* means the chaplain of seven kings.

Just as now, when some suffering arises in such places, people say, "Homage to the Buddha (*namo buddhassa*)!" so then they would say, "Homage to the great Govinda, the Brahman (*namatthu mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa*), homage to the chaplain of seven (*namatthu sattapurohitassā*)!"

mula_pali: 327. ‘‘Mahāgovindo, bho, brāhmaṇo mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihāsi, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā…pe… abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi sāvakānañca brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesi.
mula_english:
327. ‘The great Govinda, sir, the *brāhmaṇa* abided, having suffused one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness (*mettā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth.

Thus, above, below, across, everywhere, in its entirety, he abided, having suffused the all-encompassing world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will.

With a mind accompanied by compassion (*karuṇā*)…pe… with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy (*muditā*)…pe… with a mind accompanied by equanimity (*upekkhā*)…pe… having suffused (the world) with freedom from ill-will (*abyāpajjena*), he abided, and he taught his disciples the path to fellowship with the Brahma-world (*brahmaloka*).
commentary_pali: 327.Mettāsahagatenātiādinā nayena pāḷiyaṃ brahmavihārāva āgatā, mahāpuriso pana sabbāpi aṭṭha samāpattiyo ca pañca ca abhiññāyo nibbattesi. Sāvakānañca brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesīti brahmaloke brahmunā sahabhāvāya maggaṃ kathesi.
commentary_english: 327. mettāsahagatenā etc., in this way, in the Pāli [text], the *brahmavihāras* have come. The great man, however, developed all eight *samāpattis* and the five *abhiññās*. sāvakānañca brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesī, that is, he taught the path to companionship in the world of Brahmā; he spoke of the path to being together with Brahmā in the world of Brahmā.

mula_pali: 328. ‘‘Ye kho pana, bho, tena samayena mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa sāvakā sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsu. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ brahmalokaṃ upapajjiṃsu. Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsu, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā appekacce paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce tusitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce yāmānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; ye sabbanihīnaṃ kāyaṃ paripūresuṃ te gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūresuṃ. Iti kho, bho pana (syā. ka.), sabbesaṃyeva tesaṃ kulaputtānaṃ amoghā pabbajjā ahosi avañjhā saphalā saudrayā’’’ti.
mula_english: ‘“And all those who had at that time been the Great Steward’s pupils and had fully mastered his teaching, they, at the breaking up of the body after death, were reborn in a happy sphere, in the Brahma-world (brahmalokaṃ upapajjiṃsu). And those who had not fully mastered his teaching were reborn either among the Paranimmita-Vasavatti *devas*, among the Nimmanarati *devas*, among the Tusita *devas*, among the Yama *devas*, among the *devas* of the Thirty-Three Gods, or among the *devas* of the Four Great Kings. And the very lowest realm that any of them attained was that of the *gandharbas*. Thus the going-forth of all those people was not fruitless or barren, but productive of fruit and profit."’
commentary_pali: 328.Sabbenasabbanti ye aṭṭha ca samāpattiyo pañca ca abhiññāyo nibbattesuṃ. Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsūti ye aṭṭhasu samāpattīsu ekasamāpattimpi na jāniṃsu, na sakkhiṃsu nibbattetuṃ. Amoghāti savipākā. Avañjhāti na vañjhā. Sabbanihīnaṃ pasavanti gandhabbakāyaṃ pasavi. Saphalāti avasesadevalokūpapattīhi sātthā. Saudrayāti brahmalokūpapattiyā savuḍḍhi.
commentary_english:
328.
"With all, all"—those who have acquired the eight attainments (aṭṭha ca samāpattiyo) and the five superknowledges (pañca ca abhiññāyo).
"Those who did not understand all, in all, the teaching (ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsū)"—those who did not understand even one attainment among the eight attainments (aṭṭhasu samāpattīsu), and were not able to acquire it.
"Not vain (amoghā)"—with results (savipākā).
"Not barren (avañjhā)"—not barren (na vañjhā).
They bring forth all that is inferior, they beget a *gandharva*-body.
p. 2.
0237 pasavi.
"Fruitful (saphalā)"—meaningful (sātthā) through the remaining heavenly-world rebirths (avasesadevalokūpapattīhi).
"With the voice of Brahmā (saudrayā)"—with growth (savuḍḍhi) through rebirth in the Brahmā world (brahmalokūpapattiyā).

mula_pali:
329. ‘‘Sarati taṃ bhagavā’’ti? ‘‘Sarāmahaṃ, pañcasikha. Ahaṃ tena samayena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo ahosiṃ. Ahaṃ tesaṃ sāvakānaṃ brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesiṃ. Taṃ kho pana me, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, yāvadeva brahmalokūpapattiyā.

Idaṃ kho pana me, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamañca taṃ, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ kho taṃ, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.
mula_english:
329. “Do you remember that, Blessed One?”

“I remember, Pañcasikha. At that time, I was the brāhmaṇa Mahāgovinda. I taught those disciples the path to union with the Brahma-world (brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesiṃ). However, Pañcasikha, that holy life does not lead to dis-enchantment (*nirvidā*), to dispassion (*virāga*), to cessation (*nirodha*), to peace (*upaśama*), to super-knowledge (*abhijñā*), to enlightenment (*sambodha*), to *Nirvāṇa* (*nirvāṇa*), but only to birth in the Brahma-world (*brahmalokūpapattiyā*).

Now, Pañcasikha, my holy life leads unfailingly to disenchantment (*ekantanirvidā*), to dispassion (*virāga*), to cessation (*nirodha*), to peace (*upaśama*), to super-knowledge (*abhijñā*), to enlightenment (*sambodha*), to *Nirvāṇa* (*nirvāṇa*). And what, Pañcasikha, is that holy life which leads unfailingly to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to super-knowledge, to enlightenment, to *Nirvāṇa*? Just this very noble eightfold path (*ariyam aṣṭāṅgikaḥ margaḥ*): namely right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*), right thought (*samyaksaṃkalpa*); right speech (*samyagvāc*), right action (*samyakkarmānta*), right livelihood (*samyagājīva*); right effort (*samyagvyāyāma*), right mindfulness (*samyaksmṛti*), right concentration (*samyaksamādhi*). This, Pañcasikha, is the holy life that leads unfailingly to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to super-knowledge, to enlightenment, to *Nirvāṇa*.
commentary_pali:
329.Sarāmahanti sarāmi ahaṃ pañcasikha, iminā kira padena ayaṃ suttanto buddhabhāsito nāma jāto. Na nibbidāyāti na vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāya. Na virāgāyāti na vaṭṭe virāgatthāya. Na nirodhāyāti na vaṭṭassa nirodhatthāya. Na upasamāyāti na vaṭṭassa upasamanatthāya. Na abhiññāyāti na vaṭṭaṃ abhijānanatthāya. Na sambodhāyāti na kilesaniddāvigamena vaṭṭato pabujjhanatthāya. Na nibbānāyāti na amatanibbānatthāya.

Ekantanibbidāyāti ekantameva vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāya. Ettha pana nibbidāyāti vipassanā. Virāgāyāti maggo. Nirodhāya upasamāyāti nibbānaṃ. Abhiññāya sambodhāyāti maggo. Nibbānāyāti nibbānameva. Evaṃ ekasmiṃ ṭhāne vipassanā, tīsu maggo, tīsu nibbānaṃ vuttanti evaṃ vavatthānakathā veditabbā. Pariyāyena pana sabbānipetāni maggavevacanānipi nibbānavevacanānipi hontiyeva. Sammādiṭṭhiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimagge saccavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttameva.

Ekantanibbidāyā nibbidāyā Virāgāyā Nirodhāya upasamāyā Abhiññāya sambodhāyā Nibbānāyā Sammādiṭṭhi
commentary_english:
329.
"Sarāmaha," [means] I remember Pañcasikha; by this word, this *suttanta* called "spoken by the Buddha" came to be.
"Not for revulsion," [means] not in Vaṭṭa for the sake of causing revulsion.
"Not for detachment," [means] not in Vaṭṭa for the sake of detachment.
"Not for cessation," [means] not in Vaṭṭa for the sake of cessation (*nirodha*).
"Not for appeasement," [means] not in Vaṭṭa for the sake of appeasement.
"Not for direct knowledge," [means] not in Vaṭṭa for the sake of direct knowing.
"Not for awakening," [means] not through the passing away of the sleep of defilements, from Vaṭṭa, for the sake of awakening (*sambodha*).
"Not for *nirvāṇa*," [means] not for the sake of deathlessness-*nirvāṇa*.

"Solely for revulsion," [means] solely in Vaṭṭa for the sake of causing revulsion.
Here, however, "for revulsion" means insight (*vipaśyanā*).
"For detachment" means the path (*mārga*).
"For cessation, for appeasement" means *nirvāṇa*.
"For direct knowledge, for awakening" means the path.
"For *nirvāṇa*" means *nirvāṇa* itself.
Thus, in one instance, insight; in three, the path; in three, *nirvāṇa* is said; thus, this discourse on determination should be understood.
Moreover, by way of exposition, all these are synonyms of the path and synonyms of *nirvāṇa*.
What should be stated regarding right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*) and so forth has already been stated in the *Visuddhimagga* in the section on truth.

Solely for revulsion, for revulsion, for detachment, for cessation and appeasement, for direct knowledge and awakening, for *nirvāṇa*,
right view.

mula_pali:
330. ‘‘Ye kho pana me, pañcasikha, sāvakā sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, te āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti; ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, te pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā honti tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, appekacce tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino honti sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti karonti (sī. pī.). Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, appekacce tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā honti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Iti kho, pañcasikha, sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ kulaputtānaṃ amoghā pabbajjā pabbajā ahosi (ka.) avañjhā saphalā saudrayā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano pañcasikho gandhabbaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Mahāgovindasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
330. And those of my disciples, Pañcasikha, who fully understand my teaching, realize for themselves, through direct knowledge, in this very life, the uncorrupted freedom of mind (*cetovimutti*) and freedom through wisdom (*paññāvimutti*), having eliminated the corruptions (*āsavānaṃ khayā*). And those who do not fully understand the teaching, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (*pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) will be reborn spontaneously (*opapātikā*) and will attain final emancipation (*parinibbāyino*) there, not returning from that world, their nature being not to return (*anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā*).

Those who do not fully understand the teaching, some, through the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion (*rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā*), become once-returners (*sakadāgāmino*), and having come to this world only once (*sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā*), will make an end of suffering (*dukkhassantaṃ karissanti*).

Those who do not fully understand the teaching, some, through the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*), become stream-winners (*sotāpannā*), their nature being not to fall into states of woe (*avinipātadhammā*), assured (*niyatā*) and destined for full enlightenment (*sambodhiparāyaṇā*).

Thus, Pañcasikha, for all these sons of good families (*kulaputtānaṃ*), the going forth (*pabbajjā*) is not in vain (*amoghā*), not fruitless (*avañjhā*), but fruitful (*saphalā*), and yielding happiness (*saudrayā*)’’.

This is what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.

Pleased, Pañcasikha, the gandharva's son (*gandhabbaputto*), having rejoiced in the Blessed One's words (*bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā*), and having saluted the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā*), circumambulated him to the right (*padakkhiṇaṃ katvā*) and vanished from there (*tatthevantaradhāyīti*).

The Mahāgovindasutta, the sixth, is concluded (*mahāgovindasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
330.Ye na sabbenasabbanti ye cattāropi ariyamagge paripūretuṃ na jānanti, tīṇi vā dve vā ekaṃ vā nibbattenti. Sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ kulaputtānanti brahmacariyaciṇṇakulaputtānaṃ. Amoghā…pe… saphalā saudrayāti arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi.

Bhagavantaṃabhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvāti (dī. ni. 2.188) bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ cittena sampaṭicchanto abhinanditvā vācāya pasaṃsamāno anumoditvā mahantaṃ añjaliṃ sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā pasannalākhārase nimujjamāno viya dasabalassa chabbaṇṇarasmijālantaraṃ pavisitvā catūsu ṭhānesu vanditvā tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā bhagavantaṃ abhitthavanto abhitthavanto satthu purato antaradhāyitvā attano devalokameva agamāsīti.

Bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Mahāgovindasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
330. "Because they are not all in every way" means that they do not know how to fully complete the four noble paths, or they produce three, two, or one.

"Of all these sons of good family" means of sons of good family who have practiced the holy life (brahmacarya).

"Not in vain... successful, with happiness" he concluded the teaching with the pinnacle of arahantship.

Having bowed down to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) and circumambulated him (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā) (D. II. 188), accepting the Blessed One's teaching with his mind, rejoicing, praising with his voice, approving, placing a large añjali on his head, as if diving into pleasant lac juice, entering into the web of six-colored rays of the Ten-Powered One, having paid homage in the four places, having circumambulated three times, praising and extolling the Blessed One, he disappeared in front of the Teacher and went to his own heaven.

Having bowed down to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) and circumambulated him (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā)

Here ends the Mahāgovindasuttavaṇṇanā in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, commentary to the Dīghanikāya.

mula_pali: 331. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Atha kho catunnaṃ suddhāvāsakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ devānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Yaṃnūna mayampi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike paccekaṃ gāthaṃ paccekagāthaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), paccekagāthā (ka. sī.) bhāseyyāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
331. Thus have I heard: On one occasion the Blessed One (Bhagavān) was dwelling among the Śākyas at Kapilavatthu in the Great Forest, together with a large Saṅgha of approximately five hundred monks, all of them *arhats*. And most of the *devatās* from ten world-systems had gathered in order to see the Blessed One & the Saṅgha of monks.

Then the thought occurred to four *devatās* of the ranks from the Pure Abodes: “The Blessed One (Bhagavān) is dwelling among the Śākyas at Kapilavatthu in the Great Forest, together with a large Saṅgha of about five hundred monks, all of them *arhats*. And most of the *devatās* from ten world-systems have gathered in order to see the Blessed One & the Saṅgha of monks.

Let us also approach the Blessed One (Bhagavān) and, on arrival, let us each speak a verse (gāthā) in his presence.”
commentary_pali:
331.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsamayasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamapubbapadavaṇṇanā – sakkesūti ambaṭṭhasutte vuttena uppattinayena ‘‘sakyā vata, bho kumārā’’ti udānaṃ paṭicca sakkāti laddhanāmānaṃ rājakumārānaṃ nivāso ekopi janapado ruḷhīsaddena ‘‘sakkā’’ti vuccati, tasmiṃ sakkesu janapade. Mahāvaneti sayaṃjāte aropite himavantena saddhiṃ ekābaddhe mahati vane. Sabbeheva arahantehīti imaṃ suttaṃ kathitadivaseyeva pattaarahattehi.

Tatrāyaṃ anupubbikathā – sākiyakoliyā kira kapilavatthunagarassa ca koliyanagarassa ca antare rohiṇiṃ nāma nadiṃ ekeneva āvaraṇena bandhāpetvā sassāni karonti, atha jeṭṭhamūlamāse sassesu milāyantesu ubhayanagaravāsikānampi kammakarā sannipatiṃsu. Tattha koliyanagaravāsino āhaṃsu – ‘‘idaṃ udakaṃ ubhato hariyamānaṃ na tumhākaṃ na amhākaṃ pahossati, amhākaṃ pana sassaṃ ekena udakeneva nipphajjissati, idaṃ udakaṃ amhākaṃ dethā’’ti. Kapilavatthunagaravāsino āhaṃsu – ‘‘tumhesu koṭṭhe pūretvā ṭhitesu mayaṃ rattasuvaṇṇanīlamaṇikāḷakahāpaṇe ca gahetvā pacchipasibbakādihatthā na sakkhissāma tumhākaṃ gharadvāre vicarituṃ, amhākampi sassaṃ ekeneva udakena nipphajjissati, idaṃ udakaṃ amhākaṃ dethā’’ti. ‘‘Na mayaṃ dassāmā’’ti. ‘‘Mayampi na dassāmā’’ti. Evaṃ kalahaṃ vaḍḍhetvā eko uṭṭhāya ekassa pahāraṃ adāsi, sopi aññassāti evaṃ aññamaññaṃ paharitvā rājakulānaṃ jātiṃ ghaṭṭetvā kalahaṃ vaḍḍhayiṃsu.

Koliyakammakarā vadanti – ‘‘tumhe kapilavatthuvāsike gahetvā gajjatha, ye soṇasiṅgālādayo viya attano bhaginīhi saddhiṃ saṃvasiṃsu. Etesaṃ hatthino ca assā ca phalakāvudhāni ca amhākaṃ kiṃ karissantī’’ti? Sākiyakammakarāpi vadanti – ‘‘tumhe dāni kuṭṭhino dārake gahetvā gajjatha, ye anāthā niggatikā tiracchānā viya kolarukkhe vasiṃsu, etesaṃ hatthino ca assā ca phalakāvudhāni ca amhākaṃ kiṃ karissantī’’ti? Te gantvā tasmiṃ kamme niyuttaamaccānaṃ kathesuṃ, amaccā rājakulānaṃ kathesuṃ, tato sākiyā – ‘‘bhaginīhi saddhiṃ saṃvāsikānaṃ thāmañca balañca dassessāmā’’ti yuddhasajjā nikkhamiṃsu. Koliyāpi – ‘‘kolarukkhavāsīnaṃ thāmañca balañca dassessāmā’’ti yuddhasajjā nikkhamiṃsu.

Bhagavāpi rattiyā paccūsasamayeva mahākaruṇāsamāpattito vuṭṭhāya lokaṃ volokento ime evaṃ yuddhasajje nikkhamante addasa. Disvā – ‘‘mayi gate ayaṃ kalaho vūpasamissati nu kho udāhu no’’ti upadhārento – ‘‘ahamettha gantvā kalahavūpasamanatthaṃ tīṇi jātakāni kathessāmi, tato kalaho vūpasamissati. Atha sāmaggidīpanatthāya dve jātakāni kathetvā attadaṇḍasuttaṃ desessāmi. Desanaṃ sutvā ubhayanagaravāsinopi aḍḍhatiyāni aḍḍhatiyāni kumārasatāni dassanti, ahaṃ te pabbajissāmi, tadā mahāsamāgamo bhavissatī’’ti sanniṭṭhānamakāsi. Tasmā imesu yuddhasajjesu nikkhamantesu kassaci anārocetvā sayameva pattacīvaramādāya gantvā dvinnaṃ senānaṃ antare ākāse pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo vissajjetvā nisīdi.

attadaṇḍasuttaṃ

Kapilavatthuvāsino bhagavantaṃ disvāva – ‘‘amhākaṃ ñātiseṭṭho satthā āgato, diṭṭho nu kho tena amhākaṃ kalahakāraṇabhāvo’’ti cintetvā – ‘‘na kho pana sakkā bhagavati āgate amhehi parassa sarīre satthaṃ pātetuṃ, koliyanagaravāsino amhe hanantu vā pacantu vā’’ti āvudhāni chaḍḍetvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā nisīdiṃsu. Koliyanagaravāsinopi tatheva cintetvā āvudhāni chaḍḍetvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā nisīdiṃsu.

Bhagavā jānantova – ‘‘kasmā āgatattha mahārājā’’ti pucchi. Bhagavā, na titthakīḷāya na pabbatakīḷāya na nadīkīḷāya na giridassanatthaṃ, imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne saṅgāmaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā āgatamhāti. Kiṃ nissāya vo kalaho mahārājāti? Udakaṃ, bhanteti. Udakaṃ kiṃ agghati mahārājāti? Appagghaṃ, bhanteti. Pathavī nāma kiṃ agghati mahārājāti? Anagghā, bhanteti. Khattiyā kiṃ agghanti mahārājāti? Khattiyā nāma anagghā bhanteti. Appamūlakaṃ udakaṃ nissāya kimatthaṃ anagghe khattiye nāsetha, mahārājāti? ‘‘Kalahe assādo nāma natthi, kalahavasena mahārājā aṭṭhāne veraṃ katvā ekāya rukkhadevatāya kāḷasīhena saddhiṃ baddhāghāto sakalampi imaṃ kappaṃ anuppattoyevā’’ti vatvā phandanajātakaṃ kathesi. Tato ‘‘parapattiyena nāma mahārājā na bhavitabbaṃ. Parapattiyā hutvā hi ekassa sasakassa kathāya tiyojanasahassavitthate himavante catuppadagaṇā mahāsamuddaṃ pakkhandino ahesuṃ. Tasmā parapattiyena na bhavitabba’’nti vatvā pathavīundriyajātakaṃ kathesi. Tato – ‘‘kadāci, mahārājā, dubbalopi mahabbalassa randhaṃ vivaraṃ passati, kadāci mahabbalo dubbalassa. Laṭukikāpi hi sakuṇikā hatthināgaṃ ghātesī’’ti vatvā laṭukikajātakaṃ kathesi. Evaṃ kalahavūpasamatthāya tīṇi jātakāni kathetvā sāmaggiparidīpanatthāya dve jātakāni kathesi. Kathaṃ? Samaggānañhi mahārājā koci otāraṃ nāma passituṃ na sakkotīti vatvā rukkhadhammajātakaṃ kathesi. Tato ‘‘samaggānaṃ mahārājā koci vivaraṃ passituṃ nāsakkhi. Yadā pana aññamaññaṃ vivādamakaṃsu, atha te nesādaputto jīvitā voropetvā ādāya gato. Vivāde assādo nāma natthī’’ti vatvā vaṭṭakajātakaṃ kathesi. Evaṃ imāni pañca jātakāni kathetvā avasāne attadaṇḍasuttaṃ kathesi.

phandanajātakaṃ pathavīundriyajātakaṃ laṭukikajātakaṃ rukkhadhammajātakaṃ vaṭṭakajātakaṃ

Rājāno pasannā – ‘‘sace satthā nāgamissa, mayaṃ sahatthā aññamaññaṃyeva vadhitvā lohitanadiṃ pavattayissāma, amhākaṃ puttabhātaro gehadvāre na passeyyāma, sāsanapaṭisāsanampi no āharaṇako na bhavissati. Satthāraṃ nissāya no jīvitaṃ laddhaṃ. Sace pana satthā agāraṃ ajjhāvasissa, dvisahassadīpaparivāresu catūsu mahādīpesu rajjamassa hatthagataṃ abhavissa, atirekasahassaṃ kho panassa puttā abhavissaṃsu, tato khattiyaparivārova avicarissa. Taṃ kho panesa sampattiṃ pahāya nikkhamitvā sambodhiṃ patto, idānipi khattiyaparivāroyeva vicaratū’’ti ubhayanagaravāsino aḍḍhatiyāni aḍḍhatiyāni kumārasatāni adaṃsu. Bhagavā te pabbājetvā mahāvanaṃ agamāsi. Tesaṃ garugāravavasena na attano ruciyā pabbajitānaṃ anabhirati uppajji. Purāṇadutiyikāyopi nesaṃ ‘‘ayyaputtā ukkaṇṭhantu, gharāvāso na saṇṭhātī’’tiādīni vatvā sāsanaṃ pesenti. Te atirekataraṃ ukkaṇṭhiṃsu.

Bhagavā āvajjanto tesaṃ anabhiratabhāvaṃ ñatvā ‘‘ime bhikkhū mādisena buddhena saddhiṃ ekato vasantā ukkaṇṭhanti, handa nesaṃ kuṇāladahassa vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā tattha netvā anabhiratiṃ vinodessāmī’’ti kuṇāladahassa vaṇṇaṃ kathesi. Te taṃ daṭṭhukāmā ahesuṃ. Daṭṭhukāmattha, bhikkhave, kuṇāladahanti? Āma bhagavāti. Yadi evaṃ, etha, gacchāmāti. Iddhimantānaṃ bhagavā gamanaṭṭhānaṃ mayaṃ kathaṃ gamissāmāti? Tumhe gantukāmā hotha, ahaṃ mamānubhāvena gahetvā gamissāmīti. Sādhu, bhanteti. Atha bhagavā pañca bhikkhusatāni gahetvā ākāse uppatitvā kuṇāladahe patiṭṭhāya te bhikkhū āha – ‘‘bhikkhave, imasmiṃ kuṇāladahe yesaṃ macchānaṃ nāmaṃ na jānātha, tesaṃ nāmaṃ pucchathā’’ti.

Te pucchiṃsu, bhagavā pucchitapucchitaṃ kathesi. Na kevalaṃ macchānaṃyeva, tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe rukkhānampi pabbatapāde dvipadacatuppadasakuṇānampi nāmāni pucchāpetvā kathesi. Atha dvīhi sakuṇehi mukhatuṇḍakena ḍaṃsitvā gahitadaṇḍake nisinno kuṇālasakuṇarājā purato pacchato ubhosu passesu sakuṇasaṅghaparivuto āgacchati. Bhikkhū taṃ disvā – ‘‘esa, bhante, imesaṃ sakuṇānaṃ rājā bhavissati, parivārā ete etassā’’ti maññāmāti. Evameva, bhikkhave, ayampi mama vaṃso mama paveṇīti. Idāni tāva mayaṃ, bhante, ete sakuṇe passāma. Yaṃ pana bhagavā ‘‘ayampi mama vaṃso mama paveṇī’’ti āha, taṃ sotukāmamhāti. Sotukāmattha bhikkhaveti? Āma, bhagavāti. Tena hi suṇāthāti tīhi gāthāsatehi maṇḍetvā kuṇālajātakaṃ kathento anabhiratiṃ vinodesi. Desanāpariyosāne sabbepi sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahiṃsu, maggeneva ca nesaṃ iddhipi āgatā. Bhagavā – ‘‘hotu tāva ettakaṃ etesaṃ bhikkhūna’’nti ākāse uppatitvā mahāvanameva agamāsi. Tepi bhikkhū gamanakāle dasabalassa ānubhāvena gantvā āgamanakāle attano ānubhāvena bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā mahāvane otariṃsu.

kuṇālajātakaṃ

Bhagavā paññattāsane nisīditvā te bhikkhū āmantetvā – ‘‘etha, bhikkhave, nisīdatha, uparimaggattayavajjhānaṃ vo kilesānaṃ pahānāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathessāmī’’ti kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathesi. Bhikkhū cintesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā amhākaṃ anabhiratabhāvaṃ ñatvā kuṇāladahaṃ netvā anabhiratiṃ vinodesi, tattha sotāpattiphalappattānaṃ no idāni idha tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ adāsi, na kho panamhehi ‘sotāpannā maya’nti vītināmetuṃ vaṭṭati, uttamapurisasadisehi no bhavituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti te dasabalassa pāde vanditvā uṭṭhāya nisīdanaṃ papphoṭetvā visuṃ visuṃ pabbhārarukkhamūlesu nisīdiṃsu.

Bhagavā cintesi – ‘‘ime bhikkhū pakatiyāpi avissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhānā, laddhupāyassa pana bhikkhuno kilamanakāraṇaṃ nāma natthi. Gacchantā gacchantā ca vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ patvā – ‘‘attanā attanā paṭiladdhaguṇaṃ ārocessāmā’ti mama santikaṃ āgamissanti. Etesu āgatesu dasasahassacakkavāḷe devatā ekacakkavāḷe sannipatissanti, mahāsamayo bhavissati, vivitte okāse mayā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti. Tato vivitte okāse buddhāsanaṃ paññapetvā nisīdi.

Sabbapaṭhamaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā gatathero saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Tato aparo tato aparoti pañcasatāpi paduminiyaṃ padumāni viya vikasiṃsu. Sabbapaṭhamaṃ arahattappattabhikkhu – ‘‘bhagavato ārocessāmī’’ti pallaṅkaṃ vinibbhujitvā nisīdanaṃ papphoṭetvā uṭṭhāya dasabalābhimukho ahosi. Evaṃ aparopi aparopīti pañcasatāpi bhattasālaṃ pavisantā viya paṭipāṭiyāva āgamaṃsu. Paṭhamaṃ āgato vanditvā nisīdanaṃ paññapetvā ekamantaṃ nisīditvā paṭiladdhaguṇaṃ ārocetukāmo – ‘‘atthi nu kho añño koci, natthī’’ti nivattitvā āgamanamaggaṃ olokento aparampi addasa aparampi addasa. Iti sabbepi te āgantvā ekamantaṃ nisīditvā ayaṃ imassa harāyamāno na kathesi, ayaṃ imassa harāyamāno na kathesīti. Khīṇāsavānaṃ kira dve ākārā honti – ‘‘aho vata mayā paṭiladdhaguṇaṃ sadevako loko khippameva paṭivijjheyyā’’ti cittaṃ uppajjati. Paṭiladdhabhāvaṃ pana nidhiladdhapuriso viya na aññassa ārocetukāmo hoti.

Evaṃ osīdamatte pana tasmiṃ ariyamaṇḍale pācīnayugandharaparikkhepato abbhā, mahikā, dhūmo, rajo, rāhūti imehi upakkilesehi vippamuttaṃ buddhuppādapaṭimaṇḍitassa lokassa rāmaṇeyyakadassanatthaṃ pācīnadisāya ukkhittarajatamayamahāādāsamaṇḍalaṃ viya, nemivaṭṭiyaṃ gahetvā parivattiyamānarajatacakkasassirikaṃ puṇṇacandamaṇḍalaṃ ullaṅghitvā anilapathaṃ paṭipajjittha. Iti evarūpe khaṇe laye muhutte bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi.

Tattha bhagavāpi mahāsammatassa vaṃse uppanno, tepi pañcasatā bhikkhū mahāsammatassa kule uppannā. Bhagavāpi khattiyagabbhe jāto, tepi khattiyagabbhe jātā. Bhagavāpi rājapabbajito, tepi rājapabbajitā. Bhagavāpi setacchattaṃ pahāya hatthagataṃ cakkavattirajjaṃ nissajjetvā pabbajito, tepi setacchattaṃ pahāya hatthagatāni rajjāni nissajjetvā pabbajitā. Iti bhagavā parisuddhe okāse parisuddhe rattibhāge sayaṃ parisuddho parisuddhaparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāro vītadoso vītadosaparivāro vītamoho vītamohaparivāro nittaṇho nittaṇhaparivāro nikkileso nikkilesaparivāro santo santaparivāro danto dantaparivāro mutto muttaparivāro ativiya virocatīti. Vaṇṇabhūmi nāmesā, yattakaṃ sakkoti, tattakaṃ vattabbaṃ. Iti ime bhikkhū sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehī’’ti.

Yebhuyyenāti bahutarā sannipatitā, mandā na sannipatitā asaññā arūpāvacaradevatā samāpannadevatā ca. Tatrāyaṃ sannipātakkamo mahāvanassa kira sāmantā devatā caliṃsu – ‘‘āyāma, bho buddhadassanaṃ nāma bahūpakāraṃ, dhammassavanaṃ bahūpakāraṃ, bhikkhusaṅghadassanaṃ bahūpakāraṃ, āyāma āyāmā’’ti mahāsaddaṃ kurumānā āgantvā bhagavantañca taṃmuhuttaṃ arahattappattakhīṇāsave ca vanditvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu.
