Eteneva upāyena tāsaṃ tāsaṃ saddaṃ sutvā saddantaraaḍḍhagāvutagāvutaaḍḍhayojanayojanādivasena tiyojanasahassavitthate himavante, tikkhattuṃ tesaṭṭhiyā nagarasahassesu, navanavutiyā doṇamukhasatasahassesu, channavutiyā paṭṭanakoṭisatasahassesu, chapaṇṇāsāya ratanākaresūti sakalajambudīpe, pubbavidehe, aparagoyāne, uttarakurumhi, dvīsu parittadīpasahassesūti sakalacakkavāḷe, tato dutiyatatiyacakkavāḷeti evaṃ dasasahassacakkavāḷesu devatā sannipatitāti veditabbā. Dasasahassacakkavāḷañhi idha dasalokadhātuyoti adhippetā. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā hontī’’ti.

Yebhuyyenā

Evaṃ sannipatitāhi devatāhi sakalacakkavāḷagabbhaṃ yāva brahmalokā sūcighare nirantaraṃ pakkhittasūcīhi viya paripuṇṇaṃ hoti. Tatra brahmalokassa evaṃ uccattanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Lohapāsāde kira sattakūṭāgārasamo pāsāṇo brahmaloke ṭhatvā adho khitto catūhi māsehi pathaviṃ pāpuṇāti. Evaṃ mahante okāse yathā heṭṭhā ṭhatvā khittāni pupphāni vā dhūmo vā upari gantuṃ, upari vā ṭhatvā khittasāsapā heṭṭhā otarituṃ antaraṃ na labhanti, evaṃ nirantaraṃ devatā ahesuṃ. Yathā kho pana cakkavattirañño nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ asambādhaṃ hoti, āgatāgatā mahesakkhā khattiyā okāsaṃ labhantiyeva, parato parato pana atisambādhaṃ hoti, evameva bhagavato nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ asambādhaṃ, āgatāgatā mahesakkhā devatā ca mahābrahmāno ca okāsaṃ labhantiyeva. Apisudaṃ bhagavato āsannāsannaṭṭhāne mahāparinibbāne vuttanayeneva vālaggakoṭinitudanamatte padese dasapi vīsampi sabbaparato tiṃsampi devatā sukhume sukhume attabhāve māpetvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Saṭṭhi saṭṭhi devatā aṭṭhaṃsu.

Suddhāvāsakāyikānanti suddhāvāsavāsīnaṃ. Suddhāvāsā nāma suddhānaṃ anāgāmikhīṇāsavānaṃ āvāsā pañca brahmalokā. Etadahosīti kasmā ahosi? Te kira brahmāno samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā yathāparicchedena vuṭṭhitā brahmabhavanaṃ olokentā pacchābhatte bhattagehaṃ viya suññataṃ addasaṃsu. Tato ‘‘kuhiṃ brahmāno gatā’’ti āvajjantā mahāsamāgamaṃ ñatvā – ‘‘ayaṃ samāgamo mahā, mayaṃ ohīnā, ohīnakānaṃ okāso dullabho hoti, tasmā gacchantā atucchahatthā hutvā ekekaṃ gāthaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā gacchāma. Tāya mahāsamāgame ca attano āgatabhāvaṃ jānāpessāma, dasabalassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsissāmā’’ti. Iti tesaṃ samāpattito vuṭṭhāya āvajjitattā etadahosi.

Suddhāvāsakāyikāna Suddhāvāsā Etadahosī
commentary_english:
331. Thus have I heard: the Mahāsamayasutta. Here follows an explanation of the words in due order: *Sakkesū* refers to a region inhabited by princes of the Sakya clan, who, as is stated in the Ambaṭṭhasutta according to the narrative of their origin, were called “*Sakkā*” after they exclaimed, “The Sakyas are indeed capable, good sir!” In that Sakya country; *Mahāvane* means in a great forest that was self-grown and planted, united with the Himavant. *Sabbeheva arahantehī* refers to this sutta (which) was spoken on the very day when they attained arahantship. Here follows a preliminary narrative: It seems that the Sakiyas and Koliyas, having dammed up the river Rohiṇī between Kapilavatthu and Koliya with a single dam, were cultivating their crops. Then, in the month of Jeṭṭhamūla, when the crops were beginning to wither, laborers from both cities assembled. There the residents of Koliya said, “If this water is diverted to both sides, it will not be enough for you or for us. But our crops will ripen with a single watering. Therefore, let us have this water.” The residents of Kapilavatthu said, “After you have filled your storehouses, we will not be able to take ruddy gold, sapphires, and black *kahāpaṇas*, baskets and sacks in our hands, and go from house to house seeking favors at your hands. Our crops, too, will ripen with a single watering. Therefore, let us have this water.” “We will not give it to you.” “Neither will we give it to you.” Having thus increased the quarrel, one rose up and struck another a blow. The other also (struck) another. Thus, striking one another, they stirred up a quarrel by insulting the origin of the royal families. The laborers of the Koliyas said, “You take the Kapilavatthu residents and boast, you who have cohabited with your own sisters, like dogs and jackals. What can their elephants, horses, shields, and weapons do to us?” The laborers of the Sakiyas also said, “You lepers, take your children and boast, you who are destitute outcasts, living in jujube trees like animals. What can their elephants, horses, shields, and weapons do to us?” Having gone, they told the ministers appointed to that task; the ministers told the royal families. Then the Sakiyas, “We will show the strength and power of those who cohabit with their sisters!” armed for battle, they went forth. The Koliyas also, “We will show the strength and power of those who dwell in jujube trees!” armed for battle, they went forth. Then the Blessed One, arising at dawn from the attainment of great compassion, surveying the world, saw these (people) thus armed for battle, going forth. Having seen (them), considering, “Will this quarrel subside when I have gone, or not?” (he thought), “Having gone there, I will speak three *jātakas* for the subsiding of the quarrel; then the quarrel will subside. Then, for the purpose of showing harmony, having spoken two *jātakas*, I will teach the *Attadaṇḍasutta*. Hearing the teaching, the residents of both cities will give two and a half hundred young men each; I will ordain them; then there will be a great assembly,” he made a resolution. Therefore, without announcing (it) to anyone, taking his bowl and robe himself, having gone and folded his legs in the *pallaṅka* posture in the sky between the two armies, he sat down, emitting six-colored rays. *Attadaṇḍasuttaṃ* The residents of Kapilavatthu, having seen the Blessed One, “Our best kinsman, the Teacher, has come; has he seen the cause of our quarrel?” having thought, “It is not possible for us to hurl weapons at another’s body when the Blessed One has come,” casting aside their weapons, they worshiped the Blessed One and sat down. The residents of Koliyanagara also, having thought likewise, casting aside their weapons, worshiped the Blessed One and sat down. The Blessed One, knowing, asked, “Why have you come here, Great Kings?” (They replied), “Blessed One, not for the sake of bathing places, not for the sake of mountain sports, not for the sake of river sports, not for the sake of seeing the mountains, but in this place, having stirred up a battle, we have come.” “Relying on what is your quarrel, Great Kings?” “On water, Blessed One.” “What is the value of water, Great Kings?” “Little value, Blessed One.” “What is the value of the earth, Great Kings?” “Inestimable, Blessed One.” “What is the value of *khattiyas*, Great Kings?” “*Khattiyas* are inestimable, Blessed One.” “Relying on water of little value, why do you destroy *khattiyas* of inestimable value, Great Kings? In quarrels, there is no pleasure. Through the way of quarreling, Great Kings, having made enmity in an improper place, like a tree spirit bound by hatred toward a black lion, all. "Having reached this *kappa* in this way," he said, he told the *Phandanajātaka*. Then, "Great kings, one should certainly not rely on another. Relying on another, groups of quadrupeds in the Himavant, which extends for three thousand *yojanas*, stampeded to the great ocean because of the story of a single hare. Therefore, one should not rely on another," he said, he told the *Pathavīundriyajātaka*. Then – "Sometimes, great kings, even the weak see an opening, a loophole, of the powerful; sometimes the powerful see one of the weak. Even a quail killed an elephant," he said, he told the *Laṭukikajātaka*. Thus, having related three *Jātakas* to pacify the quarrel, he related two *Jātakas* to illuminate concord. How so? "Indeed, great kings, nobody is able to find an opportunity when there is concord," he said, he told the *Rukkhadhammajātaka*. Then, "Great kings, nobody was able to find an opening when there was concord. But when they made a dispute with each other, then a hunter’s son deprived them of life and went away, taking them. There is no taste in dispute," he said, he told the *Vaṭṭakajātaka*. Thus, having related these five *Jātakas*, at the end he told the *Attadaṇḍasutta*. *Phandanajātaka*, *Pathavīundriyajātaka*, *Laṭukikajātaka*, *Rukkhadhammajātaka*, *Vaṭṭakajātaka*. The delighted kings – "If the Teacher belongs to Nāgamiśra, we ourselves will kill each other with our own hands and cause a river of blood to flow; may we not see our sons and brothers at the door of our houses; may there be no one to bring us messages and counter-messages. Because of the Teacher we have received (back) our lives. If the Teacher were to dwell in a house, kingship in the four great continents with their two thousand island attendants would have come into his hand; he would have more than a thousand sons; then he would roam about with a royal retinue." The residents of both cities gave aḍḍhatiyāni aḍḍhatiyāni hundreds of princes. The Blessed One, having given them the going-forth, went to the Great Wood. Because of their regard for their teachers, discontent arose in those who had gone forth not according to their own liking. Even their former wives send them the message, "May your Reverences feel longing, household life is not stable," etc. They felt even more longing. The Blessed One, reflecting, knowing their state of discontent, (thought,) "These monks, dwelling together with a Buddha like me, feel longing; come, having described the beauty of the *Kuṇāladaha*, having led them there, I will dispel their discontent." He described the beauty of the *Kuṇāladaha*. They were desirous of seeing it. "Are you desirous of seeing the *Kuṇāladaha*, monks?" "Yes, Blessed One." "If so, come, let's go." "Blessed One, how will we, without psychic power, go to a place of going?" "You are desirous of going, I will take you and go by my power." "Good, venerable sir." Then the Blessed One, having taken five hundred monks, rose up into the sky and, having alighted at the *Kuṇāladaha*, said to those monks – "Monks, in this *Kuṇāladaha*, ask the names of the fish whose names you do not know." They asked, the Blessed One told (them) the names as they were asked. Not only of the fish, but also in that forest grove he had (them) ask and told (them) the names of the trees, at the foot of the mountain, of the bipeds, quadrupeds, and birds. Then a *Kuṇāla* bird-king, bitten on the mouth by two birds, sitting on a grasped stick, surrounded by a flock of birds, comes from the front, from the back, on both sides. The monks, seeing him, (said) – "This, venerable sir, will be the king of these birds, these are his retinue," we think. Just so, monks, this too is my lineage, my tradition. Now, revered sir, we are seeing these birds. Venerable sir, we want to hear what the Blessed One said: "This too is my lineage, my tradition." Monks, do you want to hear it? Yes, Blessed One. Then listen. Adorning it with three hundred verses, while relating the *Kuṇālajātaka*, he dispelled their discontent. At the end of the discourse, all were established in the fruit of stream-entry, and magical powers came to them along with the path itself. The Blessed One, thinking, "Let this much be enough for these monks," rose into the sky and went to the Great Forest itself. Those monks too, having gone at the time of departure by the power of the Ten-Powered One, and having returned at the time of return by their own power, having surrounded the Blessed One, descended into the Great Forest.

*Kuṇālajātaka* Having sat down on the seat spread out, the Blessed One addressed those monks: "Come, monks, sit down, I will explain the meditation subject for the abandonment of the defilements to which the three paths above are subject." Thus, he explained the meditation subject. The monks thought, "The Blessed One, knowing our state of discontent, having led [us] to the Kuṇāla Lake, dispelled our discontent. Now here, he has given the meditation subject for the three paths to us who have attained the fruit of stream-entry. It is not fitting for us to spend [our time] thinking, 'We are stream-enterers,' it is fitting for us to become like the highest men." Having paid homage at the feet of the Ten-Powered One, having risen, shaken out their sitting cloths, one by one they sat down at the roots of the cave trees.

The Blessed One thought, "These monks are by nature those whose meditation subject is not confused. For a monk who has obtained the means, there is no cause for weariness. Having gone, while going, they will develop insight, having attained arahantship, they will come to my presence thinking, "We will announce the quality attained by ourselves." When they have come, the deities in ten thousand world-spheres will assemble in one world-sphere, there will be a great assembly, it is fitting for me to sit down in a secluded place." Then, having spread out the Buddha's seat in a secluded place, he sat down.

First, the elder who had gone, having taken a meditation subject, attained arahantship together with the discriminations. Then another, then another, thus all five hundred blossomed like lotuses in a lotus pond. First, the monk who had attained arahantship, thinking, "I will announce [this] to the Blessed One," having folded up his legs, shaken out his sitting cloth, having risen, he faced the Ten-Powered One. Thus, another and another, all five hundred came in order, as if entering a dining hall. The first to arrive, having paid homage, spread out his seat, having sat down to one side, wanting to announce the quality he had attained, "Is there any other, is there not?" Having turned back, while looking at the road by which they were coming, he saw another and another. Thus, all of them having come, having sat down to one side, this one, being deferential to that one, did not speak, this one, being deferential to that one, did not speak. It is said that those whose influxes are exhausted have two characteristics: "Oh, may the world with the gods quickly comprehend the quality attained by me!" This thought arises. However, the state that has been attained, like a man who has found treasure, he does not want to announce to another.

Thus, in that assembly of noble ones, when only the sediment was present, from around the outline of the eastern Yugaṃdhara [mountain], the clouds, mist, smoke, dust, having been freed from these defilements, for the sake of seeing the delightfulness of the world adorned with the Buddha's arising, like a great silver mirror disc raised in the eastern direction, having transgressed the full moon disc, resplendent with a silver wheel being turned when grasped at the circumference, it went along the path of the wind. Thus, at such a moment, in such a second, in such an instant, the Blessed One dwells among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Forest together with a great Saṅgha of monks, approximately five hundred monks, all of them arahants.

There, the Blessed One too was born in the lineage of Mahā Sammata, those five hundred monks too were born in the family of Mahā Sammata. The Blessed One too was born in a Khattiya womb, those too were born in a Khattiya womb. The Blessed One too was a royal renunciant, those too were royal renunciants. The Blessed One too, having abandoned the white umbrella, having renounced the universal monarch's rule that had come into his hand, went forth; those too, having abandoned the white umbrella, having renounced the kingdoms that had come into their hands, went forth. Thus, the Blessed One, in a perfectly pure space, in a perfectly pure portion of the night, himself perfectly pure, with a perfectly pure retinue, without lust, with a retinue without lust, without hatred, with a retinue without hatred, without delusion, with a retinue without delusion, without craving, with a retinue without craving, without defilement, with a retinue without defilement, peaceful, with a peaceful retinue, tamed, with a tamed retinue, freed, with a freed retinue, shines forth exceedingly. Description of the qualities, whatever is possible, that much should be said. Thus, with reference to these monks, it was said, "With approximately five hundred monks, all of them arahants." “*yebhuyyenā*ti”: “the more part” or “the majority”. Many assembled, but the mindless, the non-percipient, the gods of the realm of formlessness, and the gods who have attained meditative absorption did not assemble. Then, this was the order of assembly: the neighboring deities of the Great Forest stirred, [thinking,] “Let us go! For seeing the Buddha is very beneficial, hearing the Dharma is very beneficial, seeing the monastic community is very beneficial. Let us go, let us go!” Making a great noise, they came and, bowing down to the Blessed One and to those who at that moment had attained the state of an *arhat* and were free from corrupting influences, they stood to one side. In this way, hearing each sound, for instance, at intervals of half a *gāvuta*, a *gāvuta*, half a *yojana*, or a *yojana*, and so on up to three thousand *yojanas* across in the Himalayas, three times in the sixty-three thousand cities, in the ninety-nine hundred thousand *doṇamukhas*, in the ninety-six million *paṭṭanas*, in the fifty-six jewel mines, throughout the entire *Jambudvīpa*, in the *Pūbbavideha*, in the *Aparagoyāna*, in the *Uttarakuru*, and in the two thousand lesser islands—throughout the entire world-sphere—deities assembled from this world-sphere, from the second and the third world-spheres; thus, it should be understood that deities assembled in the ten-thousand world-spheres. For here “ten-thousand world-spheres” is understood to mean ten world-realms. Therefore, it was said, “And from ten world-realms, deities assembled in the more part.” “*yebhuyyenā*”: Thus, by the deities who had assembled, the interior of the entire world-sphere, as far as the Brahmā-world, was completely filled, as if with needles constantly stuck in a needle case. Here, the elevation of the Brahmā-world should be understood thus: It is said that a stone, equal to seven storied mansions, having stood in the Brahmā-world and been thrown downwards in the iron palace, reaches the earth in four months. Thus, in such a vast space, just as flowers or smoke, having been thrown from below, do not manage to go upwards, or mustard seeds, having been thrown from above, do not manage to descend downwards, so the deities were continuous. Just as the seat of a wheel-turning monarch is uncrowded, and the powerful nobles who come and go always obtain space, but beyond that, it is very crowded; just so, the Blessed One’s seat was uncrowded, and the powerful deities and great Brahmās who came and went always obtained space. Moreover, in the Blessed One’s very near vicinity, at the Great Decease, in an area the size of the tip of a hair-point, ten, twenty, or even thirty deities, all beyond, fashioned subtle subtle bodies and stood. Sixty, sixty deities stood. “*suddhāvāsakāyikāna*nti”: of those who have their being in the Pure Abodes, i.e., those who dwell in the Pure Abodes. “*suddhāvāsā*”: “Pure Abodes” is the name for the five Brahmā-worlds that are the abodes of pure non-returners and those who are free from corrupting influences. “*etadahosī*ti”: why did this occur? It is said that those Brahmās, having attained meditative absorption, having arisen according to their allotted time, and looking at the Brahmā-abode, saw emptiness as if it were an alms hall after the meal. Then, wondering “Where have the Brahmās gone?”, and knowing about the great assembly—“This assembly is great, and we are inferior, and an opportunity is difficult for the inferior. Therefore, going, and not being empty-handed, let us compose a verse and go. And in that great assembly, we will make known our arrival and will speak of the good qualities of the one with the ten powers”— Thus, because they had arisen from their meditative absorption and had reflected, this occurred.

mula_pali:
332. Atha kho tā devatā seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya , evameva suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṃ, devakāyā samāgatā;

Āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamayaṃ, dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅgha’’nti.

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṃsu, cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsu ujukamakaṃsu (sī. syā. pī.);

ujukamakaṃsu (sī. syā. pī.)

Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā, indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā’’ti.

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Chetvā khīlaṃ chetvā palighaṃ, indakhīlaṃ ūhacca uhacca (ka.) manejā;

uhacca (ka.)

Te caranti suddhā vimalā, cakkhumatā sudantā susunāgā’’ti.

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

‘‘Yekeci buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatāse, na te gamissanti apāyabhūmiṃ;

Pahāya mānusaṃ dehaṃ, devakāyaṃ paripūressantī’’ti.

Devatāsannipātā
mula_english:
332. Then, just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, those *devatās* disappeared from among the Devas of the Pure Abodes (śuddhāvāsa) and reappeared before the Blessed One (bhagavat).

Then those *devatās*, having paid homage to the Blessed One (bhagavantam abhivādetvā), stood to one side (ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu).

Standing to one side, one *devatā* recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“At the great assembly in the wood, the hosts of gods have gathered;

We have come to this *dhamma* meeting, to see the Saṅgha (aparājitasaṅgha) that is unconquered.”

Then another *devatā* recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“There, the monks were composed, they made their minds upright (ujukaṃ akaṃsu);

Like charioteers holding the reins, the wise protect the senses (*indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā*).”

Then another *devatā* recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Having cut through barrenness (khīlaṃ chetvā), cut the cross-bar (palighaṃ chetvā), having uprooted Indra’s pillar (*indakhīlaṃ ūhacca*), unstirred;

They fare on, pure, stainless, with vision, well-controlled, noble nāgas."

Then another *devatā* recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Those, who have gone for refuge to the Buddha (buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatāse), will not go to the plane of misery (apāyabhūmiṃ);

Having abandoned the human body (mānusaṃ dehaṃ pahāya), they will fill the divine hosts (devakāyaṃ paripūressantī).”

Assembly of the Gods (devatāsannipātā)
commentary_pali:
332.Bhagavato purato pāturahesunti pāḷiyaṃ bhagavato santike abhimukhaṭṭhāneyeva otiṇṇā viya katvā vuttā, na kho panettha evaṃ attho veditabbo. Te pana brahmaloke ṭhitāyeva gāthā abhisaṅkharitvā eko puratthimacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otari, eko dakkhiṇacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ, eko pacchimacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ, eko uttaracakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otari. Tato puratthimacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otiṇṇabrahmā nīlakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā nīlarasmiyo vissajjitvā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatānaṃ maṇicammaṃ paṭimuñcanto viya attano āgatabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā buddhavīthi nāma kenaci ottharituṃ na sakkā, tasmā pahaṭabuddhavīthiyāva āgantvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito attanā abhisaṅkhataṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi.

Dakkhiṇacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otiṇṇabrahmāpi pītakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā pītarasmiyo suvaṇṇapabhaṃ muñcitvā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatānaṃ suvaṇṇapaṭaṃ pārupento viya attano āgatabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā tatheva aṭṭhāsi. Pacchimacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otiṇṇabrahmāpi lohitakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā lohitarasmiyo muñcitvā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatānaṃ rattavarakambalena parikkhipanto viya attano āgatabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā tatheva aṭṭhāsi. Uttaracakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ otiṇṇabrahmāpi odātakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā odātarasmiyo muñcitvā dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatānaṃ sumanapaṭaṃ pārupanto viya attano āgatabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā tatheva aṭṭhāsi.

Pāḷiyaṃ pana ‘‘bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsū’’ti evaṃ ekakkhaṇaṃ viya purato pātubhāvo ca abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ ṭhitabhāvo ca vutto, so iminā anukkamena ahosi, ekato katvā pana dassito. Gāthābhāsanaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ visuṃ visuṃyeva vuttaṃ.

Tattha mahāsamayoti mahāsamūho. Pavanaṃ vuccati vanasaṇḍo. Ubhayenapi bhagavā imasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe ajja mahāsamūho mahāsannipātoti āha. Tato yesaṃ so sannipāto, te dassetuṃ devakāyāsamāgatāti āha. Tattha devakāyāti devaghaṭā. Āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamayanti evaṃ samāgate devakāye disvā mayampi imaṃ dhammasamūhaṃ āgatā. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghaṃ, kenaci aparājitaṃ ajjeva tayo māre madditvā vijitasaṅgāmaṃ imaṃ aparājitasaṅghaṃ dassanatthāya āgatamhāti attho. So pana brahmā imaṃ gāthaṃ bhāsitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā puratthimacakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃyeva aṭṭhāsi.

mahāsamayo Pavanaṃ devakāyā samāgatā devakāyā Āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamaya Dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghaṃ,

Atha dutiyo vuttanayeneva āgantvā abhāsi. Tattha tatra bhikkhavoti tasmiṃ sannipātaṭṭhāne bhikkhū. Samādahaṃsūti samādhinā yojesuṃ. Cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsūti attano cittaṃ sabbe vaṅkakuṭilajimhabhāve haritvā ujukaṃ akariṃsu. Sārathīva nettāni gahetvāti yathā samappavattesu sindhavesu odhastapatodo sārathi sabbayottāni gahetvā acodento avārento tiṭṭhati, evaṃ chaḷaṅgupekkhāsamannāgatā guttadvārā sabbepete pañcasatā bhikkhū indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā, ete daṭṭhuṃ idhāgatamha bhagavāti. Sopi gantvā yathāṭhāneyeva aṭṭhāsi.

tatra bhikkhavo Samādahaṃsū Cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsū Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā

Atha tatiyo vuttanayeneva āgantvā abhāsi. Tattha chetvā khīlanti rāgadosamohakhīlaṃ chinditvā. Palighanti rāgadosamohapalighameva. Indakhīlantipi rāgadosamohaindakhīlameva. Ūhacca manejāti ete taṇhāejāya abhāvena anejā bhikkhū indakhīlaṃ ūhacca samūhanitvā. Te carantīti catūsu disāsu appaṭihatacārikaṃ caranti. Suddhāti nirupakkilesā. Vimalāti nimmalā. Idaṃ tasseva vevacanaṃ. Cakkhumatāti pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumantena. Sudantāti cakkhutopi dantā, sotatopi ghānatopi jivhātopi kāyatopi manatopi dantā. Susunāgāti taruṇanāgā. Te evarūpena anuttarena yogācariyena damite taruṇanāge dassanāya āgatamha bhagavāti. Sopi gantvā yathāṭhāneyeva aṭṭhāsi.

chetvā khīla Paligha Indakhīla Ūhacca manejā Te carantī Suddhā Vimalā Cakkhumatā Sudantā Susunāgā

Atha catuttho vuttanayeneva āgantvā abhāsi. Tattha gatāseti nibbematikasaraṇagamanena gatā. Sopi gantvā yathāṭhāneyeva aṭṭhāsi.

gatāse

Devatāsannipātavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
332. "bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ" in the Pāḷi means that they appeared as if descending in the immediate presence of the Blessed One, but this is not the meaning to be understood here.

Those [beings], having reflected on the verses while staying in the Brahma world, one descended at the eastern *cakravāḷa* (world-wheel) gate, one at the southern *cakravāḷa* gate, one at the western *cakravāḷa* gate, and one at the northern *cakravāḷa* gate.

Then, the Brahmā who descended at the eastern *cakravāḷa* gate, having attained blue *kasiṇa* (a device for focusing the mind), emitted blue rays, making it known that he had arrived to the ten-thousand *cakravāḷa* deities as if offering a jeweled garment. Because the path of the Buddha could not be obstructed by anyone, having come to the immediate path of the Buddha, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, he uttered a verse that he had created himself.

The Brahmā who descended at the southern *cakravāḷa* gate, having attained yellow *kasiṇa*, emitted yellow rays, making it known that he had arrived to the ten-thousand *cakravāḷa* deities as if draping a golden cloth. Thus, he stood there.

The Brahmā who descended at the western *cakravāḷa* gate, having attained red *kasiṇa*, emitted red rays, making it known that he had arrived to the ten-thousand *cakravāḷa* deities as if surrounding [them] with a red and excellent blanket. Thus, he stood there.

The Brahmā who descended at the northern *cakravāḷa* gate, having attained white *kasiṇa*, emitted white rays, making it known that he had arrived to the ten-thousand *cakravāḷa* deities as if draping a beautiful cloth. Thus, he stood there.

In the Pāḷi, however, it says, "bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ. atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsū" (the deities appeared before the Blessed One. Then those deities, having paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side). Thus, the appearance in front, the paying of homage, and the standing to one side are spoken of as if [occurring in] a single moment, but it happened in this sequence, and it is shown having been done together. However, the uttering of the verses is spoken of separately, each in its own place, in the Pāḷi.

There, *mahāsamayo* means a great gathering. *pavanaṃ* is said to be a forest grove. With both of these, the Blessed One said, "In this forest grove today is a great gathering, a great assembly."

Then, in order to show what that assembly was, [he said] "*devakāyā samāgatā*," meaning the bodies of deities have assembled. There, *devakāyā* means a multitude of deities. "*āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamaya*," means that having seen the deities assembled in this *dharma*-assembly, we also have come to this *dharma*-gathering.

What is the reason? "*dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghaṃ*," [means] to see the unconquered *saṃgha* (community). The meaning is that today itself, having crushed the three Māras and won the battle, we have come to see this unconquered *saṃgha*.

That Brahmā, having spoken this verse, paid homage to the Blessed One and stood right there at the eastern *cakravāḷa* gate.

*mahāsamayo pavanaṃ devakāyā samāgatā devakāyā āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamaya dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghaṃ*

Then, the second one, having come in the manner spoken of, uttered [a verse]. There, "*tatra bhikkhavo*" means the *bhikkhus* (monks) in that place of assembly. "*samādahaṃsū*" means they joined with concentration. "*cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsū*" means having removed all the crooked, bent, and dishonest states, they made their own minds straight. "*sārathīva nettāni gahetvā*" Just as a charioteer, having taken all the reins, stands without urging on or restraining the horses that are properly moving along the road, so too, these five hundred *bhikkhus*, endowed with equanimity in six respects, with guarded doors [of the senses], protect their senses, [and are] wise. We have come here to see these Blessed Ones.

He also, having gone, stood right there in his place.

*tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṃsū cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsū sārathīva nettāni gahetvā*

Then the third one, having come in the manner spoken of, uttered [a verse]. There, "*chetvā khīla*" means having cut off the stake of passion, hatred, and delusion. "*paligha*" means the very iron bar of passion, hatred, and delusion. "*indakhīla*" also means the very *indakhīla* (pillar of Indra) of passion, hatred, and delusion. "*ūhacca manejā*" means these *bhikkhus*, without desire, having uprooted and completely removed the *indakhīla* due to the absence of the agitation of craving, "*te carantī*" means they wander in all four directions, wandering without obstruction. "*suddhā*" means free from defilements.
*Vimalā* means spotless. This is a synonym for that.

*Cakkhumatā* means with five eyes, endowed with vision.

*Sudantā* means with well-tamed senses, senses that are tamed, from the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind.

*Susunāgā* means young Nāgas.

"They, in this form, have come to see the Blessed One, who is tamed by an unsurpassed teacher of yoga, [taming] young Nāgas."

He went, and stood just where he was before.

Having cut off the stake ( *khīla*), the bar (*paligha*), the post of Indra (*indakhīla*), having drawn out desire (*manejā*), they wander, pure (*śuddhā*), spotless (*vimalā*), endowed with vision (*cakkhumatā*), well-tamed (*sudantā*), young Nāgas (*susunāgā*). Then the fourth one came and spoke in the manner described.

There, *gatāse* means gone by means of going to a refuge free from doubt (*nibbematikasaraṇagamanena gatā*).

He went, and stood just where he was before.

*Gatāse*. Description of the assembly of the gods ( *devatāsannipātavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali: 333. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, dasasu lokadhātūsu devatā sannipatitā honti ( ) sī. ipotthakesu natthi, tathāgataṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca . Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etaṃparamāyeva etaparamāyeva (sī. syā. pī.) devatā sannipatitā ahesuṃ seyyathāpi mayhaṃ etarahi. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etaṃparamāyeva devatā sannipatitā bhavissanti seyyathāpi mayhaṃ etarahi. Ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni; kittayissāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni; desessāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ.
mula_english:
333. Then, the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, for the most part, the *devatās* from ten world-systems have gathered in order to see the *Tathāgata* and the *bhikkhu-saṃgha*.

Those who, in the past, were *arhats*, *sammāsambuddhās*, at most had their *devatā*-gathering like mine at the present.

Those who, in the future, will be *arhats*, *sammāsambuddhās*, will at most have their *devatā*-gathering like mine at the present.

I will tell you the names of the *deva* hosts; I will describe to you the names of the *deva* hosts; I will teach you the names of the *deva* hosts.

Listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak."

"Yes, Lord," said the monks in reply to the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
333. Atha bhagavā olokento pathavītalato yāva cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiparicchedā yāva akaniṭṭhabrahmalokā devatāsannipātaṃ disvā cintesi – ‘‘mahā ayaṃ devatāsamāgamo, bhikkhū pana evaṃ mahā devatāya samāgamoti na jānanti, handa, nesaṃ ācikkhāmī’’ti, evaṃ cintetvā ‘‘atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesī’’ti sabbaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ. Tattha etaparamāti etaṃ paramaṃ pamāṇaṃ etesanti etaparamā. Idāni buddhānaṃ pana abhāvā ‘‘yepi te, bhikkhave, etarahī’’ti tatiyo vāro na vutto. Ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhaveti kasmā āha? Devatānaṃ cittakallatājananatthaṃ. Devatā kira cintesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā evaṃ mahante samāgame mahesakkhānaṃyeva devatānaṃ nāmagottāni kathessati, appesakkhānaṃ kiṃ kathessatī’’ti? Atha bhagavā ‘‘imā devatā kiṃ cintentī’’ti āvajjanto mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetvā hadayamaṃsaṃ maddanto viya sabhaṇḍaṃ coraṃ gaṇhanto viya ca taṃ tāsaṃ cittācāraṃ ñatvā – ‘‘dasasahassacakkavāḷato āgatāgatānaṃ appesakkhamahesakkhānaṃ sabbāsampi devatānaṃ nāmagottaṃ kathessāmī’’ti cintesi.

Buddhā nāma mahantā ete sattavisesā, yaṃ sadevakassa lokassa diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, na kiñci katthaci nīlādivasena vibhattarūpārammaṇesu rūpārammaṇaṃ vā bherīsaddādivasena vibhattasaddārammaṇādīsu visuṃ visuṃ saddādiārammaṇaṃ vā atthi, yaṃ etesaṃ ñāṇamukhe āpāthaṃ nāgacchati. Yathāha –

‘‘Yaṃ bhikkhave sadevakassa lokassa…pe… sadevamanussāya diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, tamahaṃ jānāmi, tamahaṃ passāmi, tamahaṃ abbhaññāsi’’nti (a. ni. 4.24).

Evaṃ sabbattha appaṭihatañāṇo bhagavā sabbāpi tā devatā bhabbābhabbavasena dve koṭṭhāse akāsi. ‘‘Kammāvaraṇena vā samannāgatā’’tiādinā nayena vuttā sattā abhabbā nāma. Te ekavihāre vasantepi buddhā na olokenti. Viparītā pana bhabbā nāma, te dūre vasantepi gantvā saṅgaṇhanti. Tasmā tasmimpi devatāsannipāte ye abhabbā, te pahāya bhabbe pariggahesi. Pariggahetvā – ‘‘ettakā ettha rāgacaritā, ettakā dosacaritā, ettakā mohacaritā’’ti caritavasena cha koṭṭhāse akāsi. Atha nesaṃ sappāyaṃ dhammadesanaṃ upadhārayanto – ‘‘rāgacaritānaṃ devatānaṃ sammāparibbājaniyasuttaṃ kathessāmi, dosacaritānaṃ kalahavivādasuttaṃ, mohacaritānaṃ mahābyūhasuttaṃ, vitakkacaritānaṃ cūḷabyūhasuttaṃ, saddhācaritānaṃ tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadaṃ, buddhicaritānaṃ purābhedasuttaṃ kathessāmī’’ti desanaṃ vavatthapetvā puna taṃ parisaṃ manasākāsi – ‘‘attajjhāsayena nu kho jāneyya, parajjhāsayena atthuppattikena pucchāvasenā’’ti. Tato ‘‘pucchāvasena jāneyyā’’ti ñatvā ‘‘atthi nu kho koci devatānaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ gahetvā caritavasena pañhaṃ pucchituṃ samattho’’ti ‘‘tesu pañcasatesu bhikkhūsu ekopi na sakkotī’’ti addasa. Tato asītimahāsāvake dve aggasāvake ca samannāharitvā ‘‘tepi na sakkontī’’ti disvā cintesi ‘‘sace paccekabuddho bhaveyya, sakkuṇeyya nu kho’’ti ‘‘sopi na sakkuṇeyyā’’ti ñatvā ‘‘sakkasuyāmādīsu koci sakkuṇeyyā’’ti samannāhari. Sace hi tesu koci sakkuṇeyya, taṃ pucchāpetvā attanā vissajjeyya, na pana tesupi koci sakkoti.

abhabbā bhabbā sammāparibbājaniyasuttaṃ kalahavivādasuttaṃ, mahābyūhasuttaṃ, cūḷabyūhasuttaṃ, tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadaṃ, purābhedasuttaṃ

Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘mādiso buddhoyeva sakkuṇeyya, atthi pana katthaci añño buddho’’ti anantāsu lokadhātūsu anantañāṇaṃ pattharitvā olokento aññaṃ buddhaṃ na addasa. Anacchariyañcetaṃ, yaṃ idāni attanā samaṃ na passeyya, so jātadivasepi brahmajālavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayena attanā samaṃ apassanto – ‘‘aggohamasmi lokassā’’ti appaṭivattiyaṃ sīhanādaṃ nadi. Evaṃ aññaṃ attanā samaṃ apassitvā cintesi – ‘‘sace ahaṃ pucchitvā ahameva vissajjeyyaṃ, evampetā devatā na sakkhissanti paṭivijjhituṃ. Aññasmiṃ pana buddheyeva pucchante mayi ca vissajjante accherakaṃ bhavissati, sakkhissanti ca devatā paṭivijjhituṃ, tasmā nimmitabuddhaṃ māpessāmī’’ti abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya – ‘‘pattacīvaragahaṇaṃ ālokitavilokitaṃ samiñjitapasāritañca mama sadisaṃyeva hotū’’ti kāmāvacaracittehi parikammaṃ katvā pācīnayugandharaparikkhepato ullaṅghamānaṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ bhinditvā nikkhamantaṃ viya rūpāvacaracittena adhiṭṭhāsi.

Devasaṅgho taṃ disvā – ‘‘aññopi nu kho, bho, cando uggato’’ti āha. Atha candaṃ ohāya āsannatare jāte ‘‘na cando, sūriyo uggato’’ti, puna āsannatare jāte ‘‘na sūriyo, devavimānaṃ eka’’nti, puna āsannatare jāte ‘‘na devavimānaṃ, devaputto eko’’ti, puna āsannatare jāte ‘‘na devaputto, mahābrahmā eko’’ti, puna āsannatare jāte ‘‘na mahābrahmā, aparopi bho buddho āgato’’ti āha. Tattha puthujjanadevatā cintayiṃsu – ‘‘ekabuddhassa tāva ayaṃ devatāsannipāto, dvinnaṃ kīva mahanto bhavissatī’’ti. Ariyadevatā cintayiṃsu – ‘‘ekissā lokadhātuyā dve buddhā nāma natthi, addhā bhagavatā attanā sadiso añño eko buddho nimmito’’ti.

Atha tassa devasaṅghassa passantasseva nimmitabuddho āgantvā dasabalaṃ avanditvāva sammukhaṭṭhāne samasamaṃ katvā māpite āsane nisīdi. Bhagavatopi dvattiṃsa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, nimmitassāpi dvattiṃsāva, bhagavatopi sarīrā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo nikkhamanti , nimmitassāpi, bhagavato sarīrarasmiyo nimmitassa sarīre paṭihaññanti, nimmitassa sarīrarasmiyo bhagavato kāye paṭihaññanti. Tā dvinnampi buddhānaṃ sarīrato uggamma akaniṭṭhabhavanaṃ āhacca tato paṭinivattitvā devatānaṃ matthakapariyante otaritvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Sakalacakkavāḷagabbhaṃ suvaṇṇamayavaṅkagopānasīvinaddhamiva cetiyagharaṃ virocittha. Dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatā ekacakkavāḷe rāsibhūtā dvinnaṃ buddhānaṃ rasmigabbhantaraṃ pavisitvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Nimmitabuddho nisīdantoyeva dasabalassa bodhipallaṅke kilesappahānaṃ abhitthavanto –

‘‘Pucchāmi muniṃ pahūtapaññaṃ,

Tiṇṇaṃ pāraṅgataṃ parinibbutaṃ ṭhitattaṃ;

Nikkhamma gharā panujja kāme,

Kathaṃ bhikkhu sammā so loke paribbajeyyā’’ti. (su. ni. 361) –

Gāthaṃ abhāsi. Satthā devatānaṃ tāva cittakallatājananatthaṃ āgatāgatānaṃ nāmagottāni kathessāmīti cintetvā ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave
commentary_english:
333. Then the Bhagavān, looking over the gathering of deities from the surface of the earth up to the boundary of the *cakravāḷa* and up to the Akaniṣṭha Brahma-world, thought: "This is a great gathering of deities, but the *bhikkhus* do not know that this is a great gathering of deities. Come, I will tell them." Thus thinking, "Then the Bhagavān addressed the *bhikkhus*," everything should be explained in detail.

There, *etaparamā* means that this is the highest measure, therefore it is *etaparamā*.

Now, because of the absence of Buddhas, the third time the phrase "*yepi te, bhikkhave, etarahī*" was not spoken.

"*Ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave* (I will tell you, *bhikkhus*)"—why did he say this? In order to generate a pleasing state of mind in the deities.

The deities thought: "In such a great gathering, the Bhagavān will only speak the names and clans of the deities with great power; what will he say of those with little power?" Then the Bhagavān, considering "What are these deities thinking?" and inserting his hand into his mouth as if crushing heart-flesh, and as if seizing a thief with stolen goods, knowing their state of mind, thought: "I will speak the names and clans of all the deities who have come from the ten-thousand *cakravāḷas*, those with little power and those with great power."

Buddhas are indeed great beings, these special beings, and whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, reached, sought after, or examined by the mind of the world with its gods, there is nothing anywhere, in the various objects of visual form due to blue and other qualities, or the various objects of sound, etc., due to kettledrum sounds and other qualities, that exists separately that does not come into the range of their knowledge. As it is said:

"Whatever, *bhikkhus*, is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, reached, sought after, or examined by the mind of the world with its gods…pe…of the world with its gods and humans, that I know, that I see, that I fully understand" (A. Ni. 4.24).

Thus, the Bhagavān, whose knowledge is unobstructed everywhere, divided all those deities into two categories based on whether they were capable or incapable.

"*kammāvaraṇena vā samannāgatā* (those who are associated with karmic obscurations)" and other statements describe beings who are called incapable (*abhabbā*).

Even if they live in the same monastery, the Buddhas do not look upon them.

The opposite, however, are called capable (*bhabbā*), and even if they live far away, they go and gather them.

Therefore, in that gathering of deities, having abandoned those who are incapable, he took hold of those who are capable.

Having taken hold of them, he divided them into six categories based on their characteristics: "So many here are characterized by lust (*rāgacaritā*), so many are characterized by hatred (*dosacaritā*), so many are characterized by delusion (*mohacaritā*)."

Then, considering the appropriate Dharma teaching for them: "I will teach the *Sammāparibbājaniya Sutta* to the deities characterized by lust, the *Kalahavivāda Sutta* to those characterized by hatred, the *Mahābyūha Sutta* to those characterized by delusion, the *Cūḷabyūha Sutta* to those characterized by thought (*vitakka*), the *Tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadā* to those characterized by faith (*saddhā*), and the *Purābheda Sutta* to those characterized by wisdom (*buddhi*)," having determined the teaching, he again turned his mind to that assembly: "How should I know—through my own inclination, or through the arising of meaning based on the inclination of others, through questioning?"

Then, knowing that "I should know through questioning," and realizing "Is there anyone among the deities who is capable of grasping the inclinations of others and asking questions based on their characteristics?" he saw that "Not even one among those five hundred *bhikkhus* is capable."

Then, having summoned the eighty great disciples and the two chief disciples, and seeing that "They too are not capable," he thought: "If there were a *pratyekabuddha*, would he be capable?" Knowing that "Even he would not be capable," he summoned "Someone among the Śakka, Suyāma, etc."

If someone among them were capable, he would question them and then answer himself, but not even one among them is capable.

Incapable (*abhabbā*), capable (*bhabbā*), *Sammāparibbājaniya Sutta*, *Kalahavivāda Sutta*, *Mahābyūha Sutta*, *Cūḷabyūha Sutta*, *Tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadā*, *Purābheda Sutta*.

Then it occurred to him: "Only a Buddha like myself would be capable. Is there another Buddha anywhere?" Spreading infinite knowledge throughout infinite world-systems, he looked around but did not see another Buddha.

And this is not surprising, since even now he does not see anyone equal to himself. Even on the day of his birth, in the description of the Brahma-net, he did not see anyone equal to himself, saying, "I am the chief in the world," and uttered an irreversible lion's roar.

Thus, not seeing another equal to himself, he thought: "If I were to ask and answer myself, these deities would not be able to penetrate it.

But if another Buddha were to ask and I were to answer, it would be astonishing, and the deities would be able to penetrate it. Therefore, I will create a *nimmitabuddha* (created Buddha)." Having attained the *abhijñāpādakajjhāna* (absorption that is the basis for super-knowledge) and arisen from it, he resolved with mind of the form realm: "May the taking of the bowl and robe, the looking and gazing, the drawing in and stretching out, be just like my own!" Having performed the preliminary work with minds belonging to the desire realm, he established it with mind of the form realm, like the moon disc rising above the surrounding of the eastern Yugandhara mountain, breaking through and emerging.

The assembly of gods, seeing him, said: "Has another moon risen, sir?"

Then, passing beyond the moon and becoming closer, they said, "It is not the moon, the sun has risen!" Again, becoming closer, they said, "It is not the sun, it is a divine palace!" Again, becoming closer, they said, "It is not a divine palace, it is a divine son!" Again, becoming closer, they said, "It is not a divine son, it is Mahābrahmā!" Again, becoming closer, they said, "It is not Mahābrahmā, another Buddha has come, sir!"

There, the ordinary deities thought: "This gathering of deities is for one Buddha; how much greater will it be for two!"

The noble deities thought: "There are not two Buddhas in one world-system. Surely the Bhagavān has created another Buddha similar to himself!"

Then, while that assembly of gods was watching, the created Buddha (*nimmitabuddha*) came and, without bowing to the One with Ten Powers, sat down on the seat that had been prepared, making it exactly equal in the place before him.
The Blessed One also had thirty-two marks of a great man (mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni), and so did the created one. From the Blessed One's body issued forth six-colored rays (chabbaṇṇarasmiyo), and so it was with the created one. The body rays of the Blessed One struck against the body of the created one, and the body rays of the created one struck against the body of the Blessed One.

Those rays, rising from the bodies of both Buddhas, struck against the Akaniṣṭha heaven (akaniṭṭhabhavanaṃ), and then, turning back, descended upon the heads of the deities and stood firm at the face of the world-circle (cakravāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ). The entire interior of the world-circle shone like a jeweled house fastened with golden curved lattices. Ten thousand world-circle deities, massed together in one world-circle, entered into the interior of the rays of the two Buddhas and stood there.

The created Buddha, while sitting on the Bodhi-throne (bodhipallaṅke) of the Ten-Powered One, praising the abandonment of defilements (kilesappahānaṃ), recited this verse:

"I ask the sage of great wisdom, who has crossed over, is extinguished, and steadfast: how should a *bhikṣu*, having left home and renounced desires, wander rightly in the world?" (Sutta Nipāta 361)

The Teacher (satthā), thinking, "I will now tell the names and clans of the deities who have come to bring about the fitness of mind of the deities," said, "I will announce, *bhikkhus* (ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave)," and so on.

I will announce, *bhikkhus* (ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave).

vavakkhitvāna (sī. syā. pī.), avekkhitvāna (ṭīkā)

mula_english:
334. The Blessed One said this:

“I will intone a verse, where the earth-dwellers are situated;

Those who dwell in mountain caves, resolute, concentrated.

“Like mighty lions, withdrawn, with bristling hair;

With minds of white, pure, with minds clear and unperturbed.”

Knowing that even more than five hundred [were present] in the Kapilavatthu forest,

Then the Teacher addressed the disciples delighting in the teaching:

“The deva hosts have approached. Detect them, monks!”

And they generated effort, having heard the Buddha’s teaching.

To them appeared knowledge, the sight of non-humans;

Some saw a hundred, a thousand, or seventy.

A hundred some saw, a thousand non-humans;

And some saw an endless number, all directions were filled.

Having directly known all that, having ascertained it with his eye,

Then the Teacher addressed the disciples delighting in the teaching:

“The deva hosts have approached. Detect them, monks!

Those whom I will enumerate to you, with speech in due order.
commentary_pali:
334. Tattha silokamanukassāmīti akkharapadaniyamitaṃ vacanasaṅghātaṃ pavattayissāmi. Yattha bhummā tadassitāti yesu yesu ṭhānesu bhummā devatā taṃ taṃ nissitā. Ye sitā girigabbharantiādīhi tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathesi, ye bhikkhū girikucchiṃ nissitāti attho. Pahitattāti pesitacittā. Samāhitāti avikkhittā.

Puthūti bahujanā. Sīhāva sallīnāti sīhā viya nilīnā ekattaṃ upagatā. Lomahaṃsābhisambhunoti lomahaṃsaṃ abhibhavitvā ṭhitā, nibbhayāti vuttaṃ hoti. Odātamanasā suddhāti odātacittā hutvā suddhā. Vippasannāmanāvilāti vippasannaanāvilā.

Puthū Sīhāva sallīnā Lomahaṃsābhisambhuno Odātamanasā suddhā Vippasannāmanāvilā

Bhiyyopañcasate ñatvāti sammāsambuddhena saddhiṃ atirekapañcasate bhikkhū jānitvā. Vane kāpilavatthaveti kapilavatthusamīpamhi jāte vanasaṇḍe. Tato āmantayī satthāti tadā āmantayi. Sāvakesāsane rateti attano dhammadesanāya savanante jātattā sāvake sikkhattayasāsane ratattā sāsane rate. Idaṃ sabbaṃ – ‘‘silokamanukassāmī’’ti vacanato aññena vuttaṃ viya katvā vadati.

Amanussadassanatthaṃ panassa abhinīhāramattameva kataṃ. Satthāpi – ‘‘atthi tumhākaṃ ñāṇaṃ, taṃ nīharitvā tena hi te vijānāthā’’ti idameva sandhāya ‘‘te vijānātha, bhikkhavo’’ti āha.

tesaṃ pāturahu ñāṇaṃ.

Appeke satamaddakkhunti tesu bhikkhūsu ekacce bhikkhū amanussānaṃ sataṃ addasaṃsu. Sahassaṃ atha sattarinti eke sahassaṃ. Eke sattati sahassāni.

Appeke satamaddakkhu Sahassaṃ atha sattari

Sataṃ eke sahassānanti eke satasahassaṃ addasaṃsu. Appekenantamaddakkhunti vipulaṃ addasaṃsu, satavasena sahassavasena ca aparicchinnepi addasaṃsūti attho. Kasmā? Yasmā disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ, bharitā sampuṇṇāva ahesuṃ.

Sataṃ eke sahassāna Appekenantamaddakkhu disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ,

Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāyāti yaṃ tesu ekenekena diṭṭhaṃ, tañca sabbaṃ jānitvā. Vavatthitvāna cakkhumāti hatthatale lekhaṃ viya paccakkhato vavatthapetvā pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā satthā. Tato āmantayīti pubbe vuttagāthameva nāmagottakittanatthāya āha. Tumhe ete vijānātha, passatha, oloketha, ye vohaṃ kittayissāmīti ayamettha sambandho. Girāhīti vacanehi. Anupubbasoti anupaṭipāṭiyā.

commentary_english:
334. "silokamanukassāmī" means, I will cause to proceed a collection of words limited to letters and phrases.

"yattha bhummā tadassitā" means, in whichever places the earth deities are, they are dependent on those.

"ye sitā girigabbhara" etc., he told the qualities of those monks, the meaning is, the monks are dependent on the mountain caves.

"pahitattā" means, those with sent minds.

"samāhitā" means, those who are not distracted.

"puthū" means, many people.

"sīhāva sallīnā" means, like lions, they are hidden, having approached oneness.

"lomahaṃsābhisambhuno" means, having overcome hair-raising fear, they are abiding, it is said to be fearless.

"odātamanasā suddhā" means, having become pure with white minds, they are pure.

"vippasannāmanāvilā" means, they are very clear and not turbid.

"puthū sīhāva sallīnā lomahaṃsābhisambhuno odātamanasā suddhā vippasannāmanāvilā"

"bhiyyopañcasate ñatvā" means, knowing the monks who were five hundred more together with the perfectly enlightened Buddha.

"vane kāpilavatthave" means, in the forest grove born near Kapilavatthu.

"tato āmantayī satthā" means, then he addressed.

"sāvake" "sāsane rate" means, because of being born at the end of the teaching of his own doctrine, to the disciples who delight in the three trainings, who delight in the teaching.

This all, he speaks having made [it] as if said by another, from the statement "silokamanukassāmī".

"bhiyyopañcasate ñatvā vane kāpilavatthave tato āmantayī satthā sāvake sāsane rate"

"devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo" means, "The deva hosts have approached. Detect them, monks." He spoke thus to those monks for the purpose of generating their knowledge of the divine eye.

"te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsana" means, and those monks, having heard that Buddha's teaching, just then made an effort for that purpose.

"devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsana"

evaṃ katamattātappānaṃyeva "tesaṃ pāturahu ñāṇaṃ."

What kind [of knowledge]? The sight of non-humans, the knowledge of the divine eye, arose.

That was not produced by them having done preliminary work at that moment.

Indeed, that is accomplished only by the noble path.

But for the purpose of the sight of non-humans, only the intention was made.

The teacher also, thinking, "There is knowledge for you, having brought that out, then detect them," said "Detect them, monks."

"tesaṃ pāturahu ñāṇaṃ."

"appeke satamaddakkhu" means, among those monks, some monks saw a hundred non-humans.

"sahassaṃ atha sattari" means, some saw a thousand.

Some saw seventy thousand.

"appeke satamaddakkhu sahassaṃ atha sattari"

"sataṃ eke sahassāna" means, some saw one hundred thousand.

"appekenantamaddakkhu" means, they saw a great amount, the meaning is, they saw [them] even without limit, in terms of hundreds and in terms of thousands.

Why? Because "disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ," all directions were filled, they were full and complete.

"sataṃ eke sahassāna appekenantamaddakkhu disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ,"

"tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya" means, having known that all that was seen by each one of them.

"vavatthitvāna cakkhumā" means, the sighted teacher, having ascertained directly, like a line on the palm of the hand, with the five eyes.

"tato āmantayī" means, he spoke that very verse previously spoken, for the purpose of declaring the name and lineage.
You all should know, see, and observe these things which I will declare, this is the connection here.

The term "<hi rend="bold">girāhī</hi>" is by means of words.

The term "<hi rend="bold">anupubbaso</hi>" means in due order.

And then, having known all that, the one with the eye, having determined, then addressed, "<hi rend="bold">girāhī</hi>," "<hi rend="bold">anupubbaso</hi>."

335. "Seven thousand *yakkha*s, inhabitants of the land of Kapilavatthu,

possessing power, possessing radiance, possessing beauty, possessing glory,

rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting.

"Six thousand *yakkha*s from Himavat, *yakkha*s of various colors,

possessing power, possessing radiance, possessing beauty, possessing glory,

rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting.

"Three thousand *yakkha*s from Sātāgira, *yakkha*s of various colors,

possessing power, possessing radiance, possessing beauty, possessing glory,

rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting.

"Thus these sixteen thousand *yakkha*s, *yakkha*s of various colors,

possessing power, possessing radiance, possessing beauty, possessing glory,

rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting.

"Five hundred *yakkha*s from Vessāmitta, *yakkha*s of various colors,

possessing power, possessing radiance, possessing beauty, possessing glory,

rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting.

"Kumbhīra from Rājagaha, the abode of Vepulla,

more than a hundred thousand *yakkha*s attend upon him;

Kumbhīra from Rājagaha, together with them, approached the forest meeting.

commentary_english:
335. "Seven thousand *yakṣas*, terrestrial dwellers of Kapilavatthu," means that seven thousand terrestrial *yakṣas* were born depending on Kapilavatthu itself. "Powerful," means possessing divine power (*iddhi*). "Radiant," means endowed with influence. "Beautiful," means possessing bodily beauty. "Famous," means endowed with retinue. "Rejoicing, they approached," means they came with delighted minds. "The assembly of monks, the forest," means they came to this great forest, to the presence of the monks, to see the monks. Or, "assembly" (*samiti*) means a group; the meaning is that they came to see the group of monks.

"Six thousand from Hemavat, *yakṣas* of various colors," means six thousand *yakṣas* born on Mount Hemavat, and all of them were of various colors according to blue and other colors.

"Six thousand from Hemavat, *yakṣas* of various colors."

"Three thousand from Sātāgira," means three thousand *yakṣas* born on Mount Sātāgiri.

"Three thousand from Sātāgira."

"Thus these are sixteen thousand," means all of these are sixteen thousand.

"Thus these are sixteen thousand."

"Five hundred from Vessāmitta," means five hundred born on Mount Vessāmitta.

"Five hundred from Vessāmitta."

"Kumbhīra, a resident of Rājagaha," means a *yakṣa* named Kumbhīra, born in the city of Rājagaha. "The dwelling of Vepulla," means that Mount Vepulla is his dwelling, his place of residence. "More than a hundred thousand *yakṣas* attend upon him," means that more than a hundred thousand *yakṣas* attend upon him. "Kumbhīra, a resident of Rājagaha, came to the assembly, the forest," means that Kumbhīra himself, with his retinue, came to this forest to see the assembly of monks.

"Kumbhīra, a resident of Rājagaha." "The dwelling of Vepulla." "More than a hundred thousand *yakṣas* attend upon him." "Kumbhīra, a resident of Rājagaha, came to the assembly, the forest."

mula_pali:
336.‘‘Purimañca disaṃ rājā, dhataraṭṭho pasāsati.

Gandhabbānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

‘‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Dakkhiṇañca disaṃ rājā, virūḷho taṃ pasāsati tappasāsati (syā.);

tappasāsati (syā.)

Kumbhaṇḍānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Yakkhānañca adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

daddaḷhamānā (ka.)
mula_english:
336.
And Dhataraṭṭha (Dhṛtarāṣṭra), who rules as king of the Eastern Direction, is lord of the Gandharvas, a great king, glorious.

"And many are his sons named Indra (Indra-nāmā), of great strength; possessors of psychic power, radiant, handsome, glorious; rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting."

And Virūḷha (Virūḍhaka) rules as king of the Southern Direction; he is lord of the Kumbhāṇḍas, a great king, glorious.

"And many are his sons named Indra, of great strength; possessors of psychic power, radiant, handsome, glorious; rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting."

And Virūpakkha (Virūpākṣa) rules as king of the Western Direction; he is lord of the Nāgas, a great king, glorious.

"And many are his sons named Indra, of great strength; possessors of psychic power, radiant, handsome, glorious; rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting."

And Kuvera (Kubera) rules as king of the Northern Direction; he is lord of the Yakṣas, a great king, glorious.

"And many are his sons named Indra, of great strength; possessors of psychic power, radiant, handsome, glorious; rejoicing, they have approached the monks’ forest meeting."

Dhṛtarāṣṭra is of the Eastern Direction, Virūḷhaka of the Southern Direction, Virūpākṣa of the Western Direction, and Kubera of the Northern Direction.

These four Great Kings encompass the four directions, resplendent, stand in the Kāpilavatthu forest.
commentary_pali:
336.Purimañca disaṃ rājā, dhataraṭṭho pasāsatīti pācīnadisaṃ anusāsati. Gandhabbānaṃ adhipatīti catūsupi disāsu gandhabbānaṃ jeṭṭhako. Sabbe te tassa vase vattanti. Mahārājā yasassisoti mahāparivāro eso mahārājā.

Puttāpitassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalāti tassa dhataraṭṭhassa bahavo mahabbalā puttā, te sabbe sakkassa devarañño nāmadhārakā.

Puttāpi tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā

Virūḷho taṃ pasāsatīti taṃ disaṃ virūḷho anusāsati.

Virūḷho taṃ pasāsatī

Puttāpi tassāti tassāpi tādisāyeva puttā. Pāḷiyaṃ pana ‘‘mahabbalā’’ti likhanti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ sabbavāresu ‘‘mahābalā’’ti pāṭho.

Puttāpi tassā

‘‘Purimaṃ disaṃ dhataraṭṭho, dakkhiṇena virūḷhako;

Pacchimena virūpakkho, kuvero uttaraṃ disaṃ.

Cattāro te mahārājā, samantā caturo disā;

Daddallamānā aṭṭhaṃsu, vane kāpilavatthave’’ti.

Imā pana gāthā sabbasaṅgāhikavasena vuttā.

Ayañcettha attho – dasasahassacakkavāḷe dhataraṭṭhā nāma mahārājāno atthi. Te sabbepi koṭisatasahassakoṭisatasahassagandhabbaparivārā āgantvā puratthimāya disāya kapilavatthumahāvanato paṭṭhāya cakkavāḷagabbhaṃ pūretvā ṭhitā. Evaṃ dakkhiṇadisādīsu virūḷhakādayo. Tenevāha – ‘‘samantā caturo disā, daddallamānā aṭṭhaṃsū’’ti. Idañhi vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘samantā cakkavāḷehi āgantvā caturo disā pabbatamatthakesu aggikkhandhā viya suṭṭhu jalamānā ṭhitā’’ti. Te pana yasmā kapilavatthuvanameva sandhāya āgatā, tasmā cakkavāḷaṃ pūretvā cakkavāḷena samasamā ṭhitāpi – ‘‘vane kāpilavatthave’’ti vuttā.
commentary_english:
336. "The king Dhataraṭṭha rules the eastern direction" means he instructs the eastern direction. (Dhataraṭṭho pasāsatī)
"Lord of the *gandharvas*" means he is the eldest of the *gandharvas* in all four directions. (gandhabbānaṃ adhipatī)
All of them abide in his control.
"*Mahārāja* of great fame" means this *mahārāja* has a great retinue. (mahārājā yasassiso)

His many sons, named Indra, are very powerful" means Dhataraṭṭha has many powerful sons, all of whom bear the name of Śakka, king of the gods (sakassa devarañño nāmadhārakā).

"Virūḷha rules" means Virūḷha instructs that direction.

"Virūḷha rules, and his sons are like him."

In the Pāḷi [text], they write "mahabbalā" [very powerful].

In the commentary, the reading in all instances is "mahābalā" [great strength].

"Dhataraṭṭha [guards] the eastern direction, Virūḷhaka the southern;

Virūpakkha the western, Kuvera the northern direction."

"The four great kings, on all sides, the four directions;

shining brightly, they stood in the Kāpilavatthu grove."

These verses, however, were spoken in a comprehensive manner.

Moreover, the meaning here is: in the ten thousand world-systems, there are *mahārājas* named Dhataraṭṭha.

All of them, with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of *gandharvas*, having come to the eastern direction, from the great grove of Kapilavatthu onwards, filled the womb of the world-system and remained standing.

Likewise, Virūḷhaka and the others [guard] the southern direction, etc.

Therefore, he said, "On all sides, the four great kings, shining brightly, stood."

For this was said: "On all sides, having come from the world-systems, the four directions, like fires blazing on the tops of mountains, stood very brightly."

But because they came with reference only to the Kapilavatthu grove, therefore, although they filled the world-system and stood equal to the world-system, they are said to be "in the Kapilavatthu grove."

mula_pali:
337.‘‘Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā, āguṃ āgū (syā.), āgu (sī. pī.) evamuparipi vañcanikā saṭhā.

Māyā kuṭeṇḍu viṭeṇḍu veṭeṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.), viṭucca viṭū ca (syā.) viṭuṭo saha.

veṭeṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.) viṭū ca (syā.)

‘‘Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu kinnughaṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.) nighaṇḍu ca;

kinnughaṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.)

Panādo opamañño ca, devasūto ca mātali.

‘‘Cittaseno ca gandhabbo, naḷorājā janesabho janosabho (syā.);

janosabho (syā.)

Āgā pañcasikho ceva, timbarū sūriyavaccasā suriyavaccasā (sī. pī.).

suriyavaccasā (sī. pī.)

‘‘Ete caññe ca rājāno, gandhabbā saha rājubhi;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.
mula_english:
337. "Those slaves of deceivers, conjurers, tricksters came.

Māyā, Kuṭeṇḍu, Veṭeṇḍu, Viṭu with Viṭuṭa,

Candana, Kāmaśreṣṭha, Kinnighaṇḍu, and Nighaṇḍu;

Panāda, Opamañña, Mātali, the deva’s charioteer,

Cittasena the Gandharva, Naḷorājā, Janesabha;

Pañcasikha came, and also Timbaru and Suriyavaccasā.

These and other kings, Gandharvas together with rulers,

Rejoicing, they approached the assembly of monks in the forest.
commentary_pali:
337.Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā, āguṃ vañcanikā saṭhāti tesaṃ mahārājānaṃ katapāpapaṭicchādanalakkhaṇāya māyāya yuttā kuṭilācārā dāsā atthi, ye sammukhaparammukhavañcanāhi lokaṃ vañcanato ‘‘vañcanikā’’ti ca, kerāṭiyasāṭheyyena samannāgatattā ‘‘saṭhā’’ti ca vuccanti, tepi āgatāti attho. Māyā kuṭeṇḍu viṭeṇḍu, viṭucca viṭuṭo sahāti te dāsā sabbepi māyākārakāva. Nāmena panettha eko kuṭeṇḍu nāma, eko viṭeṇḍu nāma. Pāḷiyaṃ pana ‘‘veṭeṇḍū’’ti likhanti. Eko viṭucca nāma, eko viṭuṭo nāma. Sahāti sopi viṭuṭo tehi saheva āgato.

Candanokāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu nighaṇḍu cāti aparo kinnighaṇḍu nāma. Pāḷiyaṃ pana ‘‘kinnughaṇḍū’’ti likhanti. Nighaṇḍu cāti añño nighaṇḍu nāma, ettakā dāsā. Ito pare pana –

Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu nighaṇḍu cā Nighaṇḍu cā

‘‘Panādo opamañño ca, devasuto ca mātali;

Cittaseno ca gandhabbo, naḷo rājā janesabho;

Āguṃ pañcasikho ceva, timbarū sūriyavacchasā’’ti. –

Ime devarājāno. Tattha devasutoti devasārathi. Cittasenoti citto ca seno ca cittaseno ca. Gandhabboti ayaṃ cittaseno gandhabbakāyiko devaputto, na kevalaṃ cesa, sabbe pete panādādayo gandhabbā eva. Naḷorājāti naḷakāradevaputto nāmeko. Janesabhoti janavasabho devaputto. Āguṃ pañcasikho cevāti pañcasikho ceva devaputto āgato. Timbarūti timbarū nāma gandhabbadevarājā. Sūriyavacchasāti tasseva dhītā.

devasuto Cittaseno Gandhabbo Naḷorājā Janesabho Āguṃ pañcasikho cevā Timbarū Sūriyavacchasā

Ete caññe ca rājāno, gandhabbā saha rājubhīti ete ca nāmavasena vuttagandhabbarājāno aññe ca etehi rājūhi saddhiṃ bahū gandhabbā. Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vananti haṭṭhatuṭṭhacittā bhikkhusaṅghasamitiṃ imaṃ vanaṃ āgatāti attho.

Ete caññe ca rājāno, gandhabbā saha rājubhī Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vana
commentary_english:
337. "Those deceitful slaves who are magicians, deceivers, and rogues" means that those great kings have slaves who are endowed with deceitful characteristics that conceal evil deeds, are of crooked conduct, and that there are deceitful people who deceive the world with face-to-face and behind-the-back deceptions; because they are accomplished in deceit and trickery, they are called "rogues"; this is the meaning of they have arrived.

"Illusion, Kuṭeṇḍu, Viṭeṇḍu, Viṭucca, Viṭuṭo, and Sahā" means that those slaves are all illusion-makers.

Here, one is named Kuṭeṇḍu, and the other is named Viṭeṇḍu.

In Pāli, they write "Veṭeṇḍū."

One is named Viṭucca, and the other is named Viṭuṭo.

"Sahā" means that Sopi Viṭuṭo came together with them.

Chandano, Kāmaseṭṭho, Kinnighaṇḍu, and Nighaṇḍu, another is named Kinnighaṇḍu.

In Pāli, they write "Kinnughaṇḍū."

Nighaṇḍu, another is named Nighaṇḍu, this many slaves.

Beyond this, Chandano, Kāmaseṭṭho, Kinnighaṇḍu, Nighaṇḍu, Nighaṇḍu

“Panāda, Opamañña, Devasuta, and Mātali;

Cittasena the Gandharva, Naḷa the king, Janesabha;

Āguṃ Pañcasikha also, Timbaru Sūriyavacchasā.”

These are the kings of the gods.

There, Devasuta means the charioteer of the gods. (devasārathi).

Cittasena means Citto, Sena, and Cittasena.

Gandhabba means this Cittasena, a Gandharva-bodied son of the gods, not only this one, but all of those, Panāda and the others, are Gandharvas.

Naḷorājā means one named Naḷakāradevaputta.

Janesabha means Janavasabha, son of the gods.

Āguṃ Pañcasikha also means that Pañcasikha also, son of the gods, has arrived.

Timbarū means Timbarū, named Gandharva king of the gods.

Sūriyavacchasā means his daughter.

Devasuto, Cittasena, Gandhabba, Naḷorājā, Janesabha, Āguṃ Pañcasikha also, Timbarū, Sūriyavacchasā

"These and other kings, Gandharvas together with the rulers," means these Gandharva kings named, and other Gandharvas together with these kings, many Gandharvas.

“Rejoicing, they approached, the assembly of monks in the forest,” means with joyful minds they came to this forest, the assembly of the Saṅgha of monks.

These and other kings, Gandharvas together with the rulers Rejoicing, they approached, the assembly of monks in the forest

mula_pali:
338.‘‘Athāguṃ nāgasā nāgā, vesālā sahatacchakā.

Kambalassatarā āguṃ, pāyāgā saha ñātibhi.

‘‘Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā ca, āgū nāgā yasassino;

Erāvaṇo mahānāgo, sopāgā samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Ye nāgarāje sahasā haranti, dibbā dijā pakkhi visuddhacakkhū;

Vehāyasā vehāsayā (sī. pī.) te vanamajjhapattā, citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāmaṃ.

vehāsayā (sī. pī.)

‘‘Abhayaṃ tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddho;

Saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā, nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddhaṃ.
mula_english:
Then there have also come nāgas from Lake Nābhasa, Vesālī & Tacchaka.

The Kambalas, and Assataras came, and (nāgas) from Pāyāga with their kin.

The Yamunā, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the glorious nāgas came;

Erāvaṇa, the great nāga, came, together with those who went to the assembly, to the forest.

Those nāga kings who violently seize, divine birds, winged, with pure eyes;

came from the sky to the midst of the forest. Citra & Supaṇṇa are their names.

But the Buddha made the nāga kings safe, made them secure from Supaṇṇa.

Addressing one another with affectionate words, the *nāgas* & *supaṇṇas* made the Buddha their refuge.
commentary_pali:
338.Athāguṃ nāgasā nāgā, vesālā sahatacchakāti nāgasadahavāsikā ca vesālīvāsikā ca nāgā saha tacchakanāgaparisāya āgatāti attho. Kambalassatarāti kambalo ca assataro ca. Ete kira sinerupāde vasanti, supaṇṇehipi anuddharaṇīyā mahesakkhanāgā pāyāgā saha ñātibhīti payāgatitthavāsino ca saha ñātisaṅghena āgatā.

Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā cāti yamunavāsino ca dhataraṭṭhakule uppannā nāgā ca. Erāvaṇo mahānāgoti erāvaṇo ca devaputto, jātiyā nāgo na hoti. Nāgavohārena panesa vohariyati. Sopāgāti sopi āgato.

Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā cā Erāvaṇo mahānāgo Sopāgā

Yenāgarāje sahasā harantīti ye ime vuttappakāre nāge lobhābhibhūtā sāhasaṃ katvā haranti gaṇhanti. Dibbā dijā pakkhī visuddhacakkhūti dibbānubhāvato dibbā mātukucchito ca aṇḍakosato cāti dve vāre jātāti dijā pakkhayuttatāya pakkhī yojanasatantarepi yojanasahassantarepi nāge dassanasamatthacakkhutāya visuddhacakkhū. Vehāyasāte vanamajjhappattāti te ākāseneva imaṃ mahāvanaṃ sampattā. Citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāmanti tesaṃ ‘‘citrasupaṇṇā’’ti nāmaṃ.

Ye nāgarāje sahasā harantī Dibbā dijā pakkhī visuddhacakkhū Vehāyasā te vanamajjhappattā Citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāma

Abhayaṃtadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddhoti tasmā sabbepi te aññamaññaṃ saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā mittā viya bandhavā viya ca samullapantā sammodamānā āliṅgantā hatthe gaṇhantā aṃsakūṭe hatthaṃ ṭhapentā haṭṭhatuṭṭhacittā. Nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddhanti buddhaṃyeva saraṇaṃ gatā.

Abhayaṃ tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddho saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā Nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddha
commentary_english:
338. *Athāguṃ nāgasā nāgā, vesālā sahatacchakā* means that the Nāgas from Nāgasada, and the Vesālī Nāgas together with the Tacchaka-Nāga assembly have arrived.

*Kambalassatarā* means Kambala and Assatara.

These dwell at the foot of Mount Sumeru, powerful Nāgas who cannot be drawn out by the *Garudas*. *Pāyāgā saha ñātibhī* means that those dwelling at the sacred site of Prayāga have arrived together with a group of relatives.

*Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā cā* means that the Yamuna dwellers and the Nāgas born in the lineage of Dhritarashtra [have arrived].

*Erāvaṇo mahānāgo* means that Airavana is a son of the gods; by birth, he is not a *Nāga*.

He is referred to by the designation Nāga.

*Sopāgā* means that he too has arrived.

*Nāgarāje sahasā harantī* means that those who, overcome by greed, recklessly seize and carry away the Nāgas of the Nāga realm.

*Dibbā dijā pakkhī visuddhacakkhū* means that the divine twice-born birds with pure vision, twice-born because they are born from divine power, from a divine womb, and from an egg, and birds because they have wings, have pure vision because they are able to see Nāgas even at a distance of a hundred or a thousand *yojanas*.

*Vehāyasā*

*Te vanamajjhappattā* means that they have reached this great forest as if through the sky.

*Citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāma* means that their name is Citrasupaṇṇā.

*Nāgarāje sahasā harantī* *Dibbā dijā pakkhī visuddhacakkhū* *Vehāyasā*

*Te vanamajjhappattā* *Citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāma*

*Abhayaṃ*

*Tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddho* means that therefore all those who are calling out to each other with gentle words are like friends, like relatives, conversing together, rejoicing, embracing, holding hands, placing their hands on each other's shoulders, their minds filled with joy and gladness.

*Nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddha* means that the Nāgas and the *Garudas* have gone to the Buddha for refuge.

*Abhayaṃ*

*Tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddho* *Saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā* *Nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddha*

mula_pali:
339.‘‘Jitā vajirahatthena, samuddaṃ asurāsitā.

Bhātaro vāsavassete, iddhimanto yasassino.

‘‘Kālakañcā mahābhismā kālakañjā mahābhiṃsā (sī. pī.), asurā dānaveghasā;

kālakañjā mahābhiṃsā (sī. pī.)

Vepacitti sucitti ca, pahārādo namucī saha.

‘‘Satañca baliputtānaṃ, sabbe verocanāmakā;

Sannayhitvā balisenaṃ balīsenaṃ (syā.), rāhubhaddamupāgamuṃ;

balīsenaṃ (syā.)

Samayodāni bhaddante, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.
commentary_pali:
339.Jitā vajirahatthenāti indena devaraññā jitā. Samuddaṃ asurāsitāti mahāsamuddavāsino sujātāya asurakaññāya kāraṇā sabbepi bhātaro vāsavassete, iddhimanto yasassino.

Tesu kālakañcā mahābhismāti kālakañcā ca mahante bhiṃsane attabhāve māpetvā āgamiṃsu. Asurā dānaveghasāti dānaveghasā nāma aññe dhanuggahaasurā. Vepacitti sucitti ca, pahārādo namucī sahāti vepacittiasuro, sucittiasuro cāti ete ca asurā namuci ca māro devaputto etehi saheva āgato. Ime asurā mahāsamuddavāsino, ayaṃ paranimmitadevalokavāsī, kasmā etehi sahāgatoti? Acchandikattā. Tepi hi acchandikā abhabbā, ayampi tādisoyeva. Tasmā dhātuso saṃsandamāno āgato.

kālakañcā mahābhismā Asurā dānaveghasāti dānaveghasā Vepacitti sucitti ca, pahārādo namucī sahā

Satañca baliputtānanti balino mahāasurassa puttānaṃ sataṃ. Sabbe verocanāmakāti sabbe attano mātulassa rāhusseva nāmadharā. Sannayhitvā balisenanti attano balisenaṃ sannayhitvā sabbe katasannāhāva hutvā. Rāhubhaddamupāgamunti rāhuasurindaṃ upasaṅkamiṃsu. Samayodāni bhaddanteti bhaddaṃ tava hotu, samayo te bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ dassanāyāti attho.

Satañca baliputtāna Sabbe verocanāmakā Sannayhitvā balisena Rāhubhaddamupāgamu Samayo dāni bhaddante
commentary_english:
339. "Jitā vajirahatthenā" means, conquered by Indra, the king of gods.

"Samuddaṃ asurāsitā" means, because of Sujātā, the daughter of the *asura* who dwells in the great ocean, all the brothers of Vāsava, were powerful and glorious.

Among them, "Kālakañcā mahābhismā" means, Kālakañcā, creating a great and terrible form, arrived.

"Asurā dānaveghasāti dānaveghasā" means, other *asuras* named Dānaveghasa, who are archer *asuras*.

"Vepacitti Sucitti ca, Pahārādo Namucī sahā" means, the *asura* Vepacitti, the *asura* Sucitti, and also these *asuras* Namuci, Māra the son of a god, came together with them.

These *asuras* dwell in the great ocean, and this one dwells in the Paranirmitadeva heaven. Why did he come with them? Because of being uncontrolled.

They too are uncontrolled and incapable; this one is also just like that.

Therefore, associating with the elements, he has come.

Kālakañcā Mahābhismā, Asurā Dānaveghasāti Dānaveghasā, Vepacitti Sucitti ca, Pahārādo Namucī sahā

"Satañca baliputtāna" means, a hundred sons of Bali, the great powerful *asura*.

"Sabbe verocanāmakā" means, all are named after their maternal uncle, Rāhu.

"Sannayhitvā balisena" means, having gathered his army, and having all made preparations.

"Rāhubhaddamupāgamu" means, they approached Rāhu, the lord of the *asuras*.

"Samayo dāni bhaddante" means, may good be to you, now is the time for you to go to the forest meeting place of the *bhikkhus* and see the *bhikkhu* *saṃgha*.

Satañca baliputtāna, Sabbe verocanāmakā, Sannayhitvā balisena, Rāhubhaddamupāgamu, Samayo dāni bhaddante

340.‘‘Āpo ca devā pathavī, tejo vāyo tadāgamuṃ.

Varuṇā vāraṇā vāruṇā (syā.) devā, somo ca yasasā saha.

vāruṇā (syā.)

‘‘Mettā karuṇā kāyikā, āguṃ devā yasassino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

‘‘Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Veṇḍudevā sahali ca veṇhūca devā sahalīca (sī. pī.), asamā ca duve yamā;

veṇhūca devā sahalīca (sī. pī.)

Candassūpanisā devā, candamāguṃ purakkhatvā.

‘‘Sūriyassūpanisā suriyassūpanisā (sī. syā. pī.) devā, sūriyamāguṃ purakkhatvā;

suriyassūpanisā (sī. syā. pī.)

Nakkhattāni purakkhatvā, āguṃ mandavalāhakā.

‘‘Vasūnaṃ vāsavo seṭṭho, sakkopāgā purindado;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

‘‘Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Athāguṃ sahabhū devā, jalamaggisikhāriva;

Ariṭṭhakā ca rojā ca, umāpupphanibhāsino.

‘‘Varuṇā sahadhammā ca, accutā ca anejakā;

Sūleyyarucirā āguṃ, āguṃ vāsavanesino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

‘‘Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Samānā mahāsamanā, mānusā mānusuttamā;

Khiḍḍāpadosikā āguṃ, āguṃ manopadosikā.

‘‘Athāguṃ harayo devā, ye ca lohitavāsino;

Pāragā mahāpāragā, āguṃ devā yasassino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

‘‘Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Sukkā karambhā karumhā (sī. syā. pī.) aruṇā, āguṃ veghanasā saha;

karumhā (sī. syā. pī.)

Odātagayhā pāmokkhā, āguṃ devā vicakkhaṇā.

‘‘Sadāmattā hāragajā, missakā ca yasassino;

Thanayaṃ āga pajjunno, yo disā abhivassati.

‘‘Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Khemiyā tusitā yāmā, kaṭṭhakā ca yasassino;

Lambītakā lāmaseṭṭhā, jotināmā ca āsavā;

Nimmānaratino āguṃ, athāguṃ paranimmitā.

‘‘Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Saṭṭhete devanikāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Nāmanvayena āgacchuṃ āgañchuṃ (sī. syā. pī.), ye caññe sadisā saha.

āgañchuṃ (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘‘Pavuṭṭhajātimakhilaṃ pavutthajātiṃ akhilaṃ (sī. pī.), oghatiṇṇamanāsavaṃ;

pavutthajātiṃ akhilaṃ (sī. pī.)

Dakkhemoghataraṃ nāgaṃ, candaṃva asitātigaṃ’.

Varuṇā vāraṇā devā, somo ca yasasā sahāti varuṇadevatā , vāraṇadevatā, somadevatāti evaṃ nāmakā ca devā yasasā nāma devena sahāgatāti attho. Mettākaruṇākāyikāti mettājhāne ca karuṇājhāne ca parikammaṃ katvā nibbattadevā. Āguṃ devā yasassinoti etepi mahāyasā devā āgatā.

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇinoti te dasadhā ṭhitā dasa devakāyā sabbe nīlādivasena nānattavaṇṇā āgatāti attho.

Nakkhattāni purakkhatvāti nakkhattanissitāpi devā nakkhattāni purato katvā āgatā. Āguṃ mandavalāhakāti vātavalāhakā, abbhavalāhakā, uṇhavalāhakā ete sabbepi valāhakāyikā ‘‘mandavalāhakā’’ nāma vuccanti. Tepi āgatāti attho. Vasūnaṃ vāsavo seṭṭho, sakkopāgā purindadoti vasūnaṃ devatānaṃ seṭṭho vāsavo yo sakkoti ca, purindadoti ca vuccati, sopi āgato.
