340. "Water and the gods, the earth, fire, and air came then," [meaning:] having performed the preliminary work in the water-sphere and so on, the gods called "water" and so on came.

"Varuṇas, Vāraṇas, gods, Soma together with Yasa," [meaning:] Varuṇa deity, Vāraṇa deity, Soma deity—thus, the gods called by these names came together with the deity named Yasa.

"Those who are embodied by loving-kindness and compassion," [meaning:] the gods who are embodied through the preliminary work in the meditation of loving-kindness and the meditation of compassion.

"The gods who are famous came," [meaning:] these powerful gods also came.

"These ten tenfold hosts, all of varied hue," [meaning:] those ten groups of gods, standing tenfold, all came with varied hues because of blue and so on.

"These ten tenfold hosts, all of varied hue," "Veṇḍū and the gods," [meaning:] Veṇḍu deity also.

"Sahali also," [meaning:] Sahali deity also.

"Asamā and the two Yamas," [meaning:] Asamā deity also, and the two Yamaka gods.

"The gods who abide by the moon, having placed the moon in front," [meaning:] the gods who depend on the moon came having put the moon in front.

Likewise, the gods who depend on the sun came having put the sun in front.

"Having placed the constellations in front," [meaning:] even the gods who depend on the constellations came having put the constellations in front.

"The slow cloud-carriers came," [meaning:] wind-cloud carriers, rain-cloud carriers, hot-cloud carriers—all of these who are embodied as cloud-carriers are called "slow cloud-carriers."

They also came, [is the] meaning.

"Among the Vasus, Vāsava is the best, Sakko came, Purindada," [meaning:] among the Vasus deities, Vāsava is the best, he who is called Sakko also, and Purindada also, he also came.

"Veṇḍū and the gods," "Sahali also," "Asamā and the two Yamas," "The gods who abide by the moon, having placed the moon in front," "Having placed the constellations in front," "The slow cloud-carriers came," "Among the Vasus, Vāsava is the best, Sakko came, Purindada," "These ten tenfold hosts," [meaning:] these ten groups of gods also came tenfold.

"All of varied hue," [meaning:] of varied hues because of blue and so on.

"These ten tenfold hosts, all of varied hue," "Then the Sahabhū gods came," [meaning:] then the gods named Sahabhū came.

"Like a flame of fire," [meaning:] blazing like a flame of fire.

"Jalamaggi and Sikhārivā," these are said to be their names also.

"Ariṭṭhakā and Rojā," [meaning:] Ariṭṭhaka gods and Roja gods also.

"Those who appear like Umā flowers," [meaning:] these gods are named Umā flower gods.

For the radiance of their bodies is like Umā flowers; therefore, they are called "those who appear like Umā flowers."

"Then the Sahabhū gods came," "Like a flame of fire," "Ariṭṭhakā and Rojā," "Those who appear like Umā flowers," "Umā flower gods" "Varuṇas and Sahadhammās," [meaning:] these also [are] two people.

"Accutās and Anejakās," [meaning:] Accutā deity and Anejakā deity also.

"Suleyyarucirā came," [meaning:] Suleyyā and Rucirā also came.

"The Vāsavanesin gods came," [meaning:] the gods named Vāsavanesī came.

"These ten tenfold hosts," [meaning:] these ten groups of gods also came tenfold.

"Varuṇas and Sahadhammās," "Accutās and Anejakās," "Suleyyarucirā" "came," "The Vāsavanesin gods came," "These ten tenfold hosts," "Samānās and Mahāsamānās," [meaning:] Samānās also, and Mahāsamānās also.

"Mānusās and Mānusuttamās," [meaning:] Mānusās also, and Mānusuttamās also.

"Khiḍḍāpadosikās came, Manopadosikās came," [meaning:] Khiḍḍāpadosikā, Manopadosikā, and the gods came.

"Samānās and Mahāsamānās," "Mānusās and Mānusuttamās," "Khiḍḍāpadosikās came, Manopadosikās came," "Then the Haraya gods came," [meaning:] the Harideva gods came.

"And those who dwell in the red," [meaning:] the Lohitavāsinas also came.
These who have crossed over (pāragā), those who have greatly crossed over (mahāpāragā) have come here, and they are of two kinds.
These ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā) have come, these ten deva-bodies (dasadevakāyā) have come in ten ways.

Then came the reddish-brown (harayo) gods (devā), and those who dwell in red (lohitavāsino), these who have crossed over (pāragā), those who have greatly crossed over (mahāpāragā), these ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā). These gods called Sukkā, Karambhā, Aruṇā, who came together with Veghanasā, have come here.
These gods with white necks (odātagayhā), the Pāmokkha deities (pāmokkhadevā) have come.
These discerning (vicakkhaṇā) gods (devā) have come.

These gods called Sukkā, Karambhā, Aruṇā, who came together with Veghanasā, these gods with white necks (odātagayhā), the Pāmokkha deities (pāmokkhadevā), these discerning (vicakkhaṇā) gods (devā), these gods who are always joyful (sadāmattā) and the Hāragaja gods,
the mixed (missakā) gods with fame (yasassino), Pajjunna the king of the gods (devarājā) who thunders (thanayanto) has come.
He who rains on the directions (yo disā abhivassatī): whichever direction (disam) he goes (yāti), in that place (tattha tattha) the god (devo) rains (vassati).
These ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā) have come, these ten deva-bodies (dasadevakāyā) have come in ten ways.

These gods who are always joyful (sadāmattā) and the Hāragaja gods, the mixed (missakā) gods with fame (yasassino), Pajjunna the king of the gods (devarājā) who thunders (thanayanto) has come, He who rains on the directions (yo disā abhivassatī), these ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā), the Khemiyā gods, the Tusita gods who dwell in the city of Tusita (tusitapuravāsino), and the Yama gods who dwell in the Yama heaven (yāmadevalokavāsino),
the Kathaka gods with fame (yasassino), In Pāḷi they write "Kaṭṭhakā cā".
The Lambītaka gods and the Lāmaseṭṭha gods.
The Jotināmā gods and the Āsavā gods: There are gods named Jotidevā shining like a fire on the mountain peak, and those Āsā gods have come, this is the meaning.
In Pāḷi they write "Jātināmā".
The Āsā deities are called Āsavā because of their inclination.
The Nimmānaratino have come, and the Paranimmita.
These ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā) have come, these ten deva-bodies (dasadevakāyā) have come in ten ways.

The Khemiyā gods, the Tusita gods, the Yama gods, the Kathaka gods with fame (yasassino), the Lambītaka gods and the Lāmaseṭṭha gods, the Jotināmā gods and the Āsavā gods, the Āsavā gods, the Nimmānaratino have come, and the Paranimmita.
These ten bodies (dasete dasadhā kāyā).
The Saṭṭhete deva-groups (devanikāyā) are these: the sixty (saṭṭhi) deva-groups (devanikāyā), starting with the water gods (āpo ca deva) etc., are all of various colors because of blue etc.
They come with name-agreement (nāmanvayena āgacchu), they have come with a share of name (nāmabhāgena), with a name division (nāmakoṭṭhāsena).
Those others who are similar (sadisā) together (sahā): Those other gods (devā) in the remaining world-circles (sesacakkavāḷesu) who are similar (sadisā) to these in color (vaṇṇatopi) and in name (nāmatopi), all those gods are indicated with just one word (ekapadeneva), as if having made a bundle (kalāpaṃ) or a wrapping (puṭakaṃ).

The Saṭṭhete deva-groups (devanikāyā), they come with name-agreement (nāmanvayena āgacchu), those others who are similar (sadisā) together (sahā): Thus, having indicated the deva-bodies (devakāye) in those thousands of ten world-elements (dasasu lokadhātusahassesu), now, showing the reason (yadatthaṃ) for which they have come, he speaks (āha) the verse (gāthaṃ): "Pavuṭṭhajāti".
Its meaning (tassattho): The noble (ariya) Saṃgha is named Pavuṭṭhajāti, because birth is gone (vigatā jāti) for them (assa); We shall see (dakkhema passissāma) that Pavuṭṭhajāti, the one without thorns (akhīlaṃ) because of the absence of the thorns (khīlānaṃ abhāvā) of passion (rāga), hatred (dosa), and delusion (moha), the one who has crossed the four floods (oghe taritvā ṭhitattā), the one who has crossed the flood (oghatiṇṇaṃ), the one without influxes (anāsavaṃ) because of the absence of the four influxes (āsavānaṃ abhāvena).
Because they have crossed those very floods (oghānaṃ tiṇṇattā), they are better than the flood (oghataraṃ), because they do not create (akaraṇato), they are Nāga.
"Asitātiga": We shall see (dakkhema passissāma) the one gone beyond the state of darkness (kāḷakabhāvātītaṃ), shining with glory (siriyā virocamānaṃ) like the moon (candaṃva), and the one with the ten powers (dasabalañca), thus for that reason (etadatthaṃ) all those (sabbepi te) have come with name-agreement (nāmanvayena āgacchuṃ), those others who are similar (sadisā) together (sahā).

Pavuṭṭhajāti, that Pavuṭṭhajāti, the one without thorns (akhīlaṃ), the one who has crossed the flood (oghatiṇṇaṃ), the one without influxes (anāsavaṃ), the one better than the flood (oghataraṃ), the Nāga.
Asitātiga

341.‘‘Subrahmā paramatto ca paramattho ca (ka.), puttā iddhimato saha.

Sanaṅkumāro tisso ca, sopāga samitiṃ vanaṃ.

‘‘Sahassaṃ brahmalokānaṃ, mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhati;

Upapanno jutimanto, bhismākāyo yasassiso.

‘‘Dasettha issarā āguṃ, paccekavasavattino;

Tesañca majjhato āga, hārito parivārito.
commentary_pali:
341. Idāni brahmāno dassento subrahmā paramatto cātiādimāha. Tattha subrahmāti eko brahmā. Paramattopi brahmāva. Puttā iddhimato sahāti ete iddhimato buddhassa bhagavato puttā ariyabrahmāno saheva āgatā. Sanaṅkumāro tisso cāti sanaṅkumāro ca tissamahābrahmā ca. Sopāgāti sopi āgato.

‘‘Sahassaṃ brahmalokānaṃ, mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhati;

Upapanno jutimanto, bhismākāyo yasassi so’’ti. –

Ettha sahassaṃ brahmalokānanti ekaṅguliyā ekasahassacakkavāḷe dasahi aṅgulīhi dasasahassicakkavāḷe ālokapharaṇasamatthānaṃ mahābrahmānaṃ sahassaṃ āgataṃ. Mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhatīti yattha ekeko mahābrahmā aññe brahme abhibhavitvā tiṭṭhati. Upapannoti brahmaloke nibbatto. Jutimantoti ānubhāvasampanno. Bhismākāyoti mahākāyo, dvīhi tīhi māgadhikehi gāmakkhettehi samappamāṇaattabhāvo. Yasassisoti attabhāvasirīsaṅkhātena yasena samannāgato.

sahassaṃ brahmalokāna Mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhatī Upapanno Jutimanto Bhismākāyo Yasassiso

Dasettha issarā āguṃ, paccekavasavattinoti etasmiñca brahmasahasse ye pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ vasaṃ vattenti, evarūpā dasa issarā mahābrahmāno āgatā. Tesañca majjhato āga, hārito parivāritoti tesaṃ brahmānaṃ majjhe hārito nāma mahābrahmā satasahassabrahmaparivāro āgato.

Dasettha issarā āguṃ, paccekavasavattino Tesañca majjhato āga, hārito parivārito
commentary_english:
341. Now, showing the *brahmās*, he said "Subrahmā and Paramatta" etc.

There, *Subrahmā* is one Brahmā. Paramatta is also a Brahmā.

"The sons, along with the powerful one": these sons of the powerful Buddha, the Blessed One, the noble *brahmās*, came together.

"Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa": Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa Mahābrahmā also.

"Sopāga": he also came.

"A thousand Brahmā worlds, Mahābrahmā abides;

Endowed, radiant, Bhismākāya, glorious, he."

Here, "a thousand Brahmā worlds": in one finger's breadth, a thousand world-systems; in ten fingers' breadth, ten thousand world-systems; a thousand Mahābrahmās, capable of spreading light, came.

"Mahābrahmā abides": where each Mahābrahmā, having overcome the other *brahmās*, abides.

"Endowed": born in the Brahmā world (*brahmaloke* *nibbatto*).

"Radiant": endowed with power.

"Bhismākāya": having a great body, an existence equal in extent to two or three Magadhan village fields.

"Glorious": endowed with glory (*yasa*) known as the splendor of existence (*attabhāvasirisaṅkhātena* *yasena* *samannāgato*).

"Here ten lords came, each controlling": in this thousand of Brahmās, those ten lords, each wielding power individually, came.

"And from their midst came Hārita, surrounded": from the midst of those Brahmās came a Mahābrahmā named Hārita, surrounded by a retinue of a hundred thousand Brahmās.

"Here ten lords came, each controlling, and from their midst came Hārita, surrounded."

mula_pali:
342.‘‘Te ca sabbe abhikkante, sainde sinde (syā.) deve sabrahmake.

Mārasenā abhikkāmi, passa kaṇhassa mandiyaṃ.

‘‘‘Etha gaṇhatha bandhatha, rāgena baddhamatthu vo;

Samantā parivāretha, mā vo muñcittha koci naṃ’.

‘‘Iti tattha mahāseno, kaṇho senaṃ apesayi;

Pāṇinā talamāhacca, saraṃ katvāna bheravaṃ.

‘‘Yathā pāvussako megho, thanayanto savijjuko; +

Tadā so paccudāvatti, saṅkuddho asayaṃvase asayaṃvasī (sī. pī.).

asayaṃvasī (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
342. When all of them had advanced, along with the *sainde* deities together with Brahmā.

The army of Māra advanced. Behold the dullness of Kaṇha!

"Come, seize, bind! May your aim be bound by passion.

Surround [him] on all sides, lest anyone release him."

Thus there the great general, Kaṇha, urged on his army,

striking the surface with his hand, making a frightening sound.

Just as a rain-cloud, thundering, with lightning,

then he turned back, enraged, not self-controlled.
commentary_pali:
342.Te ca sabbe abhikkante, sainde deve sabrahmaketi te sabbepi sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā āgate devakāye, hāritamahābrahmānaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā āgate brahmakāye ca. Mārasenā abhikkāmīti mārasenā abhigatā. Passa kaṇhassa mandiyanti kāḷakassa mārasa bālabhāvaṃ passatha.

Etha gaṇhatha bandhathāti evaṃ attano parisaṃ āṇāpesi. Rāgena baddhamatthu voti sabbaṃ vo idaṃ devamaṇḍalaṃ rāgena baddhaṃ hotu. Samantā parivāretha, mā vo muñcittha koci nanti tumhākaṃ ekopi etesu ekampi mā muñci. ‘‘Mā vo muñcethā’’tipi pāṭho, esevattho.

Etha gaṇhatha bandhathā Rāgena baddhamatthu vo Samantā parivāretha, mā vo muñcittha koci na

Iti tattha mahāseno, kaṇho senaṃ apesayī Pāṇinā talamāhaccā Saraṃ katvāna bherava

Yathā pāvussako megho, thanayanto savijjukoti savijjuko pāvussakamegho viya mahāgajjitaṃ gajjanto. Tadā so paccudāvattīti tasmiṃ samaye so māro taṃ vibhiṃsanakaṃ dassetvā paṭinivatto . Saṅkuddho asayaṃ vaseti suṭṭhu kuddho kupito kañci vase vattetuṃ asakkonto asayaṃvase asayaṃvasī attano vasena akāmako hutvā nivatto. Bhagavā kira ‘‘ayaṃ māro imaṃ mahāsamāgamaṃ disvā ‘abhisamayantarāyaṃ karissāmī’ti antarantare mārasenaṃ pesetvā māraṃ vibhiṃsakaṃ dassetī’’ti aññāsi. Pakati cesā bhagavato, yattha abhisamayo na bhavissati, tattha māraṃ vibhiṃsakaṃ dassentaṃ na nivāreti. Yattha pana abhisamayo hoti, tattha yathā parisā neva mārassa rūpaṃ passati, na saddaṃ suṇāti, evaṃ adhiṭṭhātīti. Imasmiñca samāgame mahābhisamayo bhavissati, tasmā yathā devatā neva tassa rūpaṃ passanti, na saddaṃ suṇanti, evaṃ adhiṭṭhāsi. Tena vuttaṃ –‘‘tadā so paccudāvatti, saṅkuddho asayaṃvase’’ti.

Yathā pāvussako megho, thanayanto savijjuko Tadā so paccudāvattī Saṅkuddho asayaṃ vase
commentary_english:
342. Now when they had all drawn near, Inda with the gods and the brahmās, that is, they all arrived in the company of gods, having made Śakra, the king of the gods, the most senior; and they arrived in the company of Brahmās, having made Hāritamahābrahmā the most senior.
The army of Māra approaches, that is, the army of Māra has arrived.
Behold the stupidity of Kanhha, that is, behold the foolishness of Kālaka Māra.

Come, seize, bind, thus he commanded his own retinue.
May you be bound by passion, that is, may this entire divine circle of yours be bound by passion.
Surround [him] on all sides, may none of you release [him], that is, may not even one of you release even one of them.
There is also a reading, "Do not release [him]", this is the meaning.

Come, seize, bind! May you be bound by passion! Surround [him] on all sides, may none of you release [him]! Thus there the great general, Kanhha, commanded the army. Thus at that great assembly, Mahāsena Māra commanded the army of Māra.
Having struck the surface with [his] hand, that is, having struck the surface of the earth with [his] hand.
Having made a terrifying sound, that is, having made a terrifying sound for the sake of showing what frightens Māra.

Thus there the great general, Kanhha, commanded the army.
Having struck the surface with [his] hand, having made a terrifying sound,
Just as a rainy-season cloud, thundering and flashing with lightning, that is, like a rainy-season cloud flashing with lightning, thundering with a great roar.
Then he retreated, that is, at that time Māra, having shown that frightful thing, retreated.
Enraged, not being in control of himself, that is, being very angry and enraged, unable to bring anyone under his control, not being in control of himself, being subservient to his own will, and unwilling, he retreated.
The Blessed One knew, "This Māra, having seen this great assembly, thinking, 'I will cause an obstruction to enlightenment,' sending the army of Māra from time to time, is showing Māra's frightful form."
This is the nature of the Blessed One: where there will be no enlightenment, there he does not restrain Māra from showing a frightful form.
But where there will be enlightenment, there, as if the assembly does not see Māra's form, nor hears a sound, thus he resolves.
And in this assembly there will be great enlightenment; therefore, just as the gods do not see his form, nor hear a sound, thus he resolved.
Therefore it was said: "Then he retreated, enraged, not being in control of himself."

Just as a rainy-season cloud, thundering and flashing with lightning, then he retreated, enraged, not being in control of himself.

mula_pali:
343. Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya, vavatthitvāna cakkhumā.

Tato āmantayī satthā, sāvake sāsane rate.

‘‘Mārasenā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo;

Te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Vītarāgehi pakkāmuṃ, nesaṃ lomāpi iñjayuṃ.

‘‘‘Sabbe vijitasaṅgāmā, bhayātītā yasassino;

Modanti saha bhūtehi, sāvakā te janesutā’’ti.

Mahāsamayasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
commentary_pali:
343.Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya, vavatthitvāna cakkhumāti taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavā jānitvā vavatthapetvā ca.

Mārasenā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavoti bhikkhave mārasenā abhikkantā, te tumhe attano anurūpaṃ vijānātha, phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjathāti vadati. Ātappamakarunti phalasamāpattiṃ pavisanatthāya vīriyaṃ ārabhiṃsu. Vītarāgehi pakkāmunti māro ca mārasenā ca vītarāgehi ariyehi dūratova apakkamuṃ. Nesaṃ lomāpi iñjayunti tesaṃ vītarāgānaṃ lomānipi na cālayiṃsu. Atha māro bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Mārasenā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo Ātappamakaru Vītarāgehi pakkāmu Nesaṃ lomāpi iñjayu

‘‘Sabbe vijitasaṅgāmā, bhayātītā yasassino;

Modanti saha bhūtehi, sāvakā te janesutā’’ti.

Tattha modanti saha bhūtehīti dasabalassa sāsane bhūtehi sañjātehi ariyehi saddhiṃ modanti pamodanti. Janesutāti jane vissutā pākaṭā abhiññātā.

modanti saha bhūtehī Janesutā

Idaṃ pana mahāsamayasuttaṃ nāma devatānaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ, tasmā maṅgalaṃ vadantena abhinavaṭṭhānesu idameva suttaṃ vattabbaṃ. Devatā kira –‘‘imaṃ suttaṃ suṇissāmā’’ti ohitasotā vicaranti. Desanāpariyosāne panassa koṭisatasahassadevatā arahattaṃ pattā, sotāpannādīnaṃ gaṇanā natthi.

Devatānañcassa piyamanāpabhāve idaṃ vatthu – koṭipabbatavihāre kira nāgaleṇadvāre nāgarukkhe ekā devadhītā vasati. Eko daharo antoleṇe imaṃ suttaṃ sajjhāyati. Devadhītā sutvā suttapariyosāne mahāsaddena sādhukāramadāsi. Ko esoti. Ahaṃ, bhante, devadhītāti. Kasmā sādhukāramadāsīti? Bhante, dasabalena mahāvane nisīditvā kathitadivase imaṃ suttaṃ sutvā ajja assosiṃ, bhagavatā kathitato ekakkharampi ahāpetvā suggahito ayaṃ dhammo tumhehīti. Dasabalassa kathayato sutaṃ tayāti? Āma, bhanteti. Mahā kira devatāsannipāto ahosi, tvaṃ kattha ṭhitā suṇīti?

Ahaṃ, bhante, mahāvanavāsiyā devatā, mahesakkhāsu pana devatāsu āgacchantīsu jambudīpe okāsaṃ nālatthaṃ, atha imaṃ tambapaṇṇidīpaṃ āgantvā jambukolapaṭṭane ṭhatvā sotuṃ āraddhamhi, tatrāpi mahesakkhāsu devatāsu āgacchantīsu anukkamena paṭikkamamānā rohaṇajanapade mahāgāmassa piṭṭhibhāgato samudde galappamāṇaṃ udakaṃ pavisitvā tattha ṭhitā assosinti. Tuyhaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato dūre satthāraṃ passasi devateti? Kiṃ kathetha, bhante, satthā mahāvane dhammaṃ desento nirantaraṃ mamaññeva oloketīti maññamānā otappamānā ūmīsu nilayāmīti.

Taṃ divasaṃ kira koṭisatasahassadevatā arahattaṃ pattā, tumhepi tadā arahattaṃ pattāti? Natthi, bhante. Anāgāmiphalaṃ pattattha maññeti? Natthi, bhante. Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ pattattha maññeti? Natthi, bhante. Tayo magge pattā devatā kira gaṇanapathaṃ atītā, sotāpannā jātattha maññeti? Devatā taṃ divasaṃ sotāpattiphalaṃ pattattā harāyamānā –‘‘apucchitabbaṃ pucchati ayyo’’ti āha. Tato naṃ so bhikkhu āha – ‘‘sakkā pana devate, tava attabhāvaṃ amhākaṃ dassetu’’nti? Na sakkā bhante sakalakāyaṃ dassetuṃ, aṅgulipabbamattaṃ dassessāmi ayyassāti kuñcikachiddena aṅguliṃ antoleṇābhimukhaṃ akāsi, candasahassasūriyasahassauggamanakālo viya ahosi. Devadhītā ‘‘appamattā, bhante, hothā’’ti daharabhikkhuṃ vanditvā agamāsi. Evaṃ imaṃ suttaṃ devatānaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ, mamāyanti naṃ devatāti.

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Mahāsamayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
343. "And the Seeing One, having directly known all that, having ascertained,"—the Blessed One, having known and ascertained all that.

"The army of Māra has departed; you monks, understand that"—O monks, the army of Māra has departed; you, understanding that it is appropriate for you, should undertake the attainment of the fruit ( *phalasamāpatti* )."

"Having made effort"—they began effort for the sake of entering the attainment of the fruit (*phalasamāpatti*).

"The passionless ones departed"—Māra and the army of Māra, from the passionless noble ones, far away, departed.

"Not even a hair of them did they shake"—not even the hairs of those passionless ones did they shake.

Then Māra, concerning the monastic *saṃgha*, spoke this verse:

"The army of Māra has departed; you monks, understand that. Having made effort, the passionless ones departed; not even a hair of them did they shake.

All are victors in battle, fear is transcended, they are glorious; the disciples, known among people, rejoice together with beings."

There, "rejoice together with beings"—in the teaching of the Ten-Powered One, together with beings that have arisen, the noble ones, they rejoice, they greatly rejoice.

"*Janesutā*"—well-known, manifest, recognized among people.

Rejoice together with beings. *Janesutā*.

This, moreover, the *Mahāsamayasutta*, by name, is agreeable and pleasing to the deities; therefore, by one speaking auspiciously, in new locations, this very *sutta* should be spoken.

The deities, indeed—"We will listen to this *sutta*,"—with attentive ears, they wander.

At the conclusion of the discourse, moreover, hundreds of thousands of myriads of deities attained *arhatship*; there was no reckoning of those beginning with stream-enterers.

This is a story concerning the agreeable and pleasing nature of it to the deities—in the Koṭipabbata-vihāra, near the Nāgaleṇa-gate, in a *nāgarukkha*, a certain deity-daughter dwells.

A certain young one, inside the cave, recites this *sutta*.

The deity-daughter, having heard [it], at the conclusion of the *sutta*, with a great sound, gave approval.

"Who is that?"

"I, venerable sir, am a deity-daughter."

"Why did you give approval?"

"Venerable sir, having heard this *sutta* on the day it was spoken by the Ten-Powered One, having sat in the great forest, today I heard [it]; without losing even one syllable from what was spoken by the Blessed One, this *dharma* is well-grasped by you."

"Was it heard by you when the Ten-Powered One was speaking?"

"Yes, venerable sir."

"A great assembly of deities, indeed, occurred; where were you standing when you were listening?"

"I, venerable sir, am a deity dwelling in the great forest; when those deities of great power were coming, in Jambudīpa, I did not obtain a place; then, having come to this Tambapaṇṇidīpa, having stood in Jambukolapaṭṭana, I began to listen; there, too, when those deities of great power were coming, successively retreating, in the Rohaṇa-district, from the back part of a great village, in the ocean, having entered water up to my neck, there I stood listening."

"From the place where you were standing, did you see the Teacher from afar, O deity?"

"What are you saying? Venerable sir, the Teacher, teaching the *dharma* in the great forest, constantly regarding only me, thinking, 'She is fearing,' I was hiding in the waves."

"On that day, indeed, hundreds of thousands of myriads of deities attained *arhatship*; did you also, then, attain *arhatship*?"

"No, venerable sir."

"Did you attain the fruit of non-returner ( *anāgāmiphala* ) there, do you think?"

"No, venerable sir."

"Did you attain the fruit of once-returner (*sakadāgāmiphala*) there, do you think?"

"No, venerable sir."

"Three deities who had attained the path, indeed, had passed beyond reckoning; were you one who had arisen as a stream-enterer there, do you think?"

The deity, on that day, having attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*), fearing, said—"The venerable one is asking what should not be asked."

Then that monk said to her—"Is it possible, O deity, for you to show us your self-nature (*attabhāva*)?"

"It is not possible, venerable sir, to show my entire body; I will show a portion the size of a finger-joint to the venerable one,"—with a keyhole, he directed his finger toward the cave, it was like the time of the rising of a thousand moons and a thousand suns.

The deity, "Be heedful, venerable sirs," having venerated the young monk, departed.

Thus, this *sutta* is agreeable and pleasing to the deities; the deities cherish it.
0259"/> Thus ends the commentary on the Mahāsamayasutta in the Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathā, called Sumaṅgalavilāsinī.

mula_pali: 344. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sakkassa devānamindassa ussukkaṃ udapādi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho sakkassa devānamindassa etadahosi – ‘‘kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti? Addasā kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ magadhesu viharantaṃ pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Disvāna deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘‘ayaṃ, mārisā, bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Yadi pana, mārisā, mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’’ti kho devā tāvatiṃsā sakkassa devānamindassa paccassosuṃ.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying in Magadha, to the east of Rājagaha, near a Brahmin village called Ambasanda, to the north of that village, on Mount Vediya, in the Indasāla Cave.

At that time, Sakka, the lord of the gods, felt a strong desire to see the Blessed One.

Then Sakka, the lord of the gods, considered: "Where is the Blessed One, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one, staying now?" And Sakka, the lord of the gods, saw the Blessed One staying in Magadha, to the east of Rājagaha, near a Brahmin village called Ambasanda, to the north of that village, on Mount Vediya, in the Indasāla Cave.

Perceiving this, he addressed the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven: "Gentlemen, the Blessed One is staying in Magadha, to the east of Rājagaha, near a Brahmin village called Ambasanda, to the north of that village, on Mount Vediya, in the Indasāla Cave.

Suppose, gentlemen, we were to visit that Blessed One, the worthy and perfectly enlightened one?" "So be it, good sir," the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven replied to Sakka, the lord of the gods.
commentary_pali:
344.Evaṃme sutanti sakkapañhasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmoti so kira gāmo ambasaṇḍānaṃ avidūre niviṭṭho, tasmā ‘‘ambasaṇḍā’’ tveva vuccati. Vediyake pabbateti so kira pabbato pabbatapāde jātena maṇivedikāsadisena nīlavanasaṇḍena samantā parikkhitto, tasmā ‘vediyakapabbato’ tveva saṅkhyaṃ gato. Indasālaguhāyanti pubbepi sā dvinnaṃ pabbatānaṃ antare guhā, indasālarukkho cassā dvāre, tasmā ‘indasālaguhā’ti saṅkhyaṃ gatā. Atha naṃ kuṭṭehi parikkhipitvā dvāravātapānāni yojetvā supariniṭṭhitasudhākammamālākammalatākammavicittaṃ leṇaṃ katvā bhagavato adaṃsu. Purimavohāravasena pana ‘‘indasālaguhā’’ tveva naṃ sañjānanti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘indasālaguhāya’nti.

Ussukkaṃ udapādīti dhammiko ussāho uppajji. Nanu ca esa abhiṇhadassāvī bhagavato, na so devatāsannipāto nāma atthi, yatthāyaṃ na āgatapubbo, sakkena sadiso appamādavihārī devaputto nāma natthi. Atha kasmā buddhadassanaṃ anāgatapubbassa viya assa ussāho udapādīti? Maraṇabhayena santajjitattā. Tasmiṃ kirassa samaye āyu parikkhīṇo, so pañca pubbanimittāni disvā ‘‘parikkhīṇo dāni me āyū’’ti aññāsi. Yesañca devaputtānaṃ maraṇanimittāni āvi bhavanti, tesu ye parittakena puññakammena devaloke nibbattā, te ‘‘kuhiṃ nu kho idāni nibbattissāmā’’ti bhayaṃ santāsaṃ āpajjanti. Ye katabhīruttānā bahuṃ puññaṃ katvā nibbattā, te attanā dinnadānaṃ rakkhitasīlaṃ bhāvitabhāvanañca āgamma ‘‘uparidevaloke sampattiṃ anubhavissāmā’’ti na bhāyanti.

Ussukkaṃ udapādī

Sakko pana devarājā pubbanimittāni disvā dasayojanasahassaṃ devanagaraṃ, yojanasahassubbedhaṃ vejayantaṃ, tiyojanasatikaṃ sudhammadevasabhaṃ, yojanasatubbedhaṃ pāricchattakaṃ, saṭṭhiyojanikaṃ paṇḍukambalasilaṃ, aḍḍhatiyā nāṭakakoṭiyo dvīsu devalokesu devaparisaṃ, nandanavanaṃ, cittalatāvanaṃ , missakavanaṃ, phārusakavananti etaṃ sabbasampattiṃ oloketvā ‘‘nassati vata bho me ayaṃ sampattī’’ti bhayābhibhūto ahosi.

Tato ‘‘atthi nu kho koci samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā lokapitāmaho mahābrahmā vā, yo me hadayanissitaṃ sokasallaṃ samuddharitvā imaṃ sampattiṃ thāvaraṃ kareyyā’’ti olokento kañci adisvā puna addasa ‘‘mādisānaṃ satasahassānampi uppannaṃ sokasallaṃ sammāsambuddho uddharituṃ paṭibalo’’ti. Athevaṃ parivitakkentassa tena kho pana samayena sakkassa devānamindassa ussukkaṃ udapādi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya.

Kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatīti katarasmiṃ janapade kataraṃ nagaraṃ upanissāya kassa paccaye paribhuñjanto kassa amataṃ dhammaṃ desayamāno viharatīti. Addasā khoti addakkhi paṭivijjhi. Mārisāti piyavacanametaṃ, devatānaṃ pāṭiyekko vohāro. Niddukkhātipi vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā panesa deve āmantesi? Sahāyatthāya. Pubbe kiresa bhagavati saḷalaghare viharante ekakova dassanāya agamāsi. Satthā ‘‘aparipakkaṃ tāvassa ñāṇaṃ, katipāhaṃ pana atikkamitvā mayi indasālaguhāyaṃ viharante pañca pubbanimittāni disvā maraṇabhayabhīto dvīsu devalokesu devatāhi saddhiṃ upasaṅkamitvā cuddasa pañhe pucchitvā upekkhāpañhavissajjanāvasāne asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahissatī’’ti cintetvā okāsaṃ nākāsi. So ‘‘mama pubbepi ekakassa gatattā satthārā okāso na kato, addhā me natthi maggaphalassa upanissayo, ekassa pana upanissaye sati cakkavāḷapariyantāyapi parisāya bhagavā dhammaṃ desetiyeva. Avassaṃ kho pana dvīsu devalokesu kassaci devassa upanissayo bhavissati, taṃ sandhāya satthā dhammaṃ desessati. Taṃ sutvā ahampi attano domanassaṃ vūpasamessāmī’’ti cintetvā sahāyatthāya āmantesi.

Kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatī Addasā kho Mārisā

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti kho devā tāvatiṃsāti evaṃ hotu mahārāja, gacchāma bhagavantaṃ dassanāya, dullabho buddhuppādo, bhaddaṃ tava, yo tvaṃ ‘‘pabbatakīḷaṃ nadīkīḷaṃ gacchāmā’’ti avatvā amhe evarūpesu ṭhānesu niyojesīti. Paccassosunti tassa vacanaṃ sirasā sampaṭicchiṃsu.

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti kho devā tāvatiṃsā Paccassosu
commentary_english:
344. Thus.

" *Me sutaṃ*": The Sakkapañha Sutta.

Here follows a word-by-word explanation of that which is not explicit: "*Ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo*": That village was situated not far from the mango trees; therefore, it is called "Ambasaṇḍā."

"*Vediyake pabbate*": That mountain was entirely surrounded by a blue forest grove, resembling a jeweled altar, that had grown at the foot of the mountain; therefore, it was named “Vediyaka Mountain.”

"*Indasālaguhāyaṃ*": Formerly, this cave was between two mountains, and an *indasāla* tree was at its entrance; therefore, it became known as “Indasāla Cave.”

Then, having enclosed it with walls, installed door-windows, and made the cave beautiful with well-finished plaster work, garland work, creeper work, and various decorations, they gave it to the Blessed One.

However, according to ancient usage, they recognize it as "Indasāla Cave."

With reference to that, it was said, 'in the Indasāla Cave'.

" *Ussukkaṃ udapādi* ": Religious enthusiasm arose.

Indeed, he was a frequent visitor of the Blessed One. There was no assembly of gods where he had not been before. There was no god-son like Śakka who was diligent in *vihāra*.

Then, why did enthusiasm arise in him, as if the sight of the Buddha was unprecedented for him? Because he was terrified by the fear of death.

At that time, his life was depleted. Having seen five omens, he realized, "Now my life is depleted."

And those godsons for whom signs of death become apparent—of those, those who were born in the world of gods as a result of minor meritorious actions experience fear and terror, [thinking,] "Where shall we be reborn now?"

Those who, having done much merit, were born possessed of the quality of fearlessness, having approached giving, moral discipline, and cultivation, do not fear, [thinking,] “We will experience prosperity in the upper world of the gods.”

Enthusiasm arose.

Then Śakka, the king of the gods, having seen the omens, surveyed the city of gods, ten thousand *yojanas* in extent; Vejayanta, one thousand *yojanas* in height; the Sudhamma assembly hall of the gods, three hundred *yojanas* [in extent]; the Pāricchattaka tree, one hundred *yojanas* in height; the *paṇḍukambala* stone, sixty *yojanas*; one and a half *koṭis* of actors; the company of gods in the two worlds of gods; Nandana Grove; Cittalatā Grove; Missaka Grove; and Phārusaka Grove, all this wealth, [and,] overcome with fear, he thought, "Indeed, this wealth of mine is perishing!"

Then, thinking, "Is there any *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa*, world-father, or great Brahmā who, having extracted the dart of sorrow that is lodged in my heart, would make this wealth permanent?" and, not seeing anyone, he further saw, "The *sammāsambuddha* is capable of extracting the dart of sorrow that has arisen even in hundreds of thousands like me."

While he was thus contemplating, at that very time, enthusiasm arose in Śakka, the lord of the gods, for seeing the Blessed One.

"*Kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharati*": In which district, relying on which city, enjoying whose requisites, teaching whose immortal *dharma*, does the Blessed One dwell at this time?

"*Addasā kho*": He saw, he perceived.

"*Mārisā*": This is an endearing expression, a distinct mode of address among the gods.

It is also said, "free from suffering."

Why did he address the gods? For companionship.

Formerly, when the Blessed One was dwelling in the Salala house, he went alone to see him.

The Teacher thought, "His knowledge is not yet mature. However, after a few days have passed, while I am dwelling in the Indasāla Cave, having seen five omens and being terrified by the fear of death, having approached the gods in the two worlds of gods, having asked fourteen questions, at the end of the explanation of the questions of equanimity, he will be established in the fruit of stream-entry, together with eighty thousand gods," and so he did not give [him] an opportunity.

He [thought:] "Because formerly, when I went alone, the Teacher did not give an opportunity, certainly I do not have the support of the path and the fruit. However, when there is support in one person, the Blessed One teaches the *dharma* even to an assembly as far as the *cakkavāḷa*."

Certainly, however, there will be support from some god in the two worlds of gods. With reference to that, the Teacher will teach the *dharma*.

Having heard that, I too will calm my dejection," thinking, he addressed them for companionship.

"Where, now, is the Blessed One dwelling at this time?" "He saw." "Dear sirs!"

"Thus, good for you!" Thus the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa [said:] "May it be so, great king! Let us go to see the Blessed One! Rare is the arising of a Buddha! Good for you that, not saying, 'Let us go to a mountain sport, a river sport,' you are engaging us in such things!"
"They accepted that statement with a bow," and "Yes, may it be well with you," is what the gods of the Thirty-three said, "accept."

mula_pali: 345. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ gandhabbaputtaṃ (syā.) āmantesi – ‘‘ayaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavā magadhesu viharati pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Yadi pana , tāta pañcasikha, mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’’ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya sakkassa devānamindassa anucariyaṃ upāgami.
mula_english: Then Śakka, the lord of the gods, addressed Pañcasikha, son of a *gandharva* god, saying: “My dear Pañcasikha, the Blessed One is staying in Magadha, to the east of Rajagaha, in the Brahmin village called Ambasanda, to the north of which is Mount Vediya and the Indasala Cave. If we were to approach that Blessed One, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened one, to see him?” “Very good, Lord,” said Pañcasikha, son of a *gandharva* god, and agreeing with Śakka, the lord of the gods, taking his yellow beluva-wood lute, he followed in attendance on Śakka, the lord of the gods.
commentary_pali:
345.Pañcasikhaṃgandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesīti deve tāva āmantetu, imaṃ kasmā visuṃ āmantesi? Okāsakaraṇatthaṃ. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi ‘‘dvīsu devalokesu devatā gahetvā dhurena paharantassa viya satthāraṃ upasaṅkamituṃ na yuttaṃ, ayaṃ pana pañcasikho dasabalassa upaṭṭhāko vallabho icchiticchitakkhaṇe gantvā pañhaṃ pucchitvā dhammaṃ suṇāti, imaṃ purato pesetvā okāsaṃ kāretvā iminā katokāse upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchissāmī’’ti okāsakaraṇatthaṃ āmantesi.

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavāti so ‘‘evaṃ mahārāja, hotu, bhaddaṃ tava, yo tvaṃ maṃ ‘ehi, mārisa, uyyānakīḷādīni vā naṭasamajjādīni vā dassanāya gacchāmā’ti avatvā ‘buddhaṃ passissāma, dhammaṃ sossāmā’ti vadasī’’ti daḷhataraṃ upatthambhento devānamindassa vacanaṃ paṭissutvā anucariyaṃ sahacaraṇaṃ ekato gamanaṃ upāgami.

Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavā

Tattha beluvapaṇḍunti beluvapakkaṃ viya paṇḍuvaṇṇaṃ. Tassa kira sovaṇṇamayaṃ pokkharaṃ, indanīlamayo daṇḍo, rajatamayā tantiyo, pavāḷamayā veṭhakā, vīṇāpattakaṃ gāvutaṃ, tantibandhanaṭṭhānaṃ gāvutaṃ, upari daṇḍako gāvutanti tigāvutappamāṇā vīṇā. Iti so taṃ vīṇaṃ ādāya samapaññāsamucchanā mucchetvā agganakhehi paharitvā madhuraṃ gītassaraṃ nicchāretvā sesadeve sakkassa gamanakālaṃ jānāpento ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Evaṃ tassa gītavāditasaññāya sannipatite devagaṇe atha kho sakko devānamindo…pe… vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi.

beluvapaṇḍu atha kho sakko devānamindo…pe… vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi.
commentary_english:
345. *pañcasikhaṃ*

The *gandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesī*: He addressed the Gandharva, the son of a god, saying: "He first addresses the gods, why does he address this one separately?" For the purpose of making an opportunity.

Thus it occurred to him: "It is not fitting to approach the Teacher (satthāraṃ) like someone taking deities in both hands and striking with the yoke. But this *pañcasikha*, the attendant of the Ten-Powered One (dasabalassa), is a favorite. Having gone at a moment whenever he wishes, he asks a question, and hears the Dharma. Having sent him ahead, having him make an opportunity, having approached after an opportunity has been made by him, I will ask a question." Thus, he addressed him for the purpose of making an opportunity.

*Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavā*: Then he said: "Yes, great king, may it be well with you. Because you say, 'Let us go to see the Buddha, let us listen to the Dharma,' rather than saying, 'Come, friend, let us go to see pleasure gardens and festivals.'" Thus, strongly supporting him, having promised the word of Śakra, lord of the gods, he approached accompanying, going together, going in the same direction.

*Evaṃ bhaddaṃ tavā*: There, *beluvapaṇḍu* means yellowish like a ripe *beluva* fruit.

It is said that his lute had a golden sound box (sovaṇṇamayaṃ pokkharaṃ), an indigo handle (indanīlamayo daṇḍo), silver strings (rajatamayā tantiyo), coral frets (pavāḷamayā veṭhakā), a *vīṇāpattakaṃ* of one *gāvuta*, a string fastening place of one *gāvuta*, and an upper rod of one *gāvuta*, thus a lute measuring three *gāvutas*.

Thus, having taken that lute (vīṇaṃ ādāya), having loosened the strings which were skillfully tuned, having struck it with his fingernails, having produced a sweet song, making known to the remaining gods the time for Śakra to go, he stood to one side.

Thus, when the host of gods had assembled at the signal of his singing and playing, then Śakra, lord of the gods…pe… stood up on Mount Vediyaka.

*beluvapaṇḍu*

Then Śakra, lord of the gods…pe… stood up on Mount Vediyaka.

mula_pali: 346. Atha kho sakko devānamindo devehi tāvatiṃsehi parivuto pañcasikhena gandhabbadevaputtena purakkhato seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva devesu tāvatiṃsesu antarahito magadhesu pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi. Tena kho pana samayena vediyako pabbato atiriva obhāsajāto hoti ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo yathā taṃ devānaṃ devānubhāvena. Apissudaṃ parito gāmesu manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘ādittassu nāmajja vediyako pabbato jhāyatisu jhāyatassu (syā.), pajjhāyitassu (sī. pī.) nāmajja vediyako pabbato jalatisu jalatassu (syā.), jalitassu (sī. pī.) nāmajja vediyako pabbato kiṃsu nāmajja vediyako pabbato atiriva obhāsajāto ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo’’ti saṃviggā lomahaṭṭhajātā ahesuṃ.
mula_english:
Then, Śakra, the lord of the gods, surrounded by the Thirty-Three Gods and preceded by Pañcaśikha, the son of a gandharva god, just as quickly as a strong man might stretch out his contracted arm or contract his outstretched arm, vanished from the heaven of the Thirty-Three and appeared in Magadha, to the east of Rājagṛha, in the village of the brahmin Ambasanda, on Mount Vediya to the north of it.

And then, at that time, Mount Vediya was exceedingly radiant, as was the brahmin village of Ambasanda, by the power of the gods.

And indeed, people in the surrounding villages were saying, "Look, Mount Vediya is on fire today! It is blazing! It is burning! What is this? Mount Vediya and Ambasanda are exceedingly radiant!" And they were agitated and their hair stood on end.
commentary_pali: 346.Atiriva obhāsajātoti aññesu divasesu ekasseva devassa vā mārassa vā brahmuno vā obhāsena obhāsajāto hoti, taṃdivasaṃ pana dvīsu devalokesu devatānaṃ obhāsena atiriva obhāsajāto ekapajjoto sahassacandasūriyauggatakālasadiso ahosi. Parito gāmesu manussāti samantā gāmesu manussā. Pakatisāyamāsakāleyeva kira gāmamajjhe dārakesu kīḷantesu tattha sakko agamāsi, tasmā manussā passitvā evamāhaṃsu. Nanu ca majjhimayāme devatā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamanti, ayaṃ kasmā paṭhamayāmassāpi purimabhāgeyeva āgatoti? Maraṇabhayeneva tajjitattā. Kiṃsu nāmāti kiṃsu nāma bho etaṃ, ko nu kho ajja mahesakkho devo vā brahmā vā bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchituṃ dhammaṃ sotuṃ upasaṅkamanto, kathaṃsu nāma bho bhagavā pañhaṃ vissajjessati dhammaṃ desessati, lābhā amhākaṃ, yesaṃ no evaṃ devatānaṃ kaṅkhāvinodako satthā avidūre vihāre vasati, ye labhāma thālakabhikkhampi kaṭacchubhikkhampi dātunti saṃviggā lomahaṭṭhajātā uddhaggalomā hutvā dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā namassamānā aṭṭhaṃsu.
commentary_english:
346. *Atiriva obhāsajāto* means that on other days a radiant light would arise from the radiance of only one deva, or Māra, or Brahmā. But on that day, a surpassing radiant light arose from the radiance of devas in two heavens; a single flame, like the time when a thousand moons and suns have risen.

*Parito gāmesu manussā* means people around the villages, people all around the villages.

It seems that at the usual evening time, while children were playing in the middle of the village, Śakra approached. Therefore, seeing him, the people said thus:

"Indeed, deities approach the Blessed One in the middle watch of the night, why has this one come in the early part of the first watch? Because he is terrified by the fear of death."

*Kiṃsu nāmā* means "What is this?" Then, "Who now is this mighty deva, or Brahmā, who is approaching to ask the Blessed One a question, to hear the Dharma? How will the Blessed One answer the question, teach the Dharma?" It is a gain for us, for whom the teacher who dispels the doubt of the deities dwells not far from the monastery. We will obtain alms of food in a bowl, alms of food in a spoon to give." Thus, agitated, with hairs standing on end, with uplifted hair, placing their radiant joined hands on their heads, they stood paying homage.

mula_pali:
347. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘durupasaṅkamā kho, tāta pañcasikha, tathāgatā mādisena, jhāyī jhānaratā, tadantaraṃ tadanantaraṃ (sī. syā. pī. ka.) paṭisallīnā. Yadi pana tvaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavantaṃ paṭhamaṃ pasādeyyāsi, tayā, tāta, paṭhamaṃ pasāditaṃ pacchā mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’’ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya yena indasālaguhā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ‘‘ettāvatā me bhagavā neva atidūre bhavissati nāccāsanne, saddañca me sossatī’’ti ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi.

Pañcasikhagītagāthā
mula_english:
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed Pañcaśikha (Pañcasikhaṃ), the Gandharva (gandhabbadevaputtaṃ) son of the gods: "Tathāgatas (tathāgatā) are difficult to approach (durupasaṅkamā) by one like me. They are meditative (jhāyī), delighting in meditation (jhānaratā), and are in retreat (paṭisallīnā) at such times. But if you, dear (tāta) Pañcaśikha, were first to please (pasādeyyāsi) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ), then, dear (tāta), after you have pleased him, we (mayaṃ) might afterwards approach (upasaṅkameyyāma) that Blessed One (taṃ bhagavantaṃ), the worthy one (arahantaṃ), the fully enlightened Buddha (sammāsambuddha)."

"Very good, Lord (evaṃ bhaddantavā)," said Pañcaśikha (pañcasikho), the Gandharva (gandhabbadevaputto) son of the gods, and, assenting to Śakra (sakkassa), the lord of the gods (devānamindassa), he took his yellow beluva-wood lute (beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya) and approached (upasaṅkami) the Indasāla Cave (yena indasālaguhā). Having approached (upasaṅkamitvā), he thought: "From here (ettāvatā) the Blessed One (bhagavā) will be neither too far (neva atidūre bhavissati) nor too near (nāccāsanne), and he will hear (sossati) my voice (saddañca)," and he stood to one side (ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi).

The Song of Pañcaśikha (pañcasikhagītagāthā).
commentary_pali:
347.Durupasaṅkamāti dupayirupāsiyā. Ahaṃ sarāgo sadoso samoho, satthā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho, tasmā dupayirupāsiyā tathāgatā mādisena. Jhāyīti lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena ca ārammaṇūpanijjhānena ca jhāyī. Tasmiññeva jhāne ratāti jhānaratā. Tadantaraṃ paṭisallīnāti tadantaraṃ paṭisallīnā sampati paṭisallīnā vā. Tasmā na kevalaṃ jhāyī jhānaratāti durupasaṅkamā, idānimeva paṭisallīnātipi durupasaṅkamā. Pasādeyyāsīti ārādheyyāsi, okāsaṃ me kāretvā dadeyyāsīti vadati. Beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāyāti nanu pubbeva ādinnāti? Āma , ādinnā. Maggagamanavasena pana aṃsakūṭe laggitā, idāni naṃ vāmahatthe ṭhapetvā vādanasajjaṃ katvā ādiyi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘ādāyā’’ti.

Pañcasikhagītagāthāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
347.
*Durupasaṅkamā* means *dupayirupāsiyā*.

I am full of passion ( *sarāga*), full of hatred ( *sadosa*), full of delusion ( *samoha*). The teacher ( *satthā*) is without passion ( *vītarāga*), without hatred ( *vītadosa*), without delusion ( *vītamoha*). Therefore, the *tathāgatas* are *dupayirupāsiyā* through someone like me.

*Jhāyī* means *jhāyī* through contemplation of characteristics ( *lakkhaṇūpanijjhāna*) and through contemplation of objects ( *ārammaṇūpanijjhāna*).

*Jhānaratā* means delighting (*ratā*) in that very meditation ( *jhāna*).

*Tadantaraṃ paṭisallīnā* means secluded (*paṭisallīnā*) at that interval, or presently secluded.

Therefore, not only is a *jhāyī* who delights in meditation ( *jhānaratā*) *durupasaṅkamā*, but even one who is presently secluded is *durupasaṅkamā*.

*Pasādeyyāsī* means you should propitiate (*ārādheyyāsi*), saying, "Having caused an opportunity for me, may you give (*dadeyyāsīti*)."

*Beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāyā* means, "Surely it was taken before?" Yes, taken.

Having been attached to the shoulder ( *aṃsakūṭa*) by means of the way of going on the path ( *maggagamanavasena*), now, having placed it in the left hand ( *vāmahattha*) and having made it ready for playing ( *vādanasajjaṃ katvā*), he took it (*ādiyi*).

Therefore it was said, "Having taken (*ādāyā*)."

Explanation of the Song of Pañcasikha ( *pañcasikhagītagāthāvaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
348. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ veḷuvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya (syā.) assāvesi, imā ca gāthā abhāsi buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā –

‘‘Vande te pitaraṃ bhadde, timbaruṃ sūriyavacchase;

Yena jātāsi kalyāṇī, ānandajananī mama.

‘‘Vātova sedataṃ kanto, pānīyaṃva pipāsato;

Aṅgīrasi piyāmesi, dhammo arahatāmiva.

‘‘Āturasseva bhesajjaṃ, bhojanaṃva jighacchato;

Parinibbāpaya maṃ bhadde, jalantamiva vārinā.

‘‘Sītodakaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ, yuttaṃ kiñjakkhareṇunā;

Nāgo ghammābhitattova, ogāhe te thanūdaraṃ.

‘‘Accaṅkusova nāgova, jitaṃ me tuttatomaraṃ;

Kāraṇaṃ nappajānāmi, sammatto lakkhaṇūruyā.

‘‘Tayi gedhitacittosmi, cittaṃ vipariṇāmitaṃ;

Paṭigantuṃ na sakkomi, vaṅkaghastova ambujo.

‘‘Vāmūru saja maṃ bhadde, saja maṃ mandalocane;

Palissaja maṃ kalyāṇi, etaṃ me abhipatthitaṃ.

‘‘Appako vata me santo, kāmo vellitakesiyā;

Anekabhāvo samuppādi, arahanteva dakkhiṇā.

‘‘Yaṃ me atthi kataṃ puññaṃ, arahantesu tādisu;

Taṃ me sabbaṅgakalyāṇi, tayā saddhiṃ vipaccataṃ.

‘‘Yaṃ me atthi kataṃ puññaṃ, asmiṃ pathavimaṇḍale;

Taṃ me sabbaṅgakalyāṇi, tayā saddhiṃ vipaccataṃ.

‘‘Sakyaputtova jhānena, ekodi nipako sato;

Amataṃ muni jigīsāno jigiṃsāno (sī. syā. pī.), tamahaṃ sūriyavacchase.

‘‘Yathāpi muni nandeyya, patvā sambodhimuttamaṃ;

Evaṃ nandeyyaṃ kalyāṇi, missībhāvaṃ gato tayā.

‘‘Sakko ce me varaṃ dajjā, tāvatiṃsānamissaro;

Tāhaṃ bhadde vareyyāhe, evaṃ kāmo daḷho mama.

Vandamāno namassāmi, yassā setādisī pajā’’ti.

348.Assāvesīti sāvesi. Buddhūpasañhitāti buddhaṃ ārabbha buddhaṃ nissayaṃ katvā pavattāti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

Vande te pitaraṃ bhadde, timbaruṃ sūriyavacchaseti ettha sūriyavacchasāti sūriyasamānasarīrā. Tassā kira devadhītāya pādantato rasmi uṭṭhahitvā kesantaṃ ārohati, tasmā bālasūriyamaṇḍalasadisā khāyati, iti naṃ ‘‘sūriyavacchasā’’ti sañjānanti. Taṃ sandhāyāha – ‘‘bhadde, sūriyavacchase, tava pitaraṃ timbaruṃ gandhabbadevarājānaṃ vandāmī’’ti. Yena jātāsi kalyāṇīti yena kāraṇabhūtena yaṃ timbaruṃ devarājānaṃ nissāya tvaṃ jātā, kalyāṇī sabbaṅgasobhanā. Ānandajananī mamāti mayhaṃ pītisomanassavaḍḍhanī.

commentary_english:
348. *Assāvesī*: Sāvesi means he caused to be heard.

*Buddhūpasañhitā*: It means commencing with the buddha, having made the buddha the basis, it proceeds.

The same method of explanation applies to the other clauses too.

*Vande te pitaram bhadde, timbarum sūriyavacchase*: Here, *sūriyavacchasā* means having a body like the sun.

It is said that a ray rises from the end of the feet of that daughter of a god and ascends to the end of the hair; therefore, she appears like a young solar disc; thus, they recognize her as "Sūriyavacchasā".

Referring to that, he said, "O auspicious Sūriyavacchase, I venerate your father, Timburu, the Gandharva divine king."

*Yena jātāsi kalyāṇī*: By whom, having the nature of a cause, you were born, that Timburu, relying on the divine king, you were born, O auspicious one, beautiful in all limbs.

*Ānandajananī mamā*: It increases my joy and happiness.

*Vande te pitaram bhadde, timbarum sūriyavacchase sūriyavacchasā yena jātāsi kalyāṇī ānandajananī mamā*

*Vātova sedatam kanto*: Just as the wind is desirable and pleasing for the removal of accumulated sweat, such is its meaning.

*Pānīyamva pipāsato*: To one who desires to drink, to a thirsty person, one overcome by thirst.

*Aṅgīrasī*: Aṅgīrasī means having rays in the limbs, and addressing that, he speaks.

*Dhammo arahatāmivā*: Like the noble transcendental dharma of the *arhats*.

*Vātova sedatam kanto pānīyamva pipāsato aṅgīrasī dhammo arahatāmivā*

*Jighacchato*: To one who desires to eat, one overcome by hunger.

*Jalantamiva vārinā*: Just as someone would extinguish a blazing fire with a pot of water, so extinguish my burning of lust born from you, he says.

*Jighacchato jalantamiva vārinā*

*Yuttam kiñjakkhareṇunā*: Joined with the pollen of the lotus flower.

*Nāgo ghammābhitatto vā*: Like an elephant afflicted by the heat.

*Ogāhe te thanūdara*: Just as that elephant, having entered a pond, having drunk and having made the tip of its trunk appear, plunges in and finds ease and pleasure, so when will I, having descended into your breasts and abdomen, obtain ease and pleasure, he says.

*Yuttam kiñjakkhareṇunā nāgo ghammābhitatto vā ogāhe te thanūdara*

"Just as an elephant goaded with a goad, I have conquered my goad and lance;

I do not understand the cause, I am intoxicated by the thighs marked with auspicious signs."

Here *tuttaṃ* is said to be an iron rod for piercing the ear.

*tomara* is a piercing rod in the feet and so on.

*aṅkuso* is a curved thorn for piercing the head.

And the elephant that is in rut and beyond the goad, even when pierced by the goad, does not come under control, that one, with the pride of intoxication, "I have conquered my goad and lance, because I do not come under the control even of the goad," does not understand any cause.

Just as that elephant goaded with a goad does not understand any cause, saying, "I have conquered my goad and lance," so I too, intoxicated by the thighs endowed with auspicious marks, am inebriated, negligent, maddened, as if, I do not understand any cause, he says.

Or else, just as that elephant goaded with a goad, I too, intoxicated by the thighs marked with auspicious signs, do not understand any cause of detachment from that.

Why? Because, just as by that elephant, "I have conquered my goad and lance," I do not heed the words of anyone speaking.

*Tuttaṃ tomara aṅkuso*

*Tayi gedhitacittosmī*: O auspicious one, O thighs marked with auspicious signs, I am one whose mind is attached to you.

*Gedhitacitto*: Or, one whose mind has approached greed.

*Cittaṃ vipariṇāmita*: The mind, having abandoned its nature, remains still.

*Paṭigantum na sakkomī*: I am not able to turn back.

*Vaṅkaghastova ambujo*: Like a fish that has swallowed a hook and remains still.

*Ghaso'tipi pāṭho*, Ayamevattho: *ghaso* is also a reading; this is the meaning.
