Delighted, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, rejoiced at and approved of the Blessed One's words, saying, "So it is, Blessed One, so it is, O Sugata! My doubts are dispelled, my uncertainty is gone, having heard the Blessed One's explanation of the question."

The restraint of the *prātimokṣa*.
commentary_pali:
363.Evaṃ paṭipanno kho, devānaminda, bhikkhu papañcasaññāsaṅkhānirodhasāruppagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ paṭipanno hotīti bhagavā arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhapesi. Sakko pana sotāpattiphalaṃ patto. Buddhānañhi ajjhāsayo hīno na hoti, ukkaṭṭhova hoti. Ekassapi bahūnampi dhammaṃ desentā arahatteneva kūṭaṃ gaṇhanti. Sattā pana attano anurūpe upanissaye ṭhitā keci sotāpannā honti, keci sakadāgāmī, keci anāgāmī, keci arahanto. Rājā viya hi bhagavā, rājakumārā viya veneyyā. Yathā hi rājā bhojanakāle attano pamāṇena piṇḍaṃ uddharitvā rājakumārānaṃ upaneti, te tato attano mukhappamāṇeneva kabaḷaṃ karonti, evaṃ bhagavā attajjhāsayānurūpāya desanāya arahatteneva kūṭaṃ gaṇhāti. Veneyyā attano upanissayappamāṇena tato sotāpattiphalamattaṃ vā sakadāgāmianāgāmiarahattaphalameva vā gaṇhanti. Sakko pana sotāpanno jāto. Sotāpanno ca hutvā bhagavato puratoyeva cavitvā taruṇasakko hutvā nibbatti, devatānañhi cavamānānaṃ attabhāvassa gatāgataṭṭhānaṃ nāma na paññāyati, dīpasikhāgamanaṃ viya hoti. Tasmā sesadevatā na jāniṃsu. Sakko pana sayaṃ cutattā bhagavā ca appaṭihatañāṇattā dveva janā jāniṃsu. Atha sakko cintesi ‘‘mayhañhi bhagavatā tīsu ṭhānesu nibbattitaphalameva kathitaṃ, ayañca pana maggo vā phalaṃ vā sakuṇikāya viya uppatitvā gahetuṃ na sakkā, āgamanīyapubbabhāgapaṭipadāya assa bhavitabbaṃ. Handāhaṃ upari khīṇāsavassa pubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ pucchāmī’’ti.

Pātimokkhasaṃvaravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Thus behaving, Indra of the Gods, a monk is behaving in a way that leads to the cessation of perceptions and notions, and is in accordance with the state of an Arhat." Thus, the Blessed One concluded the teaching with the highest point of Arahantship.

Sakka, however, attained the fruit of stream-entry (srotaāpattiphala). For the Buddhas' intention is never inferior, it is always supreme. While teaching the Dharma to one or many, they take their stand on Arahantship itself. But beings, abiding in a suitable condition according to their own potential, some become stream-enterers (srotaāpanna), some once-returners (sakadāgāmī), some non-returners (anāgāmī), some Arhats. For the Blessed One is like a king, and those to be trained are like princes. Just as a king, at mealtime, takes a portion according to his own measure and offers it to the princes, and they then make a mouthful according to the measure of their own mouth, so too, the Blessed One, with a teaching in accordance with his own intention, takes his stand on Arahantship itself. Those to be trained, according to the measure of their own potential, take from it only the fruit of stream-entry (srotaāpattiphala), or only the fruit of once-returner (sakṛdāgāmiphala), non-returner (anāgāmiphala), or Arhatship.

Sakka, however, was born a stream-enterer (srotaāpanna). And having become a stream-enterer, he passed away right in front of the Blessed One and was reborn as a young Sakka. For the destination and place of arrival of beings who are passing away are not evident, it is like the path of a flame. Therefore, the remaining deities did not know. Sakka, however, because he himself had passed away, and the Blessed One, because of his unobstructed knowledge, these two people knew.

Then Sakka thought: "Indeed, the Blessed One has spoken to me only of the fruit that arises in the three places. But this path or fruit cannot be seized by flying up like a bird; it must be through a practice that is a preliminary part of the path that is to be arrived at. Come, let me ask about the preliminary practice of an Arhat who has destroyed the āsavas."

Explanation of the Pātimokkha restraint

mula_pali:
364. Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi –

‘‘Kathaṃ paṭipanno pana, mārisa, bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarāya paṭipanno hotī’’ti? ‘‘Kāyasamācāraṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Vacīsamācāraṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Pariyesanaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabba’’mpi.

‘‘Kāyasamācāraṃpāhaṃ , devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi sevitabbampi asevitabbampīti iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ, kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā kāyasamācāraṃ ‘imaṃ kho me kāyasamācāraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo kāyasamācāro na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā kāyasamācāraṃ ‘imaṃ kho me kāyasamācāraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo kāyasamācāro sevitabbo. Kāyasamācāraṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘Vacīsamācāraṃpāhaṃ , devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampī’ti. Iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ, kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā vacīsamācāraṃ ‘imaṃ kho me vacīsamācāraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo vacīsamācāro na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā vacīsamācāraṃ ‘imaṃ kho me vacīsamācāraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo vacīsamācāro sevitabbo. Vacīsamācāraṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘Pariyesanaṃpāhaṃ , devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ, kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā pariyesanaṃ ‘imaṃ kho me pariyesanaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpā pariyesanā na sevitabbā. Tattha yaṃ jaññā pariyesanaṃ ‘imaṃ kho me pariyesanaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpā pariyesanā sevitabbā. Pariyesanaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘Evaṃ paṭipanno kho, devānaminda, bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarāya paṭipanno hotī’’ti. Itthaṃ bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa pañhaṃ puṭṭho byākāsi. Attamano sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi anumodi – ‘‘evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Tiṇṇā mettha kaṅkhā vigatā kathaṃkathā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā’’ti.

Indriyasaṃvaro
mula_english:
364. Then Śakra, the ruler of the gods, having rejoiced and approved of the Blessed One's words, asked the Blessed One a further question:

"How, sir, does a *bhikṣu* practice so as to be practicing the restraint of the *prātimokṣa*?"

"Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of bodily conduct (*kāyasamācāra*): the kind to be pursued (*sevitabba*), and the kind to be avoided (*asevitabba*).

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of verbal conduct (*vacīsamācāra*): the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of seeking (*pariyesana*): the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided."

"Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of bodily conduct: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided.' Thus it was said, but with reference to what was this said? When one knows of bodily conduct that 'by cultivating this bodily conduct, unwholesome (*akuśala*) *dharmas* increase and wholesome (*kuśala*) *dharmas* diminish,' that kind of bodily conduct should not be cultivated.

When one knows of bodily conduct that 'by cultivating this bodily conduct, unwholesome *dharmas* diminish and wholesome *dharmas* increase,' that kind of bodily conduct should be cultivated.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of bodily conduct: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided.' Thus it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.

"Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of verbal conduct: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided." Thus it was said, but with reference to what was this said? When one knows of verbal conduct that 'by cultivating this verbal conduct, unwholesome *dharmas* increase and wholesome *dharmas* diminish,' that kind of verbal conduct should not be cultivated.

When one knows of verbal conduct that 'by cultivating this verbal conduct, unwholesome *dharmas* diminish and wholesome *dharmas* increase,' that kind of verbal conduct should be cultivated.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of verbal conduct: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided.' Thus it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.

"Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of seeking: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided." Thus it was said, but with reference to what was this said? When one knows of seeking that 'by cultivating this seeking, unwholesome *dharmas* increase and wholesome *dharmas* diminish,' that kind of seeking should not be cultivated.

When one knows of seeking that 'by cultivating this seeking, unwholesome *dharmas* diminish and wholesome *dharmas* increase,' that kind of seeking should be cultivated.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that there are two kinds of seeking: the kind to be pursued and the kind to be avoided.' Thus it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.

"Thus, Ruler of the Gods, a *bhikṣu* is practicing who is practicing the restraint of the *prātimokṣa*."

In this way, the Blessed One answered Śakra, the ruler of the gods, when asked a question.

Delighted, Śakra, the ruler of the gods, rejoiced at and approved of the Blessed One's words: "So it is, Blessed One, so it is, Well-Gone! My doubt is dispelled, my uncertainty is removed, by hearing the Blessed One's answer to the question!"

Control of the Senses (*indriyasaṃvaro*)
commentary_pali:
364. Tato taṃ pucchanto kathaṃ paṭipanno pana, mārisātiādimāha. Tattha pātimokkhasaṃvarāyāti uttamajeṭṭhakasīlasaṃvarāya. Kāyasamācārampītiādi sevitabbakāyasamācārādivasena pātimokkhasaṃvaradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Sīlakathā ca nāmesā kammapathavasena vā paṇṇattivasena vā kathetabbā hoti.

Tattha kammapathavasena kathentena asevitabbakāyasamācāro tāva pāṇātipātaadinnādānamicchācārehi kathetabbo. Paṇṇattivasena kathentena kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamavasena kathetabbo. Sevitabbakāyasamācāro pāṇātipātādiveramaṇīhi ceva kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadaavītikkamena ca kathetabbo. Asevitabbavacīsamācāro musāvādādivacīduccaritena ceva vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamena ca kathetabbo. Sevitabbavacīsamācāro musāvādādiveramaṇīhi ceva vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadaavītikkamena ca kathetabbo.

Pariyesanā pana kāyavācāhi pariyesanāyeva. Sā kāyavacīsamācāragahaṇena gahitāpi samānā yasmā ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ nāma etasmiññeva dvāradvaye uppajjati, na ākāse, tasmā ājīvaṭṭhamakasīladassanatthaṃ visuṃ vuttā. Tattha nasevitabbapariyesanā anariyapariyesanāya kathetabbā. Sevitabbapariyesanā ariyapariyesanāya. Vuttañhetaṃ –

‘‘Dvemā, bhikkhave, pariyesanā anariyā ca pariyesanā, ariyā ca pariyesanā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, anariyā pariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā jarādhammo, byādhidhammo, maraṇadhammo, sokadhammo, saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, jātidhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave , jātidhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ jātidhammaṃ ajeḷakaṃ jātidhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ jātidhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ jātidhammaṃ, jātarūparajataṃ jātidhammaṃ. Jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo, etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, jarādhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, jarādhammaṃ…pe… jarādhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, byādhidhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, byādhidhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ byādhidhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ byādhidhammaṃ. Byādhidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo, etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, maraṇadhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, maraṇadhammaṃ…pe… maraṇadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, sokadhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ…pe… sokadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

Kiñca, bhikkhave, saṃkilesadhammaṃ vadetha…pe… jātarūparajataṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ. Saṃkilesadhammā , hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo, etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, anariyā pariyesanāti (ma. ni. 1.274).

Apica kuhanādivasena pañcavidhā, agocaravasena chabbidhā vejjakammādivasena ekavīsatividhā, evaṃ pavattā sabbāpi anesanā anariyapariyesanāyevāti veditabbā.

‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyā pariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā jarādhammo, byādhi, maraṇa, soka, saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati. Ayaṃ ariyā pariyesanāti (ma. ni. 1.275).

Apica pañca kuhanādīni cha agocare ekavīsatividhañca anesanaṃ vajjetvā bhikkhācariyāya dhammena samena pariyesanāpi ariyapariyesanāyevāti veditabbā.

Ettha ca yo yo ‘‘na sevitabbo’’ti vutto, so so pubbabhāge pāṇātipātādīnaṃ sambhārapariyesanāpayogakaraṇagamanakālato paṭṭhāya na sevitabbova. Itaro ādito paṭṭhāya sevitabbo, asakkontena cittampi uppādetabbaṃ. Apica saṅghabhedādīnaṃ atthāya parakkamantānaṃ devadattādīnaṃ viya kāyasamācāro na sevitabbo, divasassa dvattikkhattuṃ tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ upaṭṭhānagamanādivasena pavatto dhammasenāpatimahāmoggallānattherādīnaṃ viya kāyasamācāro sevitabbo. Dhanuggahapesanādivasena vācaṃ bhindantānaṃ devadattādīnaṃ viya vacīsamācāro na sevitabbo, tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ guṇakittanādivasena pavatto dhammasenāpatimahāmoggallānattherādīnaṃ viya vacīsamācāro sevitabbo. Anariyapariyesanaṃ pariyesantānaṃ devadattādīnaṃ viya pariyesanā na sevitabbā, ariyapariyesanameva pariyesantānaṃ dhammasenāpatimahāmoggallānattherādīnaṃ viya pariyesanā sevitabbā.

Evaṃ paṭipanno khoti evaṃ asevitabbaṃ kāyavacīsamācāraṃ pariyesanañca pahāya sevitabbānaṃ pāripūriyā paṭipanno, devānaminda, bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarāya uttamajeṭṭhakasīlasaṃvaratthāya paṭipanno nāma hotīti bhagavā khīṇāsavassa āgamanīyapubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ kathesi.

Evaṃ paṭipanno kho

Indriyasaṃvaravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
364. Then, asking him, he said, "How have you undertaken [the training], friend?"

There, "for the sake of the *pātimokkhasaṃvara*" means for the sake of the supreme, best restraint in morality.

"Also, physical conduct" etc. is stated to show the *pātimokkhasaṃvara* in terms of physical conduct to be cultivated, etc.

And this, namely, the discourse on morality, should be given in terms of the path of action or in terms of the precepts.

There, when speaking in terms of the path of action, uncultivated physical conduct should be discussed first, with regard to killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.

When speaking in terms of the precepts, it should be discussed in terms of transgression of the precepts laid down at the door of the body.

Cultivated physical conduct should be discussed in terms of abstinence from killing, etc., and in terms of non-transgression of the precepts laid down at the door of the body.

Uncultivated verbal conduct should be discussed in terms of verbal misconduct, such as lying, etc., and in terms of transgression of the precepts laid down at the door of speech.

Cultivated verbal conduct should be discussed in terms of abstinence from lying, etc., and in terms of non-transgression of the precepts laid down at the door of speech.

Search, however, is only a search by means of body and speech.

Although that is included by the taking up of physical and verbal conduct, since the morality of right livelihood arises only in these two doors, not in the sky, therefore it is stated separately to show the morality of right livelihood.

There, uncultivated search should be discussed with respect to the ignoble search.

Cultivated search [should be discussed] with respect to the noble search.

For it was said:

“Monks, there are these two kinds of search: the ignoble search and the noble search.

And what, monks, is the ignoble search? Here, monks, someone being himself subject to birth seeks what is also subject to birth; being himself subject to ageing, sickness, death, sorrow, defilement, he seeks what is also subject to defilement.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to birth? Wife and children, monks, are subject to birth, men and women slaves are subject to birth, goats and sheep are subject to birth, fowl and pigs are subject to birth, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares are subject to birth, gold and silver are subject to birth.

These, monks, are possessions subject to birth, and one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to birth, seeks what it also subject to birth.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to ageing? Wife and children, monks, are subject to ageing…pe… he seeks what is also subject to ageing.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to sickness? Wife and children, monks, are subject to sickness, men and women slaves are subject to sickness, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares are subject to sickness.

These, monks, are possessions subject to sickness, and one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to sickness, seeks what is also subject to sickness.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to death? Wife and children, monks, are subject to death…pe… he seeks what is also subject to death.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to sorrow? Wife and children…pe… he seeks what is also subject to sorrow.

“And what, monks, do you call subject to defilement…pe… gold and silver are subject to defilement.

These, monks, are possessions subject to defilement, and one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to defilement, seeks what is also subject to defilement.

This, monks, is the ignoble search” (M.
Ni.
1.
274).

Moreover, all search that occurs in this way – fivefold in terms of deceit, sixfold in terms of improper scope, twenty-onefold in terms of medical practice, etc. – should be understood as the ignoble search.

“And what, monks, is the noble search? Here, monks, someone being himself subject to birth, having understood the danger in what is subject to birth, seeks the unborn, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*; being himself subject to ageing, sickness, death, sorrow, defilement, having understood the danger in what is subject to defilement, he seeks the undefiled, unsurpassed.
seeks out the secure *yogakkhema*, the *Nibbāna* free from disease.

This is called the Noble Search (*ariyā pariyesanā*).

Furthermore, it should be understood that avoiding the five hypocritical means, the six improper pastures, and the twenty-one kinds of wrong livelihood, even searching for alms according to the Dharma in an even manner, is indeed a Noble Search (*ariyapariyesanā*).

Here, whatever conduct is said to be "not to be cultivated," from the initial stage of accumulating materials, searching, employing, acting, going, and the time related to killing living beings, etc., that conduct should not be cultivated.

The other conduct, from the beginning, should be cultivated, and one should generate a mind even when unable to do so.

Furthermore, bodily conduct for the sake of causing schism in the *saṅgha*, etc., like that of Devadatta, etc., should not be cultivated. Bodily conduct that occurs two or three times a day in the manner of attending to and visiting the three jewels (*ratana*), etc., like that of the Dharma Commander, the great *thera* Mahā-Moggallāna, etc., should be cultivated.

Verbal conduct that breaks speech through archery practice, sending messages, etc., like that of Devadatta, etc., should not be cultivated. Verbal conduct that occurs through praising the qualities of the three jewels (*ratana*), etc., like that of the Dharma Commander, the great *thera* Mahā-Moggallāna, etc., should be cultivated.

The un-Noble Search (*anariyapariyesana*) of those searching, like Devadatta, etc., that search should not be cultivated. The search of those searching for the Noble Search (*ariyapariyesana*) itself, like that of the Dharma Commander, the great *thera* Mahā-Moggallāna, etc., that search should be cultivated.

Thus, "one who is practicing in this way," meaning having abandoned bodily conduct, verbal conduct, and searching that should not be cultivated, and practicing the completeness of what should be cultivated, that *bhikkhu*, Devānaminda, is said to be "one who is practicing" for the sake of restraint according to the *prātimokṣa* and for the sake of the highest, most excellent restraint of morality (*śīla*). The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) spoke of the path of preliminary actions leading to one who is without outflows (*khīṇāsava*).

Description of the Restraint of the Senses (*indriyasaṃvaravaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
365. Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi –

‘‘Kathaṃ paṭipanno pana, mārisa, bhikkhu indriyasaṃvarāya paṭipanno hotī’’ti? ‘‘Cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Sotaviññeyyaṃ saddaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Ghānaviññeyyaṃ gandhaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Jivhāviññeyyaṃ rasaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Kāyaviññeyyaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Manoviññeyyaṃ dhammaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampī’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Imassa kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Yathārūpaṃ, bhante, cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṃ cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ na sevitabbaṃ . Yathārūpañca kho, bhante, cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṃ cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Yathārūpañca kho, bhante, sotaviññeyyaṃ saddaṃ sevato…pe… ghānaviññeyyaṃ gandhaṃ sevato… jivhāviññeyyaṃ rasaṃ sevato… kāyaviññeyyaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ sevato… manoviññeyyaṃ dhammaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpo manoviññeyyo dhammo na sevitabbo. Yathārūpañca kho, bhante, manoviññeyyaṃ dhammaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpo manoviññeyyo dhammo sevitabbo.

‘‘Imassa kho me, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānato tiṇṇā mettha kaṅkhā vigatā kathaṃkathā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā’’ti.
mula_english:
365. Then, Śakra, the ruler of the gods, having rejoiced at and approved of the Blessed One's words, asked the Blessed One a further question:

"But how, sir, is a *bhikṣu* practicing restraint of the senses a practitioner?"

"Ruler of the Gods, I declare that forms cognizable by the eye (*cakṣurvijñeya rūpa*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued (*sevitabba*), and the kind to be avoided (*asevitabba*).

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that sounds cognizable by the ear (*śrotravijñeya śabda*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that odours cognizable by the nose (*ghānavijñeya gandha*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that tastes cognizable by the tongue (*jihvāvijñeya rasa*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that tangibles cognizable by the body (*kāyavijñeya sparśa*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided.

Ruler of the Gods, I declare that mind-objects cognizable by the mind (*manovijñeya dharma*) are of two kinds: the kind to be pursued, and the kind to be avoided."

When this was said, Śakra, the ruler of the gods, said this to the Blessed One:

"Venerable sir, I understand the meaning of what was spoken by the Blessed One in brief in this way, in detail:

Venerable sir, such forms cognizable by the eye, when cultivated, cause unwholesome states (*akuśalā dharma*) to increase and wholesome states (*kuśalā dharma*) to diminish, should not be cultivated. But such forms cognizable by the eye, when cultivated, cause unwholesome states to diminish and wholesome states to increase, should be cultivated.

And the same applies to sounds cognizable by the ear…odours cognizable by the nose…tastes cognizable by the tongue…tangibles cognizable by the body…mind-objects cognizable by the mind: such mind-objects, when cultivated, cause unwholesome states to increase and wholesome states to diminish, should not be cultivated.

Venerable sir, such mind-objects cognizable by the mind, when cultivated, cause unwholesome states to diminish and wholesome states to increase, should be cultivated.

"Venerable sir, as I understand the meaning of what was spoken by the Blessed One in brief in this way, in detail, these three kinds of doubt have been dispelled, uncertainty is gone, having heard the Blessed One's answer to the question."
commentary_pali:
365. Dutiyapucchāyaṃ indriyasaṃvarāyāti indriyānaṃ pidhānāya, guttadvāratāya saṃvutadvāratāyāti attho. Vissajjane panassa cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpampītiādi sevitabbarūpādivasena indriyasaṃvaradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha evaṃ vutteti heṭṭhā somanassādipañhāvissajjanānaṃ sutattā imināpi evarūpena bhavitabbanti sañjātapaṭibhāno bhagavatā evaṃ vutte sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca, etaṃ imassa kho ahaṃ, bhanteti ādikaṃ vacanaṃ avoca. Bhagavāpissa okāsaṃ datvā tuṇhī ahosi. Kathetukāmopi hi yo atthaṃ sampādetuṃ na sakkoti, atthaṃ sampādetuṃ sakkonto vā na kathetukāmo hoti, na tassa bhagavā okāsaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ pana yasmā kathetukāmo ceva, sakkoti ca atthaṃ sampādetuṃ tenassa bhagavā okāsamakāsi.

Tattha evarūpaṃ na sevitabbanti ādīsu ayaṃ saṅkhepo – yaṃ rūpaṃ passato rāgādayo uppajjanti, taṃ na sevitabbaṃ na daṭṭhabbaṃ na oloketabbanti attho. Yaṃ pana passato asubhasaññā vā saṇṭhāti, pasādo vā uppajjati, aniccasaññāpaṭilābho vā hoti, taṃ sevitabbaṃ.

evarūpaṃ na sevitabba

Yaṃ cittakkharaṃ cittabyañjanampi saddaṃ suṇato rāgādayo uppajjanti, evarūpo saddo na sevitabbo. Yaṃ pana atthanissitaṃ dhammanissitaṃ kumbhadāsigītampi suṇantassa pasādo vā uppajjati, nibbidā vā saṇṭhāti, evarūpo saddo sevitabbo.

Yaṃ gandhaṃ ghāyato rāgādayo uppajjanti, evarūpo gandho na sevitabbo. Yaṃ pana gandhaṃ ghāyato asubhasaññādipaṭilābho hoti, evarūpo gandho sevitabbo.

Yaṃ rasaṃ sāyato rāgādayo uppajjanti, evarūpo raso na sevitabbo. Yaṃ pana rasaṃ sāyato āhāre paṭikūlasaññā ceva uppajjati, sāyitapaccayā ca kāyabalaṃ nissāya ariyabhūmiṃ okkamituṃ sakkoti, mahāsīvattherabhāgineyyasīvasāmaṇerassa viya paribhuñjantasseva kilesakkhayo vā hoti, evarūpo raso sevitabbo.

Yaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusato rāgādayo uppajjanti, evarūpaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ na sevitabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana phusato sāriputtattherādīnaṃ viya āsavakkhayo ceva, vīriyañca supaggahitaṃ, pacchimā ca janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpādanena anuggahitā hoti, evarūpaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Sāriputtatthero kira tiṃsa vassāni mañce piṭṭhiṃ na pasāresi. Tathā mahāmoggallānatthero. Mahākassapatthero vīsavassasataṃ mañce piṭṭhiṃ na pasāresi. Anuruddhatthero paññāsa vassāni. Bhaddiyatthero tiṃsa vassāni. Soṇatthero aṭṭhārasa vassāni. Raṭṭhapālatthero dvādasa. Ānandatthero pannarasa. Rāhulatthero dvādasa. Bākulatthero asīti vassāni. Nāḷakatthero yāvaparinibbānā mañce piṭṭhiṃ na pasāresīti.

Ye manoviññeyye dhamme samannāharantassa rāgādayo uppajjanti, ‘‘aho, vata yaṃ paresaṃ paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ mamassā’’tiādinā nayena vā abhijjhādīni āpāthamāgacchanti evarūpā dhammā na sevitabbā. ‘‘Sabbe sattā averā hontū’’ti evaṃ mettādivasena, ye vā pana tiṇṇaṃ therānaṃ dhammā, evarūpā sevitabbā. Tayo kira therā vassūpanāyikadivase kāmavitakkādayo akusalavitakkā na vitakketabbāti katikaṃ akaṃsu. Atha pavāraṇadivase saṅghatthero saṅghanavakaṃ pucchi – ‘‘āvuso, imasmiṃ temāse kittake ṭhāne cittassa dhāvituṃ dinna’’nti? Na, bhante, pariveṇaparicchedato bahi dhāvituṃ adāsinti. Dutiyaṃ pucchi – ‘‘tava āvuso’’ti? Nivāsagehato, bhante, bahi dhāvituṃ na adāsinti. Atha dvepi theraṃ pucchiṃsu ‘‘tumhākaṃ pana, bhante’’ti? Niyakajjhattakhandhapañcakato, āvuso, bahi dhāvituṃ na adāsinti. Tumhehi, bhante, dukkaraṃ katanti. Evarūpo manoviññeyyo dhammo sevitabbo.
commentary_english:
365. In the second question, *indriyasaṃvarāya* means the restraint of the senses, that is, the guarding of the doors [of perception], the closing of the doors, this is the meaning.

In the explanation, *cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpampī* etc., is said in order to show the restraint of the senses by way of forms and so forth that should be cultivated.

There, *evaṃ vutte* means that, because it has been heard that the answers to the questions about pleasant feelings and so forth are such, Sakra, the lord of the gods, having an understanding that it will be of this form, when the Blessed One had spoken thus (p. 2.0328) said this to the Blessed One: “This is for me, venerable sir,” he spoke these words and so forth.

The Blessed One gave him an opportunity and remained silent.

For the Blessed One does not give an opportunity to someone who desires to speak but is not able to accomplish the meaning, or who is able to accomplish the meaning but does not desire to speak.

But because this one both desires to speak and is able to accomplish the meaning, therefore the Blessed One gave him an opportunity.

There, *evarūpaṃ na sevitabba* etc., this is the summary: (p. 3.0736) when a form is seen, lust and so forth arise, that should not be cultivated, should not be seen, should not be looked at, this is the meaning.

But when, by seeing something, foul perception arises, or joy arises, or the attainment of the perception of impermanence [arises], that should be cultivated.

*evarūpaṃ na sevitabba* (p. 3.0736)

When, by hearing a sound that is characterized by thought and is expressive of thought, lust and so forth arise, that kind of sound should not be cultivated.

But when, by hearing a sound that is connected with meaning and connected with the Dharma, even the song of a servant girl carrying a water pot, joy arises, or disgust arises, that kind of sound should be cultivated.

When, by smelling an odor, lust and so forth arise, that kind of odor should not be cultivated.

But when, by smelling an odor, the attainment of foul perception and so forth arises, that kind of odor should be cultivated.

When, by tasting a flavor, lust and so forth arise, that kind of flavor should not be cultivated.

But when, by tasting a flavor, foul perception of food arises, and also, relying on the strength of the body due to the condition of having tasted, one is able to step onto the noble plane (p. 2.0295), or, just as for Sīva, the nephew of the elder Mahāsīva, even while enjoying [food], the destruction of the afflictions occurs, that kind of flavor should be cultivated.

(p. 2.0295) When, by touching a tangible object, lust and so forth arise, that kind of tangible object should not be cultivated.

But when, by touching something, just as for the elders Śāriputra and so forth, the destruction of the influxes occurs, and also energy is well established, and also the later generation is assisted by bringing about conformity to their view, that kind of tangible object should be cultivated.

It is said that the elder Śāriputra did not stretch out his back on a couch for thirty years.

Likewise, the elder Mahāmoggallāna.

The elder Mahākassapa did not stretch out his back on a couch for one hundred and twenty years.

The elder Anuruddha for fifty years.

The elder Bhaddiya for thirty years.

The elder Soṇa for eighteen (p. 2.0329) years.

The elder Raṭṭhapāla for twelve.

The elder Ānanda for fifteen.

The elder Rāhula for twelve.

The elder Bākula for eighty years.

It is said that the elder Nāḷaka did not stretch out his back on a couch until his parinirvāṇa.

(p. 2.0329) When, for someone who reflects on mental objects, lust and so forth arise, [thinking,] "Oh, that which is the property and equipment of others might be mine!" and so forth, in this way or in that way, covetousness and so forth come into the path, those kinds of dharmas should not be cultivated.

"May all beings be without enmity!" in this way, by way of loving-kindness and so forth, or those dharmas of the three elders, those kinds of things should be cultivated.

It is said that those three elders, on the rain-retreat entry day, made an agreement (p. 3.0737) that unskillful thoughts, such as thoughts of sensual pleasure, should not be thought.

Then, on the day of the pavāraṇa, the elder of the Saṃgha asked the Saṃgha-novice: “Friend, in this three-month period, how much space was given for the mind to wander?” “No, venerable sir, [space] was not given to wander outside of the boundary of the monastery.”
He asked a second time, "Friend, what about you?" "Venerable sir, they did not allow me to run outside the dwelling."

Then they both asked the elder, "And what about you, venerable sir?" "Friend, they did not allow me to run outside from the group of five aggregates that are my own."

Venerable Sir, you have done what is difficult.

A *dhamma* that is perceived by the mind in this way should be cultivated.

mula_pali:
366. Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi –

‘‘Sabbeva nu kho, mārisa, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, devānaminda, sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā’’ti.

‘‘Kasmā pana, mārisa, na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā’’ti? ‘‘Anekadhātu nānādhātu kho, devānaminda, loko. Tasmiṃ anekadhātunānādhātusmiṃ loke yaṃ yadeva sattā dhātuṃ abhinivisanti, taṃ tadeva thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharanti – ‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tasmā na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā’’ti.

‘‘Sabbeva nu kho, mārisa, samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, devānaminda, sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā’’ti.

‘‘Kasmā pana, mārisa, na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā’’ti? ‘‘Ye kho, devānaminda, bhikkhū taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā te accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā. Tasmā na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā’’ti.

Itthaṃ bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa pañhaṃ puṭṭho byākāsi. Attamano sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi anumodi – ‘‘evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Tiṇṇā mettha kaṅkhā vigatā kathaṃkathā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā’’ti.
mula_english:
366. Then Śakra, the head of the gods, having rejoiced at and approved of the Blessed One's words, asked the Blessed One a further question:

‘‘Sir, are all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* adherents of a single view, a single discipline, a single desire, a single devotion?’’ ‘‘No, head of the gods, not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* are adherents of a single view, a single discipline, a single desire, a single devotion.’’

‘‘But why, sir, are not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* adherents of a single view, a single discipline, a single desire, a single devotion?’’ ‘‘The world, head of the gods, is of diverse elements and various elements.
In this world of diverse elements and various elements, beings become strongly attached to one or another element, and adhering to that with tenacity and prejudice, they assert: ‘This alone is the truth, everything else is false!’
Therefore not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* are adherents of a single view, a single discipline, a single desire, a single devotion.’’

‘‘Sir, are all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* ultimately accomplished, ultimately secure from the yoke, ultimately practicing the holy life, ultimately at the final goal?’’ ‘‘No, head of the gods, not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* are ultimately accomplished, ultimately secure from the yoke, ultimately practicing the holy life, ultimately at the final goal.’’

‘‘But why, sir, are not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* ultimately accomplished, ultimately secure from the yoke, ultimately practicing the holy life, ultimately at the final goal?’’ ‘‘Those monks, head of the gods, who are liberated through the destruction of craving are ultimately accomplished, ultimately secure from the yoke, ultimately practicing the holy life, ultimately at the final goal.
Therefore not all ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* are ultimately accomplished, ultimately secure from the yoke, ultimately practicing the holy life, ultimately at the final goal.’’

Thus the Blessed One answered Śakra, the head of the gods, when questioned.
And Śakra, the head of the gods, delighted and approved of the Blessed One’s words, exclaiming: ‘‘So it is, Blessed One, so it is, Well-Farer!
I have overcome my doubt and got rid of uncertainty through hearing the Lord’s answer to the question!’’
commentary_pali:
366.Ekantavādāti ekoyeva anto vādassa etesaṃ, na dvedhā gatavādāti ekantavādā, ekaññeva vadantīti pucchati. Ekantasīlāti ekācārā. Ekantachandāti ekaladdhikā. Ekantaajjhosānāti ekantapariyosānā.

Anekadhātu nānādhātu kho, devānaminda, lokoti devānaminda, ayaṃ loko anekajjhāsayo nānajjhāsayo. Ekasmiṃ gantukāme eko ṭhātukāmo hoti. Ekasmiṃ ṭhātukāme eko sayitukāmo hoti. Dve sattā ekajjhāsayā nāma dullabhā. Tasmiṃ anekadhātunānādhātusmiṃ loke yaṃ yadeva dhātuṃ yaṃ yadeva ajjhāsayaṃ sattā abhinivisanti gaṇhanti, taṃ tadeva. Thāmasā parāmāsāti thāmena ca parāmāsena ca. Abhinivissa voharantīti suṭṭhu gaṇhitvā voharanti, kathenti dīpenti kittenti. Idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti idaṃ amhākameva vacanaṃ saccaṃ, aññesaṃ vacanaṃ moghaṃ tucchaṃ niratthakanti.

Anekadhātu nānādhātu kho, devānaminda, loko Thāmasā parāmāsā Abhinivissa voharantī Idameva saccaṃ moghamañña

Accantaniṭṭhāti anto vuccati vināso, antaṃ atītā niṭṭhā etesanti accantaniṭṭhā. Yā etesaṃ niṭṭhā, yo paramassāso nibbānaṃ, taṃ sabbesaṃ vināsātikkantaṃ niccanti vuccati. Yogakkhemoti nibbānasseva nāmaṃ, accanto yogakkhemo etesanti accantayogakkhemī. Seṭṭhaṭṭhena brahmaṃ ariyamaggaṃ carantīti brahmacārī. Accantatthāya brahmacārī accantabrahmacārī. Pariyosānantipi nibbānassa nāmaṃ. Accantaṃ pariyosānaṃ etesanti accantapariyosānā.

Accantaniṭṭhā Yogakkhemo accantayogakkhemī. brahmacārī. accantabrahmacārī. Pariyosāna accantapariyosānā.

Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttāti taṇhāsaṅkhayoti maggopi nibbānampi. Maggo taṇhaṃ saṅkhiṇāti vināsetīti taṇhāsaṅkhayo. Nibbānaṃ yasmā taṃ āgamma taṇhā saṅkhiyati vinassati, tasmā taṇhāsaṅkhayo. Taṇhāsaṅkhayena maggena vimuttā, taṇhāsaṅkhaye nibbāne vimuttā adhimuttāti taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā.

Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā.

Ettāvatā ca bhagavatā cuddasapi mahāpañhā byākatā honti. Cuddasa mahāpañhā nāma issāmacchariyaṃ eko pañho, piyāppiyaṃ eko, chando eko, vitakko eko, papañco eko, somanassaṃ eko, domanassaṃ eko, upekkhā eko, kāyasamācāro eko, vacīsamācāro eko, pariyesanā eko, indriyasaṃvaro eko, anekadhātu eko, accantaniṭṭhā ekoti.
commentary_english:
366. *Ekantavādā*: because theirs is a one-sided doctrine (anta vādassa), not a doctrine that goes in two ways (dvedhā gatavādā); therefore, *ekantavādā*, he asks, "do they speak only one thing (ekaññeva vadantīti)?"
*Ekantasīlā*: single conduct (ekācārā).
*Ekantachandā*: single desire (ekaladdhikā).
*Ekantaajjhosānā*: single end (ekantapariyosānā).

The Blessed One said, "This world (loko), O Indra of the gods (devānaminda), is of diverse elements (anekadhātu), of various elements (nānādhātu)"; O Indra of the gods, this world is of diverse inclinations (anekajjhāsayo), of various inclinations (nānajjhāsayo).
When one person wants to go (ekasmiṃ gantukāme), the other wants to stay (eko ṭhātukāmo hoti).
When one person wants to stay (ekasmiṃ ṭhātukāme), the other wants to lie down (eko sayitukāmo hoti).
It is rare to find two beings of identical inclinations (dve sattā ekajjhāsayā nāma dullabhā).
In this world of diverse elements and various elements (tasmiṃ anekadhātunānādhātusmiṃ loke), whatever element (dhātuṃ) or whatever inclination (ajjhāsayaṃ) beings adhere to (abhinivisanti gaṇhanti), that is what they become (taṃ tadeva).
*Thāmasā parāmāsā*: by force (thāmena) and by adherence (parāmāsena).
*Abhinivissa voharantī*: having grasped well (suṭṭhu gaṇhitvā), they declare (voharanti), they narrate (kathenti), they illuminate (dīpenti), they praise (kittenti).
*Idameva saccaṃ moghamañña*: "this alone is true (saccaṃ), other things are false (moghaṃ)," that is, "our word alone is true, the words of others are vain (moghaṃ), empty (tucchaṃ), and meaningless (niratthakanti)."

Diverse elements, various elements, O Indra of the gods, [is] the world!
By force, by adherence!
Having grasped, they declare!
This alone is true, other things are false!
*Accantaniṭṭhā*: *anta* means destruction (vināso), *niṭṭhā* is the end (antaṃ atītā) that has passed beyond these; therefore, *accantaniṭṭhā*.
That which is their end (niṭṭhā), which is the highest breath (paramassāso), nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ), that is said to be the eternal (niccanti) that has transcended all destruction (sabbesaṃ vināsātikkantaṃ).
*Yogakkhemo*: is a name for nirvāṇa itself; because theirs is the absence (accanto) of *yogakkhemo*, [they are called] *accantayogakkhemī*.
He who lives the noble path (ariyamaggaṃ carantīti) in the highest sense (seṭṭhaṭṭhena), O Brahman (brahmā), is called a *brahmacārī* (celibate, religious student).
The *brahmacārī* for the sake of the highest goal is the *accantabrahmacārī*.
*Pariyosāna* is also a name for nirvāṇa.
Because theirs is the end that has transcended (accantaṃ pariyosānaṃ), [they are called] *accantapariyosānā*.

*Accantaniṭṭhā*.
*Yogakkhemo*.
*Accantayogakkhemī*.
*Brahmacārī*.
*Accantabrahmacārī*.
*Pariyosāna*.
*Accantapariyosānā*.

*Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā*: *taṇhāsaṅkhayo* means both the path (maggo) and nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ).
*Maggo taṇhaṃ saṅkhiṇāti vināsetīti taṇhāsaṅkhayo*: because the path destroys (saṅkhiṇāti vināsetīti) craving (*taṇhā*), it is *taṇhāsaṅkhayo*.
*Nibbānaṃ yasmā taṃ āgamma taṇhā saṅkhiyati vinassati, tasmā taṇhāsaṅkhayo*: because when nirvāṇa is reached (*taṃ āgamma*), craving is destroyed (*taṇhā saṅkhiyati vinassati*), therefore it is *taṇhāsaṅkhayo*.
*Taṇhāsaṅkhayena maggena vimuttā, taṇhāsaṅkhaye nibbāne vimuttā adhimuttāti taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā*: liberated by the path that destroys craving, liberated in nirvāṇa where craving is destroyed, because they are intent [on that liberation], [they are called] *taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā*.

*Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā*.
*Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā*.

Thus, the Blessed One has explained these fourteen great questions (cuddasapi mahāpañhā).
The fourteen great questions are: envy and stinginess, one question; the beloved and the unloved, one; desire, one; thought, one; proliferation, one; joy, one; sorrow, one; equanimity, one; bodily conduct, one; verbal conduct, one; seeking, one; sense restraint, one; diverse elements, one; the highest end, one.

mula_pali:
367. Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Ejā, bhante, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṃ, ejā imaṃ purisaṃ parikaḍḍhati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā. Tasmā ayaṃ puriso uccāvacamāpajjati . Yesāhaṃ, bhante, pañhānaṃ ito bahiddhā aññesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu okāsakammampi nālatthaṃ, te me bhagavatā byākatā. Dīgharattānusayitañca pana dīgharattānupassatā, yañca pana (syā.), dīgharattānusayino, yañca pana (sī. pī.) me vicikicchākathaṃkathāsallaṃ, tañca bhagavatā abbuḷha’’nti.

dīgharattānupassatā, yañca pana (syā.), dīgharattānusayino, yañca pana (sī. pī.)

‘‘Abhijānāsi no tvaṃ, devānaminda, ime pañhe aññe samaṇabrāhmaṇe pucchitā’’ti? ‘‘Abhijānāmahaṃ, bhante, ime pañhe aññe samaṇabrāhmaṇe pucchitā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana te, devānaminda, byākaṃsu? Sace te agaru bhāsassū’’ti. ‘‘Na kho me, bhante, garu yatthassa bhagavā nisinno bhagavantarūpo vā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, devānaminda, bhāsassū’’ti. ‘‘Yesvāhaṃ yesāhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), bhante , maññāmi samaṇabrāhmaṇā āraññikā pantasenāsanāti, tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ime pañhe pucchāmi, te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaṃyeva paṭipucchanti – ‘ko nāmo āyasmā’ti? Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi – ‘ahaṃ kho, mārisa, sakko devānamindo’ti. Te mamaṃyeva uttari paṭipucchanti – ‘kiṃ panāyasmā, devānaminda devānamindo (sī. pī.), kammaṃ katvā imaṃ ṭhānaṃ patto’ti? Tesāhaṃ yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Te tāvatakeneva attamanā honti – ‘sakko ca no devānamindo diṭṭho, yañca no apucchimhā, tañca no byākāsī’ti. Te aññadatthu mamaṃyeva sāvakā sampajjanti, na cāhaṃ tesaṃ. Ahaṃ kho pana, bhante, bhagavato sāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’’ti .

yesāhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) devānamindo (sī. pī.)

Somanassapaṭilābhakathā
mula_english:
367. Thus, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, having rejoiced and approved of the Blessed One's speech, said this to the Blessed One:

“Craving (*ejā*), venerable sir (*bhante*), is a disease (*roga*), craving is a sore (*gaṇḍa*), craving is a dart (*sallaṃ*), craving drags this person (*purisaṃ*) around for the sake of the arising of that very existence (*bhavassa abhinibbattiyā*). Therefore, this person undergoes various states (*uccāvacamāpajjati*).

“Whereas other ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* gave me no chance to ask these questions (*pañhānaṃ*), the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) has explained them to me. The dart (*sallaṃ*) of doubt (*vicikicchā*) and uncertainty (*kathaṃkathā*) that had long lain dormant in me, has been removed by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā abbuḷha’’nti*).”

“Do you remember, Lord of the Gods (*devānaminda*), that you asked these questions of other ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*?”

“I remember, venerable sir (*bhante*), that I asked these questions of other ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*.”

“Then, if you don’t mind, Lord of the Gods (*devānaminda*), please tell me what they said.”

“It is not troublesome for me, venerable sir (*bhante*), when the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) or anyone like him is present.”

“Then tell me, Lord of the Gods (*devānaminda*).”

“Venerable sir (*bhante*), I approach those ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who, I think, are forest-dwellers (*āraññikā*) and live in remote lodgings (*pantasenāsanāti*) and ask them these questions (*pañhe pucchāmi*). But when asked by me, they are not able to explain (*na sampāyanti*). Being unable to explain, they instead ask me, ‘What is your name, venerable sir (*āyasmā*)?’ When asked by them, I reply, ‘I am Śakra (*sakko*), Lord of the Gods (*devānamindo*)’.

They then ask me further, ‘What good deed (*kammaṃ*) have you done, venerable sir (*āyasmā*), to attain this state (*ṭhānaṃ patto*)?’ Then I teach them the *dharma* as I have heard it and as it is known to me (*yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ desemi*).

They are delighted by just that much, thinking, ‘We have seen Śakra (*sakko*), Lord of the Gods (*devānamindo diṭṭho*), and he has explained (*byākāsī*) what we asked him (*apucchimhā*)’. Instead of me becoming their disciple, they become my disciples (*sāvakā sampajjanti, na cāhaṃ tesaṃ*).

However, venerable sir (*bhante*), I am a disciple (*sāvako*) of the Blessed One (*bhagavato*), one who has entered the stream (*sotāpanno*), is not subject to downfall (*avinipātadhammo*), is assured (*niyato*), and is headed for enlightenment (*sambodhiparāyaṇo*).”
0320 Somanassapaṭilābhakathā
commentary_pali:
367.Ejāti calanaṭṭhena taṇhā vuccati. Sā pīḷanaṭṭhena rogo, anto padussanaṭṭhena gaṇḍo, anuppaviṭṭhaṭṭhena sallaṃ. Tasmā ayaṃ purisoti yasmā ejā attanā katakammānurūpena purisaṃ tattha tattha abhinibbattatthāya kaḍḍhati, tasmā ayaṃ puriso tesaṃ tesaṃ bhavānaṃ vasena uccāvacaṃ āpajjati. Brahmaloke ucco hoti, devaloke avaco. Devaloke ucco, manussaloke avaco. Manussaloke ucco, apāye avaco. Yesāhaṃ, bhanteti yesaṃ ahaṃ bhante. Sandhivasena panettha ‘‘yesāha’’nti hoti. Yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattanti yathā mayā suto ceva uggahito ca, evaṃ. Dhammaṃ desemīti sattavatapadaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Na cāhaṃ tesanti ahaṃ pana tesaṃ sāvako na sampajjāmi. Ahaṃ kho pana, bhantetiādinā attano sotāpannabhāvaṃ jānāpeti.

Somanassapaṭilābhakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
367. "Eja" means *taṇhā* (craving) because of its nature of moving (calanaṭṭhena).

That (*sā*), due to its nature of oppressing (pīḷanaṭṭhena), is *roga* (disease); due to its nature of internally corrupting (anto padussanaṭṭhena), is *gaṇḍa* (boil); due to its nature of deeply penetrating (anuppaviṭṭhaṭṭhena), is *sallaṃ* (dart).

"Therefore, this person (*tasmā ayaṃ puriso*)" means, because *ejā* impels a person (*purisaṃ*) according to deeds done by himself (*attanā katakammānurūpena*) to be born (*abhinibbattatthāya*) in various places (*tattha tattha*), therefore, this person (*tasmā ayaṃ puriso*) undergoes diverse (*uccāvacaṃ*) states (*āpajjati*) according to the influence (*vasena*) of those various existences (*tesaṃ tesaṃ bhavānaṃ*).

In the Brahma world (*brahmaloke*) he is high (*ucco hoti*), in the deva world (*devaloke*) he is low (*avaco*).

In the deva world (*devaloke*) he is high (*ucco*), in the human world (*manussaloke*) he is low (*avaco*).

In the human world (*manussaloke*) he is high (*ucco*), in the *apāya* (realm of suffering) he is low (*avaco*).

"Yesāhaṃ, bhante" means, "Of whom I am, O Bhante."

Here, through the way of combination (*sandhivasena*), it is "yesāhaṃ."

"Yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyatta" means, "Just as it was heard by me (*yathā mayā suto*), and also grasped (*uggahito ca*), thus it is (*evaṃ*)."

"Dhammaṃ desemī" means, "I teach the *dhamma*," the phrase being "sattavatapadaṃ dhammaṃ desemi."

"Na cāhaṃ tesa" means, "I, indeed, am not a disciple (*sāvako na sampajjāmi*) of those."

"Ahaṃ kho pana, bhante" etc., makes known (*jānāpeti*) his own state of being a *sotāpanna* (stream-enterer).

Narration of the Story of Gaining Joy (*somanassapaṭilābhakathāvaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
368. ‘‘Abhijānāsi no tvaṃ, devānaminda, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābha’’nti? ‘‘Abhijānāmahaṃ , bhante, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābha’’nti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, devānaminda, abhijānāsi ito pubbe evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābha’’nti?

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho samūpabbuḷho (sī. pī.) ahosi. Tasmiṃ kho pana, bhante, saṅgāme devā jiniṃsu, asurā parājayiṃsu parājiṃsu (sī. pī.). Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, taṃ saṅgāmaṃ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmassa etadahosi – ‘yā ceva dāni dibbā ojā yā ca asurā ojā, ubhayametaṃ ubhayamettha (syā.) devā paribhuñjissantī’ti. So kho pana me, bhante, vedapaṭilābho somanassapaṭilābho sadaṇḍāvacaro sasatthāvacaro na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yo kho pana me ayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā vedapaṭilābho somanassapaṭilābho, so adaṇḍāvacaro asatthāvacaro ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattatī’’ti.

samūpabbuḷho (sī. pī.) parājiṃsu (sī. pī.) ubhayamettha (syā.)
mula_english:
368.
"Do you not recall, Indra, Lord of the Gods, having previously experienced such acquisition of feeling ( *vedapaṭilābha* ) and such acquisition of joy ( *somanassapaṭilābha* )?"

"I do recall, venerable sir ( *bhante* ), having previously experienced such acquisition of feeling and such acquisition of joy."

"How then, Indra, Lord of the Gods, do you recall previously experiencing such acquisition of feeling and such acquisition of joy?"

"Formerly, venerable sir, a battle ( *devāsurasaṅgāmo* ) between the gods and the asuras was joined.
In that battle, venerable sir, the gods were victorious ( *devā jiniṃsu* ), and the asuras were defeated ( *asurā parājayiṃsu* ).
Then, venerable sir, having conquered in that battle, the thought occurred to me, the victor in battle: 'Now the gods will enjoy both the divine nourishment ( *dibbā ojā* ) and the nourishment of the asuras ( *asurā ojā* ).'
But that acquisition of feeling and acquisition of joy, venerable sir, which was connected with blows and weapons, did not lead to disenchantment ( *nibbidā* ), dispassion ( *virāga* ), cessation ( *nirodha* ), peace ( *upasama* ), higher knowledge ( *abhiññā* ), enlightenment ( *sambodha* ), or nirvāṇa ( *nibbāna* ).
However, that acquisition of feeling and acquisition of joy that I obtained, venerable sir, by hearing the Dharma ( *dhammaṃ* ) from the Blessed One ( *bhagavato* ), that which is not connected with blows and weapons, does lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, higher knowledge, enlightenment, and nirvāṇa."
commentary_pali: 368.Vedapaṭilābhanti tuṭṭhipaṭilābhaṃ. Devāsurasaṅgāmoti devānañca asurānañca saṅgāmo. Samupabyūḷhoti samāpanno nalāṭena nalāṭaṃ paharaṇākārappatto viya. Etesaṃ kira kadāci mahāsamuddapiṭṭhe saṅgāmo hoti tattha pana chedanavijjhanādīhi aññamaññaṃ ghāto nāma natthi, dārumeṇḍakayuddhaṃ viya jayaparājayamattameva hoti. Kadāci devā jinanti, kadāci asurā. Tattha yasmiṃ saṅgāme devā puna apaccāgamanāya asure jiniṃsu, taṃ sandhāya tasmiṃ kho pana bhantetiādimāha. Ubhayametanti ubhayaṃ etaṃ. Duvidhampi ojaṃ ettha devaloke devāyeva paribhuñjissantīti evamassa āvajjantassa balavapītisomanassaṃ uppajji. Sadaṇḍāvacaroti sadaṇḍāvacarako, daṇḍaggahaṇena satthaggahaṇena saddhiṃ ahosi, na nikkhittadaṇḍasatthoti dasseti. Ekantanibbidāyāti ekanteneva vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāyāti sabbaṃ mahāgovindasutte vuttameva.
commentary_english:
368. *Vedapaṭilābha* means *tuṭṭhipaṭilābhaṃ*.

*Devāsurasaṅgāmo* means *devānañca asurānañca saṅgāmo*.

*Samupabyūḷho* means *samāpanno nalāṭena nalāṭaṃ paharaṇākārappatto viya*.

It is said that sometimes there is a battle on the surface of the great ocean, but there is no mutual killing with cutting, piercing, etc.; there is only a matter of victory and defeat, like a stick-puppet fight.

Sometimes the gods conquer, sometimes the asuras.

Referring to that battle in which the gods conquered the asuras for not returning again, he said, "*tasmiṃ kho pana bhante*," etc.

*Ubhayame**ta*nti means *ubhayaṃ etaṃ*.

Even the two kinds of *ojaṃ* here in the world of gods, they will enjoy it, thus arose strong joy and gladness to him contemplating.

*Sadaṇḍāvacaro* means *sadaṇḍāvacarako, daṇḍaggahaṇena satthaggahaṇena saddhiṃ ahosi, na nikkhittadaṇḍasatthoti dasseti*.

*Ekantanibbidāyā* means *ekanteneva vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāyāti sabbaṃ mahāgovindasutte vuttameva*.

mula_pali:
369. ‘‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, devānaminda, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedesī’’ti? ‘‘Cha kho ahaṃ, bhante, atthavase sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Idheva tiṭṭhamānassa, devabhūtassa me sato;

Punarāyu ca me laddho, evaṃ jānāhi mārisa.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, paṭhamaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Cutāhaṃ diviyā kāyā, āyuṃ hitvā amānusaṃ;

Amūḷho gabbhamessāmi, yattha me ramatī mano.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, dutiyaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Svāhaṃ amūḷhapaññassa amūḷhapañhassa (?), viharaṃ sāsane rato;

amūḷhapañhassa (?)

Ñāyena viharissāmi, sampajāno paṭissato.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, tatiyaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Ñāyena me carato ca, sambodhi ce bhavissati;

Aññātā viharissāmi, sveva anto bhavissati.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, catutthaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Cutāhaṃ mānusā kāyā, āyuṃ hitvāna mānusaṃ;

Puna devo bhavissāmi, devalokamhi uttamo.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, pañcamaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Te ye (?) paṇītatarā devā, akaniṭṭhā yasassino;

ye (?)

Antime vattamānamhi, so nivāso bhavissati.

‘‘Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, chaṭṭhaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.

‘‘Ime kho ahaṃ, bhante, cha atthavase sampassamāno evarūpaṃ vedapaṭilābhaṃ somanassapaṭilābhaṃ pavedemi.
mula_english:
"But what is it, lord of gods, that seeing which advantage, you declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy?"

"It is these six advantages, venerable sir, that seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"While staying right here, being a god, mindful,

and I have gained renewed life, know this, sir."

"This, venerable sir, is the first advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"Having passed away from the divine body, giving up non-human life,

without delusion I will enter a womb, where my mind delights."

"This, venerable sir, is the second advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"I, of undeluded wisdom, delighting in dwelling in the Dispensation,

I will live righteously, fully aware and mindful."

"This, venerable sir, is the third advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"And as I live righteously, if enlightenment should come to pass,

I will live unknown, that very one will be the end."

"This, venerable sir, is the fourth advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"Having passed away from the human body, giving up human life,

I will be a god again, supreme in the world of gods (devaloka)."

"This, venerable sir, is the fifth advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"Those devas (devā), more excellent, Peerless, glorious,

in the final round, that will be the dwelling."

"This, venerable sir, is the sixth advantage that, seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."

"It is these six advantages, venerable sir, that seeing which, I declare such attainment of feeling, such attainment of joy."
commentary_pali:
369.Pavedesīti kathesi dīpesi. Idhevāti imasmiññeva okāse. Devabhūtassa me satoti devassa me sato. Punarāyu ca me laddhoti puna aññena kammavipākena me jīvitaṃ laddhanti, iminā attano cutabhāvaṃ ceva upapannabhāvañca āvikaroti.

Diviyā kāyāti dibbā attabhāvā. Āyuṃ hitvā amānusanti dibbaṃ āyuṃ jahitvā. Amūḷho gabbhamessāmīti niyatagatikattā amūḷho hutvā. Yattha me ramatī manoti yattha me mano ramissati, tattheva khattiyakulādīsu gabbhaṃ upagacchissāmīti sattakkhattuṃ deve ca mānuse cāti imamatthaṃ dīpeti.

Diviyā kāyā Āyuṃ hitvā amānusa Amūḷho gabbhamessāmī Yattha me ramatī mano

Ñāyena viharissāmīti manussesu upapannopi mātaraṃ jīvitā voropanādīnaṃ abhabbattā ñāyena kāraṇena samena viharissāmīti attho.

Ñāyena viharissāmī

Sambodhice bhavissatīti idaṃ sakadāgāmimaggaṃ sandhāya vadati, sace sakadāgāmī bhavissāmīti dīpeti. Aññātā viharissāmīti aññātā ājānitukāmo hutvā viharissāmi. Sveva anto bhavissatīti so eva me manussaloke anto bhavissatīti.

Sambodhi ce bhavissatī Aññātā viharissāmī Sveva anto bhavissatī

Punadevo bhavissāmi, devalokasmiṃ uttamoti puna devalokasmiṃ uttamo sakko devānamindo bhavissāmīti vadati.

Puna devo bhavissāmi, devalokasmiṃ uttamo

Antime vattamānamhīti antime bhave vattamāne. So nivāso bhavissatīti ye te āyunā ca paññāya ca akaniṭṭhā jeṭṭhakā sabbadevehi paṇītatarā devā, avasāne me so nivāso bhavissati . Ayaṃ kira tato sakkattabhāvato cuto tasmiṃ attabhāve anāgāmimaggassa paṭiladdhattā uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī hutvā avihādīsu nibbattanto avasāne akaniṭṭhe nibbattissati. Taṃ sandhāya evamāha. Esa kira avihesu kappasahassaṃ vasissati, atappesu dve kappasahassāni, sudassesu cattāri kappasahassāni, sudassīsu aṭṭha, akaniṭṭhesu soḷasāti ekatiṃsa kappasahassāni brahmaāyuṃ anubhavissati. Sakko devarājā anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati visākhā mahāupāsikāti tayopi hi ime ekappamāṇaāyukā eva, vaṭṭābhiratasattā nāma etehi sadisā sukhabhāgino nāma natthi.

Antime vattamānamhī So nivāso bhavissatī
commentary_english:
369. "pavedesī" means he spoke, he indicated. "idhevā" means in this very place. "devabhūtassa me sato" means of the deity, of my being. "punarāyu ca me laddho" means also, renewed life was obtained by me; thereby, he reveals both the fact of his death and the fact of his rebirth.

"diviyā kāyā" means divine existences. "āyuṃ hitvā amānusa" means having abandoned divine life, non-human. "amūḷho gabbhamessāmī" means because of determined destiny, having become unconfused. "yattha me ramatī mano" means wherever my mind delights, there in a kṣatriya family, etc., I will enter a womb; in seven instances, among gods and humans, he indicates this meaning.

diviyā kāyā āyuṃ hitvā amānusa amūḷho gabbhamessāmī yattha me ramatī mano

"ñāyena viharissāmī" means even having arisen among humans, because of the unsuitability of depriving a mother of life, etc., I will live justly, with reason, equally; this is the meaning.

ñāyena viharissāmī

sambodhi"ce bhavissatī" means this refers to the path of the once-returner; if I will be a once-returner, he indicates. "aññātā viharissāmī" means unknown, desiring to know, I will live. "sveva anto bhavissatī" means that very one will be the end for me in the human world.

sambodhi ce bhavissatī aññātā viharissāmī sveva anto bhavissatī

puna"devo bhavissāmi, devalokasmiṃ uttamo" means again, in the world of the gods, the highest, Śakra, the lord of the gods, I will become, he says.

puna devo bhavissāmi, devalokasmiṃ uttamo

"antime vattamānamhī" means in the last becoming, while continuing. "so nivāso bhavissatī" means those who, by life and by wisdom, are the highest and most excellent, more exquisite than all the gods, at the end, that will be my dwelling . This one, it seems, having died from that state of being Śakra, in that existence, because of having regained the path of non-returning, becoming one who goes upstream, one who goes to Akaniṣṭha, while being reborn in Aviha, etc., in the end, will be reborn in Akaniṣṭha. Referring to that, he said thus. This one, it seems, will dwell for a thousand aeons in Aviha, two thousand aeons in Atappa, four thousand aeons in Sudassa, eight in Sudassī, sixteen in Akaniṣṭha; thus, experiencing a Brahmā life of thirty-one thousand aeons. Śakra, the divine king, Anāthapiṇḍika, the householder, Visākhā, the great female lay follower—these three, indeed, are of the same measure of life, called beings delighted in the round; there is no one similar to these who shares in happiness.

antime vattamānamhī so nivāso bhavissatī

mula_pali:
370.‘‘Apariyositasaṅkappo , vicikiccho kathaṃkathī.

Vicariṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, anvesanto tathāgataṃ.

‘‘Yassu maññāmi samaṇe, pavivittavihārino;

Sambuddhā iti maññāno, gacchāmi te upāsituṃ.

‘‘‘Kathaṃ ārādhanā hoti, kathaṃ hoti virādhanā’;

Iti puṭṭhā na sampāyanti sambhonti (syā.), magge paṭipadāsu ca.

sambhonti (syā.)

‘‘Tyassu yadā maṃ jānanti, sakko devānamāgato;

Tyassu mameva pucchanti, ‘kiṃ katvā pāpuṇī idaṃ’.

‘‘Tesaṃ yathāsutaṃ dhammaṃ, desayāmi jane sutaṃ janesuta (ka. sī.);

janesuta (ka. sī.)

Tena attamanā honti, ‘diṭṭho no vāsavoti ca’.

‘‘Yadā ca buddhamaddakkhiṃ, vicikicchāvitāraṇaṃ;

Somhi vītabhayo ajja, sambuddhaṃ payirupāsiya payirupāsayiṃ (syā. ka.).

payirupāsayiṃ (syā. ka.)

‘‘Taṇhāsallassa hantāraṃ, buddhaṃ appaṭipuggalaṃ;

Ahaṃ vande mahāvīraṃ, buddhamādiccabandhunaṃ.

‘‘Yaṃ karomasi brahmuno, samaṃ devehi mārisa;

Tadajja tuyhaṃ kassāma dassāma (syā. ka.), handa sāmaṃ karoma te.

dassāma (syā. ka.)

‘‘Tvameva asi tuvamevasi (pī.) sambuddho, tuvaṃ satthā anuttaro;

tuvamevasi (pī.)

Sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, natthi te paṭipuggalo’’ti.
mula_english:
370. Unfulfilled in aims, doubtful, questioning.

Wandering a long road, seeking the *tathāgata*.

"Among those ascetics, I imagine, living in seclusion;

I go to serve those who seem to be fully awakened ones, thinking 'Surely they are enlightened.'"

"'How does reverence occur? How does irreverence occur?'"

When asked thus, they do not satisfy, regarding the path and its practices.

"But when they know me, that I, Śakra, have come among the gods,"

"They ask me, 'Having done what, did you attain this?'"

"To them, I teach the Dharma as I have heard it, comprehensible to people;"

"Thereby they become delighted, saying, 'We have seen Vāsava!'"

"But now I’ve seen the Buddha, the dispeller of doubt;

Today, I am without fear, having attended upon the Fully Awakened One."

"The Buddha, the slayer of the dart of craving, the incomparable one;"

I pay homage to the great hero, the Buddha, kinsman of the sun.

Just as we worship Brahmā, along with the gods, O venerable one;

So likewise today we worship you, come, let us do reverence to you.

"You are the Fully Awakened One, you are the unsurpassed Teacher;"

"In the world with its gods, there is no equal to you."
commentary_pali:
370.Apariyositasaṅkappoti aniṭṭhitamanoratho. Yassu maññāmi samaṇeti ye ca samaṇe pavivittavihārinoti maññāmi.

Ārādhanāti sampādanā. Virādhanāti asampādanā. Na sampāyantīti sampādetvā kathetuṃ na sakkonti.

Ārādhanā Virādhanā Na sampāyantī

Ādiccabandhunanti ādiccopi gotamagotto, bhagavāpi gotamagotto, tasmā evamāha. Yaṃ karomasīti yaṃ pubbe brahmuno namakkāraṃ karoma. Samaṃ devehīti devehi saddhiṃ, ito paṭṭhāya idāni amhākaṃ brahmuno namakkārakaraṇaṃ natthīti dasseti. Sāmaṃ karomāti namakkāraṃ karoma.

Ādiccabandhuna Yaṃ karomasī Samaṃ devehī Sāmaṃ karomā
commentary_english:
370. *apariyositasaṅkappo* means unfulfilled wish.
*yassu maññāmi samaṇe* means those recluses who live in solitude, I think.

*ārādhanā* means accomplishment.
*virādhanā* means non-accomplishment.
*na sampāyantī* means they are not able to accomplish and speak.

*ādiccabandhuna* means Ādicca is also of the Gotama clan, the Blessed One is also of the Gotama clan, therefore he said thus.
*yaṃ karomasī* means that which we formerly do as homage to Brahmā, we do.
*samaṃ devehī* means together with the gods, from here on, now there is no making of homage to Brahmā for us, he shows.
*sāmaṃ karomā* means we do homage.

*ādiccabandhuna*, *yaṃ karomasī*, *samaṃ devehī*, *sāmaṃ karomā*

mula_pali:
371. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘bahūpakāro kho mesi tvaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavantaṃ paṭhamaṃ pasādesi. Tayā, tāta, paṭhamaṃ pasāditaṃ pacchā mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamimhā arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Pettike vā ṭhāne ṭhapayissāmi , gandhabbarājā bhavissasi, bhaddañca te sūriyavacchasaṃ dammi, sā hi te abhipatthitā’’ti.

Atha kho sakko devānamindo pāṇinā pathaviṃ parāmasitvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānesi – ‘‘namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā’’ti.

Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne sakkassa devānamindassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’’nti. Aññesañca asītiyā devatāsahassānaṃ , iti ye sakkena devānamindena ajjhiṭṭhapañhā puṭṭhā , te bhagavatā byākatā. Tasmā imassa veyyākaraṇassa sakkapañhātveva adhivacananti.

Sakkapañhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then Sakka, ruler of the gods, said to Pañcasikha, son of a *gandharva*: “You have been of great help to me, dear Pañcasikha, in that you were the first to please the Blessed One. Because you were the first to please him, we were later able to approach and see the Blessed One, the *arhat*, the fully enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*). I will establish you in a fatherly position, you shall be king of the *gandharvas*, and I will give you Bhaddā Suriyavacchasā, whom you desired.”

Then Sakka, ruler of the gods, touched the earth with his hand and exclaimed three times: “Homage to that Blessed One, the *arhat*, the fully enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*)!”

And while this explanation was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless *dharma*-eye arose in Sakka, ruler of the gods: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.” And also in eighty thousand other deities. Thus, the questions that Sakka, ruler of the gods, had asked, were explained by the Blessed One. Therefore, this exposition is called "Sakka's Questions" (*sakkapañha*).

The Sakka's Questions *sūtra*, the eighth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
371.Parāmasitvāti tuṭṭhacitto sahāyaṃ hatthena hatthamhi paharanto viya pathaviṃ paharitvā, sakkhibhāvatthāya vā paharitvā ‘‘yathā tvaṃ niccalo, evamahaṃ bhagavatī’’ti. Ajjhiṭṭhapañhāti ajjhesitapañhā patthitapañhā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Iti sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāyaṃ

Sakkapañhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
"Having touched" (parāmasitvā): with a delighted mind, as if striking a friend's hand with his own hand, or striking the earth to bear witness, [saying,] "Just as you are immovable, so am I devoted."

"Asked question" (ajjhiṭṭhapañhā): a requested question, a desired question.

The rest is clear throughout (sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti).

Thus ends the commentary on the Sakkapañha Sutta in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, commentary on the Dīgha Nikāya.

mula_pali:
372. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṃ nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhaddante’’ti bhadanteti (sī. syā. pī.) te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

Uddeso
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living among the Kurus, where there was a town of the Kurus named Kammāsadhamma.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” those *bhikṣus* replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

Outline.

mula_pali:
373. ‘‘Ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā, sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.

‘‘Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

Uddeso niṭṭhito.

Kāyānupassanā ānāpānapabbaṃ
mula_english:
“Monks, this is the direct path for the purification of beings, for overcoming sorrow and lamentation, for the disappearance of pain and sadness, for gaining the right path, for the realization of *Nirvana*: that is to say, the four foundations of mindfulness.

"Which four? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body (*kāye kāyānupassī viharati*), ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings (*vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati*), ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating mind in mind (*citte cittānupassī viharati*), ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating mind-objects in mind-objects (*dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati*), ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

The summary is finished.

Contemplation of the Body: The Section on Mindfulness of Breathing.
commentary_pali:
373.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamapubbapadavaṇṇanā – ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggoti kasmā bhagavā idaṃ suttamabhāsi? Kururaṭṭhavāsīnaṃ gambhīradesanāpaṭiggahaṇasamatthatāya. Kururaṭṭhavāsino kira bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo utupaccayādisampannattā tassa raṭṭhassa sappāyautupaccayasevanena niccaṃ kallasarīrā kallacittā ca honti. Te cittasarīrakallatāya anuggahitapaññābalā gambhīrakathaṃ paṭiggahetuṃ samatthā honti. Tena nesaṃ bhagavā imaṃ gambhīradesanāpaṭiggahaṇasamatthataṃ sampassanto ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu kammaṭṭhānaṃ arahatte pakkhipitvā idaṃ gambhīratthaṃ mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttaṃ abhāsi. Yathā hi puriso suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭakaṃ labhitvā tattha nānāpupphāni pakkhipeyya, suvaṇṇamañjūsaṃ vā pana labhitvā sattaratanāni pakkhipeyya, evaṃ bhagavā kururaṭṭhavāsiparisaṃ labhitvā gambhīradesanaṃ desesi. Tenevettha aññānipi gambhīratthāni imasmiṃ dīghanikāye mahānidānaṃ majjhimanikāye satipaṭṭhānaṃ, sāropamaṃ, rukkhopamaṃ, raṭṭhapālaṃ, māgaṇḍiyaṃ, āneñjasappāyanti aññānipi suttāni desesi.

Apica tasmiṃ janapade catasso parisā pakatiyāva satipaṭṭhānabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, antamaso dāsakammakaraparijānāpi satipaṭṭhānapaṭisaṃyuttameva kathaṃ kathenti. Udakatitthasuttakantanaṭṭhānādīsupi niratthakakathā nāma nappavattati. Sace kāci itthī ‘‘amma, tvaṃ kataraṃ satipaṭṭhānabhāvanaṃ manasikarosī’’ti pucchitā ‘‘na kiñcī’’ti vadati, taṃ garahanti ‘‘dhiratthu tava jīvitaṃ, jīvamānāpi tvaṃ matasadisā’’ti. Atha naṃ ‘‘mā dāni puna evamakāsī’’ti ovaditvā aññataraṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ uggaṇhāpenti. Yā pana ‘‘ahaṃ asukasatipaṭṭhānaṃ nāma manasikaromī’’ti vadati, tassā ‘‘sādhu sādhū’’ti sādhukāraṃ katvā ‘‘tava jīvitaṃ sujīvitaṃ, tvaṃ nāma manussattaṃ pattā, tavatthāya sammāsambuddho uppanno’’tiādīhi pasaṃsanti. Na kevalañcettha manussajātikāva satipaṭṭhānamanasikārayuttā, te nissāya viharantā tiracchānagatāpi.

Tatridaṃ vatthu – eko kira naṭako suvapotakaṃ gahetvā sikkhāpento vicarati. So bhikkhunupassayaṃ upanissāya vasitvā gamanakāle suvapotakaṃ pamussitvā gato. Taṃ sāmaṇeriyo gahetvā paṭijaggiṃsu. Buddharakkhito tissa nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Taṃ ekadivasaṃ purato nisinnaṃ disvā mahātherī āha – ‘‘buddharakkhitā’’ti. Kiṃ, ayyeti? Atthi te koci bhāvanāmanasikāroti? Natthi, ayyeti. Āvuso, pabbajitānaṃ santike vasantena nāma vissaṭṭhaattabhāvena bhavituṃ na vaṭṭati, kocideva manasikāro icchitabbo, tvaṃ pana aññaṃ na sakkhissasi, ‘‘aṭṭhi aṭṭhī’’ti sajjhāyaṃ karohīti. So theriyā ovāde ṭhatvā ‘‘aṭṭhi aṭṭhī’’ti sajjhāyanto carati.

Taṃ ekadivasaṃ pātova toraṇagge nisīditvā bālātapaṃ tapamānaṃ eko sakuṇo nakhapañjarena aggahesi. So ‘‘kiri kirī’’ti saddamakāsi. Sāmaṇeriyo sutvā ‘‘ayye buddharakkhito sakuṇena gahito, mocema na’’nti leḍḍuādīni gahetvā anubandhitvā mocesuṃ . Taṃ ānetvā purato ṭhapitaṃ therī āha – ‘‘buddharakkhita, sakuṇena gahitakāle kiṃ cintesī’’ti? Na, ayye, aññaṃ kiñci cintesiṃ, aṭṭhipuñjova aṭṭhipuñjaṃ gahetvā gacchati, katarasmiṃ ṭhāne vippakirissatīti, evaṃ ayye aṭṭhipuñjameva cintesinti. Sādhu, sādhu, buddharakkhita, anāgate bhavakkhayassa te paccayo bhavissatīti. Evaṃ tattha tiracchānagatāpi satipaṭṭhānamanasikārayuttā. Tasmā nesaṃ bhagavā satipaṭṭhānabuddhimeva janento idaṃ suttamabhāsi.

Tattha ekāyanoti ekamaggo. Maggassa hi –

ekāyano

‘‘Maggo pantho patho pajjo, añjasaṃ vaṭumāyanaṃ;

Nāvā uttarasetū ca, kullo ca bhisisaṅkamo’’ti.

Bahūni nāmāni. Svāyamidha ayananāmena vutto, tasmā ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggoti ettha ekamaggo ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo na dvidhā pathabhūtoti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Atha vā ekena ayitabboti ekāyano. Ekenāti gaṇasaṅgaṇikaṃ pahāya vūpakaṭṭhena pavivittacittena. Ayitabbo paṭipajjitabbo, ayanti vā etenāti ayano, saṃsārato nibbānaṃ gacchantīti attho. Ekassa ayano ekāyano. Ekassāti seṭṭhassa. Sabbasattaseṭṭho ca bhagavā, tasmā bhagavatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kiñcāpi hi tena aññepi ayanti, evaṃ santepi bhagavatova so ayano tena uppāditattā. Yathāha ‘‘so hi, brāhmaṇa, bhagavā anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā’’tiādi (ma. ni. 3.79). Ayatīti vā ayano, gacchati pavattatīti attho. Ekasmiṃ ayanoti ekāyano, imasmiññeva dhammavinaye pavattati, na aññatthāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yathāha – ‘‘imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhatī’’ti (dī. ni. 2.214). Desanābhedoyeva heso, atthato pana ekova. Apica ekaṃ ayatīti ekāyano. Pubbabhāge nānāmukhabhāvanānayappavattopi aparabhāge ekaṃ nibbānameva gacchatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Yathāha brahmā sahampati –

Ekassā

Ekāyanaṃ jātikhayantadassī,

Maggaṃ pajānāti hitānukampī;

Etena maggena tariṃsu pubbe,

Tarissanti ye ca taranti oghanti. (saṃ. ni. 5.409);

Keci pana ‘‘na pāraṃ diguṇaṃ yantī’’ti gāthānayena yasmā ekavāraṃ nibbānaṃ gacchati, tasmā ‘‘ekāyano’’ti vadanti, taṃ na yujjati. Imassa hi atthassa sakiṃ ayanoti iminā byañjanena bhavitabbaṃ. Yadi pana ekaṃ ayanamassa ekā gati pavattīti evaṃ atthaṃ yojetvā vucceyya, byañjanaṃ yujjeyya, attho pana ubhayathāpi na yujjati. Kasmā? Idha pubbabhāgamaggassa adhippetattā. Kāyādicatuārammaṇappavatto hi pubbabhāgasatipaṭṭhānamaggo idhādhippeto, na lokuttaro, so ca anekavārampi ayati, anekañcassa ayanaṃ hoti.

Pubbepi ca imasmiṃ pade mahātherānaṃ sākacchā ahosiyeva. Tipiṭakacūḷanāgatthero pubbabhāgasatipaṭṭhānamaggoti āha. Ācariyo panassa tipiṭakacūḷasumatthero missakamaggoti āha. Pubbabhāgo bhanteti? Missako, āvusoti. Ācariye pana punappunaṃ bhaṇante appaṭibāhitvā tuṇhī ahosi. Pañhaṃ avinicchinitvāva uṭṭhahiṃsu. Athācariyatthero nahānakoṭṭhakaṃ gacchanto ‘‘mayā missakamaggo kathito, cūḷanāgo pubbabhāgamaggoti ādāya voharati, ko nu kho ettha nicchayo’’ti suttantaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya parivattento ‘‘yo hi koci , bhikkhave, ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṃ bhāveyya satta vassānī’’ti imasmiṃ ṭhāne sallakkhesi. Lokuttaramaggo uppajjitvā satta vassāni tiṭṭhamāno nāma natthi, mayā vutto missakamaggo na labbhati. Cūḷanāgena diṭṭho pubbabhāgamaggova labbhatīti ñatvā aṭṭhamiyaṃ dhammasavane saṅghuṭṭhe agamāsi.

Porāṇakattherā kira piyadhammasavanā honti, saddaṃ sutvāva ‘‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ, ahaṃ paṭhama’’nti ekappahāreneva osaranti. Tasmiñca divase cūḷanāgattherassa vāro, tena dhammāsane nisīditvā bījaniṃ gahetvā pubbagāthāsu vuttāsu therassa āsanapiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa etadahosi – ‘‘raho nisīditvā na vakkhāmī’’ti. Porāṇakattherā hi anusūyakā honti. Na attano rucimeva ucchubhāraṃ viya evaṃ ukkhipitvā vicaranti, kāraṇameva gaṇhanti, akāraṇaṃ vissajjenti. Tasmā thero ‘‘āvuso, cūḷanāgā’’ti āha. So ācariyassa viya saddoti dhammaṃ ṭhapetvā ‘‘kiṃ bhante’’ti āha. Āvuso, cūḷanāga, mayā vutto missakamaggo na labbhati, tayā vutto pubbabhāgasatipaṭṭhānamaggova labbhatīti. Thero cintesi – ‘‘amhākaṃ ācariyo sabbapariyattiko tepiṭako sutabuddho, evarūpassāpi nāma bhikkhuno ayaṃ pañho āluḷeti, anāgate mama bhātikā imaṃ pañhaṃ āluḷessantīti suttaṃ gahetvā imaṃ pañhaṃ niccalaṃ karissāmī’’ti paṭisambhidāmaggato ‘‘ekāyanamaggo vuccati pubbabhāgasatipaṭṭhānamaggo’’.

Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṃ caturo padā;

Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṃ, dvipadānañca cakkhumā.

Eseva maggo natthañño, dassanassa visuddhiyā;

Etañhi tumhe paṭipajjatha, mārasenappamaddanaṃ;

Etañhi tumhe paṭipannā, dukkhassantaṃ karissathāti. –

Suttaṃ āharitvā ṭhapesi.

Maggoti kenaṭṭhena maggo? Nibbānagamanaṭṭhena nibbānatthikehi magganīyaṭṭhena ca. Sattānaṃ visuddhiyāti rāgādīhi malehi abhijjhāvisamalobhādīhi ca upakkilesehi kiliṭṭhacittānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhatthāya. Tathā hi imināva maggena ito satasahassakappādhikānaṃ catunnaṃ asaṅkhyeyyānaṃ upari ekasmiṃyeva kappe nibbatte taṇhaṅkaramedhaṅkarasaraṇaṅkaradīpaṅkaranāmake buddhe ādiṃ katvā sakyamunipariyosānā aneke sammāsambuddhā anekasatā paccekabuddhā gaṇanapathaṃ vītivattā ariyasāvakā cāti ime sattā sabbe cittamalaṃ pavāhetvā paramavisuddhiṃ pattā. Rūpamalavasena pana saṃkilesavodānapaññattiyeva natthi. Tathā hi –

Maggo Sattānaṃ visuddhiyā

‘‘Rūpena saṃkiliṭṭhena, saṃkilissanti māṇavā;

Rūpe suddhe visujjhanti, anakkhātaṃ mahesinā.

Cittena saṃkiliṭṭhena, saṃkilissanti māṇavā;

Citte suddhe visujjhanti, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā’’.

Yathāha – ‘‘cittasaṃkilesā, bhikkhave, sattā saṃkilissanti, cittavodānā visujjhantī’’ti. Tañca cittavodānaṃ iminā satipaṭṭhānamaggena hoti. Tenāha ‘‘sattānaṃ visuddhiyā’’ti.

Sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāyāti sokassa ca paridevassa ca samatikkamāya pahānāyāti attho, ayañhi maggo bhāvito santatimahāmattādīnaṃ viya sokasamatikkamāya, paṭācārādīnaṃ viya paridevasamatikkamāya saṃvattati. Tenāha ‘‘sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāyā’’ti. Kiñcāpi hi santatimahāmatto –
