Atha kho setabyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā setabyāya nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūtā uttarenamukhā gacchanti yena siṃsapāvanaṃ yena siṃsapāvanaṃ, tenupasaṅkamanti (sī. pī.).
mula_english:
At that time, Prince Pāyāsi had arisen with the following evil view: "Indeed, there is no other world ( *paro loko*), there are no beings who are spontaneously born (*sattā opapātikā*), there is no fruit (*phalaṃ*) or result (*vipāko*) of deeds well done or ill done (*sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ*)."

The Brahmins and householders of Setabya heard: "The *śramaṇa* Kumārakassapa, a disciple (*sāvako*) of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, while wandering in Kosala with a great *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, with about five hundred *bhikkhus*, has arrived at Setabya and is staying north of Setabya in the *Siṃsapāvana* (Simsapa Forest)."

Now, concerning the venerable Kumārakassapa, such a good report (*kalyāṇo kittisaddo*) has spread about: "He is learned (*paṇḍito*), experienced (*byatto*), wise (*medhāvī*), well-informed (*bahussuto*), a fine speaker (*cittakathī*), able to give good replies (*kalyāṇapaṭibhāno*), venerable (*vuddho*), and an *arhat* (*arahā*)."

Then the Brahmins and householders of Setabya, having left Setabya, gathered in groups and crowds and went northwards to the *Siṃsapāvana* (Simsapa Forest).

mula_pali:
408. Tena kho pana samayena pāyāsi rājañño uparipāsāde divāseyyaṃ upagato hoti. Addasā kho pāyāsi rājañño setabyake brāhmaṇagahapatike setabyāya nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūte uttarenamukhe gacchante yena siṃsapāvanaṃ yena siṃsapāvanaṃ, tenupasaṅkamante (sī. pī.), disvā khattaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho, bho khatte, setabyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā setabyāya nikkhamitvā saṅghasaṅghī gaṇībhūtā uttarenamukhā gacchanti yena siṃsapāvana’’nti ettha pana sabbatthapi evameva dissati, natthi pāṭhantaraṃ?

‘‘Atthi kho, bho, samaṇo kumārakassapo, samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi setabyaṃ anuppatto setabyāyaṃ viharati uttarena setabyaṃ siṃsapāvane. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘paṇḍito byatto medhāvī bahussuto cittakathī kalyāṇapaṭibhāno vuddho ceva arahā cā’ti arahā ca (syā. ka.). Tamete tamenaṃ te (sī. ka.), tamenaṃ (pī.) bhavantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bho khatte, yena setabyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā setabyake brāhmaṇagahapatike evaṃ vadehi – ‘pāyāsi, bho, rājañño evamāha – āgamentu kira bhavanto, pāyāsipi rājañño samaṇaṃ kumārakassapaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’ti. Purā samaṇo kumārakassapo setabyake brāhmaṇagahapatike bāle abyatte saññāpeti – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’ti. Natthi hi, bho khatte, paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ bho’’ti kho so khattā pāyāsissa rājaññassa paṭissutvā yena setabyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā setabyake brāhmaṇagahapatike etadavoca – ‘‘pāyāsi, bho, rājañño evamāha, āgamentu kira bhavanto, pāyāsipi rājañño samaṇaṃ kumārakassapaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’’ti.

arahā ca (syā. ka.) tamenaṃ te (sī. ka.), tamenaṃ (pī.)
mula_english:
408. At that time, Prince Pāyāsi had gone up to the upper story of his palace for his midday rest.

Prince Pāyāsi saw the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā leaving Setabyā, in a large group, heading north towards the *siṃsapā* forest. <note>Because they were heading toward the *siṃsapā* forest, they were approaching.</note> Seeing this, he addressed his steward, "Why, steward, are the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā leaving Setabyā, in a large group, heading north towards the *siṃsapā* forest?"<note>Here, it appears the same everywhere, there is no variant reading.</note>

"Sir, the renunciate Kumārakassapa, a disciple of the renunciate Gotama, is wandering in Kosala with a large *bhikkhu-saṃgha* of about five hundred *bhikkhus*. He has arrived at Setabyā and is staying to the north of Setabyā in the *siṃsapā* forest. Concerning the venerable Kumārakassapa, a good report has spread: 'He is learned, experienced, wise, well-informed, a fine speaker, able to give good replies, venerable, and an *arhat*.' "<note> *Arhat* and so on.</note> "They are going to see the venerable Kumārakassapa."<note>They, that is.</note>

"Then, steward, go to the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā; having gone, tell the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā, 'Prince Pāyāsi says this: "Please wait, Prince Pāyāsi will also go to see the renunciate Kumārakassapa."' Already, the renunciate Kumārakassapa has been persuading the foolish and inexperienced *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā that 'there is another world, there are beings who arise spontaneously (*opapātikā*), there is fruit and result of good and bad actions (*karma*)'. But there is no other world, there are no beings who arise spontaneously, there is no fruit and result of good and bad actions."

"Very well, sir," said the steward, and after promising Prince Pāyāsi, he went to the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā; having gone, he said to the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Setabyā, "Prince Pāyāsi says this: 'Please wait, Prince Pāyāsi will also go to see the renunciate Kumārakassapa.'"

mula_pali:
409. Atha kho pāyāsi rājañño setabyakehi brāhmaṇagahapatikehi parivuto yena siṃsapāvanaṃ yenāyasmā kumārakassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā kumārakassapena saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Setabyakāpi kho brāhmaṇagahapatikā appekacce āyasmantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce āyasmatā kumārakassapena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yenāyasmā kumārakassapo tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

Natthikavādo
mula_english:
Then Prince Payasi (Pāyāsi rājañño), accompanied by the Brahmins (brāhmaṇagahapatikehi) and householders of Setavya, went to the Simsapa Forest (Siṃsapāvanaṃ) where the Venerable Kumāra-Kassapa was. Having approached, he exchanged greetings (sammodi) with the Venerable Kumāra-Kassapa, and when this courteous and amiable talk (sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ) was finished, he sat down at one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdi).

And some of the Brahmins (brāhmaṇagahapatikā) and householders of Setavya saluted the Venerable Kumāra-Kassapa (Kumārakassapaṃ abhivādetvā) and then sat down to one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu), while some first exchanged courtesies (sammodiṃsu) with him, and when this courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu). Some saluted him with joined palms (añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā), in the direction of the Venerable Kumāra-Kassapa, and sat down to one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu). Some announced their name and clan (nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā) and sat down to one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu). Some kept silent (tuṇhībhūtā) and sat down at one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu).

The doctrine of non-existence.

mula_pali:
410. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho pāyāsi rājañño āyasmantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ahañhi, bho kassapa, evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhī – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti. ‘‘Nāhaṃ, rājañña, evaṃvādiṃ evaṃdiṭṭhiṃ addasaṃ vā assosiṃ vā. Kathañhi nāma evaṃ vadeyya – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’ti?

Candimasūriyaupamā
mula_english:
Then Prince Pāyāsi, having sat down to one side, said this to the Venerable Kumāra-Kassapa: “Reverend Kassapa, I hold to this tenet and this view: There is no other world ( *paro loko*), there are no spontaneously born beings (*sattā opapātikā*), there is no fruit or result (*phalaṃ vipāko*) of good or evil deeds (*sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ*).”

“Well, Prince, I have never seen or heard of such a tenet or view as you declare. How could anyone say such a thing: ‘There is no other world, there are no spontaneously born beings, there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds’?”

The Simile of the Moon and Sun

mula_pali: 411. ‘‘Tena hi, rājañña, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi, yathā te khameyya, tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājañña, ime candimasūriyā imasmiṃ vā loke parasmiṃ vā, devā vā te manussā vā’’ti? ‘‘Ime, bho kassapa, candimasūriyā parasmiṃ loke, na imasmiṃ; devā te na manussā’’ti. ‘‘Imināpi kho te, rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotu – itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’ti.
mula_english: ‘Then, Prince, I will question you about that very thing here. Answer as you see fit. What do you think, Prince? Are these suns and moons in this world or in another? Are they gods or humans?’ ‘These suns and moons, Master Kassapa, are in another world, not in this one; they are gods, not humans.’ ‘In the same way, Prince, you should consider: “There is another world, there are beings who arise spontaneously (*opapātikā*), there is a result (*vipāka*) and fruit (*phala*) to actions (*kamma*) that are well-done (*sukata*) and badly-done (*dukkaṭānaṃ*)".’
commentary_pali:
411.Ime bho, kassapa, candimasūriyāti so kira therena pucchito cintesi ‘‘ayaṃ samaṇo paṭhamaṃ candimasūriye upamaṃ āhari, candimasūriyasadiso bhavissati paññāya, anabhibhavanīyo aññena, sace panāhaṃ ‘candimasūriyā imasmiṃ loke’ti bhaṇissāmi, ‘kiṃ nissitā ete, kittakapamāṇā, kittakaṃ uccā’tiādīhi paliveṭhessati. Ahaṃ kho panetaṃ nibbeṭhetuṃ na sakkhissāmi, ‘parasmiṃ loke’ iccevassa kathessāmī’’ti. Tasmā evamāha.

Bhagavā pana tato pubbe na cirasseva sudhābhojanīyajātakaṃ kathesi. Tattha ‘‘cande cando devaputto, sūriye sūriyo devaputto’’ti āgataṃ. Bhagavatā ca kathitaṃ jātakaṃ vā suttantaṃ vā sakalajambudīpe patthaṭaṃ hoti, tena so ‘‘ettha nivāsino devaputtā natthī’’ti na sakkā vattunti cintetvā devā te na manussāti āha.

sudhābhojanīyajātakaṃ devā te na manussā
commentary_english:
411. “These, O Kashyapa, are the *candimasūriyā*.” When asked by that elder, he thought, "This *samaṇa* first brought the simile of the *candimasūriye*, he will be like the *candimasūriya* in wisdom, unexcelled by another. If I should say, ‘The *candimasūriyā* are in this world,’ he will entangle me with questions like, ‘What are they based on? What is their measure? How high are they?’

I will not be able to disentangle this. I will just tell him, ‘[They are] in another world.’”

Therefore, he spoke in this way.

The Blessed One then, before that, not long before, told the *sudhābhojanīyajātakaṃ*.

There it says, “The moon is a *devaputta* in the moon, the sun is a *devaputta* in the sun.”

The *jātaka* or *suttanta* told by the Blessed One is widespread in all of *sakalajambudīpa*. Therefore, thinking, “It is not possible to say that there are no *devaputtas* living here,” he said, “They are gods, not humans.”

*sudhābhojanīyajātakaṃ*

They are gods, not humans.

mula_pali:
412. ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ kassapo evamāha, atha kho evaṃ me ettha hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti. ‘‘Atthi pana, rājañña, pariyāyo, yena te pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti? ‘‘Atthi , bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ viya, rājaññā’’ti? ‘‘Idha me, bho kassapa, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpī abhijjhālū byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī. Te aparena samayena ābādhikā honti dukkhitā bāḷhagilānā. Yadāhaṃ jānāmi – ‘na dānime imamhā ābādhā vuṭṭhahissantī’ti tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘santi kho, bho, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ye te pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpī abhijjhālū byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjantī’ti. Bhavanto kho pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpī abhijjhālū byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī. Sace tesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ, bhavanto kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissanti. Sace, bho, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyyātha, yena me āgantvā āroceyyātha – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’ti . Bhavanto kho pana me saddhāyikā paccayikā, yaṃ bhavantehi diṭṭhaṃ, yathā sāmaṃ diṭṭhaṃ evametaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Te me ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā neva āgantvā ārocenti, na pana dūtaṃ pahiṇanti. Ayampi kho, bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

Coraupamā
mula_english:
‘‘Even though you, Reverend Kassapa, say this, I still think like this: ‘There is no other world, there are no spontaneously born beings, there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds.’"

‘‘Have you any reasons for this assertion, Prince?’’

‘‘Yes, Reverend Kassapa, I have a reason for thinking like this: ‘There is no other world, there are no spontaneously born beings, there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds.’"

‘‘What is that, Prince?’’

‘‘Reverend Kassapa, I have friends, colleagues, and blood-relations who take life, take what is not given, commit sexual offenses, tell lies, use abusive, harsh, and frivolous speech, who are greedy, full of hatred, and hold wrong views ( *micchādiṭṭhi*). Eventually, they become ill, suffering, diseased. And when I am sure they will not recover, I go to them and say: “There are certain ascetics and Brahmins who declare and believe that those who take life, take what is not given, commit sexual offenses, tell lies, use abusive, harsh, and frivolous speech, who are greedy, full of hatred and hold wrong views, will, after death at the breaking-up of the body, be born in a state of woe, an evil place, a place of punishment, in hell ( *apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti*).” You are takers of life, takers of what is not given, committers of sexual offenses, tellers of lies, users of abusive, harsh, and frivolous speech, greedy, full of hatred, and holders of wrong views. And if what these ascetics and Brahmins say is true, that is where you will go. Now if, after death, you go to a state of woe, an evil place, a place of punishment, in hell, come to me and declare that there is another world (* *atthi paro loko*), there are spontaneously born beings (* *atthi sattā opapātikā*), there is fruit and result of good and evil deeds (* *atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko*)." You, gentlemen, are trustworthy and dependable, and what you have seen shall be as if I had seen it myself, so it will be.” But although they agreed, they neither came to me, nor did they send a messenger. And that is why, Reverend Kassapa, I believe there is no other world…’"
commentary_pali:
412.Atthi pana, rājañña, pariyāyoti atthi pana kāraṇanti pucchati. Ābādhikāti visabhāgavedanāsaṅkhātena ābādhena samannāgatā. Dukkhitāti dukkhappattā. Bāḷhagilānāti adhimattagilānā. Saddhāyikāti ahaṃ tumhe saddahāmi, tumhe mayhaṃ saddhāyikā saddhāyitabbavacanāti attho. Paccayikāti ahaṃ tumhe pattiyāmi, tumhe mayhaṃ paccayikā pattiyāyitabbāti attho.

Corādiupamāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
412. "Is there, O king, a way (*pariyāyo*)?" means he asks, "Is there a cause (*kāraṇaṃ*)?".

"*Ābādhikā*" means afflicted with distress (*ābādha*) characterized by dissimilar sensations (*visabhāgavedanāsaṅkhātena*).

"*Dukkhitā*" means attained to suffering (*dukkhappattā*).

"*Bāḷhagilānā*" means excessively sick (*adhimattagilānā*).

"*Saddhāyikā*" means, "I trust you (*ahaṃ tumhe saddahāmi*), you are trustworthy to me (*tumhe mayhaṃ saddhāyikā saddhāyitabbavacanāti attho*)."

"*Paccayikā*" means, "I rely on you (*ahaṃ tumhe pattiyāmi*), you are reliable to me (*tumhe mayhaṃ paccayikā pattiyāyitabbāti attho*)."

Explanation of similes beginning with a thief (*corādiupamāvaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali: 413. ‘‘Tena hi, rājañña, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājañña, idha te purisā coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā dasseyyuṃ – ‘ayaṃ te, bhante, coro āgucārī; imassa yaṃ icchasi, taṃ daṇḍaṃ paṇehī’ti. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, imaṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kāretvā (syā. ka.) kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ rathiyāya rathiyaṃ (bahūsū) siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa āghātane sīsaṃ chindathā’ti. Te ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā taṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa āghātane nisīdāpeyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so coro coraghātesu – ‘āgamentu tāva bhavanto coraghātā, amukasmiṃ me gāme vā nigame vā mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, yāvāhaṃ tesaṃ uddisitvā āgacchāmī’ti , udāhu vippalapantasseva coraghātā sīsaṃ chindeyyu’’nti? ‘‘Na hi so, bho kassapa, coro labheyya coraghātesu – ‘āgamentu tāva bhavanto coraghātā amukasmiṃ me gāme vā nigame vā mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, yāvāhaṃ tesaṃ uddisitvā āgacchāmī’ti. Atha kho naṃ vippalapantasseva coraghātā sīsaṃ chindeyyu’’nti. ‘‘So hi nāma, rājañña, coro manusso manussabhūtesu coraghātesu na labhissati – ‘āgamentu tāva bhavanto coraghātā, amukasmiṃ me gāme vā nigame vā mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, yāvāhaṃ tesaṃ uddisitvā āgacchāmī’ti. Kiṃ pana te mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpī abhijjhālū byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā labhissanti nirayapālesu – ‘āgamentu tāva bhavanto nirayapālā, yāva mayaṃ pāyāsissa rājaññassa gantvā ārocema – ‘‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti? Imināpi kho te, rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotu – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.
mula_english:
413. ‘Well then, Prince, I will question you about this very matter.

Answer as you think fit.

What do you think, Prince? Suppose they were to bring a thief before you, caught in the act, and say: “This man, Lord, is a thief caught in the act. Sentence him to any punishment you wish.”

And you might say: “Bind this man’s arms tightly behind him with a strong rope, shave his head closely (khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā), and lead him to the rough sound of a drum (kharassarena paṇavena) through the streets (rathikāya rathikaṃ) and squares (siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ) and out through the southern gate (dakkhiṇena dvārena), and there at the place of execution (āghātane) in the south of the city, cut off his head (sīsaṃ chindatha).”

And they, saying: “Very good” in assent, might bind that man’s arms tightly behind him with a strong rope, shave his head closely (khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā), and lead him to the rough sound of a drum (kharassarena paṇavena) through the streets (rathikāya rathikaṃ) and squares (siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ) and out through the southern gate (dakkhiṇena dvārena), and there at the place of execution (āghātane) in the south of the city, make him sit down (nisīdāpeyyuṃ).

Now if that thief were to say to the executioners: “Good executioners, in such and such a village (gāme) or town (nigame) I have friends (mittāmaccā), colleagues and blood-relations (ñātisālohitā), please wait till I have visited them,”

would the executioners cut off the head of that very thief while he was still babbling?

“No, Reverend Kassapa, that thief would not get his wish from the executioners, saying: ‘Good executioners, in such and such a village (gāme) or town (nigame) I have friends (mittāmaccā), colleagues and blood-relations (ñātisālohitā), please wait till I have visited them.’”

"Rather, the executioners would just cut off his head while he was still babbling."

“So, Prince, this thief, being a human (manusso) among human executioners (manussabhūtesu coraghātesu) would not get his wish: ‘Good executioners, in such and such a village (gāme) or town (nigame) I have friends (mittāmaccā), colleagues and blood-relations (ñātisālohitā), please wait till I have visited them.’”

“How can your friends, colleagues and blood-relations (mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā) who are killers of living beings (pāṇātipātī), takers of what is not given (adinnādāyī), misconducting themselves in sexual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārī), liars (musāvādī), speakers of malicious speech (pisuṇavācā), speakers of harsh speech (pharusavācā), speakers of frivolous chatter (samphappalāpī), covetous (abhijjhālū), with minds full of ill will (byāpannacittā), and holding wrong views (micchādiṭṭhī)—having died (kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā) and gone to a place of misery (apāyaṃ), to a bad destination (duggatiṃ), to ruin (vinipātaṃ), to hell (nirayaṃ)—prevail upon the warders of hell (nirayapālesu), saying: ‘Good warders of hell, please wait while we go to Prince Payasi (pāyāsissa rājaññassa) and report to him: “Indeed, there is another world (paro loko), there are beings who are spontaneously born (sattā opapātikā), there is fruit and result (phalaṃ vipāko) of good and bad actions (sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ.’”

By this method too, Prince, let it be thus: 'Indeed, there is another world (paro loko), there are beings who are spontaneously born (sattā opapātikā), there is fruit and result (phalaṃ vipāko) of good and bad actions (sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ).'”
commentary_pali: 413.Uddisitvāti tesaṃ attānañca paṭisāmitabhaṇḍakañca dassetvā, sampaṭicchāpetvāti attho. Vippalapantassāti ‘‘putto me, dhītā me, dhanaṃ me’’ti vividhaṃ palapantassa. Nirayapālesūti niraye kammakāraṇikasattesu. Ye pana ‘‘kammameva kammakāraṇaṃ karoti, natthi nirayapālā’’ti vadanti. Te ‘‘tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā’’ti devadūtasuttaṃ paṭibāhanti. Manussaloke rājakulesu kāraṇikamanussā viya hi niraye nirayapālā honti.
commentary_english: 413. uddisitvā: Meaning, having pointed out those selves and the restored goods and having caused acceptance. vippalapantassa: Meaning, one who laments in various ways, saying, "I have a son, I have a daughter, I have wealth." nirayapālesū: Meaning, among the hell-wardens who are functionaries of karma in hell. Those who say, "Karma alone does the work of karma; there are no hell-wardens." They reject the *devadūtasutta*, saying, "Those hell-wardens, O *bhikkhus*." For in hell, there are hell-wardens, just as in the human world, in royal families, there are functionary humans.

mula_pali:
414. ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ kassapo evamāha, atha kho evaṃ me ettha hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’ti. ‘‘Atthi pana, rājañña, pariyāyo yena te pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti? ‘‘Atthi, bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ viya, rājaññā’’ti? ‘‘Idha me, bho kassapa, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratā anabhijjhālū abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhī. Te aparena samayena ābādhikā honti dukkhitā bāḷhagilānā. Yadāhaṃ jānāmi – ‘na dānime imamhā ābādhā vuṭṭhahissantī’ti tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘santi kho, bho, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ye te pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratā anabhijjhālū abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhī te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantīti . Bhavanto kho pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratā anabhijjhālū abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhī. Sace tesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ, bhavanto kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissanti. Sace, bho, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyātha, yena me āgantvā āroceyyātha – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’ti. Bhavanto kho pana me saddhāyikā paccayikā, yaṃ bhavantehi diṭṭhaṃ, yathā sāmaṃ diṭṭhaṃ evametaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Te me ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā neva āgantvā ārocenti, na pana dūtaṃ pahiṇanti. Ayampi kho, bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

Gūthakūpapurisaupamā
mula_english:
414. “Even though the esteemed Kassapa says this, nevertheless, this is what I think: ‘Indeed, there is no other world ( *paro loko*), there are no beings who are spontaneously born ( *sattā opapātikā*), there is no fruit or result ( *phalaṃ vipāko*) of good and bad actions ( *sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ*)’

“But, Prince ( *rājañña*), is there any reason why you hold this view: ‘Indeed, there is no other world, there are no beings who are spontaneously born, there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions’?”

“I have, Reverend Kassapa, a reason why I hold this view: ‘Indeed, there is no other world, there are no beings who are spontaneously born, there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions.’”

“How is that, Prince?”

“Here, Reverend Kassapa, I have friends, companions, relatives, and blood-relations who abstain from killing living beings ( *pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā*), abstain from taking what is not given ( *adinnādānā paṭiviratā*), abstain from sexual misconduct ( *kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā*), abstain from false speech ( *musāvādā paṭiviratā*), abstain from malicious speech ( *pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā*), abstain from harsh speech ( *pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā*), abstain from frivolous speech ( *samphappalāpā paṭiviratā*), are not covetous ( *anabhijjhālū*), have minds free from ill-will ( *abyāpannacittā*), and have right view ( *sammādiṭṭhī*).

Eventually they become ill, suffering, and seriously diseased ( *ābādhikā honti dukkhitā bāḷhagilānā*).

When I know for sure that they will not recover from that illness, I approach them and say this: ‘There are some ascetics and Brahmins who hold such views and say such things – those who abstain from killing living beings, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, abstain from malicious speech, abstain from harsh speech, abstain from frivolous speech, are not covetous, have minds free from ill-will, and have right view – after the breakup of the body, after death ( *kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā*), they will be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world ( *sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantīti*).

These esteemed individuals abstain from killing living beings, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, abstain from malicious speech, abstain from harsh speech, abstain from frivolous speech, are not covetous, have minds free from ill-will and have right view.

If what those ascetics and Brahmins say is true, then after the breakup of the body, after death, these esteemed individuals will be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

If, Reverend Kassapa, after the breakup of the body, after death, you should go to a good destination, a heavenly world, then come back to me and tell me: ‘Indeed, there is another world ( *paro loko*), there are beings who are spontaneously born ( *sattā opapātikā*), there is fruit or result of good and bad actions ( *sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko*).’

You, esteemed individuals, are reliable and trustworthy in my eyes, and what is seen by you is as good as seen by myself; so it will be.”

Having agreed with me by saying “Very well,” they neither come back and tell me, nor do they even send a messenger.

This, too, Reverend Kassapa, is a reason why I hold this view: ‘Indeed, there is no other world, there are no beings who are spontaneously born, there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions.’”

The Simile of the Cesspool Man

mula_pali:
415. ‘‘Tena hi, rājañña, upamaṃ te karissāmi. Upamāya midhekacce upamāyapidhekacce (sī. syā.), upamāyapiidhekacce (pī.) viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti. Seyyathāpi, rājañña, puriso gūthakūpe sasīsakaṃ sasīsako (syā.) nimuggo assa. Atha tvaṃ purise āṇāpeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, taṃ purisaṃ tamhā gūthakūpā uddharathā’ti. Te ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā taṃ purisaṃ tamhā gūthakūpā uddhareyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, tassa purisassa kāyā veḷupesikāhi gūthaṃ sunimmajjitaṃ nimmajjathā’ti. Te ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā tassa purisassa kāyā veḷupesikāhi gūthaṃ sunimmajjitaṃ nimmajjeyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, tassa purisassa kāyaṃ paṇḍumattikāya tikkhattuṃ subbaṭṭitaṃ ubbaṭṭethā’ti suppaṭṭitaṃ uppaṭṭethāti (ka.). Te tassa purisassa kāyaṃ paṇḍumattikāya tikkhattuṃ subbaṭṭitaṃ ubbaṭṭeyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, taṃ purisaṃ telena abbhañjitvā sukhumena cuṇṇena tikkhattuṃ suppadhotaṃ karothā’ti. Te taṃ purisaṃ telena abbhañjitvā sukhumena cuṇṇena tikkhattuṃ suppadhotaṃ kareyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, tassa purisassa kesamassuṃ kappethā’ti. Te tassa purisassa kesamassuṃ kappeyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, tassa purisassa mahagghañca mālaṃ mahagghañca vilepanaṃ mahagghāni ca vatthāni upaharathā’ti. Te tassa purisassa mahagghañca mālaṃ mahagghañca vilepanaṃ mahagghāni ca vatthāni upahareyyuṃ. Te tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘tena hi, bho, taṃ purisaṃ pāsādaṃ āropetvā pañcakāmaguṇāni upaṭṭhāpethā’ti. Te taṃ purisaṃ pāsādaṃ āropetvā pañcakāmaguṇāni upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājañña, api nu tassa purisassa sunhātassa suvilittassa sukappitakesamassussa āmukkamālābharaṇassa odātavatthavasanassa uparipāsādavaragatassa pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitassa samaṅgībhūtassa paricārayamānassa punadeva tasmiṃ gūthakūpe nimujjitukāmatā nimujjitukāmyatā (syā. ka.) assā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho kassapa’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Asuci, bho kassapa, gūthakūpo asuci ceva asucisaṅkhāto ca duggandho ca duggandhasaṅkhāto ca jeguccho ca jegucchasaṅkhāto ca paṭikūlo ca paṭikūlasaṅkhāto cā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, rājañña, manussā devānaṃ asucī ceva asucisaṅkhātā ca, duggandhā ca duggandhasaṅkhātā ca, jegucchā ca jegucchasaṅkhātā ca, paṭikūlā ca paṭikūlasaṅkhātā ca. Yojanasataṃ kho, rājañña, manussagandho deve ubbādhati. Kiṃ pana te mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratā anabhijjhālū abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhī, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā te āgantvā ārocessanti – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’ti? Imināpi kho te, rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotu – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

nimujjitukāmyatā (syā. ka.)
mula_english:
415. Then, Prince, I will give you a simile. Some wise people understand the meaning of a statement by means of a simile. Suppose, Prince, a man had fallen head first into a cesspit. Then you would tell your men: “Pull that man out of the cesspit!” And they would say: “Very good,” and pull that man out of the cesspit. Then you would tell them to clean his body thoroughly of the filth with bamboo scrapers. And they would say: “Very good,” and clean his body thoroughly of the filth with bamboo scrapers. Then you would tell them to give his body a triple shampoo with yellow loam. They would give his body a triple shampoo with yellow loam. Then you would tell them to anoint that man with oil and then to clean him three times with fine soap- powder. And they would anoint that man with oil and then clean him three times with fine soap-powder. Then you would tell them to dress that man's hair and beard. And they would dress that man's hair and beard. Then you would tell them to adorn that man with fine garlands, ointments and clothes. And they would adorn that man with fine garlands, ointments and clothes. Finally you would tell them to lead that man up to your palace and let him indulge in the pleasures of the five senses. And they would lead that man up to your palace and let him indulge in the pleasures of the five senses.

What do you think, Prince? Would there be any desire in that man – who had been well bathed, well anointed, well groomed with hair and beard properly dressed, adorned with garlands and ornaments, wearing clean, white clothes, who had ascended to the upper story of the palace – once he was well provided and fully furnished with the five qualities of sensual pleasure, and being waited upon, to plunge again into that cesspit?” “No, venerable Kassapa.” “What is the reason for that?” “Because, venerable Kassapa, that cesspit is unclean, considered to be unclean, evil-smelling, considered to be evil-smelling, horrible, considered to be horrible, revolting, and considered to be revolting.”

"Just so, Prince, human beings are unclean, considered to be unclean, evil-smelling, considered to be evil-smelling, horrible, considered to be horrible, revolting, and considered to be revolting to the gods. Indeed, Prince, the smell of human beings is offensive to the gods even at a distance of a hundred *yojana*s. Why would your friends, companions and relatives who abstain from killing living beings, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from misconduct in sexual matters, abstain from false speech, abstain from malicious speech, abstain from harsh speech, abstain from idle chatter, are free from covetousness, have minds free from ill will, and have right view – having been reborn after the body’s dissolution, after death, in a happy destination, a heavenly world – come back and announce: ‘There is another world, there are beings reborn spontaneously, there is fruit and result of good and bad deeds’? Therefore, Prince, admit that there is another world, that there are spontaneously born beings, and that there is fruit and result of good and evil deeds.”
ka.

commentary_pali:
415.Veḷupesikāhīti veḷuvilīvehi. Sunimmajjathāti yathā suṭṭhu nimmajjitaṃ hoti, evaṃ nimmajjatha, apanethāti attho.

Asucīti amanāpo. Asucisaṅkhātoti asucikoṭṭhāsabhūto asucīti ñāto vā. Duggandhoti kuṇapagandho. Jegucchoti jigucchitabbayutto. Paṭikūloti dassaneneva paṭighāvaho. Ubbādhatīti divasassa dvikkhattuṃ nhatvā tikkhattuṃ vatthāni parivattetvā alaṅkatapaṭimaṇḍitānaṃ cakkavattiādīnampi manussānaṃ gandho yojanasate ṭhitānaṃ devatānaṃ kaṇṭhe āsattakuṇapaṃ viya bādhati.

Asucī Asucisaṅkhāto Duggandho Jeguccho Paṭikūlo Ubbādhatī
commentary_english:
415. *veḷupesikāhī* means by means of *veḷuvilī*. *sunimmajjathā* means just as it is well immersed, so immerse [yourselves], remove [it], is the meaning.

*asucī* means unpleasant. *asucisaṅkhāto* means that which is known as impure, being a part of an impure mass. *duggandho* means the smell of a corpse. *jeguccho* means connected with what should be despised. *paṭikūlo* means bringing aversion by merely seeing it. *ubbādhatī* means having bathed twice during the day and changed clothes three times, the smell of even adorned and decorated humans such as a wheel-turning monarch afflicts the gods standing at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*, like a corpse stuck in their throats.

*asucī*, *asucisaṅkhāto*, *duggandho*, *jeguccho*, *paṭikūlo*, *ubbādhatī*.

mula_pali:
416. ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ kassapo evamāha, atha kho evaṃ me ettha hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti. ‘‘Atthi pana, rājañña, pariyāyo …pe… ‘‘atthi, bho kassapa, pariyāyo…pe… ``yathā kathaṃ viya, rājaññāti? ‘‘Idha me, bho kassapa, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā, te aparena samayena ābādhikā honti dukkhitā bāḷhagilānā. Yadāhaṃ jānāmi – ‘na dānime imamhā ābādhā vuṭṭhahissantī’ti tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘santi kho, bho, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ye te pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyatanti. Bhavanto kho pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā. Sace tesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ, bhavanto kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissanti, devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ. Sace, bho, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyātha devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ, yena me āgantvā āroceyyātha – `itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipākoti. Bhavanto kho pana me saddhāyikā paccayikā, yaṃ bhavantehi diṭṭhaṃ, yathā sāmaṃ diṭṭhaṃ evametaṃ bhavissatīti. Te me ‘sādhū’ti paṭissutvā neva āgantvā ārocenti, na pana dūtaṃ pahiṇanti. Ayampi kho, bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

Tāvatiṃsadevaupamā
mula_english:
416. ‘Whatever you may say about that, Reverend Kassapa, I still think there is no other world, there are no spontaneously born beings, there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds.’

‘Is there, great king, a way…?

‘Is there, Reverend Kassapa, a way…?

‘How is that, great king?’

‘Here, Reverend Kassapa, my friends, officials, relatives, and blood relations abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from telling lies, abstain from intoxicants that cause negligence. Later, they become sick, suffering, and seriously ill.

When I know that they will not recover from that illness, I approach them and say this: “There are some ascetics and Brahmins who declare and believe that those who abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from telling lies, abstain from intoxicants that cause negligence will, after death, at the breaking up of the body, be reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, in the company of the gods of the Thirty-three.”

Reverend Kassapa, my friends abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from telling lies, abstain from intoxicants that cause negligence.

If what those ascetics and Brahmins say is true, my friends will, after death, at the breaking up of the body, be reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, in the company of the gods of the Thirty-three.

Now if, Reverend Kassapa, after death, at the breaking up of the body, you should be reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, in the company of the gods of the Thirty-three, come to me and declare that there is another world, there are spontaneously born beings, there is fruit and result of good and evil deeds.

Reverend Kassapa, my friends are trustworthy and reliable, and whatever they have seen, as they have seen it themselves, that is how it will be.’

They agree with me that it is good, but they neither come to me and declare it, nor do they send a messenger.

That, Reverend Kassapa, is my reason for maintaining: “There is no other world, there are no spontaneously born beings, there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds.”’

The Simile of the Thirty-Three Gods
commentary_pali: 416. Puna pāṇātipātādipañcasīlāni samādāyavattentānaṃ vasena vadati. Tāvatiṃsānanti idañca dūre nibbattā tāva mā āgacchantu, ime kasmā na entīti vadati.
commentary_english:
Furthermore, he speaks in terms of the appropriation and maintenance of the five precepts, beginning with refraining from killing (*pāṇātipātādipañcasīlāni samādāyavattentānaṃ vasena vadati*).

"<hi rend="bold">tāvatiṃsāna</hi>nti: "And these, being born far away, should not come here. Why do these not come?" he says.

mula_pali:
417. ‘‘Tena hi, rājañña, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya, tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Yaṃ kho pana, rājañña, mānussakaṃ vassasataṃ, devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ eso eko rattindivo rattidivo (ka.), tāya rattiyā tiṃsarattiyo māso, tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo, tena saṃvaccharena dibbaṃ vassasahassaṃ devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ. Ye te mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ. Sace pana tesaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘yāva mayaṃ dve vā tīṇi vā rattindivā dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārema, atha mayaṃ pāyāsissa rājaññassa gantvā āroceyyāma – ‘‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’ti. Api nu te āgantvā āroceyyuṃ – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho kassapa. Api hi mayaṃ, bho kassapa, ciraṃ kālaṅkatāpi bhaveyyāma. Ko panetaṃ bhoto kassapassa āroceti – ‘atthi devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā ‘evaṃdīghāyukā devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā. Na mayaṃ bhoto kassapassa saddahāma – ‘atthi devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā ‘evaṃdīghāyukā devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā’’ti.

Jaccandhaupamā
mula_english:
417. “Then, Prince, I will question you about that very thing; answer as you see fit.

That which is for human beings a hundred years, Prince, is for the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (Tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ) one day and night, thirty of those nights make a month, twelve of those months make a year, and a thousand of those years is the life-span of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (Tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ).

Those friends and companions, relatives and blood-kin, who abstain from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā), abstain from taking what is not given (adinnādānā paṭiviratā), abstain from misconduct in sexual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā), abstain from false speech (musāvādā paṭiviratā), abstain from occasions for carelessness due to intoxicants consisting of liquor, beer, and spirits (surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā), those who, upon the breakup of the body, after death, have arisen in a good destination, a heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā), companionship with the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (Tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ).

Suppose they were to think, 'After we have indulged in the divine five strands of sense pleasure (dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārema) for two or three days and nights (dve vā tīṇi vā rattindivā), then we will go to Prince Pāyāsi (pāyāsissa rājaññassa) and announce, "Indeed, there is another world (paroloko), there are beings who are spontaneously born (sattā opapātikā), there is fruit and result of good and bad actions (sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko)."'

Could they come and announce (āgantvā āroceyyāma), 'Indeed, there is another world (paroloko), there are beings who are spontaneously born (sattā opapātikā), there is fruit and result of good and bad actions (sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko)'?"

"No, Reverend Kassapa (bho Kassapa).

Moreover, we might long have been dead (ciraṃ kālaṅkatāpi bhaveyyāma), Reverend Kassapa (bho Kassapa).

Who has told Reverend Kassapa (bhoto Kassapassa āroceti) – 'There are gods in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (devā Tāvatiṃsā)' or 'The gods in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (devā Tāvatiṃsā) are of such long life (evaṃdīghāyukā)'?

We do not believe Reverend Kassapa (bhoto Kassapassa saddahāma) – 'There are gods in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (devā Tāvatiṃsā)' or 'The gods in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (devā Tāvatiṃsā) are of such long life (evaṃdīghāyukā).' "

The Simile of the congenitally blind.

mula_pali:
418. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, rājañña, jaccandho puriso na passeyya kaṇha – sukkāni rūpāni , na passeyya nīlakāni rūpāni, na passeyya pītakāni mañjeṭṭhakāni (syā.) rūpāni, na passeyya lohitakāni rūpāni, na passeyya mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, na passeyya samavisamaṃ, na passeyya tārakāni rūpāni, na passeyya candimasūriye. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘natthi kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, natthi kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi nīlakāni rūpāni, natthi nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi pītakāni rūpāni, natthi pītakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi lohitakāni rūpāni, natthi lohitakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, natthi mañjiṭṭhakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi samavisamaṃ, natthi samavisamassa dassāvī. Natthi tārakāni rūpāni, natthi tārakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Natthi candimasūriyā, natthi candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī. Ahametaṃ na jānāmi, ahametaṃ na passāmi, tasmā taṃ natthī’ti. Sammā nu kho so, rājañña, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho kassapa. Atthi kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, atthi kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Atthi nīlakāni rūpāni, atthi nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī…pe… atthi samavisamaṃ, atthi samavisamassa dassāvī. Atthi tārakāni rūpāni, atthi tārakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī. Atthi candimasūriyā, atthi candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī. ‘Ahametaṃ na jānāmi, ahametaṃ na passāmi, tasmā taṃ natthī’ti. Na hi so, bho kassapa, sammā vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, rājañña, jaccandhūpamo maññe paṭibhāsi yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi’’.

‘‘Ko panetaṃ bhoto kassapassa āroceti – ‘atthi devā tāvatiṃsā’’ti vā, ‘evaṃdīghāyukā devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā? Na mayaṃ bhoto kassapassa saddahāma – ‘atthi devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā ‘evaṃdīghāyukā devā tāvatiṃsā’ti vā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, rājañña, evaṃ paro loko daṭṭhabbo, yathā tvaṃ maññasi iminā maṃsacakkhunā. Ye kho te rājañña samaṇabrāhmaṇā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti , te tattha appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā dibbacakkhuṃ visodhenti. Te dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena imaṃ ceva lokaṃ passanti parañca satte ca opapātike. Evañca kho, rājañña, paro loko daṭṭhabbo; natveva yathā tvaṃ maññasi iminā maṃsacakkhunā. Imināpi kho te, rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotu – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.
mula_english:
418. Imagine, Prince, a man blind from birth who could not see dark or light forms ( *rūpāṇi*), or blue forms, or yellow forms, or red forms, or crimson forms, could not see what was even and uneven, could not see the star forms, and could not see the moon and sun. He might say: “There are no dark and light forms, and no one who sees dark and light forms. There are no blue forms, and no one who sees blue forms. There are no yellow forms, and no one who sees yellow forms. There are no red forms, and no one who sees red forms. There are no crimson forms, and no one who sees crimson forms. There is nothing even and uneven, and no one who sees anything even and uneven. There are no star forms, and no one who sees star forms. There is no moon or sun, and nobody who can see them. I do not know these, I do not see these, therefore these do not exist.”

Would he be speaking rightly, Prince? “No, Reverend Kassapa. There are dark and light forms, and those who see dark and light forms. There are blue forms, and those who see blue forms…pe… There is what is even and uneven, and one who sees what is even and uneven. There are star forms, and those who see star forms. There is a sun and a moon, and those who see the sun and the moon. ‘I am not aware of this thing, I cannot see it, and therefore it does not exist.’ He would not be speaking rightly.”

“Well, Prince, it appears that your reply is like that of the blind man when you ask how I know about the Thirty-Three Gods and their longevity.”

“But, Reverend Kassapa, who has told you that the Thirty-Three Gods ( *devā tāvatiṃsā* ) exist, and that they are so long-lived? I don’t believe the Thirty-Three Gods ( *devā tāvatiṃsā* ) exist or are so long- lived.”

“Prince, the other world ( *paro loko* ) cannot be seen the way you think, with the physical eye ( *maṃsacakkhunā*). Prince, those ascetics and Brahmins ( *samaṇabrāhmaṇā* ) who seek in the jungle-thickets and the recesses of the forest for a resting-place that is quiet, with little noise—they stay there unwearied, ardent, restrained, purifying the divine eye ( *dibbacakkhuṃ* ), and with that purified divine eye ( *dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena* ) that exceeds the powers of human sight, they see both this world ( *lokaṃ* ) and the next, and spontaneously born beings ( *opapātike*). That, Prince, is how the other world ( *paro loko* ) can be seen, and not the way you think, with the physical eye ( *maṃsacakkhunā*). Therefore, Prince, admit that there is another world ( *paro loko* ), that there are spontaneously born beings ( *sattā opapātikā*), and that there is fruit and result of good and evil deeds ( *sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko* ).”
commentary_pali: 418.Jaccandhūpamomaññe paṭibhāsīti jaccandho viya upaṭṭhāsi. Araññavanapatthānīti araññakaṅgayuttatāya araññāni, mahāvanasaṇḍatāya vanapatthāni. Pantānīti dūrāni.
commentary_english: 418. *jaccandhūpamo maññe paṭibhāsī* means he appeared like someone blind from birth. *araññavanapatthānī* means forests (*araññāni*) because they are connected to solitary places, and forest regions (*vanapatthāni*) because they are dense, large forests. *pantānī* means distant.

mula_pali:
419. ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ kassapo evamāha, atha kho evaṃ me ettha hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’ti . ‘‘Atthi pana, rājañña, pariyāyo…pe… atthi, bho kassapa, pariyāyo…pe… yathā kathaṃ viya, rājaññā’’ti? ‘‘Idhāhaṃ, bho kassapa, passāmi samaṇabrāhmaṇe sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme jīvitukāme amaritukāme sukhakāme dukkhapaṭikūle. Tassa mayhaṃ, bho kassapa, evaṃ hoti – sace kho ime bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā evaṃ jāneyyuṃ – ‘ito no matānaṃ seyyo bhavissatī’ti. Idānime bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā visaṃ vā khādeyyuṃ, satthaṃ vā āhareyyuṃ, ubbandhitvā vā kālaṅkareyyuṃ, papāte vā papateyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho ime bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā na evaṃ jānanti – ‘ito no matānaṃ seyyo bhavissatī’ti, tasmā ime bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā jīvitukāmā amaritukāmā sukhakāmā dukkhapaṭikūlā attānaṃ na mārenti ( ) natthi (syā. pī.). Ayampi kho, bho kassapa, pariyāyo, yena me pariyāyena evaṃ hoti – ‘itipi natthi paro loko, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

Gabbhinīupamā
mula_english:
419. Even though venerable Kaśyapa says this, still it occurs to me thus: "Indeed, there is no other world ( *paro loko*), there are no spontaneously born beings (*sattā opapātikā*), there is no fruit (*phalaṃ*) or result (*vipāko*) of good (*sukata*) or bad actions (*duukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ*)."
“Is there, O king, a way…pe… There is, venerable Kaśyapa, a way…pe… How is that, O king?” “Here, venerable Kaśyapa, I see ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇe*) who are virtuous (*sīlavante*), have good qualities (*kalyāṇadhamme*), desire to live (*jīvitukāme*), desire not to die (*amaritukāme*), desire happiness (*sukhakāme*), and are averse to suffering (*dukkhapaṭikūle*).
It occurs to me, venerable Kaśyapa, thus: ‘If these good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā*) knew that after death they would be better off (*seyyo bhavissatī*),
then these good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā*) would now take poison, take a knife, hang themselves, or jump off a cliff.
But because these good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā*) do not know that after death they will be better off (*seyyo bhavissatī*), therefore these good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā*) desire to live (*jīvitukāmā*), desire not to die (*amaritukāmā*), desire happiness (*sukhakāmā*), are averse to suffering (*dukkhapaṭikūlā*), and do not kill themselves.
That, venerable Kaśyapa, is a reason, whereby it occurs to me thus: “Indeed, there is no other world ( *paro loko*), there are no spontaneously born beings (*sattā opapātikā*), there is no fruit (*phalaṃ*) or result (*vipāko*) of good (*sukata*) or bad actions (*duukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ*).”

Analogy of the pregnant woman
commentary_pali: 419.Kalyāṇadhammeti teneva sīlena sundaradhamme. Dukkhapaṭikūleti dukkhaṃ apatthente. Seyyo bhavissatīti paraloke sugatisukhaṃ bhavissatīti adhippāyo.
commentary_english:
419. *Kalyāṇadhamme* means beautiful *dharmas* (sundaradhamme) through that very conduct (*sīlena*).

*Dukkhapaṭikūle* means not desiring suffering (*dukkhaṃ apatthente*).

*Seyyo bhavissatī* means the intention (*adhippāyo*) is that there will be happiness in a good rebirth in the next world (*paraloke sugatisukhaṃ bhavissatīti*).

mula_pali:
420. ‘‘Tena hi, rājañña, upamaṃ te karissāmi. Upamāya midhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, rājañña, aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa dve pajāpatiyo ahesuṃ. Ekissā putto ahosi dasavassuddesiko vā dvādasavassuddesiko vā, ekā gabbhinī upavijaññā. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo kālamakāsi. Atha kho so māṇavako mātusapattiṃ mātusapatiṃ (syā.) etadavoca – ‘yamidaṃ, bhoti, dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ mayhaṃ ; natthi tuyhettha kiñci. Pitu me pitu me santako (syā.) bhoti, dāyajjaṃ niyyādehī’ti nīyyātehīti (sī. pī.). Evaṃ vutte sā brāhmaṇī taṃ māṇavakaṃ etadavoca – ‘āgamehi tāva, tāta, yāva vijāyāmi. Sace kumārako bhavissati, tassapi ekadeso bhavissati; sace kumārikā bhavissati, sāpi te opabhoggā upabhoggā (syā.) bhavissatī’ti. Dutiyampi kho so māṇavako mātusapattiṃ etadavoca – ‘yamidaṃ, bhoti, dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ mayhaṃ; natthi tuyhettha kiñci. Pitu me, bhoti, dāyajjaṃ niyyādehī’ti. Dutiyampi kho sā brāhmaṇī taṃ māṇavakaṃ etadavoca – ‘āgamehi tāva, tāta, yāva vijāyāmi. Sace kumārako bhavissati, tassapi ekadeso bhavissati; sace kumārikā bhavissati sāpi te opabhoggā upabhoggā (syā.) bhavissatī’ti. Tatiyampi kho so māṇavako mātusapattiṃ etadavoca – ‘yamidaṃ, bhoti, dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā , sabbaṃ taṃ mayhaṃ; natthi tuyhettha kiñci. Pitu me, bhoti, dāyajjaṃ niyyādehī’ti.

‘‘Atha kho sā brāhmaṇī satthaṃ gahetvā ovarakaṃ pavisitvā udaraṃ opādesi uppātesi (syā.) – ‘yāva vijāyāmi yadi vā kumārako yadi vā kumārikā’ti. Sā attānaṃ ceva jīvitañca gabbhañca sāpateyyañca vināsesi. Yathā taṃ bālā abyattā anayabyasanaṃ āpannā ayoniso dāyajjaṃ gavesantī, evameva kho tvaṃ, rājañña, bālo abyatto anayabyasanaṃ āpajjissasi ayoniso paralokaṃ gavesanto ; seyyathāpi sā brāhmaṇī bālā abyattā anayabyasanaṃ āpannā ayoniso dāyajjaṃ gavesantī. Na kho, rājañña, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā apakkaṃ paripācenti; api ca paripākaṃ āgamenti. Paṇḍitānaṃ attho hi, rājañña, samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlavantānaṃ kalyāṇadhammānaṃ jīvitena. Yathā yathā kho, rājañña, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti, tathā tathā bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavanti, bahujanahitāya ca paṭipajjanti bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Imināpi kho te, rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotu – ‘itipi atthi paro loko, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko’’’ti.

uppātesi (syā.)
mula_english:
420. Well then, Prince (rājañña), I will give you a simile (upamā). For some wise people understand what is said by means of similes. Once upon a time, Prince (rājañña), a certain Brahmin (brāhmaṇa) had two wives (pajāpati). One had a son ten or twelve years old (dasavassuddesiko vā dvādasavassuddesiko vā), while the other was pregnant and nearing her time (gabbhinī upavijaññā). Then that Brahmin (brāhmaṇa) died (kālamakāsi). Then this youth (māṇavaka) said this to his mother’s co-wife (mātusapattiṃ): “Lady (bhoti), whatever wealth (dhana), possessions (dhañña), silver (rajata) or gold (jātarūpa) there may be, is all mine; there is nothing here for you. My father (pitu) made me his heir (dāyajjaṃ niyyādehi).”

Thus addressed, that Brahmin (brāhmaṇī) lady said to the youth (māṇavaka): “Wait, young man (tāta), until I give birth (yāva vijāyāmi). If the child is a boy (kumārako), one portion will be his, and if it is a girl (kumārikā), she will become your servant (opabhoggā).” The youth (māṇavaka) said the same to his mother’s co-wife (mātusapattiṃ) a second time: “Lady (bhoti), whatever wealth (dhana), possessions (dhañña), silver (rajata) or gold (jātarūpa) there may be, is all mine; there is nothing here for you. My father (pitu) made me his heir (dāyajjaṃ niyyādehi).” That Brahmin (brāhmaṇī) lady said the same to the youth (māṇavaka) a second time: “Wait, young man (tāta), until I give birth (yāva vijāyāmi). If the child is a boy (kumārako), one portion will be his, and if it is a girl (kumārikā) she will become your servant (opabhoggā).” The youth (māṇavaka) said the same to his mother’s co-wife (mātusapattiṃ) a third time: “Lady (bhoti), whatever wealth (dhana), possessions (dhañña), silver (rajata) or gold (jātarūpa) there may be, is all mine; there is nothing here for you. My father (pitu) made me his heir (dāyajjaṃ niyyādehi).”

Then the Brahmin (brāhmaṇī) lady took a knife (satthaṃ gahetvā) and, going into an inner room (ovarakaṃ pavisitvā), cut open her belly (udaraṃ opādesi), thinking: “If only I could find out whether it is a boy or a girl!” And thus she destroyed herself (attānaṃ) and the living embryo (jīvitañca gabbhañca), and the wealth (sāpateyyañca) as well. Just as fools (bālā abyattā) do who seek their inheritance (dāyajjaṃ gavesantī) unwisely (ayoniso), heedless of hidden danger (anaya byasanaṃ āpannā). In the same way you, Prince (rājāñña), will foolishly (bālo abyatto) enter on hidden dangers (anaya byasanaṃ āpajjissasi) by unwisely (ayoniso) seeking for another world (paralokaṃ gavesanto), just as that Brahmin (brāhmaṇī) lady did in seeking her inheritance (dāyajjaṃ gavesantī). But, Prince (rājāñña), those ascetics (samaṇa) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) who observe morality (sīlavanto) and are well-conducted (kalyāṇadhammā) do not seek to hasten the ripening (paripācenti) of that which is not yet ripe (apakkaṃ), but rather they wisely await its ripening (paripākaṃ āgamenti). Their life (jīvitena) is profitable (attho hi) to those ascetics (samaṇa) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇānaṃ), O Prince (rājāñña). For the longer such moral (sīlavanto) and well-conducted (kalyāṇadhammā) ascetics (samaṇa) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) remain alive (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti), the greater the merit (bahuṃ puññaṃ) that they create (pasavanti); they practise for the welfare (bahujanahitāya) of the many, for the happiness (bahujanasukhāya) of the many, out of compassion (lokānukampāya) for the world, for the profit (atthāya) and benefit (hitāya) of devas (deva) and humans (manussānaṃ). In the same way, Prince (rājāñña), you should consider (evaṃ hotu): “There is another world (paro loko), there are spontaneously born beings (opapātikā sattā), there is fruit and result (phalaṃ vipāko) of good (sukata) and evil (dukkaṭānaṃ) deeds (kammānaṃ).”
